Inter‐Comparison of Snow Depth Over Antarctic Sea Ice From Ocean Reanalyzes and Observations
abstract: Abstract Snow depth on Antarctic sea ice is a critical climate variable affecting energy and mass balance, yet its observation and modeling remain challenging. We present a systematic intercomparison of snow depth from six ocean reanalysis products, two satellite retrievals, and ship‐based and airborne observational constraints. Results indicate that reanalysis and satellite products show consistent large‐scale climatological snow depth patterns, with the highest depths in the Weddell Sea. However, substantial differences remain in magnitude, seasonal phasing, spatial variability, and trends.

abstract: This is a human-written perspective paper on artificial intelligence (AI). We are all in a global AI experiment that has exciting prospects and questionable ethics. abstract: Atmospheric water generation is increasingly considered for decentralised freshwater production, yet system selection and operation are still commonly based on nominal manufacturer ratings that poorly represent variable field conditions. abstract: Abstract. This study assesses the potential impacts of future climate change on annual median and extreme wave conditions in the North Sea and the Baltic Sea using a ensemble of up to 14 and 8 regional projections, respectively. The ensemble includes simulations based on IPCC CMIP3 and CMIP5 scenarios, incorporating a range of global and regional climate models, initial conditions, and emission scenarios to reflect diverse sources of uncertainty. title: Physics-informed LSTMNet for short-term marine buoy trajectory prediction under dynamic ocean environmental conditions
abstract: Introduction Marine buoys are essential aids to navigation, yet their positions can vary continuously under dynamic environmental forcing. It is therefore important for navigational safety, maintenance planning, and reducing search-and-recovery costs to achieve accurate short-term prediction of buoy displacement. title: Bilingua‐DPP‐IV: A Bimodal Fusion Convolutional Neural Network Model for Prediction of Dipeptidyl Peptidase IV Inhibitory Peptides
abstract: MOTIVATION: Dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV) is a key therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes, and its inhibitory peptides are a promising class of therapeutic agents. However, the discovery of these promising drugs has been restricted, as many existing computational predictors are based on datasets that have remained static for several years. title: A Cross-Scale 3D Attention and Boundary-Aware Network for Sea–Land Segmentation
abstract: Coastal segmentation struggles with complex terrain configurations and discontinuous edge demarcation. abstract: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. abstract: Abstract. Glacier surface mass balance (SMB) is a key climate indicator and a central driver of glacier change. Direct SMB observations remain sparse and unevenly distributed. Hence, transferable SMB models are essential for large-scale assessments and projections. Here, we propose the GLAcier-UNiversal Temperature Index model (GlaUnTI) for this purpose. title: ¿La Inteligencia Artificial nos hace más inteligentes o dependientes? Una mirada desde la vida universitaria
abstract: Hoy es muy común que los estudiantes universitarios usen herramientas como ChatGPT para resumir textos, resolver ejercicios, escribir trabajos o aclarar dudas. Esto genera una pregunta que nos toca de cerca: ¿estas herramientas nos ayudan a pensar mejor o nos acostumbran a no pensar? En este artículo revisamos estudios recientes sobre el efecto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en el aprendizaje, el pensamiento crítico y la resolución de problemas. abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) distributions provide a foundation for understanding upper-ocean ecosystem dynamics and biogeochemical variability. We developed the source-target coupled network (ST-CoupleNet), a physics-guided transfer learning framework that combines Earth system model simulations with observation-constrained reconstructions to estimate subsurface Chl-a in the Northwest Pacific Ocean. title: Perceptions, Experiences, And Ethical Attitudes Toward Artificial Intelligence Among Undergraduates: A Qualitative Study
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into Nigerian higher education has transformed how students learn, complete assessments, and conceptualize knowledge. Yet while quantitative studies have documented Nigerian students' favorable perceptions and growing use of AI tools, qualitative understanding of how undergraduates in this context perceive, experience, and ethically evaluate these technologies remains less developed. title: Dynamics-informed deep learning for predicting extreme events
abstract: Abstract Predicting extreme events in high-dimensional chaotic dynamical systems remains a fundamental challenge because these events are rare, intermittent and often driven by transient dynamical mechanisms that are difficult to identify from limited observations. We propose a fully data-driven framework for real-time forecasting of extreme events based on an interpretable, mechanism-aware precursor that tracks the transient instabilities preceding event onset. abstract: Introduction Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are an increasing climate hazard for coastal aquaculture, yet regional assessments may not resolve how exposure varies across the locations where farms operate. abstract: This study investigates the effects of hypoxic altitude on postural stability using statistical analysis and feature-selection-based machine learning. abstract: Over the past decade, emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been increasingly reported in aquatic environments. Still, the environmental behavior of numerous emerging PFAS remains poorly understood. This study investigated trophic dynamics and contamination patterns of both legacy and emerging PFAS revealed by HRMS, in the food web of common sole (benthic) and European sea bass (demersal). abstract: Accurate prediction of local scour around river-training structures during flood events remains a major challenge because scour evolution is governed by highly nonlinear interactions among hydraulic conditions, structural permeability, sediment transport, and time-dependent bed morphology. In this study, fifteen local European plum varieties collected from the Central and Eastern Black Sea Region of Türkiye were evaluated during [2022 and 2023 year] to characterize their morphological and biochemical diversity and to identify the key biochemical determinants of antioxidant activity. abstract: Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) braided composites have considerable application potential in aerospace, defense, transportation, and marine engineering owing to their excellent structural integrity and mechanical properties. However, during the 3D braiding process, yarns are susceptible to fluctuations in creel tension, wear of yarn-guiding components, and variations in process parameters, causing fiber anomalies such as fiber breakage and fuzzing. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic disturbances and climate change, despite providing ecological services, including biodiversity conservation, coastal protection, and blue carbon storage. Long-term evaluations of mangrove dynamics and associated environmental conditions remain limited, particularly in the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world. abstract: Abstract Fecal-contaminated water causes diseases and even death. Current microbial water safety tests require pathogen incubation, taking 24–72 h and costing $20-$50 per test. This paper presents a solution (DeepScope) that classifies microscopic images of unincubated water samples by a composite water-safety determination, meeting UNICEF’s ideal Target Product Profile numerical performance thresholds for presence/absence testing, with an estimated per-test cost of $0.44. abstract: Working fluid selection is critical to the efficiency of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) systems, where the inherently small temperature difference between warm surface and cold deep seawater limits achievable efficiency. Solar-boosted OTEC (SOTEC) addresses this where solar thermal energy raises the warm seawater source temperature. abstract: Manual visual counting remains the standard procedure for estimating Kent mango ( Mangifera indica L.) yield in northern Peru, an inconsistent practice that compromises harvest planning, transport dimensioning and commercial negotiation. abstract: Centralized control that optimizes ship behavior is an effective approach for managing marine traffic in congested waters. This study proposed a decision-making framework that generates optimal control actions for all ships in a sea area using traffic data represented as a graph. In this framework, control actions that optimize overall marine traffic are learned through reinforcement learning (RL). abstract: Rapid urbanisation in North Africa frequently neglects the diverse needs of citizens, resulting in spatial injustice. This research investigates the disconnect between top-down planning and actual space utilisation in Constantine, Algeria, by testing an integrated framework that combines citizen-generated data with deep learning techniques. abstract: Soil thermal conductivity is a key parameter in geothermal design, buried infrastructure, frozen-ground engineering, agricultural heat-transfer assessment, and subsurface energy systems. abstract: In this work we examine pedagogical role and underlying mechanisms of generative AI in helping young children with imitative poetry composition because it is complex task that can be difficult for students in classroom. abstract: Ever more frequent and severe heat waves and resulting coral bleaching threaten to drive reef corals to extinction unless they can rapidly increase resilience against rising temperatures. abstract: Traffic-based air quality proxy models that perform well in compact urban settings have not been evaluated in megacity environments where complex topography, sea–land breeze circulation, and strong meteorological modulation are expected to dominate pollutant transport. abstract: Las organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro (OSAL) desempeñan un rol social fundamental donde las demandas comunitarias superan la capacidad estatal. abstract: El artículo aborda cómo en la era del aceleracionismo extremo, con la tecnología de la inteligencia artificial teniendo un rol protagónico debido a su carácter omniabarcador, la filosofía parece quedar obsoleta. abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. abstract: Pedology has seen a significant revolution due to the adoption of modern sensors that can provide fast, non-invasive and high resolution measurements of soils. abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can support differential diagnosis, but final-answer accuracy does not by itself establish diagnostic safety. abstract: It is complicated to comprehend the shear strength behavior of steel fiber-reinforced concrete (FRC) because of various parameters that are involved. abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. abstract: Abstract Extreme cold weather events can have devastating impacts on energy production, and human livelihood. abstract: Remote sensing is essential for mapping mangrove forest ecosystems, yet accuracy and spatial resolution remain limited, particularly in Africa, where mangroves are fragmented, reference data and cloud-free images are scarce. The state-of-the-art of mangrove forest mapping relies on native-resolution imagery using machine learning. abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is widely used for seawater desalination, water treatment, and product concentration, yet long-term performance degradation remains difficult to predict because fouling and membrane deterioration arise from coupled physical, chemical, and biological phenomena under variable industrial conditions. abstract: Abstract This study aims to evaluate an automated approach for mapping areas affected by land use and land cover change using Sentinel-1 SAR imagery time series and machine learning models trained through a novel pseudo-labeling framework. title: Why the midlatitude ocean is warming faster in summer than in winter
abstract: Abstract Observed sea surface temperature (SST) records and global climate model simulations nearly ubiquitously show that the mid-latitude oceans are warming 75% faster during late boreal summer than late boreal winter. In this study we show that the enhanced late-summer response is a fundamental property of the climate system by first documenting the mid-latitude response to a wide range of forcings, then explaining the seasonality using a seasonal oceanic mixed layer model (MLM). abstract: To proactively react to unknown uncertainties caused by a rapidly changing climate, we propose to adopt diverse, adaptive, and robust engineering (DARE): Earth’s ecosystems naturally thrive in spite of unknown uncertainties by incorporating diversity, adaptability, and robustness in their “designs”. abstract: Despite years of research, the processes controlling warm-rain formation remain uncertain. abstract: China’s decarbonization puzzle is stark: energy-related CO₂ emissions climbed to about 12.6 Gt in 2023—roughly one-third of the global total—even as industrial automation surged, with 276,288 robots installed that year, the most worldwide. abstract: Multiclass classification is essential in machine learning as it allows systems to differentiate between three or more categories using intricate, multidimensional data. abstract: The convergence of the climate and ocean agendas has become a defining feature of contemporary global governance. abstract: Large regions and coastal urban communities face significant climate-related risks, including coastal and river flooding, inundations, and sea-level rise. title: Self-Hostable YOLO11 Service for Marine Fish Data Curation
abstract: Marine fisheries sustainability requires accurate, real-time data on fish populations. This need is currently unmet due to the high costs of manual surveys and the slow, third-party monitoring solutions. This paper introduces a novel self-hostable web service designed for efficient aquatic monitoring and curation of YOLO format datasets. Utilizing FastAPI for asynchronous processing and a YOLO11n architecture, this service enables rapid and high-accuracy fish detection, streamlining the creation of new training data. title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
abstract: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP).

title: Push and pull factors of relocation in the coastal zone: what matters most?
abstract: Abstract Permanent relocation is increasingly proposed as an effective long-term strategy for coastal areas affected by recurrent flooding. While the literature on coastal relocation has been steadily growing—particularly on policy processes, financial mechanisms, and lived experiences—less attention has been given to understanding the reasoning behind relocation decisions. This study provides empirical evidence on the factors that drive willingness to relocate from a telephone survey administered in high-risk coastal settings on the Delmarva Peninsula in Maryland and Hampton Roads, Virginia.

abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. abstract: Nearshore hardbottom (NSHB) habitats occur in shallow coastal waters throughout the Florida Keys and support sessile benthic invertebrate communities dominated by sponges and octocorals. abstract: Background Sea turtle rehabilitation is widely practiced worldwide, yet standardized benchmark indicators for objectively evaluating rehabilitation quality are currently lacking. abstract: Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency. abstract: Subfossil trees preserved in lakes, peatlands, and submerged coastal environments represent one of the most valuable high-resolution archives for reconstructing Holocene climate and environmental variability. Sweden hosts an exceptional diversity of such archives, spanning from subalpine lake systems in northern Lapland to raised bogs and submerged Baltic landscapes in the south, yet no comprehensive synthesis of Swedish subfossil dendrochronological research has previously been undertaken. abstract: Sea export operations depend heavily on human resources because freight forwarding personnel coordinate documentation, customs procedures, container handling, shipping schedules, and communication among stakeholders. Human-related failures may result in documentation errors, shipment delays, additional costs, regulatory penalties, and service disruptions. title: Digital technology, agricultural resilience, and food security: a mini review
abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly deployed to strengthen food security under climate stress, resource constraints, and geopolitical disruption. This review synthesizes two largely separate bodies of scholarship: an international literature on digital agriculture and the four classical dimensions of food security, and a rapidly expanding Chinese literature on the digital economy and agricultural economic resilience. abstract: This research examines how city images of Istanbul’s Historic Peninsula are evolving with artificial intelligence and expanding user-generated content. abstract: Continental crustal growth mechanisms remain a pivotal frontier in geoscience. abstract: Lichens are widely recognized as biological indicators of environmental quality because their physiological condition reflects long-term atmospheric and ecological changes. However, conventional lichen assessment relies primarily on manual visual inspection by trained specialists, limiting the scalability of environmental monitoring. title: How volant seabirds benefit from sub-surface predators during multi-predator feeding aggregations
abstract: Multi-predator feeding aggregations are common in marine ecosystems and frequently involve seabirds. Often labelled opportunistic 'scroungers', volant seabirds derive diverse benefits from the association with sub-surface predators (such as cetaceans, pinnipeds, Teleosts) which can significantly enhance their hunting performance. In this opinion piece, we outline the major mechanisms through which sub-surface predators benefit volant seabirds, based on recent quantitative evidence and hypotheses that warrant further research. title: Lidocaine inhibits macrophage M2 polarization and breast cancer progression in association with SCN4A/SLC7A5-related glutamine metabolic reprogramming
abstract: To predict the potential targets and mechanisms of lidocaine in breast cancer using network pharmacology and bioinformatics, and to experimentally validate its modulation of SCN4A/SLC7A5-related metabolic and immune pathways. Lidocaine targets were obtained from PubChem, SwissTargetPrediction, CTD, SEA and BATMAN-TCM. Breast cancer targets were retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM and TTD. Differentially expressed genes and WGCNA module genes were analyzed from GSE22820. Core genes were identified by Lasso regression, SVM-RFE and random forest. title: Inteligencia artificial autónoma y derecho tributario en Ecuador: diseño de un modelo de gobernanza algorítmica para la determinación fiscal, explicabilidad y protección de los derechos del contribuyente
abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) with increasing degrees of autonomy changes how tax administrations detect risk, cross-check information and prepare decisions with individual legal effects. This study designs an algorithmic governance model for tax assessment in Ecuador that combines technological efficiency, explainability and protection of taxpayers’ rights. title: El árbitro aumentado en el Arbitraje Comercial Internacional 5.0: ¿De la lex mercatoria a la lex algorítmica en la transformación del soft law arbitral?
abstract: This paper examines the evolution of arbitration within the context of the technological transformation driven by artificial intelligence (AI), advancing the concept of International Commercial Arbitration 5.0 as a new developmental stage of the arbitral system. title: Systematic Design of Intelligent Base Station for Fishery Aquaculture
abstract: In an era characterized by accelerating environmental changes and technological advancements, this research project focuses on developing a photovoltaically powered, intelligent aquaculture base station system to promote efficient automated fisheries development. title: Future Machines on the Moon: Robotic Autonomy, Human Supervision and the Emerging Security Dimension of Lunar Operations
abstract: Lunar exploration has shifted from single flights to a planned buildup of permanent infrastructure. NASA flew four astronauts around the Moon on Artemis II in April 2026, and within eight weeks announced the first three robotic Moon Base missions along with close to a billion dollars in contracts for surface rovers, cargo landers and hopping drones. A parallel programme led by China and Russia, the International Lunar Research Station, is working towards a basic configuration by 2035 with a nuclear power unit delivered between 2033 and 2035. title: Alfabetización mediática e informacional en la Universidad de Valladolid
abstract: This study assesses the level of Media and Information Literacy (MIL) across the main groups within the university community —students, Teaching and Research Staff (TRS), and Technical, Management, and Administrative Staff (TMAS)—and identifies patterns and strategic areas for improvement in the context of contemporary informational challenges. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was adopted, based on the administration of three structured questionnaires tailored to each group and aligned with the UNESCO conceptual framework for Media and Information Literacy. title: An improved CNN-BiLSTM video-based rainfall intensity estimation method based on attention mechanisms and residual connection variants
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate monitoring of rainfall intensity is essential for forecasting and managing floods. The surveillance video-based rainfall measurement method has potential for high spatial and temporal resolution rainfall monitoring. Existing video-based rainfall estimation models have incorporated temporal information; however, challenges remain in improving accuracy and robustness under different environmental conditions. title: Antimicrobial and Anti-inflammatory Activities of Bacteriocin-like Inhibitory Substance-producing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum against Vaginitis-associated Pathogens
abstract: Vaginal dysbiosis is characterized by disruption of the vaginal microbial community, pathogen overgrowth, and mucosal inflammation. Here, we integrated in vitro screening, whole-genome sequencing, LC-MS/MS profiling, machine learning, and a murine bacterial vaginosis (BV) model to characterize potentially beneficial Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strains. title: AI-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED GENERATIVE DESIGN: A TEACHING FRAMEWORK FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTONICS INTEGRATING RESEARCH FINDINGS, DESIGN PRECEDENTS, AND INTELLIGENT RECOGNITION AND JUDGMENT
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered design courses, but its use often stops at tool operation. Taking Landscape Architectonics, an undergraduate course in landscape architecture programs, as the vehicle, this paper builds a teaching framework for generative design that integrates four elements: research findings, design precedents, AI-based recognition and judgment, and AI generation. The core claim is simple. title: A Nonlinear Extension of Parametric Model Embedding for Dimensionality Reduction in Parametric Shape Design
abstract: ABSTRACT Dimensionality reduction is essential in simulation‐based shape design, where high‐dimensional parameterizations hinder optimization, surrogate modeling, and systematic design‐space exploration. Parametric Model Embedding (PME) addresses this issue by constructing reduced variables from geometric information while preserving an explicit backmapping to the original design parameters. However, PME is intrinsically linear and may become inefficient when the sampled design space is governed by nonlinear geometric variability. journal: International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering

title: Reproductive Biology of Pomadasys commersonnii (Lacepède, 1801) (Family: Haemulidae) collected from Karachi Coast: Reproductive biology of P. commersonnii
abstract: Pomadasys commersonnii (Lacepède, 1801) is a commercially important fish species distributed along the Arabian Sea coast, yet information on its reproductive biology from Pakistan remains limited. A total of 105 specimens were collected monthly from commercial landings at Karachi Fish Harbour from January to December 2022. The specimens ranged in total length from 31.08 to 53.68 cm, with an overall mean of 47.15 ± 9.15 cm, while mean body weight was 1875.11 ± 501.05 g. title: Multispectral representation of Distributed Acoustic Sensing data: A framework for physically interpretable feature extraction and visualisation
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables continuous monitoring of dynamic strain along tens of kilometres of optical fibre, generating massive datasets whose interpretation and automated analysis remain challenging. DAS data can be understood as a time-distance image array. However, the absence of standardised representation methods limits both the physical interpretability and the development of automated image-based analysis pipelines. title: Cross-feeding interactions and nutrient provision revealed by metabolic modelling of a sponge microbiome
abstract: Abstract Marine sponges harbor diverse communities of microorganisms that are essential for the host survival and function. Omics analyses have in recent years described the functional diversity and potential of sponge symbionts, however it is unclear if and how they interacted with each other and the host to provide essential metabolites for growth. To address this knowledge gap, we generated and curated genome-scale metabolic model (GSMM) for 19 bacterial symbionts that account for 95 % of the community abundance in the sponge Phyllospongia foliascens. title: ZanIA: aplicación multiplataforma basada en inteligencia artificial para el análisis nutricional de alimentos por imagen conforme a la NOM-043-SSA2-2012
abstract: Overweight and obesity represent a major public health problem in Mexico: according to the 2023 ENSANUT Continua survey, 37.3% of adults are overweight and 38.9% are obese, while combined prevalence among adolescents reaches 40.4%. Given the lack of accessible tools that translate official nutritional regulations into practical guidance, ZanIA was developed—a multiplatform application that uses artificial intelligence (Gemini model) to analyze photographs of meals and generate nutritional information (calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrates) aligned with the NOM-043-SSA2-2012 standard. title: Engineering adaptive polysaccharide biomaterials: integrated biotechnology framework for regenerative medicine
abstract: Natural polysaccharides are versatile building blocks for regenerative biomaterials because of their structural diversity, generally favorable biocompatibility and biodegradability, chemical tunability, and capacity for biologically relevant interactions. Advances in biotechnology and materials engineering have expanded their role from primarily structural matrices to multifunctional platforms that can influence cellular, immune, and biochemical processes during tissue repair. title: GWDRO-Lung: Gromov–Wasserstein distributionally robust learning for calibrated pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction across imaging cohorts
abstract: Low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) screening detects pulmonary nodules whose malignancy risk must be triaged, yet deep-learning risk models often lose both accuracy and calibration when transferred to a different scanner, protocol, or population. We developed GWDRO-Lung, a chest CT framework that treats cross-cohort transfer as a coupled problem of structural mismatch, distributional instability, and calibration. title: A wavelet kernel design for the detection of sperm whale echolocation clicks
abstract: Sperm whales ( Physeter macrocephalus ) produce powerful, broadband echolocation clicks that are used to detect and identify prey in deep ocean environments. Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) systems provide a non-invasive method to study the abundance of these animals, but face the challenge of false detections due to transient noise sources. In this paper, we propose a wavelet-based method to identify regions of interest (ROIs) containing sperm whale (SW) clicks by exploiting the impulsive characteristics of the clicks. title: La Inteligencia Artificial como mediación pedagógica: una mirada crítica al fortalecimiento de la competencia argumentativa en la educación básica secundaria.
abstract: The rapid incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into education calls for reflection on its pedagogical meaning, particularly regarding the development of higher-order thinking skills such as argumentation. This article aims to analyze, from a theoretical and critical perspective, the conditions under which AI can become a pedagogical mediation rather than merely a tool for strengthening argumentative competence among secondary school students. The work is developed through a review and discussion of recent research on generative AI, writing, critical thinking, and technological mediati

title: Exploring Pyridazine Pharmacophores for the Development of Novel Therapeutics Against Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive and diverse form of breast cancer characterized by the absence of progesterone and Estrogen receptors and HER2 expression, which limits conventional therapeutic options and contributes to poor prognosis. Chemotherapy remains the standard of care, but multidrug resistance, tumor heterogeneity, and systemic toxicities restrict long-term efficacy. title: Liderazgo adaptativo e innovador: articulación entre innovación pedagógica y gestión estratégica en la educación superior
abstract: The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. In this context, academics who assume academic program leadership responsibilities occupy an intermediate position between teaching practice and strategic management, although the literature frequently addresses these dimensions separately. title: AI Tools and EFL Identity: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Gender and Cultural Representation in AI-Generated Reading Materials for Gulf University Students
abstract: The incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classroom has revolutionized the production of teaching content. However, the ideological implications of AI-generated content have been markedly under-researched in non-Western contexts. This study employs Fairclough’s three-dimensional framework of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) on a corpus of 45 AI-generated EFL reading texts produced by the ChatGPT-4o, Google Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Microsoft Copilot in response to five standardized instructional prompts. title: Global advances in Generative AI for renewable energy and implications for sustainable energy transitions in Africa
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. It aims to: (i) map GenAI applications in renewable-energy systems; (ii) distinguish demonstrated results from proposed African opportunities; (iii) evaluate evidence quality, transferability, and deployment feasibility; and (iv) identify context-specific research and policy
institutions: National Advanced School of Public Works

title: Encountering antibiotic resistance: Current challenges and emerging solutions in the post-antibiotic era
abstract: Antibiotic resistance has become one of the greatest threats to global health in this century, causing many health problems in many countries. In contrast, the multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial strains developed mechanisms to encounter surrounding toxic compounds in their environments, making their treatment more difficult. Moreover, these pathogens possess different resistance, which allows them to survive and proliferate in hostile environments. title: Tropicalisation of rocky shore gastropod communities along the Baja California Peninsula
abstract: Abstract Tropicalisation is restructuring marine communities globally. Despite extensive research in subtidal habitats, the extent of tropicalisation and its impact on rocky intertidal communities remains poorly understood. Here we integrated contemporary field surveys with genetic barcoding, historic surveys, museum collections, and fossil records to document changes in the rocky shore gastropod communities along approximately 3,120 km of the Baja California Peninsula coastline. title: Del eco algorítmico a la voz original: educación sensible y desfondamiento
abstract: The massive irruption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) constitutes an ontological event that challenges contemporary education beyond mere technical efficiency or academic integrity. This study justifies the critical urgency of addressing the structural "groundlessness" of the human person in the face of current algorithmic saturation and technological idolatry. title: A disentangled CNN–transformer framework for big data-driven intelligent brand visual generation
abstract: Big data has driven the rapid growth of brand visual design demand, yet existing intelligent generation methods suffer from detail distortion and poor cross-cultural adaptability. This study proposes a style-disentangled Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer framework for intelligent brand visual generation. A dual-branch architecture extracts local details via CNN and global style via Transformer, with an embedding mixer enabling balanced feature fusion. title: Explicit Spin Regulation as an Emerging Design Paradigm in Heterogeneous Catalysis
abstract: Conspectus Catalytic activity, selectivity, and durability arise from coupled electronic, structural, interfacial, transport, and spin-related processes. Conventional catalyst design has relied largely on electronic effects, strain or stress engineering, active-site construction, and local reaction environment control. Although these strategies have enabled major advances, they do not fully capture the spin degrees of freedom associated with open-shell transition-metal centers and magnetically responsive catalysts. title: Contrasting Chinese-English translation strategies by ChatGPT and DeepSeek in subtitling magic culture-specific items: a case study of Nezha 1 and Nezha 2
abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in audiovisual translation, yet limited research has examined how large language models translate culture-specific items (CSIs) in fantasy films. This study investigates the Chinese-English translation strategies employed by ChatGPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3.1 for magic CSIs and the influence of prompt design on strategy selection. Drawing on Franco Aixelá’s taxonomy, a mixed-methods analysis was conducted on 90 magic CSIs from Nezha 1 and Nezha 2. title: When to refuse cosmetic treatment – AI‐decision support for differentiating melanocytic and non‐melanocytic facial lesions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Flat pigmented skin lesions in chronically sun-exposed face and scalp areas present diagnostic challenges. Particularly, solar lentigo, pigmented actinic keratosis and lentigo maligna show overlapping features. Erroneous laser treatment of lentigo maligna for cosmetic reasons will inevitably delay diagnosis and compromise patient safety. This study assessed the performance of a market-approved convolutional neural network (CNN) versus dermatologists in differentiating melanocytic from non-melanocytic face and scalp lesions (FSL). title: INLA-RF: A hybrid modeling strategy for spatio-temporal environmental data
abstract: Environmental processes often exhibit complex, non-linear patterns and discontinuities across space and time, posing significant challenges for traditional geostatistical modeling approaches. To overcome this weakness a hybrid modeling strategy can be proposed. This hybrid strategy combines the interpretability and principled uncertainty quantification of statistical models with the predictive flexibility of machine learning methods. title: Halite crystallization at Sfax solar salterns, Tunisia, driven by brine geochemistry and biogeochemical interactions
abstract: Solar salterns are hypersaline systems characterized by evaporation-driven salinity gradients that promote the precipitation of evaporite minerals. Here, we investigate the influence of halophilic microbial communities on halite crystallization along the salinity gradient of the Sfax solar saltern (Tunisia). Geochemical analyses of 26 brine samples (mean salinity range ~28–570 g L −1 ) demonstrated marine-fed evaporative sequences, allowing the selection of three representative basins along a gradient of 150 g/L to 280 g/L (M22, B22, and TS5 sites). title: Executive Sensemaking of Generative AI Adoption at Enterprise Scale: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Cross-Industry Executive Perspectives
abstract: This qualitative study examines how senior executives from technology, financial services, and consumer goods publicly make sense of enterprise-scale generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) adoption. Using a purposively selected, bounded single-case design, it applies reflexive thematic analysis to the complete transcript of one moderated industry panel. title: Digital Disruption in Insurance and Skills Development: Advancing the INSETA Mandate: A Conceptual Review of Technology-Driven Workforce Transformation in the Global and African Insurance Sector
abstract: Purpose: This conceptual review examines the forces driving digital disruption in the global and African insurance sectors and evaluates their implications for employment, professional competencies, and talent management, with particular attention to the role of skills-development institutions such as South Africa’s Insurance Sector Education and Training Authority (INSETA). Methodology: Drawing on Human Capital Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study synthesizes peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, and institutional publications published predominantly between 2024 and 2026.

title: Erosión cognitiva en la industria 5.0:
abstract: Technical, social, avant-garde, global, and cognitive pressures are driving the adoption of new technologies characterized by constant updates and automation most notably generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and autonomous agents. While the stated intention is to augment and enhance human capabilities regarding complex challenges, skills, and critical thinking rather than replacing them recent empirical evidence suggests the actual trend is moving in the opposite direction, to the detriment of consumers. title: Dimensionality reduction of atmospheric concentration fields using a 3D convolutional autoencoder with spatial attention mechanism
abstract: Abstract High-dimensional atmospheric chemistry simulations produce volumetric concentration fields that are costly to store and repeatedly process in inverse-modelling and data-assimilation workflows. This study evaluates reduced representations for CO concentration fields from WRF-Chem over Novosibirsk and CAMS over Europe. We propose a three-dimensional convolutional autoencoder with a lightweight spatial attention module (SAM3D) and compare it with linear, spectral, tensor-based, interpolation, manifold-learning, and neural-network baselines. title: Developing scenario-based, near-term iterative forecasts to inform water management
abstract: Near-term, iterative ecosystem forecasts with scenarios representing alternate management decisions have high potential for providing valuable insights on how decisions may impact future ecological conditions. Scenario-based forecasts may be particularly useful for informing the decision-making around freshwater ecosystems managed for multiple objectives. We applied a near-term, iterative forecasting system at Lake Alexandrina, Australia, which is located at the nexus of one of the world’s largest catchments and a protected coastal wetland. title: An ensemble JCHAIDStar framework for improved landslide susceptibility prediction using Bagging and Random Subspace techniques
abstract: This study developed a landslide susceptibility map for the mountainous area of northern Vietnam, located within the administrative boundary of the former Ha Giang Province and now under Tuyen Quang Province, to support the identification of landslide-prone areas and disaster risk reduction. The input data included a landslide inventory of 963 locations and 13 conditioning factors representing topographic, hydrological, geological, climatic, and human-related conditions. title: Evaluation and bias correction of reanalysis wind data for resource assessment and long-term power prediction
abstract: Reliable long-term wind-power prediction requires linking short-term mast measurements with long-term reanalysis data. This study developed integrated methodology using measurements from five coastal and near-coastal sites, four reanalysis datasets, seven Power Law exponent methods, and seven bias-correction techniques. The proposed Day–Hour Lookup-Table Power Law produced lowest average mean absolute error, root mean square error (RMSE) and standard deviation of error of 0.23, 0.35 and 0.33 m/s, respectively, and maintained relative RMSE of 4.31–6.30% during chronological hold-out validation.

title: An interpretable DM-PINN for retrieving mangrove canopy carbon, nitrogen, and potassium contents using Sentinel-2 and SDGSAT-1 observations along China's southeastern coast
abstract: Mangroves are among the most important blue carbon ecosystems, contributing substantially to global carbon sequestration and biodiversity conservation. Canopy carbon (CCC), nitrogen (CNC), and potassium (CKC) contents provide critical indicators of nutrient cycling, ecosystem functioning, and ecological health. However, the structural complexity and strong spatial heterogeneity of mangroves present major obstacles to understanding the spectral response mechanisms and achieving reliable large-scale retrieval of these biochemical parameters. title: IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF PSCRB TRAINING TO ENHANCE SEAFARERS’ SAFETY KNOWLEDGE AND EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
abstract: This community-service study evaluated the implementation of Proficiency in Survival Craft and Rescue Boats (PSCRB) training to examine changes in participants’ safety knowledge and emergency preparedness within the STCW framework. The evaluation focused on knowledge of safety procedures, emergency readiness, and survival capability at sea. A mixed-methods descriptive evaluation was complemented by pre- and post-training assessment of 25 participants. title: Past trends and future projections: a spatio-temporal analysis of land cover change in the uMngeni catchment using remote sensing and CMIP6 scenarios
abstract: Understanding long-term land-cover dynamics in the uMngeni catchment is critical for safeguarding ecosystem integrity and sustaining biodiversity under increasing anthropogenic and climatic pressures. However, spatially explicit assessments of these transformations remain limited, particularly under future climate change. This study analysed land-cover changes from 1991 to 2021 using Landsat (5, 7, and 8) imagery and random forest classification. title: Digital Transformation Policies for Sustainable Tourism: A Comparative Policy Analysis of the European Union and Albania
abstract: This study analyzes how digital transformation and environmental sustainability are articulated as a common policy agenda known as the “twin transition” in the tourism sector, comparing the European Union (EU) as a mature regulatory and financing framework with Albania as an EU candidate country undergoing rapid but uneven digitalization. journal: International Journal of Law and Societal Studies

title: Aerobic anoxygenic phototrophs are widespread and active members of Greenland Ice Sheet microbiomes
abstract: The Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) hosts diverse microbial communities where glacier ice algae, snow algae, and cyanobacteria act as key primary producers across bare ice, snow, and cryoconite habitats, yet the ecological roles of associated heterotrophic prokaryotes remain poorly understood. Aerobic anoxygenic phototrophs (AAPs), known to couple light harvesting to heterotrophy and enter trophic relationships with algae in marine systems, suggesting they may represent an important but underexplored functional group in supraglacial ecosystems. title: A perspective and roadmap for emerging toxic flood hazards affecting ecosystems and society
abstract: Abstract Floods increasingly interact with anthropogenic pollution sources, remobilize legacy pollution, release emerging pollutants and harm critical infrastructure, transforming hydrologic extremes into compounding pollution disasters. Here we introduce the term ‘toxic floods’ to provide a perspective on emerging floods which mobilize, transport, and deposit hazardous contaminants, creating exposure pathways for ecosystems and humans. title: GEODESC web applications for collaborative description of geological materials – a legacy of the JOIDES Resolution era
abstract: Expedition scientists on the JOIDES Resolution ( JR ) during the Ocean Drilling Program (ODP), Integrated Ocean Drilling Program, and International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) carried out visual descriptions of hundreds of kilometers of cores to characterize the sequences drilled for subsequent subsampling and analysis. title: Research Priorities for a Circular Economy for Plastic Sustainability in the Caribbean
abstract: Abstract Caribbean countries bear a disproportionate burden of marine plastic pollution because of their small landmass, high population density, and insufficient waste management infrastructure. Many Caribbean nations depend on informal, unmanaged landfills, underscoring an urgent need for more resilient, sustainable systems. This perspective synthesizes existing data to map the region’s plastic waste landscape and leverages regional expertise to identify key research priorities. title: Optimización de la predicción de retención estudiantil en la educación superior: un análisis comparativo de modelos de aprendizaje automático supervisados y no supervisado
abstract: This research addresses the problem of student dropout in higher education in El Salvador, using machine learning models. To do so, a historical dataset from a private university was used, which includes more than 83,000 student records between the years 2019 and 2024. In the exploratory analysis phase, unsupervised techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means, and hierarchical clustering were applied to segment students and identify profiles with similar demographic, academic, and economic characteristics. journal: Revista Ciencia Tecnología e Innovación en Ingeniería y Arquitectura (CTI-FIA)

title: Application of radar remote sensing for cyclone damage mapping in Bangladesh: a coherence-based approach
abstract: Abstract. Rapid and reliable assessment of cyclone-induced damage remains a major challenge in coastal regions where cloud cover and accessibility limit conventional approaches. This study presents a coherence-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for identifying as well as quantifying cyclone-induced surface changes in coastal districts in Bangladesh. Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 data were analyzed using interferometric coherence to capture spatial and temporal variations associated with five major cyclones: Amphan (2020), Sitrang (2022), Mocha (2023), Hamoon (2023), and Remal (2024). title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. title: Microplastics and bisphenol A in the edible mussel Perna perna from southeastern Brazil: occurrence and dietary exposure assessment
abstract: Abstract Edible bivalves are an important route of human exposure to environmental contaminants because they are consumed whole and accumulate particulate and chemical hazards from coastal waters. This study assessed microplastics (MPs) and bisphenol A (BPA) in the brown mussel Perna perna from Espírito Santo Bay, southeastern Brazil, and estimated dietary exposure under average- and high-consumption scenarios. Sixty mussels were analyzed: 30 for MPs and 30 for BPA, of which 18 yielded valid quantitative BPA results. MPs were detected in all analyzed mussels, with a mean abundance of 1.44 ± 1.

title: Predefined‐Time Scaled Containment Control for Nonlinear Multi‐Agent Systems With Prescribed Performance Guarantees
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the practical predefined‐time (PT) scaled containment control (SCC) problem for multi‐agent systems (MASs) subject to unknown nonlinear dynamics and external disturbances. The theoretical framework begins with the presentation of a practical PT stability criterion and the formal definition of SCC. abstract: Large river deltas are important coastal carbon sinks, yet how changes in sediment supply are associated with subsurface microbial communities and biogeochemical processes remains poorly understood. abstract: PM 2.5 concentration time series are characterized by obvious chaotic behavior, mutually superimposed multi-period components and notable temporal fluctuations, which pose considerable difficulties to the high-precision prediction of PM 2.5 concentration. abstract: ABSTRACT The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. abstract: The growing incorporation of variable solar and wind power in electrical grids leads to serious issues concerning reliability due to the complexity of spatial and temporal behavior caused by factors like variations in environmental conditions, degradation of equipment, failures of sensors, and exceptional operating conditions. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been widely utilized to estimate the compressive strength ( f c ) of fly ash (FA) concrete due to its high efficiency and accuracy. abstract: Animal-borne tri-axial accelerometers are increasingly used to investigate animal behaviour and energetics. abstract: Introduction Non-toxigenic non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae (NOVC) are opportunistic aquatic pathogens that cause extraintestinal infections including bacteremia, particularly in patients with underlying comorbidities. abstract: The paper presents the results of a comprehensive regional analysis of the Anabar Shield’s fault tectonics, conducted via modern Earth remote sensing and tectonophysical simulation techniques. abstract: Catalytic infrared (CIR) radiation curing has shown excellent performance in curing thermosetting powder coatings. abstract: Accurate Land Use/Land Cover Change (LULCC) modelling and forecasting are crucial for understanding environmental dynamics and guiding sustainable land management in rapidly urbanising regions. This study compares the predictive accuracy and reliability of two hybrid models, Cellular Automata–Markov (CA–Markov) and Cellular Automata–Artificial Neural Network (CA–ANN) for Southwestern Nigeria. abstract: Deep learning has transformed vegetation mapping from UAV imagery, yet state-of-the-art segmentation models require hundreds to thousands of expertly annotated images, creating prohibitive labor costs for conservation applications targeting endangered flora. abstract: Floating Car Data (FCD) have been increasingly adopted by cities and transportation agencies to monitor traffic conditions. Despite the advantages of broad spatial coverage and high temporal resolution, such data provide only a partial representation of urban traffic, with systematic biases across corridors and time periods. abstract: Biomimetic aerodynamic design draws inspiration from biological structures and flow-control mechanisms to improve the aerodynamic performance of aircraft and automobiles. This paper reviews representative biomimetic concepts, including humpback-whale leading-edge tubercles, shark-skin riblets, boxfish-inspired body shapes, dragonfly-wing corrugations, and bird-inspired wingtip structures. abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems, between the terrestrial and marine domain, harbor a diverse and specialized microbial community, including Actinomycetia members, which produce a variety of functionally distinct bioactive metabolites. abstract: Hospital-trained deep learning models for echocardiographic wall motion abnormality detection achieve strong performance under standard clinical acquisition conditions but often degrade substantially when deployed on autonomous robotic acquisition systems. abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. abstract: Communities, governments, and agriculture worldwide are increasingly turning to managed aquifer recharge (MAR) as an important element of their water resources planning.A wide range of MAR approaches capture available water during wet periods, times of low demand, or water that would otherwise be lost, and move this water underground for later recovery or other benefits.MAR can address a diversity of issues, including water shortages, emergency supply, groundwater depletion, land subsidence, seawater intrusion, water-quality degradation, streamflow depletion, and endangered groundwater-depende

abstract: Cianjur Regency was often hit by landslides. In 2022, this regency was affected by landslide, leading to several civilian deaths, injuries, along with damaged houses and infrastructure. To minimize the impact, determining landslide susceptibility level was proven to be an essential step in maximally plan- ning disaster management. Therefore, this study aimed to develop landslide susceptibility model in Cianjur Regency using the Geographic Information System (GIS). title: Development of an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book using tourism posters for junior high school students
abstract: Background- Poetry writing is an important productive literacy skill in the Merdeka Curriculum, yet instruction remains predominantly theoretical. Students may experience difficulties in idea generation, diction, and imagination due to limited contextual and visual support. Objectives- This study aimed to (1) identify instructional needs; (2) develop an AI-assisted maritime poetry writing book integrating illustrated data cards and marine tourism posters; and (3) evaluate its effectiveness. abstract: Traffic-related air pollution constitutes one of the primary threats to public health and environmental sustainability in urban centers worldwide.Historic centers face particular challenges because their narrow streets, irregular urban configuration, and high vehicle concentration during peak hours hinder the implementation of conventional environmental monitoring systems.This research assessed the pollutant emissions generated by vehicular traffic in the historic center of Ayacucho, Peru, an Andean city located at 2,761 meters above sea level with approximately 29,476 inhabitants in the study

abstract: The widespread use of the water‐soluble paraquat (PQ) herbicide has found to be linked with numerous toxic outcomes to humans as well as aquatic animals, while the on‐site and rapid measurement is still challenging due to unsuitability and lack of selectivity of the existing techniques. This study presents a selective, sensitive, and low‐cost electrochemical sensor for detecting residual PQ in water by combining a core–shell molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)@SiO 2 @Fe 3 O 4 material with a portable screen‐printed carbon electrode (SPCE). title: A LiDAR-driven urban energy benchmarking framework for mapping building energy intensity and carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities
abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization and intensifying heat extremes are accelerating building energy demand and associated carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities. However, quantifying building-level energy performance at high spatial resolution remains challenging because building morphology, floor area, and energy-consumption data are rarely integrated within a comprehensive framework. title: Assessment of methane emissions from European countries using satellite and surface observations
abstract: Abstract. Europe is a global leader in mitigating methane emissions through comprehensive policies, including the EU Methane Strategy and commitments under the Global Methane Pledge. National bottom-up inventories are widely regarded as high quality; however, atmospheric observations remain essential for independent verification and tracking emission reductions. Here, we present a multi-year (2019–2023) top-down assessment of European methane emissions using a Bayesian inversion of satellite observations from TROPOMI and surface measurements from ICOS. title: Layered interventions for climate resilience: an analysis of household recovery and food security outcomes in Southern Malawi
abstract: Abstract This study assesses the implications of layered resilience-building interventions in climate-vulnerable regions of Malawi, with a focus on household recovery capacity and food security outcomes during the 2024 El Niño–induced drought in Malawi. Household resilience is proxied by self-reported recovery duration following climatic shocks, while food security is measured using Food Consumption Scores (FCS). institutions: Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources

title: Frequentist Versus Bayesian Hedonic Regression for Miami House Prices: Prediction Intervals, Coverage Calibration, and Prior Sensitivity
abstract: Housing price prediction requires both accurate point estimates and a useful description of prediction uncertainty. This study compares frequentist, regularized, Bayesian, and machine-learning approaches using the Miami Housing 2016 dataset. After removing duplicate properties, 13,776 observations were analyzed, with log sale price used as the response variable. Six models were compared: ordinary least squares (OLS), Ridge, Lasso, Bayesian Ridge, Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD), and Random Forest. Random Forest achieved the strongest point-prediction performance, with a test R 2 of 0.9

title: Mamba-enhanced RT-DETR for ship detection in optical remote sensing images
abstract: Ship detection from optical remote sensing images remains challenging due to cluttered sea–land backgrounds, large scale variations, low-contrast small targets, and dense ship occlusion. Existing detectors struggle to balance global modeling capability, detection precision, and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a Mamba-enhanced Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) framework for high-precision ship detection and identification. title: First record of the non-native leafhopper Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 (Hemiptera, Cicadellidae, Deltocephalinae, Opsiini) in Bulgaria
abstract: We report Hishimonus hamatus Kuoh, 1976 from Bulgaria for the first time. We collected 36 specimens, including a nymph, at eight localities in six widely separated cities. All records originated from urban parks and gardens. Identification was based on external morphology and the male genitalia. The broad geographic spread of the records, from the Black Sea coast and southern Bulgaria to the Danube region in the north-west, suggests that this adventive East Asian leafhopper is already more widely distributed in Bulgarian urban areas than currently documented.

title: Projected Global Mortality and Economic Burden from Wildfire Smoke under Climate Change
abstract: Abstract Climate change is intensifying the frequency and severity of wildfires, amplifying landscape fire-sourced smoke (LFS), and its global health effects. However, future global LFS-attributable deaths and their associated attributable death costs remain poorly quantified. We projected global LFS-derived air pollution and the associated mortality and mortality-related economic burden from 2020 to 2100 under alternative climate and socioeconomic scenarios. title: Flowering phenology of herbarium specimens reveals century‐scale shifts in allergenic pollen seasonality
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Pollen allergies are a primary cause of seasonal allergic rhinitis, which affects over 500 million people globally, damaging quality of life and incurring significant costs in medical treatment and reduced work productivity. Many countries monitor pollen to inform allergy sufferers about seasonal pollen levels. In Norway, airborne pollen has been monitored for 45 years. title: Industrial Paradigm of Multidimensional Poverty in Karawang Regency (Determinant Analysis and Policy Implementation)
abstract: Karawang Regency is known as one of the largest processing industry centers in West Java, with the sector's contribution of around 71 percent to GDP on a Constant Price Basis in 2024. However, the dominance of the industrial economy has not been followed by an inclusive poverty reduction: the number of absolute poor people will increase by March 2024, the open unemployment rate remains above the West Java average, and the inequality of expenditure between the poor is widening. title: Influencing factors and genetic model of low-resistivity shales: a case study of the Longmaxi Formation, Southern Sichuan Basin, China
abstract: Low-resistivity anomalies are widely developed in the Wufeng–Longmaxi Formation marine shales of the Sichuan Basin, but their complex conductive mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering accurate reservoir evaluation. This study investigates the characteristics and formation mechanisms of low-resistivity shales in southern Sichuan Basin by integrating well logging resistivity, geochemical analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), carbon dioxide and nitrogen adsorption (CO 2 /N 2 ad

title: An adaptive behavioural zero-trust security framework with proactive cryptographic caching for continuous authentication in 5G non-terrestrial networks
abstract: Abstract 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are key to future global broadband and military communications, but their high latency and dynamic topologies require security approaches beyond perimeter defences and static authentication. To overcome these vulnerabilities, we propose an adaptive behavioural zero trust security framework (BZTSF) for continuous 5G NTN authentication. Our method continuously evaluates node trustworthiness using network signal information processed by an isolation forest machine learning algorithm. abstract: In the present work, alkaline Suaeda monoica biochar (BTBC) and its CoFe₂O₄-modified composite (FCB) were synthesized and comparatively evaluated for Congo red (CR) adsorption from aqueous solutions. The incorporation of CoFe₂O₄ significantly enhanced the adsorption performance of biochar, with FCB exhibiting substantially higher adsorption capacity and faster kinetics than BTBC under varying conditions of contact time, adsorbent dosage, initial dye concentration, temperature, and pH. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 infection in stranded porpoises and dolphins in Chile
abstract: Between 2022 and 2023, a significant increase in mortality among marine birds and pinnipeds along the Pacific coasts of Peru and Chile was linked to the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV H5N1). In response, the Chilean Fisheries and Aquaculture Service (SERNAPESCA) initiated a survey to document cetacean strandings and assess the presence of HPAIV H5N1 via molecular analysis of swab samples. abstract: Accurate and spatially explicit mapping of forest fuel types is essential for developing integrated wildfire risk management strategies, estimating fire danger, and modeling fire propagation in fire-prone Mediterranean ecosystems. While time series of Copernicus Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery at 10 m spatial resolution have proven effective for regional fuel mapping, severe spectral and spatial ambiguities persist in distinguishing complex canopy structures, heterogeneous shrublands, and pastures. title: The roles of interfacial water in electrocatalytic water splitting across diverse electrolyte environments
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic water splitting is central to green hydrogen production, yet its efficiency is increasingly governed by both active-site energetics and the nanoscale water layer at the electrode-electrolyte interface. Interfacial water directly influences water dissociation, proton and hydroxide transport, and catalyst stability. abstract: Abstract In structural health monitoring, full-field response sensing and monitoring are essential to establish a digital twin model. However, directly measuring all required structural loads and responses is costly and impractical. Simultaneous estimations of structural loads and responses are consequently developed, which is, however, an ill-posed problem. title: Insights into energy consumption and carbon emissions from freight industry in China
abstract: Against China’s commitments to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, the freight industry, a major energy consumer and emitter, demands attention. This study estimated the energy consumption and carbon emissions from the freight industry in China based on the data of 2022–2024 official turnover, energy source types and IPCC “top-down” CO 2 emission factors. abstract: Diabetic foot infection (DFI) significantly increases the risks of hospitalization and amputation, with biofilm infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) being key drivers of treatment failure. Here, we analyzed MRSA/CREC biofilm-infected ulcer tissues from patients using proteomics and metabolomics. title: The Causal Effect of Cross‑Border E‑Commerce Pilot Zones on Urban Export Growth: Evidence from Multi‑period Difference‑in‑Differences
abstract: Amid the rapid expansion of digital trade, China's Cross-border E-commerce Comprehensive Pilot Zones (CECPZs) represent a key institutional innovation to boost urban foreign trade. Using the CECPZ rollout as a quasi-natural experiment in a prefecture-level city panel (2000-2024) and a multi-period Difference-in-Differences design, baseline TWFE estimates indicate that designation substantially raises urban exports. abstract: Exploring how rural digitalization influences the green transformation of cultivated land and its spatial spillover effects holds significant implications for resolving the contradiction between cultivated land conservation and sustainable agricultural development, as well as advancing agricultural and rural modernization. abstract: The current study developed an amine-terminated zirconium metal-organic framework (UiO-66-NH2) to effectively adsorb lanthanum (La3+) from water. The UiO-66-NH2 was confirmed by various analytical techniques. The optimization of La3+ removal was achieved through response surface methodology. abstract: Background Biosorption using marine algae biosorbents is a sustainable and effective method for removing of heavy metals from aquatic environments. title: Four Quality-Control Failure Modes in Public Wireline-Log Archives: Measured Effects and a Reproducible Workflow, With Examples From Wyoming and Kansas
abstract: Public wireline-log archives are widely reused in petrophysical and machine-learning studies, yet the processing steps required to make them analytically usable are rarely reported. We processed 1,210 logs from the Teapot Dome archive in Wyoming, together with a 300-well pilot drawn from 29,089 Kansas Geological Survey records, and found four processing failures, each of which produced an error larger than the signal it was supposed to resolve. title: Catastrophe theory and AHP modelling of landslide susceptibility using multi-source geodata in southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous and structurally complex terrains, posing significant threats to lives, infrastructure, and sustainable development. Accurate Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (LSM) is therefore essential for hazard mitigation and land-use planning. This study develops a Catastrophe Theory (CT)-based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Index (LSMI) that integrates surface and subsurface conditioning factors derived from geological, geomorphological, geophysical, and climatic datasets. abstract: Design and additive manufacturing of multiscale metallic porous structures remain challenging because achieving complex geometries with high structural fidelity after metal conversion is difficult. abstract: Polymer-based protective coatings are moving from passive barriers toward adaptive chemical interfaces that regulate transport, adhesion, inhibitor release, fouling resistance and damage recovery under harsh service conditions. This review examines organic and polymer-rich coatings designed for corrosive, marine, humid, acidic, alkaline and biologically active environments from a polymer and surface chemistry perspective. title: Impact of Technology on the Environment: A Secondary-Research Study for MCA
abstract: Technology has become part of almost every daily task, and the way it interacts with the natural world is tangled. Satellites, renewable-energy equipment and software can all be used to safeguard natural habitats. Yet building and running them takes heavy electricity, draws on finite mineral deposits and, once devices wear out, leaves a growing pile of discarded electronics. abstract: Interventions addressing physical functioning and social generalization together remain scarce for adolescents with autism. This study developed the Aquatic Relay Social Coupling Window (ARSCW) model, which treats the instant of relay handoff as the smallest tolerable unit of social dosage and integrates sensory filtering by the aquatic medium, mandatory temporal coupling imposed by the relay format, and emotionally neutral collaboration driven by competitive goals. title: One health perspectives on pharmaceutical and clinical effluents driving multidrug resistance in aquatic ecosystems: a comprehensive review
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has emerged as one of the most pressing global health challenges, yet the contribution of environmental reservoirs to the spread of multidrug resistance (MDR) remains insufficiently integrated into mainstream discussions. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 167 peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2026 to examine how pharmaceutical manufacturing effluents and clinical waste drive the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and multidrug-resistant bacteria in aquatic ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Legacy oil and gas wells are an incompletely quantified source of greenhouse gas emissions and offer leakage pathways for subsurface gas migration if inadequately isolated. abstract: La permanencia estudiantil en modalidades no convencionales constituye un desafío asociado con condiciones académicas, personales, tecnológicas y sociales. El objetivo fue describir las condiciones vinculadas con la experiencia de permanencia de estudiantes del Sistema de Enseñanza Abierta (SEA) de la Universidad Veracruzana. abstract: Reducing crop cadmium (Cd) uptake via beneficial rhizosphere microbes offers a low-cost, sustainable strategy for ensuring agricultural product safety. abstract: Offshore assets deteriorate through mechanisms that reinforce one another: corrosion removes section and raises the local stress, the elevated stress accelerates fatigue, and fatigue damage exposes fresh metal to the marine environment. title: A comprehensive review of underground CO2 storage and associated risks
abstract: Geological carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) storage has emerged as one of the most promising technologies for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and achieving global carbon neutrality. This review provides a comprehensive overview of CO 2 geological storage with emphasis on storage formations, trapping mechanisms, storage capacity assessment methods, monitoring techniques, risk assessment, mitigation strategies, and the key factors governing long-term storage security. abstract: Bacterial biofilms are highly structured microbial communities which allow organisms to persist under different environmental challenges such as limitation of nutrients, oxidative stress, host immune defense, and antimicrobial agents. While antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has been well recognized as a key factor contributing to treatment failure, more and more evidence reported that biofilm-associated persistence is initially caused by antimicrobial tolerance rather than genetically encoded resistance. abstract: Objective This study aims to evaluate the current status of the nursing practice environment in a maternal and child specialized hospital, identify its associated influencing factors, and provide an empirical reference for formulating targeted optimization strategies for the nursing practice environment. title: How does energy transition in China amidst climate risk shocks influence residents’ welfare?
abstract: China regards energy transition as a significant measure to handle global climate change and foster the harmonious coexistence of human beings and nature. This article matches the urban energy transition index with China Family Panel Studies data to systematically examine and evaluate the impact of energy transition on residents’ happiness. abstract: This research paper explores the representation of digital control through smart spaces in Don DeLillo’s The Body Artist and Cosmopolis from the perspectives of Jannice Kall and Shoshana Zuboff. abstract: Amidst environmental challenges stemming from rapid economic growth and intensified energy market volatility due to geopolitical tensions, China faces multifaceted challenges in energy conservation, industrial restructuring, and economic development. abstract: Ozone (O 3 ) pollution has become a central concern in regional air-quality management. abstract: The increasing geo-economic competition between China and India has significantly reshaped South Asia’s strategic landscape, positioning Pakistan at the center of an evolving regional power contest. This study analyses the fundamental drivers of Sino-Indian geo-economic competition and its strategic ramifications for Pakistan’s economic development, security posture, and foreign policy orientation. title: Land suitability analysis for taro (Colocasia esculenta) cultivation based on topo-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system
abstract: Taro ( Colocasia esculenta ), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species (NUCS), is regarded as a climate-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries.
