title: Spatial distribution and severity of soil acidity across land uses in Gozamen District, Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: Ethiopia is facing a soil pH problem that has not yet been accurately measured due to limited research on this issue. This study attempts to quantify the range of acid soils and develop land use-specific soil acidity characteristics in the selected kebeles of Gozamen District of northwestern Ethiopia through field soil survey, GIS, and digital soil mapping. Soil samples were taken using stratified random sampling over six kebeles of the Gozamen District. Soil pH was analyzed based on the standard procedure of FAO (2020) and GLOSOLAN (2019). title: An explainable swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer framework with wavelet-based spatial–temporal feature modeling and activation function analysis for rainfall classification across Pakistan’s climatic regimes
abstract: Abstract Accurate rainfall occurrence prediction is essential for climate risk management, flood preparedness, and water resource planning, particularly in climatically diverse regions such as Pakistan. This paper develops and compares a multi-phase classification of rainfall based on daily IMERG precipitation data over six representative Pakistani cities spanning very low-, moderate-, and high-rainfall regimes, i.e., Gharo, Gilgit, Islamabad, Karachi, Swat, and Turbat. title: Time capsules of infection: Updating the distribution of Aphanomyces astaci in Croatia using archived crayfish specimens
abstract: The crayfish plague pathogen Aphanomyces astaci Schikora, 1906 is one of the most damaging invasive pathogens affecting European freshwater ecosystems, causing declines in native crayfish populations. In Croatia, crayfish plague was first reported in the late 19 th century and was subsequently molecularly confirmed in 2016. title: Transcriptomic identification of high-altitude illness candidate genes and physiological mechanisms: a multidimensional bioinformatics study with 106 drug–food homologous substance target prediction
abstract: Introduction High-altitude (HA) illness threatens health after acute high-altitude exposure, but its molecular mechanisms and effective interventions remain unclear. Drug–food homologous (DFH) substances have potential for HA illness intervention, yet their active components and targets are unknown. Methods Datasets related to HA illness, as well as 106 DFH substances and their corresponding chemical components, were obtained in this study. abstract: Background Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention. Methods We integrated network toxicology, an ensemble of 112 machine-learning classifiers and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with six GEO cohorts to nominate fibrotic-lung genes, which were intersected with predicted MTX targets to prioritize candidates relevant to MTX-PF. title: GIS-based assessment of population and dwelling exposure to landslide-prone areas in the Valencian Community (Spain)
abstract: The spatial identification of population exposure to landslide-prone areas is essential for risk-informed territorial planning, particularly where impacts affect peri-urban and dispersed residential areas rather than consolidated urban centres. This study presents a GIS-based, multi-scale methodology to quantify and locate population and dwelling exposure beyond administrative boundaries by integrating landslide susceptibility mapping, residential cadastral data, and high-resolution population information from the 2021 census grid. title: Institutional fragmentation and rule-of-law coordination in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: a maritime soft power perspective
abstract: Introduction International assessments of maritime cities have shifted from hard infrastructure indicators toward institutional quality metrics such as maritime finance and law and attractiveness and competitiveness. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), with its distinctive “one country, two systems, and three jurisdictions” configuration, faces gaps in cross-jurisdictional rule connectivity that may limit its maritime soft power—a challenge that existing single-jurisdiction assessment frameworks do not fully capture, highlighting the need for rule-of-law coordination. title: The power of healthcare reform: the effect of cross-provincial direct settlement on poverty among rural older adults in China
abstract: The implementation of the policy of direct settlement of cross-provincial medical expenses in China has effectively improved access to medical care for vulnerable migrant groups. Using data from the 2012–2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), this research applies a generalized Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to examine the impact of the policy on poverty among rural older adults, with Propensity Score Matching–Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID) used as a robustness check. title: Spectral classification of OB-type stars using tree-based ensemble methods and evaluation of their explainability
abstract: The advent of large-scale spectroscopic surveys will deliver tens of thousands of spectra of blue massive stars spanning a wide range of spectral types (SpTs) and luminosity classes (LCs). This data volume renders traditional spectral classification techniques increasingly impractical and motivates the development of automated classification tools. We aim to develop a robust machine learning framework for the automated spectral classification of massive OB-type stars by assessing the performance and evaluating the interpretability of several tree-based ensemble algorithms. title: Bebas-Aktif and Pragmatic Assertiveness: Continuity and Change in Indonesia’s Foreign Policy under Prabowo Subianto
abstract: This article examines whether Indonesian foreign policy under President Prabowo Subianto (October 2024–August 2026) represents a doctrinal departure from bebas-aktif or a programmatic reconfiguration of strategic autonomy. It develops the Doctrinal Continuity–Instrumental Reconfiguration (DCIR) model, integrating foreign-policy-change theory, role theory, leader-centered Foreign Policy Analysis, and hedging. title: Soil Salinity under Climate Change in Pakistan: Emerging Challenges and Sustainable Management Approaches for Agriculture
abstract: Soil salinity is a major constraint to agricultural productivity, soil health, and food security in Pakistan, particularly under changing climatic conditions. Rising temperatures, increased evapotranspiration, irregular precipitation, droughts, flooding, and sea-level rise can intensify salt accumulation and alter soil–water interactions. This review examines the emerging challenges associated with climate change and soil salinity in Pakistan, focusing on their impacts on soil properties, crop physiology, agricultural production, and rural livelihoods. title: Pre-stack seismic prediction of physical parameters of gas hydrate reservoirs based on rock-physics models and Bayesian statistical inversion
abstract: Rock-physics models serve as a bridge, establishing quantitative relationships between physical properties and elastic parameters of gas hydrate reservoirs, thereby guiding the prediction of reservoir properties using pre-stack seismic data. However, classical rock-physics modeling methods for hydrate reservoirs, based on pore-filling and load-bearing modes, are idealized assumptions regarding the microscopic occurrence modes of hydrates. title: Improved RT-DETR-based detection and counting of shrimp in EK80 acoustic echogram images
abstract: Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object-detection models. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT-DETR. title: SIMULATION-DRIVEN METHOD FOR WATER COVERAGE MONITORING FROM MULTI-SENSOR SATELLITE IMAGERY
abstract: Monitoring water coverage in intertidal zones is challenging due to the lack of satellite sensors that simultaneously provide both high spatial and high temporal resolution. Landsat offers detailed spatial information but is limited by its 16-day revisit cycle, whereas Himawari-8 provides frequent observations but at coarse spatial scales. Existing multi-sensor fusion approaches, such as STARFM and ESTARFM, attempt to bridge this gap but rely on the assumption of linear or abrupt land cover changes, which is inadequate for capturing the gradual and non-linear dynamics of tidal environments. title: Impact of Radio Wave Refractivity on Mobile Network Portability Threshold in Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigates the influence of radio wave refractivity on mobile network portability thresholds in Bayelsa State, Nigeria, focusing on the effects of radio refractivity (W-unit), atmospheric temperature (K), relative humidity (%), and atmospheric pressure (hPa) on mobile network signal strength. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining field measurements and statistical analysis to assess the Quality of Service (QoS) of GSM network providers in Biogbolo and Etegwe, Yenagoa. title: The 2 May 2025 Mw 7.4 Drake Passage Earthquake: Insights Into Tectonics at the Shackleton Fracture Zone–Chilean Trench Transition
abstract: Abstract On 2 May 2025, an Mw 7.4 earthquake occurred ∼120 km off the southern tip of Tierra del Fuego, at the transition of the Shackleton Fracture Zone and the Chile Trench. This event exhibits reverse‐faulting mechanisms with relatively steeply dipping planes and is the largest recorded along this complex plate boundary. title: Colorimetría y atmósfera como constructores de percepción emocional audiovisual: una revisión sistemática.
abstract: El cine y los contenidos audiovisuales están cambiando gracias a la evolución del color y las tecnologías visuales. Actualmente, aspectos como la colorimetría, la gradación y la composición influyen de forma directa en las emociones del público. A través de una revisión sistemática basada en el método PRISMA, esta investigación examina cómo los estudios recientes aprovechan la narrativa visual, la fotografía y la teoría del color para explicar estas reacciones. title: Multi-scale ship detection with high-resolution SAR images based on improved YOLOv8
abstract: To improve the detection accuracy of SAR ship targets under complex background clutter, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 detection method for SAR ship detection tasks. Three optimization strategies are adopted, including CA attention module, improved DSConv convolution module, and Shape-IoU loss function. title: Unraveling nonlinear ecosystem water use efficiency dynamics and environmental drivers across Iran using remote sensing and XGBoost-SHAP
abstract: Understanding how ecosystems regulate the trade-off between carbon assimilation and water loss is essential for assessing ecohydrological stability in water-limited regions. This study investigated ecosystem water use efficiency (WUE) dynamics across Iran from 2001 to 2025 using an integrated framework combining multi-source remote sensing datasets, polynomial trend analysis, optimized eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Morris global sensitivity analysis (Morris GSA). title: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
abstract: Abstract. Spatially and temporally resolved observations of precipitation water isotopes are essential for quantifying groundwater recharge, constraining hydroclimate variability, and calibrating paleoclimate proxies, yet such datasets remain scarce for monsoon-influenced volcanic islands characterized by steep topography and strong maritime and continental interactions. abstract: Concept Drift Detectors are the methods that are used to identify the patterns and behaviors of data that changes over time. These methods are tested separately on different datasets, which makes it difficult to compare which detector is suitable for particular situation. title: Spatial spillover effects of urban forest policy on urban green production efficiency: evidence from China’s National Forest City Construction
abstract: As environmental constraints tighten and urban green transformation continues, whether National Forest City Construction (NFCC) can improve urban green production efficiency (GPE) and generate cross-regional spillovers remains an important theoretical and policy question. Using panel data for 277 cities at the prefecture level or above in China from 2006 to 2024, this study applies a spatial Durbin difference-in-differences (SDM-DID) model to estimate the effect of NFCC on GPE. title: ThermoZone-TR: an explainable ERA5-Land degree-day framework for reassessing Türkiye’s TS 825 building climate zones
abstract: Türkiye’s thermal insulation standard, TS 825, was reissued in its 2024 edition with six climate zones and, for the first time, a cooling component, and it has governed all new building permits since April 2025. The zones are assigned at province level from station records averaged over 1992–2021, which leaves two questions open: how much climate variation a single provincial class conceals, and how quickly a fixed window falls behind a warming climate. abstract: Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient that constrains productivity across many terrestrial ecosystems. Soil microorganisms regulate P transformation through distinct functional strategies, yet how these strategies vary with land use and environmental conditions across chronically P-impoverished landscapes remains poorly understood. abstract: Background The fucoidan extracted from sea cucumber Pearsonothuria graeffei (Fuc- Pg ) has beneficial anti-inflammatory and lipid-lowering effects, suggesting its potential anti-atherosclerotic properties. title: Natural Hazards, Critical Infrastructure Systems, and Resilience Enhancement: A Structured State-of-the-Art Review and a Synthesis-Based Rapid Assessment Framework
abstract: Abstract Critical infrastructure systems (CISs) are increasingly exposed to natural hazards whose impacts are amplified by infrastructure interdependence, urban complexity, and the growing prevalence of compound and cascading events. title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
abstract: Leveraging its capability for large-scale, repeated monitoring, remote sensing has increasingly supported nitrogen and phosphorus estimation in surface waters. However, the evolution of this field from proxy-based nutrient retrieval to integration with process-based models remains insufficiently synthesized. abstract: While extensive research exists on microfinance as a tool for smoothing consumption at the household level in poor communities, studies on the progression beyond consumption to household economic development are just beginning to emerge. This paper addresses the limited knowledge by examining how investment-focused microfinance loans enable poor households to transition from consumption smoothing to household economic development within rural communities. title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. title: Local ecological knowledge and attitude toward the Great Cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo) among the fishermen's community at Beni Haroun Dam, Algeria
abstract: Incorporating the perspectives of local fishing communities and their ecological knowledge (LEK) can enhance policymaking and improve wildlife and economic management strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the local ecological knowledge of fishermen at Beni Haroun Dam regarding the Great Cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo) a species legally protected under Algerian law, and to reveal their conservation attitudes toward this species. abstract: We report Pagurus chevreuxi (Bouvier, 1896) for the first time from Spanish waters of the Gulf of Cádiz, filling a gap in this species’ documented distribution along the Iberian Atlantic margin. The specimen was collected at 418 m depth on Gazul mud volcano during the CIRCASUR2025 survey and identified using diagnostic morphological characters and mitochondrial 16S rRNA sequence data. title: GIS-based spatial prioritization of natural-hazard exposure and recorded COVID-19 case counts in Lemery, Batangas, Philippines
abstract: Local governments often maintain separate natural-hazard maps and health-surveillance records but lack a transparent method for identifying areas where these concerns overlap. abstract: Purpose This study investigates how advanced machine learning (ML) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models can enhance forecasting accuracy and portfolio decision-making under environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-driven and uncertainty-sensitive market conditions. abstract: Urban greening in desert cities is closely related to atmospheric visibility and near-surface water conditions, yet its environmental performance depends on vegetation condition, landscape configuration, atmospheric context, and irrigation demand. Taking Dubai as the study area and 2010, 2015, and 2020 as reference years, this study integrates Landsat imagery, GLC_FCS30D land-use data, atmospheric visibility, precipitation, and surface soil moisture to examine the spatial and temporal coordination between visibility-related atmospheric conditions and water availability. title: Wire arc additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4 V alloy: a review
abstract: One of the notable additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) also known as wire-arc directed energy deposition (DED-Arc), has become a promising processing method to economically build large-sized components with relatively reasonable accuracy and greater deposition rates compared to other additive manufacturing processes. abstract: ABSTRACT The escalation of conflict in the Middle East in 2026 and the disruptions affecting major maritime chokepoints, particularly the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el‐Mandeb/Red Sea corridor, threaten global food security through higher energy, fertilizer, and shipping costs. title: Ecological structuring of biosynthetic potential across terrestrial soil-associated Streptomyces genomes
abstract: Streptomyces populations represent one of the richest reservoirs of microbial specialized metabolites, although the ecological organization of their biosynthetic diversity remains insufficiently resolved at large genomic scales. In the present study, 14,597 publicly available genome assemblies were initially screened. title: From waste to resilience: the future of wastewater
abstract: Global water scarcity, influenced by climate change, population increase, and the exhaustion of freshwater resources, requires wastewater recycling. This article emphasizes the importance of wastewater within a circular and climate-resilient economy that functions as a source of clean water, fertilizers, and energy. abstract: Introduction Mangrove litter decomposition contributes to coastal carbon and nutrient cycling, yet changes in litter mass may not fully reflect changes in elemental composition. abstract: Background Rising global temperatures and precipitation variability are intensifying extreme weather events and threatening human health worldwide. In Kenya, climate change is projected to significantly alter the distribution and severity of climate-sensitive diseases, particularly affecting vulnerable populations. This study projects climate extremes and associated health impacts in Kenya through 2050 under two emission scenarios: SSP245 (moderate mitigation) and SSP585 (high emissions). abstract: This study examined the effects of the Media Literacy and Education course on the media use patterns of social studies pre-service teachers. abstract: To solve the dilemma of excessively high financing costs of small and medium-sized enterprises, we can draw on digital inclusive finance as a new path; this model is essentially a product born from the combination of digital technology and the idea of inclusiveness. From 2011 to 2022, this paper analyzes the annual records of 12,864 medium and small listed enterprises covering Shanghai and Shenzhen. abstract: Sulfated polysaccharides derived from marine algae have attracted considerable interest in innate immunity research due to their structural diversity and pronounced immunomodulatory activities. Ulvan, carrageenan, and fucoidan, derived from green, red, and brown algae, respectively, represent three paradigmatic classes of algal sulfated polysaccharides. abstract: India produced an estimated 369.05 million tonnes of horticultural produce from 29.48 million ha in 2024–25. title: Schrödinger’s Penguin? Divergent population trajectories and the challenge of assessing the threat status of the Erect-crested penguin
abstract: "Schrödinger's Cat" is a quantum mechanics thought experiment in which a cat in a sealed box is considered both alive and dead until the box is opened and its true state observed. title: Geochronology and geochemistry of granitic dikes in the Xiaogushan gold deposit NE China and implications for gold mineralization
abstract: The Xiaogushan cryptoexplosive breccia-type gold deposit is located within the eastern Hebei-western Liaoning gold belt along the northern margin of the North China Craton. title: Detection of Cervical Nodal Metastasis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Using Elastic Scattering Spectroscopy: Ex Vivo Diagnostic Modeling Study
abstract: Background: Cervical nodal metastasis remains one of the strongest determinants of treatment planning and prognosis in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Histopathology remains the reference standard, but it does not provide immediate information at the point of surgical specimen assessment. Elastic scattering spectroscopy (ESS) offers rapid, label-free optical interrogation of tissue microstructure, and may support ex vivo nodal assessment. title: Comparative physiological and photosynthetic responses of three mangrove species to salinity stress and exogenous melatonin
abstract: Extreme salinity is a major environmental constraint affecting plant growth and physiological performance in coastal ecosystems. Although mangroves are naturally adapted to saline environments, their tolerance and physiological responses vary among species, and the effects of exogenous melatonin (MT) under different salinity levels remain insufficiently understood. This study compared the physiological and photosynthetic responses of Aegiceras corniculatum , Kandelia obovata , and Rhizophora stylosa under NaCl-only and corresponding NaCl + MT treatments. title: Active Visual Perception: Opportunities and Challenges
abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision. title: Evaluation of UAV Flight Planning Strategies on the Accuracy of Glacier Mapping in Rugged Antarctic Terrains: A Case Study of Horseshoe Island
abstract: Changes in the Earth’s radiation balance have increased global average temperatures, accelerating glacier melt in Antarctica. Monitoring this process has become of great importance for future modeling studies. Therefore, obtaining accurate, reliable, and most importantly rapid, logistically feasible, and cost-effective measurements of glacier melt is critically important for regions with harsh conditions such as Antarctica. title: Sequence-based identification and characterization of mer operon-related genes from Kongsfjorden sediments
abstract: Mercury resistance is commonly associated with the mer operon, which comprises genes involved in mercury sensing, regulation, transport, and transformation. In the present study, metagenomic DNA extracted from Kongsfjorden sediments, Svalbard, was screened using a previously reported merRTΔP-targeting primer pair, followed by PCR, cloning, Sanger sequencing, and subsequent in silico analyses to characterise putative mercury-resistance-associated genetic components. title: Enteropathy in inborn and acquired errors of immunity: histological patterns and clinical correlates
abstract: Introduction Enteropathy is a significant and under-recognised complication of inborn errors of immunity (IEI), frequently misclassified as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or coeliac disease due to overlapping and non-specific histopathological findings. Diagnostic criteria remain poorly defined, contributing to substantial diagnostic delay and associated morbidity. title: The influence of health conditions, lifestyle factors, and stress on seafarers’ self-rated health — a cross-sectional study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-rated health (SRH) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active-duty seafarers. A total of 22,432 international seafarers who were on board were included in the analysis of an electronic survey distributed via 52 shipping and manning companies in February-March 2024. title: Hydrodynamic Response of Rectangular Floating Breakwaters near Sidewalls: A Comparative SBFEM Study of Side-Plate and Stepped-Seabed Configurations
abstract: Abstract Reducing substructure clearance modifies wave–structure interaction and can increase hydrodynamic loads on the floating breakwaters. The present study therefore evaluates the resulting changes in wave-induced forces and overturning moments rather than directly quantifying wave-transmission performance. title: Central rapidity net baryon density and baryon number carriers in high-energy collisions
abstract: This article focuses on the experimental progress of net baryon density measurements in the central rapidity region, spanning from the AGS and SPS to the RHIC and LHC energy regimes. It comparatively analyzes the interpretation capabilities of three theoretical frameworks for net baryon density distributions across different energy regions: the valence quark transport model, the hadron cascade and hydrodynamics model, and the gluon junction model. title: Microplastics as evolving particle–chemical–microbial interfaces: plastisphere ecology, ecotoxicity, and safety-informed remediation
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are not environmentally static particles; aging, fragmentation, contaminant acquisition, organic conditioning, and microbial colonization progressively convert them into dynamic particle–chemical–microbial interfaces. This transformation is central to their environmental fate and risk because plastisphere communities can alter particle transport, contaminant partitioning, nutrient cycling, antimicrobial-resistance dynamics, and polymer transformation. title: CMIP6 Climate Model Ensemble-Based Assessment of Future Changes in Air Temperature and Atmospheric Precipitation over Uzbekistan under SSP Scenarios
abstract: Reliable projections of temperature and precipitation underpin water and agricultural planning in arid Central Asia, yet most Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) assessments for the region are domain-averaged and do not resolve the contrasting physical-geographical zones of Uzbekistan. This study assesses projected changes in both variables over the national territory using observation-constrained CMIP6 ensembles under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios. title: Multiscale drivers of accidental epiphytism in temperate Europe
abstract: Accidental epiphytes — terrestrial plants that opportunistically establish in trees — occur across climatic regions, but the conditions that allow them to colonise arboreal habitats remain poorly understood. We combined field surveys along a coastal western European transect, from the Netherlands to northern Spain, with curated community-science records and used Bayesian models to test whether accidental epiphyte occurrence, abundance and richness are associated with habitat setting, host size and macroclimatic positioning within each species’ climatic envelope. title: Application of scanning river surface flow field monitoring system in monitoring complex flow regimes of waterways
abstract: Real-time and accurate monitoring of the surface velocity of rivers is crucial for hydrological research, water resource management, and the safety assurance of waterways. The traditional contact flow measurement method has limitations such as installation difficulties, high maintenance costs, and difficulty in real-time monitoring under complex hydrological conditions. Therefore, this study developed and deployed a non-contact scanning river flow field monitoring system. title: Improving prenatal thalassemia carrier detection with a combined MCV and MCH strategy: a 24-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Carrier screening for thalassemia conventionally uses a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) cutoff ≤ 80 fL. However, silent carriers harboring mild mutations often present with borderline indices, which, if missed, may result in offspring with hemoglobin H disease or other significant hemoglobinopathies. Thus, we aimed to evaluate whether alternative hematological cutoffs could reduce this detection gap. title: Mapping the environmental-health interface in micro- and nanoplastics research: a bibliometric analysis, 2009–2025
abstract: Introduction Research on micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) connects environmental exposure with biological mechanisms and health-related outcomes. Bibliometric searches at this interface can retrieve ecotoxicological, model-organism, mechanistic, and human-health records and should not be interpreted as inventories of confirmed disease studies. We mapped the growth, collaboration, and thematic structure of this query-defined environmental-health interface. title: Solvation‐Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide‐Temperature Operation of High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep‐sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature‐sensitive ion transport, Li + solvation, and interfacial chemistry. title: Contribution of chemical components to cloud condensation nuclei prediction across multiple continental sites
abstract: Aerosol–cloud interactions represent a major uncertainty in climate projections. Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are particles upon which cloud droplets form, yet in situ CCN measurements remain scarce. Aerosol chemical component exerts important control over CCN activity. It remains unclear how reliably aerosol chemical composition predicts CCN number concentration (N CCN ). This study compiled a dataset of N CCN (supersaturation of 0.1 to 1%) collocated with aerosol chemical components at 20 global continental sites, spanning from remote natural to heavily polluted regions. title: Integrative taxonomy of the temporary fish parasitic isopod Gnathia gunayalaensis n. sp. (Isopoda: Gnathiidae) from Panama, with supplementary data on Gnathia magdalenensis Müller, 1988
abstract: Abstract Gnathiid isopods are common ectoparasites of fishes whose unusual life history has created challenges for characterising their biodiversity and biogeography. Based on morphological and molecular data, we describe a new species, Gnathia gunayalaensis n. sp., from Panama in the Southwestern Caribbean ecoregion of the Tropical Atlantic realm. The new species can be identified by a distinctly pointed superior, inferior and produced frontal margin, and by falciform mandibles with a finely serrated inner margin of the blade. title: Projecting the real through active inference: a unified model of reality construction from neuronal dynamics to social consensus a neuroscientific framework for psychopathology
abstract: How does the brain transform a chaotic stream of sensory signals into a stable, shared experience of reality? This theoretical paper proposes that the brain does not passively receive the world, but actively projects it – it continuously generates predictions about sensory inputs and updates its internal model when predictions fail, a process formally described by the free energy principle and active inference. title: More seeds yield more shoots, but not higher per-seed establishment in a clam-mediated seagrass restoration experiment
abstract: Seagrass restoration increasingly relies on seed-based approaches, yet optimal seeding densities and deployment methods remain poorly resolved. We evaluated the relative effects of seed density and clam-mediated seed placement on eelgrass ( Zostera marina ) establishment in a field restoration experiment in Back Sound, North Carolina. title: Do large language models keep the hedge? Uncertainty preservation when large language models summarize aviation and maritime incident reports
abstract: Safety-incident reports are written with deliberate epistemic caution: A reporter marks what was seen, what was inferred, and what remains unsure, and a dropped hedge can turn a tentative observation into an apparent cause. As large language models take over summarizing such reports for triage, indexing, and search, whether they preserve that caution becomes a property of the safety record itself. title: A multivariate causal chain detection methodology assessed on the ENSO modulation of the Northeastern Brazil precipitation
abstract: Abstract This study presents a novel data-driven methodology for extraction causal chains from high-dimensional climate datasets, with a particular focus on detecting and visualizing the pathways that link climate anomalies across geographically distant regions. The proposed framework is designed to be computationally efficient while maintaining high interpretability, making it suitable for large-scale analytical applications in climate science. title: Variation of total organic carbon concentrations in rainwater in Hanoi City, Vietnam
abstract: Organic carbon in precipitation represents an important pathway linking atmospheric processes with terrestrial and aquatic carbon cycling, yet data from rapidly urbanizing tropical and subtropical cities remain scarce. This study investigated total organic carbon (TOC) concentrations in 264 rainwater samples collected from 21 wards across Hanoi, Vietnam, between May 2023 and December 2025. title: Mechanism-defined secondary hypertension enables precision diagnosis and treatment: an evidence review
abstract: Background Secondary hypertension is under-recognised despite the availability of mechanism-based diagnostic tests and, for several aetiologies, potentially curative or highly targeted therapy. The clinically important question is not only which causes exist, but how reliably mechanisms translate into diagnosis and cause-directed treatment. title: Numerical investigation of energy absorption behaviour of additively manufactured functionally graded lattice structures for automotive crash box applications
abstract: In the quest to improve crash safety in automotive structures, lightweight energy absorbing lattice architectures have gained considerable attention. This study presents a combined numerical and experimental investigation of additively manufactured uniform and functionally graded (FG) lattice structures for automotive crash-box applications. Four lattice topologies Body-Centered Cubic (BCC), Body-Centered Cubic with vertical stiffeners (BCCz), Octet Truss, and Re-entrant Auxetic are evaluated under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. title: Detección de objetos de última generación: una revisión del rendimiento y modelos avanzados frente a los estándares en la agricultura inteligente
abstract: Precision agriculture incorporates computer vision techniques to automate image analysis and optimize monitoring tasks in production systems. This paper presents a comparison of object detection models applied to a practical precision agriculture case study, using a proprietary dataset of grape bunch images, with a methodology extensible to standard datasets such as COCO. title: From monitoring to maintenance support: a critical review of wind turbine condition monitoring systems and their integration into maintenance practice
abstract: Although condition monitoring systems (CMS) provide detailed information about the health of critical wind turbine components, their practical application in wind farm operations and maintenance (O&M) remains limited, significantly diminishing their value. The reasons for this situation are not merely technical issues, rather, a complex interplay of various factors besides the condition monitoring algorithms themselves. abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical overview of water pollution and monitoring under conflict conditions. Water pollutants are grouped into conflict-related contaminants, including explosive compounds, ammunition additives, uranium and heavy metals; conventional pollutants, including nutrients, heavy metals and organic matter; and hazardous pollutants also occurring in civilian activities, including petroleum hydrocarbons, pesticides, phenols, pharmaceuticals, personal care products and microplastics. title: Engineering mechanics of bio-inspired architected cementitious materials (ACM) and composites (ACC) enabled by digital fabrication
abstract: Concrete is inherently weak and brittle under tension, making it susceptible to cracking under mechanical and environmental loading. Recent advances in digital fabrication enable control over spatial arrangements of cementitious materials across meso-to-macro length scales, shifting cementitious design from passively formed microstructures to intentionally engineered architecture. title: Supporting post-bushfire biodiversity through citizen science tourism: recovery, regeneration, and reflections
abstract: The Australian 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires had profound ecological and socio-economic impacts on Kangaroo Island, threatening iconic species including koalas, Kangaroo Island dunnarts, and glossy black cockatoos, and disrupting local tourism. In response, and co-designed with multiple stakeholders, Passport to Recovery (P2R) was developed as a tourist-focused, place-based citizen science program to quickly integrate multiple biodiversity monitoring projects into a single, cohesive experience. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a Causal‐Aware Dynamic Knowledge Graph (CA‐DKG) framework that systematically fuses FMEA domain knowledge with data‐driven causal discovery from SCADA time series. We first develop a heterogeneous knowledge graph construction method that unifies structured FMEA failure triples with sensor monitoring relationships, providing a unified representation framework for cross‐source fault information covering components, failure modes, root causes and operational variables. title: Modeling of Average Global Climate Change by 2200
abstract: According to a predictive global climate model described and used in a recent study (April 2025), future climate change is relatively insensitive to various greenhouse gas (GHG) emission scenarios, despite their significant differences. The author concluded that it is likely necessary to move even closer to pre-industrial CO₂ concentrations to truly reverse the current trend. abstract: Background Lung cancer continues to maintain a high mortality rate, with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) being its most common type. As an emerging environmental pollutant, 6PPD-quinone is attracting increasing attention. Through network toxicology, we constructed a prognostic model and validated it with molecular docking and dynamics simulations, revealing its underlying molecular mechanisms. title: Diagnostic accuracy of a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system: a retrospective study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort. title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. title: Conditioned media derived from HepG2 cells treated with phosphoeleganin synthetic-derived compound PE/2 improve cytokine balance and metabolic response in 3T3-L1 adipocytes
abstract: Background The liver–adipose axis regulates insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism, and its dysregulation contributes to metabolic disorders. PE/2, a semisynthetic derivative of the marine natural product phosphoeleganin, reduces IL-6 expression and secretion, enhancing insulin sensitivity in liver cells (HepG2). abstract: ABSTRACT Regular monitoring of pipeline defects is crucial for the safe operation of municipal environmental infrastructure. However, tiny structural degradation, topological discontinuities, low‐light interference, and the slender morphology of defects pose significant challenges for accurate detection. In complex pipeline environments, existing detectors generally suffer from insufficient structural‐frequency perception and morphology‐insensitive localization. title: Evaluating mangrove establishment trajectories and carbon recovery potential using a spatial age-based framework
abstract: Abstract Mangrove restoration is a vital nature-based solution for climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation. However, large-scale mangrove restoration success is predominantly evaluated using area-based metrics, which fail to capture the complex temporal trajectories of forest structural and functional recovery. title: Environmental controls of mangrove propagule and seedling establishment: salinity, hypoxia, sulfide, sediment instability, and early root function
abstract: Mangrove propagules and seedlings encounter interacting environmental constraints before secure anchorage and functional root systems develop. This narrative review synthesizes hydrological, physiological, biogeochemical, and sediment evidence to organize establishment into propagule delivery, retention, rooting, seedling persistence, and progression toward sapling recruitment. title: Chronology-aware generation of early Chinese black-and-white traditional motifs via an edge-aware self-attention variational autoencoder
abstract: Chinese black-and-white traditional motifs are important visual records of cultural symbolism, ritual expression, and stylistic evolution, yet their small and poorly annotated image collections limit computational analysis and generation. Here, we present a chronology-aware generative framework for digital heritage representation using a curated dataset of 300 traditional pattern images from four historical periods. title: Spatially Constrained Self-Organizing Maps for Seismic Facies Analysis
abstract: Abstract Understanding and characterizing seismic facies is essential for reconstructing depositional settings, identifying stratigraphic boundaries, and supporting reservoir evaluation in both exploration and development contexts. In this study, we present a spatially constrained self-organizing map (SOM) framework for seismic facies analysis that integrates multi-attribute information while incorporating local spatial consistency during training. title: Forecasting Annual Capture Fisheries Production in Somalia Using ARIMA Models
abstract: The study aims to forecast the production of Somalia's capture fisheries for the five years that follow, from 2024 to 2028, using the Box-Jenkins method and employing in-sample data spanning 50 years, from 1974 to 2023. Among the alternative models, ARIMA (1,1,1) was determined by the study to be the most suitable. abstract: Introducción. El erizo negro Arbacia nigra (Molina, 1782) (Echinoidea: Arbaciidae) forma parte de la diversidad marina peruana. Objetivo. abstract: Abstract. Air quality monitoring and climate studies require continuous, vertically resolved observations to characterize aerosols and their impact on radiation, cloud microphysics, and atmospheric composition. In this study, we present CONIOPOL (CONIOlogy + POLarization), an automated depolarization-based classification algorithm developed with the polarized Automatic Lidar Ceilometer (ALC), CL61 (Vaisala Oyi, FIN) installed at Uccle, Belgium. title: An explainable reinforcement learning framework for energy-aware cluster head selection in smart-city IoT wireless sensor networks
abstract: Cluster head (CH) selection is a decisive control mechanism for prolonging the operational lifetime of Internet-of-Things (IoT)-enabled wireless sensor networks (WSNs) that underpin smart-city sensing. title: Ecotourism: A Key Strategy For Realizing Golden Indonesia 2045: Penelitian
abstract: The Golden Indonesia 2045 initiative aims to transform Indonesia into a globally competitive, inclusive, and sustainable developed nation by the centenary of its independence. However, challenges such as environmental degradation, climate change, and interregional economic inequality demand a reorientation of the national development paradigm from extractive modalities to a green economy. title: Monitoring seasonal and long-term forest canopy dynamics using Sentinel-2 imagery and Random Forest on the Google Earth Engine platform
abstract: Understanding forest canopy dynamics is critical for assessing the condition, resilience, and conservation priorities of protected landscapes. This study evaluated the spatiotemporal and seasonal variation in mapped forest canopy density within the Orchha Wildlife Sanctuary, Madhya Pradesh, India, using multi-seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery and a Google Earth Engine (GEE)-based Random Forest (RF) classification framework. abstract: Abstract. This study presents a semi-systematic synthesis of scientific literature published between 2015 and 2025 on climate risk in African cities. From an initial set of 1,832 records identified through broad climate- and urban-related keywords, 273 articles were selected through title and abstract screening. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study combines quantitative mapping of geographic coverage, climate hazards, methodologies, and keyword networks with expert review and AI-assisted synthesis of research gaps. abstract: Abstract Estuaries are under threat globally from a wide range of stressors, with rates of ecosystem metabolism – respiration (R), gross primary production (GPP), and net ecosystem metabolism (NEM) – representing a way for resource managers to quantify their impacts. In this study, we assessed how natural and anthropogenic stressors have altered metabolism within the extensively modified Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (“Delta”) in California, USA. abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. This study evaluates a feature-level fusion workflow that integrates Sentinel-2 optical indices and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter for crop-type mapping in Candipuro District, Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. abstract: Reliable short-term inflow forecasting is critical for optimizing hydroelectric power plant (HPP) operations, where water availability is directly influenced by dynamic and often extreme weather patterns. Inaccurate inflow estimations can result in either uncontrolled water spills or reservoir levels dropping below operational thresholds, both leading to reduced energy efficiency and potential operational risks. abstract: Using the UrbanSound8K dataset as a representative case, this study investigates how lightweight acoustic models can be trained with limited labeled data in resource-constrained environments. Because conventional knowledge distillation confines knowledge transfer to a single target dataset, it leaves the rich prior knowledge in external audio sources largely unused. abstract: An accurate and timely flood prediction that relies on streamflow information is important for developing an early warning system to minimize the negative effects of floods. abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic optimisation algorithm based on the semi-aquatic behaviour of the red-eared slider (Trachemys scripta elegans). Design/Methodology/Approach: An experimental research design was adopted. The proposed algorithm models two behavioural stages of the red-eared slider: “foraging in water” as an exploration mechanism and “sunbathing on a platform” as an exploitation mechanism. abstract: Abstract. Deterministic model predictions can struggle to adequately capture extreme events such as floods and droughts, which are of particular relevance in hydrology. This limitation arises because deterministic models collapse the conditional runoff distribution to a single point estimate. abstract: Microclimate prediction is critical for optimizing larval growth and productivity in Black Soldier Fly (BSF) insectariums, where temperature and humidity exhibit nonlinear and time-varying dynamics. Conventional models such as Vector Autoregression (VAR) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) often struggle to balance accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability in IoT-based environments. abstract: Although loss of control (not under command, NUC) is one of the leading triggers of maritime accidents, the quantitative role of human and organizational factors in the process by which it evolves into a risk of grounding and collision has been largely neglected. Traditional approaches primarily treat this situation as a technical reliability issue; however, whether a loss of control leads to a disaster is often determined not by the failure itself, but by human and organizational performance in the first few minutes following the failure. abstract: Cross-subject electroencephalogram (EEG) recognition remains a fundamental challenge because large inter-subject variability causes severe distribution shifts that substantially degrade the generalization ability of existing learning models. title: Island invertebrate responses to single‐ and multi‐species invasive rodent eradications
abstract: Abstract Globally, islands have been invaded by invasive mammals with devastating impacts on biodiversity. In response, eradication programs have increased in number, scale, and success. However, the conservation benefits for small and cryptic invertebrates are rarely quantified. Monitoring invertebrate communities can provide insights into the ecosystem‐level response to eradications. abstract: Cybersecurity is the sum of processes, policies, and technical measures applied against threats to information and communication infrastructure. With the digital transformation movements across all sectors, the importance of cybersecurity is increasing day by day. abstract: ABSTRACT Remote sensing of colonial wildlife has largely focused on estimating population size, providing limited insight into internal demographic structure and spatial organization. We present a transferable, individual‐based framework that integrates morphology‐informed classification and spatial metrics to extract demographic composition and social spacing from high‐resolution unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery. abstract: Extreme congestion occupies only a small portion of traffic records but carries disproportionate operational consequences for traffic-management systems. Conventional point and probabilistic forecasters are optimised primarily for average accuracy and therefore often underfit rare, severe speed reductions. abstract: A single-modality approach to neurodegenerative disease classification is often limited by heterogeneous clinical manifestations, modality-specific feature distributions, and incomplete data availability. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
abstract: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. abstract: Chili pepper productivity in Indonesia is highly sensitive to climate variability, particularly solar radiation. This study aims to predict solar radiation to optimize chili pepper productivity across four distinct topographic zones in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. abstract: Foundation models produce strong patch-level representations in histopathological image analysis; however, domain shifts across different centers, staining protocols, and scanner conditions can limit the direct generalizability of these representations. abstract: Cervid overpopulation is increasingly altering temperate forest ecosystems worldwide, when browsing pressure exceeds ecosystem resilience, with consequences that extend beyond individual species to the structure and functioning of entire communities. abstract: Wetlands play a crucial role in regulating regional climate through their effects on surface energy balance and evapotranspiration. abstract: Groundwater is a major water resource for irrigation and domestic use, especially in arid and semi-arid regions where freshwater is scarce and the total amount of rainfall is limited. Hence, monitoring both quality and quantity parameters of this source is necessary for optimal water resources management, environmental studies, and ecosystem modeling, as well as ecological planning. Groundwater level (GWL) variation is influenced by numerous driving factors, both natural and human-induced. abstract: Dam-break flow modelling involves a trade-off as resolving steep gradients requires high-order discretisations, yet these tend to generate spurious oscillations near discontinuities. Moreover, classical limiters used to suppress such oscillations rely largely on single-parameter algebraic indicator rules. This study replaces the procedure with a fuzzy c-means flux-blending framework for the finite-volume solution of the shallow water equations. abstract: Fleets of connected autonomous vehicles have to solve two problems at once: they must agree on who goes first, and each of them must stay clear of traffic that nobody controls. This paper presents ASC-MAPPO, an attention- and safety-constrained variant of multi-agent proximal policy optimization designed for exactly that coupling. title: From stretchable materials and functional fibers to intelligent textile sensing systems
abstract: Abstract Wearable sensors that offer significant adaptability and comfort demonstrate substantial potential for discrete, seamless integration into garments, enabling diverse applications for remote monitoring. The transformation of rigid electronic devices into flexible and stretchable sensors, achieved by integrating conductive materials with compliant dielectrics, has enabled the development of robust sensors. title: Mathematical Foundation of Digital Twins
abstract: A digital twin (DT) is a computational model that evolves over time to persistently represent the structure, behavior, and context of a unique physical system or process. DTs are characterized by a dynamic and continuous two-way flow of information between the computational model and the physical system. Data streams from the physical system are assimilated into the computational model to reduce uncertainties and improve predictions of the model, which in turn is used as a basis for controlling the physical system, optimizing data acquisition, and providing decision support. abstract: High-frequency millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) communications are promising for 6G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) services but remain vulnerable to dynamic vehicular mobility, bursty heterogeneous traffic, and heavy-tailed physical blockage. Conventional routing approaches often rely on memoryless channel models, non-differentiable soft-computing heuristics, or centralized optimization that may not adequately capture blockage persistence and tail-latency risks. title: Climate-Related Challenges, Risk, Environmental Health Promotion: An Interdisciplinary Approach
abstract: Climate change has intensified the frequency, severity, and geographic reach of extreme weather events, posing growing risks to human and environmental health worldwide. This study is a descriptive-analytical systematic literature review (PRISMA), combined with a case study of an interdisciplinary research group, examining scientific production and official data on global climate-related disasters from 2004 to 2024, with emphasis on historical trends and geographic distribution. title: Parrot Mambo Minidrone as a benchmark platform for low-cost UAV research: a review of control, autonomy, software validation, safety and experimental evaluation
abstract: Low-cost minidrone platforms are increasingly used in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) research for safe indoor experimentation, controller development and engineering education. The Parrot Mambo Minidrone is particularly attractive because of its compact size, onboard sensing, MATLAB/Simulink compatibility and suitability for real-time validation. This review critically synthesises 137 studies published between 2018 and 2026 involving the Parrot Mambo, including studies where it appears alongside other UAV platforms. abstract: Rapid urbanization has altered rainfall–runoff processes in many cities and increased the hydraulic burden on urban drainage systems during short-duration, high-intensity storms. Taking a representative drainage system in Dongxihu District, Wuhan, as a case study, this study investigates urban waterlogging under a 20-year return-period design storm. An integrated 1D–2D hydrodynamic framework was established using EPA-SWMM and LISFLOOD-FP. abstract: Abstract Valorization of yak collagen byproducts offers a sustainable route to food-derived bioactive peptides. To prioritize candidate peptides from yak collagen-derived sequences, we developed AgeAttnMLP, an ESM-2-based screening model that achieved an AUC of 0.891 under conventional five-fold cross-validation and 0.879 under an additional cluster-aware grouped evaluation. title: Bay of Bengal cyclones fuel non-monsoon extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau, particularly outside the summer monsoon season, strongly affects glacier mass balance and downstream water availability, yet the moisture transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study combines high-resolution measurements of the isotopic composition of atmospheric water vapour at Nam Co Lake with isotope-enabled climate model simulations to investigate an extreme snowfall event on 25 October 2022. title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF ACI ). title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
abstract: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. abstract: Camera‐based computer vision remains the dominant approach to facial expression recognition (FER), but its performance depends on controlled conditions, including stable lighting, unobstructed views, and fixed camera angles, while continuous recording raises privacy concerns. Soft, skin‐conformable sensors offer an alternative by detecting facial muscle activity directly through mechanical deformation or biopotential signals. abstract: Summary Seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI) are important tools for investigating subsurface structures and properties. Open-source seismic modeling and inversion tools enable researchers to test new methods, reproduce published results, and use waveform data to characterize the subsurface. However, building flexible FWI workflows still requires substantial effort to integrate wave solvers, misfit functions, and inversion algorithms. title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. abstract: The customer experience of e-commerce logistics depends on the time limit for order fulfillment, and the late delivery risk should therefore be identified at the time of placing an order. This paper builds a distribution delay risk prediction framework based on XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting) and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations). abstract: Abstract This paper addresses high-precision tracking control for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems under the stringent requirement that the convergence time of the tracking error be explicitly preassigned by the user. To meet this requirement, a predefined-time sliding-mode control (PTSMC) scheme is developed. abstract: Advancing managed aquifer recharge (MAR) is critical towards tackling global freshwater shortages. In this study, layered geological horizons and engineered sorbent sinks were upscaled into a multilayer model to optimize passive underground desalination, using saline groundwater ( C 0 = 35000 mg/L) extracted from depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides a notion for the use of electroencephalography (EEG) in the field of cognitive science. In particular, we investigated the brain activity of operators while spotting the differences in similar‐looking pictures at three levels of difficulty. abstract: Abstract Multi-qubit gates are crucial to realizing quantum algorithms. Direct implementation of these gates will facilitate a reduction in circuit depth. However, existing model-based methods rely on precise characterization of the system Hamiltonian as well as execution of the control fields, which present challenges in obtaining high fidelity multi-qubit gates. abstract: Research on Arctic securitization centers on the Arctic states; non-Arctic observers have received less systematic attention. This article examines Germany, an Arctic Council observer since 1998, and asks how its official framing of the Arctic changed between 2013 and 2024. It applies qualitative comparative content analysis in MAXQDA to Germany’s three Arctic Policy Guidelines (2013, 2019, 2024). abstract: Accurate sowing-quality assessment of maize seedling trays requires both reliable seed localisation and correct correspondence between detected seeds and physical tray cells. This study presents a semi-automated machine-vision framework combining heatmap-based seed-centre localisation, sliding-window inference, global non-maximum suppression (NMS), and four-corner-calibrated adaptive grid assignment. abstract: Optimizing the mechanical properties of high‐carbon steels requires precise control over complex phase transformations driven by heat‐treatment pathways. abstract: This study examines 976 intangible cultural heritage items within the Pearl River Basin. It aims to reveal their static spatial distribution characteristics, dynamic evolution patterns, and influencing factors, laying a foundation for cultural preservation and regional sustainable development in the basin. abstract: Steel support structures for offshore energy platforms require large volumes of steel and complex manufacturing, making them one of the most expensive elements of any offshore project. Capital expenditure (CAPEX), which includes material procurement, manufacturing, transportation, and installation, typically makes up around 70% of the total lifecycle cost of these structures. abstract: Abstract Taste and odour (T&O) issues caused by geosmin and 2-MIB persist worldwide in drinking water. These compounds in freshwater reservoirs mainly stem from cyanobacterial activity, influenced by interactions among microbes, nutrients, and physical processes like stratification and redox cycling. abstract: ABSTRACT Global governance no longer confronts merely a democratic deficit but active delegitimation: International organizations are losing democratic member majorities and facing domestic politicization and defunding, whereas autocracies capture the vocabulary of democratization for statist ends. This article argues that under these conditions, the next step in global democratic design is a participation infrastructure that citizens and civil society can build without prior treaty change. abstract: Salmonella enterica remains a major foodborne pathogen in poultry-processing environments, where its persistence is largely attributed to biofilm formation on food-contact and non-food-contact surfaces. Despite extensive research on Salmonella control, persistent contamination continues to challenge food safety due to the complex interplay among isolate-specific traits, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). abstract: Against the backdrop of sustainable development and China’s Dual Carbon Goals, Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition continuously interact to shape urban sustainable development. abstract: Abstract This article examines the state of the art in AI literacy and STEM education and identifies emerging frontiers and research priorities to inspire cutting-edge empirical and theoretical research. The reviewed research is grounded in established AI literacy frameworks and shows that there is potential for students’ development of a critical and technologically informed AI literacy. abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of discharge observables in electrical wire explosions is challenging due to the inherent nonlinearities in plasma behavior, especially when experimental datasets are limited. This study presents a hybrid physics-informed modeling framework that combines analytical scaling laws with a reinforcement learning-based residual correction strategy to improve prediction accuracy across the charging-voltage range of 9.0–12.9 kV. abstract: The family Tetraodontidae comprises 193 valid species of teleost fish distributed in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. Available cytogenetic information for 31 species indicates extensive variability in diploid chromosome number (2n) ranging from 28 to 46. abstract: Bellandur Lake in Bangalore, India represents one of the most severely polluted urban water bodies in South Asia, necessitating systematic monitoring for environmental management. abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forests are becoming increasingly vulnerable to wildfires. Given this, there is an urgent need for accurate, high-resolution data on canopy fuel characteristics to facilitate fire behavior modeling and guide risk mitigation efforts. abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. abstract: The shipping industry is vital to global trade, with China’s ports leading in scale for years. This study assesses the resilience and economic impacts of tropical cyclones on five key Chinese ports, using Shanghai, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Xiamen, and Qinzhou as case studies. title: Trend Analysis and Prediction of Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) Change in General Santos City
abstract: This study analyzed land use and land cover (LULC) changes in General Santos City and predicted possible future LULC patterns for 2043 and 2063. It quantified changes in six LULC classes from 2003 to 2063 using a quantitative geospatial modeling approach. Landsat Imagery was the primary dataset, while validation points from historical imagery and spatial drivers, including aspect, elevation, slope, and distance to roads and rivers, were incorporated into the model. LULC maps were generated through supervised classification and validated through accuracy assessment before being used in the CA-A
journal: Research Frontiers International Journal of Social Science and Technology

title: Navigating High-Cost Supply Chains: A Tripartite Framework of Marketing, Digital, and HR Synergies in Emerging Economies
abstract: The structural inefficiencies and high costs inherent to supply chains in emerging economies necessitate a departure from isolated operational strategies. This study investigates the synergistic impact of a novel tripartite framework—comprising relationship marketing, digital engagement, and human resource (HR) synergy—on logistics operational efficiency within the archipelagic context of Indonesia. Employing a quantitative survey design, data were collected from 83 logistics professionals at a leading integrated multimodal transport enterprise and rigorously analyzed utilizing Structural Equa
journal: International Journal of Education Vocational and Social Science

title: Probing Atmospheric Gravity‐Wave‐Relevant Representations in a Weather Foundation Model via Multi‐Method Fine‐Tuning
abstract: Abstract Weather foundation models pretrained on reanalysis data may encode subgrid‐scale physics beyond their forecasting objectives. Using Aurora, we probe this with a multi‐method fine‐tuning framework: agreement across structurally different adaptation strategies signals shared backbone information, while a matched randomly initialized control isolates pretraining's contribution. We evaluate six methods (0.5%–100% of trainable parameters) for predicting ERA5‐resolved, T21‐filtered gravity‐wave momentum fluxes (313–1,820 km). Evidence for a pretraining benefit is strongest for the zonal flu

title: A balanced set of standardized affective environmental images for climate change research
abstract: Evocative visual imagery is central to research on affective pathways of environmental engagement, yet existing stimulus sets often overrepresent negative imagery and make it difficult to compare positive and negative affective responses under comparable conditions. We developed a balanced database of affective environmental images designed to support controlled comparisons of positive and negative environmental imagery. In total, 587 participants rated 203 images depicting consequences of unmitigated climate change and context-matched positive alternatives on pleasantness and activation. Part

title: SymbolFusion uses relation constraints in neurosymbolic graph learning to model literary structure and emotion trajectories
abstract: Abstract Literary texts contain recurring imagery, typed symbolic relations, and long-range emotion shifts that sequence models do not represent explicitly. This paper presents SymbolFusion, a relation-constrained neuro-symbolic graph framework that predicts imagery and symbolic candidates from raw text, validates three literary relation types through an auditable node-relation compatibility function, and propagates emotion only across valid graph paths. No gold symbolic or affective annotation is supplied during validation or testing. The 3,120-passage corpus is divided by literary work into

title: PELATIHAN PERAWATAN MOTOR TEMPEL KEPADA OPERATOR DAN AWAK KAPAL SUNGAI DI DESA MUARA PADANG KABUPATEN BANYUASIN
abstract: Keandalan motor tempel merupakan salah satu faktor penting dalam mendukung keselamatan dan keberlangsungan operasional kapal sungai. Keterbatasan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal dalam melakukan perawatan preventif dapat meningkatkan risiko gangguan mesin selama pelayaran. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan operator serta awak kapal sungai dalam melakukan pemeriksaan dan perawatan dasar motor tempel. Kegiatan dilaksanakan oleh Politeknik Transportasi Sungai, Danau, dan Penyeberangan Palembang di Gedung Serba
institutions: Politeknik Transportasi Sungai, Danau, dan Penyeberangan Palembang

title: Fuzzy logic and frequency ratio based landslide susceptibility mapping using geo environmental and hydro meteorological factors in pithoragarh, uttarakhand
abstract: Mass movement events leads to severe infrastructural and socioeconomic damage across the Himalayan belt, particularly in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, India, where over nearly 1,000 events have been recorded in the last two decades. Modelling landslide susceptibility in such highly several, monsoon dominated terrains requires frameworks capable of handling significant spatial and lithological uncertainty. This study assesses and map out regional landslide vulnerability using a Multi Criteria Decision Analysis methodology based on fuzzy logic and frequency ratio. A spatial database comprising fourt

title: When the Night Stops Cooling: Modeling Extreme Warm Nights Across California Weather Stations
abstract: This paper investigates which factors influence extreme warm nights across California using NOAA GHCN-Daily station observations. We defined extreme warm nights using station-specific 95th percentile summer TMIN thresholds based on a historical baseline period. For each station-year, the percentage of valid summer nights classified as extreme warm nights was calculated. A random forest regression model was then used to explore the effect of year, latitude, longitude, elevation, and distance to coast on extreme warm-night frequency. title: Domain adaptation affects adversarial robustness in autonomous steering models
abstract: Abstract Domain adaptation is commonly used to transfer autonomous steering models across regions with different road configurations, such as from right-hand to left-hand traffic. While prior work has largely evaluated adaptation using clean target-domain steering accuracy, its effect on adversarial robustness remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluates two steering architectures, PilotNet and ResNet-18, under four adaptation strategies: U.S.-trained, flipped U.S.-trained, U.S.-trained + fine-tuned, and flipped U.S.-trained + fine-tuned. title: Source-only cross-year prediction of perceived AI capability with a theory-anchored, loss-specific two-stage model
abstract: Introduction Understanding how developers judge AI's ability to handle complex tasks can help organizations monitor attitudes toward AI at work. Repeated surveys provide an opportunity to study these judgments, but models used across years must combine useful prediction with clear interpretation of the roles of trust and favorability toward AI. Adding work-related information or changing the prediction objective can alter the coefficients used to describe those relationships. This study examines whether these goals can be separated using Theory-Anchored Residual Surface learning (TARS). Method

title: SPECIFICATION SENSITIVITY IN URBAN AIR-QUALITY FORECASTING AND SIMULATED CONTROL
abstract: Model comparisons in urban air-quality forecasting can be sensitive to choices in data preparation and evaluation. We examine this sensitivity using a neural continuous-time model and nine baselines on 59,628 hours of composite air quality index (AQI) observations from Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata. A separate traffic–pollution simulator examines reward-weight sensitivity in proximal policy optimisation (PPO).
