title: Latent Structure in Chess Positions
abstract: En este trabajo entrenamos autoencoders para entender representaciones latentes de posiciones de ajedrez. Utilizamos una base de datos de partidas de Lichess filtradas por nivel de juego y control de tiempo, y representamos cada posición como un tensor de múltiples canales. Entrenamos un autoencoder para reconstruir dichas posiciones y posteriormente analizamos el espacio latente mediante Análisis de Componentes Principales (PCA). Nuestros resultados muestran que las primeras componentes capturan información relevante del juego, tales como el enroque y las características de la apertura. Reali
institutions: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

title: Dip-aligned structural constraints for suppression of partially coherent seismic noise using self-supervised learning
abstract: Summary Partially coherent noise, including swell and scattered noise, remains difficult to suppress because its spatial correlation and structural similarity to reflection events reduce the effectiveness of methods that assume random, incoherent, or stationary noise. This problem is particularly challenging for self-supervised blind-spot denoising, where correlated noise can violate the independence assumptions used to separate signal from noise. title: Reptiles in the One Health ecology of antimicrobial resistance, with insights into zoonotic pathogens: reservoirs, transmission pathways, and public health implications
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge at the interface of human, animal, and environmental health. Reptiles—including wild populations, pets, farmed species, and internationally traded animals—are increasingly recognized as participants in One Health AMR networks, occupying ecological interfaces that facilitate interactions among wildlife, domestic animals, humans, and the environment. Their diverse microbiota and exposure to both natural and anthropogenically influenced habitats create opportunities for the acquisition and dissemination of antimicrobial-resistant bacte

title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists
abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

title: Benchmarking time-series foundation models for multitask predictive maintenance in digital twins
abstract: Digital twins provide a comprehensive virtual representation of physical assets, distinguishing themselves from traditional control systems through long-term diagnostic and prognostic capabilities. However, current digital twin architectures face a critical scalability barrier: they rely on dedicated, single-purpose models for every distinct query, task, physical scale, and operating context, resulting in unsustainable engineering overhead. To address this limitation, there is an urgent need for flexible, general-purpose analytical backbones capable of interpreting diverse time-series data wit

title: Hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling processes, and irrigation suitability assessment of groundwater in the Sanjiang Plain, China
abstract: Abstract Groundwater is vital for global irrigation water supply, and its quality directly affects sustainable agricultural development. However, studies on irrigation water quality and its dominant controlling factors in semi-humid regions remain limited. Therefore, taking the Sanjiang Plain as a case, hydrochemical analysis, irrigation water quality assessment, and multivariate statistical methods were employed to systematically reveal the hydrogeochemical characteristics, irrigation suitability, and their dominant controlling mechanisms. institutions: Heilongjiang Vocational Institute of Ecological Engineering

title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
abstract: Abstract Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. title: Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways
abstract: Abstract. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash-flood research. By integrating bibliometric and topic analyses with qualitative synthesis, we reveal pronounced geographical and thematic imbalances, with research concentrated in Europe and Asia. journal: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research

title: Modeling and optimization of battery-based energy storage systems for UAVs
abstract: The paper presents the improvement of the energy efficiency of drones used in different missions. In this paper, a model for Li-ion batteries is created, made through equivalent electrical circuits. This method facilitates the examination of the relationship between the required energy consumption and the electrical response of the battery to demands. title: Electrochemical Detection of PFAS Contaminants Across Environmental and Pharmaceutical Matrices:Sensing Mechanisms, Nanomaterial Platforms, Biological Monitoring, and Regulatory Convergence
abstract: PFAS are a class of over 14,000 synthetic compounds characterized by a stable carbon-fluorine bond that confers resistance to thermal and biological degradation, resulting in common contamination of various aquatic matrices at concentrations ranging from sub-parts per trillion to parts per billion.Demand for directly deployable sensitive quantification methods has been spurred by increasingly stringent regulatory responses such as the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposed maximum contaminant levels of 4 ppt for PFOA and PFOS in 2024 under its third Fourth Unregulated Contaminant
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell equipped with an amplification system coupled with a secondary PV ‐assisted module: Utilization as eco‐sustainable electrical power supply for carbon monoxide gas sensor
abstract: Abstract Autonomous environmental telemetry requires continuous, maintenance‐free power sources capable of driving commercial sensing electronics. This study reports the development of a self‐powered bio‐electrochemical sensing platform utilizing a garden soil‐based microbial fuel cell (s‐MFC) coupled with a hybrid power management system (PMS) to drive a commercial off‐the‐shelf (COTS) carbon monoxide (CO) gas sensor. title: Analytical Noise-Variance Assessment of Receiver-Side Optical Filtering for Background-Noise Mitigation in Free-Space Optical Communication under Atmospheric Turbulence
abstract: Receiver-side optical filtering trades useful-signal attenuation against noise suppression in free-space optical communication. We analyse a 40 Gbps, 1.54 km OptiSystem link at 1552.52 nm using six filter responses. A normalized variance metric combines received power and signal-to-noise ratio. IIR, Gaussian and Bessel responses increase Q from 6.94 to 8.81–8.94 and signal-to-noise ratio from 16.83 to 18.90–19.03 dB. journal: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Transportation Systems and Ocean Engineering

title: What do we mean by consistency in weather forecasts?
abstract: Abstract Many sectors rely upon weather information, yet raw numerical weather prediction (NWP) output alone is rarely sufficient to support real‐world decisions. Post‐processing has therefore been developed to make NWP data more usable. However, different post‐processing approaches produce data with different properties, preserving some kinds of consistency while discarding others. At present, it is difficult to discuss these techniques clearly because there is no shared understanding of what is meant by consistency. title: Geospatially interpretable long-term flood risk assessment using integrated weighting and LightGBM–SHAP
abstract: Long-term flood risk assessment is vital for identifying persistent hazard-prone areas and supporting risk-informed spatial planning in rapidly urbanising regions. This study developed an interpretable geospatial framework integrating AHP, LightGBM–SHAP, and reliability-weighted game-theoretic weight fusion for the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region using annual flood-related dataset for 2001–2025. Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences

title: Decoupling Gauge Factor and Baseline Resistance Through Crack–Percolation Hybrid Design for Flexible Multimodal Strain Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible strain sensors for wearable systems, soft robotics, and distributed electronics exhibit a coupling between gauge factor (GF) and baseline resistance (R 0 ), as both depend on a structural parameter, limiting independent control of sensitivity and electrical characteristics. Here, a single‐walled carbon nanotubes (SWNT)/SU‐8/cracked‐polydimethyl‐siloxane (PDMS) (SSC) platform is introduced to decouple GF and R 0 through two independent fabrication parameters. title: Efficient real-time vehicle tracking via lightweight YOLO and DeepSORT integration
abstract: Detecting and tracking vehicles ahead during driving is a critical technology for ensuring driving safety and enhancing the driving experience. However, traditional detection and tracking models often suffer from high computational intensity and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. This paper introduces a lightweight vehicle tracking model that integrates YOLO and DeepSORT. title: Cryptography-Based Large Language Model Watermarking and Its E-commerce Applications
abstract: With the widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs), security traceability, copyright protection, and compliance regulation of their generated content have become critical issues requiring urgent resolution. While LLM watermarking technology holds promise for addressing these issues, existing research primarily focuses on theoretical construction in general scenarios, lacking adaptability exploration for vertical industries. title: Copper and zinc from slurry applications shape grassland soil microbial community structure in a long-term experiment
abstract: Soil microbes are crucial in maintaining soil and plant health, underpinning agronomic productivity. This study investigates antimicrobial copper- and zinc-laden cow and pig slurry applications on soil microbial community structures in an approximately 50-year long-term slurry experiment on a permanent grassland located in County Down, Northern Ireland. Illumina and PacBio rRNA sequencing (analysing 16S and ITS genera) were used to investigate soil samples (to 15 cm depth) from the experiment’s treatments. title: A hybrid ice hydrometeor retrieval algorithm for submillimeter-wave radiometers in support of the PolSIR and PMM missions
abstract: Abstract. This paper presents an ice hydrometeor retrieval algorithm for submillimeter-wave radiometers in support of the upcoming PolSIR (Polarized Submillimeter Ice Cloud Radiometer) and PMM (Precipitation Measuring Mission) satellite missions. The algorithm employs a hybrid Bayesian Monte Carlo Integration (BMCI) and Optimal Estimation Method (OEM) approach, which leverages the strengths of the BMCI method but extends the retrieval capability beyond the limitations of the a priori database when BMCI alone fails to identify enough database cases matching the observations. title: An informatics workflow for label-scarce cross-domain segmentation of geological outcrop fractures from UAV photogrammetric imagery
abstract: Abstract Accurate extraction of geological outcrop fracture networks from UAV photogrammetric imagery supports rock-mass characterization, discontinuity mapping, and geotechnical interpretation. However, automated segmentation remains challenging because fractures are often thin, low-contrast, discontinuous, and visually confused with heterogeneous textures, weathering patterns, and shadows. Pixel-level annotation is also labor-intensive, resulting in limited labeled data for newly surveyed areas. title: A web development method for transmission line O&M components based on multi-source data sensing and deep reinforcement learning algorithms
abstract: Transmission corridors in high-altitude and micro-topographic regions are chronically subjected to strong electromagnetic pulse interference, multi-physics field coupling, and extreme climatic stressors. This results in temporal asynchrony and spatial mismatch in multi-source monitoring data, while environmental disturbances cause confidence drift in single data sources. Furthermore, traditional O&M systems lack topological awareness and dynamic decision-making capabilities, leading to disruptions in the O&M process chain. title: An improved remora optimization algorithm for optimizing a support vector machine based network anomaly traffic detection model
abstract: To improve the detection performance of anomalous network traffic, a network anomaly traffic detection model was developed by integrating an improved Remora Optimization Algorithm (IROA) with Support Vector Machine (SVM). Specifically, the White Shark Optimizer was incorporated into the host-switching mechanism of the Remora Optimization Algorithm to enhance global exploration. An adaptive weight operator was adopted to refine the experiential attack process, thus improving the convergence accuracy. title: Shallow Arctic delta lakes develop open water stratification, sub-thermocline oxygen supersaturation, and winter chemoclines that resist mixing at ice-off
abstract: Cool, shallow lakes have historically been treated as simplified limnologic systems that readily mix vertically during open water. Arctic delta lakes are generally shallow and are understudied in comparison to other arctic lakes and differ hydrologically and biogeochemically. However, recent work shows that even shallow Arctic lakes can develop densimetric stratification. Open water vertical mixing was assessed among two lakes in the Mackenzie Delta with similar areas but differing depths (1.7 m and 3.2 m). title: Interpretable Symbolic Regression Modelling of Stacking Sequence Effects in Jute/Ramie and Jute/Flax Hybrid Composites
abstract: In this study, a symbolic regression-based framework was developed to investigate the tensile and flexural behavior of natural fiber-reinforced hybrid composites with different stacking sequences. Experimental data from eleven six-layer laminates, including jute, ramie, flax, jute/ramie, and jute/flax configurations, were reanalyzed. Due to the limited dataset size, the proposed approach was considered an exploratory and interpretable modelling framework rather than a universal predictive model. title: Abrupt permafrost thaw overwhelms vegetation-driven erosion reduction in sediment export on the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Vegetation greening and abrupt permafrost thaw are reshaping sediment dynamics across the Tibetan Plateau, yet their relative effects on sediment delivery remain poorly quantified. Here we show that retrogressive thaw slumps are disproportionately important sediment sources, with erosion rates two to three orders of magnitude above undisturbed landscapes and source-to-channel connectivity generally exceeding 60%. title: A Standardized Chewable Conductive Hydrogel Sensor for Direct Monitoring of Masticatory Dynamics
abstract: ABSTRACT Chewing is a fundamental orofacial function closely related to nutrition, digestion, and quality of life, yet current assessment methods generally rely on indirect signals or endpoint measurements and provide limited process‐level information. Here, a hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC)/polyacrylamide (PAM) conductive hydrogel is developed as a standardized chewable sensor that integrates the test substrate with force‐to‐electrical signal transduction, enabling direct monitoring of masticatory dynamics. title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State‐Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge‐intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision‐making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. title: Reconstructing multi-temporal Glacier area changes to improve mass balance estimates in the Southeastern Tibetan Plateau (2000–2025)
abstract: The southeastern Tibetan Plateau (SETP), a critical component of the “Asian Water Tower”, hosts a large concentration of maritime temperate glaciers that are highly sensitive to climate change. However, persistent cloud cover, seasonal snow, and supraglacial debris complicate consistent long-term glacier mapping, while the use of static glacier boundaries may introduce temporal mismatches in altimetry-based glacier mass-change estimates. title: PaE:Adeep reinforcement learning-based two-level online solution for uncertain moving-target traveling salesman problems
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates an uncertain Moving-Target Traveling Salesman Problem (MT-TSP), in which the future motion trajectories of targets are uncertain. The objective is to maximize the number of visited targets within a bounded region while minimizing the total travel distance. To address the challenges introduced by dynamic target maneuvers, we propose a two-level online solution framework, termed PaE (Plan and Execute), which leverages the current observations of targets to solve the problem in real time. title: Evolution of Architectural Design: A Historical Analysis of the Rivers State Government House from Independence to Present
abstract: The architectural transformation of the Rivers State Government House serves as a lens for examining the interplay between political authority, historical influence, and cultural identity in Nigeria. This study traces the evolution of its design from colonial-era structures to modern government complexes, analysing how governance, modernisation, and external architectural trends have shaped its development. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) cultivation in India: A critical review of status, constraints and future directions
abstract: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is an economically important berry crop worldwide, due to its distinctive flavour, nutritional value and health benefits. In recent years, it has been cultivated not only in temperate regions, but also in subtropical and tropical regions. It has become one of the high-value horticultural crops in India, due to the growing consumer demand and good returns to farmers. title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study
abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). institutions: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: Green English language teaching approach to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls
abstract: The present study examined the effect of using green English pedagogy to develop critical reading skills and environmental awareness among secondary school students for girls. Sixty Jordanian grade 9 EFL students participated in the present study. They were enrolled in the Serfa secondary school for girls, education directorate of Lwa'a Al-Qasr. The participants were assigned as control and experimental groups. title: Spatio-temporal distribution of microplastics in the protected transboundary Thaya/Dyje River (Central Europe): implications of hydrological connectivity for microplastic monitoring
abstract: Microplastic (MP) concentrations in rivers are highly dynamic, varying across space, depth, and hydrological conditions, yet conventional monitoring approaches often capture only a fraction of this variability. This study investigated the spatio-temporal distribution of microplastics along a 30 km reach of the hydrologically regulated Thaya/Dyje River within the transboundary Thayatal/Podyjí National Park. title: Wind Power Scenario Generation Based on Dual‐Domain Generator and Improved Spectral Bias Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: Scene generation is a core technology for quantifying wind power uncertainty. Addressing issues such as insufficient scene realism and low spectral matching accuracy in traditional generation models, this paper proposes a frequency domain generative adversarial network (FD‐GAN) method for wind power scene generation based on a dual‐domain generator and improved spectral deviation. journal: IEEJ Transactions on Electrical and Electronic Engineering

title: Analysis of the effects of different protease types on volatile compounds and oxidative properties of blackthroat seaperch ( Doederleinia berycoides ) liver oil
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of different proteases on the extraction, flavor profile, and oxidative stability of blackthroat seaperch (Doederleinia berycoides) liver oil obtained by aqueous enzymatic extraction. Trypsin-assisted extraction yielded oil with the greatest oxidative stability. Combined analysis by gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified aldehydes as the characteristic volatile compounds in the liver oil. title: Design of an IoT-Based Electrical and Automatic Conveyor System for a Floating Waste Collector
abstract: Floating waste accumulation in rivers, lakes, and urban waterways has become a persistent environmental problem that requires efficient and low-cost collection technologies. This study aims to design and implement an Internet of Things (IoT)-based electrical and automatic conveyor system for a floating waste collector prototype. title: A dual-enhanced random forest model for fatigue life prediction under multi-level variable amplitude loading
abstract: To address two limitations (hyperparameter sensitivity and black-box fitting) of random forest (RF) models in predicting fatigue life under multi-level variable amplitude loading, a dual-enhanced random forest model (Dual-ERF) is proposed. First, Q-Learning reinforcement learning is introduced to improve the Langevin Equation Evolution (LEE) model, forming the Q-LEE model. title: Mycosphere microbiome assembly and metabolic reprogramming in Phallus rugulosus revealed by multi-omics integration
abstract: The mycosphere, defined as the soil zone influenced by fungal hyphae, hosts a distinct microbiome that plays a critical role in host development. Nevertheless, the assembly rules and metabolic functions in macrofungi remain poorly understood. This study aims to disentangle these processes in the edible fungus Phallus rugulosus . We integrated metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics to compare mycosphere soil (MS) and bulk soil (BS) of P. rugulosus . title: Application of the fuzzy analytical hierarchy process for flood vulnerability assessment in Sylhet District, Bangladesh
abstract: Floods are among the most frequent and destructive natural hazards, and their frequency and intensity have increased under recent climatic and environmental changes. Sylhet District is one of the most flood-vulnerable regions of Bangladesh, where riparian and low-lying communities face recurrent flood-related challenges. This study assesses flood vulnerability in Sylhet District using the Fuzzy analytical hierarchy process (Fuzzy AHP), a multi-criteria decision-making technique that improves conventional AHP by incorporating uncertainty and ambiguity in expert judgment. abstract: This study jointly evaluated physicochemical and microbiological water-quality data from 16 samples collected at the Dicle Dam intake structure in January, March, June, and September between 2022 and 2025, together with the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) and Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) derived from Sentinel-2A imagery. title: THE ROLE OF ENGLISH IN MODERN EDUCATION
abstract: This article highlights the relevance and importance of learning foreign languages in the modern world and education system. In the process of globalization, international cooperation, the development of science and technology are making knowledge of foreign languages an important competence. The article analyzes the role of learning foreign languages in personal development, academic success and intercultural communication. It also considers issues of increasing the effectiveness of language learning through the use of innovative methods and information technologies in the educational process

title: Design and Validation of an Automated X-Ray Imaging System for Pipe Weld Inspection
abstract: X-ray imaging is widely used for the inspection of welded pipes to detect internal defects such as discontinuities and weld imperfections. In this study, an automated X-ray imaging system capable of performing internal or external inspection depending on pipe diameter was designed and analyzed. Prior to the design stage, a site survey was conducted to determine system layout and material handling conditions, confirming the use of an overhead crane for pipe feeding. title: Numerical Simulation of Temperature Moisture Field for Cylindrical Chinese Herbal Medicines During Preheating balancing Stage of Hot air Drying
abstract: Aiming at the preheating balancing process in hot air drying of cylindrical Chinese herbal medicines, a one-dimensional radial cylindrical heat mass transfer numerical model is established to reveal the evolution law of internal temperature and moisture content within short time scale. The conservative finite volume method is adopted for spatial discretization, and the Crank Nicolson implicit scheme combined with the Thomas algorithm is used to solve the equations. title: Process structure property correlation and multi response optimization of friction stir welded copper joints
abstract: Abstract Friction stir welding (FSW) of copper is challenging due to its high thermal conductivity, which complicates heat management and joint integrity. This study investigates the process–structure–property relationship in FSW of 5 mm thick commercially pure copper plates using a conventional vertical milling machine as a cost-effective alternative to dedicated FSW systems. title: Seismic resilience of high-rise buildings: optimizing active tuned mass dampers with advanced control strategies considering soil-structure interaction
abstract: This paper investigates the seismic control of a 40-story high-rise building equipped with a Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) and an Active Tuned Mass Damper (ATMD) while considering Soil–Structure Interaction (SSI) effects. The structure is evaluated under four foundation conditions, including fixed-base, soft-soil, medium-soil, and dense-soil cases. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to optimize the design parameters of the TMD and ATMD systems, including the mass ratio, frequency ratio, damping ratio, and, for the ATMD, the control gain of the New Algorithm (NA). title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
abstract: Abstract. The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for identifying and quantifying precipitation. Hence, SMLs can serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementary to conventional instruments. However, a significant challenge for opportunistic sensors, such as SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart, i.e., commercial microwave links (CMLs), stems from potential ownership issues, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. title: Propagating meteorological uncertainty in physically based mountain snow modeling
abstract: Abstract. Snow estimation in mountainous regions is uncertain because meteorology varies with topography, in situ observations are sparse and biased, and snow models have structural and scale limitations. Probabilistic methods are increasingly recognized as essential for quantifying and propagating these uncertainties in hydrological assessment. This study generates meteorological forcing ensembles designed for mountainous terrain and applies them for probabilistic, physically based snow modeling. institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: Within‐lake length adjustment improves otolith shape discrimination among lake trout Salvelinus namaycush populations
abstract: Distinguishing fish populations is a long-standing challenge in fisheries management, and otolith shape provides a low-cost marker of population structure. Fish size strongly influences otolith shape; however, within-lake size variation can obscure differences among populations. Here, a within-lake length adjustment of otolith elliptic Fourier descriptors increased the otolith shape differences detected among three populations of Manitoban lake trout Salvelinus namaycush (n = 153). title: Isolating the exposomic impact of acute war and displacement within chronic crisis using multimodal, AI-enabled phenotyping
abstract: Abstract Wars often unfold within contexts of prolonged instability, yet little is known about how acute conflicts interact with cumulative exposomic adversity to shape mental health processes. Here we studied clinical and subclinical symptoms in a Lebanese sample across three groups—one assessed before the 2024 war and two assessed after, with or without displacement—within a shared background of chronic crises. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: IoT-enabled individual poultry monitoring with lightweight step-counting for health assessment
abstract: To address the challenges of quantifying individual physical activity, delayed detection of health anomalies in high-density environments, and the lack of objective data supporting welfare-oriented farming in large-scale floor-rearing poultry farms, this paper proposes and implements an Internet of Things-based system for individual poultry behavior monitoring and digital management. The system consists of three core components: an energy-efficient smart anklet, a solar-powered multi-modal communication base station, and a cloud management platform. title: Entropy guided spectral phenological feature engineering using Sentinel-2A data for Pan-Arctic vegetation classification
abstract: Arctic vegetation plays a critical role in regulating terrestrial ecosystem structure and function. Existing remote-sensing classification products are often limited in thematic detail and accuracy because of the region’s inaccessibility and the underuse of high-dimensional spectral and phenological information. This study established a Pan-Arctic vegetation classification system comprising Barren Tundra (BT), Sparse Tundra (ST), Cyperaceae Tundra (CT), Graminoid Tundra (GT), Wet Tundra (WT), Grass, and Shrub. Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography

title: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. title: ALTFN: a novel unsupervised domain adaptation bearing fault diagnosis framework using joint global and local information
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an Adaptive Lightweight Time-Frequency Network (ALTFN) to address insufficient fault feature representation and degraded generalization performance under varying working conditions. ALTFN integrates Adaptive Time-Frequency Transformer (ATFT) and Depthwise Separable Convolution (DSC) into a dual-branch architecture to achieve joint global-local representation learning. title: Model-based and neural-aided approaches for dog dead reckoning
abstract: Modern canine applications span medical and service roles, while robotic legged dogs serve as autonomous platforms for high-risk industrial inspection, disaster response, and search and rescue operations. For both, accurate positioning remains a significant challenge due to the cumulative drift inherent in inertial sensing. To bridge this gap, we propose three algorithms for accurate positioning using only inertial sensors, collectively referred to as dog dead reckoning (DDR). title: Wheat in Crisis: Variability of Wheat Area in Lebanon 2017–2025
abstract: Wheat is a vital staple crop worldwide. However, its production has been increasingly challenged in Lebanon in recent years by multi-factorial crises intersecting socio-economic, political, security, and climate factors. This study provides the first national, multi-year monitoring of wheat area in Lebanon (2017–2025), linking satellite observations with crisis impacts. We conducted a multi-temporal supervised classification across the 2017–2018 to 2024–2025 seasons, using Google Earth Engine, Sentinel-2 imagery, and Random Forest classifier, achieving an 87% overall accuracy. title: Optimization of multi-echelon multi-product supply chains using discrete event simulation
abstract: This study details the application of a novel multi-echelon, multi-product hybrid supply chain optimization framework known as the Optimizing Known Warehouses (OKW) framework, which consists of mathematical and computer simulation models, to analyze the effects of changes in inventory policies for products delivered by two (2) different case-study manufacturing supply chains. The methods used are the Bayesian optimization algorithm and linear programming to optimize inventory and routing in the supply chains. title: The microbial aerial thread: co-restoring source and sink across dryland-urban gradients
abstract: Dryland ecosystems serve as major sources of atmospheric bioaerosols through aeolian transport of dust-associated microorganisms. These microbial communities are dispersed across vast distances, connecting dryland soils and vegetation to distant recipient ecosystems, particularly urban areas. This review synthesizes current understanding of microbial ecology in arid soils, microbial dispersal through dust, and interactions with urban ecosystems. title: Winter wheat yield prediction using temporal fusion of multispectral imagery and LiDAR point clouds acquired from a ground-based phenotyping platform
abstract: Winter wheat yield reflects the combined development of canopy structure and physiological status, making multitemporal structural and spectral observations potentially valuable for pre-maturity prediction. We used a ground-based phenotyping platform to acquire five-band multispectral imagery at 14 growth stages and LiDAR point clouds at 10 growth stages. title: Database-Pipeline Interactions Shape Taxonomic Inference in 16S rRNA Bacterial Community Profiling
abstract: Abstract High-throughput sequencing has transformed microbiome study by enabling cost-efficient, high-resolution profiling of microbial communities using 16S rRNA gene amplicons. Despite its widespread adoption, taxonomic inference remains highly dependent on the choice of reference database and bioinformatic pipeline. To provide a systematic benchmark, we evaluated three widely used 16S rRNA reference databases, Greengenes2 (GG2, v2022.10), SILVA 138.1, and RDP19, across representative analytical workflows, including QIIME2 (Q2; full-length and V4 classifiers) and a USEARCH/VSEARCH-based pipe

title: Pan-genomics in One Health: linking pathogens, hosts, and environments
abstract: The One Health approach recognizes the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health for managing global health challenges. The increasing incidence of zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and environmental degradation underscores the relevance of integrated surveillance strategies. In this context, pan-genomics has emerged as a valuable tool for characterizing the genetic diversity of bacterial pathogens across hosts, geographic regions, and ecological niches. By distinguishing core from accessory genome components, pan-genomic analyses inform vaccine target identificatio

title: Distribution of Microplastics in Freshwater Mussels across a Watershed
abstract: Microplastic research is an emerging field of study, and we do not yet fully understand the scope or effects of microplastic pollution. Microplastics are ubiquitous in the environment, but the field suffers from a lack of unified, accessible protocols and an ecosystems approach to evaluating microplastic contamination. During autumn 2020, we collected water, mussel, and sediment samples from five sites along the Yadkin–Pee Dee River Basin, North Carolina. title: The roof grouting and active support technology of roadways based on stratified mining
abstract: Abstract This study aims to enhance roadway support effectiveness and construction efficiency. The study proposes a synergistic technology integrating roof grouting with active support techniques in stratified mining environments, enhanced by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms that adaptively optimize grouting parameters in real time. A mechanical model of a roadway in stratified mining is established, along with a grouting parameter optimization framework based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG). title: A lightweight YOLO based framework for real-time seat belt detection in intelligent traffic surveillance
abstract: Abstract Road accidents remain a major cause of fatalities worldwide, and proper seat belt usage significantly reduces the risk of severe injuries and death. Ensuring compliance through automated traffic surveillance systems is therefore essential; however, reliable real-time detection remains challenging due to illumination variations, occlusions, windshield reflections, and low contrast between seat belts and vehicle interiors. title: Post-use evaluation of Beijing's Second Green Belt country parks based on LSTM model analysis
abstract: The country parks in Beijing’s Second Green Belt are important to urban green space expansion and recreation. Therefore, exploring park visitors’ real needs and expectations has practical significance. Online review data and the LSTM model were used to analyze and systemically study four aspects of the country park – location layout, landscape environment, functional service, and physical and mental perception. title: A data-driven method coupling multiple physical constraints for correcting structural errors in groundwater contaminant transport models
abstract: Abstract. Model structural errors are pervasive in groundwater contaminant transport modeling under complex environmental conditions, hindering accurate prediction of contamination transport. Data-driven methods (DDMs) coupled with physical constraints provide an effective approach for correcting structural errors and improving prediction. title: Operational-Response-Aware Two-Stage Stochastic Scheduling of Renewable Port Microgrids under Arrival-Driven Congestion and Demand Amplification
abstract: Electrified container ports are coupled logistics–energy systems in which uncertain vessel arrivals determine berth occupancy, shore-power activation, cargo-handling intensity, and the residual demand balanced by renewable generation, battery storage, and the utility grid. This study develops a scenario-based stochastic framework linking a non-homogeneous vessel-arrival process to queue-consistent berth occupancy, congestion-responsive demand, photovoltaic and wind uncertainty, battery dispatch, and grid exchange. title: Linking Active Madden–Julian Oscillation to High–Very High Rainfall During Large-Scale Flood Events in Banten and Jakarta
abstract: The modulation of rainfall extremes by the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) over Indonesia and the Maritime Continent is well established, but less is known about how consistently this relationship is represented in documented large-scale flood-impact records. This study provides an event-based assessment of active MJO phases 3–5 on high–very high (HVH) rainfall associated with large-scale flood events across seasonal rainfall zones (ZOMs). title: Impact-based flood-damage assessment in Japan under longitudinal typhoon-track perturbations and levee-height variations during Hagibis (2019)
abstract: Abstract Impact-based flood-damage assessment integrates hydrometeorological information with vulnerability and exposure data to generate comprehensive evaluation of flood damage. This study uses the Integrated Land Simulator to assemble an impact-based flood-damage assessment framework for Typhoon Hagibis (2019), one of the most powerful typhoons to strike Japan in recent years. To systematically evaluate how typhoon-track position and levee height influence flood damage, we conduct longitudinal typhoon-track perturbation experiments and levee-height variation scenario analyses. title: Quantifying Geodiversity in the State of Rio de Janeiro Using a Spatial Grid-Based Approach
abstract: Abstract This article presents a quantitative geodiversity assessment of Rio de Janeiro State using spatial analysis methods applying hexagonal grids and cartographic processing at multiple resolutions. Geodiversity is the variability, relationships, and assemblages of geological, geomorphological, pedological, and hydrological components and processes. It is fundamental in natural sciences, as it supports biodiversity and society by delivering ecosystem services and shaping the natural and cultural environments. title: Optimization of Drying Parameters of Periwinkles ( Turritella Communis) Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Optimization of drying parameters of periwinkles (Turritella communis) using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to obtain high quality product, it is very vital as improper drying conditions can affect the composition of the dried Periwinkles and thereby increases the risk of it running into deterioration of the nutrient contents of the product and post-harvest loss. Periwinkles were processed by washing, sorting into required weight (1kg). journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY

title: Operating-Condition-Aware Fault Diagnosis of Variable-Speed Aviation Piston Pumps Using Interpretable Multi-Domain Features
abstract: In variable-speed aviation piston pumps, changes in rotational speed, flow demand, and load can shift fault-related spectral content and make fixed-frequency features sensitive to operating condition. This study evaluates an operating-condition-aware and physically interpretable diagnostic procedure using open experimental data from a nine-piston swashplate-type aviation piston pump. title: Practical Prescribed‐Time Control for Strict‐Feedback Nonlinear Systems Subject to Sensor Faults and Input Saturation
abstract: ABSTRACT This article proposes a novel and practical prescribed time control (PPTC) method for strict feedback nonlinear systems (SFNSs) subject to input saturation and sensor faults. This method fills the research gap in existing literature, which only addresses a single constraint (either input saturation or sensor faults) rather than their simultaneous occurrence. title: Scale‐space image analysis for mapping spotted knapweed in grassland ecosystems
abstract: Premise: This study investigates the value of scale-space representations of spatial features for the identification and mapping of invasive plants using high-resolution multispectral imagery. Scale-space representations combine the two-dimensional spatial domain with a third dimension representing spatial scale, such that features can be represented across both space and image spatial resolution. title: Informing the public about earthquakes in Canada: exploring the application of a new geocommunication model
abstract: Canadian geoscience initiatives include the research of natural hazards, their potential impacts on people, infrastructure, and the environment, and how these impacts might be mitigated. Engagement activities and educational resources are often an important component of such endeavours. Earthquake-related programs, in particular, are the focus of the work presented here. For instance, Canada has a new Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) system, which was activated in western British Columbia (BC) in 2024 and in eastern Ontario and southern Quebec in 2025. title: Seasonal wetting and drying dynamics drive greenhouse gas emissions across Australia’s river network
abstract: Streams and rivers are major contributors to global emissions of carbon dioxide and methane, yet seasonal hydrological variability in discharge and river surface area is often not fully represented in large-scale emission estimates. Here, we integrate riverine and dry riverbed carbon dioxide and methane data with geospatial data of the Australian drainage network to predict emissions at a monthly time-step. title: A meteorological big data-driven method for generating chaotic time-series curves of power supply loads for wind-solar-storage hybrid systems
abstract: The wind-solar-storage hybrid system represents an efficient and clean energy supply mode. However, its power supply load is influenced by multiple factors and exhibits complex chaotic time-series characteristics, which pose significant challenges to system operation scheduling and load forecasting. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method for generating chaotic time-series curves of the power supply load in such hybrid systems based on meteorological big data. title: From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. title: Joint optimization of inland waterway methanol bunkering station siting and vessel operations with cross-port bunkering
abstract: The early-stage deployment of green methanol-powered inland vessels faces a fundamental infrastructure dilemma: limited vessel cruising range increases the need for en-route bunkering, whereas spatially dispersed demand makes dense construction of fixed bunkering stations economically burdensome. Existing inland bunkering-network studies largely associate fuel supply capability with fixed facility nodes, leaving the potential of mobile bunkering services to reshape infrastructure deployment insufficiently explored. title: Ecological Governance as Niche Diplomacy: South Korea's Engagement with the Lower Mekong Basin
abstract: Drought, saltwater intrusion, and biodiversity loss are only part of the problem facing the Lower Mekong Basin. Layered on top is a scramble among external powers for regional influence. Has South Korea managed to carve out something distinct amid this competition—a functional niche built on environmental and technical cooperation, rather than the usual infrastructure-and-security playbook? institutions: University of Science and Technology - The University of Da Nang

title: Assessing threats to freshwater ecosystems: implications for water security management in Spain
abstract: Human threats to freshwater ecosystems overall compromise water security, and identifying these threats is essential to set up the required strategies in managing water resources. The article focuses on Spain as the region of study since this country maintains a long-lasting conflict between the use of water resources and the impacts on freshwater ecosystems. Spain has a double-sided water reality, both in spatial (dry Mediterranean versus humid Atlantic ecoregions) and in temporal terms (interannual climate variability). title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Tool Descriptions Are Smelly! Towards Improving AI Agent Efficiency with Augmented MCP Tool Descriptions,
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduces a standard specification that defines how Foundation Model (FM)-based agents should interact with external systems by invoking tools. However, to understand a tool’s purpose and features, FMs rely on natural-language tool descriptions, making these descriptions a critical component in guiding FMs to select the optimal tool for a given (sub)task and to pass the right arguments to the tool. title: Whole genome sequencing and tuberculosis surveillance and control: a critical view from resources limited settings
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly presented as a transformative tool for tuberculosis (TB) surveillance, drug-resistance detection, and precision treatment (1,2). Its scientific value is not in dispute. As countries work toward the milestones of the WHO End TB Strategy (3), however, an important question for resource-limited settings is not whether genomic tools work, but where they should sit among competing priorities. institutions: Universidad Católica de Santiago de Guayaquil

title: A Gateway-Based Approach for Integrating Digital Compass Data into Controller Area Network (CAN) in Precision Farming Systems
abstract: The integration of high precision orientation sensors into resilient communication infrastructures is a key requirement for next-generation autonomous systems. Digital compass sensors typically generate data in the NMEA format, whereas distributed control architectures in mobile robotics predominantly utilize the CAN 2.0B protocol. This study presents the design and implementation of a microcontroller-based hardware-software gateway that enables seamless interoperability between these heterogeneous communication standards within autonomous agricultural platforms. title: Emergent constraints improve near-term temperature projections over China: Evaluations against observations based on the preindustrial baseline
abstract: Abstract Emergent constraints are widely used to reduce uncertainties in climate projections, yet their reliability has rarely been evaluated against observations. We apply an established emergent constraint approach based on historical global surface air temperature (GSAT) trends and local residual warming trends to temperature change projections over China during 2006-2025 in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phases 5 and 6 (CMIP5/6) ensembles. title: Microbial cell factories for gamma-linolenic acid biosynthesis: metabolic engineering, downstream processing, and future perspectives
abstract: Gamma-linolenic acid (GLA) is a vital anti-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acid, yet its traditional supply from plant seeds such as evening primrose and borage is constrained by low yields and climatic instability. Consequently, microbial cell factories present a sustainable and season-independent alternative for scalable GLA production. This review critically synthesizes recent biotechnological advancements in utilizing oleaginous microorganisms as production platforms. title: From genome to phenotype: advances, challenges and One Health perspectives in the genomic prediction of antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has substantially improved the detection and surveillance of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) by enabling the rapid identification of acquired resistance genes, resistance-associated point mutations, and mobile genetic elements. However, the presence of a resistance determinant does not necessarily establish its functional contribution to the antimicrobial phenotype. title: Long-term spatiotemporal dynamics, hotspot persistence, and extreme AOD days over Bursa, Türkiye
abstract: Satellite-based aerosol optical depth (AOD) enables long-term monitoring of atmospheric aerosol loading in regions with sparse ground-based observation networks. In this study, the spatial and temporal variability of 550 nm AOD over Bursa during 2003–2025 was investigated using Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Multi-Angle Implementation of Atmospheric Correction (MAIAC) MCD19A2 Collection 6.1 data at 1 km spatial resolution. title: Assessing urban growth dynamics in Cooch Behar city using the Shannon entropy model
abstract: Urban land increase is often conflated with spatial redistribution when entropy is interpreted as a direct measure of growth. This study quantifies built-up change in Cooch Behar City, India, from 1990 to 2022 while distinguishing land-cover compositional entropy from built-up spatial entropy. Landsat images from three epochs were classified using supervised maximum-likelihood classification. abstract: This paper focuses on the fault detection filter problem for unmanned surface vehicle systems via an improved dynamic event-triggered protocol under deception attacks. Taking into account factors such as external disturbances and potential system faults, a motion model for the unmanned surface vehicle system in a complex environment is constructed. title: Automated grain-size characterization of GTAW Ti-6Al-4 V weldments using OpenCV and comparison with ASTM-based intercept methods
abstract: Quantitative measurement of grain size in the fusion zone (FZ) of Ti-6Al-4 V GTAW weldments is difficult because the large, uneven grain morphologies can introduce operator bias in conventional metallography. In this study, a calibrated openCV based image-processing workflow was developed, and its results were compared with those of the Jeffries planimetric, the Heyn linear-intercept, and Abrams three-circle methods of ASTM E112. title: Detection of the sporadic E layer using crowdsourced WSPR signal reports during the ascending phase of cycle 25
abstract: The sporadic E (Es) layer is a transient electron-density irregularity in the partially ionized E-region whose occurrence strongly modulates VHF radio propagation and can interfere with aviation navigation and maritime communications. Building on Deacon et al., who demonstrated the feasibility of detecting Es with amateur-radio WSPR (Weak Signal Propagation Reporter) signals, this study scales the approach to a full year using global WSPR data from 2021 (early ascending phase of solar cycle 25; annual mean sunspot number 29.6) and the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise

title: A geospatial and community perception analysis of the impacts of land use and land cover change on ecosystem service values
abstract: Rapid urbanization in developing countries is causing significant changes in land use and land cover (LULC), which affect ecosystem service values (ESVs). This study investigates the impacts of LULC changes on ESV in the Gazipur city area of Bangladesh over a 30-years from 1991 to 2021. The analysis was conducted using satellite imagery from Landsat-5 TM (1991 and 2006) and Landsat-8 OLI-TIRS (2021), with a supervised classification approach to prepare LULC maps and the Benefit Transfer Method for ESV evaluation. title: Evaluating alternative trade network configurations under geopolitical risk: a multi-scale systems approach
abstract: Rising geopolitical risks and supply-chain disruptions have increased interest in transport-network diversification and alternative connectivity systems. This article presents a scenario-based comparison between a traditional maritime chokepoint configuration centered on the Strait of Hormuz and a prospective diversified multimodal corridor connecting the Middle East and Europe. abstract: Toponymic records embedded in Arabic, Persian, and Chinese manuscript traditions provide evidence for reconstructing the historical geographies of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. This review uses a structured narrative and conceptual-synthesis methodology to compare place-name transmission across languages, scripts, manuscript genres, and political regimes. title: Improving the CLASSIC (v1.8) snow model to better simulate Arctic snowpacks
abstract: Abstract. This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. title: IMU- and LSTM-CNN-based multi-gait recognition for a lower limb exoskeleton
abstract: This study presents a platform-specific and subject-independent validation of an IMU-based LSTM-CNN gait-recognition pipeline on a self-developed lower-limb exoskeleton. Ten healthy participants performed five locomotion modes, including level walking, stair ascent, stair descent, standing up, and sitting down. Each participant completed five level-walking trials and ten trials for each of the remaining four locomotion modes, resulting in 450 original recording trials. IMU signals collected from the thigh, shank, and foot were segmented using a 128-sample sliding window with a 64-sample step.

abstract: Abstract To effectively recognize and manage wildlife mortality events, we need to understand who, what, why and how – who are the individual animals and species involved; what are the surrounding circumstances in time and space in which they are found; what are the causes and contributors to illness, injury and/or death; why is this happening in this time and place? title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. title: From resource orchestration to robustness and resilience: the role of data analytics capability in bulk commodity maritime supply chains
abstract: Introduction Bulk commodity maritime supply chains are increasingly exposed to climate-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions, port congestion, transportation uncertainty, and other external shocks. title: Microbial diversity and adaptation Strategies in the nunataks of Western Dronning Maud Land, Antarctica
abstract: Antarctic soil ecosystems harbor unique microbial communities that survive under prolonged low temperatures, high UV radiation, desiccation, oligotrophic conditions and other environmental stresses. This study aimed to characterize the culturable microbial communities and explore potential adaptation strategies of microorganisms inhabiting the unique inland nunataks of the Jutulsessen and Ahlmannryggen ranges in Western Dronning Maud Land (WDML), Antarctica. abstract: In the present study, the antioxidant capacity, cholinesterase-inhibitory activity, and antiproliferative effects of Sparganium erectum extracts were investigated. title: A mixed-integer linear programming approach to container terminal layout optimization: application to the port of Piraeus
abstract: Abstract This study addresses the issue of designing a container terminal layout by developing a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) mathematical model. The methodology is applied to Pier II of the Piraeus Container Terminal. The mathematical formulation of the problem systematically incorporates real-world spatial constraints and operational factors related to container storage areas, while evaluating alternative scenarios to identify optimal layouts. title: Probabilistic fatigue reliability assessment of girth-weld surface cracks in API 5L X65 offshore pipelines under cyclic global bending using a Kriging surrogate
abstract: Fatigue cracking at girth welds threatens offshore-pipeline integrity and requires uncertainty in flaw size, crack-growth behaviour, loading and weld geometry to be considered. A probabilistic fatigue-reliability framework is developed for a semi-elliptical surface crack in an API 5L X65 pipeline under cyclic global bending. abstract: The maritime industry is under increasing pressure from environmental regulations, and therefore, it is required to provide energy solutions that comply with sustainable practices immediately. The study conducted by the researchers indicates the creation of a hydrogen fuel cell model that is designed specifically for the MATLAB Simulink high-speed passenger vessels. title: QUALITY OF WORK-LIFE AS A PREDICTOR OF LECTURERS’ JOB ENGAGEMENT IN COLLEGES OF EDUCATION IN SOUTH EAST, NIGERIA
abstract: The study examined quality of work-life as a predictor of lecturers’ job engagement in Colleges of Education in South East, Nigeria. Two research questions guided the study and two null hypotheses were tested at 0.05 level of significance. A correlational research design was adopted for the study. abstract: With the application of nanoscale materials, nanomedicine is redefining and improving the delivery of pharmaceuticals and molecular bioimaging probes, providing novel approaches to disease diagnosis, management, and treatment. As in many other fields, renewable materials are becoming increasingly important in nanomedicine because they offer sustainable alternatives to fossil-based resources and are often biodegradable and biocompatible. abstract: Accurate renewable energy demand forecasting is important for medium- and long-term power-system planning. This study proposes PSO-TPA-LSTM-Stacked, a compact forecasting framework that integrates particle swarm optimization (PSO), temporal pattern attention (TPA), and stacked long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. abstract: Understanding the variation characteristics of impact pressure induced by dam-break waves is essential for a deeper understanding of the impact pressure mechanisms on structures and for enhancing their impact resistance. In this study, large-scale laboratory experiments were conducted in a flume with varying upstream and downstream water depths, bed slopes, and channel lengths. abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from fossil fuels and industry in South Africa amounted to 401.89 million tonnes in 2023, with implications for climate change and global warming. South Africa has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by the year 2050. However, the transition to a low-carbon economy must be pursued sustainably and equitably, given South Africa’s reliance on coal and its status as a leading global coal producer. abstract: Chromium contamination in sugarcane soils is often combined with co-metals and salinity caused by tannery effluent, electroplating effluent, paper mill wastewater, vinasse fertigation and filter cake. Hence, single element toxicity assessment does not provide realistic assessment of its exposure. abstract: Natural products (NPs) are the largest source of bioactive molecules with therapeutic properties. Currently, there are compound databases containing thousands of NPs, from which it is possible to select those with the best absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) profiles, which greatly increases their chances of success in clinical trials. abstract: Abstract Landslide susceptibility maps (LSMs) depict the spatial probability of landslide occurrence, typically using data-driven models based on past event distributions. However, these models often overlook temporal changes, assuming that past patterns reliably predict future events. In a rapidly changing world, influenced by factors such as climate change and urbanization, this assumption may lead to inconsistencies in LSMs over time, reducing their predictive accuracy. abstract: The rediscovered type specimen of the polyclad flatworm Plehnia arctica (Plehn, 1896), collected during Kükenthal’s 1889 Spitzbergen expedition and presumed lost for more than a century, was rediscovered in the collection of the Phyletisches Museum Jena (PMJ). abstract: The Russia–Ukraine conflict has disrupted global commodity markets, particularly crude oil, natural gas, wheat, and corn, leading to increased price volatility and affecting exchange rate dynamics. This study aims to analyze the Granger-causal relationship between global commodity prices and the USD/IDR exchange rate using the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). title: Ecosystem health and its constraint transitions in Plateau cities: insights from Lhasa, China
abstract: Abstract High-altitude urban ecosystems are exposed to pronounced ecological vulnerability and increasing human pressures. Existing assessments have primarily characterized overall health status and its spatiotemporal variation, whereas temporal changes in the configuration of underlying constraints have received less attention. As the capital of the Xizang Autonomous Region of China, Lhasa’s unique geographic and climatic setting on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau poses distinctive challenges for ecosystem health assessment. abstract: Halal tourism studies in Indonesia have largely focused on Sharia-compliant services, such as halal food, worship facilities, and religious tourism, while the development of urban Islamic tourism remains relatively limited. This study analyzes the development of halal tourism through an urban Islamic tourism approach in Pontianak City. EVs technology causes fundamental changes in vehicle architecture and dynamics including increased overall weight due to battery packs, altered torque delivery, and regenerative braking systems. title: Understanding and reducing methane emissions: insights into anthropogenic, natural sources, and novel mitigation techniques
abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) is a potent, short-lived greenhouse gas. Among the major well-mixed greenhouse gases, it ranks second only to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in its contribution to anthropogenic radiative forcing. Although methane remains in the atmosphere for approximately 12 years, its 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) is approximately 27–30 times greater than that of CO 2 (IPCC AR6), making rapid mitigation a critical near-term climate strategy. abstract: Wildfire is a major disturbance in terrestrial ecosystems. Previous studies have shown that since the Last Glacial Maximum, wildfire activity across the East Asian and Indian summer monsoon regions has been closely associated with precipitation variability on suborbital to millennial timescales. However, continuous records of long-term wildfire dynamics and their relationships with regional moisture variability remain scarce in the alpine regions along the southeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau. abstract: Long-term monitoring records from roller-compacted concrete (RCC) gravity dams in cold regions are scarce, although freeze–thaw cycling and large seasonal temperature ranges act there together with hydrostatic loading. This study analyzes 9.1 years of daily records (2016–2025) from 190 instruments on a 71 m RCC gravity dam in Xinjiang, China. In this article, the vast consultation of scientific literature, archaeological, historical and anecdotal sources, allowed to outline a global reasoned vision on the olive origin, its spread during early history and how olive fruit fly may represent as proxy for tracing its early diffusion. abstract: Abstract Cooperative path planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires the simultaneous achievement of target navigation, collision avoidance, and formation coordination in complex obstacle environments. Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods often suffer from sparse rewards, local deadlocks, and conflicts between formation maintenance and obstacle avoidance, which can destabilize policy learning. abstract: Abstract Urban wetland parks serve as vital infrastructure for climate resilience, yet a critical epistemological gap remains between their objective thermodynamic performance and the subjective thermal well-being of visitors. abstract: This paper introduces an integrated Digital Twin framework for monitoring and managing transport infrastructure, with a specific focus on bridges, through the integration of multi-source geospatial and structural survey data. title: The EU's Indo‐Pacific Strategy and South Korea: Convergence, Perceptions, and Prospects for Strategic Cooperation
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the evolving European Union–South Korea relationship through the framework of the EU's Indo‐Pacific Strategy (IPS). Drawing on interviews with policymakers, officials, and influencers, it traces six decades of bilateral ties, highlighting Korea's 2022 IPS and its convergence with EU priorities in digital governance, green transition, and sustainability. abstract: As digital transformation accelerates and environmental regulations become more stringent, increasing attention has been paid to how maritime firms translate digital resources into environmental value. Drawing on organizational information processing theory and the natural resource-based view, this study develops a multistage model to examine the relationship between supply chain digitalization and environmental performance. abstract: Abstract Chinese export porcelain bowls are heritage materials associated with Ming maritime trade, yet their morphology remains insufficiently quantified. title: Prediction of lignan content in sesame seeds using near-infrared hyperspectral imaging and regression modeling
abstract: Abstract Sesame ( Sesamum indicum L.) seeds contain lignans, including sesamin and sesamolin, which possess important health-promoting properties. abstract: In recent years environmental management has been raised to a new level in the context of cultural heritage sites. Climate change, urbanization, mass tourism, and limited institutional resources and management capacities are the most pressing challenges facing cultural heritage today. title: Global expansion of compound drought–heatwave risk
abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. abstract: Pitting corrosion is one of the most prevalent and detrimental forms of localized corrosion in stainless steels exposed to chloride-containing environments. abstract: Military force design is a dynamic process that includes complex relations among innovation, adaptation, conservatism, enlargement, and shrinkage, and other forms of change or stability arising from the ongoing interaction among the military, its environment, and, primarily, its enemies. title: First record of Prostoma clepsinoides Dugès, 1828 (Nemertea, Eumonostilifera) from Hachijo-jima Island, Japan
abstract: Prostoma clepsinoides Dugès, 1828 is reported from Hachijo-jima Island, Tokyo, Japan, based on a mitochondrial COI barcode sequence from one freshwater specimen. The specimen was collected from a spring-fed stream and grouped with published sequences currently assigned to P. clepsinoides . To our knowledge, this is the first published record of Prostoma from Hachijo-jima Island. No morphological voucher specimen was retained because the entire specimen was used for DNA extraction.

abstract: Este estudio analiza la forma en la que el profesorado percibe la integración de la inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) en el ámbito educativo y de qué manera esta tecnología influye en la reconfiguración de su identidad profesional. title: Prediction of HIV incidence in Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, China: a time series study
abstract: Objective In China, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region has a high incidence of HIV, and the situation regarding its prevention and control remains challenging. This study aimed to compare the predictive performance of three time series models, SARIMAX (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors), Prophet with exogenous variables, and random forest, using rolling validation, and to provide references for HIV prevention and control in Xinjiang. title: Combined model for document classification based on the comparative evaluation of semi-supervised models
abstract: La escasez de documentos etiquetados limita la clasificación automática de documentos y eleva los costos de etiquetado. En este contexto, el aprendizaje semi-supervisado (SSL) constituye una alternativa viable; sin embargo, la selección de modelos adecuados se dificulta por la ausencia de análisis comparativos que evidencien sus fortalezas y limitaciones. title: Nanoparticle Fabrication and Optimization: From Green Chemistry to Transformative Applications in Life Sciences, Medicine, and Public Health
abstract: Nanotechnology has changed many fields by allowing scientists to work with matter at the atomic and molecular levels. NPs including metal (e.g., Ag, Au), metal oxide (e.g., ZnO, FeO), polymeric (e.g., PLGA), and carbon-based (e.g., carbon nanotubes), have special chemical, biological, and physical properties. This review paper discusses a lot of detail about making and improving nanoparticles, guided by the 12 principles of green chemistry ideas to make sure they are safe for living things and last for a long time. Traditional synthesis methods, employ toxic chemicals and use a lot of energy.

title: Topology-aware and constraint-guided deep reinforcement learning for climate-resilient control of urban stormwater systems
abstract: Introduction Urban stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by extreme precipitation events, leading to hydraulic surcharge when system capacity is exceeded. Traditional rule-based control (RBC) is reactive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) does not explicitly exploit drainage‐network topology or ensure physically consistent control. This study introduces Constraint-guided Graph-PPO (PIG‐PPO), a topology‐aware reinforcement learning framework designed to improve stormwater control under extreme precipitation conditions. title: A Gray-Distribution-Based Adaptive Laser Stripe Center Extraction Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Accurate laser stripe center extraction is critical for high-precision line-structured laser 3D reconstruction. Many existing methods assume that the cross-sectional grayscale distribution of a laser stripe follows a fixed pattern. However, in practical scanning, variations in working distance, object geometry, and surface material lead to significant changes in grayscale distributions across the same stripe, which introduce center localization errors and degrade reconstruction accuracy and robustness. title: Luz invisible que revela moléculas: el papel de la radiación infrarroja en la química
abstract: Infrared (IR) radiation is a part of the electromagnetic spectrum that is invisible to the human eye but very important for the chemical sciences. Using IR, particularly IR spectroscopy, chemists can identify compounds, verify product quality, or monitor the progress of a chemical reaction without destroying samples. This article provides a clear explanation of the operating principles of IR, as well as its applications in modern chemistry and its potential future developments, with examples ranging from the food industry to space exploration.

title: Gas Turbine Propulsion Systems for Naval Vessels: Energy Flow Calculation Methodology and HighPressure Rotor CFD Simulation
abstract: This paper addresses the modernization of naval propulsion systems through the adoption of gas turbine technology, with emphasis on thermodynamic calculation methodology and rotor flow simulation. The study is centred on the Rolls Royce gas turbine, employed in naval propulsion applications and covers all thermodynamic states from atmospheric air intake through the two-stage compression process, combustion chamber, high-pressure and lowpressure turbine stages, to the power turbine exhaust. title: Drying and rewetting of riverbed sediments results in cold to neutral biogeochemical moments
abstract: Abstract Sediment respiration in streams/rivers impacts global biogeochemical cycles, yet is mostly studied under perennially-inundated conditions despite all river corridors having variably inundated areas and most streams going dry each year. Previous experiments observed sediment rewetting to cause elevated or suppressed aerobic respiration, indicating variation across studies. To deepen understanding, we conducted 21-day wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams spread across the contiguous United States. title: Integration of Renewable Energy and Hybrid Power System for Sustainable Transportation: A Vessel-to-Grid Approach
abstract: Sustainable maritime transportation requires electrical systems that are reliable, energy-efficient, and capable of integrating cleaner energy sources. This study develops and evaluates a small-scale hybrid power prototype that combines a 50 Wp photovoltaic (PV) source as the renewable-energy component with a mini steam power source as a complementary generator, using an ESP32 microcontroller, INA219 sensors, MPPT control, a buck-boost converter, and relay-based automatic switching.
