abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfur leaching from metal sulfide electrocatalysts undermines formate intermediate stability during CO 2 reduction, yet existing protection strategies remain static. Here, we introduce an interfacial dynamic locking mechanism that actively stabilizes sulfur under reaction conditions. title: Structural diagnosis and evolution of urban resilience in dryland oasis urban agglomerations from an eco-immunological perspective
abstract: Dryland oasis urban agglomerations face increasing drought risk, but gains in long-term adaptive capacity may not translate into stronger structural resilience because additive indices allow strong dimensions to offset weak ones. This study developed a partially non-compensatory four-dimensional super-trapezoid resilience model (TE4) integrating resistance, recovery, adaptive capacity, and institutional learning and preparedness, and applied it to ten city- and county-level units on the Northern Slope of the Tianshan Mountains during 2014–2024. title: Mineralization mechanism and pollutant immobilization characteristics of vaterite induced by Bacillus velezensis and Pseudomonas putida
abstract: Exploring strain-specific differences in bacterial vaterite biomineralization can supplement the basic theoretical research of biomineralization and reveal the biogeochemical linkages between microbially induced carbonate formation and in-situ pollutant sequestration in soil environments. In this study, Bacillus velezensis LB002 and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 were used as representative bacterial strains to compare strain-dependent vaterite formation and pollutant sequestration behavior. title: Thailand Land Surface Temperature Variation and Forecasting
abstract: Climate change has emerged as a global challenge, influenced by human activities, industrial operations and energy systems that depend on non-renewable energy such as carbon, gas, and petroleum. These activities have contributed to long-term shifts in temperature and broader climatic conditions. Land Surface Temperature (LST) has become an important standard for informing weather-related strategies at regional scales. title: Forest green-up in the Pearl River Basin: trends, driving factors, and relationships with net primary productivity
abstract: The spring green-up date (GUD), a critical indicator of ecosystem response to climate change, profoundly influences terrestrial productivity. However, the complex drivers of GUD remain elusive, while the contentious relationship between GUD and net primary productivity (NPP) challenges the universal validity of the hypothesis that earlier green-up enhances productivity. title: A Multi-Criteria Decision Support System for Product Selling Price Determination: A Comparative Analysis of Weighted Product and Simple Additive Weighting Methods
abstract: Determining an appropriate product selling price is a critical decision in retail business because it directly affects profitability, market competitiveness, and business sustainability. However, small retail businesses often rely on subjective judgment and manual calculations, which can lead to inconsistent pricing decisions when multiple factors must be considered simultaneously. This study develops a Multi-Criteria Decision Support System to determine product selling prices by comparatively applying the Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) and Weighted Product (WP) methods. title: Data visualisation as an ‘emotional repository’
abstract: Understanding the role of emotions in engagements with data visualisations (graphs, charts, maps) is important given their increasing circulation in everyday life and their influence on how people make sense of social and political issues. This paper builds on sociological perspectives on emotions and advances existing research on the interplay between data visualisation and emotions by proposing the concept of ‘emotional repository’ to describe data visualisations. abstract: Abstract. Geosciences are often described as interdisciplinary, yet research and training remain fragmented across sub-disciplines and institutions. To understand how early career scientists (ECS) experience and practice interdisciplinarity, and which support structures actually help, we conducted an online survey within the German Geo.X research network. title: Comparative in Silico Toxicological Assessment of 16 Selective COX-2 Inhibitors (Coxibs) Using Multi-Platform Predictive Models
abstract: Selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitors (coxibs) offer reduced gastrointestinal toxicity compared to traditional non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), yet their safety remains controversial as evidenced by several market withdrawals due to severe cardiovascular and hepatic risks. This study systematically evaluated 16 human and veterinary coxib compounds for mutagenicity, carcinogenicity, micronucleus activity, and hepatotoxicity through a multi-platform in silico approach using VEGA-QSAR, ToxTree, and T.E.S.T. software. abstract: In-situ tunnel expansion is commonly conducted while maintaining existing traffic operation. Under such conditions, the traffic-maintaining side is simultaneously affected by construction disturbance, deterioration of existing structures, complex geological conditions, and operational traffic loads. Its risk sources are characterized by multi-source coupling, chain transmission, and dynamic evolution. title: HOW MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON ARCHITECTURE AND TRAINING HYPERPARAMETERS AFFECT PREDICTIVE PERFORMANCE IN UAV-BASED SOYBEAN PHENOTYPING
abstract: Multilayer perceptron (MLP) models have been increasingly applied to high-throughput phenotyping using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-derived multispectral imagery. However, the effects of network architecture and training hyperparameters on predictive performance remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the number of neurons, hidden layers, training epochs, and cross-validation folds, as well as the performance of different combinations of these factors in MLP models to predict soybean phenotypic traits using vegetation indices. title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
abstract: This scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). title: Photosynthesis Phenotyping: Where Are We and How Should We Move Forward?
abstract: Photosynthesis phenotyping is increasingly important for crop improvement, but its main limitation is not measurement throughput alone. It is the physiological interpretation of scalable signals. Direct methods, including gas exchange, CO2 response analysis, isotope-based approaches, and canopy flux measurements, define photosynthetic carbon assimilation and capacity, but remain difficult to deploy at scale. abstract: Abstract Global and Regional Climate Models (GCMs and RCMs) provide projections for climate change impact assessments. However, their performance may vary across locations and climate variables, introducing uncertainty into the estimation of future climate actions on infrastructure. This study presents a multi-criteria framework for evaluating climate-model performance and adapting the Factor of Change (FC), which describes variations in characteristic values used in structural design. abstract: Understanding soil water content dynamics under saline conditions remains a major challenge for effective soil and water management in agricultural systems. This study aimed to optimize the correction of soil water content measurements obtained from gypsum blocks under the combined effects of salinity and matric suction using Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Soil samples were collected from agricultural fields in Guangdong Province, China, representing three distinct soil textures: sandy loam, clay, and clay loam. abstract: Frictional sliding is ubiquitous in both natural phenomena and engineering systems, often occurring under dynamic normal stress conditions, yet the theoretical understanding of such scenarios remains limited. This study employs a verified one-dimensional spring-block model, incorporating rate- and state-dependent friction law, to investigate the evolution of stick–slip behavior under cyclic normal stress perturbations. title: SAFETY CULTURE AND MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES DRIVING ORGANIZATIONAL EFFECTIVENESS IN MARITIME TRANSPORT
abstract: This study empirically investigates how safety culture, customer relationship management (CRM), and quality management jointly drive organizational effectiveness within Thailand’s maritime transport sector. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV) theoretical framework, the research examines these vital intangible capabilities as synergistic drivers of sustained competitive advantage. title: Transformación en la comunicación académica y profesional de Ecuador y Perú, mediante la adopción de la IA
abstract: La expansión de la inteligencia artificial en la comunidad educativa y profesional está transformando la creación de contenidos, generando oportunidades y desafíos que requieren análisis contextualizados. Este estudio examina los niveles de conocimiento, frecuencia de uso y ventajas percibidas de la IA en usuarios de Ecuador y Perú, países con sistemas educativos comparables. title: Fire Regime in Wasur National Park, Indonesia: Climatic Influences and Indigenous Burning Practices
abstract: This study examines the fire regime and its driving factors in Wasur National Park, Indonesia. This study employs a MODIS hotspot time-series analysis to examine the relationship between hotspot detections and climatic variables, supported by in-depth interviews with key informants from Kanume, an indigenous people living in Wasur NP. title: Impacto de la inteligencia artificial generativa en procesos de creación de animación digital e ilustración.
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa ha llegado a cambiar las reglas en la creación de imágenes, transformando los flujos de trabajo tradicionales y redefiniendo la ontología del artista. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el impacto de las herramientas algorítmicas en los procesos de creación de la animación digital y la ilustración desde un enfoque teórico-conceptual. title: Resilience of standalone microgrids: indicators, enhancement strategies, and challenges—an integrative review
abstract: Microgrids have emerged as a promising solution for improving energy access, enhancing local energy independence, and strengthening resilience against environmental, technical, and operational disturbances. Resilience refers to the ability of a system to withstand, adapt to, and recover from disruptive events while maintaining reliable operation. title: A preliminary assessment of the field diet and trophic position of the two-spotted cricket Gryllus bimaculatus using DNA metabarcoding and stable isotope analysis
abstract: Although Gryllus bimaculatus is widely used as a laboratory model organism, its ecology under natural conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we provide a preliminary assessment of the field diet and trophic ecology of wild G. bimaculatus using stable isotope analysis and gut-content DNA metabarcoding. Stable isotope analysis provided a preliminary estimate of the trophic position of G. bimaculatus , suggesting that it occupies an intermediate position between herbivores and carnivores. title: Flood pulse attributes of the upper Amazon River floodplains: spatiotemporal patterns and sensitivity to digital terrain model selection
abstract: Abstract Flood extent, depth, duration, and connectivity are key attributes of the seasonal flood pulse in Amazon floodplains, but characterizing them consistently remains difficult in forested, low-relief terrain. abstract: Introduction Legal and policy responses to climate mobility remain overwhelmingly oriented toward displacement, relocation and cross-border protection, overlooking the right of people to remain in their homes under conditions of dignity and security. abstract: Nanomaterials have been present for centuries as colloidal materials in historical objects such as Lycurgus Cup, medieval church windows and weapons made of Damascus steel. abstract: Seismic assessment of reinforced-concrete (RC) buildings requires understanding behavior beyond the elastic range. Linear analysis cannot reveal yielding or capacity loss; nonlinear dynamic analysis is costly, and few studies report pushover output for a regular frame and an existing building. abstract: Climate scientists have been interested in the causes of the significant rise in temperatures, resulting in cold and heat waves, and consequently, periods of drought and flooding in various parts of the world. abstract: The study aimed to account for the influence of otherness on a social enterprise's provision of tax services to clients in the Northern Territory of Australia. It collected quantitative data from client interviews conducted before the social enterprise provided taxation services. In this study, water and sediment samples were collected from four urban rivers in Changzhou during winter and summer. 16S rDNA, ITS amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis were used to characterize microbial composition and its functional potential. abstract: This study evaluates potential cultural ecosystem service (CES) supply, potential demand and modelled least-cost accessibility pathways across Jiangsu Province on a common 1 km grid for 2014, 2019 and 2020. abstract: In order to provide offloading services for computationally demanding and time-sensitive operations on vehicles, multi-access edge computing has emerged as a successful paradigm. abstract: Abstract Metamaterials provide exceptional properties arising from their well-defined engineered structures in which periodic features ranging from the nanoscale to the macroscale are manufactured to yield the desired characteristics. abstract: Post-harvest handling of fresh fish by small-scale fishermen is highly dependent on effective temperature control to minimize quality deterioration during storage and transportation. title: Expanding the geographic and host range of moss-nostocacean symbioses in central Europe
abstract: Since their re-discovery, Moss-cyanobacterial symbioses are of increasing interest, especially Nostoc-feather moss symbioses. Efforts to document Nostoc-feather moss symbioses have historically been centered in Scandinavia and the North American Boreal forest zone. title: Evaluation of the safe operating space during low flow for water allocation and climate change scenarios in the Danube
abstract: A basin-to-local evaluation framework, quantifying safe operating space (SOS) for low-flow water allocation and climate change along the Danube, is presented, linking basin hydrology to local operations for navigation, ecology, run-of-river hydropower, drinking water, and nuclear power plant cooling. The water allocation model (RIBASIM), forced by the hydrological model (wflow_sbm), embeds explicit demands on the mainstem under ‘what-if’ scenarios, while the numerical model (RSim-3D) simulates corresponding water levels at an Upper Danube case study. title: Inteligencia Artificial en la Animación Digital: Impacto en el Mercado Laboral y la Toma de Decisiones Creativas
abstract: Este estudio analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la toma de decisiones estratégicas de la animación digital y sus consecuencias laborales. Mediante una revisión sistemática documental PRISMA de 50 artículos (2021–2026), se evalúa cómo la IA genera eficiencia operativa (reducción de tiempos de renderizado, automatización de tareas repetitivas) pero también desplaza empleos tradicionales, especialmente en México y América Latina, donde más de 200,000 animadores enfrentan riesgo de disrupción en cinco años. title: Dual activities of lysis and capsule degradation enable the bacteriophage protein Lys33795 to effectively disrupt Streptococcus suis biofilms
abstract: Streptococcus suis (S. suis) is an encapsulated zoonotic pathogen that can form recalcitrant biofilms. Bacteriophage-derived endolysins and depolymerases represent promising antibiofilm agents, but currently, no report has described protein which displays both of lytic and capsule degradation activities simultaneously. Here, we mined the porcine gut virome and identified Lys33795, a dual-activity antibacterial protein that degrades both capsule and peptidoglycan of S. suis. title: Differential Allometric Patterns of Shell Growth in Two Invasive Pomacea Species Amid Water Hyacinth Beds in Central China
abstract: Allometric relationships represent common laws of relative growth between size and weight of different organisms, including mollusks. Although allometries between shell size and weight of highly invasive apple snails ( Pomacea spp.) vary globally, food‐source effects on these relationships remain unclear, challenging local conservation for freshwater biodiversity. After successful invasion of Pomacea spp. at the largest lake of Huangshi City, Daye Lake, in central China, allometries between shell size and weight of the mollusk populations feeding on different plants remain unknown. abstract: Abstract In terms of quality test, ultrasonic wave velocity test, static mechanical test and dynamic compression test, the physical and static mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete after water immersion for 180 d were studied, and the effects of water saturation and impact load on the mechanical properties of geopolymer concrete were analyzed. title: Synthesis and Characterization of Bi2O3-SnO2 Type-II Heterojunction Nanostructure with Tunable Band Edge Modulation for Enhanced Visible-Light-Driven Photocatalytic Water Purification
abstract: In this study, wastewater tainted with dyes presents a significant environmental problem that calls for effective and reusable photocatalysts to remove pollutants under visible light. The purpose of this work is to create and describe a BiO₃–SnO₂ heterojunction nanocomposite for the photocatalytic degradation of Rhodamine B (RhB) and Methyl Orange (MO). This work is interesting since it evaluates the composite's degradation performance toward two distinct dyes in addition to the impacts of catalyst dose and starting dye concentration, reaction kinetics, reactive species, and reusability. title: Sub-chronic toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in Danio rerio: evidence from hematological, biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological biomarkers
abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) have emerged as widespread aquatic contaminants with the potential to induce multiple toxic effects in fish. This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics and sub-chronic toxicity of PS-MPs in Danio rerio over 20 days. SEM revealed irregular and aggregated PS-MPs with micrometre-scale dimensions (approximately 1–200 µm), while DLS showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 1,115.5 nm with a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.569. Acute toxicity analysis determined the LC 50 value of PS-MPs to be 89.1 μg/L, and morphogenetic abnormalities were also observed.

title: Regional Urban Heat Island Risk Mapping Using PCA and Fuzzy Clustering
abstract: Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects pose increasing challenges in rapidly urbanizing tropical regions, where land-cover transformation and population concentration intensify spatial thermal risk. This study proposes an integrated Principal Component Analysis-Fuzzy C-Means spatial framework to classify and map regional UHI risk across Sulawesi Island, Indonesia, using multi-source geospatial data. Land surface temperature, vegetation condition, built-up intensity, and population density were harmonized on a 1 km grid for the 2024-2025 period. title: Advancing Micro-Ecotone Mapping Using UAV Photogrammetry and GIS
abstract: Ecotones are transitional boundaries between ecosystems and essential to regulating biodiversity and ecological processes. Although ecotones are often wider transition zones like aquatic-terrestrial boundaries, they can happen at fine spatial scales (micro-ecotones) and occur over only a few meters or even centimeters. In the past, ecotones have been examined using one-dimensional transects or coarsely resolved remote sensing data for analysis. title: A Comprehensive Study of Logistics 5.0 Adaptation & Challenges in the Indian Supply Chain Industry
abstract: Logistics 5.0 indicates the combination of Industry 5.0’s important principles such as human-centricity, resiliency, and sustainability with the advanced digital capabilities of Logistics 4.0. While a growing number of developed countries are starting to adopt AI, digital twins, collaborative robots, and human-machine decision-making systems, there is still only limited evidence available regarding Logistics 5.0 implementation in India. title: In Silico Identification of Putative Fruit Crop-Derived Antibacterial Peptides Against Aeromonas hydrophila
abstract: Aquaculture is a fish-producing subsector of agriculture that has a significant role in India’s economy and livelihood. The major threat to fish production is the outbreak of bacterial infections that creates severe losses every year. Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic invader of human and aquatic animals, ubiquitously present in the aquatic environment. Antibiotics are the common control measure, but their indiscriminate use has resulted in the development of resistance by the pathogen. title: Integrated assessment of meteorological drought impacts on terrestrial water storage and vegetation dynamics in East Africa
abstract: Abstract Water is essential for life, and effective hydrological management is crucial for economic stability and quality of life. Poor water resource governance can lead to scarcity, displacement, or even fatal consequences. Hydrological conditions in East Africa are influenced by drivers such as demographic expansion, industrialization, droughts, and vegetation dynamics. This study explores how total water storage in the region responds to drought intensity and vegetation variability. title: ANALISIS LAJU EROSI DAN AKRESI PANTAI TELUK SEPANG MENGGUNAKAN DIGITAL SHORELINE ANALYSIS SYSTEM (DSAS)
abstract: Pantai Teluk Sepang merupakan kawasan pesisir yang dinamis dan berhadapan langsung dengan Samudera Hindia. Perubahan garis pantai dapat memengaruhi keberlanjutan infrastruktur, permukiman, dan ekosistem pesisir sehingga diperlukan pemantauan yang konsisten. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis laju erosi dan akresi Pantai Teluk Sepang menggunakan Digital Shoreline Analysis System (DSAS) berdasarkan tiga tahun pengamatan, yaitu 2020, 2022, dan 2024. title: Coping with Climate Change in Southeastern Europe: The Case-Studies of Greece and Bulgaria and Their Growing Cooperation with Israel
abstract: The article analyzes the main challenges posed by climate change in Greece and Bulgaria and examines the policies adopted by both countries to address its effects through climate adaptation measures. In this context, the article highlights the importance of technological innovation in climate adaptation policies and explores the emerging cooperation between Greece and Israel, as well as between Bulgaria and Israel, in the fields of environmental protection and climate adaptation.

abstract: Hydrochemical data are essential for understanding groundwater flow, hydrobiogeochemical processes, contamination sources, and assessing groundwater quality. Despite the increasing availability of complex hydrochemical datasets, current tools for processing and visualizing these data-mainly spreadsheets and commercial GUI software-have significant limitations in scalability, reproducibility, and flexibility. abstract: Abstract Accurate counting and morphological analysis of welding electrodes and wire stubs are essential for warehouse data management in welding factories. However, the visual recognition of welding material stubs in real-world industrial applications is frequently hindered by issues such as missed detections, false detections, and imprecise boundary localization. title: Technical Evaluation of the Smart Water Jug-Plastic Bottle Disposal System
abstract: This study evaluated the technical performance and behavioral impact of the Smart Water Jug–Plastic Bottle Disposal System (SWJ – PBDS) as a strategy at Ocampo National High School – Senior High School (ONHS-SHS). The research addressed the escalating issue of plastic waste, focusing on reducing plastic bottle consumption through innovative smart sensor technology. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining descriptive and quasi-experimental designs. The descriptive component details the system’s characteristics via surveys, gathering data on user experiences and operational aspects
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. title: Data-driven forecasting of Flu, RSV, and COVID-19 related outcomes in the United States and Canada via Hankel dynamic mode decomposition
abstract: The (large) season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history make the forecasting of infectious diseases a challenging problem. Here, we examine the extent to which advances in data-driven dynamical modeling can provide accurate predictions by benchmarking the performance of one such method, Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), on the 2024-2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada. title: Seismo-ripples
abstract: Earthquake prediction has long been considered one of the greatest challenges in the global scientific community due to the complex and uncertain nature of seismogenic processes, along with the prevailing consensus that earthquakes are inherently unpredictable. Here, we present a novel and potentially transformative concept—seismo-ripples—resonance signals consistently observed in seismic, magnetic, and ionospheric data prior to major earthquakes. abstract: ABSTRACT The time‐varying formation tracking control problem in the context of switching communication topologies for nonlinear multi‐agent systems (MASs) containing matched nonlinear terms is researched in this paper. abstract: La digitalización de la administración tributaria peruana ha trasladado una parte creciente del control del crédito fiscal del impuesto general a las ventas hacia registros electrónicos y cruces automatizados. El objetivo fue sintetizar la evidencia científica, normativa e institucional sobre auditoría tributaria digital, facturación electrónica y crédito fiscal, y derivar una propuesta preliminar de indicadores de priorización aplicables al Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos. title: Seasonal flood inundation area and repetitive flood exposure shape the fundamental patterns of flood exposure in China from 2000 to 2020
abstract: Remote sensing of floods and associated exposure is essential for understanding and managing flood risks, yet exposure differences among floods with varying frequencies remain underexplored. Using MODIS time-series data, this study mapped infrequent flood inundation area (IFIA) and seasonal flood inundation area (SFIA) across China during 2000–2020. Differences in flood extent and built-up land exposure were assessed using the Mann–Kendall test, improved Theil–Sen algorithm, and one-way analysis of variance. Cumulative flood inundation area reached 3.52 × 10⁶ km², with SFIA accounting for 40%.

abstract: Benzimidazole is a privileged nitrogen-containing fused heterocyclic scaffold that has attracted considerable interest in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry because of its structural versatility, favorable physicochemical properties and broad biological profile. The benzimidazole nucleus comprises a benzene ring fused with an imidazole ring containing two nitrogen atoms, providing multiple sites for structural modification and interaction with biological targets. title: Development of a nonparametric spatial standardized precipitation–temperature index for regional drought characterization
abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging natural hazards, caused by prolonged shortages of precipitation and changes in temperature that reduce water availability. Reliable assessment of drought conditions across space is essential for sustainable water resource management and effective climate adaptation. However, most existing drought indices are designed for temporal analysis and often rely on probability distribution assumptions that may not adequately capture the spatial variability of drought-related variables. abstract: Mining is essential for economic development; however, the increasing number of tailings dam failures has become a major environmental and public health concern. This review aimed to characterize mining tailings dam disasters reported worldwide between 2015 and 2025 and summarize the available evidence on their human health impacts. title: Managerial competencies and the Iceberg theory: A framework for digital performance management in South African public entities
abstract: Orientation: The rapidly changing global technological advancements brought up significant challenges for managers to develop and maintain relevant competencies. Research purpose: The main purpose of the study was to develop a managerial competencies conceptual framework that could be applied by managers in South African public entities. abstract: Este estudio formaliza la receta técnica de un cheesecake semifrío mediante el uso de herramientas de modelación lineal para optimizar su escalado industrial. abstract: The transition from conchocelis to conchosporangial branches is not only a key stage in the life cycle of Pyropia/Porphyra but also directly affects the yield and quality of economically important species such as Pyropia haitanensis . abstract: This research develops a coordinated control, estimation, and dispatch framework for a solar-photovoltaic-integrated electric-vehicle charging station (EVCS) with battery storage and grid backup, and reports four contributions. title: Effectiveness of Ballast Water Management Convention Implementation at Samarinda Port
abstract: The implementation of the Ballast Water Management Convention (BWMC) is an important instrument in controlling ecological risks due to the movement of aquatic organisms through ship ballast water. Although Indonesia has ratified the BWMC, the effectiveness of its implementation at the port operational level, especially river ports, still requires empirical evaluation. title: Performance and eco-efficiency of high-strength concrete incorporating a screened quaternary low-carbon binder

title: Assessment of Fire Safety Preparedness in Selected Public Markets in Port Harcourt
abstract: Fire incidents in public markets present significant risks to life, property, and economic activities. Ensuring adequate fire safety preparedness requires understanding stakeholders’ awareness, the functionality of infrastructure, and the capacity of emergency services to respond effectively. This study assessed fire safety preparedness in selected public markets in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, focusing on awareness, infrastructure adequacy, emergency response capacity, challenges, and strategies for improvement. abstract: The electrification of port operations is reshaping the technical relationship between logistics performance, energy demand, infrastructure condition and data reliability. Although digital twins are increasingly used for port monitoring and decision support, many frameworks continue to assume clean sensing, synchronised data streams and stable observability. This study develops an uncertainty-aware digital twin framework for resilient low-carbon port infrastructure under electrification and sensor degradation. abstract: Ageing infrastructure in Saudi Arabia faces interacting threats from material deterioration, altered occupancy, extreme environmental exposure and uncertain construction records. Conventional refurbishment decisions often respond to observable defects or available budgets without explicitly connecting structural risk, code applicability and continued service. abstract: ABSTRACT This work develops an optimized backstepping (OB) control by combining the fault‐tolerant mechanism and dynamic surface (DS) technique for a class of nonlinear strict‐feedback systems with actuator failure. abstract: Regulatory agencies are increasingly required to make decisions about the deployment of infrastructure such as 5G mobile networks under conditions of scientific uncertainty, making ecological evidence relevant to innovation governance. abstract: Red soil is the second most extensively eroded soil type in China, predominantly distributed in the southern regions. Vegetative measures are widely recognized as an effective approach for controlling soil erosion in red soil areas, as they enhance slope stability and substantially reduce soil loss. abstract: Background Park exposure has been linked to multiple physical and mental benefits for older adults, and their actual exposure may be influenced by both objective and perceived environmental factors. However, it remains unclear which factors cause older adults’ perceived environment to diverge from the objective one, how such perceptions vary within this population, and, especially at the park scale, what the independent effects of these two types of environmental factors are and how much they relatively contribute. abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a psychological as well as environmental challenge, and the vulnerability of the younger generation in Pakistan due to the adverse effects of climate change is of particular concern. This study examined the relationship between distress associated with exposure to climate disasters, climate-change hope, and Eco-anxiety among Pakistani youth and the moderating role of political trust and perceived agency. abstract: Maritime simulators play a key role in training and assessing cadets’ operational competencies, especially within the framework of the STCW Convention. abstract: Background/Objectives: Personal Data Spaces (PDSs) are promoted as infrastructures that strengthen citizen participation in health data governance through transparency and individual control. abstract: This review paper presents a technical overview of contemporary battlefield ground surveillance radars and critically examines their capabilities and inherent limitations from a system and signal-processing perspective. abstract: Past climate change has repeatedly reshaped Earth's biomes, yet how their expansion and contraction influence biodiversity patterns through time remains unclear. abstract: Bangladesh consistently ranks among the countries with the highest fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pollution levels globally, yet evidence on the association between PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy and preterm birth (PTB) remains limited. abstract: This study represents how personal memory, grief, and human connection are revealed in Ruth Ozeki’s novel A Tale for the Time Being through Jacques Derrida’s theory of hauntology. The primary purpose of this research is to scrutinize how the novel contrasts physical life-writing, such as handwritten diaries, with modern digital networks to understand how we preserve memories and process loss today. abstract: Indigenous knowledge transmission embedded in community cultural practices often remains unrecognised within formal schooling, leaving valuable local pedagogical traditions underutilised. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Traditional expert systems struggle to manage high-stakes healthcare supply chain risks, such as drug shortages and counterfeiting, since knowledge bases require manual updating. This paper proposes a framework combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), fuzzy inference, and Dempster-Shafer evidential reasoning to extract and structure risk knowledge from unstructured documents. abstract: This article examines South Korea’s evolving grand strategy as a geopolitical swing state under intensifying US–China competition. abstract: Abstract This article examines two tendencies in contemporary Latin American science fiction, drawing on Mark Fisher’s terms Terminator and Avatar . title: Water and carbon fluxes in vineyards under climate change – A review of Eddy-Covariance studies currently dominated by irrigated Mediterranean systems
abstract: Viticulture faces a double challenge under climate change: optimizing water use and contributing to the sequestration of atmospheric CO2. abstract: Precipitation seasonality is a fundamental characteristic of monsoon climates, with direct implications for regional water resources and ecosystem stability. abstract: Introduction Urban expansion in arid regions drives vital socio-economic development but places significant pressure on urban systems through land competition and infrastructure strain. title: Recent advances in contaminant analysis in Coptidis rhizoma
abstract: Given the clinical and international significance of Coptidis rhizoma, contaminant analysis is essential to meet evolving quality and safety requirements. This review summarizes research on pesticide residues, heavy metals, and emerging contaminants in Coptidis rhizoma. For pesticide residues, chromatography–mass spectrometry methods have been adopted for regulatory testing. For heavy metals, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry is widely used. abstract: El presente artículo analiza la relación entre las metodologías de enseñanza, la inteligencia artificial, la innovación educativa y la gestión de la calidad universitaria, con el propósito de identificar condiciones que favorezcan una integración pedagógica, ética, inclusiva y sostenible en la educación superior. abstract: Background Sex-associated differences in early surgical care may occur within individual sarcoma entities. We examined recorded tumor characteristics, initial resection location, margin status, and re-excision in extremity leiomyosarcoma. Methods This exploratory retrospective study included 79 patients with initial resection during 2000–2015 who ultimately received treatment at a tertiary sarcoma center. title: Avaliação da filtração em margem no riacho Zumbi do Pacheco na Região Metropolitana do Recife.
abstract: A técnica de filtração em margem (FM) é uma alternativa não-convencional para o tratamento da água para consumo humano. Essa solução baseada na natureza, prática já consolidada ao redor do mundo em países desenvolvidos, vem chamando atenção dos países em desenvolvimento, principalmente por ter um menor custo de implantação e operação. title: Studying and investigating the feasibility of utilizing buried condensers in steam power plants
abstract: Conventional steam power plants reject a substantial fraction of their thermal energy through condenser systems, while this low-grade waste heat remains largely unutilized. This study proposes and evaluates a novel integrated concept in which buried condenser pipelines simultaneously function as a condenser cooling system and a seasonal thermal energy storage (STES) medium by storing rejected heat within the surrounding soil for subsequent winter recovery. abstract: This study assessed the level of AI-induced technostress among students in selected secondary schools in Mbo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. title: Unlocking the future of farming: How digitalization transforms agriculture and enhances food security in rural China
abstract: Farm digitalization is necessary to transform traditional agriculture into sustainable food production systems to feed millions of undernourished people worldwide. The adoption of digitalization at the farm level is affected by many factors, including sociodemographic characteristics, perceptions of farm managers, and entrepreneurial mindset of farmers. Therefore, this study explores the factors affecting the adoption of digitalization at the farm level and its subsequent impact on the diet quality and food security of rural households in China. abstract: A fossil deer skeleton, including cranial appendages, of an intermediate-aged individual, as indicated by the wear stage of the M3/m3, was newly discovered from the Lower Miocene Togari Member (ca. 18 Ma) of the Akeyo Formation, Mizunami Group in central Japan and classified as a new species of Procervulus (Cervidae, Artiodactyla, Mammalia), P. mizunami sp. nov . title: Dedicated Convection Window Design for Activating Internal Self‐Generation Convection to Accumulate Vapor Diffusion
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation technology offers a groundbreaking approach to water treatment. However, the relentless pursuit of high energy efficiency has encountered a bottleneck in vapor generation, necessitating consideration of vapor diffusion. title: A multi-scale framework for identifying and validating managed aquifer recharge sites in semi-arid Kazakhstan
abstract: Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) has emerged as an effective approach for enhancing groundwater resources in water-scarce regions under increasing climate variability and growing water demand. However, most GIS-based MAR studies are limited to regional suitability mapping, whereas the hydrogeological feasibility of identified sites is rarely verified under field conditions. This study presents a multi-scale framework integrating regional GIS-based screening with detailed site-scale verification to improve the reliability of MAR suitability assessment in southeastern Kazakhstan. title: SCADA-based multiobjective calibration of hydraulic models for multi-fluid petroleum pipelines
abstract: Cross-country, multi-fluid pipeline networks are critical for petroleum transport, yet their operation remains challenging because of dynamic hydraulic conditions, fluid transitions, and limited diagnostic capability between periodic inspections. This study presents a SCADA-based calibration framework that transforms routine operational data into a well-calibrated, system-wide hydraulic model for multi-fluid petroleum pipelines. title: Rising stroke burden in Uganda: A national time-series analysis and forecasts, 2016–2028
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low- and middle-income Countries. However, evidence on national temporal trends and potential impacts in Uganda remains limited. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028. abstract: Wax accumulation and gel formation remain critical flow assurance obstacles in the extraction and conveyance of waxy crude oils, whereby precipitation, crystal development, aggregation, ageing, rheological behavior, and wall deposition are interrelated yet distinct processes. title: Chemical Equilibrium Modulated Crystallization of 2D Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance and Robust Dual‐Mode Photonic Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum‐well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection. title: Transforming Contingency Plans into BPMN-Based Disaster Management Workflows: A Design Science Research Study in Agam Regency
abstract: This study addresses the operational bottlenecks in regional disaster management caused by static, narrative-based Contingency Plans. It aims to bridge the semantic gap between legal bureaucratic prose and machine-readable BPMN workflow specifications to facilitate modern e-Government integration in Agam Regency. We applied a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to systematically extract and transform passive policy texts into structured Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) workflows. title: Reclaimed water in agriculture: A transnational strategy for a more water-resilient SUDOE
abstract: Reclaimed water in agriculture: A transnational strategy for a more water-resilient SUDOE Javier J. Cancela and María Huerta, discuss how the I-ReWater Strategy aims to make reclaimed water a safe, reliable resource for more water-resilient agriculture. Water scarcity is no longer an occasional challenge for south-west Europe. Longer droughts, rising temperatures and growing competition for freshwater are placing increasing pressure on agriculture. At the same time, large volumes of treated urban wastewater are still discharged without being reused.

title: Mapping Digital Platforms and Their Infrastructural Foundations for Biodiversity: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss is increasingly recognized as a grand challenge requiring new forms of innovation, coordination, and knowledge integration across organizational and institutional boundaries. While digital technologies have substantially advanced how biodiversity is monitored, measured, and managed, less is known about how digital platforms and their underlying infrastructures can support innovation processes aimed at biodiversity protection and regeneration. title: Forest bathing as a pathway toward ecological identity: a community case study
abstract: Climate and ecological disruption can affect wellbeing, social relationships, and connection to place; when experienced across generations, these widespread disruptions can lead to collective trauma, becoming culturally embedded in identities shared at a community-level. This paper proposes a theoretical model demonstrating the reciprocal relationship between collective trauma and ecological dissociation, defined as diminished capacity for relational connection with the more-than-human world. title: Auditing platform metrics for communication research: a cross-platform case study of TikTok and Instagram engagement
abstract: Introduction Social media metrics are increasingly used in communication research to study public engagement, content visibility and platform dynamics. Cross-platform comparisons, however, can mislead when metrics are treated as equivalent without prior validation. This article examines this problem through a methodological case study of TikTok and Instagram engagement associated with UAE and Dubai tourism content. title: Antioxidant activity and formulation development of cucumber (Cucumis sativus) extract for an under-eye hydrogel mask
abstract: The periorbital region is susceptible to oxidative stress and visible signs of skin aging. Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) is a natural source of antioxidant-related constituents. This study compared ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) and shaking extraction (SKE) of cucumber and developed an antioxidant-oriented under-eye hydrogel mask. title: Complementary root and mycorrhizal foraging strategies for phosphorus acquisition among arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal trees in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) availability is widely recognized as an important constraint on plant growth in many subtropical forest ecosystems, yet how contrasting mycorrhizal strategies mediate the use of inorganic and organic P forms remains unclear. title: Numerical Investigation of Flow Direction and Inlet–Outlet Configuration Effects on Thermo-Hydraulic Performance in T-Junction Tubes
abstract: Direct comparisons of diverging and converging T-junction configurations under identical operating and boundary conditions remain limited, restricting the design-oriented selection of suitable flow arrangements. This study numerically investigates the effects of flow direction and inlet–outlet topology on the thermo-hydraulic performance of a symmetric equal-diameter T-junction with water as the working fluid. abstract: In broiler pens, temperature, humidity and air quality are all controlled by a single factor: ventilation. Yet much of the control research has focused on temperature alone. This review treats the first four weeks of broiler production as an engineering problem. abstract: Introduction Escherichia coli O157:H7 ( E. coli O157 ) poses a severe global health threat, particularly due to its ability to form recalcitrant biofilms and the paradoxical exacerbation of life‑threatening haemolytic uraemic syndrome by conventional antibiotics. This study identifies piceatannol as an effective agent that suppresses E. coli O157 biofilm formation in vitro and acts as an adjuvant to enhance antimicrobial efficacy. abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. abstract: Efficient extracellular secretion remains a major bottleneck in microbial cell factories, motivating the search for chassis organisms with native high-throughput transport capacity. Klebsiella quasipneumoniae (Kqp), a recently delineated member of the Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex, encodes diverse secretion-related systems, including RND-type efflux pumps, type II and type VI secretion systems (T2SS/T6SS), outer membrane vesicle (OMV) pathways, and capsular polysaccharide (CPS) export machinery. abstract: Text-to-video retrieval answers user queries through searches based on concepts and embeddings. However, due to limitations in the size of the concept bank and the amount of training data, answering queries in the wild is not always effective because of the out-of-vocabulary problem. Furthermore, neither concept-based nor embedding-based search can perform reasoning to consolidate search results for complex queries that include logical and spatial constraints. abstract: La transición hacia una gestión del talento basada en algoritmos predictivos ha transformado radicalmente el reclutamiento y la evaluación del desempeño. Aunque estas herramientas prometen una precisión matemática y eficiencia operativa, su implementación genera tensiones psicológicas profundas tanto en candidatos como en empleados. title: Framing the unknowable: The role of language and frame multiplicity in early‐stage startup pitches
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Early‐stage startup pitches must make largely unknowable futures plausible. As such, they bear a rhetorical burden. This study theorizes how multiple frames jointly shape this burden and, consequently, affect investor evaluations. Specifically, it considers how future growth frames interact with concreteness and novelty frames. title: Visual-inertial odometry with adaptive image enhancement for low-light
abstract: Abstract Accurate state estimation is fundamental to the autonomous navigation of mobile robots. However, traditional visual-inertial odometry (VIO) often suffers from severe performance degradation in environments with insufficient illumination and sparse textures. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust, tightly-coupled monocular VIO algorithm leveraging adaptive image enhancement. abstract: Abstract The growing demand for lightweight and sustainable materials has prompted the development of natural fibre-reinforced polymer composites with multi-functional properties. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) invita a revisar la relación entre la calidad de un trabajo universitario, el estudiante que lo firma y el aprendizaje que la institución pretende reconocer. title: Career Anxiety Among Students: Bibliometric Analysis of Scholarly Papers Published from 2016 to 2025
abstract: Career anxiety amongst students has emerged as a rather topical issue in the realm of psychology and education; however, at present, there is no comprehensive bibliometric analysis that would allow tracing the evolution of knowledge in this field. The purpose of this paper is to present the results of the bibliometric analysis of 525 peer-reviewed scientific papers on career anxiety amongst students, published freely in electronic form during 2016 – 2025. title: “Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany (Italy): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling
abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany (Italy) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi-source geospatial datasets.

abstract: Abstract Santos and Guarujá have a long history of shallow landslides, with rupture surfaces generally reaching depths of up to 3 m. The slopes are underlain by gneissic and migmatitic bedrocks, where failures occur in immature residual soils, often at the soil–saprolite interface and exacerbated by anthropogenic interventions. title: Physicochemical quality and irrigation suitability of groundwater resources in the Feija aquifer (southeastern Morocco)
abstract: Groundwater is the primary water resource in the arid Feija plain (Zagora, Morocco), but its quality is increasingly threatened by climate change and intensive agriculture. This study assessed the physicochemical quality and irrigation suitability of the Feija aquifer. Over three years (2022–2024), 96 groundwater samples were collected from eight wells (P1–P8) in all four seasons to assess spatial and temporal variability. abstract: Biofilms formed by multidrug-resistant (MDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter baumannii are a major cause of chronic nosocomial infections and therapeutic failure. title: A versatile on-axis visualization system for the macromolecular crystallography beamline BM07 at the ESRF
abstract: We describe the design of a new dual-magnification on-axis microscope adapted for actinic illumination on beamline BM07 at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF). title: Land Cover Change, Ecosystem Service Implications, and Economy–Land Use Decoupling:
abstract: Land cover change plays a critical role in shaping watershed ecological conditions and supporting regional economic activities. This study analyzes land cover dynamics in the Tiworo Watershed, Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, for 2014, 2019, and 2024, and examines their relationship with sectoral economic growth. title: Neotypification of Three Names in Myristica (Myristicaceae)
abstract: ABSTRACT In absence of the original materials, neotypes are proposed for three names. These are Myristica cagayanensis, Myristica hellwigii , and Myristica sulcata. These neotypifcations will be helpful in correct application of these three names.

title: Specimen-based records of the rarely collected weevil Cyamobolus sturmii Boheman, 1837 (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Molytinae) from the Yaeyama Islands, southwestern Japan, with the first record from Iriomote Island and notes on adult microhabitat
abstract: We report recent specimen-based records of the rarely collected weevil Cyamobolus sturmii Boheman, 1837 from Ishigaki Island, together with the first record from Iriomote Island, in the Yaeyama Islands, southwestern Japan. Adults were found during the daytime inside presumed emergence holes in dead wood of Diospyros maritima Blume on Ishigaki Island, providing new information on adult microhabitat. title: Inteligencia artificial y pensamiento crítico en estudiantes de educación básica
abstract: La incorporación de herramientas de inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos plantea nuevas posibilidades para el aprendizaje, pero también interrogantes acerca de la manera en que los estudiantes valoran, contrastan y utilizan la información generada por estas tecnologías. El presente estudio tiene como objetivo comprender cómo la interacción con herramientas de inteligencia artificial se relaciona con las experiencias y significados atribuidos al pensamiento crítico por estudiantes de educación primaria. abstract: Granular jamming enables soft actuators to transition rapidly between compliant and rigid states, yet the disordered microstructure of jammed particles has long precluded rapid predictive modeling. abstract: Persistent heat and dryness increasingly shape climate risk by extending exposure time, yet future projections are often communicated as pixel-wise changes that obscure recurrent spatial organisation. abstract: La gamificación educativa y el aprendizaje distribuido contaban con fundamentos teóricos y evidencia independiente, pero su integración en plataformas adaptativas mediante acceso lúdico condicionado al desempeño académico permanecía insuficientemente articulada. abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa se incorpora a la práctica escolar antes de que muchas instituciones dispongan de criterios consolidados para orientar su uso. abstract: Given the escalating water and energy crises worldwide, the development of passive desalination systems has become inevitable. abstract: Abstract The U.S. federal government undertook a flurry of new actions to monitor and regulate methane emissions beginning in years 2021 and 2022, including the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). The IRA and Waste Emissions Charge (WEC) represent a historic legislative effort to regulate U.S. methane emissions, yet its early effectiveness remains empirically unverified. Here we estimate changes in U.S. oil and gas methane emissions during 2019--2024 using an inverse model constrained by satellite observations. abstract: Abstract As robotic technologies become more integrated into society, there is a growing demand for systems that are not only technically robust, but also socially accepted, safe, and designed for long-term use. Biologically-Inspired Design (BID), Human-Centered Design (HCD), and Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) each offer valuable theories, methodologies, and tools to support the design and evaluation of such systems. title: Assessing the impact of sand mining on economic growth and environmental degradation across countries
abstract: Changes in land use, carbon emissions, biodiversity loss, natural resource scarcity, and ecosystem degradation pose significant threats to global sustainability. While previous research has examined various environmental challenges, the role of sand extraction remains comparatively unexplored. This study investigates the impact of sand mining, economic growth, income inequality, democracy, environmental policy stringency, and biodiversity loss on environmental quality, measured by ecological footprint, land-use change, and carbon emissions in the BRICS, G7, and MENA countries during 1990–2022.

abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. abstract: By 2030, pluvial flooding is estimated to cause nearly $500 billion in global damage, affecting 54 million people (UNDRR, 2015) each year. abstract: Montane forests of the Tropical Andes are among the most diverse and endemic-rich ecosystems in the world; however, they remain insufficiently documented, particularly in remote and topographically complex landscapes. abstract: Le recours à l'automédication constitue un enjeu majeur de santé publique dans les pays en développement, particulièrement dans les milieux urbains précaires où les contraintes économiques et l'accès limité aux soins favorisent cette pratique. title: Sustainability stories in Swedish riding schools: an ecolinguistic analysis of policy documents and interviews
abstract: The equine sector provides employment opportunities and leisure activities for a substantial number of people in Sweden. Although these activities are closely connected to nature and dependent on ecosystem services, the sector faces significant ecological challenges. This article explores how representatives of the equine sector—particularly riding schools—conceptualize and articulate their work with environmental sustainability in policy documents and “talk about” everyday practice. The analysis is informed by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and grounded in an ecolinguistic framework
journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Integrated orthophoto-GPR-GOCAD modeling for shallow cavity detection: a case study in Qinglong County, China
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) geological modeling is an essential tool for assessing digital mine safety and detecting underground cavities. This study systematically reviews the capabilities, advantages, and limitations of mainstream 3D geological modeling software, integrating orthophoto imagery and ground-penetrating radar (GPR) data with the GOCAD platform to construct a three-dimensional model of shallow cavity-related anomalies in Qinglong Manchu Autonomous County, Hebei Province. title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. abstract: Abstract Surface texturing has been widely used to improve the performance of friction pairs. title: Inteligencia Artificial y Emprendimiento: Oportunidades, Barreras y Modelos de Adopción en el Contexto Empresarial Ecuatoriano
abstract: La disponibilidad de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) contrasta con las dificultades de las empresas de menor tamaño para integrarlas en sus operaciones. En Ecuador, este problema se agrava por la dispersión de la evidencia y la confusión entre digitalización, expectativas y adopción efectiva. El objetivo fue analizar las oportunidades y barreras documentadas para el emprendimiento ecuatoriano y examinar el alcance de TAM, UTAUT y la teoría de difusión de innovaciones como marcos interpretativos. title: Characterisation and modelling of lightning strokes as point events in time and space
abstract: Abstract. Lightning is a spatio-temporal phenomenon comprised of individual strikes with specific occurrence times and spatial coordinates. This study models and characterises lightning strikes from single thunderstorms, treating each strike as a point event. Utilising real-world datasets, we characterise and model lightning strikes’ physical properties. Our analysis involves two severe UK thunderstorm systems selected based on published synoptic analyses. journal: Natural hazards and earth system sciences

title: Lightning Overvoltage Protection Technologies for High‐Speed Railway Traction Power Supply Systems: Current Status and Future Prospects
abstract: ABSTRACT The traction power supply system of high‐speed railways is exposed to complex lightning environments over the long term. Overvoltage generated by direct lightning or induced lightning can propagate along the overhead contact line, traction substations, onboard high‐voltage system and mobile grounding system, thereby threatening equipment insulation and affecting the reliable operation of the system. title: Inteligencia artificial en la administración de justicia penal: garantías y desafíos constitucionales en Ecuador
abstract: La inteligencia artificial en la justicia penal promete celeridad y apoyo a la decisión, pero puede comprometer la motivación, la defensa, la presunción de inocencia y la imparcialidad judicial. El estudio analizó su uso en la justicia penal ecuatoriana desde las garantías constitucionales. Con enfoque cualitativo descriptivo-analítico, se analizaron documentalmente la Constitución, el Código Orgánico Integral Penal, el Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial, la ley de protección de datos personales, jurisprudencia constitucional y doctrina indexada. title: The Geographic Moran Effect: Theory, Methods, and Interpretation
abstract: ABSTRACT The Moran effect traditionally refers to the synchronization of population dynamics driven by shared environmental forcing rather than direct interactions among populations. Although extensively studied in population ecology, the Moran effect has received limited attention in geography, and its applicability remains insufficiently explored. In this study, we build upon the classical Moran effect in population ecology as a conceptual foundation, developing a more comprehensive conceptual framework in a geographic context. title: Location Optimization Using Wireless Sensor Network with Blockchain: A Trust-Aware, Multi-Objective Framework

title: Chronic circadian misalignment in military personnel: a potential contributor to neuroinflammation risk
abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to neurological disorders; however, its role is often viewed as a secondary consequence rather than a primary driver of brain dysfunction. We argue that chronic circadian misalignment should be reconceptualized as a potential, modifiable contributor to neuroinflammatory risk, rather than viewed solely as a secondary consequence. title: Integration of Green Economy and Social Entrepreneurship for Sustainable Regional Development: Evidence from Community Empowerment Programs in North Sumatra
abstract: This study examines how the integration of green economy practices and social entrepreneurship shapes sustainable regional development through community empowerment programs in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Employing a mixed methods sequential explanatory design, the study combines quantitative survey analysis using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with qualitative in-depth interviews to explain how ecological efficiency and socially driven innovation jointly strengthen household economic capacity and regional resilience. title: Assessing Land Use and Land Cover Change in the Jamanxim River Region (Brazilian Amazon) from 2015 to 2025 Using CBERS-4/PAN Imagery
abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) changes in the Amazon are among the main drivers of biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and the intensification of climate change. This study aimed to analyze the multitemporal dynamics of LULC around the Jamanxim River, Pará, Brazilian Amazon, between 2015 and 2025, using high-resolution imagery from the CBERS-4/PAN satellite. The study area covers 492.74 km², including part of the Jamanxim National Forest, a conservation unit under strong pressure from agricultural expansion and logging activities. title: TCLNet: A Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection
abstract: Infrared object detection plays an important role in low-light and complex-environment perception. However, infrared images often exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio, weak target-background contrast, and limited texture information, which can degrade detection performance in small-target and cluttered-background scenarios while making it difficult to balance detection accuracy and model complexity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TCLNet, a Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection. title: Decentering the Sharia Court: Practical Authority and Islamic Legal Pluralism in Sierra Leone
abstract: Scholarship on Islamic legal pluralism has largely taken the Sharia court as its measure of institutional significance, asking how Islamic norms are incorporated, accommodated, or made enforceable by the state. Sierra Leone resists that starting point. Its Constitution and the local courts Act 2011 recognise customary adjudication, and the Mohammedan Marriage Act gives civil effect to Muslim marriages, yet no Sharia court exists and no Islamic adjudicatory jurisdiction has been delegated to any religious institution. This article asks how Sharia-informed mediation acquires practical authority

title: La regulación de jueces basados en IA en los sistemas judiciales: estándares internacionales, principios rectores y vacíos normativos
abstract: La integración de sistemas de inteligencia artificial en la administración de justicia ha transformado progresivamente la función jurisdiccional, pero su desarrollo normativo no ha seguido el mismo ritmo. Esta revisión por alcance tuvo como objetivo cartografiar la producción académica e institucional sobre estándares internacionales, principios rectores y vacíos normativos en la regulación de los denominados "jueces basados en IA". title: Recent Advances in Cushioning Materials for Postharvest Application: Material Sources, Fabrication Techniques, and Mitigation of Mechanical Damage
abstract: Mechanical damage caused by vibration, impact, and compression during postharvest handling, transportation, and distribution is one of the main factors leading to losses and quality deterioration of fruits and vegetables. Cushioning packaging has therefore become an effective strategy for mitigating mechanical damage and maintaining produce quality. However, most conventional cushioning materials are petroleum-based plastics. title: Robust site-specific radiometric calibration of PlanetScope NDVI using UAS-based reference data for precision agriculture
abstract: Index images provide opportunities for monitoring phenotypic characteristics such as plant height and disease symptoms, as well as the detection of pest presence. This allows for targeted application of agrochemicals and the implementation of preventive measures, leading to increased yields and reduced environmental impact. The study focuses on the radiometric inconsistencies between satellite-based imagery and high-resolution unmanned aerial system (UAS) imagery. title: What Challenges Face Carbon Tax Implementation in Indonesia?
abstract: This study analyzes the technical procedures and administrative challenges of implementing a carbon tax in Indonesia. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, this research combines primary data from questionnaires and interviews with tax officials with secondary data from recent academic literature and regulations. The findings indicate that the carbon tax in Indonesia is formally regulated under Law No. 7 of 2021, involving processes such as identifying tax subjects and objects, measuring emissions, reporting, and enforcement. title: What is user engagement? revisited: A comprehensive review of the concept of user engagement from 2010 to 2025. An Annual Review of Information Science and Technology (ARIST) paper
abstract: Abstract User engagement (UE) has long been proposed as a holistic framework for understanding user‐technology interactions and a mediator for outcomes of digital technology use, such as learning, health behavior change, information acquisition, and social connectivity. This literature review, encompassing 367 multidisciplinary, empirical journal and conference papers, investigated how UE was conceptualized between 2010 and 2025 by examining authors' implicit and explicit definitions of UE, use of theoretical frameworks, and methods for operationalizing the concept. title: Scottmoria andinorientalis (Lecythidaceae): a new species from the southeastern Andean slopes of Ecuador
abstract: Background and Aims: Scottmoria is a monophyletic genus of Neotropical Lecythidaceae that encompasses 46 species, ranging from Honduras to Bolivia. During the revision of the genus, a new species from the Andean slopes of southeastern Ecuador has been found, that is formally described and presented here. Methods: All specimens in the herbaria AAU, B, COL, GB, GUAY, K, LOJA, MO, NY, QCA, QCNE, and US were studied. Measurements were done from dried herbarium specimens, fresh and preserved material. title: Soil–diversity relationships in refugial endemic coniferous forests of the Balkan Peninsula
abstract: Background Refugial coniferous forests of South-East Europe represent unique and poorly studied forest ecosystems. Shaped by contrasting maritime and continental climatic influences and complex orography, these forests support several endemic and relict tree species. Methods We investigated soil and vegetation properties and their relationships in pure stands of Serbian spruce ( Picea omorika (Pančić) Purk.), Macedonian pine ( Pinus peuce Griseb.) and Bosnian pine ( Pinus heldreichii Christ.). journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: Ancient Greek votive epigraphy: Ancient religion between individual choice and cultural trends
abstract: Ancient votive inscriptions, numbering in the tens of thousands across the Mediterranean, offer direct evidence for religious practice but have rarely been studied comprehensively across time and space due to their sheer volume. This paper presents a "distant reading" analysis of approximately 11,000 Greek dedicatory inscriptions (sixth century BCE - seventh century CE) drawn primarily from the GIST/I.PHI digital corpus. title: Leadership Communication in the Implementation of Technology-Based Learning in Rural Junior High Schools
abstract: Background: Digital transformation in education requires school leaders to coordinate technology, human resources, and communication effectively, particularly in rural schools where infrastructure, digital literacy, and access to technological resources remain limited. In such settings, leadership communication is important for reducing resistance to technological change, strengthening teachers’ readiness, and facilitating the effective integration of technology into teaching and learning. title: Influence of differential structural deformation on pore structure and fractal characteristics of shale reservoirs: a case study of the Longmaxi Formation in the Yongchuan area, South Sichuan Basin
abstract: In complex structural settings, clarifying the influence of differential structural deformation on reservoir pore systems is crucial for shale gas exploration. This study investigates the shale reservoirs of the first member of the Longmaxi Formation in the Yongchuan area of the Sichuan Basin, with emphasis on the effects of differential structural deformation on pore characteristics and their fractal properties. title: The proof-of-concept for raindrop size distribution retrieval using combined dual-frequency radar DFR
abstract: Abstract. Accurate retrieval of raindrop size distributions (DSDs) is essential for understanding cloud and precipitation microphysics. The dual-frequency ratio (DFR) measured by dual-frequency radars is independent of the normalized intercept parameter (Nw) and depends solely on the mass-weighted mean diameter (Dm). title: Integrated biomass-to-energy and wastewater resource recovery in Southern Ghour, the lowest land elevation on earth: Opportunities for sustainable energy and water management
abstract: Jordan's energy security is essential given the nation's heavy reliance on imported oil and gas. Southern Ghour is a distinctive arid agricultural zone situated on the Earth's lowest land elevation, closely linked to energy demand, agricultural waste generation, and water scarcity. Between 2019 and 2024, Southern Ghour generated approximately 84,134 tons of waste and residues annually, including 31,554 tons of agricultural byproducts and 52,580 tons of animal waste. title: Effects of transient surface water–groundwater exchange on the transport of organic micropollutants: temporary storage, retardation, and remobilization
abstract: Surface water–groundwater (SW–GW) interfaces are commonly evaluated as steady attenuation barriers, although field conditions are rarely steady. Storms, floods, seasonal stage fluctuations, tides, pumping, and managed recharge reconfigure exchange fluxes and flow paths. This critical review synthesizes how transient exchange alters organic micropollutant (OMP) transport and fate, distinguishing direct OMP observations from hydrological analogy, controlled experiments, models, and conceptual inference. title: Quantifying Temperature‐Driven Surface Ozone Formation: Insights From Field Observations
abstract: Abstract Tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) pollution has emerged as an increasingly prominent environmental challenge, especially in the context of global warming. This study quantitatively assessed key factors influencing O 3 formation using field observations in cities spanning from northern to southern China and eastern China (Beijing, Haikou, and Suzhou) combined with an interpretable XGBoost‐SHAP model. title: A validated ordinal diagrammatic severity scale for zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Cucurbita moschata: Screening for tolerant accessions in Peru
abstract: The squash (Cucurbita moschata), a landrace crop with a denomination of origin in Lambayeque, Peru, represents a valuable genetic resource with potential for tolerance or resistance to potyviruses. Among these, zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV) is one of the most destructive viral pathogens affecting cucurbits worldwide. This study aimed validate a diagrammatic ordinal scale for assessing ZYMV disease severity under field conditions and to identify resistant accessions. title: Occupational Networks: Labor Market Structure and Gender Gap in Argentina
abstract: Este trabajo analiza la estructura del mercado laboral argentino mediante un enfoque de redes complejas que vincula ocupaciones (CIUO-08) y ramas de actividad económica (CAES 1.0). Utilizando microdatos de las encuestas ENES (2019) y ESAyPP (2021), se construye una red bipartita de alta resolución y sus correspondientes proyecciones unipartitas para desentrañar patrones de interdependencia no visibles con métodos tradicionales. abstract: Background Antibiotic resistance is currently a global concern, leading to serious complications in both clinical and non-clinical settings, and is particularly dreaded in developing countries. In the search for alternative treatments against bacterial infections, nanotechnology has opened up unexpected new horizons in the scientific world, thanks to the great variety of available nanomaterials that have potential antimicrobial activity.
