title: Assessment of heat index variability and urban heat island dynamics across Abeokuta and Shagamu, Southwestern Nigeria
abstract: Southwestern Nigeria is undergoing rapid land-use change that is intensifying urban warming, yet empirical evidence remains limited for cities such as Abeokuta and Shagamu. This study assessed heat conditions by analysing Heat Index (HI) values derived from temperature and relative humidity measured at sixteen sites between February 2020 and March 2021 using digital temperature–humidity loggers. Sites were classified as urban or rural through field observations and validated using remote-sensing land cover analysis within a 1 km buffer. title: ChatGPT, integridad académica y plagio: percepciones de estudiantes universitarios de educación
abstract: El uso de ChatGPT en la educación superior plantea desafíos para distinguir entre el apoyo tecnológico y la sustitución del trabajo intelectual. Este estudio analizó las perspectivas de los estudiantes sobre su uso y sus implicaciones para la integridad académica, con énfasis en las prácticas asociadas al plagio durante 2025. Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa basada en la fenomenología hermenéutica, en la que participaron nueve estudiantes de los programas de educación inicial, primaria y secundaria de la Escuela de Educación Superior Pedagógica de Loreto. title: Assessing the spatio-temporal cumulative drought effects on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile
abstract: Droughts are long-lasting events that can drive persistent functional changes in ecosystems, particularly in drought-prone areas like Mediterranean forests. We integrated a phenology-based anomaly method, combining kernel density estimation (KDE) with cumulative sums (CUSUMs) to assess long-term drought impacts on two Mediterranean forest types in Central Chile. Using MODIS Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), the Moisture Stress Index (MSI), and Evapotranspiration (ET) from 2000 to 2024, we quantified cumulative deviations in canopy productivity, moisture conditions, and energy exchange. title: Invasive Predator Eradication Programme Yields Recovery of an Endangered Native Mammal
abstract: ABSTRACT Removal of invasive predators is widely used to mitigate their impacts on native species, yet the conservation outcomes are rarely quantified, limiting evidence‐based assessments of these conservation actions. We evaluated the outcomes of a coordinated, landscape‐scale American mink ( Neogale vison ) eradication programme encompassing 18,500 km 2 in eastern England, UK. title: Antibacterial efficacy and mechanism of action of VTC3-knockout Saccharomyces cerevisiae against multidrug- resistant pathogenic bacteria
abstract: Introduction Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial infections are a global public health crisis, and traditional antibiotic therapies are becoming increasingly ineffective. Probiotics represent a promising strategy in this context. Methods In this study, we examined the antibacterial activity and mechanism of action of Saccharomyces cerevisiae with VTC3 gene knockout ( VTC3- KO). title: Drone data enables high-resolution mapping and reveals hydro-topographic properties of high Arctic tundra vegetation
abstract: Abstract High Arctic tundra vegetation is highly fragmented, reflecting micro-topographical heterogeneity that governs local patterns of snow accumulation and soil moisture, and thus the distribution of plant communities. In this case study from Svalbard, we show the potential of using high-resolution earth observation data obtained with an uncrewed aerial system (UAS) to map and classify tundra vegetation communities, highlighting the importance of fine-scale hydro-topographic features. title: Inteligencia artificial generativa, carga laboral y bienestar profesional en docentes universitarios en Ecuador
abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa (IAG) está transformando la educación superior, y aunque genera expectativas de reducción de carga laboral, también promueve nuevas demandas cognitivas y éticas. El estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa y la carga laboral y el bienestar profesional en docentes universitarios de Quito, Ecuador. title: Starch synthesis enzymes mediate oxidative stress-induced grain quality decline in rice under saline-alkali stress
abstract: Introduction Soil salinization is a major constraint on rice production and grain quality, yet the physiological mechanisms linking saline-alkali stress to grain quality deterioration remain poorly understood. Methods This study investigated the physiological cascade through which saline-alkali stress deteriorates grain quality, using four rice genotypes of contrasting salt tolerance as physiological models. title: Country and Culture First: Towards Relational Governance for Culturally Regenerative Universities
abstract: Abstract In the context of planetary, social and epistemic crises, this paper explores how universities might transform governance practices to support culturally regenerative futures. Drawing on a cooperative inquiry within an international research group, the study develops the concept of relational governance as an alternative to dominant corporate models shaped by neoliberal logics. title: What we can learn from nature to restore human vision
abstract: Irreversible vision loss, affecting millions of people worldwide, most often ends in the death of retinal neurons that the human eye cannot replace. Across the tree of life, however, evolution has repeatedly produced strategies that address the core problems of vision restoration: zebrafish and salamanders regenerate functional retinas and lenses, and a wide range of species have tuned photoreceptors, optics, and neural circuits to extract maximal information from light. title: Hybrid photovoltaic–thermoelectric generator renewable energy systems-a comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. Solar energy conversion systems, such as photovoltaic (PV) cells and thermoelectric generators (TEG), play a significant role in addressing this need. PV systems primarily convert visible and ultraviolet (UV) light from sunlight, while TEGs utilize the infrared (IR) spectrum to generate electrical energy. Combining PV systems with TEGs allows for more comprehensive utilization of the solar spectrum, resulting in improved energy production. title: Spatiotemporal evolution and coupling of “Forest–Cropland–Water” ecosystem vulnerability in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: The Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB), China's "golden waterway" and "green barrier", relies on its "Forest-Cropland-Water" system for carbon sequestration, grain production, and water conservation. Tracking its vulnerability and coordination on a spatiotemporal scale reveals barriers to balancing ecological security with sustainable growth. Our study innovatively proposes a multi-system coupling evaluation framework. title: Comparative transcriptomics of outbreak-associated Salmonella Heidelberg, Typhimurium, and monophasic Typhimurium reveals differential expression of stress tolerance, virulence, and biofilm-associated genes
abstract: Non-typhoidal Salmonella enterica remains a leading cause of foodborne illness worldwide, with certain serovars more commonly implicated in outbreaks linked to specific food matrices. However, gene expression differences between distinct serovars remain poorly understood, which may limit the ability to reduce the overall outbreak and illness burden. This study presents an RNA-Seq evaluation of six outbreak-associated, stationary-phase S. enterica transcriptomes representing serovars Salmonella Heidelberg, Salmonella Typhimurium, and monophasic Salmonella Typhimurium (I 4,[5],12:i-). title: Postbiotics as Regulators of Gene Expression and Enzymatic Activity in Fish and Shellfish: Implications for Growth, Immunity, and Reproduction
abstract: Postbiotics, a novel class of non-viable probiotic-derived feed additives, are emerging as a promising, sustainable alternative to antibiotics and live probiotics in aquaculture. abstract: Background Stagnant government health expenditure (GHE) and declining development assistance for health (DAH) threaten universal health coverage (UHC) for women in low-income countries (LICs) and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs). abstract: Reservoirs exposed to similar environmental drivers frequently exhibit markedly different ecological responses. title: “Special” format advertising in traditional media: ad placement, prices, and market outlook in Spain
abstract: This article aims to identify emerging trends and understand the impact of special advertisements on the current Spanish media landscape, through the study of their placement, prices, level of creativity, and the perceptions of industry professionals. Through a mixed methodology, the results show an increase in the number of these placements on television and radio, but at percentages lower than conventional formats, as well as a drop in the real price of ads despite the increase in rates, with greater discounts for special formats.

abstract: Digital twins are increasingly used as operational interfaces that connect physical assets, engineering models, and instantaneous data. abstract: Spring thaw in permafrost regions is associated with episodic bursts in atmospheric methane concentration. We aimed to analyze the genotype and frequency distribution of thalassemia in a general hospital in Chengdu and provide a reference for genetic counseling and prenatal diagnosis. Methods A total of 6,357 subjects referred to Xindu District People’s Hospital of Chengdu for thalassemia screening between June 2021 and December 2025 were collected. title: A scalar mismatch: the IETF’s sustainability approaches in a framework of infinite growth and abundance
abstract: Until recently, environmental harms were largely absent from internet governance discussions and their study.This article offers an analyses of how the environmental impact of internet infrastructure is discussed within the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) arguing that sustainability becomes a justification regime for the internet's continued existence and growth in a world in crisis.Taking a discard studies approach, I explore what is and what must be discarded for the internet to continue to operate through a thematic analysis of 26 position papers submitted to the Internet Architectur

title: Fetal bovine and calf serums differ in their contents of endocannabinoids, unsaturated fatty acids, monoacyl-glycerols, N-acyl-ethanolamines, oxylipins, and cytokines
abstract: Cell culture relies heavily on serum supplementation, but serum composition makes it difficult to ensure reproducibility and consistency of experimental results. Consequently, research10 groups must test multiple batches to ensure the functionality and reproducibility of their models. The commonly used serums are fetal bovine serum (FBS) and calf serum (CS), which have been recognized as crucial in modulating cellular processes. title: Exact Traveling Wave Solutions of Extended Kadomtsev–Petviashvili Equation via Modified Rational Sine–Cosine and New Extended Direct Algebraic Methods
abstract: This paper investigates the (2 + 1)–dimensional extended Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation (eKPE), importantly describing multidimensional nonlinear wave phenomena. Its exact traveling wave solutions are constructed using the modified rational sine–cosine method and the new extended direct algebraic method (NEDAM). The obtained solutions are expressed in diverse functional forms, including trigonometric, hyperbolic, rational, exponential, and complex-valued structures. title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Antimicrobial Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae: Current Challenges and Emerging Therapeutic Interventions
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has arisen as a paramount worldwide public health challenge of the twenty-first century, with Klebsiella pneumoniae identified as a key priority pathogen by the World Health Organization. This opportunistic Gram-negative bacterium causes several healthcare-associated and community-acquired illnesses, such as pneumonia, urinary tract infections, bloodstream infections, liver abscesses, and sepsis. journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Translating shipowner requirements into multipurpose shipyard design priorities using PAPRIKA–QFD
abstract: Multipurpose shipyards integrate shipbuilding, ship repair, and ship recycling within shared physical and organisational systems, yet customer-driven approaches for translating shipowner requirements into technical priorities across these operational domains remain limited. This study applies and adapts a sequential Potentially All Pairwise RanKings of all possible Alternatives (PAPRIKA)–Quality Function Deployment/House of Quality (QFD/HoQ) procedure to an anonymised Indonesian multipurpose shipyard. title: LoRa-Based Smart Transmission Tower Monitoring System Using ESP32, IoT, and Hive MQ MQTT
abstract: High-voltage electrical transmission towers form the backbone of modern power distribution networks. These structures are frequently located in remote, geographically challenging terrains exposed to harsh environmental factors, making them vulnerable to mechanical tilt, severe structural vibration, high ambient temperatures, and electrical overloads. Traditional manual inspection techniques are costly, labor-intensive, and inherently non-real-time, leading to delayed maintenance interventions and catastrophic structural or electrical failures. title: Geospatial analysis of land degradation and desertification in the semi-arid Shabelle River Basin, Somalia
abstract: Land degradation and desertification pose major environmental challenges in semi-arid regions such as the Shabelle River Basin in Somalia. This study assessed vulnerability to land degradation and desertification from 2000 to 2025 using multi-temporal Landsat images, CHIRPS rainfall data, Google Earth Engine and GIS techniques. A Desertification Vulnerability Index (DVI) was developed by combining nine environmental indicators, including NDVI, SAVI, BSI, SI, NDBI, NDMI, MNDWI, LST and rainfall, using a weighted overlay analysis. title: Multiplexing and demultiplexing of structured light through phase modulation
abstract: Abstract The multiplexing of Laguerre–Gaussian (LG) beams is a promising technique for increasing the capacity of optical communication systems. However, conventional (de)multiplexing schemes based on interferometry and Dove prisms are often quite bulky. In this work, we demonstrate a compact two-channel scheme that employs a Michelson interferometer for LG beam multiplexing, based on polarization division and orbital angular momentum (PDM-OAM). title: El monitoreo acústico pasivo como herramienta para estudios de diversidad funcional en aves
abstract: El monitoreo acústico pasivo (MAP) se ha consolidado como una herramienta fundamental para el estudio de la ecología de aves. Sin embargo, aún son escasos los estudios que aplican el MAP en el análisis de diversidad funcional en aves. En este trabajo describimos las ventajas del MAP para estimar la diversidad funcional así como sus limitaciones. Además, revisamos los enfoques disponibles para incorporar la detección en la estimación de métricas funcionales, presentamos una demostración matemática de algunas limitaciones de los métodos actualmente utilizados, y realizamos simulaciones que evalú

title: A meta-precautionary solution to the dilemma of precaution
abstract: Abstract This article draws on the cross-disciplinary literature on risk, uncertainty and precaution to address a central dilemma put forward against precautionary principles. According to this dilemma, weak versions of precautionary principles, which hold that policymakers can justifiably adopt precautionary measures even when they lack certainty of impending harm, fail to justify adopting any precautionary measures. institutions: London School of Economics and Political Science

title: Research on Micro-Regeneration Design of Historic Districts Based on the Resilient City Concept
abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating urbanization and frequent environmental crises, building resilient cities has become an urgent priority. As carriers of urban memory, historic districts are facing new challenges in micro-renewal. Grounded in the concept of resilient cities, this study targets the integration of energy sustainability and urban adaptability, drawing on theories of urban ecology and building adaptability. title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
abstract: The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI-driven techniques, and other high-tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross-contaminate each other during operation or recycling. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: SACRED PLACES IN A SHADOW AS A RESOURCE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF RELIGIOUS TOURISM: A CASE STUDY IN SOUTHWESTERN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to analyze less familiar Orthodox sites in Blagoevgrad District of Southwestern Bulgaria, defined here as “sacred places in a shadow” as a factor for religious tourism development, specifically through community-led charitable activities for their renovation. Observations and visual data serve as the starting point of the analysis. Next, the study applies the mixed-methods approach, integrating field observation and visual documentation of six selected sites with 34 in-depth interviews. title: Mechanistic pathways of cosmetic ingredient toxicity: a critical review of in vitro and in vivo evidence
abstract: Every day, billions of people apply cosmetic products containing dozens of bioactive compounds whose combined toxicological profile has never been formally evaluated. Human biomonitoring confirms systemic deposition of these compounds in blood, adipose tissue, placenta, and breast milk worldwide. title: Dual‐Functional Acetate Intercalation in NiMn‐LDH Cathode: Interlayer Pillaring and Electronic Delocalization Toward Advanced Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are regarded as attractive candidates for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their further development remains constrained by sluggish ion/electron transport and limited structural stability of cathode materials. To overcome these limitations, we designed an acetate‐intercalated NiMn layered double hydroxide cathode (Ac‐NiMn‐LDH) using a template‐guided assembly route. title: Review of the P-graph Framework and its Applications
abstract: Abstract The P-graph framework was originally developed for solving Process Network Synthesis (PNS) problems in chemical plant design. Using axioms-based combinatorial tools, it reduces the optimization search space by orders of magnitude compared with direct superstructure optimization of the problem topology. P-graph tools also systematically generate maximal network structures, which eliminates human error in problem formulation. journal: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability

title: RECENT ADVANCES IN DIRECT SEEDED RICE: PHYSIOLOGICAL ADAPTATION, CROP MANAGEMENT, AND GENETIC IMPROVEMENT
abstract: Owing to insufficient water, labour shortages and accelerating climate change, direct seeded rice (DSR) has emerged as a feasible and resource-efficient alternative to conventional transplanted puddled rice (TPR) systems, conserving water and reducing methane emissions. title: Association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D₃ and retinol in Chinese children (2019–2023): an isoform-specific cross-sectional analysis
abstract: Background China’s national pediatric supplementation program exclusively uses vitamin D₃ (cholecalciferol). Yet, the association between circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D₃ [25(OH)D₃] and retinol in Chinese children has not been fully characterized with isoform-specific assays in a large, temporally expanded cohort. This study aimed to characterize the non-linear dose–response relationship between serum 25(OH)D₃ and retinol and to examine how this association varies across demographic and seasonal strata. title: Assessment of the effect of pre-impact loading on the residual strength and fatigue life of additively manufactured composite sandwich panels
abstract: This study is dedicated to the investigation of the influence of the pre-impact loading on the residual properties of composite sandwich panels. The methodology was proposed for pre-impact testing followed by quasi-static and cyclic tension of structurally representative composite specimens and structural elements. The material was additively manufactured sandwich panels consisted of honeycomb core made of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) thermoplastic and two load-bearing face sheets made of ABS reinforced with 15% carbon fibers. title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
abstract: PURPOSE: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. METHODS: A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge." title: HIPA: A Human Information Processing Architecture for LLM Responses in Ergonomic Design
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for UI/UX evaluation and design decision support; however, their responses are often generated as implicit and unstructured outputs, making cognitive processes and judgment rationale difficult to trace. Moreover, the quality of LLM-based judgments may vary depending on users’ prompting proficiency, limiting the consistency of AI-assisted evaluation. title: A proposal for a systematic hazard factor analysis for complex systems using Hierarchical System Theoretic Process Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a Hierarchical System Theoretic Process Analysis (HSTPA), a hazard analysis method for a system consisting of many components with complex functions. HSTPA is an extension of the System Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), which is used in the early stages of system development to analyse hazard factors arising from interactions between components. journal: SICE Journal of Control Measurement and System Integration

title: Microencapsulation of sardine fish oil using different molecular weight chitosan and polymer blends: a comparative study on oxidative stability and encapsulation characteristics
abstract: Fish oil is a valuable source of long-chain omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids; however, it is more prone to oxidative degradation which limits its incorporation into food and nutraceutical products. Microencapsulation offers an effective strategy to protect these bioactive lipids by creating a physical barrier against environmental stressors. In the present study, low- and medium-molecular-weight chitosan, in combination with bovine gelatin and maltodextrin, were evaluated as wall materials for encapsulation of sardine fish oil by spray drying. title: Eco-anxiety and perception of environmental threats: case study of Czech adolescents
abstract: Introduction Eco-anxiety is an increasingly important psychological response to the climate crisis, particularly among adolescents, whose developmental stage is characterised by identity formation, emotional change, and future-oriented thinking. This study explored how adolescents experience and interpret eco-anxiety. Methods This qualitative case study employed semi-structured interviews with five Czech adolescents aged 15–19 years who reported concerns about climate change. title: Inclusión educativa e interculturalidad en la integración académica de estudiantes universitarios amazónicos
abstract: Context: Educational inclusion and interculturality in the academic integration of Amazonian university students are examined against the mismatch between inclusive policies and Indigenous worldviews in Peru's central Amazon region. Objective: To examine how inclusion strategies predict academic integration and how interculturality moderates this relationship. Methods: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design (QUAN → QUAL) was adopted. title: Novel index on the propensity for digital transformation in agriculture (PADiTIndex)
abstract: Abstract Digital agriculture is one of the levers that will enable food systems to adapt and remain resilient in the face of climate change. However, in addition to being generally slow to take off, its adoption is not geographically uniform. While studies at the producer level have investigated the rationale for this disparity, we argue that it could be that different countries and markets are prepared to absorb digital technologies into their value chains. This study assesses the propensity of different countries and markets to digitally transform their agriculture using a new proposed index
institutions: Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: From Battery Ageing to Water Treatment: Catalytic Upcycling of Spent Lithium-ion Battery Electrodes
abstract: The growing stock of spent lithium-ion batteries and the increasing demand for advanced water treatment represent two closely connected sustainability challenges. Conventional battery recycling primarily targets the recovery of lithium and transition metals as purified salts or regenerated electrode materials. These routes often dismantle or overlook the chemically complex structures retained within aged electrodes. title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. title: Metabolic sensing in 3D models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: probing pH, oxygen, and lactate dynamics to decode chemoresistance
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the deadliest malignancies due to its late diagnosis, extensive desmoplasia, and strong chemoresistance. Recent advances in three-dimensional (3D) in vitro modelling have provided new insights into tumor-stroma interactions and metabolic adaptations that drive disease progression. This review summarizes the pathogenesis and tumor microenvironment (TME) hallmarks of PDAC, emphasizing the metabolic heterogeneity characterized by altered pH, oxygen, and lactate gradients. title: Polymer Identification of Dominant Microplastics in Wastewater Using FTIR and RSM Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (<5 mm) have emerged as persistent environmental pollutants, and wastewater treatment plants (STPs) are recognized as major pathways for their release into aquatic environments. The present study investigated the abundance, morphology, and polymer composition of microplastics in wastewater using an integrated approach combining RSM‐based imaging and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. title: Proposals (48–51) and nomenclatural novelties for the class Mulgedio-Aconitetea and related vegetation in Russia
abstract: We outline the nomenclatural novelties that became necessary following a comprehensive inventory of the syntaxonomic diversity of the class Mulgedio-Aconitetea in Russia. This inventory was conducted as part of the ongoing project “Vegetation Classification of Russia”. As a result, we present four nomenclatural proposals, validate one alliance name and four association names, and publish five new associations. title: Digital Structural Engineering for Resilient Saudi Infrastructure: Integrating ETABS, SAP2000 and BIM-Based Analysis for Retrofit and Expansion Projects
abstract: Expansion and adaptation of existing Saudi infrastructure require credible analysis of changing structural capacity without sacrificing construction safety or operational continuity. This critical review examines how ETABS, SAP2000 and building information modelling can be combined for the assessment, strengthening and extension of buildings and associated civil assets. title: An exploratory survey of common and unexpected insect associates of Arnica montana L. capitula in the French Pyrenees
abstract: Although arthropods inhabiting Arnica montana capitula may affect both plant reproductive success and the quantity and quality of flower heads harvested for medicinal use, little is known about the composition of this assemblage. We used morphological sorting and COI DNA barcoding to identify arthropods collected from 115 capitula in a natural population managed under sustainable harvesting, with insects being the only group found. abstract: Introducción: La inteligencia artificial (IA) puede contribuir al desarrollo del inconsciente autorregulador del alumnado universitario mediante andamiajes digitales que consolidan hábitos de atención, planificación y reflexión metalingüística. title: Dynamic changes of mitochondrial homeostasis and immune-inflammatory signaling during hemorrhagic shock resuscitation associated ischemia–reperfusion injury
abstract: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock is a common and life-threatening condition following severe trauma, characterized by reduced effective circulating blood volume and insufficient tissue perfusion, ultimately leading to an imbalance between oxygen supply and demand as well as progressive multi-organ dysfunction. Fluid resuscitation is essential for restoring hemodynamic stability; however, it may simultaneously trigger or aggravate ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI). title: Revealing the Hydrothermal System of La Soufrière Volcano (Guadeloupe) Through Nodal Ambient Noise Tomography
abstract: Abstract La Soufri'ere de Guadeloupe is an active volcano of the Lesser Antilles Volcanic Arc. Its last eruption halted in 1977, yet hydrothermal activity has increased over recent years, raising summit instability hazards. The link between hydrothermal fluids and detachment landslide surfaces is well established and exacerbated by inflation, pressurization, and fluid flow lubrication. title: Recent Advances in Scalable and Defect‐Controlled Colloidal Photonic Crystals: From Assembly Mechanisms to Wearable Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal photonic crystals (CPCs) serve as versatile optical platforms for healthcare sensing and real‐time physiological monitoring. Recent developments have focused on scalable assembly techniques and the integration of CPCs with stimuli‐responsive hydrogels. To systematically review these recent developments, this article first provides an analysis of the kinetic mechanisms governing defect formation in CPC systems. title: Benchmarking convection-permitting climate simulations for hydrometeorological characterizations: a comparative study of WRF-SAAG and observation-based products in Chile
abstract: Abstract. Over the last years, significant progress has been made in the development of convection-permitting climate models (CPCMs), especially for improving precipitation modeling in regions with complex terrain. Recently, the South American Affinity Group (SAAG) developed a novel high-resolution dataset — hereafter referred to as the WRF-SAAG dataset — by dynamically downscaling the ERA5 reanalysis using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model over South America for the period 2000–2021. title: Enhanced rock weathering opportunity in Ghana: a scenario-dependent reconnaissance framework
abstract: National enhanced rock weathering (ERW) maps can overstate decision confidence when environmental heterogeneity, uncertain geological evidence, and modeling assumptions are compressed into a single suitability score. This study developed the Ghana Rock Enhanced Weathering Opportunity Index (GREW-OI), a 2.5-arc-min reconnaissance framework that separates hydroclimatic opportunity, acid-soil co-benefit, and mapped candidate-lithology proximity and integrates them using a weighted geometric mean. title: Assessing digital technology use for clinical learning in undergraduate health professional education in Ethiopia
abstract: Background. The use of digital technologies in clinical placement training is becoming increasingly significant in global health education. However, limited research has been conducted on the use of digital technology in clinical placement training in low-income countries. Objective. To assess the use of digital technology in the workplace by undergraduate health professional students throughout their clinical placements. Methods. abstract: There is an inherent trade-off between ecological restoration goals and the survival needs of inhabitants in desertification control. From an ecological perspective, large-scale planting of trees and grasses, sand fixation through enclosed forest cultivation, and rotational cropping are core measures for curbing shifting sands, restoring soil and water, and building robust ecological barriers to prevent further desertification. abstract: A theory is elaborated illuminating the nature of moral injury based on evolutionary biology and psychoanalytic object-relations and self psychology, which explains how the betrayal of a moral trust can produce not only the negative moral emotions and losses of social and spiritual engagement characteristic of moral injury, but also the entire spectrum of adverse peri-and post-traumatic stress states. title: Application of the Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm to the Optimization of the K-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm in Rain Classification
abstract: Rain classification consists of several categories of rain, such as light rain, moderate rain, and heavy rain. Classification is also useful in managing water resources and disaster mitigation, both floods and landslides. One of the methods used to classify rainfall is K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). However, KKN has a weakness, namely in determining the value of the parameter k which is not maximized. abstract: The rapid development of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology requires drone detection systems that are accurate, fast, and capable of real-time operation. This study investigates the effect of camera type variations on drone detection performance and UAV control response using YOLOv8 and YOLOv11 models. The experiment was conducted using five cameras, namely iPhone 12 Pro, MacBook Air M1, Infinix Smart 20, Logitech BCC950, and Logitech HD720P, with actual target distances ranging from 1 to 5 m. title: Photostabilization of PVC/PS/PMMA Blend Films by Metal Oxide Nanoparticles under Accelerated UV Aging

title: Escalating Antimicrobial and Antifungal Resistance: Mechanistic Insights and Natural Product-Based Interventions
abstract: Background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and antifungal resistance (AFR) have emerged as significant health risks in the world, with recent (2024-2025) data on the growth in resistance of pathogens (Acinetobacter baumannii, Candida aureus, Trichophyton indotineae, etc.) causing treatment failure and mortality. title: Cyperus flavicomus (Cyperaceae), long misnamed C. macrostachyos: a comprehensive taxonomic reassessment with annotated synonymy and voucher-backed global distribution
abstract: The pantropical annual flatsedge widely known as Cyperus macrostachyos Lam. (Cyperaceae; Cyperus subg. Cyperus, former segregate genus Pycreus) has been described under no fewer than 30 names over the past two centuries, variously treated as one or two species, with no substantive consensus on circumscription or nomenclature. In North America, the species is instead recognized as C. flavicomus Michx. title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
abstract: Abstract Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri ; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter . title: Characterization of KPC-287 conferring high-level ceftazidime–avibactam resistance in an ST11-KL64 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate
abstract: Background Klebsiella pneumoniae is a major global public health threat because of its increasing antimicrobial resistance and capacity for dissemination. Ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ/AVI) is a key therapeutic option for infections caused by KPC-producing Enterobacterales , but emerging KPC variants compromises its efficacy. Here, we characterized multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae isolate KP22-83 and investigated the contribution of KPC-287 to antimicrobial resistance, bacterial fitness, and virulence. abstract: Golf courses occupy millions of acres globally and have documented potential to support biodiversity in fragmented urban and peri-urban landscapes. Yet no standardized measure exists for assessing biodiversity performance at the scale of an individual facility. This paper develops the Golf Course Biodiversity Index (GCBI), a proposed 17-indicator composite index adapted from the City Biodiversity Index (CBI). title: Evolution of neurometabolic frugality in harvester ants
abstract: Despite the importance of neurometabolic cost in brain size evolution, quantitative data on brain metabolic rates (MRs) are lacking. We measured ex vivo brain MRs among species of the ant genus Pogonomyrmex to test three hypotheses: (i) more socially complex species have higher brain MRs; (ii) smaller-bodied species have higher brain mass-specific metabolic rates (MSMRs); and (iii) more recently derived species have evolved more metabolically 'frugal' brains. title: Regulation of Quantum Communication at the Regional Level: The Experience of China and Russia
abstract: Quantum communication is among the key segments of the data economy in Russia and of the digital economy in China. Both countries are developing legal frameworks for the quantum communication. In Russia, this process takes place predominantly at the federal level, whereas China has an integrated regulatory system in which provinces with advancing quantum technologies also play an active role in adopting legal instruments for their regulation. abstract: The rapid development of High-Altitude Platform Station Mobile Service and IMT-2020 networks introduces interference challenges in the 700 MHz band designated under WRC-19 Article 5.313A and WRC-23. This study determines the minimum separation distance to prevent interference between HAPS Mobile Service and IMT-2020 networks in Indonesia. title: The Impact Of The Family Hope Program (PKH) On Community Welfare: Evidence From Kalu-Kalukuang, Pangkep Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study analyzes the effect of the implementation of the Family Hope Program (Program Keluarga Harapan, PKH), Indonesia's conditional cash transfer scheme, on community welfare in Kalu-Kalukuang Urban Village, Liukang Kalmas District, Pangkep Regency. A quantitative approach with an associative design was employed. The population comprised 183 PKH beneficiary families (Keluarga Penerima Manfaat, KPM), and the sample consisted of 125 respondents. title: Limited efficacy of enrofloxacin against Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs
abstract: Mesomycoplasma ovipneumoniae is an important respiratory pathogen in sheep that leads to pneumonia and reduced productivity, commonly upon co-infection with other opportunistic microbes. Whether M. ovipneumoniae infection can be successfully treated with antibiotics is unclear. Our pilot study evaluated the efficacy of enrofloxacin (Baytril ® ) for treating experimental M. ovipneumoniae infection in domestic lambs. abstract: This study aims to verify the applicability of the downscaled method for identifying risk locations at the scale of building and district. We referred to the established methods used in study of civil engineering and utilized five key topographical features. title: Detection of Neonicotinoid-Contaminated Drinking Water by D-SERS and SIMCA Class Modeling
abstract: Abstract Neonicotinoids are insecticides widely used in agriculture and are highly toxic to invertebrates. There is evidence linking the use of neonicotinoids to declines in bee populations. Due to their high persistence, these compounds can remain in soil and water for long periods and are frequently detected in surface water, groundwater, and even drinking water, thereby posing risks to human health. title: 'Old Wine, New Wineskins': Prolegomenon to a Socio-Theology of the Internet
abstract: This article draws on a variety of theological, sociological, and anthropological threads of thought from Otto to Berger, from Pascal to Martin, to (dis)entangle metaphorical and implicitly religious properties of the Web. By adding a religio-spiritual dimension to the unending quest to understand the fuller circle of ideas in which technology is implicated, the thought-worlds of sociology and theology can be brought into more constructive conversation than has typically been the case in the modern period. title: Berlin Walls in our neighborhood: a social justice excursion for community college students in chemistry
abstract: Abstract Social inequalities, pervasive in the modern world, silently shape access to education and educational outcomes, especially in the sciences. Yet, natural science curricula rarely acknowledge these influences, often under the assumption that their commitment to objectivity must imply political and socioeconomic neutrality. This paper presents an educational initiative that addresses this disconnect by integrating elemental analytical chemistry with social justice themes. abstract: This article aims to develop a multimodal discourse analysis framework grounded in Indonesian national character values to examine relationships among verbal, visual, and layout elements in English-language disaster texts, focusing on the flash floods and landslides in North Sumatra in late 2025. title: Tail shedding in two Cretaceous lizards: autotomic structures revealed by X-ray CT scanning
abstract: Tail shedding is a widespread anti-predator strategy in modern lizards, facilitated by specialized autotomic structures in the caudal vertebrae. These structures include a fracture plane and, in some taxa, a pseudospine that creates predetermined breaking points along the tail. In caudal vertebrae, the position of the fracture plane relative to the transverse processes varies among extant squamates and has been used as a phylogenetic character. abstract: While global investments in urban green infrastructure (UGI) are accelerating, the long-term performance of these nature-based solutions is increasingly compromised by a critical disconnect between initial design and post-construction stewardship. To unpack this governance blind spot, this study analyzes 62 peer-reviewed publications. abstract: La línea de investigación presentada en este trabajo tiene como objetivo formular e implementar una metodología para la creación de traductores de lenguas con bajos recursos en América del Sur. El lenguaje forma parte de la cultura e identidad de las comunidades, especialmente en pueblos originarios. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the growing presence of country music on the Billboard Charts between 1990 and 2024, examining the factors behind the genre’s mainstream crossover and commercial rise. Drawing on a mixed-methods approach, the study combines analysis of Billboard Year-End charts, Chartmetric data, and song credits. abstract: Albinism is a large group of disorders characterized by a loss of pigment in ectoderm-derived tissues - most noticeably impacting the skin, hair, and eyes. abstract: Moisture-induced damage is one of the leading causes of premature failure in asphalt pavements, and the search for sustainable filler materials that can delay stripping and stiffness loss remains an active research area. This study evaluates the elastic stiffness and indirect tensile strength ratio (ITSR) of asphalt concrete modified with blends of palm kernel shell ash (PKSA) and oyster shell ash (OSA) under full moisture conditioning. abstract: Objective: This study focused on investigating the financial literacy (FL) and financial well-being (FWB) of Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) students in Türkiye, as well as the sociodemographic determinants of FL and FWB. abstract: Abstract Occasional boom-bust cycles have long characterized national wine industries, but without them coinciding with the cycles of other countries. Today's wine crisis is different in that prices for all but high-quality wines are depressed in all major wine-producing countries, and the world is awash with a large surplus of (especially red) non-premium wine. This article first outlines the nature and extent of the crisis. It explores its various causes, arguing that they are structural rather than just cyclical. title: Tracking recent extremes and interannual variability of global fire emissions using a near-real-time extension to the Global Fire Emissions Database
abstract: Abstract. The Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED) is widely used to quantify spatiotemporal variability and long-term trends in burned area and fire emissions, supporting assessments of fire impacts on ecosystems and atmospheric composition. GFED has historically relied on observations from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), but orbital drift and planned sensor decommissioning pose challenges for maintaining record continuity and near-real-time (NRT) monitoring. title: Workplace Welfare Services in Promoting Employee’s Work-Life Balance; Ecological System Perspective at PT. USSI Pinbuk Prima Software
abstract: Background: Digital work patterns can blur the boundaries between work and personal life, particularly in project-based information-technology work. Objective: This study aims to analyze how work welfare services are implemented at PT. USSI Pinbuk Prima Software contributes to shaping employee work-life balance through a social work perspective, especially the Person in Environment approach. Methods: The research uses a descriptive qualitative method with data collection techniques in the form of in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation studies of employees and company management.

title: High-resolution soil moisture forecasts for drought early warning in Germany
abstract: Abstract Drought early warning increasingly relies on high-resolution monitoring, but the skill of daily soil moisture forecasts at lead times of 1–2 weeks driven by real-time meteorological ensembles has rarely been evaluated. The Hydrological Sub-seasonal Forecasting System (HS2S) extends an established national drought-monitoring framework into high-resolution probabilistic soil moisture forecasts up to two weeks ahead for Germany at 0.015625° resolution. title: Arabica Coffee Seedling Growth under Drought with Potassium, Boron, and Trichoderma spp.
abstract: Drought stress during the seedling stage can restrict vegetative growth and compromise the successful establishment of Arabica coffee (Coffea arabica L.) under field conditions. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of potassium (K), boron (B), and Trichoderma spp. on the morphological growth responses of LS 795 Arabica coffee seedlings under drought stress and during subsequent recovery. abstract: The energy delivered by a photovoltaic (PV) panel depends on how closely its surface stays perpendicular to the incident solar beam. abstract: El presente trabajo muestra los tipos de obstáculos presentes en intérpretes en formación durante la retroalimentación de la coevaluación en un ejercicio de interpretación simultánea. abstract: Introduction Aedes albopictus is an invasive species that has spread widely across Europe. In addition to being an irritating pest, it poses a significant public health threat due to its ability to transmit various arboviruses. Despite its biology and ecology having been extensively studied, quantitative evidence of its house-entering behaviour is lacking. abstract: Introduction This study examines factors influencing Taiwanese adults aged 55 and above in their willingness to choose natural burials, an emerging nature-based solution (NbS) for sustainable urban land management. Applying the Theory of Planned Behavior alongside social marketing’s 4Ps, environmental awareness, and perceived security derived from attachment to adult children. abstract: Do you think humans are the only ones that can make smart choices? We tested whether the tiny larvae of mealworms can make decisions based on what they learn. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric simulation chambers are essential for studying oxidation processes, yet many experiments rely on single-precursor systems at concentrations that limit their representativeness for the chemical complexity of urban air. Here, we present a framework linking emission inventories, chamber experiments, and field observations by constructing emission fingerprints of major urban sources, including vegetation, volatile chemical products, cooking emissions, and gasoline and diesel exhaust. abstract: Rapid urbanization and land-use change are reshaping ecological spaces in urban agglomerations, underscoring the need to identify conservation and restoration priorities under alternative development pathways. Taking the Yangtze River Delta as a case study, this study integrates landscape ecological risk assessment, morphological spatial pattern analysis, and circuit theory to evaluate ecological security network responses under business-as-usual, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios for 2035. abstract: This study investigates the enhancement of the mechanical performance and self-healing capacity of concrete using Bacillus paramycoides cells immobilized on raw rice husk (RH) as a bacterial carrier. abstract: In the post-pandemic era, global governance has increasingly shifted toward regional cooperation. abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. abstract: We report the occurrence of the predaceous diving beetle Hydroglyphus hamulatus (Gyllenhal, 1813) in the Czech Republic. These data raise the number of Czech diving beetles to 127 confirmed and eight questionably present species. The new records likely reflect a recent European migration wave and highlight the conservation value of post-mining lakes, a habitat resembling northern European oligotrophic lakes that are rare in Central Europe.

abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy (OVT) offers great potential as an immunotherapy by lysing cancer cells and inducing immunogenic cell death, inciting an anti-tumor immune response. abstract: The Peruvian Andean Amazon is home to small-scale dairy livestock production that sustains numerous rural families, but whose heterogeneity complicates the design of targeted interventions. abstract: Science-policy interfaces in the field of biodiversity have undergone significant progress in the recent years, becoming important spaces for communication and consultation. The establishment of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES) is just one such example. abstract: Background Obesity-related metabolic dysfunction and chronic inflammation are well-established drivers of the carcinogenesis and progression of endometrial cancer (EC). abstract: Introduction Gastrointestinal parasites (GIPs) are a major constraint to the health and productive performance of ruminant livestock across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). abstract: Background and Aim: Toxoplasma gondii is a globally important zoonotic protozoan, and felids serve as definitive hosts. abstract: Introduction The phylogenetic relationships within the genus Purpureocillium remain incompletely resolved. In this study, we reconstructed the phylogeny of Purpureocillium using multilocus nuclear and mitochondrial sequence data and evaluated the taxonomic status of a newly collected fungal species from southwestern China. abstract: Tomato bacterial wilt is a devastating disease caused by Ralstonia solanacearum . title: Consumption Habits and Streaming Attendance of University Students in Ecuador
abstract: Digital streaming services have transformed audiovisual consumption habits. This study examines their use and relationship with attention and perceived academic performance among Ecuadorian university students. title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Sustainability Communication Research (2000–2026)
abstract: Sustainability communication is a strategic communication approach that aims to raise awareness of environmental, social, and economic issues and enhance public engagement in line with sustainable development goals. Particularly since 2020, it has gained increasing importance as the climate crisis, environmental issues, and the Sustainable Development Goals have become more prominent. abstract: The Indigenous education movements in Hawaiʻi and Aotearoa New Zealand (Aotearoa) have demonstrated decades of advancement and success, yet we are still confronted with a predominantly Western-centric teaching and learning context that resists recognising Indigenous education as an essential foundation for all educators (Hutchings & Lee-Morgan, 2016; Wilson-Hokowhitu & Goodyear-Ka‘ōpua, 2019). abstract: Assessment policies contribute to the discussion of broad and perpetual societal change. Since the previous assessment policies were in place, the Nova Scotia provincial government has made a series of moves to centralize authority in the province, creating renewed interest in revisiting current local assessment policy in the public education system. Groundwater in coal-bearing strata serves as the direct water-filling source for coal mining, and its water abundance significantly impacts the intensity of the mine water inflow. abstract: Understanding changes in tree cover within agricultural landscapes is critical for assessing the resilience of rural communities and consequent land use dynamics in conflict-affected regions. abstract: Treatment resistance is usually attributed to genetic or adaptive changes within tumor cells. Here, we propose that, in some tumors, resistance also depends on specific interactions between malignant and non-malignant cells. abstract: Abstract Grassland fuels can be patchy across space and time, especially on landscapes where multiple grassland plant communities co-occur. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is now among the foremost threats to global health, and the pipeline of new antibiotics has not kept pace with it. title: La comunicación estratégica frente a la desinformación digital: desafíos para fortalecer la confianza ciudadana en las instituciones públicas del Ecuador
abstract: La expansión de plataformas digitales, sistemas algorítmicos e inteligencia artificial generativa ha incrementado la velocidad, escala y sofisticación con que circula la desinformación, creando riesgos para la credibilidad de las instituciones públicas y la calidad del debate democrático. El objetivo de este estudio es analizar cómo la comunicación estratégica puede fortalecer la confianza ciudadana frente a la desinformación digital en las instituciones públicas ecuatorianas. title: Nutritional strategies for bone stress injury prevention in military trainees: historical evolution, current evidence, and future directions
abstract: Bone stress injuries exist along a continuum from stress reactions to stress fractures. They carry prolonged recovery times, high recurrence risk, and substantial economic burden, and they pose a direct threat to military readiness. Nutritional status modifies injury susceptibility by influencing skeletal adaptation to mechanical loading, bone modeling and remodeling, and structural integrity. Yet the historical evolution and effectiveness of nutritional policies intended to reduce the bone stress injury prevalence in the military remain poorly understood. title: Nutritional diversity and bioactive potential of thirteen wild edible insects in India: implications for sustainable food and nutrition security
abstract: Background Edible insects are increasingly recognized as sustainable alternative food resources owing to their high nutritional value, diverse bioactive compounds, and low environmental footprint. However, comprehensive nutritional characterization of many wild edible insect species remains limited. Therefore, this study evaluated the nutritional composition, amino acid and fatty acid profiles, bioactive properties, and multivariate nutritional relationships of 13 wild-harvested edible insect species traditionally consumed in Nagaland, India. title: Postnatal mothers’ knowledge, perceptions and sociocultural influences on donor human milk acceptance in Richards Bay, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
abstract: Background Donor human milk (DHM) is a critical alternative for vulnerable infants when maternal milk is unavailable, but its clinical utilisation in South Africa is constrained by limited understanding of how maternal knowledge, perceived safety, cultural meanings and social contexts shape local acceptance. Aim To explore postnatal mothers’ knowledge, perceptions and sociocultural influences shaping acceptance of DHM in Richards Bay, KwaZulu-Natal. title: Integration of multi-source hydroclimatic variables for enhanced drought monitoring
abstract: Agricultural drought monitoring requires integrated indicators that capture the coupled variability of soil moisture and TerraClimate Actual Evapotranspiration (AET) while accounting for uncertainty in multi-source datasets. However, using existing drought indices and model-based indicators alone can be constrained by scale differences, heterogeneous errors, and incomplete representation of drought-related processes, particularly in climatically heterogeneous agricultural regions. institutions: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University

title: Sulfur‐ and Selenium‐Decorated Coumarins: Synthetic Strategies Involving Cyclization and Late‐Stage Functionalization
abstract: Chalcogen-containing coumarins have attracted considerable attention as a versatile class of heterocyclic compounds because sulfur- and selenium-substituted derivatives can significantly influence molecular reactivity, electronic characteristics, and biological activity. Over the past decades, synthetic approaches toward these compounds have advanced through two main strategies: direct construction of the coumarin framework through cyclization processes and late-stage functionalization of preformed coumarin scaffolds. title: Implementasi Metode Fuzzy Tsukamoto Berbasis Web untuk Prediksi Produk Penjualan pada Toko Farid Mart
abstract: Sales prediction constitutes a critical component in retail inventory management as it directly affects stock availability and operational efficiency. Farid Mart Store encounters challenges in determining optimal Stock levels due to fluctuating demand and reliance on manual calculation methods. This study aims to design and implement a web-based system for predicting product sales using the Fuzzy Tsukamoto method. title: Gut-liver axis in liver pre-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities
abstract: The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis. The formation of pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive “soil” for disseminated tumor cells. However, how the gut-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood. title: The mediating role of social distance on the association between audience-protagonist similarity and fear: a case of fear of COVID-19
abstract: Objective This study examined the effects of news content on fear of COVID-19 by examining perceived social distance and audience-protagonist similarity. Method Participants ( N = 78) read a fictitious news story about a COVID-19 patient (similar/dissimilar protagonist) and then rated social distance regarding this protagonist and their fear of COVID-19. Results The results showed that participants exposed to a similar protagonist reported significantly lower perceived social distance, and that social distance was moderately negatively correlated with fear of COVID-19. title: A high-resolution spatial model of the primate gut microbiome defines niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism
abstract: The spatial organization of the gastrointestinal microbiome is shaped by strong physicochemical gradients along the gut, yet many region-associated microbial niches remain poorly resolved in humans. Here, we used the rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) as a spatially resolved primate model to profile 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and targeted bile acid metabolomics, complemented by comparative human datasets. title: Genetic and immunological determinants of mosquito-borne virus susceptibility and climate change: Europe and Latin America-Caribbean perspectives
abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the geographic distribution of mosquito-borne viruses (MBVs), increasing the risk of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus transmission in regions that have historically experienced limited exposure. While most studies have focused on environmental suitability and vector expansion, future disease patterns will also depend on host susceptibility and broader epidemiological and public health factors. title: Türkiye’deki KOBİ’lerin RATMI, MACAD ve L-MABAC Yöntemleri Kullanılarak Yapılan Uzun Vadeli Performans Analizi
abstract: Bu çalışmada, 2013-2022 yılları arasında Türkiye’deki küçük ve orta ölçekli işletmelerin (KOBİ’ler) makroekonomik performansı, özellikle dış şoklara karşı yapısal kırılganlıklar dikkate alınarak incelenmiştir. title: Early warning and anticipatory action in intelligence governance: a case of regional Government in Riau, Indonesia
abstract: Regional early warning governance has become increasingly important as multidimensional threats such as social conflict, environmental crises, and regional instability develop beyond the traditional scope of disaster management. However, regional early warning governance continues to face challenges, particularly fragmented information systems, limited local human resource capacity, weak coordination among local governments, community actors, and security forces, budget constraints, and limited public awareness. title: Determinants of continuance intention toward eLearning usage in higher education institutions
abstract: Abstract This study aims to examine the key determinants influencing students’ continuance intention towards eLearning usage in higher education institutions in Iraq. It proposes an integrated model combining the Expectation-Confirmation Model (ECM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2), extended with the construct of digital literacy. abstract: Abstract. title: What makes planned adaptation worth engaging with? Multi-rational appraisal and transition risk in Uttarakhand, India
abstract: Planned adaptation projects channel climate finance to rural communities, yet the pathways connecting intervention design to household participation are often assumed rather than examined. We ask how participating farmers evaluated an externally designed adaptation bundle and what made engagement appear worthwhile on their terms. Drawing on sixteen gender-segregated focus group discussions with farmers who had opted into the project, and interviews with project implementers and agricultural officials, we examine an Adaptation Fund–supported project in Uttarakhand, India. title: Piloting Digital Leadership, Technology Acceptance, and Literacy–Numeracy Instruments in Early Childhood Education
abstract: Strengthening foundational literacy and numeracy in early childhood education (ECE) may depend partly on how principals lead digital change and how educators perceive technology, but, to our knowledge, no published instrument set measures these constructs together for Indonesian ECE. title: Two new species of Hygrocybe subg. Hygrocybe (Hygrophoraceae, Agaricales) from southeast China
abstract: The genus Hygrocybe is a species-rich group of macrofungi widely distributed across the world; however, species within this genus show high morphological variability and significant regional differences, and taxonomic revisions are ongoing. In this study, based on specimens from Anhui and Jiangxi provinces, China, we describe two previously unreported species, Hygrocybe zhibaiensis and H. longchuanensis , using morphological studies and phylogenetic analyses based on internal transcribed spacer (ITS) and large subunit ribosomal (LSU) sequences. title: Design challenges and enabling technologies for ultra-high-speed electric drive systems
abstract: Ultra-high-speed electric drive systems are a key route toward higher power density in electric vehicles, aerospace propulsion, and industrial applications, with series-production traction machines now exceeding 20,000 r/min and laboratory prototypes approaching or exceeding 100,000 r/min. title: Biogenic fabrication of zinc oxide nanoparticles for enhanced germination and early seedling establishment of rice under salinity stress
abstract: Introduction Salinity stress restricts rice ( Oryza sativa L. ) germination and early establishment through osmotic stress, ionic toxicity, and excessive reactive oxygen species production. Although ZnO nanoparticles (ZnONPs) can enhance salinity tolerance, the influence of their biological synthesis source on nanoparticle properties and efficacy remains poorly understood. title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. title: Integration of IoT-based healthcare devices within the smart grid architecture model: a conceptual framework with economic and energy assessment for elderly care in Europe
abstract: Introduction This study investigates the integration of IoT-enabled medical devices within the Smart Grid Architecture Model (SGAM) to support elderly home-based care in Europe. The study develops a conceptual SGAM–IoT framework that maps healthcare devices, actors, communication pathways, and functions across the SGAM interoperability layers, domains, and zones, with particular attention to interoperability, data exchange and integration between the home environment, healthcare services, and energy-aware infrastructure. title: GTPase GBP7 promotes HSV-1 infection by interacting with and activating eEF1A1 to accelerate the protein translation process
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are immune GTPases induced by interferons (IFNs) and comprise GBPs1-7. In this study, GBP7, a less studied member of the GBPs, was identified to possess Herpes simplex virus I (HSV-1) promoting effects on replication both in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of GBP7 or loss of its GTPase activity demonstrated significant antiviral effects. Consistently, GBP7-/- mice infected with HSV-1 showed higher survival and milder symptoms. abstract: Este estudio examinó si la hiperconectividad y la sobreexposición a pantallas se asocian con el rendimiento cognitivo y con las dificultades de regulación emocional a través de una cadena mediadora formada por el tecnoestrés y la ansiedad académica. abstract: Introducción: El perfil blando es importante en ortodoncia porque influye en la apariencia y función del rostro, y conocerlo ayuda a planificar mejor los tratamientos. Objetivo: determinar la relación del perfil blando facial con las diferentes maloclusiones esqueletales según el índice de maduración cervical en una base de datos radiológica en pacientes de 8 a 20 años de la ciudad de Cuenca en el periodo 2022-2023. title: Reimagining Bucharest’s Central Station: PPP and Air Rights as Tools for Metropolitan Integration
abstract: Railway-station redevelopment is increasingly associated with transit-oriented development, land-value capture, and metropolitan regeneration, yet post-socialist station areas remain insufficiently examined through an integrated spatial, operational, and financing lens. This paper addresses that gap through a scenario-based case study of the Gara de Nord (Bucharest’s North Train Station)–Basarab rail complex in Bucharest (GN-B). title: Integrative taxonomy of Trichogramma vitessoides sp. nov. (Hymenoptera, Trichogrammatidae), an egg parasitoid of Heortia vitessoides from southern China
abstract: Egg parasitoids of the genus Trichogramma Westwood, 1833 are widely used in integrated pest management, but their minute size and reduced morphology complicate identification. Using integrative taxonomy, we describe Trichogramma vitessoides Hu & Yang, sp. nov . from Guangdong, China, based on a laboratory colony established from parasitoids reared from naturally parasitised egg masses of Heortia vitessoides (Moore, 1885) (Lepidoptera, Crambidae), a defoliator of Aquilaria sinensis (Lour.) title: Repurposing farnesyltransferase inhibitors tipifarnib and lonafarnib as antibacterial agents: proteomic and functional analyses
abstract: Farnesyltransferase inhibitors (FTIs) like tipifarnib and lonafarnib, originally developed as anticancer agents, show antibacterial activity against Gram-positive pathogens through an unknown mechanism of action. Here, we investigated the proteomic response of Bacillus subtilis 168 (Gram-positive) and an efflux-deficient Escherichia coli Δ tolC mutant (Gram-negative) to sublethal concentrations of FTIs. title: Is China still considered an emerging market? Divergent viewpoints
abstract: Purpose China is an indispensable and dynamic member of the global community. The purpose of this viewpoint is to consider whether China still exhibits the characteristics of an emerging market first introduced in the literature in 1981. Design/methodology/approach Two international business scholars approach China's categorization as an emerging market through the lens of the traditional emerging market definition. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the morphological and SEM‐based micromorphological characteristics of 11 Galium L. taxa representing eight sections occurring in Eskişehir Province, Türkiye, to identify taxonomically informative characters. Morphological and micromorphological assessments were conducted on stems, leaves, flowers, and mericarps, with particular emphasis on epidermal cell morphology, stomatal distribution, trichome characteristics, and surface ornamentation. title: Motivational tools in project teams: A scoping review of the literature (2021–2025)
abstract: Research background and purpose The aim of the research was to map and categorise scientific knowledge on motivational tools used in project teams in the post-pandemic period (from 2021 onwards). By structuring the fragmented literature, the author's goal was to organise the dispersed research on post-pandemic project team motivation. Additionally, it identified the industry sectors most represented in the research area. The author uncovered gaps to guide future empirical investigations. title: From Obligations to Choice: Meanings of Marriage among Generation Z in Asia
abstract: This scoping review collects empirical studies exploring the conceptualization, perception, and decision-making of Generation Z regarding marriage in Asia. This study examined literature related to meaning-making as marriage constructs, readiness standards that introduce individual decision trajectories, and sociocultural factors such as socioeconomic context, gender norms, family systems of support or control, and language use in social media. title: Análisis cromático para caracterización de dipterofauna de la familia Piophilidae con fines forenses
abstract: Forensic entomology is an essential discipline for determining the Postmortem Interval; however, the description of color in species of the Piophilidae family remains a subjective process that depends on the expert's perception and lighting conditions. This study addresses this issue throught chromatic analysis to standardize the characterizing of forensic-interest Piophilidae entomological samples in Ecuador. title: Designing a culturally responsive mindfulness-based blood pressure program: the IndigenousMIND/MB-BP protocol
abstract: Introduction Indigenous cultures across Turtle Island have long promoted wellness through language, ceremony, storytelling, movement, community connection, and relationships with the natural world. These cultural practices may serve as important pathways for healing and health promotion. At the same time, Indigenous communities experience disproportionate rates of cardiovascular disease (CVD), with hypertension representing a major modifiable risk factor. title: Elucidation of the Dyeing Mechanism and Performance Enhancement of Purified Hematein from Caesalpinia sappan on Cotton Fibers
abstract: Natural plant dyes are eco-friendly but face limited cotton application due to low color yield and poor fastness. Although prior studies have optimized dyeing parameters and mordanting, the critical role of dye purity—especially isolation of single bioactive chromophores from crude extracts—remains neglected. This work fills that gap by purifying hematein from Caesalpinia sappan. title: Effect of the C = C double bond in biodiesel compounds on copper corrosion
abstract: Abstract Biodiesel is a mixture of fatty acid methyl esters in which the chemical structure, hydrocarbon chain length, saturation or unsaturation, and position of the C = C double bond in each methyl ester influence the biodiesel’s properties. In this study, pure mixtures of short-chain methyl esters (methyl acrylate and methyl propionate, methyl 3-butenoate and methyl butyrate) were selected as model systems to evaluate the effect of the C = C bond on copper corrosion behavior. title: Screening high symbiotic matching combinations of rhizobia and alfalfa varieties in saline soil
abstract: Rhizobium inoculation can improve alfalfa performance, but responses depend on both plant genotype and growing environment. We first screened 14 rhizobial strains plus one commercial inoculant with Medicago varia ‘Caoyuan No. 3’ (CY3) in a greenhouse pot experiment, together with an uninoculated control (16 treatments; three pots per treatment). Based on plant height, root length, leaf number, nodule number, and above- and belowground biomass after two months, SJN, HH, and HK were selected as higher-performing strains, whereas XBC, SWL, and XH were retained as lower-performing comparators. title: Uncovering New Insights into Green Space Accessibility with Mobile Location Data
abstract: Accessibility to urban green spaces is recognized to have wide-ranging benefits for population health. Yet, the ways in which green space accessibility is quantified remain limited, with popular approaches based on measuring the spatial distribution of opportunities with respects to population locations. These measures cannot consider real and lived human interactions with green spaces and therefore theorize the accessibility potential of populations. title: Cover crop rotations improve soil health in commercial tropical vegetable systems, but responses depend on soil type
abstract: Sustainable vegetable production requires healthy soils. While the effects of cover cropping as a conservation practice on mid- and long-term soil health improvement in temperate row crops are well studied, the short-term recovery of soil health in tropical vegetable systems is less documented. We evaluated the effects of shifting from a vegetable–fallow rotation to a vegetable–cover crop rotation of legumes or legume-grass in commercial farms of two municipalities on the semi-arid southern coast of Puerto Rico: Guánica (a loamy Typic Calciargids) and Santa Isabel (a clayey Typic Haplusterts).

title: Unraveling the multitarget mechanisms of aloe emodin against periodontitis: a synergy of network pharmacology and experimental validation
abstract: Background Chronic periodontitis is a prevalent inflammatory disease that leads to destruction of periodontal tissues, resulting in tooth loss. While mechanical debridement and adjunctive antibiotics are commonly used, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by anatomical complexity and concerns over antibiotic resistance and side effects. Aloe-emodin (AE), a naturally occurring anthraquinone compound, exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. However, its mechanisms in periodontitis remain unclear. title: Religious Regulation as Indirect Discrimination? Religious “Color‐Blindness” and Democratic Legitimacy Among Religious Majorities and Minorities
abstract: ABSTRACT Background What is the impact of “colorblind” religious discrimination political attitudes of religious minorities? Cross‐national research exploring religious regulation's impact on democratic support among religious has given priority to the analysis of explicit forms of religious discrimination while also focusing exclusively on religious minorities as a subgroup. This article addresses this gap in the literature by measuring how neutral regulation of religion drives divergent evaluations of state legitimacy and democracy in general between religious minorities and majorities. title: Energy and Economic Analysis of Optimum Insulation Thickness for Exterior Walls in Sakarya Province
abstract: In this study, the effects of thermal insulation thickness applied to the exterior walls of residential buildings on energy consumption and economic performance were investigated under the climatic conditions of Sakarya Province. The analyses were conducted in accordance with the TS 825 standard. Annual heating and cooling energy demands were calculated using average heating degree-day (HDD) and cooling degree-day (CDD) values for the 2015–2024 period to represent long-term climatic conditions.
