title: From Exploration to Reflection: STEAM Assisted by Performance Assessment to Strengthen High School Students’ Reflective Thinking in Biology Learning
abstract: The urgency of this research lies in the need to strengthen high school students’ reflective thinking skills in biology learning through STEAM assisted by performance assessment. Reflective thinking is an essential competency in biology learning. However, preliminary findings indicated that this ability remained low among high school students, as students tended to rely on rote learning without critically interpreting their learning experiences, making it difficult for them to achieve a deep conceptual understanding. title: Sero-prevalence, risk factor and force of infection estimates for foot-and-mouth disease in two cattle rearing areas of Cameroon
abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to be a major global disease, directly impacting endemic regions and indirectly affecting FMD-free regions. Reliable estimates of key epidemiological parameters, such as transmission rates, from empirical field data are scarce yet essential for developing statistical and mathematical models to assess control strategies and inform policy. title: Woolwich massage increases the smoothness of breast milk production in early postpartum mothers
abstract: Breast milk is the optimal nutritional intake for infants. However, breastfeeding coverage in Badung Regency remains suboptimal at 85.4%, largely due to insufficient breast milk production in early postpartum. This quasi-experimental study with a pre-test and post-test control group design was conducted in October 2025. The study population comprised mothers on postpartum days 3–7. Using an unpaired numerical two-group comparison formula, 27 participants per group were recruited via consecutive sampling based on established inclusion and exclusion criteria. title: Event-Triggered Dynamic Urbanisation and Urban Land Expansion: A Case Study of Bangalore, India
abstract: Since the 1990s, Bangalore has undergone rapid urbanisation, largely driven by the growth of IT parks, attracting multinational corporations and a significant population influx. The development of transportation infrastructure, including new roads, transit systems and international airports, along with the construction of malls and other developments, further fuelled the urban growth. title: Agrobiodiversity as the central axis of territorial management: a participatory sustainability framework supporting underutilized and climate-resilient Andean roots and tubers in Peru's agrobiodiversity zones
abstract: Underutilized and climate-resilient roots and tubers are foundational to Andean food systems, but their persistence depends not only on genetic resources and breeding, but also on seed circulation, farmer preferences, diets, markets, governance, livelihoods, and cultural transmission. This study developed a sustainability-monitoring framework for Peru’s Agrobiodiversity Zones (ZABD)—collectively governed territories dedicated to the in situ conservation and use of native agrobiodiversity—and obtained participatory evidence related to the content and face validity of its indicator set. title: From Regeneration to Sustainable Entrepreneurship: Inclusive Innovation Capability and Social Legitimacy in Vietnamese Entrepreneurial Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT Firms increasingly commit to sustainability, yet ecological degradation and social exclusion continue to intensify. This has prompted interest in regenerative approaches that restore rather than preserve socio‐ecological systems, although evidence on their organisational consequences remains scarce. Drawing on the natural resource‐based view, this study examines whether regenerative orientation promotes sustainable entrepreneurship through inclusive innovation capability, and whether social legitimacy conditions that process. abstract: Abstract To investigate the spatial distribution, pollution status, sources, and health risks of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in the topsoil of three counties/cities (Shuangliao City, Lishu County, and Gongzhuling City) in southern Jilin Province, 138 topsoil samples (0–20 cm depth) were collected and analyzed for eight elements (As, Cd, Cr, Pb, Hg, Cu, Ni, and Zn). abstract: Introduction Numerous studies have used the Assessing Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA) battery to evaluate physical fitness (PF) and its positive impact on the health of school-age children, assessing various components of fitness. Despite its widespread use, no bibliometric review has systematically examined research trends or scientific output related to the ALPHA-Fitness battery. abstract: Las entidades públicas que prestan servicios esenciales a la población enfrentan cambios que requieren adaptación, eficiencia e innovación ante la transformación digital y las demandas sociales del entorno. abstract: La formación docente en educación musical enfrenta el reto de integrar la tecnología digital de manera crítica, creativa y pedagógicamente significativa. title: Integrated Assessment of Climate and Land Use/Land Cover Change Effects on Hydrological Responses in the Hare River Watershed, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: This study assesses the integrated impacts of land use/land cover (LULC) change and climate change on hydrological responses in the Hare watershed, Southern Ethiopia, using the SWAT model. Historical climate trends, LULC dynamics, and future climate projections based on CMIP6 scenarios were analyzed. The model was calibrated and validated using observed stream flow data. Results indicate that LULC change and climate variability significantly influence surface runoff, evapotranspiration, base flow, and water yield. title: Tea Microbiomes and Metabolic Transformations From Fresh Leaf to Fermentation and Gut: Implications for Quality and Health
abstract: Microbiomes influence tea quality, safety, and health from production to consumption, yet most studies and reviews examine individual stages. This review uses the Tea Plant-Fermentation-Gut Continuum to assess cross-stage microbial and metabolic connectivity, not as an established transmission chain. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents OP‐Follower , a fully onboard, pure vision‐based, obstacle‐aware person‐following framework for quadruped robots. title: Mechanistic insights into PFAS-induced toxicity: from lipid membrane perturbation to ion channel and transporter dysregulation
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants associated with a wide range of adverse health outcomes, including metabolic, developmental, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Recent evidence suggests that PFAS can act as membrane-active compounds, directly interacting with lipid bilayers. title: Structural characteristics and regulatory mechanisms of the ocular surface microbiota and their relationship with ocular surface health
abstract: This review delineates the spatial distribution of ocular surface microbiota (OSM) and its dynamic interplay with ocular health. Culture-independent surveys employing 16S rRNA and metagenomic sequencing reveal an ultra-low-biomass ecosystem characterized by restricted α-diversity. Firmicutes , Actinobacteria and Proteobacteria are the dominant phyla. Corynebacterium , coagulase-negative staphylococci, Propionibacterium and Streptococcus show high prevalence and temporal stability. These four genera form a conserved core. abstract: Abstract. Ground-based microwave radiometers provide continuous, all-weather observations of boundary-layer temperature and humidity, closing a critical near-surface observation gap. The Advanced Radiative Transfer Modeling System – ground-based (ARMS-gb) is a fast radiative transfer model specifically designed to simulate the brightness temperatures these instruments observe. title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. title: Integrating multiple disciplines to locate the origins of domestication of crops
abstract: The origins of initial domestication of crops have long intrigued researchers across disciplines, with implications for genetic resource utilization and conservation. Building on the pioneering multidisciplinary methodologies proposed by de Candolle and expanded by Vavilov, this narrative review synthesizes the roles of botany, biogeography, genetics, archaeology, linguistics, and history to identify domestication origins. title: Sub-aerial biofilms on urban stone surfaces: community structure and microbial co-occurrence networks
abstract: Sub-aerial biofilms (SABs) play a key role in the biodeterioration of stone cultural heritage, yet their microbial composition may vary depending on the colonized lithic substrate. The aim of this study was to analyze the taxonomic composition of SABs in relation to the type of stone substrate. The material consisted of ten SAB samples, including eight collected from a historic cemetery in Kraków and two from retaining walls within the city. abstract: Conventional adenomas and serrated lesions are two major precursor lesions of colorectal cancer. They arise through distinct carcinogenic pathways, namely the conventional adenoma–carcinoma sequence and the serrated neoplasia pathway. These pathways differ substantially in their underlying molecular mechanisms, implying that the risk factor profiles for the two types of lesions may be different. abstract: Introduction We have attempted a final count-down of all resources available to human society in future and converted this to monetary value for 2026. Methods Simulations using the WORLD7 Integrated Assessment Model explore how long the available resources will support wealth and value creation in the global society. title: Servicios E-Learning en la satisfacción de los usuarios
abstract: El E-Learning se ha convertido en una herramienta fundamental para el desarrollo profesional y la continuidad educativa, especialmente tras la pandemia por COVID-19. El objetivo de esta revisión sistemática fue analizar los factores asociados a la satisfacción de los usuarios en plataformas virtuales. title: Urban-rural gap in mathematics achievement: problem comprehension and linguistic barriers
abstract: Learning inequalities between students from urban and rural institutions are accentuated when the language of instruction differs from the mother tongue. This research analyzed the gaps in mathematical problem solving and the associated linguistic factors, through an explanatory cross-sectional study with 395 secondary school students from public institutions in Ayacucho, Peru. title: Natural polysaccharides as modulators of mitochondrial homeostasis: structural determinants, pharmacological mechanisms, and translational challenges
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a convergent pathological feature of neurodegenerative, metabolic, cardiovascular, hepatic, and cancer-related disorders, making mitochondrial homeostasis an important therapeutic target. Natural polysaccharides (NPs) are structurally diverse macromolecules that have emerged as promising multifunctional modulators of mitochondrial homeostasis. This review summarizes the structural basis and mechanistic actions underlying the mitochondrial regulatory effects of NPs. title: Overcoming insect pest challenges for sustainable rice production in the Americas
abstract: Rice production in the Americas has expanded to meet a rising demand, but insect pests continue to threaten yields, grain quality, and farmer incomes. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the major insect pests affecting rice systems across the Americas and evaluates the performance, trade-offs, and complementarities of existing and emerging controls. abstract: Abstract We present a statistical analysis of the intense earthquake swarm near Santorini, Greece, in 2025. abstract: Reproductive phenology influences ecosystem functioning and climate sensitivity in tropical montane cloud forests, but phase‑specific climatic thresholds and the temporal coupling between flowering and fruiting remain poorly quantified over decadal scales. title: Social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India: A qualitative evidence synthesis
abstract: Background and objectives There is a high prevalence of social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India. This review was conducted to explore the phenomenon of social isolation and loneliness among older persons in India. Methods We searched PubMed, SCOPUS, CINAHL and Google Scholar with an appropriately designed search strategy to identify qualitative or mixed methods studies that explored the phenomenon of social isolation and loneliness among elders in India with restrictions of English language papers published between 2015-2025. title: Linking Biodiversity Risk Management to Supply Chain Financing: Strategic Financing Transformation Under Physical Climate Risk
abstract: ABSTRACT Using panel data on Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2011 to 2024, this study examines the association between biodiversity risk management (BRM) and trade credit provision (TCP). Our results show that BRM positively impacts corporate TCP. Heterogeneity analyses show that the positive effect is statistically significant among non‐heavily‐polluting firms, high‐tech firms, firms in more competitive markets, and firms facing less stringent environmental regulation. title: GIS-based inventory and utility assessment of spring resources in the Kashmir Himalaya
abstract: Introduction Mountain springs are the primary source of drinking water and support the livelihoods of many people in the Indian Himalayan Region. These springs face pressure from human activities, land-use changes, and climate change. Detailed records of springs in the Kashmir Himalaya are scarce, making planning and conservation difficult. title: Practical identifiability and parameter estimation of compartmental epidemiological models
abstract: Abstract Practical parameter identifiability in ODE-based epidemiological models is a known issue, yet one that merits further study. It is essentially ubiquitous owing to noise and errors in real data. In this study, to avoid uncertainty stemming from data of unknown quality, simulated data with added noise are used to investigate practical identifiability in two distinct epidemiological models. title: In vitro Transdifferentiation Approaches for Dissecting Vascular Cell Identity in Arabidopsis
abstract: Plant vascular tissues consist of multiple cell types that together coordinate long-distance transport, signaling, and perform diverse metabolic functions. While extensive research uncovered key regulators of vascular patterning and function, the dissection of individual vascular cell types has been hindered by their inaccessibility in planta and the interdependence among the cell types. abstract: Background Persistent difficulties in written English remain a concern among university-level English as a foreign language (EFL) learners in Somalia, including students who have received English instruction for several years. This study examined the nature and patterns of linguistic errors in the written English of advanced undergraduate EFL learners in Mogadishu. title: Edible films and coatings for sustainable food packaging: a critical review of materials, functional performance, sustainability, and industrial translation
abstract: Edible films and coatings (EFCs) are promising alternatives to conventional petrochemical food packaging due to their biodegradability and potential to extend food shelf life (SL). However, successful commercialization requires balancing mechanical strength, barrier performance, food safety, sensory acceptability, cost, and environmental sustainability. abstract: Between 1840 and 1949, the Jiangnan region, represented by Jiangsu Province and Shanghai, experienced the proliferation of foreign-influenced architecture. The eclectic integration of architectural forms produced a postcolonial paradox, increasingly blurring the distinction between Western colonial influence and indigenous cultural subjectivity. This paper examines modern foreign public buildings in Jiangnan through a mixed method, integrating literature analysis, entropy weight method, and case study analysis to investigate autonomous paths for the localisation of foreign architecture. abstract: Modern technological society is highly vulnerable to extreme geomagnetic storms, yet the terrestrial upper limit of such events remains poorly constrained because continuous instrumental geomagnetic records cover only a relatively short historical period. abstract: Abstract The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an “immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said.” Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. title: Evaluating the impact of homoeopathy in managing the morbidity associated with grade III and IV lower limb lymphoedema in adults with lymphatic filariasis
abstract: Introduction Lymphatic filariasis is a major public health burden, particularly in endemic regions, with millions suffering from chronic lymphoedema and hydrocele. abstract: Central Asia has become a region in which the relative position of China and Russia is shifting in China’s favour, yet this shift has not produced open rivalry. Its implementation in rural schools is particularly relevant because it enables curricular content to be connected with students' surroundings, everyday experiences, and sociocultural characteristics. title: Naiveté or Strategic Ambiguity? Examining Economic, Demographic and Security Narratives in India's Refugee Policy
abstract: ABSTRACT The decadal transition in the Indian politico‐legal stance on refugees, from a human rights tilt to national security concerns, invites a close examination. India maintains a theoretical safe distance from the international legal framework on refugees by not acceding to the 1951 Refugee Convention, while on the ground, it extensively engages—politically and judicially—with refugee‐related domestic legal issues. In the absence of a dedicated legal framework, the refugees, categorised based on temporalities and spatialities, face a highly unpredictable executive and judicial discretion.

title: Population dynamics and habitat use of cervids in southern Argentine Mesopotamia
abstract: Abstract Cervids constitute one of the most representative mammalian groups inhabiting the natural environments of the Argentine Mesopotamia; however, ecological information regarding their population patterns within productive systems associated with natural habitats remains limited. The aim of this study was to analyze the relative abundance, activity patterns, and temporal overlap between the exotic Axis axis and the native Subulo gouazoubira in two characteristic natural environments of southern Argentine Mesopotamia: native forest and riparian forest. title: Micro/nanoplastics–metal(loid) co-exposure in rice: evidence, mechanisms, and food-safety implications
abstract: Micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) and metal(loid)s frequently co-occur in rice agroecosystems, where legacy metal(loid) contamination and continuing plastic inputs may jointly threaten soil quality and rice safety. Co-exposure complicates risk assessment because rice responses cannot always be predicted from MNP-only or metal(loid)-only treatments. title: Landscapes of deep time: botanical paleoart for depicting paleoecosystems
abstract: Visual reconstructions play a central role in paleoecology, where past ecosystems must be inferred from fragmentary and indirect evidence. Paleoart has long contributed to this task, yet it has traditionally been dominated by a zoocentric perspective in which vegetation functions as a secondary or decorative element. This article examines botanical paleoart as a distinct and necessary practice for depicting paleoecosystems, arguing that plants are not merely background components but primary ecological agents that structure landscapes, climates, and evolutionary trajectories through deep time.

title: Islet extracellular matrix remodelling in type 2 diabetes: implications for β-cell failure and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is characterised by progressive insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, ultimately resulting in impaired glucose homeostasis. abstract: This study examines the integration of Maqashid al-Shariah and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the development of sustainable Islamic economics. The increasing global emphasis on sustainability through the SDGs framework has encouraged Islamic economics to position itself not only as a sharia-compliant system but also as a contributor to global development agendas. abstract: Zuotai, known as the “king of medicines” in Tibetan pharmacology, is a crucial ingredient in precious formulations such as Seventy-flavor Pearl Pills. abstract: Background Current Alzheimer’s diagnostics lack integration with Traditional Chinese Medicine’s syndrome differentiation framework, making it difficult to fully capture the clinical heterogeneity and multidimensional nature of the disease. abstract: Improving Quality of Life (QoL) and achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in rural regions of developing nations such as India poses notable challenges. abstract: Parasitic helminth infections remain a major global health burden in humans and livestock, with treatment hindered by drug resistance, poor bioavailability, and rapid degradation of conventional anthelmintics. Nanotechnology offers effective alternatives through nanocarrier systems (polymeric, lipid, metallic, and green-synthesized) that enhance drug solubility, stability, targeted delivery, and sustained release, while reducing toxicity. title: Physical, Mechanical, and Microstructural Characterization of Guinea Corn Husk Particleboards Bonded with Gum Arabic and Recycled PET
abstract: Traditional wood-based particleboards (PBs) heavily rely on amino-formaldehyde synthetic resins, a paradigm that exacerbates global deforestation and presents severe carcinogenic health hazards via volatile emissions. To address these ecological and toxicological vulnerabilities, this study investigates a novel, eco-friendly composite architecture utilizing guinea corn husk (GCH) as a bio-based filler matrix, integrated with a hybrid binder system composed of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and gum Arabic (GA). abstract: Based on morphological comparisons and molecular phylogenetic analyses, a new species of the genus Leptobrachella from Mayanghe National Nature Reserve, Guizhou Province, China, is described, Leptobrachella mayanghe sp. nov . Phylogenetic analyses of mitochondrial 16S rRNA and COI gene sequences supported the new species as an independent lineage. title: A striking new subgenus and species of Asian horned toads (Anura, Megophryidae, Megophryinae) from Xizang, China
abstract: Motuo County, located in the eastern Himalayas and within the lower section of the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, is characterized by steep elevational gradients and complex topography, supporting high levels of biodiversity and endemism that remain insufficiently explored. Based on integrated evidence from morphological comparisons and molecular phylogenetic analyses, a new subgenus and a new species of Asian horned toads from Motuo County, Xizang, China, are described. title: Anotaciones para estructurar una revisión sistemática: actualización y claves metodológicas con flujo S0-S3
abstract: Las revisiones sistemáticas y los metaanálisis constituyen instrumentos para sintetizar evidencia, orientar decisiones clínicas y definir prioridades de investigación. Este manuscrito actualiza y amplía un planteamiento docente previo sobre la estructura de una revisión sistemática. Desde entonces se han producido cambios en las guías de reporte, en la evaluación del riesgo de sesgo, en la gestión de protocolos, en la integración de herramientas digitales y en la exigencia de reproducibilidad. title: Proton Signaling Biology From Ancient Bioenergetics to Neural Communication: An Exploration of Keratan Sulfate as a Potential Proton-Modulatory Molecule
abstract: This mini review examines the potential roles of proton signaling in the peripheral and central nervous systems and its proposed regulation by keratan sulfate (KS). Protons are central to bioenergetics and rapid chemical signaling, linking metabolism to membrane excitability and receptor activity across tissues. Nanoscale-to-microscale pH transients may add a further layer of intercellular communication in the nervous system through proton-sensitive ion channels and receptors. title: A century of streamwater quality degradation by input from urban water infrastructure as revealed by tree-ring records
abstract: Abstract The transfer of water from urban water networks to natural streams is a driver of streamwater quality degradation that likely occurs worldwide. We develop a new proxy using tree-ring strontium isotope ratios ( 87 Sr/ 86 Sr) to reconstruct multidecadal histories of municipal-water contributions to natural streams. title: Black adults show cross-sectional associations between sleep quality and episodic memory retention: an investigation of underlying factors
abstract: Non-Hispanic Black adults have poorer sleep quality than non-Hispanic White adults (hereafter, Black, White), which may underlie disparities in cognition. Epidemiological evidence suggests episodic memory may be more sensitive to poor sleep quality in older Black adults as compared to older White adults. title: CropRotationViz: An open-source R framework for multi-scale crop rotation analysis and visualization
abstract: Crop rotation analysis is fundamental to understanding agricultural landscape dynamics, yet the complexity of multi-annual, spatially explicit agricultural data presents significant analytical challenges. A key difficulty lies in tracking field parcels whose boundaries change over time through administrative splits, mergers, or reorganizations. This process requires robust spatial intersection approaches that can reconcile multi-temporal polygon geometries. abstract: Frequent nut consumption is associated with reduced cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and mortality, particularly in individuals with diabetes, highlighting their potential health benefits. This study investigated the acute postprandial glycemic, insulinemic, and triglyceride responses to white bread consumed with peanuts and cashews in three forms: whole nuts, nut butter, and nut milk. title: Intranasal CBT101 demonstrates favorable safety and neurophysiological evidence of central activity in healthy male volunteers
abstract: Objectives CBT101 is a creatine prodrug under development for disorders driven by impaired neuronal energy homeostasis, with initial development focused on creatine transporter deficiency and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. This first-in-human study aimed to assess the safety and tolerability of single and repeated ascending intranasal doses of CBT101 in healthy male volunteers and explored neurophysiological evidence of central pharmacodynamic activity using quantitative EEG (qEEG) and event-related potentials (ERPs). title: Quantitative risk assessment of BSE transmission if insects are reared on residual streams containing animal proteins
abstract: Insect production can play an important role in the bioconversion of residual streams from agri-food production into valuable nutrients for feed and food and as such advance the transition from a linear to a circular food production system. However, under current EU legislation, insect rearing on residual streams containing animal proteins is not allowed because of the risk of animal disease transmission including bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE). title: Assessment of the Financial Development of CIVETS Countries Using the MAXC-CRISUS-Based RAWEC Model
abstract: Given the decisive role of financial systems in economic growth, investment, and resource allocation, the comparative assessment of financial development levels is considered a key indicator in analyzing countries’ development processes. This study aims to analyze the financial development performance of CIVETS countries for the 2000–2020 period using the integrated MAXC-CRISUS-RAWEC-Borda Count model. title: Domesticated bacterial origin genes regulate homeostasis of the insect gut microbiome and empower adaptation
abstract: Abstract Sap‐sucking insects, represented by the globally distributed leafhoppers, have evolved a wide range of adaptive traits and play multiple ecological roles. However, their successful survival strategies in nature remain poorly understood. To explore the adaptive mechanisms of sap‐sucking insects, we established a research system using three representative leafhopper species from the same family and found that they have acquired multiple cholesterol‐dependent cytolysins ( CDCs ) derived from gram‐positive bacterial genes. abstract: Lesotho has enacted the Lesotho Inclusive Education Policy (LIEP) to guide the conduct of inclusive education. However, the extent of the implementation of the policy on inclusive schooling in the rural communities of Lesotho is yet to be ascertained. Two research questions were raised and answered in this qualitative study. The study adopted the bioecological system theory as a theoretical lens. abstract: La presente investigación tiene como objetivo general: Determinar el impacto de la ansiedad y la depresión en el aprendizaje de los estudiantes de 10 a 13 años de la Unidad Educativa Juan León Mera porque la adolescencia es una etapa caracterizada por cambios emocionales donde la ansiedad y la depresión se han convertido en problemáticas frecuentes que repercuten en el rendimiento académico. abstract: Abstract Trophoblast lineages are essential for placental development and play indispensable roles in mammalian development. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing trophoblast lineage specification, particularly trophectoderm formation, remain elusive. Here, we show that transient overexpression of the transcription factor Cebpa in mouse pluripotent stem cells efficiently generates trophectoderm-like cells that recapitulate key transcriptional features of trophectoderm. title: Catalyzing Halal Industry Development in a Non-Muslim Society: The Role of Indonesian Muslim Diaspora in South Korea
abstract: The rapid expansion of the global halal industry has created opportunities for halal ecosystem development in non-Muslim societies. In South Korea, however, halal industry growth faces challenges related to limited infrastructure, fragmented certification systems, and social stigma toward Islam and halal practices. This study examines the role of the Indonesian Muslim diaspora in catalyzing halal industry development in South Korea. title: Functional peptide therapeutics for veterinary osteoarthritis: mechanisms, delivery systems, and translational priorities
abstract: Introduction Veterinary osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic whole-joint disorder that causes pain, gait impairment, reduced activity, and diminished quality of life in companion and performance animals. Current multimodal management includes weight control, rehabilitation, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, prostaglandin E2 EP4 receptor antagonists, anti-nerve growth factor monoclonal antibodies, intra-articular therapies, and nutraceuticals. abstract: Abstract Northern Thailand experiences severe PM₂.₅ pollution during the dry season from biomass burning, yet the response to incremental emission reductions remains poorly quantified. abstract: Purpose This study examines the influence of digital marketing levers – email, mobile, social media, and content marketing – on the purchase intention of Tunisian Generation X consumers in the automotive sector. abstract: Abstract While the Vicsek model is widely used to understand active systems, the explicit relationship between structural evolution and the order transition remains an open question. Here we investigate this relationship in the original Vicsek system. abstract: Background Optimal vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty in femoropopliteal atherosclerotic occlusive disease remains counteracted by dissection and recoil. abstract: Introduction Anaemia remains an important public health concern among children under five years in sub-Saharan Africa, with nutritional, socioeconomic, and other environmental factors potentially contributing to impaired haemoglobin status and growth. abstract: ABSTRACT This article presents the results of a research project aimed at identifying the Social Representations of a group of preservice teachers who participated in a museum internship and inferring the influence of these representations on educational practice in this context. abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. abstract: Introduction The question of how individuals make meaning of, and cope with, the threat of war remains underexplored, particularly in highly secular societies and in contexts of anticipated rather than directly experienced conflict. Methods This article reports findings from a qualitative study of meaning-making coping among people in Sweden, a country that has not experienced war within its borders for more than two hundred years but that now faces heightened geopolitical tension. abstract: Background Workplace social capital has been shown to alleviate occupational stress and enhance job wellbeing and satisfaction. However, limited research has examined the mediational pattern involving workplace social capital between EI and organizational commitment among clinical nurses. abstract: Digital transformation reshapes global economic paradigms and offers a pathway for resource-dependent regions to transcend the “resource curse.” By leveraging panel data from 111 Chinese resource-based cities between 2011 and 2019, this study empirically examines whether the burgeoning digital economy facilitates departure from resource-dependent stagnation. title: Enhanced precipitable water vapor inversion and rainstorm monitoring based on GNSS PPP regional tropospheric modeling
abstract: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) is critical for severe weather forecasting, yet existing GNSS Precise Point Positioning (PPP) retrieval methods are limited by neglecting tropospheric horizontal gradients and lacking regional coverage. Moreover, PWV alone cannot reliably determine precipitation onset. abstract: Virtual reality (VR) games are becoming increasingly popular for entertainment. When integrated into speech and language therapy (SLT) practice, VR can be an innovative tool that supports therapeutic interventions by offering new opportunities for immersive interaction and greater motivation for individuals with language disorders to participate in therapy. abstract: Introduction Although Generation Z (Gen Z) is widely regarded as the most environmentally engaged cohort in the tourism market, favorable sustainability attitudes do not reliably translate into green purchasing behavior. The psychological mechanism underlying this attitude-behavior gap remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Over the past two decades, social networking services have become a pervasive and integral part of young adults’ lives. At the same time, a growing body of evidence points to their negative effects on mental health and their potentially addictive nature. In this context, the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) was developed to assess problematic social media use (PSMU). abstract: Background Pancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive and lethal gastrointestinal malignancies, and ferroptosis resistance contributes to chemoresistance. Tumor-educated macrophages(TAMs) are key components of the tumor microenvironment, but whether and how they regulate ferroptosis in pancreatic cancer cells remains largely unknown. abstract: Gentrification has predominantly been examined through economic restructuring, demographic change, and spatial reorganization, while its sensory and embodied dimensions remain underexplored in urban sociology. This study reconceptualizes gentrification as a multi-layered urban transformation regime operating not only through material and economic change but also through the reconfiguration of sensory urban experience. abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that predominantly affects elderly people and is characterized by cognitive decline and dementia. Protein tyrosine phosphatase-1B (PTP1B) is known to modulate pro-inflammatory mediators, and its overexpression in the brain has been implicated in AD-associated neuroinflammation. abstract: El trabajo busca individualizar hipótesis concretas de daños que en la actualidad sufre o podría sufrir una persona en el ámbito de la neurotecnología. abstract: Este artículo analiza cómo profesionales de la medicina, la sociología y la informática conceptualizan el tecnocuidado a partir de entrevistas en profundidad. abstract: Dairy production is an important component of Uzbekistan's food system but is associated with environmental burdens. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan to quantify environmental impacts, identify hotspots, evaluate uncertainty, and assess environmental improvement options. abstract: Introduction Aquatic mosses are recently gaining attention for commercial use, stimulating the development of new biomass cultivation approaches. This study explores the potential of by-products from aquatic moss propagation as natural plant biostimulants, addressing the need for low-waste production and sustainable agricultural strategies. abstract: Non-ribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPS) are multi-modular enzymes that produce secondary metabolites. The diverse and functionally important biosurfactants derived from various microbes have numerous applications across multiple industries. abstract: The Strychnos madagascariensis (Black Monkey Orange) is commonly found in tropical and subtropical Africa. Black monkey orange (BMO) species can strive in hot and relatively dry conditions of Southern Africa. It is one of the diverse indigenous fruit species (IFSs) in Bushbuckridge Local Municipality (BLM), Mpumalanga Province in South Africa. The BMO fruit can be consumed fresh or processed into flour known as “Nfuma” in southern Mozambique. The same processed product is known as “Nkwakwa” within BLM. title: A community-level view of Wolbachia DNA positivity across mosquito assemblages in eastern China
abstract: Wolbachia is a widespread mosquito-associated endosymbiont with important implications for vector biology and microbial ecology. However, field studies often examine Wolbachia within individual mosquito species, which can obscure how host community structure shapes the microbial signal observed at a sampling site. Here, we analyzed Wolbachia DNA positivity in a taxonomically curated collection of 2,434 mosquitoes from Huai'an, Lu'an, and Xuzhou in eastern China. title: Research progress of polyunsaturated fatty acids in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanisms to treatment
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a growing clinical burden through recurrent intestinal inflammation, malnutrition, treatment-related toxicity, and incomplete mucosal healing. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) are plausible dietary regulators of this burden, yet their effects cannot be reduced to a simple anti-inflammatory role for n-3 PUFAs and a pro-inflammatory role for n-6 PUFAs. title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Off-Grid Pole-Mounted Photovoltaic Configurations for Accessible and Inaccessible Sites in Arid Climates
abstract: This paper presents an integrated techno-economic synthesis for selecting pole-mounted off-grid photovoltaic configurations, consolidating six experimental and analytical studies into a unified multicriteria decision framework. The analysis is grounded in a one-year high-resolution outdoor experimentation (Aug. 25, 2025 – Aug. 24, 2026) at the QEERI Outdoor Test Facility in Doha, Qatar, complemented by validated analytical models addressing environmental and structural constraints. title: Performance evaluation of laser diffraction and sieve-pipette techniques for grid-scale hydraulic characterization of lateritic vadose zones
abstract: The vadose zone plays a vital role in sustaining society and ecosystems on the Earth. The complexity of vadose zones, coupled with expensive and laborious field investigations pose a formidable challenge in their characterization, and hence they are neglected in hydrogeologic studies. This study demonstrates a novel scientific framework for the grid-scale hydraulic characterization of vadose zones using the laser diffraction (LD) technique and grain-size analysis (GSA) models. title: Low-glycemic index functional flour modulates gut microbiota in association with anti-obesity effects in mice
abstract: Background Obesity has become a prevalent global chronic disease, and dietary intervention is a safe and effective strategy for obesity prevention and management. Laminaria japonica and Lentinula edodes are widely consumed edible resources in China, while the lipid-lowering efficacy of functional noodles supplemented with their dietary fibers remains unclear. Moreover, the potential synergistic effects of combining these fibers with other functional plant ingredients have not been systematically explored. title: Chronic Electroconvulsive Shock Disrupts Hippocampal Physiology and Impairs Associative Memory in Mice
abstract: ABSTRACT Electroconvulsive therapy ( ECT ) is a highly effective treatment for depression but it has undesirable side effects on various aspects of cognition, including memory. Patients may display retrograde amnesia for autobiographical events and anterograde amnesia in tests of recall and recognition memory. These amnestic effects are likely to depend, at least in part, on changes in the hippocampus. abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a pulsed laser irradiation in liquid (PLIL) strategy that concurrently induces phase transformation, morphological reconstruction, and single‐atom stabilization in bismuth oxide (Bi 2 O 3 ) for efficient carbon‐dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR). PLIL transforms α‐Bi 2 O 3 microrods to δ‐Bi 2 O 3 nanosheets, while simultaneous anchoring atomically dispersed Cu sites within the δ‐Bi 2 O 3 lattice. title: Strategies for widening participation in the biomedical science at London South Bank University—a case study
abstract: Introduction and context Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic (BAME) professionals make essential contributions to UK healthcare, biomedical science research, academia, and the life sciences industry, yet remain underrepresented in senior roles. Three barriers recur: limited access to the discipline, a weak sense of belonging, and few visible role models. This study presents targeted strategies implemented within London South Bank University's Biomedical Science Programme (BMS) to address these barriers at key stages of students' career development journey. title: Multidimensional molecular strategies for crop photoperiod adaptation and latitudinal expansion
abstract: The traditional regional distribution of agriculture was historically constrained by crops’ inherent dependence on local environmental cues, particularly photoperiod and temperature. Natural domestication and artificial selection have progressively reduced this dependence on native ecosystems, resulting in a profound restructuring of global agricultural patterns. title: Carcass characteristics and meat quality of Fijian native chickens and their crosses with broilers under different production systems
abstract: Meat quality and carcass traits are amongst the reasons why native chickens are popular amongst consumers and it is important that these traits are not lost when improving their growth performance through crossbreeding with fast growing breeds. The aim of this study was to compare the meat quality and carcass traits of Fijian native chickens and their crossbreeds with broilers under conventional and scavenging systems. title: Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies: Reconstructing Cognitive Justice in Minangkabau Legal Historiography
abstract: Colonial legal historiography in Minangkabau has long portrayed matrilineal adat and Islamic law as antagonistic systems, casting adat as static custom and Islam as an external imposition. This article repositions the formula Syarak Mangato, Adaik Mamakai (SMAM), rendered here as “Sharia Prescribes, Adat Applies,” as an analytical method for dismantling this binary, rather than treating the formula merely as a cultural description, as much of the existing scholarship has done. abstract: El repertorio dramático de Luis Vélez de Guevara nos ha llegado casi en su totalidad tras las correspondientes adaptaciones escénicas e impresas y sin control de la transmisión por parte del poeta. A través de métodos estilométricos ofrecemos propuestas de inclusión y exclusión de obras teatrales al corpus velecista. title: Climate change and citrus fruit quality: links with plant physiology and mineral nutrition
abstract: Citrus production across growing regions is increasingly exposed to rising atmospheric CO 2 , higher temperatures, and greater variability in water availability, with Mediterranean orchards facing particularly pronounced climatic pressures. These climatic drivers affect citrus performance through interconnected changes in photosynthesis, root functioning, flowering, salinity responses, redox regulation, and source–sink relationships, with consequences for productivity and fruit quality. title: Phage therapy for multidrug-resistant Serratia marcescens infection: mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges
abstract: Multidrug-resistant and carbapenem-resistant Serratia marcescens ( S. marcescens ) infections are increasingly difficult to treat because of intrinsic and acquired antimicrobial-resistance mechanisms, limited therapeutic options, and the organism’s capacity to persist within biofilms. Phage therapy has therefore emerged as a potential precision antimicrobial strategy against refractory S. marcescens infections. title: Diverse Uses of Lantibiotics: Exploring New Approaches to Combat Antibiotic Resistance
abstract: ABSTRACT Rising multidrug resistance demands novel antimicrobials. Lantibiotics are ribosomally synthesized peptides with unique post‐translational modifications (including lanthionine) that confer potent bactericidal activity against Gram‐positive species. Their membrane‐disruptive and cellular inhibitory mechanisms make them promising candidates for next‐generation antibiotics to combat escalating antibiotic resistance. abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) show immense potential in next‐generation display technologies due to their exceptional optoelectronic properties. However, their operational stability and luminescence brightness remain core bottlenecks restricting their commercialization. title: Climate shocks, disability, and mathematics learning in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Climate shocks already disrupt schooling in sub-Saharan Africa. Children with disabilities, for their part, face deep barriers to enrolment, retention and achievement across the region. A smaller body of work suggests that climate shocks in early childhood may also raise the number of children who become disabled. These three literatures have grown up apart, and none has been tied to the economics of human capital. This review brings together four strands of evidence. title: Ornithonyssus bacoti (tropical rat mite): a critical review of biology, vector potential, and integrated management
abstract: The tropical rat mite, Ornithonyssus bacoti (Hirst, 1913), is an obligate hematophagous gamasid mite of global veterinary, animal, and public health importance. While traditionally recognized as a cause of rodent mite dermatitis in humans, its potential involvement in zoonotic pathogen transmission requires rigorous critical evaluation. title: Furan fatty acids reprogram hepatic lipid metabolism via acyl-CoA conjugates in obesity
abstract: Dietary fish oil (FO) and omega-3 fatty acids are associated with cardiometabolic benefits, yet their molecular mediators remain incompletely defined. Furan fatty acids (FuFAs), a distinct lipid class enriched in FO, have emerged as potential regulators of metabolic health. Here, we identify and quantify FuFA species in prescription omega-3 formulations and natural fish oils, and synthesize structurally engineered analogs designed to isolate antioxidant activity and β-oxidation susceptibility from FuFA bioactivity. title: Oxyfunctionalization of Primary Benzylic C(sp3)–H Bonds with Water by a Molybdenum-Dependent Dehydrogenase
abstract: Abstract The selective oxyfunctionalization of C(sp3)–H bonds remains a central challenge in chemical synthesis. Although oxygenases and peroxygenases provide biocatalytic alternatives to metal-based chemical methods, their practical use is constrained by costly cofactor regeneration, toxic co-substrates, or limited selectivity. abstract: The gut–brain axis has emerged as a central mechanistic framework linking dietary bioactives, microbial ecology, and neurodegenerative disease progression. Similar microbiome-related mechanisms have also been implicated in colorectal cancer, suggesting potential shared links between microbial dysbiosis, inflammation, and disease progression. title: Seed weight grading improves germination and seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
abstract: Abstract Seed weight is a critical factor influencing germination, seedling establishment, and subsequent crop development. Khasi Mandarin exhibits considerable variation in seed weight, and limited information is available on the effect of seed weight on germination and seedling performance. This study assesses the effects of seed grades on seed germination, seedling growth and vigour in Khasi Mandarin. title: Universal features in atmospheric particulate matter dynamics
abstract: We study statistical properties of atmospheric particulate matter fluctuations using six years of daily PM2.5 concentration data from fifty-four Indian cities. Despite diverse urban settings and heterogeneous climatic conditions, we find that the fluctuations show strikingly universal behaviour in both the distributional properties and temporal dynamics. title: Classification-constrained retrieval of PM 2.5 vertical profiles from fluorescence-raman-mie polarization lidar
abstract: Abstract. The vertical distribution of PM2.5 during urban haze events is jointly affected by aerosol composition, boundary-layer structure, and regional transport. Empirical PM2.5 retrievals based on lidar-derived extinction coefficients can be biased by the optical contribution of coarse-mode mineral particles. This study used fluorescence–Raman–Mie polarization lidar observations in Beijing to identify anthropogenic pollution aerosols (APA), desert dust (DD), and mineral dust (MD) using the particle depolarization ratio (PDR) and fluorescence capacity (Gf). title: Computational optimization of diesel particulate filter geometry: coupled effects of cell density and filter diameter on filtration efficiency and back pressure
abstract: Diesel particulate filters (DPFs) are widely used in diesel exhaust after-treatment systems to reduce particulate emissions while maintaining acceptable exhaust back pressure. This study examines the coupled effects of filter diameter and channel density, expressed as cells per square inch (CPSI), on clean-filter DPF performance using computational fluid dynamics (CFD), response surface methodology (RSM), analysis of variance (ANOVA), and equal-weight multi-response desirability analysis. title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives
abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. abstract: Mesoscopic fluctuations reveal stochastic dynamics of molecules in both inanimate and living matter. We investigate how small-number fluctuations shape the collective dynamics of molecular motors using motile cilia as model system. title: Intermittent hypoxia interventions for inducing ventilatory acclimatization to high altitude?
abstract: Accumulation of ∼200 h of hypoxia exposure (pre-acclimatization) has been suggested to prevent the development of acute mountain sickness when a person is subsequently exposed to high altitude. These pre-exposures are typically undertaken intermittently at or near the place of residence, primarily during sleep in hypoxic tents, and are likely to induce effective ventilatory acclimatization. title: Temporal and production-related determinants of microbial counts in pingo, the natural starter culture of minas artisanal cheese
abstract: Minas Artisanal Cheese (MAC) is among the most widely consumed and recognized artisanal cheeses in Brazil, produced from raw milk, rennet, salt, and a natural starter culture known locally as pingo. Pingo is an endogenous starter culture generated by backslopping, which carries into MAC cheese both technologically beneficial microorganisms and spoilage contaminants. title: Animal state and husbandry context profiles in limited-access zoo welfare assessment: evidence from 20 mammalian species
abstract: Animal welfare assessment draws on evidence about both the animal’s observed state and the husbandry conditions in which it lives, but these sources of evidence are related rather than equivalent. Under limited-access conditions, combining them too early may obscure where welfare concern is located and may encourage unsupported interpretation of observed states as consequences of current husbandry. abstract: MODIS/EFFIS burned-area archives provide reproducible information on wildfire occurrence, perimeter geometry, administrative attribution, mapped area, date fields, and land-cover composition. However, their translation into proportionate municipal documentation, monitoring, coordination, and territorial-management evidence remains only partially formalized, especially in volcanic–urban interfaces where relatively compact burned-area records may still generate non-negligible administrative pressure. title: Long-term salinity is associated with deteriorated soil properties, rhizosphere microbiome restructuring, and elevated wheat crown rot: evidence from a 19-year gradient experiment and a 3-year remediation verification
abstract: Soil salinization threatens global agricultural sustainability and may elevate soil-borne disease risk through coordinated changes in soil conditions and the rhizosphere microbiome, yet long-term field evidence remains limited. Here, a 19-year controlled field experiment with an artificial salinity gradient (non-saline, moderate, and severe) was conducted to characterise salinity-associated responses of soil physicochemical properties, wheat crown rot (WCR), and the rhizosphere microbiome. title: Phytochemical composition and acaricidal potential of Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis extracts against Varroa destructor in Apis mellifera colonies
abstract: The ectoparasitic mite Varroa destructor is one of the main sanitary threats to Apis mellifera colonies worldwide, prompting the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic acaricides. This study evaluated the effects of hydroethanolic extracts from Argemone mexicana and Ricinus communis on phoretic V. destructor infestation and mite fall under field conditions. title: Análisis de Emparejamiento Óptimo: aplicaciones novedosas en la intersección entre la demografía y los estudios de cambio climático
abstract: El cambio climático reconfigura los ecosistemas, las economías y las trayectorias de vida, pero la investigación rara vez captura su carácter dinámico y procesual. Este artículo presenta una revisión conceptual y metodológica orientada a sintetizar y discutir el potencial del Análisis de Emparejamiento Óptimo (OMA por sus siglas en inglés: Optimal Matching Analysis) para el estudio de respuestas demográficas al cambio climático desde una perspectiva temporal. abstract: This study investigated follicular growth patterns, corpus luteum dynamics and endocrine profiles during natural and hormonally induced estrous cycles in Arunachali yak maintained at the ICAR–NRC on Yak, Nyukmadung, Arunachal Pradesh, India. Thirty-six apparently healthy, cyclic female yaks of second to fourth parity were equally assigned to natural estrus (Group I) or hormonally induced estrus using a modified Ovsynch protocol (Group II). title: Performance and uncertainty analysis of rural waste-to-energy systems under stochastic feedstock supply
abstract: This study evaluates the operational performance of three configurations of an Integrated Resource and Recovery Centre (IRRC) as a decentralised rural waste-to-energy (WtE) system using Monte Carlo simulation. Twelve months of empirical feedstock data were incorporated into a probabilistic, scenario-based model to assess how stochastic variations in the availability of vegetable waste and manure affect daily electricity generation. title: The growing repertoire of putative pathogen interaction genes in the Biomphalaria glabrata vs Schistosoma mansoni system
abstract: Schistosomiasis is major neglected tropical disease of humans that is caused by trematodes in the genus Schistosoma. Humans are infected during contact with water in which schistosomes are being shed from their intermediate hosts, freshwater snails. Snail control is effective at reducing transmission, but can be expensive and ecologically problematic. Therefore, there is substantial interest in understanding the genetic mechanisms behind variation in snail resistance to infection by schistosomes, with the goal of leveraging that information to reduce transmission at the snail stage. title: Assessment of forensic evidence utilized in wildlife cases in the Australian judicial system
abstract: Australia’s endemic animals are poached from the wild to supply the global illegal wildlife trade. Wildlife forensic science is applied in Australian criminal investigations and has been documented in the scientific literature but lacks an evaluation on how forensic evidence is used in court. The aim of our study was to identify taxa and forensic evidence involved in cases and highlight where additional forensic evidence could have been valuable. abstract: Situada em uma região de grande biodiversidade, a bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires vem sofrendo sucessivas e intensas mudanças no uso e cobertura da terra, trazendo impactos ambientais provocadas pelas atividades econômicas da região. Ressaltando a necessidade do monitoramento dessas transformações, esta pesquisa objetivou analisar as transformações no uso e cobertura da terra na bacia hidrográfica do rio Teles Pires nos últimos 36 anos. abstract: Introduction Developing functional foods with high bioactivity often compromises sensory characteristics, making optimization essential. Methods This study evaluated the functional composition, antioxidant activity, vitamin content, microbiological safety, sensory acceptability, and phenolic bioaccessibility during simulated gastrointestinal digestion of a pumpkin–apple–honey–walnut appetizer enriched with 1%–5% of rosehip extract or powder. title: Chinese HSCT patients' perceptions and experiences of nutrition management during transplant-unit hospitalization: a qualitative study
abstract: Background Malnutrition and inadequate oral intake are common during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), yet little is known about how patients perceive and experience nutrition management during transplant-unit hospitalization. Objective To explore Chinese HSCT patients' perceptions and experiences of nutrition management during transplant-unit hospitalization. title: From electrode swelling to structural integration: a quantitative electro-chemo-mechanical framework for electric-vehicle batteries
abstract: Electro-chemo-mechanical coupling is well established in electric-vehicle batteries, yet its translation from electrode behavior to pack- and vehicle-level performance remains difficult. This mini-review organizes the evidence around five transferable descriptors: electrode/cell swelling, contact or stack pressure, stiffness and strength, mechanical-abuse tolerance, and inactive structural mass or volume. title: Bio-inspired SiO2/Polydopamine functionalized PET fabrics for enhanced ultraviolet protection and thermophysiological comfort
abstract: The development of multifunctional textile surfaces with enhanced ultraviolet (UV) protection, thermophysiological comfort, and thermal insulation is of considerable interest for protective clothing and wearable applications. This study systematically evaluates the effects of a bio-inspired polydopamine (PDA)-assisted SiO 2 coating on the thermophysiological comfort and UV-protective performance of PET fabrics, establishing the relationship between surface modification and multifunctional textile performance. title: Hydraulic, Economic, and Environmental Assessment of Throughput-Increase Strategies in Intermittently Pumped Water Treatment Systems
abstract: Abstract In regions facing water scarcity, optimising existing treatment infrastructure is increasingly important. In the São Paulo Metropolitan Region, low per capita water availability and declining reservoir levels have increased reliance on the São Lourenço water treatment system. The system, however, operates below full capacity because pumps are shut down on peak-tariff hours to cut electricity costs. abstract: Brazilian extractive reserves constitute a model for the territorial governance of protected areas. With a focus on the territorial rights of traditional populations, they can serve as a catalyst for transformative change that reconciles the conservation of nature with the sustainable use of natural resources. title: Simultaneous measurements of gas- and aerosol-phase water-soluble organic nitrogen in the winter urban atmosphere of Chengdu, China
abstract: Abstract. Partitioning gaseous water-soluble organic nitrogen (WSON) to the aerosol phase is a major formation pathway of atmospheric secondary organic aerosols (SOA). We conducted simultaneous wintertime measurements of WSON in both gas and aerosol phases at an urban site in Chengdu, located in the Sichuan Basin (SCB), China, to investigate the concentration, gas-particle partitioning processes, and driven factors of WSON. title: How personality traits and cultural value orientation moderate the pathway from musical emotional expression to group cohesion in choral rehearsal
abstract: Introduction Choral singing is widely valued for building cohesion in community, educational, and well-being settings, yet the route by which emotional expression during rehearsal becomes group cohesion remains poorly specified, and most work still centers on individual feeling rather than on group-level interaction. Grounded in emotional contagion and social identity theory, this study proposes and tests a dual-moderated mediation model. title: Integrating Perceived ESG Dimensions Into Behavioral Models of Sustainable Tourism Consumption: Perspective From the Theory of Planned Behavior
abstract: Tourism is an important driver of socio-economic development. However, its rapid growth has increased pressure on the environment and host communities. Hence, it becomes increasingly urgent to understand that how tourists perceive sustainability and how these perceptions shape their behavioral decisions. Therefore, this study develops an integrated framework by incorporating perceived Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors into the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). title: Adaptation of the Loneliness and Solitude Scale (LSS) into Turkish
abstract: Experiences of loneliness and solitude are significant phenomena that are closely associated with individuals' psychological health and adaptation processes. The present study sought to adapt the Loneliness and Solitude Scale (LSS), which conceptualizes physical isolation through closely related yet functionally distinct dimensions, into Turkish and to examine its psychometric characteristics. This cross-sectional scale adaptation study was conducted with a sample of 377 young adults aged between 18 and 35. title: Integrating infrared thermography, behavioral assessment, and meat quality analysis to evaluate the effects of environmental enrichment in broiler chickens
abstract: Introduction Environmental enrichment (EE) is used in broiler production to improve welfare, but findings on design preferences, behavior, production, and meat quality are heterogeneous. An integrative approach combining live and postmortem assessments may clarify the EE effects. This study evaluated the effects of different EE models on leg health, behavior, and meat quality in broilers. Methods Three hundred one-day-old Cobb 500 broilers were reared under commercial conditions until 49 days of age (DOA). title: Steel mill scale in concrete and mortar: a critical review of the evidence base and a proposed framework for future quantitative synthesis
abstract: Steel mill scale is an iron-oxide-rich by-product of hot rolling that is generated at roughly 1%–3% of the mass of steel processed and is still largely landfilled or downcycled. Its high iron content, high specific gravity and fine flake morphology have prompted a growing number of laboratory investigations into its use in concrete and mortar, principally as a partial replacement for fine aggregate and, far more rarely, for cement. title: Examining West African Regional Integration on the Scale of Anglophone-Francophone Linguistic Strain
abstract: The hope of the eventual transformation of the Economic Community of West African States into a cohesive regional union, accentuated with the dynamism and transformation of the institution from 1975 to the present, reflects evolving exigencies. However, five decades down the line, the dream of a fully integrated West African community remains a pipe dream. The nascent nationalism manifesting as a military uprising in the sub-region further obfuscates attempts at characterising the milieu within globalisation and regionalism contexts. title: Data-driven multi-criteria evaluation of intelligent cockpit configuration strategies in Chinese battery electric vehicles
abstract: Introduction In this study, we examine how documented cockpit equipment differentiates selected Chinese-brand battery electric vehicles (BEVs). We compare configuration richness with and without a price criterion and identify recurring equipment arrangements, rather than using specifications as a proxy for tested cockpit performance. Methods The dataset comprises 36 purposively selected model–trim combinations from 13 brands. title: From therapeutic landscape perception to revisit intention: the mediating role of restorative experience in Palandöken Urban Forest
abstract: Purpose This study examines the mediating role of restorative experience in the associations between therapeutic landscape perception, visitor satisfaction, and revisit intention in Palandöken Urban Forest. Methodology A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 413 visitors through face-to-face questionnaires and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Therapeutic landscape perception was measured through the natural, aesthetic, and social landscape dimensions. title: BREEZE: Bioclimatic Route Evaluation for Environmental haZard avoidancE
abstract: Exposure to environmental stressors such as heat and air pollution is rising in urban areas, placing soft mobility users (e.g., pedestrians, cyclists, and scooter riders) at particular risk—a challenge that will only intensify with climate change. This study develops a comprehensive multi-dimensional exposure assessment framework — BREEZE (Bioclimatic Route Evaluation for Environmental haZard avoidancE) — for urban soft mobility routes that integrates environmental stressor modeling, dynamic population weighting, and citizen-oriented navigation tools. title: Reality stabilization: a unified framework for psychosis and post-psychotic depression
abstract: Both quantum mechanics and cognitive neuroscience challenge the classical view of a passively perceived reality. Instead, they suggest that reality arises through a process of selection and stabilization from a field of possibilities. This article proposes that this “reality stabilization” framework can unify our understanding of psychosis and post-psychotic depression—two conditions that are currently studied as distinct phenomena, and which existing models of predictive coding, dopaminergic dysregulation, and network neuroscience rarely integrate into a single account. title: Translation at a distance: United Nations visiting missions and the making of international decolonization
abstract: How did the United Nations, in their early years become an actor in the process of decolonization? This article shifts attention away from the diplomatic negotiations conventionally associated with international decolonization and toward the United Nations visiting missions, a largely overlooked instrument of the Trusteeship System entrusted with an epistemic mandate to investigate, inspect, and report on conditions in dependent territories. title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. title: Checklist of Korean Mymaridae (Hymenoptera, Chalcidoidea) with new records and descriptions of two new species of Zeyanus from South Korea and Japan
abstract: A checklist of Mymaridae (Hymenoptera, Chalcidoidea) in South Korea is presented, comprising the previously recorded 15 genera and 31 species and also the five newly recorded taxa, totaling 36 species. Two new species of Zeyanus Huber, Z. knuz Triapitsyn & Kim, sp. nov . and Z. sunayez Triapitsyn & Kim, sp. nov ., are described and illustrated from South Korea and Japan. An updated key to females of Zeyanus species is provided. Newly recorded from South Korea are Mymar ermak Triapitsyn & Berezovskiy, M. maritimum Triapitsyn & Berezovskiy, and M. pulchellum Curtis. title: Dialogue Act Script: A Structured Framework for Generating Multilingual and Multicultural Dialogues
abstract: Non-English dialogue datasets are scarce, and models are often trained or evaluated on translations of English-language dialogues, an approach which can introduce artifacts that reduce their naturalness and cultural appropriateness. This work proposes Dialogue Act Script (DAS), a structured framework for encoding, localizing, and generating multilingual dialogues from abstract intent representations. title: The teleost inflammasome as a biosensor in developmental toxicology
abstract: Introduction Standard environmental risk assessment frameworks, such as the OECD 236 Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity (FET) test, rely heavily on macroscopic morphological endpoints that may fail to detect subtle, sublethal molecular disruptions before phenotypic damage becomes apparent. Mechanism-based biomarkers capable of ultra-early toxicity prediction are therefore needed. The teleost inflammasome, particularly the interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and gasdermin (GSDM) execution pathway, represents a promising high-resolution molecular biosensor for developmental toxicity screening. title: The Effect of Teaching Materials Produced Using 3D Printing in Social Studies Education on the Motivation, Attitudes, and Achievement of Fifth-Grade Students
abstract: This investigation primarily explores the pedagogical implications of integrating instructional artifacts manufactured via three-dimensional (3D) printing technologies within fifth-grade social studies education, specifically monitoring shifts in student motivation, subject-directed attitudes, and academic outcomes. Using a quasi-experimental approach, the study employed pre-test and post-test non-equivalent control group design. title: The Origins of Modern Turkish Cypriot Literature and Its First Novel: Bir Bakış (A Glance)
abstract: Written by Muzaffereddin Galib, Bir Bakış (“A Glance”) 1892) is examined as the earliest known Turkish serialized novel published in Cyprus, where “first” functions not as an aesthetic judgment but as an indicator of earliness grounded in publication context and supported by archival materials. title: Fertilizer regimes reshape microbial interaction networks without altering sugarcane rhizosphere diversity
abstract: Abstract. Sugarcane (Saccharum spp.), an economically important crop in the food and bioenergy industries, has historically played a central role in the economy of Cuba, shaping its agricultural landscape and international relations. Although production has declined in recent decades, sugarcane remains a strategic crop, with its byproducts contributing to national energy and industrial outputs. However, the way in which long-term fertilization interacts with soil microbial communities under varying edaphoclimatic conditions remains largely unknown. title: Immunometabolic crosstalk between dysfunctional adipose tissue and the brain: implications for postoperative cognitive dysfunction in obesity
abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is an important complication after surgery, particularly in patients with pre-existing metabolic and inflammatory vulnerability. Obesity may increase susceptibility to postoperative cognitive decline, but its independent association with POCD and the underlying mechanisms remain uncertain. This review critically examines a proposed adipose–immune–brain pathway linking obesity-associated adipose dysfunction to perioperative neurocognitive outcomes. institutions: West China Second University Hospital of Sichuan University

title: Rethinking collaborative governance in Papua: toward institutional transformation
abstract: After more than two decades of implementing the Special Autonomy policy, Papua continues to lag behind other regions in Indonesia in terms of development. The complex legal, political, and human rights context, combined with the region's diverse social, economic, cultural, environmental, and natural resource characteristics, poses significant challenges to the implementation of current approaches. title: Roadbase performance and modification mechanisms of TBM-excavated gneiss muck utilizing a fiber–geopolymer synergistic stabilization system
abstract: The disposal of TBM muck has become a pressing issue in tunnel construction. This study addresses the utilization of 295,000 m 3 of gneiss muck excavated from the DXL Tunnel in western China by modifying it with low‑calcium fly ash (FA), ground granulated blast‑furnace slag (GGBS), carbide slag (CCS), and basalt fiber (BF) to produce a roadbase material. The optimal mix, designated X‑FGC (FA:GGBS:CCS = 9:4:1 with 0.3% 12‑mm BF), was determined via response surface methodology. title: Circuit-constrained molecular neuroethology in the medicinal leech Hirudo verbana
abstract: Medicinal leeches have long served as classic systems in comparative neuroethology because individual neurons can be identified across animals and linked to well-defined behaviors. This review argues that Hirudo verbana is now positioned for a new phase in which this identified-cell framework can be connected directly to molecular mechanisms. We first outline the organization and experimental accessibility of the leech nervous system, then evaluate genomic and transcriptomic resources as tools for testing physiologically constrained hypotheses rather than as endpoints in themselves. title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution, convergence trends, and influencing factors of ecological efficiency in Chinese cities is crucial for achieving coordinated development between socioeconomic progress and the ecological environment. This paper assesses the ecological efficiency level of 279 prefecture-level cities in China by adopting the super-efficient EBM model. title: The Scaleup Costs, Size, and Statistics Challenge to Democratic Deliberation on Health Policy
abstract: Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini-publics. These forums' participants are selected randomly from the general public (sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors). After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations. title: Settler-colonial entanglements: Using Par/Des(i) to understand Black and Racialized international student experiences in Canada
abstract: This scholarly paper discusses the complex positioning of Black and Racialized international students (BRIS) in Canada, both as marginalized bodies and complicit in perpetuating settler colonialism. It delves into the paradoxical role these students play within the framework of Canadian higher education, which is deeply entwined with the country's colonial history and contemporary policy shifts aimed at managing the influx of international students.
