title: Urban energy peaking in China: timing, persistence, rebound risk, and regional heterogeneity
abstract: Introduction Determining whether urban energy demand has entered a persistent post-peak phase is important for assessing China’s energy transition. A historical maximum alone, however, does not establish a durable turning point because energy consumption may subsequently rebound or remain close to its previous peak. Methods Using a balanced panel of 336 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2000 to 2022, this study develops a diagnostic framework that distinguishes historical maxima from effective peaks and evaluates post-peak persistence, rebound risk, transition status, and trend changes. title: Integrated melissopalynological and phenolic profiling reveals antioxidant and antimicrobial potential of Turkish honeys
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive characterization of 23 Turkish honey samples through an integrated approach involving melissopalynological, chemical, antioxidant, and antimicrobial analyses. Fourteen phenolic compounds were quantified by HPLC, while total phenolic content (TPC), FRAP, and DPPH radical-scavenging assays were used to assess antioxidant-related properties. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against six pathogenic microorganisms using minimum inhibitory concentration values. title: Community differentiation and assembly of soil nosZ-type denitrifiers across dominant plant communities in an alpine wetland of Qinghai Lake
abstract: Background Nitrous oxide (N₂O) reduction mediated by nosZ -harboring microorganisms represents the terminal step of denitrification and an important biological sink for N₂O in wetland soils, yet how naturally occurring dominant plant communities are associated with the diversity, taxonomic differentiation, and assembly of nosZ -type communities in alpine wetlands remains poorly understood. title: Aplicación del enfoque multi-método al estudio de ciclos entropía-reciclaje en sistemas de agua sostenibles
abstract: Context: Anthropogenic pressures have intensified entropy in urban hydrological systems, affecting water availability, quality, and long-term sustainability. However, entropy remains underutilized as an operational variable in water management studies. Methodology: This study applies a multi-method approach integrating documentary analysis, fieldwork (n = 179), and geospatial modeling. title: Potential for enteric methane emissions mitigation in zebu cattle through Leucaena leucocephala and Gliricidia sepium leaf supplementation compared with cottonseed cake in West Africa
abstract: In West Africa, legume trees are widely used by agro-pastoralists to enhance livestock productivity, yet their potential to mitigate enteric methane (eCH₄) remains insufficiently documented. This study evaluated the effects of supplementing Panicum maximum hay with leaves of Leucaena leucocephala and Gliricidia sepium leaves on feed intake, apparent digestibility, and eCH₄ emissions in Sudanese Fulani zebu bulls (244 ± 24.3 kg). title: Is physical climate risk priced in India’s financial sector? A monthly index approach, 2014–2024
abstract: Floods, cyclones and heatwaves are no longer viewed as humanitarian crises; they also have significant financial implications by affecting borrowers’ ability to repay loans, increasing potential liabilities of insurers and influencing how investors assess and price financial risks. Whether financial markets actually respond to this physical climate risk remains an open question, particularly in emerging economies like India, where climate exposure is high but market-based evidence is scarce. title: Benchmarking conditioners in Liang–Kleeman Information Flow: application to land–atmosphere interactions in humid forests
abstract: Abstract. The Liang–Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF) framework has been increasingly used to identify causality in Earth–system dynamics in recent years. Yet, uncertainties remain regarding how the causal graph changes when mediators and confounders (conditioners) are introduced, i.e., divergence between the bivariate and conditioned forms. title: Del residuo agroindustrial al biochar diseñado: composición, estructura molecular y aplicaciones de alto valor agregado
abstract: En este artículo se examina cómo la composición de la biomasa agroindustrial y las condiciones de pirólisis determinan la estructura molecular y el desempeño funcional del biochar desde una perspectiva de ingeniería de materiales. title: Fire return intervals are very short at Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, especially in dry miombo woodlands—a survival analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Fire shapes savanna and woodland landscapes, but the temporal spacing of recurrent fires remains poorly quantified in African miombo ecosystems. Understanding how fire-return intervals vary across vegetation and landscape settings is important for interpreting fire-regime heterogeneity, vegetation recovery, and fire-management needs. We assessed Fire-return intervals across the Niassa Special Reserve, Mozambique, and evaluated whether fire recurrence differed among major vegetation types. title: Teacher-Learners Interaction and Grade VI Academic Outcomes in Edukasyon Sa Pagpapakatao of Bislig City SPED Center, Bislig City Division: A Descriptive-Correlational Approach
abstract: This descriptive-correlational study examined the relationship between teacher–pupils’ interaction and the academic performance of Grade VI pupils in Edukasyon sa Pagpapakatao (EsP) at Bislig City SPED Center during School Year 2025–2026. The study involved 63 Grade VI pupils selected through complete enumeration. Teacher–pupils’ interaction was assessed in terms of emotional support, classroom management, and instructional support using the adapted Classroom Assessment Scoring System–Student Report (CLASS-SR), while academic performance was measured through official quarterly grades. title: Bifunctional Carbon‐Sensitized Hollow Heterojunctions for Dual‐Mode Sensing of Emerging Contaminant 6‐PPD
abstract: ABSTRACT N‐(1,3‐dimethylbutyl)‐N′‐phenyl‐p‐phenylenediamine (6‐PPD), a ubiquitous rubber tire antioxidant, poses a severe threat to ecological safety due to its pronounced ecotoxicity. This work achieves the unprecedented dual‐mode photoelectrochemical and electrochemical (PEC‐EC) sensing of 6‐PPD through a dual‐mode platform endowed with bifunctional catalytic signal amplification. title: Lessons learned from developing serious games for upper-limb rehabilitation in children
abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and serious games have demonstrated growing potential in physical therapy, exergaming, and the promotion of physical activity across diverse patient populations. However, the development of therapeutic games, particularly for rehabilitation in children, still lacks consolidated guidelines and structured frameworks. title: Biomass conversion in thermo‐catalytic reforming reactor: process modeling and kinetic insights for integrated intermediate pyrolysis
abstract: Abstract A sustainable energy transition in the 21st century necessitates efficient biomass‐to‐energy conversion technologies, with pyrolysis playing a crucial role. Thermo‐catalytic reforming (TCR) combines intermediate pyrolysis with a catalytic post‐reforming stage, producing higher‐quality bio‐oil, char, and syngas than conventional pyrolysis. However, process models capable of predicting TCR performance across different feedstocks remain limited. This work presents an Aspen Plus‐based kinetic process model that couples both TCR reaction stages, primary pyrolysis, and catalytic post‐reform
institutions: Fraunhofer Institute for Environmental, Safety and Energy Technology UMSICHT

title: Dark tourism: concepts, practices, ethical challenges and future research
abstract: Purpose This review paper critically synthesizes contemporary scholarship on dark tourism, integrating conceptual foundations, visitor motivations, management practices, ethical dilemmas, sustainability challenges, and emerging research directions. It aims to advance a coherent understanding of responsible dark tourism development through an interdisciplinary lens. title: Regular fiscal and accounting supervision and firms’ cost of equity capital: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment using the pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision
abstract: Fiscal and accounting supervision has become an integral part of China’s Party and state supervisory system. Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2017 to 2022, this study exploits the Ministry of Finance’s 2020 pilot reform to strengthen fiscal and accounting supervision as a quasi-natural experiment to examine its impact on firms’ cost of equity capital. The results show that the reform significantly reduces the cost of equity through information governance, behavioural guidance and expectations management. title: Erasing the invisible: targeting persister cells to cure minimal residual disease
abstract: Abstract Despite revolutionary advances in immunotherapy and targeted therapies, tumor recurrence driven by minimal residual disease (MRD) and drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells remains a critical challenge in oncology. MRD, a reservoir of residual cancer cells undetectable by conventional imaging but identifiable via sensitive molecular techniques like next-generation sequencing and ctDNA analysis, serves as a prognostic biomarker for relapse across hematologic and solid malignancies. title: Retos de la evaluación del aprendizaje en la educa-ción superior: hacia una evaluación formativa y transparente.
abstract: La evaluación del aprendizaje en educación superior enfrenta una tensión estructural entre modelos tradicionales centrados en la certificación y las demandas contemporáneas de una formación orientada al desarrollo de competencias. La masificación de las aulas, la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial y la persistente subjetividad en la calificación configuran un escenario que exige repensar los dispositivos evaluativos. Esta revisión sistemática se propone analizar los principales retos de la evaluación en educación superior y sistematizar las características de un modelo formativo-transpare

title: Pláticando Juntos: family storytelling and socioemotional development in immigrant communities
abstract: Immigration socialization, defined as the process through which immigrant parents communicate with their children regarding immigration history, identity, and status, puts unique demands on parents within mixed-status families. These demands encompass the emotional labor involved in understanding legal vulnerability, navigating developmental readiness, and conveying a history that their children did not directly experience. title: From Avocado Seed Waste to Green Synthesis Laser-Induced Graphene: A Rapid, Direct, Low Cost and Flame-Retardant-Free Route
abstract: Abstract Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has emerged as a versatile method for producing porous, conductive graphitic structures from carbon-rich precursors. In this work, an unconventional and sustainable precursor—Fuerte avocado seed (Persea americana Mill) waste—was explored for the green synthesis of LIG via CO₂ laser engraving. Avocado seed powder was processed into compact pellets and systematically irradiated under varying synthesis parameters, including laser power, scan speed, irradiation area, number of passes, and processing atmosphere. title: Age discrimination in public transportation: The case of the Ekşi Sözlük platform
abstract: This study examines how age discrimination toward the free-transit rights of individuals aged 65 and older is reproduced through the discussions on the Ekşi Sözlük platform. The data consist of 1,762 user entries collected under the Ekşi Sözlük heading “toplu taşımada 65 yaş beleşçiliği kaldırılsın” (“abolish free-riding by 65-year-olds on public transit”). title: Media and Digital Imperialism
abstract: This text introduces the Special Issue “Imperialism, Information, Communication, and Culture in the Phase of Digitalisation”. It argues that digitalisation reconfigures, rather than replaces, the foundations of imperialism. It briefly revisits the historical emergence of imperialism, examines how digital platforms reconfigure media imperialism, and summarises theoretical approaches to the relationship between imperialism and digital technologies. Finally, it presents the contributions gathered in the Special Issue.

title: THE CONCEPT OF ‘BÖRİK’ (BÖRK) IN KAZAKH: AN ETYMOLOGICAL, LEXICAL AND CULTURAL STUDY
abstract: The concept of börik (börk) in Kazakh possesses a deeply rooted history in terms of its etymological, lexicological, dialectological, and cultural dimensions. Preserved continuously from Old Turkic to modern Turkic dialects, this term initially referred merely to a type of headgear; however, over time it underwent a semantic expansion and acquired powerful symbolic meanings associated with identity, status, protection, and social belonging. title: Psychological and behavioral experiences of individuals investing in cryptocurrency in an uncertain environment: a phenomenological approach
abstract: Introduction This study explores, from a phenomenological perspective, how cryptocurrency investors experience emotional, cognitive, and social processes in an uncertain environment and how these experiences influence decision-making, risk management, and identity perception. Methods This qualitative phenomenological study involved semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 19 participants selected through criterion sampling. title: A four-decadal (1981–2024) quality-assured ground-based soybean phenology dataset from Northeast China: a FAIR-compliant resource for climate impact and agricultural adaptation studies
abstract: Although satellite remote sensing has been widely used to monitor land surface phenology, long-term, high-quality ground-based observations are essential for validating and calibrating these products, particularly for understanding agricultural ecosystem responses to climate change. However, such ground-truth datasets remain scarce, limiting the full potential of Earth system data applications. Here we present a comprehensive ground-based soybean phenology dataset for Northeast China, a region critical to national food security. title: Reconceptualizing sports tourism destination competitiveness through the knowledge-based view: evidence from Iran
abstract: Sports tourism destination competitiveness has been theorized predominantly through static, asset-based frameworks that privilege physical infrastructure and promotional capacity, yet these accounts offer limited purchase in knowledge-intensive, innovation-driven tourism systems. This study advances a dynamic alternative, drawing on the Knowledge-Based View to reconceptualize competitiveness as an ecosystem-level process rooted in the collective mobilization and transformation of knowledge. title: Emerging Roles of Gold Nanoparticles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis and Imaging: A Promising yet Underexplored Frontier
abstract: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. abstract: Foreign influencers are playing a growing role in China's live-streaming commerce industry. Yet, little is known about how consumers respond to foreign influencers’ ability to communicate and adjust across cultures. To address this gap, the present study draws on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and distinguishes between two consumer perceptions: Intercultural Communication Competency (ICC) and Intercultural Adaptability (ICA). title: Multiscale vascular responses to passive heat stress: from endothelial injury to adaptive remodeling
abstract: The escalating occurrence of extreme high temperature weather exposes individuals to passive heat stress more frequently, resulting in strain on the vascular system. One example of this strain is the doubling of cardiac output during heat stress, achieved through an increase in heart rate and the redirection of blood flow from non-cutaneous tissues. These combined stressors can present substantial risks, potentially leading to syncope and cardiovascular collapse. title: Vector-borne zoonotic bacteria in Tunisia: from fragmented data to an integrated One Health surveillance framework
abstract: Vector-borne and vector-associated bacterial zoonoses represent an important component of infectious disease epidemiology in Tunisia. This review synthesizes available evidence on major bacterial groups, including Rickettsia , Bartonella , Anaplasma , Ehrlichia , Borrelia , Coxiella burnetii , and other arthropod-associated bacteria, using a One Health framework integrating human, animal, vector, wildlife, and environmental compartments. abstract: The South American coati (Nasua nasua) is a mammal of the order Carnivora and family Procyonidae, characterized by scansorial locomotion. Accordingly, several anatomical and functional studies examined its thoracic limbs. Nevertheless, the anatomical descriptions and terminology differ among those studies, and none considered the evolutionary derivations of the brachium and antebrachium muscles based on topology, innervation and anatomical variants. abstract: Azadirachta (Meliaceae) is a small genus comprising economically and ecologically important plants, including A. indica , which is widely used in traditional medicine and other applications such as natural pest control and cosmetics. Several studies have previously been conducted on Azadirachta , including its phytochemistry and associated microfungi, particularly endophytic species inhabiting the A. indica host. title: La Reinvención del Aprendizaje: Claves del Conectivismo para la Educación Digital
abstract: En las instituciones educativas actuales persiste una confusión conceptual. Se asume que el manejo de dispositivos tecnológicos equivale al aprendizaje mediado por su uso. Esta premisa alimenta un enfoque instrumental que convierte la innovación en una continuidad de prácticas educativas similares a las de la década de los noventa, pero con dispositivos digitales. El artículo examina el conectivismo, teoría propuesta por George Siemens (2005) y Stephen Downes (2019), para extraer ideas que permitan repensar la educación digital. title: Institutional dynamics of circular and climate-adaptive water governance in Bengaluru
abstract: Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change threaten global urban water security, with projections indicating that over 1 billion urban residents will face water short ages. In many Global South cities, water crises are infrastructural as well as institutional challenges rather than merely hydrological ones, yet city-level analyses of these institutional barriers remain scarce. title: Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles
abstract: To date, the circular economy (CE) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate. title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species
abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds—including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules—that may modulate gut microbiota–host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.

abstract: Southeast Asia’s scam-compound networks expose a persistent gap in regional security governance: the institutions required to dismantle transnational criminal economies are, in some jurisdictions, compromised by the networks they are expected to regulate. Although scholarship on minilateralism demonstrates the capacity of small coalitions to act beyond consensus-bound institutions, its application has focused predominantly on great-power competition. abstract: Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remain a major clinical challenge because antimicrobial resistance is increasing and conventional antibiotic therapy is limited. This study aimed to isolate and characterize lytic bacteriophages active against clinical MRSA isolates and evaluate their therapeutic efficacy when applied subcutaneously at the site of implantation of a nano-layered double hydroxide (LDH)-modified bone cement implant. abstract: Increasingly, governments are moving from using GDP as the primary measure of economic progress to using wellbeing frameworks, which aim to measure wellbeing. abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the key determinants of humanitarian logistics effectiveness in Malaysia’s flood disaster management and develop the good humanitarian logistics practices model (GHLPM) as an integrated framework to enhance coordination, quality assurance and operational readiness. title: Eficacia de los barnices fluorados en la prevención de la caries dental y en la disminución de la sensibilidad dental.
abstract: El objetivo de este estudio fue evaluar la eficacia de la aplicación profesional de barniz de fluoruro de sodio al 5 % en la prevención de caries dental y en la reducción de la hipersensibilidad dentinaria en comparación con un placebo. title: PP2A targeting: balancing anticancer potential and neurological risk
abstract: Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a multifunctional serine/threonine phosphatase that regulates cell-cycle progression, oncogenic signaling, neuronal development, synaptic homeostasis, and protein proteostasis. Its dysregulation contributes to cancer, whereas impaired PP2A activity in the nervous system is linked to neurodevelopmental disorders and neurodegenerative proteinopathies, including tau and α-synuclein pathology. title: Climate Change and Dispersal Limitation Reshape Future Habitat Accessibility for Lady Amherst's Pheasant ( Chrysolophus amherstiae ) in China
abstract: ABSTRACT Montane forest birds are highly vulnerable to climate warming because their habitats are often fragmented, topographically constrained, and difficult to track through dispersal. For Lady Amherst's Pheasant ( Chrysolophus amherstiae ), future climate risks remain poorly understood, especially the mismatch between habitat suitability and habitat accessibility. abstract: Abstract Urban areas are increasingly exposed to mudflow hazards as unplanned urban expansion intersects with steep drainage basins and extreme rainfall events intensify under climate change. Physics-based models offer powerful tools for hazard assessment, yet their performance in densely built environments remains insufficiently explored. abstract: The sudden shift to new normal education changed the work of elementary teachers in Cotabato City, but local evidence on their lived experiences, challenges, and ways of coping remained limited. This study explored the experiences, challenges, and coping mechanisms of elementary school teachers in the Cotabato City Division during School Year 2020–2021. abstract: Smartphone mHealth apps (mHealth apps) have played a highly positive role in medical services, which provides a new direction for users' medical services and health management. Although smartphone mHealth apps provide many benefits for users, people know little about the factors that drive elderly users to adopt this new service platform in the context of an aging population. abstract: Prevention of pollen exposure is a way to assist allergic individuals to better cope with their disease. To enable this prevention, a prediction of next day(s) pollen flight is needed. abstract: This study aims to analyze the epistemological transformation concerning the nature and legitimacy of knowledge in the context of modernity and postmodernity through İhsan Oktay Anar’s The Atlas of Misty Continents. abstract: Accurate quantification of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture is critical for establishing credible baselines, identifying emission hotspots, and prioritizing mitigation strategies. abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate multiple mechanisms associated with glioblastoma (GBM) therapy resistance, which remains a major challenge in GBM treatment. abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization frequently outpaces sanitation infrastructure, leaving vulnerable residents without essential services. This study develops and applies a GIS-based spatial decision-support framework combining multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), and network-based accessibility analysis to assess location suitability and prioritize public toilet development in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. abstract: ABSTRACT Setting urban water connection fees is a complex policy problem: Fees must balance affordability, equity, and adequate cost recovery. This study determined the implementation of Development Education programs along objectives and content integration, teaching strategies, instructional materials and monitoring evaluation and mechanisms in selected public schools in Lapu-Lapu City. abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. title: Climate change and conflict: The vicious cycles undermining climate action, and what can be done to break them
abstract: Abstract In this review, we synthesize evidence to argue that climate change and conflict are mutually reinforcing. We first examine conflict as a barrier to mitigation, focusing on four faultlines that slow climate action: (a) ideological polarization, (b) “elite versus ordinary people” narratives, (c) intranational, place‐based conflicts, and (d) international disputes. abstract: Early detection and control of high- and low-pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI, LPAI) in family poultry flocks remain challenging in settings where mortality from enzootic diseases such as Newcastle disease (ND) and infectious bursal disease (IBD) is persistently high. abstract: ABSTRACT We study the dynamics of the racial wealth gap (the wealth of Black households relative to white ones) using a dynamic equilibrium model of overlapping generations. title: Playing together, living together: Community-based music learning as a catalyst for rural wellbeing
abstract: This article explores how participatory instrumental music tuition can strengthen wellbeing, confidence, and social cohesion for adults living in rural Scotland. Focusing on the town of Millport, Isle of Cumbrae, the study was conducted as part of the Community Instrumental Music Service for Rural Scotland (CIMSRS), an initiative designed to address barriers to adult music learning caused by isolation, limited provision, and economic constraints. Nineteen adults aged between 25 and 75 took part in weekly group violin and viola sessions, culminating in a community performance. Through individua

title: Advances in photothermal-driven tumor immunomodulation and synergistic therapy
abstract: Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a local treatment that uses photothermal conversion agents (PTAs) to absorb light and produce heat in tumor tissue. The direct result is tumor ablation. At the same time, heat-damaged tumor cells may undergo immunogenic cell death (ICD). This process is often accompanied by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), followed by dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation. Because of this immune effect, PTT has been explored as a partner for immunotherapy. It may be useful in tumors where antigen presentation is weak or where the immune mic

title: Senior Executive Pay and Corporate Sustainability Performance: The Roles of Green Innovation, Governance and State Ownership in China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between senior executive pay and corporate sustainability performance using 14,524 firm‐year observations of Chinese A‐share listed firms over the period 2019–2023. This period provides consistent data availability and encompasses China's transition towards the 2020 dual‐carbon policy. Drawing on agency, managerial power, stakeholder and resource dependence theories, we investigate nonlinear effects, green innovation as a mediating mechanism, and governance and ownership as boundary conditions. We find that senior executive pay is positively associa
journal: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management

title: Faker Island: Profiling misinformation sharers on the French Twittersphere
abstract: What are the distinctive characteristics of misinformation sharers? So far, most studies have focused on the U.S., a two-party system with a highly polarized media landscape, leaving open the question of what misinformation sharers look like in other socio-political contexts. Research has also prioritized testing causal links between cognitive or political variables and misinformation sharing, while paying less attention to fine-grained descriptions of who these users are. To address this gap, we analyze the French Twittersphere using ideological inference methods and a matching procedure. Dra
journal: Journal of Quantitative Description Digital Media

title: “Discovering World Englishes has lessened my burden in English language education”
abstract: Abstract The growth of World Englishes (WE) in Applied Linguistics has provided important contributions to English language education and teacher professional development. Critical frameworks in WE have raised awareness and inspired knowledge creation about linguistic diversity in contexts where local teachers have been marginalized for being non-native speakers of English. Contributing to the understanding of English use and English language education dynamics in the expanding circle, this study reports the findings of a qualitative study examining how a group of ten in-service Colombian Engl

title: Mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine interventions in the gastric ‘inflammation-to-carcinoma’ cascade: advances in in vitro models from monolayer cells to organoids
abstract: Gastric cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The Correa cascade, progressing from chronic gastritis through precancerous lesions to adenocarcinoma, provides the framework for understanding gastric mucosal stepwise malignant transformation. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulas, such as Zuojin Pills and Wuji Pills, have been historically used to treat gastric disorders including epigastric pain and acid regurgitation, yet their mechanisms of action in blocking the inflammation-to-carcinoma transition remain incompletely understood. The mechanistic diversit

title: Forest endophytes as a biological resource insights into their role in sustainable agriculture and agroforestry
abstract: Abstract Forest ecosystems are the hidden reservoir of beneficial microorganisms, particularly for endophytes, that colonize plant tissue internally without causing any disease symptoms and play a key role in plant health and ecosystem sustainability. Forest-derived endophytic bacteria and fungi are crucial in nutrient cycling, stress resistance and growth promotion via phosphorus solubilization, nitrogen fixation and synthesis of phytohormones. Those microbes allow plants to survive in low-nutrient and stressful environments. This review offers insights into the diversity, abundance, distribu

title: Transients and Stellar Activity as Revealed by Ultraviolet Diagnostic Tracers
abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet (UV) observations offer unique insights into transient and variable astrophysical phenomena, from the Sun and nearby stars to supernovae and star-forming galaxies. Here, we summarise and review the diagnostic power of the UV spectrum for probing the physical conditions, dynamics and energetics of these events. We trace the historical development of UV astronomy from early satellite missions to the current landscape shaped by the Hubble Space Telescope, the GALaxy Evolution eXplorer, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and AstroSat /UVIT. Particular emphasis is placed on res

title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints
abstract: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synt

title: Identifying Arctic states vulnerable to rapid ice loss with a convolutional neural network
abstract: This work investigates the incidence of rapid ice-loss events in the Arctic, in which a substantial fraction of September sea-ice is lost in only a few years. Such events are seen to occur in climate model simulations forced with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations, but not as yet in the relatively short observational record. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using six large climate model ensembles to diagnose vulnerability to rapid ice-loss events. The trained model is shown to separate higher and lower risk states in out-of-sample climate models via a leave-one-out cross-val

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers

title: Traditional and Recent Approaches for Infrared Small Target Detection : Overview, Challenges and Perspectives (Part 1)
abstract: Infrared small target detection is often used in different civilian and military applications to detect static or moving targets in scenes like in ground, air and sea surveillance. Research in this field started more than three decades ago, and the last two decades have witnessed very significant publications in this field following the rise of low-rank and sparse decomposition (model-based methods) and deep learning models (data-based methods). Furthermore, several surveys can be found in the literature but none of them addresses an overall review in this field. In this context, the aim of th

title: MemRevise: A Self-Revising Memory for Conversational Search
abstract: In conversational search, users correct misun-derstandings, revise their requests and return to earlier topics, so part of the history no longer reflects what they want. Existing benchmarks do not isolate such turns. Current search methods either re-read the history or keep a record of every turn, and none of them marks earlier content as dropped. We introduce CONVREVISE, a benchmark of 4,429 test questions in six tiers of returns and revisions over TopiOCQA, CORAL and OR-QuAC. We also propose MEMREVISE, which combines a revisable memory graph, a 3B writer distilled from teacher memories, and

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) systems must maintain efficient and safe energy delivery under variations in geometry, coupling, load, alignment, and operating conditions. Machine-learning methods are increasingly applied to accelerate structural design, estimate operating parameters and states, and support adaptive control and scheduling. This review develops a task-oriented framework organized around three interconnected domains: structural design and optimization, parameter and state estimation, and control and optimization. Supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid or physics-i

title: Data-driven forecasting of tropical cloud forest phenology: A dynamical systems and machine learning hybrid approach
abstract: Forecasting how species and ecosystems respond to climate change is a critical challenge in ecology, particularly in hyper-diverse tropical biomes. While traditional phenological models often rely on preconceived functional forms, this study introduces a data-driven hybrid approach that integrates dynamical systems theory with machine learning to forecast flowering and fruiting cycles. Using a robust 35-year dataset from a Venezuelan tropical cloud forest, we reconstruct the system's state-space using delay vectors inspired by Takens' theorem, incorporating climate forcing variables such as te

title: Mapping Arctic Polynyas from Sea Ice Concentration Data Using Hierarchical Partitioning and Differentiated Region Growing: Sensitivity to Threshold and Product Choices
abstract: Accurately delineating Arctic coastal polynyas from sea ice concentration data remains challenging because of complex coastal geometry and spatially heterogeneous ice conditions. We develop a daily sea ice concentration (SIC) mapping framework based on hierarchical partitioning, connected-component analysis, and differentiated region growing for polynya and open-water regions. Applied to September-May ice seasons from 2002/03 to 2024/25, the framework achieves a mean overall accuracy of 96.74% and a mean kappa coefficient of 0.93 in the 63-scene visual assessment. China Automotive Technology and Research Center

title: Graph Neural Networks for Astrophysics and Cosmology
abstract: Physics seldom makes breakthroughs when we consider objects only in isolation. Instead we model and measure how objects sit among their neighbours, spatial, temporal, or otherwise: a galaxy in its environment, a halo in its history, a photon hit in a detector. Graphs are ideally suited for encoding exactly these relations, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) learn the geometric functions that respect them. This review presents the use of GNNs for astrophysics and cosmology, and argues that GNNs often suit physics and physical data better than any alternative: they fit the native geometry of the d

title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
abstract: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. While sonar provides robust large-scale geometry, it lacks spectral and high-resolution textural information required to record fine morphological features - a critical limitation in under-ice environments, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing conditions

title: Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
abstract: Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $η(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on sp

title: Sea-Net: A Small and Inherently Interpretable Neural Network for Time Series Classification
abstract: Traditional time-series classification methods often operate as black boxes, providing a class prediction without indicating which time point or time interval within the series led to that prediction. To improve temporal interpretability, MILLET (Multiple Instance Learning with Temporal Explanation), which combines an InceptionTime encoder with Conjunctive Pooling, provides both classification and temporal explanations. However, MILLET contains approximately 424 K parameters, making it unsuitable for deployment on resource-constrained micro-controllers, and it achieves an overall time-series a
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning in Oncology
abstract: Deep learning has enabled substantial advances in oncology, including cancer detection and diagnosis, medical image analysis, tumor characterization, treatment planning, response assessment, and outcome prediction. However, conventional data-driven models often require large annotated datasets, exhibit limited generalization across heterogeneous clinical settings, and lack explicit mechanisms for incorporating the physical, physiological, and biological principles underlying cancer development and treatment. Physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) integrates governing physical laws, mechanistic

title: Ranked Right, Sized Wrong: Ensemble Spread Fails Silently at Streamflow Extremes
abstract: Deep learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory networks, are increasingly used for operational streamflow forecasting, with ensemble spread providing a signal of predictive uncertainty. As climate change increases the frequency of hydroclimatic extremes, these models will increasingly operate under flow conditions that are rare in their historical records. We therefore evaluate whether ensemble spread remains informative under increasing flows, examining both its magnitude relative to error and its ability to rank errors. Prediction error is approximately $2\times$ the corrected spr

title: A novel machine learning framework based on proper orthogonal decomposition for turbine wake flow predictions in natural waterways
abstract: We developed a machine learning (ML) surrogate trained on instantaneous large eddy simulation (LES) data filtered using proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) to predict mean flow fields in natural rivers with complex geometries. The surrogate enables efficient prediction of mean flow fields downstream of marine hydrokinetic (MHK) turbine arrays at a fraction of the computational cost of high fidelity simulations, facilitating turbine layout optimization in natural waterways where bathymetry, turbulence, and turbine interactions influence the available energy resource. We demonstrate the capabi

title: Latent space configuration for neural network finetuning, fast ranking, and embedding dimensionality reduction
abstract: Finding K most similar elements for a query in a large gallery of neural network (NN) embeddings is essential in various areas of computer science and industrial applications of artificial intelligence. This paper proposes search algorithms for structured latent spaces (LS) of NNs which allow to speed up top K item retrieval owing to O(1) complexity small candidate gallery subset search. ArcFace-pretrained IResNet50 models are finetuned using Latent Space Configuration (LSC) methodology to obtain new distribution of embeddings with desired geometric properties. Applying the proposed algorithms

title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph
institutions: Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (Switzerland)

title: Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion
abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence is widely assumed to scale with effort: more researchers, papers and investment should accelerate discovery. Theories of technological growth instead locate the difficulty of discovery in the space of ideas. Here we show that neither scale nor space is enough: breakthroughs depend on diverse attention, which collective concentration can deplete. Across 36 years of computer science, we analyze 7.2 million papers, 73,089 peer reviews and 3.7 million researchers and their topic shifts. The field expanded while its attention narrowed sharply after the Transforme

title: ONCship: A Large-Scale Underwater Acoustic Corpus for Ship Recognition
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved underwater acoustic vessel recognition. However, existing publicly available datasets are typically limited in scale, hindering large-scale representation learning and downstream task evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce ONCship, a large-scale underwater acoustic dataset comprising 4521 hours of curated recordings from Ocean Networks Canada (ONC) hydrophones and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. We evaluate the proposed dataset across three tasks: self-supervised representation learning, vessel-type classifi

title: An exact finite-state representation of viscoelastic memory for accelerated sea-level modeling: SLEvolve v1.0
abstract: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. As these models are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet simulations, glacial-cycle calculations, and large ensembles, standard pseudo-spectral 1-D solvers face a steep computational barrier: they evaluate the viscoelastic response by explicitly re-summing every past load increment, scaling quadratically with time steps as $O(N^2)$. Here we show that this computational penalty is an artifact of algorithmic formula

title: Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning for Cloud Cryptojacking Detection: Effects of Preprocessing and Evaluation Protocols
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied to cloud cryptojacking detection. Classical machine learning models remain among the most widely used approaches for cloud cryptojacking detection. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of six widely used classical machine learning models for AI-based cloud cryptojacking detection under different preprocessing and evaluation settings. Because no public cloud-native cryptojacking dataset is currently available, experiments were conducted using two publicly available proxy datasets, DS2OS and NSL-KDD. The evaluated models include Random

title: Unmasking Compensating Errors in Numerical Weather Models: A Process-Additive Neural Network Approach
abstract: This work introduces a Process Additive Neural Network (PANN) framework to disentangle compensating biases in atmospheric models, where errors in different physical processes can offset each other and obscure their origins. Using a single-column model, each PANN branch represents the tendency error associated with a separate physical process, and the summed branch outputs approximate the total error relative to a reference tendency. Once trained successfully, the branch outputs are expected to provide process-level error attributions and, when averaged, estimates of process-level bias. Initial

title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part I: Framework and Recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target detection and recognition are essential to marine surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Despite substantial advances in deep learning, existing systems typically produce binary detection decisions, categorical labels, or scalar confidence scores, offering limited insight into the physical evidence underlying their outputs. Large language models (LLMs) offer an opportunity to move underwater acoustic sensing toward interpretable, evidence-grounded understanding; however, generic audio encoders struggle to capture the distinctive physical characteristics of under

title: HypoNet Nankai PS: rapid hypocenter determination for the Nankai Trough using physics-informed neural networks with three-dimensional P- and S-wave velocity models
abstract: Rapid and accurate hypocenter determination based on three-dimensional (3D) seismic velocity models is essential for seismic monitoring in subduction zones, yet it remains computationally demanding. HypoNet Nankai, a hypocenter determination package that uses physics-informed neural network (PINN) travel-time inference for a realistic 3D P-wave velocity model of the Nankai Trough subduction zone, was designed to address this problem, but supported only P-wave arrival times. Here, we present HypoNet Nankai PS, which extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times. We first constructed
institutions: Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology

title: YingLan: A Multimodal Ocean Foundation Model for Unified Representation Learning from Heterogeneous Observations
abstract: Multimodal ocean modeling remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity in data structures, physical semantics, and spatiotemporal characteristics across satellite imagery, gridded oceanographic fields, and buoy observations. Existing approaches largely focus on task-specific ocean modeling, while learning transferable representations from heterogeneous observations remains an open problem. To address this challenge, we propose YingLan, a multimodal ocean foundation model that integrates physics-attribute-conditioned dynamic encoding, Spatiotemporal Increment Coupling (STIC), and ocean-

title: Physics-based deep learning for non-stationary adaptive multiple suppression
abstract: Surface-related multiple elimination (SRME) is an indispensable processing step in marine seismic exploration, comprising two main components: multiple prediction and adaptive subtraction. While the multiple prediction is theoretically data-driven and relies on the data itself, the adaptive subtraction step requires a fairly subjective manual control. Our approach introduces a purely data-driven and physics-based deep learning (PDL) algorithm for improving the adaptive multiple subtraction to significantly enhanced performance. There are two main innovations in the proposed deep-learning (DL)

title: Lightweight Machine Learning for Classifying Disaster-Related Social Media Posts
abstract: Classifying disaster-related social-media posts into humanitarian information labels is challenging because individual messages are typically short and context-limited, humanitarian categories can overlap semantically, and the CrisisBench label distribution is strongly imbalanced. This study investigates whether lightweight lexical machine-learning methods can provide effective and computationally efficient classification under these conditions. Using the CrisisBench v1.0 English humanitarian task, comprising 87,455 records across predefined Train, Development and Test splits, we conduct a con

title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions
abstract: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is computationally expensive for iterative building design. Deep learning surrogates offer faster predictions, but generalization across varying room dimensions remains challenging. This study compares two geometry-conditioned neural network surrogate models for rapid indoor airflow and temperature field prediction under varying room sizes. During the architectural design stage, this method is relevant for real-time assessment of whether conditioned supply air will effectively provide fresh and cool air throughout rooms with varying heights and lengths. title: Manifold-Informed Neural Networks for Low-Label ECG Electrolyte Inference
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) supervise on the residual of a known differential operator. Many high-stakes inference problems admit no such operator: clinical signals, behavioral measurements, materials properties. We introduce the Manifold-Informed Neural Network (MINN), a PINN-parallel paradigm that replaces the physics operator residual with a manifold operator residual: a discrete Poisson equation $\mathbf{L}_G \mathbf{H} = s_ϕ(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{m})$ on a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph in the learned latent space, with a learned, task-aware source. title: FireGraphNet: Sub-daily wildfire spread prediction with directed graph neural networks
abstract: Wildfire decisions are made in hours, yet most learned spread models predict daily on targets including burned area. We propose FireGraphNet which formulates 12-hour growth as node classification on directed H3 graphs, with candidates ahead of the front and wind alignment, terrain, fuel continuity and barriers on edges. On satellite perimeters it achieves average precision 1.7-1.9x the strongest distance baseline on test California fires and 1.62x out of state. title: Physics-Shaped, Not Physical: Auditing Physics-Guided Underwater Image Restoration
abstract: Physics-guided networks for underwater image restoration predict transmission and backscatter and invert the image-formation model, yet rarely test whether this physics does any work. We audit one representative design, PhysGuide-Net, with four controlled experiments: five-seed ablations on UIEB with zero-shot evaluation on the complete LSUI (4279 pairs) and AUIED3K (3000 pairs) sets; a data-efficiency study with a capacity-matched control that removes the formation model; and a validation of the predicted maps against measured range on Sea-thru. institutions: National Taiwan University of Science and Technology

title: Will AI kill us all---or just make mathematicians obsolete?
abstract: AI's recent advances have fueled predictions of human intellectual obsolescence and fears for the future of mathematics. I argue that, impressive as these achievements are, they do not establish AI's capacity to invent new concepts and theories or sustain autonomous recursive self-improvement. Human intelligence also involves judgment, imagination, and embodied experience that standard measures fail to capture. Mathematics extends beyond proving theorems: its creative core lies in conceptual discovery and understanding. AI can strengthen this enterprise, but realizing its promise requires prot

title: Physical-Variable-Informed Deep Learning for Robust Diagnosis in Industrial Fluid Transport Systems
abstract: Industrial fluid transport systems are monitored through heterogeneous sensing streams, but robust fault diagnosis remains difficult because response signals vary with operating conditions and differ from physical variables in sampling rate, observation duration and data granularity. To address these challenges, we propose a physical-variable-informed deep learning framework (PhyNet) for robust fault diagnosis under real-world sampling heterogeneity. PhyNet treats physical variables as global operating constraints and response signals as local diagnostic evidence. Its physical-to-response cros
institutions: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Dynamical Batching: How Class-Cycling Training Shapes the Internal Structure of Neural Networks
abstract: We investigate whether cyclically varying the class composition of training batches can modify both the performance and the internal organization of neural networks. Motivated by nonequilibrium systems, in which cycling between related sub-goals can make switching between their solutions increasingly efficient, we introduce Dynamical Batching (DB), a sampling protocol that periodically emphasizes each class while leaving the loss and the optimizer unchanged, and compare it with Uniform Batching (UB), in which every mini-batch has equal class proportions. title: Improved Precipitation Variability in the Community Atmosphere Model through Implementation of a Neural-Network Deep Convection Scheme
abstract: Conventional deep convection schemes remain a primary source of uncertainty in global climate models, yet replacing them with data-driven alternatives while maintaining physical consistency and numerical stability is an open challenge. We present a hybrid configuration of the Community Atmosphere Model version 6 (CAM6), in which a fully connected deep neural network replaces the Zhang-McFarlane deep convection scheme (ZM), while radiation, turbulence, and other cloud processes are left unchanged. The network is trained on output from a storm-resolving global model - the global System for Atmos
institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: TailWeather: from tail to extremes, a global climatological dataset for machine-learning weather forecasting
abstract: Abstract. Weather forecasting models are usually judged by their average skill, yet average skill says little about the rare conditions that matter most. Testing forecasts on those conditions requires a target defined consistently everywhere. Disaster catalogs record harm, but they are sparse and shaped by reporting; climatological tails can be defined everywhere, but rarity does not imply harm. We present TailWeather, a global, land-only, 0.25° dataset of climatological tail events derived from ERA5, covering 1981–2022 and early January 2023. title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning
abstract: We develop an error model for a Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) device that represents the effects of physical faults experienced in a CubeSat mission in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). The CubeSat carries an off-the-shelf low-power Ferroelectric RAM (FRAM) chip and runs repeated read/write tests according to a predefined pattern. We compare every memory snapshot received from the satellite with a reference bitmap to identify bit errors. title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
abstract: Over the past decade, substantial efforts have been devoted to developing machine learning (ML) methods for extracting materials data and, where possible, materials knowledge directly from the scientific literature. This review traces the evolution of these methods from heuristic, rule-based pipelines through natural language processing (NLP) models and transformer-based encoders to, lastly, large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems capable of extracting materials information across multiple modalities, including text, tables, and figures. title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
abstract: The physics-informed neural network (PINN) faces significant challenges when solving compressible multi-medium flows, including the inability to locate interface positions, poor approximation of discontinuities, and difficulty in handling high-pressure-ratio problems between media with large stiffness differences. To address these issues, we propose PINN with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition (PINN-LPCDD), a framework that incorporates the sharp interface method (SIM) into PINNs for solving compressible multi-medium flows. title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels
abstract: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. title: PrecipCorrDiff: A Deep Learning Framework for Generating 0.0625$^\circ$ High-Resolution IMD Gridded Precipitation Data
abstract: High-resolution precipitation datasets are essential for weather forecasting, hydrological modeling, and climate risk assessment, yet observation-based gridded products often lack the spatial detail required for regional applications. Here we present PrecipCorrDiff, a diffusion-based downscaling framework built by modifying the original corrector diffusion based archetecture that incorporates a customized loss function and a multi-scale residual generation strategy to improve the precipitation especially the representation of extremes. PrecipCorrDiff generates 0.0625° resolution India Meteorol

title: AQUAACT: A Joystick-Level Underwater Teleoperation Dataset and Closed-Loop Benchmark
abstract: Underwater robots support a growing range of work, from inspecting offshore structures and pipelines to surveying reefs and accompanying divers. Most of these tasks, however, are still flown by hand by a pilot, which raises the question of whether they can be carried out autonomously instead. On land, vision-language-action (VLA) models already let robots carry out tasks autonomously from language instructions, which makes them a natural candidate for taking the pilot's place. title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
abstract: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known. We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation. title: Weakly Supervised Fish Segmentation through Point-Supervised Tracking and Motion-Informed Language
abstract: Understanding the properties of fish populations is increasingly important. Analyzing fish length, width, and mass is integral to maintaining healthy stock in the aquaculture industry, while counting wild fish populations supports marine conservation and coastal reef restoration efforts. Deep learning-based segmentation models offer a promising means of obtaining such information at scale. Most of these models, however, require costly and time-consuming per-pixel segmentation labels for training, which can take up to two minutes per fish to annotate manually. title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems
abstract: Multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) realizes concurrent acoustic communication and localization, yet the frequency selectivity of the acoustic channel creates uneven positioning capabilities across subcarriers. This paper proposes a localization-oriented subcarrier and power allocation scheme for multi-anchor underwater ISAC systems. We build a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derive closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) under frequency-selective channels with colored noise. title: PolUR: Polarization Aware Multimodal Degradation Perception for Underwater Image Restoration
abstract: Recovering high-quality images from degraded underwater observations is crucial for underwater exploration. Polarization observations show promise as an effective source of complementary physical cues for recovering target radiance under clear-water conditions. However, existing methods have yet to jointly model raw intensity information and polarization cues to enable image restoration driven by an understanding of mixed degradations (color casts, haze, and low light). title: Physical Processes Driving Year-to-Year Surface Temperature Variability Changes in a Warming Climate
abstract: Under anthropogenic greenhouse forcing, climate models project a decrease in year-to-year temperature variability in the mid-to-high latitudes and an increase in the tropics and subtropics. Here, we examine year-to-year temperature variability in the CESM Large Ensemble in concert with an idealized stochastic moist energy balance model (SMEBM) with effective surface heat capacity and local feedback parameter specified based on CESM. title: SEA-HELM Audio: Evaluating Multilingual ASR-LLM Pipeline Performance Across SEA-HELM Subsets
abstract: We introduce SEA-HELM Audio, a Southeast Asian (SEA) multilingual evaluation framework that extends the text-based SEA-HELM benchmark to assess performance degradation in cascaded automatic speech recognition and large language model (ASR-LLM) pipelines. Using synthesized speech, we compare speech-input and text-input performance across five languages (Chinese, English, Malay, Indonesian, and Tamil) on multiple-choice reasoning and instruction-following tasks. We evaluate open-weight and commercial ASR-LLM systems using identical verifiers and quantify the speech gap as the difference between

title: Adaptive Prescribed Performance Trajectory Tracking for Uncertain Autonomous Underwater Vehicles With Input Saturation
abstract: Accurate trajectory tracking is essential for autonomous underwater vehicles operating with uncertain hydrodynamics and limited thruster authority. This paper develops a low-complexity adaptive prescribed performance controller for uncertain underwater vehicle dynamics with coupled and saturated inputs. The proposed method adapts the performance functions directly through the mismatch between the requested and saturated control inputs, enlarging the performance funnels only when the available actuation cannot meet the nominal specifications. title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. title: OceanTensorCube and ST-MMT: A Multimodal Data and Transformer System for Seven-Day Forecasting of Pyropia Bleaching
abstract: Bleaching of cultured Pyropia (laver) causes losses in Korean seaweed farming. We present a system that forecasts bleaching seven days ahead for farm clusters. OceanTensorCube aligns 32 channels from public marine, meteorological, ocean-model and satellite sources on a 30 m grid, and ST-MMT, a 9.2-million-parameter spatiotemporal transformer with hub-style multi-head cross-attention between variable groups, maps a 14-day input window to a seven-day-ahead bleaching probability. title: Energy-Aware Earth System Science: A Community Roadmap
abstract: Earth system models underpin the evidence that informs net-zero policy, yet their energy demands are rarely considered when judging model quality. Using archived output from 159 models spanning five generations of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP), we show that model error has fallen at a constant rate of 13.5 per cent per doubling of compute since 1995. Halving CMIP6 error would require 28 times more compute. title: Input-Constrained Active Disturbance Rejection Control for AUVs
abstract: This paper addresses the control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in dynamic environments, where wave-induced forces, modelling errors, and actuator limitations make reliable control challenging. Active disturbance rejection control (ADRC), together with an extended state observer (ESO), estimates lumped uncertainties online, simplifying control design using nominal models. title: UDL-RT: A unified differentiable all-sky microwave radiative transfer model with learnable parameterizations
abstract: Radiance-based retrievals and data assimilation require radiative transfer models (RTMs) to simulate radiances and quantify their sensitivities to atmospheric and surface conditions. Conventional RTMs often rely on separately maintained forward, tangent-linear, and adjoint codes, complicating model development and extension. title: Data-driven and physics-guided hindcasting of measured wave spectra
abstract: Short-range hindcasts of measured wave spectra are evaluated using a recurrent model initialized by one hourly buoy spectrum and supplied with local wind, fetch and depth. Measurements from three Baltic Sea stations are combined for training in 2017--2020, validation in 2021 and testing in 2022. ERA5 reanalysis supplies winds throughout the twelve-hour prediction interval. The comparison examines supervision of spectral variance, peak frequency and peak amplitude, followed by empirical wind-sea bounds and a local relaxation constraint. title: Graph-Learned Spring SST Evolution and Land-Ocean Synergy Improve Yangtze Summer Rainfall Prediction
abstract: Seasonal prediction of Yangtze summer rainfall is challenged by nonstationary oceanic precursors. Here we demonstrate that accounting for the evolution of spring SST and state-dependent land surface information improves predictability. Graph total variation (GTV) is applied to March-May SST fields over the western Pacific, Niño3.4, and tropical Indian Ocean to identify spatially coherent, month-specific SST coefficients for each grid cell and month to form a scalar GTV index. title: Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck: A Hybrid Diffusion-Autoregressive Framework for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: Autoregressive models (ARMs) face a "Sequentiality Bottleneck" in reasoning, while diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallelism but lack semantic coherence. To addresses both limitations, we propose Collaborative Reasoning Asymmetric Learning (CoRAL), a hybrid framework via an Asymmetric Planner-Executor (APE) architecture: a DLM Planner generates K diverse reasoning trajectories in parallel, while a large ARM Executor selects the optimal plan and synthesizes the final answer. title: Sounds Cheesy - Bridging the Texture Gap Between Dairy and Plant-Based cheese with Non-Contact Ultrasound and AI
abstract: Plant-based cheeses often fail to reproduce the texture of dairy cheese. Closing this gap is slow because the reference methods, texture profile analysis (TPA) and sensory panels, destroy the sample and are poorly suited to screening many formulations in a timely and cost-effective manner. Here we show that non-contact, air-coupled ultrasonic imaging combined with machine learning can characterise cheese texture rapidly and without damaging the sample. title: Learning to Forecast on Multiple Spatiotemporal Hierarchies
abstract: Hierarchical forecasting exploits aggregation structures that expose multiple views of the same underlying spatiotemporal forecasting problem, while ensuring coherence among forecasts. Individual series provide fine-grained information, while progressively coarser aggregates reveal temporal and spatial patterns at different scales. In the associated deep learning architectures, the hierarchy determines which aggregate series are available and how they are processed together with individual series (e.g., through reconciliation or message-passing operators). title: Tropical Cyclone Attributes in Sparse Autoencoder Features of an AI Weather Model
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) weather models now forecast weather events skillfully, but how they represent these events internally remains unknown. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide sparse features for probing hidden states, but how information about multiple physical attributes of an event is organized across them remains unclear. Using tropical cyclones in GraphCast as a test case, we analyze 2,115 six-hourly timesteps from 205 cyclones, relating SAE activations to position, intensity, and pressure structure across five Layer-8 decompositions and 16 processor layers. title: Key Findings for Small UAS for Post-Disaster Damage Assessment from the CURSE'26 Exercise
abstract: The CLARKE building and road damage assessment AI classifier was incorporated into the Catastrophic Unmanned Remote Sensing Exercise (CURSE) 2026, which trained 23 small uncrewed aerial systems (sUAS) teams from state and local agencies and non-governmental organizations in Florida and Missouri on how to collect imagery for an incident command Remote Sensing Cell. Although CLARKE has been operationally deployed to two hurricanes (Debby and Helene), CURSE'26 presented an opportunity to evaluate the machine learning model with a larger set of never-before-seen orthomosaics. title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. title: The Evolution of In-Premise Networks In the Era of Immersive Services: From Copper to Fiber-to-The Room [Invited Tutorial]
abstract: The telecommunications industry is shifting toward an experience-driven era defined by immersive applications that impose stringent network demands. While passive optical network (PON)-based Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) architectures have historically delivered high-capacity broadband, a growing performance gap between access and indoor networks necessitates driving fiber deeper into premises. Complementing existing copper and WiFi technologies, Fiber-to-the-Room (FTTR) is emerging as a critical enabler. title: Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy
abstract: With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude information networks (LAINs) must provide reliable communication, environmental sensing, and target identification to support efficient and safe airspace operation. Although integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) provides a foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing, identification must also be incorporated to meet airspace safety and regulatory requirements. institutions: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training. title: Querying Multimodal Scientific Papers with AI: Practices and Preferences Across Blind, Low-Vision, and Sighted Scientists
abstract: Visual diagrams, figures, and tables are central to scientific papers, and convey information beyond what is captured in text. While blind or low-vision (BLV) scientists have traditionally relied on static alternative text to access figures in papers, the rise of artificial intelligence (AI) has made interactive question-answering (QA) a feasible paradigm for visual exploration; yet little is known about how scientists use visual QA in practice or how to improve its accessibility. title: Day-ahead power prediction at the SMARTEOLE wind farm: evaluation of the Alpila|WIND engine 0.9.0 against measured production
abstract: This report compares the day-ahead farm power of the Alpila|WIND engine 0.9.0 with the measured production of the SMARTEOLE wind farm (seven Senvion MM82 turbines, 14.35 MW, northern France) from February to May 2020. The data are from the SMARTEOLE wind farm control open dataset. The physics-based engine contains no machine-learning components and no parameters fitted to the farm or to the evaluation data. title: Coarse-Grained Predictive Resource Allocation Framework enabling In-Premise XR Collaborations
abstract: Immersive extended reality (XR) applications are key enablers of human-centric connectivity in next-generation networks. However, meeting their high-throughput, ultra-low-latency, and high-reliability demands while preventing cyber-sickness remains a critical challenge, especially in environments with non-deterministic wireless connectivity. Fiber-To-The-Room (FTTR), extending widely deployed Fiber-To-The-Home (FTTH) infrastructure, offers a promising solution.
