title: Know Yourself and Know Your Neighbour: A Syntactically Informed Self-Supervised Compositional Sentence Representation Learning Framework using a Recursive Hypernetwork
abstract: Sentence representation learning is still an open challenge in Natural Language Processing. In this work, we propose a new self-supervised framework for learning sentence representations, using a special type of neural network called a recursive hypernetwork. Our proposed model composes the representation of a sentence from representations of words by applying a recursive composition through the parse tree. title: Beyond the record: evaluating probabilistic AI weather forecasts deep in the tail
abstract: Can probabilistic artificial intelligence (AI) weather forecasts retain skill beyond their training domain? We compare four state-of-the-art AI models (ArchesWeatherGen, U-Cast, WeatherNext2 and GenCast-mini) with the physics-based IFS-ENS over land in 2022, at 1.5° resolution and lead times of 2--10 days. Monthly ERA5 records from 1979--2021 define common historical boundaries, and we characterize new records set in 2022 by their depth, i.e., the exceedance margin relative to local historical variability. title: Divide-and-Conquer Neural Bayes Estimation for Spatial and Spatiotemporal Point Process Models
abstract: Spatial and spatiotemporal point process models are widely used to analyze event data across many scientific disciplines, but likelihood-based Bayesian inference is often computationally prohibitive due to intractable likelihoods, high-dimensional latent structures, and dependence on event history. Existing approximate and likelihood-free methods mitigate some of these challenges, but often at the cost of reduced statistical efficiency, imperfect uncertainty quantification, or information loss from reliance on predefined summary statistics. title: Huayu-Global: Skillful real-time quasi-global precipitation retrieval
abstract: Satellite precipitation products face a persistent trade-off: real-time estimates are timely but less accurate, whereas the most reliable products are often released months after observation. This delay keeps high-quality precipitation information outside the decision window for flood warning and disaster response. Here we report Huayu-Global, a cross-constellation deep-learning system that combines three geostationary sensor streams from five satellites through a common retrieval framework and generates coherent quasi-global precipitation fields every thirty minutes. title: Digital Typhoon Dataset V3: Benchmarking for Multi-spectral Extension and Analyzing Systematic Bias in Intensity Regression
abstract: This paper presents the Digital Typhoon Dataset V3, a new version of the longest typhoon satellite image dataset spanning nearly 50 years, designed to benchmark machine learning models on long-term spatio-temporal data. The latest addition to Dataset V3 is multispectral satellite data, enabling multi-channel models. We investigate data-splitting strategies and present benchmarking results for the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Experimental results show that, under the current dataset construction and experimental setting, multi-channel inputs do not clearly outperform single-channel inputs
institutions: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

title: Evaluating Predictor-Corrector Dependence in Hard-Constrained Climate Emulators
abstract: Climate emulators often enforce physical constraints by correcting each state predicted by a neural network, but evaluating only the corrected forecast conflates predictor skill with the effect of the correction. We introduce an evaluation framework that separates these contributions by comparing corrected forecasts, pre-correction predictions along corrected trajectories, and autonomous rollouts with correction disabled. title: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs
abstract: Deep learning (DL) models can now run on microcontrollers (MCUs). Through neural architecture search (NAS), we can search DL models that meet the constraints of MCUs. Among various constraints, energy and latency costs of the model inference are critical metrics. To predict them, existing research relies on coarse proxies such as multiply-accumulations (MACs) and model's input parameters, often resulting in inaccurate predictions or requiring extensive data collection. title: Input- and Feature-Space Correction for Cross-Hospital IHC Grading
abstract: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are trained predominantly on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images but are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for immunohistochemistry (IHC), where cross-hospital differences can impair grading. However, systematic comparisons of correction methods for cross-hospital IHC grading remain limited. title: Accounting for model error in ensemble variational data assimilation through learned generative dynamics
abstract: Many approaches have recently been proposed to combine data assimilation with machine learning for improved forecasts with geophysical models. Here, we focus on combining advanced sequential data assimilation schemes with a generative forecasting model which accounts for complex model errors. This generative model provides a stochastic approximation of the conditional distribution of the successor state given the current state. title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). In pHRI tasks, robots are expected to perform task-space motions robustly while remaining compliance with human disturbance, which proposes distinct control objectives. Most existing approaches focus mainly on either robustness or compliance and rely on force sensors for real-time tracking. title: Using Set Learning to Improve Set-Valued Classifiers on Long-tailed Data
abstract: Set-valued classification (SVC) offers a practical approach to communicating uncertainty while maintaining accuracy by predicting variable-sized sets per input rather than fixed-sized sets (e.g. top-1 or top-5). However, set-valued classifiers (SVCs) exhibit significantly degraded performance on long-tailed and imbalanced datasets, a setting for which they are ostensibly well-suited. This becomes apparent under macro-average evaluation, which weighs all classes equally. title: GhostLock: Learning-Assisted Blind GPS Signal Nullification Without Victim-Side Information
abstract: The Global Positioning System (GPS) provides critical positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services for numerous safety- and mission-critical applications, making it an attractive target for physical-layer attacks. While GPS spoofing and jamming have been extensively studied, GPS Signal Nullification (GSN)-a physical-layer attack that suppresses authentic satellite signals through destructive interference prior to acquisition-remains largely unexplored. title: CartoVec: General-Purpose Location Embeddings from Open Map Data
abstract: Geographic coordinates are common inputs in applied machine learning, but latitude and longitude describe position rather than the surrounding environment. Image-grounded location encoders learn this context from satellite or ground-level imagery; structured open map data offers another source of supervision whose utility for continuous coordinate encoders remains less explored. title: INCONVENIENT: A Benchmark to Assess LLM Generalization Capabilities from Convenience Samples
abstract: Machine learning models for tabular prediction typically assume that training data are representative of the population on which they will be deployed. In practice, however, data are often collected based on convenience, availability, or cost, resulting in systematic sampling biases that can distort feature--target relationships and undermine real-world generalization. On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
abstract: Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. title: Building age estimation based on widely available multi-source1 geospatial data
abstract: Building age is fundamental for urban infrastructure safety, operation, and planning, as it directly affects structural safety, and sustainable development. Existing methods mostly rely on detailed building information such as street view, function, or materials, which are harder to obtain than geospatial data like satellite imagery and Digital Surface Models (DSMs). However, existing methods based on those geospatial data mainly rely on optical imagery and local texture features, limiting their ability to capture structural information and distinguish buildings from different periods. title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
abstract: Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. title: Topology optimization of shipboard components for Navy shock certification via the Dynamic Design Analysis Method
abstract: Shipboard equipment must survive the transient loads of underwater explosions. The U.S. Navy certifies such equipment with the Dynamic Design Analysis Method (DDAM), a modal response analysis driven by Navy shock design spectra. DDAM is well established as a verification tool, yet it is rarely used as a design driver in topology optimization. The design spectrum depends on the modal mass, a non-smooth coupling that classical sensitivity formulations do not address. title: Online Seakeeping Forecast Coupling System Identification With Nonlinear Pseudo Spectral Potential-Flow
abstract: This paper presents a grey-box framework for a robust deterministic, real-time prediction of coupled surge-heave-pitch motion in waves. Rather than prescribing a complete hydrodynamic model from captive model tests or relying on a black-box surrogate, three coupled compact, dynamics equations are identified with constrained ridge-regression of a short time-history of free-running body motion data in waves. title: A GPU-Resident Pipeline for Multi-Robot 3D Inspection with Limited Perception
abstract: We present a complete, GPU-resident pipeline for multi-robot 3D inspection of underwater structures. Given a triangle mesh and a fleet of $K$ robots, each carrying a short-range, limited field-of-view camera, the pipeline computes 6-DOF trajectories that jointly cover a target fraction of the surface while minimizing a linearly interpolated makespan/total-cost objective. abstract: Robustness studies of vision-language models (VLMs) grade degradation on nominal severity scales ("level 1-5") that carry no physical units, and they rarely ask whether a model's confidence follows the loss of visibility. title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
abstract: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. GCMagicc v1: a fast generative emulator for multivariate climate-impact ensembles
abstract: Abstract. Projecting the impacts of climate change requires large ensembles of climate variables that match historical observations, align with the warming ranges assessed by the IPCC, and can efficiently run new future emissions scenarios, including the newest generation of climate model scenarios (CMIP7) and pathways consistent with countries’ Paris Agreement pledges. abstract: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. title: Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
abstract: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. title: Polyscene: Scenario Planning as Diversity Planning
abstract: Scenario planning is a foresight practice in which analysts construct a small set of plausible futures and prepare an organisation for each. Each scenario is a narrative that must be plausible, internally consistent, relevant and challenging, and the set as a whole must be differentiated. The practice remains manual: a workshop (i.e., a facilitated meeting in which a small group of experts writes the narratives) considers only the factors it has time for, carries the biases of the experts who run it, and cannot be redone whenever conditions change. title: Planning under Noise with Neural Operators
abstract: Planning under uncertain control execution noise requires reliable feedback policies across diverse environments. We introduce Planning Under Noise (PUN), a neural operator that learns noise-aware value fields for planning in unseen geometries. SAFTER: Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability for Robust Reinforcement Learning under Distribution Shift
abstract: Learning safe policies that generalize to unseen environments is difficult under bounded actuation, where an unsafe decision may become unrecoverable. Conventional control barrier function (CBF) filters enforce only instantaneous safety and ignore future recoverability. We propose SAFTER (Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability), which embeds a differentiable, closed-form backup-CBF filter into Soft Actor-Critic training. abstract: The automated detection of baleen whale calls generally requires large annotated datasets, which are not available for many species and populations. We investigate whether pretrained bioacoustic embeddings, combined with a prototypical few-shot classifier, allow such calls to be detected and classified from only a handful of labelled examples. Two embedding networks are compared: Perch, a general-purpose bioacoustic model trained predominantly on birdsong, and WhaleVAD, a task-specific blue- and fin-whale call detector. abstract: Internal solitary wave (ISW) remote sensing requires task parameters and spatial information to be transferred across image acquisition, detection, stripe extraction, and propagation prediction. Here, we present ISW-Agent, which integrates large language model (LLM) interpretation with n8n workflows and independent scientific models through structured task constraints, geospatial transformations, and stage-specific output validation. title: Contrastive learning for video reuse detection
abstract: The incorporation of footage from other sources has long been a concern from a copyright perspective, as such usage can harm the interests of rights holders. Recent trends in the ``remixing'' of social media content and the development of bespoke stock libraries for specialist causes mean that methods to identify content reuse will have a range of applications. In this paper, we develop a framework based on a Siamese network fine tuned using contrastive learning to identify potential sources for key frames in a given video. title: Uncertainty-aware AI-enabled framework for predicting hydrogen dispersion in confined spaces to enhance operator situational awareness
abstract: We present a two-stage AI-enabled framework for enhancing operator situational awareness during compressed hydrogen bunkering in maritime confined spaces. In the event of a leak, the framework first estimates the unknown leakage rate from early sensor readings and then forecasts how the hydrogen cloud will disperse over the next time steps, providing operators with a predicted concentration map together with confidence bounds. The framework is based on two independent AI models building one AI system. The AI system is designed as a decision-support tool. It augments sensor readings, and thus e
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: Observation Assimilation Transformer: Probabilistic Weather Analysis from Sparse Station Observations
abstract: We present the Observation Assimilation Transformer (OAT), a geometry-aware neural process that corrects and refines a prior numerical weather prediction (NWP) field into a high-resolution posterior field by assimilating sparse observations. OAT is an encoder-decoder transformer that considers a set of observed locations and their NWP prior to condition predictions at a set of arbitrary unobserved query locations. Its sparse attention mechanism makes it scalable to thousands of station observations and depends on relative positions between locations, never on the absolute coordinates. The mode
institutions: Board of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology
Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology MeteoSwiss

title: AdaptMIL: Domain Adaptation for Multiple Instance Learning in Digital Pathology
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) support a wide range of histopathology tasks on whole-slide images through multiple instance learning (MIL). Despite recent progress, these models remain sensitive to cross-hospital distribution shifts: performance often degrades when a task head (e.g., classification) is trained on data from one hospital and then used on data from another hospital. To address this challenge, we propose AdaptMIL, a training strategy for integrating domain adaptation into MIL training. AdaptMIL is motivated by our finding that directly applying domain adaptation objectives dur

title: Modeling Discourse Profiles in Climate Misinformation Discourse
abstract: Prior work on climate misinformation detection typically classifies individual comments or claims using text alone. This framing overlooks a key property of online climate discourse: misinformation is often produced, reinforced, and sustained through recurring rhetorical patterns that reappear across comments and threads. Using a large-scale TikTok climate discourse dataset, we construct discourse profiles by clustering climate-related comments into recurring rhetorical patterns. We then incorporate these profiles into fine-grained climate misinformation classifiers using a late-fusion archite

title: TerraNostra-Bench: Benchmarking Spatial Downscaling and Temporal Rollout for Global 1-km Land-Use Reconstruction
abstract: Uncertainty in the terrestrial carbon cycle remains a major constraint in climate projections, partly due to imperfect land surface representations in Earth system models. We propose a data-driven framework for high-resolution land-use reconstruction, treated as a semantic-segmentation task, that combines coarse-resolution scenario data and climate classification with static geophysical features to produce annual land-use maps at 1 km resolution. We introduce TerraNostra-Bench, a change-aware evaluation protocol that separates spatial downscaling from autoregressive temporal rollout and scores
institutions: CMCC Foundation - Euro-Mediterranean Center on Climate Change

title: GAMF-Net: Grouped Availability-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Smartphone Skin Lesion Classification
abstract: Smartphone clinical images provide a low-cost data source for computer-aided skin lesion classification in resource-constrained settings, but images alone cannot fully capture patients' medical histories and lesion symptoms. To address the lack of structured organization among heterogeneous clinical variables, the ambiguity between observed and imputed values, and the risk that clinical information may interfere with visual evidence, we propose GAMF-Net, a grouped availability-aware multimodal fusion network. Ten clinical variables are divided into three semantic groups---demographics, history

title: Same Target, Different Origins: Aligning Latent Rollout for Consistent PDE Emulation
abstract: Neural PDE solvers commonly generate multi-step predictions through autoregressive rollout, recursively applying a learned evolution operator and feeding each prediction back as input for the next step. Approximation errors can therefore propagate through the rollout, causing predictions at a shared target time to depend on their temporal origins and rollout depths. For a well-posed deterministic PDE flow, however, states at different times along the same physical trajectory should, under exact evolution, reach the same target state. To this end, we propose Align Latent Rollout (ALR), a regula

title: A100: A Hybrid Vision Foundation Model for Agricultural Plant Image Analysis
abstract: The use of accurate vision models for crop monitoring, disease diagnosis, and plant phenotyping in agriculture is hindered by the lack of expertly annotated data, especially in developing countries. We propose A100, an agricultural vision foundation model that is pre-trained using self-supervised learning on 3 million unlabeled images from fields covering more than 100 crop species. A100 uses a hybrid CNN-Transformer backbone that fuses MBConv stages for local feature extraction with Transformer stages for global contextual representation. A100 uses pre-training with the integration of DINO se
institutions: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Bhopal

title: Learning to Reason Like a Cytopathologist:Clinically Grounded Multiscale Evidential Learning for Cervical Cytology
abstract: Cervical cytology presents a fundamentally ambiguous diagnostic landscape, where equivocal categories such as Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance (ASC-US) occupy a morphological grey zone that is definitional. For clinical decision support, the goal extends beyond assigning a definitive label to every sample: cases must also be distinguished by whether the available evidence supports a confident decision or warrants further consideration, a distinction conventional classification models are not designed to explicitly represent. We propose a multiscale evidential framework that
institutions: Singapore University of Technology and Design

title: Revolutionizing 6G Wireless Networks with RISs: Enhancements in Sensing and Communications
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have emerged as one of the most promising technologies for the next-generation wireless networks, offering advantages such as cost efficiency, low power consumption, flexible deployment, and large effective aperture. Extensive studies have demonstrated the capabilities of RISs to enhance communication performance, including coverage extension, sum-rate improvement, interference suppression, security enhancement, etc. As 6G networks continue to evolve, wireless sensing is expected to play a pivotal role alongside communication. Undoubtedly, RISs posses

title: Audio-Visual Dog Identification and Tracking in Real-World Videos
abstract: Identifying individual dogs from barks in real-world videos remains challenging and largely unexplored. Solving this problem would enable long-term behavioral analysis, veterinary monitoring, and animal welfare monitoring by attributing vocalizations and behaviors to the correct individual. Real-world videos are challenging because multiple dogs may bark simultaneously, become occluded, or move in and out of view. Prior studies show that canine vocalizations and visual appearance contain discriminative identity information, but these modalities have largely been studied independently. We prese
institutions: The University of Texas at Arlington

title: HyperTaxa: Multiscale Genome Representations for Generalized Microbial Taxonomic Inference
abstract: Reliable microbial taxonomic inference is challenged by the rapid growth of newly sequenced organisms and incomplete reference coverage. While alignment- and database-driven tools remain essential for reference-backed identification, they are not designed for learned inference over species absent from genome-level training. We introduce HyperTaxa, a taxonomy-aligned representation learning framework for open-set microbial taxonomic inference. HyperTaxa encodes whole genomes as multiscale hyperspectral k-mer transition fields and aligns these representations to a taxonomy-derived semantic space

title: TabGift: A Context-Efficient Foundation Model for Tabular Data Generation
abstract: Tabular data generation aims to synthesize realistic samples from limited observations while faithfully capturing the underlying data distribution. Tabular foundation models (TFMs), pretrained on diverse tabular tasks and adapted through in-context learning, have demonstrated strong predictive capabilities, suggesting the potential of extending this paradigm to tabular data generation. However, the strong predictive performance of TFMs often relies on sufficiently large context sets, whereas tabular generation is typically needed precisely when target data are scarce. Extending the foundation-

title: CFC26: Building Evaluations for Deployment in Sonar-Based Fish Counting
abstract: Accurate counts of fish populations are essential for monitoring ecosystems and making decisions for conservation, harvest limits, and river management. In many field deployments, these counts are obtained from sonar videos that experts must inspect manually, making large-scale monitoring slow, expensive, and difficult. Automated counting systems have been proposed as a scalable alternative, but so far this promise has been difficult to realize in deployment. Developing evaluations that better reflect real-world deployment conditions will help close this gap and drive improvements in counting

title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
abstract: Over 4 billion years, Earth's atmosphere has been transformed from a composition devoid of molecular oxygen (O$_2$) to one where O$_2$ is now 21% of our modern atmosphere by volume. With high quantities of O$_2$, an ozone (O$_3$) layer can form and partially shield the surface from biologically harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV). The evolution of the O$_3$ layer has previously been simulated under the modern Sun by independent groups with separate models. Here, we present simulations of Earth's atmosphere from four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and a 3D chemistry-climat

title: Hyperbolic Time Series Forecasting with Learnable Decomposition and Manifold Dynamics
abstract: Multiscale structure is central to time series forecasting: temporal signals contain slowly varying trends, intermediate seasonal patterns, and high-frequency residuals. Traditional forecasters model this multiscale structure in Euclidean space, without representing the ordering it induces among components. We identify that cascaded decomposition orders components by their characteristic frequencies, forming a natural frequency hierarchy. title: Wet-Biased Data Pipelines Mislead the Training and Evaluation of Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Generative models for precipitation nowcasting are trained and evaluated predominantly on wet-biased datasets, which over-represent precipitation events to emphasize rare extremes. Selecting test cases based on target observations is known to favor forecasts that match the selected distribution rather than the intended deployment distribution. We show analytically how this target-dependent sampling also shifts the conditional distribution learned by generative models. When training and test sampling match, even an ideal model learns precisely the distribution favored by evaluation, allowing th
institutions: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)
Agenzia Regionale Prevenzione e Ambiente della Regione Emilia-Romagna

title: Monotone Piecewise-Linear Harmonization of Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance With Unsupervised Deep Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features Learning
abstract: Surface reflectance products derived from optical satellite may exhibit systematic inconsistencies across acquisition dates, because atmospheric correction is generally performed independently for each image. Such residual biases distort the temporal behavior of invariant ground targets and reduce the reliability of multitemporal surface reflectance analysis. This study proposes Deep Multitemporal Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (DeepMGCCA), an unsupervised deep multiview pseudoinvariant feature learning framework that integrates Deep Generalized Canonical Correlation Analysis (GCCA

title: Glass-Box Deep Reinforcement Learning for High-Speed Flow Control
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is challenging long-held assumptions in active flow control. By learning directly from interaction with a flow, DRL agents can find actuation strategies for nonlinear, unsteady flows without explicit models, often exploiting mechanisms that classical control would not anticipate. High-speed flows are a demanding test of this promise: shocks, shock/boundary-layer interactions, transition, aerothermal loading and microsecond-scale dynamics strain both algorithms and hardware. Yet most demonstrations remain idealized, low-speed simulations with limited evidence o

title: Physical Operating-Condition-Guided Vision-Language Matching for Cavitation Diagnosis in Industrial Pipeline Systems
abstract: Cavitation diagnosis in industrial pipeline systems is challenging because acoustic responses vary substantially with operating conditions, while similar time-frequency patterns may correspond to different cavitation states. To address this issue, we propose a physical operating-condition-guided vision-language matching (POC-VLM) for cavitation diagnosis. POC-VLM first constructs physical operating-condition-aware semantic descriptions by explicitly incorporating sample-specific operating variables into candidate cavitation texts. A time-frequency-conditioned text adaptation module then dynami
institutions: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Causal Integrated Gradients: Scalable Feature Attribution Along Causal Paths
abstract: Existing feature attribution methods that account for feature dependencies do not scale to high dimensions. We propose causal integrated gradients (CIG) and causal expected gradients (CEG), which extend integrated gradients to incorporate prior causal structure among input features while retaining its computational efficiency and, under conditions on the causal graph, its axiomatic guarantees. In many settings, some causal structure between features is already known, for example, that a transcription factor causally regulates a target gene's expression. Yet existing gradient-based methods cann

title: Variable Masking for Climate Emulation in ACE
abstract: In the recent AI Model Intercomparison Project (AIMIP) benchmark, the ACE2.1-ERA5 emulator was shown to underestimate the true near-surface warming trend both during the training period and the out-of-sample extrapolation period. In this work, we present M-ACE2S (Masked-ACE2S), a modified version of the stochastic ACE2S model, which uses variable masking during training and reduces the reliance of M-ACE2S on any single input channel. We show that M-ACE2S improves long-term near-surface air temperature prediction. We also present a novel data normalization strategy called "global mean removal",

title: A decomposition-integration framework coupling singular spectrum analysis with a volatility-adaptive LSTM for stock price forecasting
abstract: Financial time series exhibit multi-scale, high-noise, and non-stationary volatility dynamics. Decomposition--integration frameworks built on complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) have advanced this field, yet existing CEEMDAN hybrids remain unstable: high-frequency mode mixing contaminates downstream predictors, and the heterogeneous volatility of decomposed components is not matched by any volatility-adaptive mechanism. To address these gaps, this paper proposes CEEMDAN-SE-SSA-VMGL. CEEMDAN adaptively decomposes the original series, and sample-entropy-d
institutions: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

title: Forecast lead time and the timing of crew deployment for weather-driven power outages using AI weather models
abstract: Utilities request mutual aid crews to restore power after severe storms, and requesting early secures more crews but relies on less accurate forecasts. We examined how forecast lead time affects the value of outage predictions for crew deployment, using operational forecasts from two AI weather models, GraphCast and FourCastNet, to predict outage occurrence for counties across the contiguous United States 24 to 120 hours ahead. Forecasts were evaluated by the share of outage burden captured by the counties where crews would be staged. Captured burden declined with lead time: the loss between t

title: A Controlled Evaluation of Curvature Inspired Scalar Feature Scaling for Domain Generalization
abstract: Domain-specific curvature is an appealing idea for domain generalization (DG), but curvature learning can denote substantially different computations. This paper evaluates one deliberately narrow implementation: the code calls it HyperDG, but it rescales Euclidean encoder features during training by learned positive scalars and uses an ordinary linear classifier on unscaled Euclidean features at inference. It does not implement a Lorentz or Poincaré representation, geodesic prediction, or a Sharpness-Aware Minimization inner loop. We audit the executed objective and evaluate six conditions on

title: A Tutorial on Quantum Amplitude Embedding with Data Re-Uploading
abstract: Amplitude embedding lets a variational quantum model read many classical features with few qubits, but the model output is then only a quadratic form in the normalized input. Data re-uploading, which encodes the input repeatedly between trainable blocks, can be used to enrich such a model. Because every additional upload of an amplitude embedding repeats a costly state preparation, the gain that an upload buys has to be known before the gates are spent. This tutorial thus addresses the problem of explaining what data re-uploading adds to an amplitude-embedded model and how large the gain is. W

title: BEACON: Bridging Multimodal Semantics and Asynchronous Propagation for Cloud System Anomaly Detection
abstract: Modern large-scale cloud systems continuously generate massive and multimodal observability data, such as time-series metrics, log records, and system dependency graphs, which reflect the health state of the system. To ensure reliable cloud system operation, anomaly detection models identify abnormal states by analyzing these multimodal observations. However, existing approaches rely on simple fusion strategies and graph learning, ignoring the semantic gap among modalities and the asynchronous spatio-temporal dependencies across system instances over time. To this end, we propose BEACON, a fra

title: Auditable and Deployable Multi-Agent Motion Planning via Posetal Games from Legal Guidelines
abstract: When robots are deployed in the real-world, they must interact with other agents and accomplish their own goals while adhering to legal constraints. These potentially conflicting objectives are often only partially prioritized, making scalarized objectives or fully specified hierarchies unsuitable. We present a framework for multi-agent motion planning under legal requirements based on games with partially ordered preferences (posetal games). Scenario-independent legal guidelines order abstract legal concerns, from which we automatically derive agent preferences and a legal game for any concre

title: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP): Towards standardisation of global glacier projections
abstract: The Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP) provides an international framework for the coordinated evaluation and comparison of global glacier evolution models and their projections of glacier change. Its fourth phase, GlacierMIP4, updates previous global glacier projections through a standardised experimental design. For the first time, the protocol includes simulations extending to 2300 and an overshoot scenario for a subset of climate projections and requires monthly output of individual mass-balance components such as melt, accumulation and refreezing, in addition to annual res

title: Constructed regional photovoltaic generation fields improve ultra-short-term distributed solar forecasting
abstract: Ultra-short-term forecasting of densely distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems remains challenging because external meteorological and satellite products may not adequately resolve rapid local variations, while heterogeneous PV systems exhibit different generation responses under similar atmospheric conditions. Meanwhile, dense PV fleets provide spatially distributed measurements that reveal regional generation dynamics. Here, we reformulate fleet-level PV forecasting from modeling discrete station time series to predicting explicit, spatially structured regional PV generation fields. We develo

title: Generative Recommenders Forget the Long Tail: Restoring Memorization in Retrieval and Ranking
abstract: Generative recommenders replace the retrieve-then-rank cascade with a single model: beam search over semantic item identifiers performs retrieval, and the same likelihood performs ranking. We show that this shared score makes them forget long-tail items twice. In retrieval, beam search keeps identifier prefixes by the probability mass of their subtrees, so tail items are pruned early, and a wider beam admits few more of them. institutions: University of Science and Technology of China

title: Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Descriptors as Colored Multigraphs
abstract: The combinatorial explosion in monomial counts limits the extension of global permutationally invariant polynomial (PIP) potential energy surfaces to larger molecular systems. We use graph-theoretic language to reformulate PIPs as colored multigraphs and develop a series of theoretical and computational tools. First, we introduce an offline PIP generation algorithm whose cost has an upper bound independent of atom count for a fixed degree cutoff and number of element types. Second, we introduce a new online PIP evaluation algorithm, termed tensor-network descent. For the full PIP set through d
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Correlation-Aware Reconstruction for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Reconstruction-based detectors for multivariate time series anomaly detection typically learn a single entangled representation of normal behavior and flag anomalies based on reconstruction error. However, real-world anomalies are not only isolated spikes in a single channel but also disruptions in the relationships between channels, where each sensor individually appears normal, but their joint behavior deviates from the norm. Because these models compress both temporal evolution and inter-channel structure into this single space, they lack an explicit mechanism to isolate such inter-channel

title: GraphCast-Mamba: Learning Non-Markovian Corrections for Weather Forecasting
abstract: Unresolved atmospheric processes can introduce history dependence beyond the short input windows used by many weather forecasting models. We introduce GraphCast--Mamba, which augments a frozen, pretrained $1^\circ$ GraphCast backbone with a trainable Mamba correction branch combining graph message passing and Mamba layers. The branch retains a temporal memory state across successive six-hour forecast steps, learning corrections informed by temporal context beyond GraphCast's two-frame input. Training is confined to the correction branch, using ERA5 data from 2015--2021. After 2,500 optimizer u

title: TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings
abstract: Real-world tables are often heterogeneous, combining numerical features with free-form string columns. Table foundation models (TFMs) excel on numerical tables but require strings to be encoded numerically, while large language models (LLMs) hold semantic knowledge but are not designed for tabular predictions. Most existing bridges use LLMs as plug-in encoders for cell strings, yet how to extract representations effectively for tabular learning remains underexplored. We show that the interface between LLMs and tables matter as much as the LLM itself. Applied cell-wise, larger LLMs do not give
institutions: Systems, Applications & Products in Data Processing (Germany)

title: DynaFilter: Cloud-driven Dynamic Filtering for Satellite Edge Intelligence
abstract: Modern satellite edge systems, including those performing remote sensing tasks such object detection and tracking, are characterized by severely limited bandwidth and intermittent connections, making continuous data transmission to the cloud impractical. Existing edge-cloud systems, however, either require heavy pre-processing before analysis, for instance, full decompression of imagery data, or transmit all compressed data regardless of relevance. To address these challenges, we design DynaFilter, a dynamic filtering technique that enables satellite edge devices to perform selective region-of

title: Spatio-temporal precipitation downscaling at hourly resolution based on km-scale regional simulations
abstract: Effectively preparing for changes in extreme flooding requires understanding present and future rainfall extremes with return periods up to $\sim$100-1000 years, including changes in intensity, spatial structure at km-scale and sub-daily temporal variability. Conventional km-scale climate models give greatly increased realism compared to typical global climate models (GCMs) but are too computationally costly to allow enough simulations for robustly quantifying changes in extremes. This work presents an approach based on video diffusion to generate realistic precipitation at 8.8km-hourly resolu

title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) combined with reinforcement learning (RL) can support adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making by comparing expected and observed network behavior. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network. For each action, the same channel simulator is evaluated under an attack-free and an attacked configuration. Receiver-level residuals are combined with spatial jamming footprints and accumulated to form a normalized suspicion vecto

title: FTFM: Factorized Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are becoming a powerful alternative to conventional tabular learning, adapting to new datasets in context without task-specific training. Current architectures, however, face a trade-off: models that preserve cell-level representations are expensive because they repeatedly attend across rows and columns, while faster models collapse each row into a fixed embedding and lose this fine-grained state. We introduce Factorized Tabular Foundation Models (FTFM), which preserve cell representations while factorizing their computation through one contextual latent per ro

title: Tricking Synthetic Image Detectors with Amortized Generative Attacks
abstract: Rapid advances in image synthesis have increased the need for reliable synthetic-image detectors, yet their robustness to transferable attacks remains incomplete and understudied. Existing evaluations generally examine whether an attack constructed against one detector transfers to another, but rarely isolate how its effectiveness changes when the attacked images originate from different generators. institutions: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

title: Every minute counts: Wind farm power control during imbalance settlement using distributional soft actor-critic
abstract: Wind farms can provide flexibility by curtailing their output during periods of excess generation in the power grid. This can be done through implicit balancing, where the power setpoints of the farm are adapted to anticipate the imbalance price. By doing so, the wind farm helps reduce the resulting system imbalance while also lowering its own costs. However, implicit balancing is challenging since the imbalance prices are unknown in advance and hard to predict. Furthermore, the control strategy of the wind farm can affect the imbalance price formation. To address both challenges, we develop a

title: Shortcut-Resistant CAM Distillation for Long-Tailed Recognition
abstract: Real-world datasets often follow a long-tailed distribution, making generalization to tail classes difficult. We revisit this problem through the lens of shortcut learning, where models prefer the easiest predictive cues (e.g., background or textures) over object-centric semantics, especially under scarce and biased supervision. We find that this tendency is amplified for tail classes: limited examples often share similar contexts, making non-semantic signals highly correlated and thus tempting shortcuts, whereas head classes with diverse appearances and environments encourage more stable obje
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: Are You Sure Your LLM Is Sure? Repairing and Auditing Confidence
abstract: Confidence scores determine whether an LLM answer is accepted, reviewed, or regenerated, yet scalar recalibration can only correct errors visible through the score itself. We introduce RADAR (Repair, Adopt, and Diagnose After Recalibration), a reliability framework that separates confidence repair from deciding whether to deploy the repair and auditing the errors that remain. Under squared loss, we decompose prediction risk into outcome noise, information hidden by the score, and mapping error; restricting repair to order-preserving maps additionally introduces a pooling gap. title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
abstract: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models
abstract: With the advancement in language modeling, research on adversarial images has recently shifted from image classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs). Despite the new, text-prompt-driven nature of VLMs, we find that existing VLM adversaries have largely overlooked the dynamics of text prompts. In a typical use case, adversarial images can protect visual privacy by rejecting VLMs from answering questions about the image. However, existing protections are prompt-agnostic, i.e., indiscriminately rejecting any question, including those for potential legitimate use of the image. To address this li

title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
abstract: Variable roles describe recurring behaviors such as accumulation, traversal, and retaining the best candidate encountered. We use Sajaniemi's independently defined taxonomy to study which role distinctions can be recovered from large language models, how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) retain those distinctions, and whether associated directions support control of generation. We introduce static annotation rules for all eleven roles and a corpus of 126,926 natural-code files across five languages. Across five model-SAE systems, residual probes outperform individual SAE features and tested lexical b
institutions: RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project

title: Integrated Novelty Detection Systems: From Sensor Networks to Multi-Novelty Computer Vision
abstract: Novelty detection is crucial in various technological and scientific domains. Its importance spans from ensuring the reliability of sensor networks to enhancing the adaptability of computer vision systems. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and complex, effective anomaly detection is essential for maintaining reliability and accuracy. This work addresses novelty detection in weather sensor networks and computer vision. In weather sensor networks, particularly for monitoring rainfall, detecting blocked rain gauges can significantly impact data reliability, food security, and disast

title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions
abstract: Foundation models for tables and relational databases are increasingly used for predictive tasks across various scientific and industrial domains. However, adapting existing models to unseen datasets requires tens of thousands of examples. Here we introduce RT-J, an 86M-parameter relational foundation model (RFM) that makes accurate predictions even with hundreds of in-context examples or fewer. To achieve this, we first assemble the Join, a large collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks. We pretrain with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells, us

title: SurvICL: a Foundation Model for in-context Survival Analysis
abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) now outperform gradient-boosted trees in classification and regression. Yet in survival analysis, which predicts when an event occurs from censored data, often on small clinical cohorts, we find that no existing TFM beats the half-century-old Cox model. We address this issue by introducing SurvICL, a TFM that predicts survival curves in-context. SurvICL is pretrained on purely synthetic datasets generated from a novel flexible proportional-odds prior that outperforms other prior types in our ablation study. Unlike most other survival models, SurvICL is trained

title: MIRA: A Multimodal Illustrated Deep Research Agent for Controllable Reports
abstract: Deep research agents are increasingly capable of searching the open web and synthesizing evidence, yet they remain poorly suited to controllable report generation in multimodal deep research. This task requires agents to handle interleaved textual and visual inputs, gather multimodal evidence through multi-step web search, and deliver comprehensive illustrated reports under user-specified requirements. Existing systems face two limitations. During reasoning, they often underuse images discovered along the search trajectory; during generation, they tend to produce fixed-form answers with limite
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
abstract: Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small-v1.0, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. title: Statistical Downscaling of Daily Precipitation from ERA5 Atmospheric Fields to IMERG over West Africa
abstract: Global reanalyses are too coarse to resolve the convective systems that produce most West African monsoon rainfall. In this work, we use U-Net based architectures to downscale daily ERA5 fields (0.25°) to IMERG V07 satellite precipitation (0.1°) over West Africa for the June to October seasons of 2000 to 2024, using geopotential, temperature, humidity and wind at three pressure levels together with elevation and land fraction. institutions: Institut de Recherche pour le Développement

title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
abstract: Progressive neuronal loss is the hallmark of neurodegenerative disease, yet how loss of neurons shapes the pattern of cognitive decline remains poorly understood. Here we systematically ablate neurons (computational units) in language models spanning recurrent long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer architectures and apply limited fine-tuning as a simple proxy for compensatory plasticity. With whole-unit ablation, LSTMs degrade gradually with syntactic and semantic faculties declining in parallel across mild-to-moderate damage. title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
abstract: Despite recent advances, current AI systems remain highly susceptible to domain shifts, particularly in biomedical imaging, where images are usually acquired under substantially different experimental conditions. Although recent domain adaptation methods have made substantial progress, significant performance gaps under domain shift persist. To measure progress in this regard, we introduce BatchBench, a leaderboard that evaluates and compares the robustness of AI systems on biomedical images from unseen experimental batches and data sources. BatchBench is built on JUMP-CP, one of the largest p

title: Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Self-supervised joint embedding learning aligns representations of augmented views while regularizing their distribution to prevent collapse. Regularization aims to shape the overall representation distribution, but most joint embedding methods restrict its computation to the active minibatch. We propose out-of-batch regularization, which maintains a dataset-level state in CPU memory and uses globally constructed per-instance targets during minibatch training. Evaluated on natural images and biomedical datasets, these anchors approximate the full-dataset regularization gradient more faithfully

title: Bio-Inspired Magnetic Navigation Using Gradient Descent With Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filtering
abstract: Navigation in GPS-denied environments is commonly based on magnetic maps, which are used to correct trajectory drift and enable relocalization. However, such navigation systems suffer from a strong dependence on magnetic maps that are complex, heavy, and costly to construct. Bio-inspired magnetic navigation (BIMN) does not rely on magnetic maps, making it simpler and more frugal. In this paper, we present a gradient descent BIMN method based on the Rao-Blackwellized particle filter (RBPF) for local gradient estimation. We show that magnetic navigation can be performed without magnetic maps, as

title: Cross-Prompt Inference Mitigates Rare-Class Suppression in Imbalanced VLM Finetuning
abstract: When a vision-language model is finetuned on class-imbalanced data, rare-class recall can fall well below the model's own zero-shot performance. In this regime, we uncover a surprising matched-prompt penalty whereby the standard choice of reusing the descriptive finetuning prompt at inference can yield lower rare-class recall than using a different descriptive prompt. We call this inference-time strategy cross-prompt inference. title: Clarity-Driven Adaptive Mission Planning for a Solar-Powered Autonomous Surface Vessel
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive methodology, backed by simulation and experimental results, for an adaptive mission planning strategy that is mathematically grounded in the maximization of the information-driven quantity of clarity. In particular, the methodology introduced in this work addresses the use of sustainably powered autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) to perform scientific missions that prioritize locations of maximum interest. Because these locations of maximum interest are not known a priori but are rather identified based on in-situ measurements, online adaptation is essential

title: Inductive Learning of Concept Embeddings from Cross-Linguistic Colexification Patterns with Textual Attributes
abstract: The advent of distributional semantics as a framework for computational semantics marked a paradigm shift in the nature of representations, by which meanings are represented as dense vectors commonly known as word embeddings. Computational approaches to historical or typological language comparison, on the other hand, still mostly rely on discrete representations, while the potential of embedding-based methods remains largely untapped in this context. title: Can AI Forecast the Extremes? Evaluating Probabilistic Weather Models on Tropical Cyclones
abstract: Weather prediction is undergoing an important shift, with data-driven AI models outperforming leading numerical weather prediction systems on average at a fraction of the computational cost. Yet, whether this success extends to extreme events remains contested. Earlier evaluations have exposed important shortcomings, but have largely focused on deterministic models and metrics, leaving the capabilities of the latest probabilistic models less understood. title: RegCL: Compact Continual SAM Adaptation for Visual Grounding in Multi-Sensorial Media
abstract: Multi-sensorial media systems, including AR/VR, remote operation, and embodied AI, require visual grounding modules that remain reliable as sensing environments and application domains evolve. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides a strong foundation for dense visual segmentation, but its performance degrades on specialized and dynamically arriving domains such as medical imagery, camouflaged scenes, and shadow-dominant environments. Existing continual learning methods often rely on replay data or growing domain-specific modules, limiting compact deployment in evolving media pipelines. To

title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures
abstract: Exposure indices that map technical capabilities onto occupational abilities have become a standard tool for anticipating how AI may reshape work, but existing measures either cover software AI or proxy robotics through patents and installation data that reflect the industrial robots of past decades. We construct the first abilities-based exposure measures for robotics and physical AI, and the first to span occupations, industries, and geographies. Following the framework of Felten et al. (2018, 2021), we build a robotics capability taxonomy of 16 capabilities in eight domains from 78 academic

title: Watts If? A Benchmark for Counterfactual Reasoning About the AI Data Center Buildout
abstract: An AI data center is committed years before it draws a watt: a few discrete choices (grid or on-site gas, evaporative or dry cooling, which county to file in) fix its capital, water draw, and carbon path, and LLMs are now asked to help screen them with no test of whether they track what each commitment rules out. We introduce DCBench-440, with two arms reported separately: 200 generative questions over STRIPS worlds for five US deal archetypes, with search-verified gold answers and no tested shortcut above 12% on any question type, and 240 multiple-choice questions grounded in quoted site reco

title: First Passage Attention
abstract: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. title: Towards Consistent Geospatial Representations: Aligning One Encoder to Many Foundation Models
abstract: Geospatial foundation models (GFMs) differ widely in pretraining objective, modality and resolution, and none leads across benchmarks. We ask whether their representations are complementary, and whether a single encoder can inherit that complementarity. We introduce Pangaea-Latents, an extension of the Pangaea benchmark providing frozen embeddings of $5$ GFMs over its $11$ datasets, along with reproduced baselines, and find GFM embeddings to be neither redundant nor disjoint. title: Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight
abstract: When every rollout for a problem fails, GRPO receives neither a successful exemplar nor a nonzero group-relative advantage, so it learns nothing from exactly the problems it most needs to learn. The failed reasoning can nevertheless suggest what to try next. We present Replay-Selected Hindsight Distillation (RSHD), which turns failed attempts into an additional, tested source of supervision during GRPO training. title: TimeRSI: Towards Self-Improved Agentic Deployment for Time-Series Foundation Models
abstract: Time-series foundation models provide strong zero-shot forecast, but deployment for real-world applications still requires task-specific designs for model inputs and outputs. Direct inference can leave domain knowledge and recurring forecast errors unaddressed, while tailored pipelines require substantial human expertise and effort. We introduce TimeRSI, a self-improving agentic deployment system around frozen forecasting models. A coding agent translates task descriptions into executable pipeline changes. It tests each revision on historical forecasting windows and uses observed errors to gui

title: CAST: Cast-Admissible Generative Design and Shape Optimization with Paired Depth Images
abstract: Deep generative design can produce complex geometries, but unconstrained representations may create undercuts that prevent release from a two-part mold. We present CAST, which reformulates three-dimensional shape generation under a selected mold-opening constraint as a two-dimensional image generation problem using paired top and bottom depth images. title: Learning angles for quantum approximate optimization
abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its variants are leading algorithms to help solve challenging combinatorial optimization problems. QAOA maps these problems to Ising Hamiltonians such that their ground state is the desired solution. Candidate solutions are then drawn from a variational quantum circuit. The performance of QAOA hinges on a set of variational angles. However, finding good angles is an instance-specific and computationally expensive non-convex classical optimization task. Here, we learn the mapping from the problem instance to high-quality QAOA angles. Our

title: Learning smooth dynamics via Kinematic Interpolants
abstract: Inferring dynamics from real-world experimental data is inherently ambiguous, as many plausible dynamical systems can explain the same positional observations at measurement times. For higher fidelity modeling of applications ranging from single-cell RNA to vortex dynamics and even flocking of birds, scientific observables increasingly also include velocity estimates that serve to resolve this issue. However, incorporating this rich information in a scalable manner, free of simulation or unnecessary approximations, has remained a difficult challenge. In this paper, we introduce Kinematic Inter

title: MELD: Recursive Self-Improvement via Hierarchical Coordination for Multi-Agent Scientific Discovery
abstract: Multi-agent scientific discovery with large language models raises a coupled learning problem: research assignments determine both which experiments are pursued and the experiences from which agents adapt. We introduce MELD, a unified hierarchical test-time training framework that jointly adapts a team-level Coordinator policy and agent-level individual Scientist policies within a single discovery process. title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the backbone of many state-of-the-art multimodal systems, but often encode spurious and harmful associations from their training data. While prior work focuses on removing known biases from VLMs, methods for discovering unanticipated associations for retrieval tasks remain underexplored. We introduce SPELUNKA, an automated, inference-time framework for finding unanticipated distributional biases for retrieval tasks in VLMs without pre-specified labeled subgroups, inference-time human supervision, or model fine-tuning. title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system
abstract: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\barω_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. title: Learning $ω$-Powered Conditional Distributions with Importance-Weighted Flow Matching
abstract: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) with guidance scale $γ$ is commonly motivated by the $ω$-powered conditional distribution obtained by setting $ω=γ$, but CFG does not, in general, sample from this distribution exactly. We study whether the powered target can instead be learned explicitly. We introduce Importance-Weighted Conditional Flow Matching (IW-CFM), which reweights conditional flow-matching examples using density ratios obtained from frozen conditional and unconditional flow models. title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
abstract: Despite their extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks. We study how to amortize sequential Bayesian experimental design (BED) into an LLM by explicitly training the reasoning that guides action selection using information-gain rewards. Our approach specifies the experimental generative model independently of the LLM's own beliefs, allowing us to optimize expected information gain under a model of our choosing. title: Agentic Communication Networks: When Agents Become Network Entities
abstract: Autonomous agents are moving from application-layer components to active participants in networked systems. They not only generate traffic but also perceive context, express intent, invoke services, coordinate with other agents, and act under task, policy, and resource constraints. This evolution exposes a mismatch between emerging agentic interactions and conventional endpoint- and traffic-centric network abstractions. title: MUSEBENCH: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Music Detection and Artifact Analysis
abstract: Advances in generative AI have made it possible to produce music that is nearly indistinguishable from human compositions, raising the question of whether such works can be reliably distinguished from human compositions. We present MUSEBENCH, a large-scale benchmark for AI-generated music detection and artifact analysis, comprising over 361K tracks. title: Interpretable Graph Partitioning for Spatial Prediction
abstract: Spatial prediction estimates unobserved values from spatially distributed observations. Although flexible predictive models are increasingly available, their practical use remains limited when interpretability is essential. In this study, we formulate a graph partitioning problem to construct a global surrogate model that approximates black-box predictions with simpler representations. Specifically, we select connected subgraphs to minimize within-cluster residuals in vertex-level predictions. title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
abstract: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. We formalize a feedback-driven process in which accepted revisions persist across runs. The framework separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms. It distinguishes changes to interpreted state from revisions to tools and code, repository-level control logic, and plugin composition. title: Physics-Constrained Modeling and Inference of the Equation of State for Dissociative Materials
abstract: Equations of state (EOSs) describe how a material's internal energy and pressure change with temperature and density. They are inputs to hydrodynamic simulations in materials science and planetary science. We model the ion-thermal free-energy term for dissociative materials, where molecular bonds break apart to form new species under extreme conditions. title: Solvent Fluctuations Enable Photoionization of Aqueous Nitrite Microdroplets
abstract: Nitrite photochemistry in atmospheric aerosols and natural waters is a major source of hydroxyl radicals and reactive nitrogen oxides. Contrary to the prevailing view that in the environment aqueous nitrite photochemistry proceeds exclusively through photoexcitation followed by homolytic bond cleavage, we show that visible light directly ionizes aqueous nitrite in individual micron-sized droplets. title: Brittle by Design? Multi-Scenario Reinforcement Learning for Robust Mission Coordination in Systems of Systems
abstract: As systems engineering (SE) shifts from monolithic systems to Systems of Systems, Mission Engineering (ME) has emerged as a new line of thinking in SE. Mission environments are uncertain and dynamic, and outcomes depend on how mission assets interact with them, rendering static architectures brittle and calling for flexible yet analytically rigorous ME approaches. We propose an intelligent mission coordination methodology integrating high-fidelity digital mission models with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for adaptive task allocation. title: Digital Twin-Conditioned RSS-Fingerprint Localization in Cell-Free Millimeter-Wave Networks
abstract: Digital twins (DTs) can generate dense synthetic fingerprints for localization via ray tracing, yet the sim-to-real domain gap limits their direct use, particularly in cell-free millimeter-wave (mmWave) deployments where distributed geometries and blockage-induced sparsity widen the mismatch. We propose DT-conditioned (DTCond), a framework that fuses real and DT beam-domain fingerprints as complementary inputs through per-domain encoders, learnable per-access point (AP) attention, and calibrated uncertainty. title: From Weather to Enhanced Weathering: Weather Foundation Models for Carbon Dioxide Removal at Operational Scale
abstract: Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon removal solution with the potential to remove gigatons of CO$_2$ per year, but quantifying that removal today requires dense soil sampling and laboratory analysis. We evaluate five weather Foundation Models (FMs) as frozen encoders feeding lightweight decoders, under a leave-one-field-out protocol on 5,192 chronosequences from 264 fields across Brazil and the US. title: UtoMe: Observation-Uncertainty-Guided Token Merging for Weather Foundation Models
abstract: Weather transformers process dense reanalysis fields whose reliability varies across variables, locations, and weather regimes. Token merging can reduce computation, but feature similarity alone does not account for this heterogeneous input uncertainty. We introduce UtoMe, an observation-uncertainty-guided token merging framework that combines dynamics saliency with ensemble data assimilation spread as a relative input-reliability proxy. title: RTISSLAM: In-air Imaging Sonar SLAM using a Robust Pose Graph and Occupancy Grid Mapping
abstract: Sonar was one of the first sensors with which mobile robots built maps, and in-air sonar keeps working where cameras and lidar fail, in darkness, smoke, dust and next to glass. Classical sonar SLAM, however, relied on geometric features or occupancy grids built from sparse range readings, and both struggle with the specular reflections that dominate indoor sonar. In this letter, we introduce RTISSLAM, a novel sonar-only SLAM system for an embedded 3D imaging sonar, which combines the robust pose graph of BatSLAM 2.0 as back-end with an occupancy grid as map. title: Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment
abstract: Multimodal entity alignment (MMEA) is fundamental to integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs), yet existing paradigms remain critically vulnerable to incomplete modalities and cross-graph structural asymmetries. This paper exposes a fundamental oversight in current MMEA research: treating feature missingness and topological discrepancies as isolated preprocessing or denoising challenges, which overlooks their destructive coupling during multimodal fusion. title: TabMosaic: Unified In-Context Diffusion for Tabular Generative Tasks
abstract: Generative modeling for tabular data has advanced to the point where models can synthesize realistic records, recover missing values, and generate samples conditioned on class labels or observed attributes. Despite recent advances, existing approaches either require table-specific training or restrict in-context learning to single-cell prediction. In this work, we formulate these tabular generative tasks as a single problem: modeling the joint conditional distribution of an arbitrary set of target cells given the observed cells of an unseen table. title: Identification of effective transport physics and optimal feedback control: Experimental demonstration on a 1600-fan wind generator
abstract: Distributed-input distributed-output (DIDO) systems arise in numerous engineering applications where large numbers of actuators generate spatially distributed physical fields that are monitored by distributed sensors. Developing physically interpretable models that enable real-time optimal control of these systems remains challenging because of the high dimensionality and strong spatial coupling between inputs and outputs. title: Calibrated Typed Decisions for Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction
abstract: Information extraction models often perform well on the datasets they are trained on, but transferring to new domains and annotation guidelines remains challenging. Supporting user-specified types alone does not resolve this problem. We present CalOn, a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction across datasets and schemas. The model jointly encodes text and type definitions, then directly identifies entity spans, relations between spans, and event triggers and arguments. title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control, so the regions and seasons that cloud cover hits hardest end up under-sampled. title: One-shot Human Video-Guided Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have recently achieved remarkable progress by leveraging large-scale robot datasets and foundation models for general-purpose robot manipulation. However, their ability to rapidly adapt to novel manipulation tasks beyond the training distribution remains limited. Existing approaches often require task-specific robot demonstrations and additional training, which are labor- and compute-intensive, limiting the scalability of VLA adaptation to open-world scenarios. title: GLST: Global-Local Spatio-Temporal Memory Decomposition Framework for Online Chained-Goal Navigation
abstract: Autonomous navigation in real-world environments often requires long-horizon operation under partial observability and evolving goals. Existing mapless navigation approaches predominantly assume fixed goals throughout an episode, limiting applicability to practical scenarios where goals change online during execution. We study online chained-goal navigation, where goals evolve through existing-goal redirection or new-goal emergence without explicit transition signals. title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Multimodal LLMs are typically trained by first aligning a vision encoder with a language model via projector training on large image-caption datasets, followed by joint training of the full multimodal model. Despite its widespread use, the role of the projector training stage remains poorly understood. We find that (i) using only $10$ to $20\%$ of the data for training the projector already recovers most downstream performance gains, and (ii) projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated while largely preserving performance. title: From Prompts to Posteriors: Can LLM Agents Perform Bayesian Inference in Context?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied across the scientific discovery pipeline, from synthesizing literature to generating hypotheses to informing experimental design. A unifying principle behind these tasks is the need to continuously update beliefs as evidence accumulates, for which Bayesian inference provides a natural framework. However, existing work assumes that LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating in context, instead relying on simplifications and heuristics.
