abstract: Contactless vital-sign monitoring can improve comfort and hygiene in long-term, sleep, home, and clinical monitoring, but robust estimation of heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), and oxygen saturation (SpO2) remains a coupled sensing and algorithmic problem. Narrative approaches have therefore gained relevance, as they promote self-reflection, identity construction, and exploration of possible futures. This paper examines two school-based narrative guidance pathways designed by the University of Turin: a photovoice-inspired pathway and a rap music pathway. abstract: Abstract Statistical model checking (SMC) analyses stochastic models by simulation: it samples many runs, evaluates the property of interest on each of them, and returns an estimate together with a statistical guarantee. abstract: Marine propulsion shafting operates under complex, variable conditions, where stern bearing wear and pedestal settlement redistribute loads, migrate vibration energy, and distort the shaft orbit, threatening safe operation. To address insufficient fault samples, difficulty in measuring degradation states directly, and limited interpretability of purely data-driven models, we propose a multilayer perceptron (MLP) condition assessment method driven by measured and digital twin data fusion. A digital twin framework comprising geometric, physical, rule-based, and behavioral models was constructed.

abstract: Abstract Reconstructing past climates is challenging because pre‐instrumental observations are geographically sparse and proxy records are noisy; data assimilation offers one approach to address these limitations. Although such reconstructions are now widespread, the extent to which different proxy archives determine their accuracy remains unclear. abstract: Abstract Antarctic sea ice has declined since 2015, but placing this trend in a longer‐term context remains challenging. Ice core methanesulfonic acid (MSA) offers a potential record of sea ice variability beyond the instrumental period, yet its applicability in sectors including the Weddell Sea remains unclear. abstract: This study presents for the first time the integration of the low-cost REMO Ocean Data Assimilation System (RODAS) into the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) for assimilating Sea Surface Temperature (SST) observations. RODAS is an Ensemble Optimal Interpolation (EnOI)-based data assimilation system originally developed for use with the HYCOM model. title: Compound marine heatwaves and atmospheric boundary layer jets drive enhanced coastal precipitation
abstract: Heavy coastal precipitation is traditionally attributed to atmospheric dynamics, but the influence of co-occurring oceanic thermal extremes remains largely unexplored. Using satellite observations and reanalysis data from 1998 to 2023 over the South China Sea (SCS), we investigate the synergistic impacts of marine heatwaves (MHWs) and atmospheric boundary layer jets (BLJs). abstract: Abstract Previous studies have documented long-term changes in Antarctic sea ice extent and its interannual variability. Using satellite-derived SIC observations for 1979–2024 and a wavelet-based measure of interannual variance, we investigate changes in wintertime (July–September) SIC variability across the Southern Ocean. abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH 4 ) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the diachronic development of the Ancient Greek suffix - eu - from a nominal marker into a verbalizer, focusing on the transition of - euō verbs from stative to activity/eventive meanings. abstract: Coral reefs are one of the most biologically diverse ecosystems in the ocean, but are now under increasing threat from climate related ocean warming. While numerous studies have focused on the impact of sea surface temperature (SST) on coral reef condition, those that specifically looked into whether long-term background SST variability had an impact on reef stability have had conflicting results, with some analyses showing negligible association and others showing significant associations. abstract: The ambition to model the Earth at a 1:1 scale through planetary computing presents a challenge that transcends technical constraints. This article analyzes Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 not merely as a commercial product, but as a critical exponent of the Earth-as-interface paradigm, sustained by a distributed infrastructure of massive geospatial data and cloud computing. abstract: Abstract. The vertical distribution of distinct aerosol components fundamentally governs atmospheric shortwave heating rates and radiative effects. abstract: The development of approaches that can autonomously fill and heal material voids and yield composites with tailorable properties is increasingly relevant in engineering. abstract: In marine organisms with complex life cycles, the planktonic larval stage is among the most sensitive to environmental variation, affecting dispersal potential in early life. abstract: Abstract Traditional sound-absorbing materials face a trade-off between structural thickness and pressure resistance imposed by the mass law. abstract: Abstract Winter sea surface temperature (SST) in the South China Sea is a precursor of North China hydroclimate, but the relationship’s long-term stability remains uncertain. abstract: Abstract Calco-carbonic reactive transport controls the dissolution of limestone by carbonic acid, a key process shaping the hydraulic and geochemical evolution of carbonate aquifers. abstract: Tropical cyclone genesis (TCG) in the Northwest Pacific is strongly influenced by the interaction of large-scale oceanic and atmospheric environmental fields. This study investigates the spatiotemporal characteristics of TCG from 1991 to 2020 and examines the modulation mechanisms of major environmental factors. Tropical cyclone records from the China Meteorological Administration best-track dataset are combined with NOAA ERSST.v5 sea-surface temperature data and ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis fields. abstract: Numerical models provide essential tools for evaluating dynamics and responses of aquatic resources under different management actions and environmental conditions. With a global decline in oyster reefs, the development of mechanistic oyster reef models can support their management and restoration. title: Recent change in northward migration of the East Asian summer front and increased compound wet–hot conditions
abstract: The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. Using a front-tracking algorithm applied to ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2025), we identify northward migration of the EASF during both the active frontal season and late summer, with a more robust 1.92° shift in late summer. abstract: Abstract The Consortium for the Advancement of Marine Arctic Science (CAMAS) has been created in response to the need for improved capabilities in Earth system modeling, specifically focused on the Arctic marine system. abstract: Abstract Tropical teleconnection associated with El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is widely recognized for regulating multiple physical processes in the Southern Ocean. However, despite its influence on Southern Ocean wind patterns, the response of surface flow has received little attention. abstract: Metocean analyses are fundamental to offshore and coastal engineering, maritime operations, and renewable energy development, where reliable estimates of winds, waves, currents, sea level, and related variables are required for structural design, safety assessment, and operational planning. abstract: The European Macaronesian region (Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands) represents a key biogeographic transition zone in the Northeast Atlantic. While its large-scale gradients are well recognized, the extent to which long-term variability and vertical structure shape ecosystem dynamics remains poorly quantified. Here, we synthesize nearly three decades of satellite and reanalysis data (1993–2025) to resolve the seasonal, interannual, and vertical variability of physical (sea temperature, currents) and biological (chlorophyll a , phytoplankton, zooplankton, micronekton) variables. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric mineral dust and black carbon (BC) aerosols play important roles in the Earth's climate system, yet direct observations over the Southern Ocean (SO) are scarce. In this study, we present the characteristics of airborne water‐insoluble particles (WIPs) collected during a cruise of the R/V Shirase in the Australian and Indian sectors of the SO from December 2022 to March 2023. abstract: Abstract Coral populations on inshore reefs of the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) face increasing pressures from environmental stressors. Genetic diversity and connectivity are key determinants of coral adaptive capacity. Acropora kenti forms at least four genetically distinct clusters distributed across hundreds of kilometres along the GBR. abstract: The relationship between the wolf and the wild reindeer in the Arctic has always been a focal point for researchers and northern Indigenous communities. abstract: Abstract Climate monitoring is essential for agricultural planning and environmental management, especially in regions with a low density of meteorological stations, such as the state of Mato Grosso, Brazil. In this context, atmospheric reanalysis products, such as ERA5-Land, have emerged as alternatives to fill observational gaps. abstract: Abstract Voluntary Observing Ship (VOS) wind reports constitute one of the densest marine in situ datasets, yet they carry a persistent, wind-speed-dependent negative bias that intensifies at low wind speeds. abstract: Abstract Offshore Freshened Groundwater (OFG) reservoirs are regarded as a potentially significant resource stored in continental shelves. While the role of subsurface geological conditions in controlling OFG has been widely recognized, the influence of the topography of the hosting continental shelf on OFG evolution remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies, prevalent across the global ocean, play a crucial role in the transport and mixing of climate‐sensitive tracers such as heat, salt, and nutrients. abstract: As a critical energy-saving component in reverse osmosis desalination systems, turbine-type energy recovery devices require rigorous dynamic stability evaluation. abstract: Abstract Extreme sea levels (ESLs) threaten coastal zones, and global assessments suggest that future ESLs grow with rising mean sea level (MSL) as the main driver. abstract: The Tolo Thrust, located in eastern Indonesia, is a potentially tsunamigenic structure capable of generating destructive tsunamis that threaten coastal communities surrounding Tolo Bay. abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. title: Ship fuel consumption prediction and speed optimization under weather forecast uncertainty using ensemble forecasts
abstract: Optimizing vessel speed is an effective method for reducing fuel consumption and emissions in shipping, and an accurate prediction of fuel consumption is essential for generating effective speed strategies. However, due to the complexity of ocean-atmosphere interactions and the uncertainty of weather phenomena, weather and sea condition forecast data can contain errors, which affects fuel consumption prediction accuracy. abstract: Abstract. The Pine Island Ice Shelf can be analysed within three distinct sectors: northern, southern, and central. abstract: Abstract Shallow circulations in the tropics are related to the sea surface temperature distribution, longwave cooling above the boundary layer, and shallow convection in both observations and models. To understand the influences sea surface temperature has on the shallow circulation strength, fixed sea surface temperature distributions are applied in experiments using an idealized general circulation model with uniform insolation and no rotation. abstract: This study presents a site-specific seismic-source probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment for Manzanillo, Colima, a coastal city in Mexico vulnerable to local tsunamis due to its proximity to the subduction zone along the Mesoamerican Trench. Historical records show that the region has been affected by significant tsunamis, most notably in 1932 and 1995. title: Meteorological Impact Assessment Software for Maritime Transport in the Western Part of the Black Sea
abstract: Maritime transportation in the western part of the Black Sea is strongly affected by meteorological conditions such as wind, waves, and visibility. This paper presents a software system designed to evaluate and predict these impacts using real-time and historical data. abstract: The Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ) is the focal region for imminent deep-sea nodule mining, with over 1.1 million square kilometres already under exploration licence. Although the International Seabed Authority has designated Areas of Particular Environmental Interest (APEIs) to protect regional biodiversity from mining impacts, there has been no formal assessment of whether this network functions as a coherent connected system. abstract: Abstract. Supraglacial channel networks (SCNs) represent critical components of the surface drainage system on Antarctic ice shelves, facilitating the redistribution of meltwater, including into and out of supraglacial lakes, potentially influencing ice-shelf stability. However, the seasonal and interannual variability in their spatial extent, structural evolution, and climatic sensitivity remain poorly quantified, particularly compared to observations of supraglacial lakes. abstract: This paper presents a preliminary census of artificial cavities within the municipal territory of Sutri (Latium, Italy). The census, based on a review of historical sources and technical documentation, combined with direct field observations, led to the identification and mapping of more than 120 cavities. title: Methods and Results of the Analysis of the Spatial Structure of the Siberian High
abstract: A methodology has been developed for quantitative assessment of the spatial structure of the Siberian High (SH) based on calculating the center of gravity of the positive sea level pressure anomaly field. On its basis and using ERA5 data, the position of the SH center of gravity, the radius of inertia (a measure of compactness), and the total intensity were calculated for the period of 1950–2025. title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract: Abstract. Cloud vertical structure plays a central role in regulating Earth’s radiation balance and hydrological cycle, yet it remains poorly represented in weather and climate models due to limited high-resolution observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band cloud radars, we provide the first high-spatiotemporal-resolution characterization of cloud vertical structure across China for 2024 and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. abstract: The northern coast of Senegal, located on the western edge of the Sahel, is characterized by high climate variability, the repercussions of which directly affect the region's socio-economic activities, particularly market gardening in the Niayes area. This study aims to analyze the variability of rainfall and temperatures at the Thies, Louga, and Saint-Louis weather stations over the period 1994-2024, through the study of temporal trends, interannual anomalies, and breaks in the climate series. title: On predictability of slip, rupture geometry, and speed of the 2025 M7.8 Mandalay, Myanmar, earthquake
abstract: Abstract The 2025 M 7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. title: Numerical Investigations of the Thermofluid Performance of a Solar Collector Tube used in Maritime Applications
abstract: The increasing demand for reducing fuel consumption and improving energy efficiency in maritime industry has intensified interest in solar thermal systems for auxiliary energy supply. In this study, a numerical model of a solar collector tube is developed in COMSOL Multiphysics. The main objective of this paper is to evaluate the thermal performance of a solar collector tube from the thermofluid behavior perspective. title: Bio-inspired trailing edge optimization for a double-suction pump impeller: a hybrid NSGA-II and CFD approach
abstract: Energy consumption reduction in pump systems has attracted increasing attention. Improving the efficiency of double-suction pumps can contribute to reducing energy consumption due to their extensive applications. This paper aims to optimize the double-suction pump by introducing the bionic structure inspired by the pectoral fin structure of humpback whales. In particular, this paper targeted the design improvement of the trailing edge of the double-suction pump impeller based on the tubercle structure on the pectoral fin. title: Atmospheric pressure, temperature, and online search activity for epilepsy: A daily time‐series study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Meteorological conditions have been investigated as potential short-term correlates of epileptic seizures, but findings remain inconsistent. title: Contrasting distribution and biomass trends of two sympatric redfish (Sebastes) species off Southeast Greenland
abstract: Sustainable harvest of fish stocks requires regular monitoring of abundance and biomass in space and time. In Southeast Greenland, two Sebastes species, beaked redfish ( Sebastes mentella ) and golden redfish ( S. norvegicus ), coexist and have been harvested together. However, the species differ greatly in stock status as beaked redfish are depleted, while golden redfish have a surplus of exploitable biomass. title: Structural integrity and ultimate strength of tubular joints in naval architecture
abstract: Tubular joints are fundamental components in the design of offshore platforms, naval vessels, and marine superstructures, offering high strength-to-weight ratios and favourable hydrodynamic behaviour. Because their welded intersections concentrate multiaxial loads, they are among the most vulnerable regions of any marine tubular framework. abstract: Abstract. Forecast busts – episodes of abnormally low forecast skill – remain a persistent challenge for numerical weather prediction despite steady improvements in forecasting skill. Previous studies have highlighted the roles of moist mesoscale processes and diabatically generated potential vorticity (PV) anomalies in triggering rapid error growth and downstream circulation misrepresentation, processes whose representation is highly sensitive to model grid spacing. abstract: ABSTRACT Ultra‐thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites (µt‐TBDC) are emerging as a transformative alternative to conventional continuous‐fiber composites, offering the potential to overcome longstanding limitations in manufacturability, waste, and design flexibility. abstract: Abstract A waterspout was observed on 5 March 2024 over the ocean near Okinawa, Japan, south of the center of an extratropical cyclone. Doppler radar observations revealed a mesocyclone above the waterspout, suggesting that the mesocyclone was responsible for the waterspout formation. abstract: Metro stations, characterized by enclosed spatial configurations, are highly vulnerable to extreme flooding, posing severe threats to human life and property. Understanding the hydrodynamic processes of flood intrusion and their implications for evacuation routes is therefore essential for urban flood risk reduction. title: Stratosphere–troposphere exchange and surface ozone pollution over tropical regions: a case study of Rossby wave breaking and tropopause folding
abstract: Abstract. Stratosphere-troposphere exchange (STE) is a key process by which ozone-rich stratospheric air enters the troposphere, influencing surface air quality. This study analyses an atypical STE event over North America between 6 and 14 March 2016, coinciding with a Phase I ozone contingency in Mexico City. abstract: Abstract. High-elevation alpine catchments are particularly affected by the global rise in temperature. Understanding the drivers of climate-induced changes in the hydrological response of these catchments in the past is relevant for developing future adaptation strategies for water resources and risk management. However, the study of long-term changes since the last Little Ice Age (around 1850) is strongly limited by the availability of hydrometeorological observation data. abstract: Abstract We investigate the seasonal variability of atmospheric infrasound and its contribution to Newtonian noise (NN) at the Sos Enattos site, a leading candidate location for the Einstein Telescope (ET). abstract: The heterogeneity in optically active nanomaterials often hinders efforts to understand their basic photophysics and can limit their use in practical applications. abstract: Ocean wave energy has garnered significant attention as a sustainable power source, with the Oscillating Water Column (OWC) device emerging as a highly effective technology for wave-to-electricity conversion. Within this system, the Wells turbine serves as a critical component for energy extraction. abstract: Indonesia, as a tropical maritime continent, exhibits a seasonal rainfall pattern influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). abstract: Abstract Wetting-induced collapse of loess can trigger significant negative skin friction (NSF) along pile shafts, leading to adverse effects on pile load transfer and bearing performance. title: Improved Feed Additives and Grazing Management are Likely Suboptimal Strategies for Reducing the Carbon Costs of Beef
abstract: I analyze research thrusts meant to reduce the carbon costs of the most resource intensive food item, beef. Using numerical modeling and data, I analyze the two most vigorously promoted ideas: Improving feed additives for reducing methane emissions, and enhancing soil carbon sequestration via better managed grazing. abstract: Abstract We investigate the spatiotemporal dynamics of aerosol pollution in the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP) and the North China Plain (NCP), two of the world’s most populated regions, against their anthropogenic emissions. Utilizing CAMS EAC4 reanalysis, CAMS-GLOB-ANT emission inventories, and ERA5 meteorological data for the year 2019, we analyze the seasonally changing relationship between PM-forming emissions and ambient PM 2.5 concentrations. abstract: The evolution of the Yangtze River is key to deciphering tectonic-climate-geomorphology coupling in East Asia, yet its integration age, whether Eocene, Miocene, or Quaternary, remains hotly contested. title: BEMT-based blade twist optimisation of a tiltrotor in hover using artificial bee colony algorithm
abstract: Abstract In this study, the aerodynamic effects of rotor blade twist geometry on the hover performance of the XV-15 tiltrotor were investigated. For this purpose, the twist distribution of the XV-15 tiltrotor was optimised under hover conditions using the artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm coupled with a Blade Element Momentum Theory (BEMT)-based numerical model validated against the NASA Ames experimental data. The blade twist was parameterised using a fifth-order continuous polynomial, whose coefficients were optimised to minimise the power coefficient while maintaining a constant thrust.

abstract: Abstract Pollen allergy is an increasing public health concern in Europe, as climate warming alters flowering phenology and airborne pollen dynamics. This study analysed temporal and spatial changes in pollen seasons in Estonia using aerobiological monitoring data from Tartu, Tallinn, and Pärnu. abstract: Volcanic ashfall has only recently been recognized as a destabilizing hazard for small craft, as evidenced by vessel capsizing during the 2011–2012 Cordón Caulle eruption in Argentine Patagonia. To solve the Stokes equations in geodynamics, we apply a preconditioned conjugate-gradient (PCG) method to the pressure Schur complement system. The algorithm is dominated by sparse matrix-vector products, vector inner products, vector updates, and repeated velocity subproblem solves, all of which map onto GPU architectures. title: HYDRODYNAMIC COEFFICIENTS AND NUMERICAL VERIFICATION OF A RECTANGULAR BARGE: A FREQUENCY-DOMAIN PANEL-METHOD STUDY
abstract: Rectangular barges are widely used for their high payload capacity and stability, but their bluff geometry creates complex hydrodynamic responses requiring accurate analysis for safe operation. In this study, Hydrodynamic Coefficients and Numerical Verification of a Rectangular Barge: A Frequency-Domain Panel-Method Study was carried out to determine the hydrodynamic behaviour of a 70.0 m × 30.0 m × 7.0 m rectangular barge with 5.0 m draft and 10,762.5 t displacement. title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
abstract: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.0) triggered major subaqueous delta collapses, generating massive tsunamis with maximum run-ups of ~50 m and ~13 m, respectively. title: Extreme Atmospheric Moistening and Drying Events at Ny‐Ålesund and Their Relation to Weather Systems
abstract: Abstract Understanding the role of water vapor in Arctic amplification requires a detailed evaluation of its spatio‐temporal variability. In this work, we use an integrated water vapor (IWV) data set from a ground‐based microwave radiometer at Ny‐Ålesund, Svalbard, covering 2012–2024, to characterize temporal IWV variability. We also identify extreme atmospheric moistening and drying events based on a new detection method and relate them to large‐scale circulation patterns and airmass pathways. title: An observational perspective on extreme precipitation indices over the mountainous regions of Northwest Himalaya
abstract: The Northwest Himalaya region is highly susceptible to extreme rainfall events due to its steep topography and complex climatic variability, which can trigger significant hydro-meteorological hazards, including heavy snowfall, hailstorms, floods, and droughts. The erratic precipitation patterns, both in the short and long term, exacerbate these hazards. title: Assessment of Human Thermal Stress Dynamics and Regional Drivers Across the Arabian Peninsula During 1990–2022 From Observations
abstract: ABSTRACT Human thermal stress is intensifying in the Arabian Peninsula (AP); however, a lack of consensus in observational evidence continues to limit a quantitative understanding of trends and the relative influence of the meteorological drivers underlying regional variability. title: Distinct pathways organize poleward-transported Arctic cyclones
abstract: Abstract Poleward-transported (PT) cyclones account for a substantial part of winter Arctic cyclone activity, but their routes into the Arctic have rarely been examined as a distinct aspect of cyclone variability. Using objectively identified winter cyclone tracks for 1979–2025, we find that PT cyclones preferentially follow four recurrent pathways rather than entering the Arctic randomly. title: Sub‐Seasonal Forecasting of Precipitation and Soil Moisture in CFSv2 Near Gulf Coast Tropical Cyclone Landfall Locations
abstract: Abstract Landfalling tropical cyclones (TCs) produce intense winds, heavy precipitation, and damaging storm surges along the Gulf and East coast of the U.S. There is growing evidence that high antecedent soil moisture (SM) conditions preceding landfall can maintain or even intensify TCs over land, sustaining strong winds and precipitation further inland. In this study, we investigate the ability of the 9‐month Climate Forecast System Version 2 (CFSv2) operational forecast to represent near surface SM at forecast lead times (LTs) from hours to weeks over the Gulf coast TC landfalling region. title: Iberulite fall and formation mechanism during a Sahara dust event in Switzerland in February 2021
abstract: Abstract. Sahara dust events can promote the formation of micrometer‑sized spherical mineral aggregates known as iberulites as they are usually found on the Iberian Peninsula. Iberulites have not, to our knowledge, been reported from Central Europe. Two formation mechanisms – in- and below scavenging – have been given. Strong iberulite fall (IFs) were observed in Western Switzerland in February 2021 when large amounts of dust were transported from the Moroccan-Algerian border towards Central Europe during a Saharan Dust Event (SDE). title: Resolution Dependence of the Climate Feedback Parameter in Km‐Scale Climate Models
abstract: Abstract Global storm‐resolving models (GSRMs) provide new opportunities to investigate the climate response to warming with explicitly resolved deep convection. title: Hydrodynamic Analysis of Aquaculture Net Cages Under Coupled Netting-Fish-Sediment Interactions
abstract: To address the limitations of existing studies that neglect sediment feedback and thus underestimate the complexity of the flow field, this study develops a three-dimensional hydrodynamic model for aquaculture cages that couples a porous-media representation of netting with a two-way discrete-phase model for sediment transport. title: Evaluating Statistical Downscaling Techniques for Regional Hydroclimatic Change Projections Over CONUS
abstract: Abstract Projecting the impacts of future climate change is critical for water managers planning infrastructure resilience strategies. Global earth system model output is generally too coarse to provide the detailed, localized information needed for impact assessment, and the computational cost of running higher‐resolution global simulations over sufficiently long periods is prohibitive. Downscaling methods span a wide range of computational cost, and statistical approaches in particular offer a relatively inexpensive way to refine climate model output into a more actionable form. title: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
abstract: Abstract. Nuclear conflicts could ignite intense urban fires that inject considerable amounts of black carbon (BC) into the upper atmosphere, with the potential to disrupt global climate. While uncertainties in the total BC injection remain large, relatively few modeling studies and limited model diversity have explored the climatic response to low-to-moderate BC injections, leaving key aspects of their climate impact poorly understood. abstract: Abstract We combine CONUS404 convection‐permitting climate simulations with the physics‐based WRF‐Hydro model to assess how climate warming may influence flood frequency and seasonality across the Midwestern United States. This framework captures interactions among precipitation, soil moisture, and snowpack that shape flood generation. Both simulated warming and historical records show a regional shift toward more extreme warm‐season, rainfall‐driven floods. abstract: Abstract. As climate change increases frequency and intensity of hot extremes, understanding how elevated temperatures influence surface ozone (O3) across different chemical regimes is critical. We combine observations from summer 2022 in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) with targeted United Kingdom Chemistry and Aerosols (UKCA) Box experiments to quantify and attribute the temperature sensitivity of ground-level O3 in a VOC-limited urban megacity (Shanghai) and a predominantly NOx-limited rural region (Lishui). title: An assessment of Northern Hemisphere warm spell trends across seasons: spring warm spells increasing faster than projected
abstract: Abstract Consecutive days of anomalously warm temperatures (warm spells) can severely impact human health and ecosystems, whatever time of year they occur. Previous research has typically focused only on warm-season warm spells—heatwaves; here, we assess trends in warm spells in all seasons across Northern Hemisphere midlatitude land using observational data (Berkeley Earth and ERA5) and CMIP6 climate models. abstract: Abstract Longwave (LW) scattering, the redirection of infrared radiation by cloud and aerosol particles, is often neglected in current global climate models (GCMs). However, studies have suggested that LW scattering can influence the Earth's energy budget and climate sensitivity, indicating a need to improve the representation and understanding of this radiative effect. abstract: The regional impacts of extreme climate events have been worsening over the last two decades and have intensified over the years. abstract: The development of renewable energy is a key approach to reducing fossil fuel dependence. This study examines the effect of modifying duct geometry into a convergent nozzle shape in an Oscillating Water Column (OWC) system. Experiments were conducted in a laboratory wave flume using sensors to measure wave height and pressure across nine wave period variations. title: Drainage of Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake in Antarctica observed by double-differential SAR interferometry
abstract: Hundreds of subglacial lakes in Antarctica have been reported by using radio-echo sounding and satellite altimetry, but the detection of small and short-lived hydrological events has remained challenging due to limited spatial and temporal resolution. In this study, we applied the Double-Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DDInSAR) technique to analyze surface-elevation changes associated with the Kronshtadskiy subglacial lake near the Amery Ice Shelf, East Antarctica. title: Extensive glacier loss in the coterminous United States
abstract: Glaciers populate the mountain ranges of the western conterminous United States and despite their importance to alpine hydrology, their area and volume change have never been comprehensively evaluated. Our study shows that since the mid-twentieth century about one-quarter of the glaciers have disappeared and the overall area and volume are reduced by one-third. The pattern of glacier shrinkage suggests most glaciers in the conterminous United States are largely maintained by local topographic influences due to their small size. title: Dynamic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves
abstract: This study investigates the seismic response of jacket-supported offshore wind turbines subjected to obliquely incident SV and Rayleigh waves, considering dynamic soil–structure interaction (SSI). The analysis is conducted using the OpenFAST numerical framework, extended with an SSI model to represent the dynamic impedance of pile foundations. abstract: ABSTRACT Lago Maggiore is situated in an overdeepened valley reach at the southern margin of the European Alps, and its thick sediment infill allows the reconstruction of the postglacial valley and lake evolution. We study here the sedimentary succession in the lower Ossola Valley, which is infilled by ~500 m of deposits. title: No Evidence for Strongly Enhanced Northern Hemisphere Cooling From Extratropical Versus Tropical Eruptions
abstract: Abstract Volcanic eruptions in the Northern Hemisphere extratropics have been reported to produce several times greater cooling in that region than tropical eruptions of similar magnitude. Using a large ensemble of simulations spanning the eruption size range from 5 to 40 Tg of stratospheric sulfur, we find that the extratropical‐to‐tropical cooling ratio is consistently within a factor of two, indicating no enhancement beyond the effect of aerosols being confined to a single hemisphere. abstract: Abstract The Earth Cloud Aerosol and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) provides critical spaceborne high spectral resolution LiDAR observations for global aerosol profiling. However, integrating these vertically resolved aerosol extinction coefficient profiles into column Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) introduces systematic biases from physical observation boundaries, which currently lack global validation and quantitative attribution. abstract: Abstract Record-breaking heatwaves arise from the interplay between long-term warming and transient atmospheric circulation anomalies, yet the mechanisms by which atmospheric circulation variability contributes to unprecedented heatwave severity remain an active area of investigation. Here, we investigate the unprecedented late-summer 2024 super heatwave with concurrent dry conditions (LS24) over the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), which produced the largest late-summer temperature anomaly during 1979–2024. abstract: Abstract Vertical exchange between the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) and the free troposphere (FT) is a key pathway for aerosol transport and can substantially influence surface air quality. title: Measurement report: Soil reactive nitrogen gas emissions in the Tibetan Plateau
abstract: Abstract. The Tibetan Plateau, highly sensitive to climate change, exerts strong atmospheric oxidation capacity partly through rapid cycling of atmospheric reactive nitrogen (Nr). Soil Nr emissions play a crucial role in atmospheric nitrogen cycling and oxidation capacity, yet their emissions on the Tibetan Plateau remain poorly quantified. title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways
abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. abstract: Reducing uncertainty in regional surface air temperature (SAT) projections is essential for climate-resilient planning in countries such as Iran, where complex terrain and limited adaptive capacity heighten climate vulnerability. This study systematically evaluated 51 CMIP6 models, the conventional equally weighted multi-model ensemble (MME) and performance-based Weighted Multi-Model Ensemble (WMME) against CRU_TS4.08 observations for historical SAT over Iran during 1980–2014. abstract: Abstract Wildfire danger in Southern California is strongly influenced by episodic offshore wind events and extreme atmospheric dryness, conditions that are not fully captured by the standard Canadian Fire Weather Index (CFWI), which was developed for boreal forest environments using noon-based meteorological inputs and has been widely applied by various climatic and ecological regimes. title: Does the urban presence of a city in the central Amazon induce more extreme precipitation?
abstract: Abstract In recent years, significant efforts have been made to understand how urban environments influence local weather, particularly extreme precipitation events. However, studies conducted to date for the largest city in the Amazon, Manaus, have focused mainly on investigating the effects of urbanization based on case studies, often limited to just one extreme precipitation event. abstract: The article examines the transformation of the concept of statehood in the context of climate change and technological advancement, with particular emphasis on the case of Tuvalu. It addresses the question of whether a state that has lost its physical territory may continue to exist as a subject of international law. abstract: Abstract. We quantify water vapor supersaturation (Sv) at warm cloud base by describing the ascent of a saturated (cloudy) air parcel as a reversible cloud-adiabatic process. abstract: Abstract Midlatitude cut‐off lows (COLs) strongly influence weather, climate, and regional ozone (O 3 ) variability, yet their seasonal impacts on near‐surface O 3 and underlying mechanisms remain inadequately understood. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Tribal nations across the United States face disproportionate flood impacts yet remain significantly underrepresented in national‐scale assessments, creating a critical equity gap in climate adaptation. We address this deficiency through a climate‐to‐local‐inundation framework for the Santee Sioux Nation, Nebraska, by forcing 10‐m hydrodynamic simulations with a 42‐year paired historical and pseudo‐global‐warming CONUS404 runoff event set. abstract: Abstract Earthquakes affect surrounding fault systems through multiple mechanisms. abstract: Abstract Satellite remote sensing of ozone has progressed from daily global observations by polar‐orbiting platforms to hourly regional monitoring by geostationary platforms. However, retrieving detailed vertical profiles remains challenging because satellite measurements have inherently limited vertical sensitivity. title: Projected weakening of Northern Hemisphere summertime high-latitude waveguide and teleconnection variability
abstract: Summertime high-latitude teleconnections shape persistent circulation anomalies and surface climate extremes across the Northern Hemisphere, yet their future evolution under anthropogenic warming remains poorly constrained. Using 31 CMIP6 models under SSP5-8.5, we examine projected changes in the high-latitude waveguide, teleconnection variability, and the resulting surface air temperature (SAT) response. abstract: Abstract. The effect of urban land use on convective storms with deep and persistent rotating updrafts (supercell storms) is systematically investigated using ensembles of idealized numerical simulations. abstract: Abstract Archaea play essential roles in global biogeochemical cycles, yet their diversity in environmental samples remains understudied. Limited coverage of universal primers towards archaea, their very low abundance relative to bacteria in the studied samples, inefficient cell lysis and the incompleteness of reference databases complicate archaeal 16S rRNA gene sequencing. abstract: A lack of observations of turbulent fluxes over continental glaciers limits our understanding of the mechanisms that control glacier variations and associated water resource changes across the Tibetan Plateau (TP). abstract: A major source of uncertainty in inverse modelling of greenhouse gas emissions are deficits in atmospheric transport models, in particular in the description of vertical mixing within the planetary boundary layer (PBL). abstract: Abstract Slow slip events (SSEs) represent an aseismic transient slip mode that repeats quasi‐periodically, near or partially overlapping with the megathrust earthquake zone. abstract: The study addresses a retrieval of wind vector fields from satellite data. An algorithm developed for the 0.7 μm channel of the MSU-GS/VE instrument aboard the Arktika-M series satellites is presented. abstract: Groundwater-recharge planning in semi-arid hard-rock aquifers is uncertain when site selection relies only on surface indicators. This study integrates geographic information system (GIS) analysis, vertical electrical sounding (VES), and Dar-Zarrouk parameters to screen candidate sites for recharge and surface-water storage interventions in Kangti Mandal, Telangana, India. abstract: This article examines the applicability of the mesh-free Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method for numerical simulation of surfable solitary waves propagating over an artificial seabed in a wave pool. The simulations were performed using DualSPHysics, with particular attention given to the accurate reproduction of the free-surface profile. title: Morphological Characteristics of Tropical Precipitation Features Producing Extreme Instantaneous Rain Rates in GPM and DYAMOND Global Storm Resolving Models
abstract: Abstract The influence of the spatial organization of tropical convection on the production of extreme instantaneous localized tropical rain rates remains poorly constrained, both in observations and in models. Using retrievals from the Ku‐band radar onboard the GPM satellite, we identify tropical precipitation features (PFs) and quantify their morphological characteristics. abstract: ABSTRACT Wenchuan earthquake–induced landslides generated large volumes of sediment that formed lateral sediment deposits in mountainous river channels, significantly altering flow structures and channel evolution. Under such strongly non-uniform flow conditions, accurate estimation of bed shear stress remains challenging. title: Substantial spatial heterogeneity in growing season dynamics across northern environments
abstract: Abstract Arctic tundra and boreal forest landscapes exhibit substantial microclimatic temperature variability, driven by strong topographic gradients, heterogeneous snowmelt patterns, and contrasting vegetation structures. However, this fine-scale variability is often poorly represented in reanalyses, climate models, and conventional weather station networks. In this study, we use a total of 347 microclimate loggers deployed across three regions in northern Fennoscandia during 2020–2024 to examine how the onset, end, duration, and degree days of the growing season vary across the landscapes. abstract: The article focuses on decarbonized hybrid energy systems based on solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) and gas turbines (GTs). The relevance of the work is driven by the global necessity to transition to low-carbon energy generation technologies. The main objective of the research is to conduct a thermodynamic analysis and optimize the parameters of the SOFC – GT hybrid system operating on two types of fuel: pure hydrogen and methane. abstract: Abstract. The MISR Research Aerosol retrieval algorithm (RA) was developed in parallel with the MISR standard operational algorithm (SA), to explore innovative retrieval ideas for possible implementation in the SA, and to provide higher-spatial-resolution results with enhanced sensitivity to particle properties, where possible. title: Developing a Climate Impact Indicator Framework for the UK Agri‐Food Sector: A Literature Review and Stakeholder Co‐Production Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Consistent monitoring and reporting of the impacts of weather in a changing climate is a key component in being able to attribute future risk and losses to weather variations. This allows the production of evidence required to facilitate mitigation, adaptation strategies and influence policy implementation. The agri‐food sector has always been impacted by weather and climate, but whilst data are consistently produced for metrics relating to the sector, there is no consistent reporting of how weather and climate are influencing these. title: Technological solutions for diamond drilling and cutting of massive concrete structures during reconstruction and demolition of bridge establishments
abstract: The article provides an overview and analysis of modern diamond drilling and cutting technologies used in the reconstruction, widening, and dismantling of massive reinforced concrete bridge structures. Based on the long-term experience of NPP SK MOST LLC since 1994, the article describes key methods used in practice, including diamond drilling of precision holes, cutting with circular saws and diamond wire, and breaking concrete with wedge jacks and hydraulic nippers. title: Heat-related urban mortality attributable to human-induced climate change in Europe from 2000 to 2025
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat, with major implications for population health. Although previous studies have attributed heat-related mortality to climate change during individual events, the longer-term contribution of human-induced warming to urban mortality burdens across Europe remains poorly quantified. abstract: Abstract Fluid transport in nanometer-scale channels underlies nanofluidic technologies and geological systems, yet measured capillary filling rates in hydrophilic channels are often far slower than classical theory predicts. Here we show, using a coupled flow model based on classical density functional theory combining hydrodynamics, electrokinetics and capillarity, that electrokinetic resistance and locally elevated viscosity near the channel walls jointly suppress flow, capturing the measured slowdown across independent experiments. title: Assessing the consistency of X CO 2 products from DQ-1 ACDL and passive satellites using a unified comparison framework
abstract: Abstract. Spaceborne active CO2 IPDA lidar provides an active remote-sensing approach for XCO2 observations that differs from passive NIR/SWIR remote sensing. However, comparisons between DQ-1 ACDL and passive optical satellite XCO2 products remain limited. Here we compare DQ-1 ACDL with OCO-2, OCO-3, GOSAT, and GOSAT-2 XCO2 products from June 2022 to December 2024 using a unified framework that combines CAMS-based spatiotemporal coherence assessment, satellite sampling availability, daily 2° aggregation, spatiotemporal collocation, and XCO2 column-definition correction. title: Biomass Burning in Australia: No Evidence for Carbonyl Sulfide (OCS) Enhancement in Fire Plumes From In‐Situ Measurements During SouthTRAC
abstract: Abstract Determining the atmospheric abundance and the emission sources of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) plays a crucial role for the sulfur budget in the atmosphere. In addition to its main anthropogenic and biogenic sources, biomass burning is assumed to be an essential, but not well constrained source of OCS. From November 2019 onward extensive bushfires along the eastern coast of Australia released huge amounts of trace species into the atmosphere; during one flight of the SouthTRAC campaign air masses were observed carrying signatures of these fires along the southern coast of South America. title: Impact Crater Hydrothermal Systems Support Rapid Microbial Enrichment and Diverse Metabolic Potential
abstract: Impact crater hydrothermal systems, formed after asteroid and comet impacts, have been proposed as promising habitats for life on early Earth and as key targets in the search for life on planetary bodies such as Mars, since they provide liquid water and active geochemical turnover. title: Areal reduction factors from high-resolution rain gauges in Austria
abstract: Abstract. Areal Reduction Factors (ARFs) are widely used to convert point design precipitation derived from intensity–duration–frequency (IDF) curves into areal precipitation values for hydrological design. Despite their importance, ARFs remain highly uncertain, particularly for short durations and small areas, due to insufficient representation of precipitation spatial variability. title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991–2018
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. title: Sensitivity of the summertime diurnal precipitation cycle over three representative regions of China to convective trigger and closure treatments in a single-column model
abstract: Abstract. Using a single‑column model, we investigate how trigger and closure treatments in ZM, TDK, and UNICON convection schemes affect DCP over China. For late-afternoon rainfall, TDK and ZM schemes with standard CAPE closure simulate precipitation peaks around noon, substantially earlier than observed. title: CHARACTERISATION AND ESTIMATION OF THE WIND ENERGY POTENTIAL OF THE TOWN OF MELFI IN CHAD
abstract: This study characterised and estimated the wind energy potential of the town of Melfi in the Guera province of central Chad, situated at 11.06 north latitude and 17.93 east longitude at an altitude of 416 m. The data consisted of an hourly time series of wind speed and direction observed at 10 m above ground level over six years, from August 2020 to August 2026, comprising 52,536 valid data points. title: Supersaturation Fluctuation Modulates Warm Rain Formation in Cumulus Clouds: Implications for Hygroscopic Cloud Seeding
abstract: Abstract Recent observational studies have demonstrated that supersaturation fluctuations (SS’) in clouds induced by turbulence at scales smaller than 100 m can significantly affect microphysical processes such as aerosol activation and droplet condensation. However, subgrid‐scale SS’ is often ignored in the current model. title: Acoustic‐Seismic Coupling Signals From Aircraft Reveal Firn‐Ice Transition and Near‐Surface Elastic Structure of Antarctic Ice
abstract: Abstract Predicting the response of Antarctic ice to climate change requires detailed knowledge of its shallow structure, but direct measurements are challenging. Traditional seismic surveys are logistically demanding, and surface remote sensing provides limited information about subsurface layers. Here, we introduce uncontacted airborne seismology, a method that uses aircraft‐generated sounds and their conversion into seismic waves at the ice surface to probe the ice interior. title: Future Northeastward Shift of Extratropical Transition of Tropical Cyclones Over the North Atlantic in Downscaling Projections
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) often undergo extratropical transition (ET) at the midlatitudes, becoming post‐tropical cyclones (PTCs). We combine a logistic regression PTC identification model with synthetic TC tracks and intensities from the Columbia HAZard model (CHAZ) to project future ET completion over the North Atlantic (NA). title: HTAP3-OPNS: ozone, PM, nitrogen and sulphur deposition – multi-model experiments to support the revision of the CLRTAP Gothenburg Protocol
abstract: Abstract. HTAP3-OPNS is a multi-model exercise designed to support the revision of the Gothenburg Protocol under the UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP). Using an ensemble of Chemical Transport Models (CTMs) and Chemistry-Climate Models (CCMs), this study investigates the long-range transport and impacts of ground-level ozone, particulate matter (PM), and nitrogen and sulphur deposition across different global regions. abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the capability of the MLUCM BEP + BEM to reproduce intra-urban variability of air temperature and relative humidity in Lecce (Italy) during summer 2025. abstract: The ancient villages in western Guangdong integrate farming, clan and Confucian culture, carrying local memory and local identity. However, urbanization and labor outflow have caused dilapidated buildings and memory faults, facing the dual crisis of "physical damage" and "lack of expression". title: Detecting long-term canopy change and vegetation shifts in northern peatlands using LAI and climate data
abstract: Abstract. Peatlands store vast amounts of carbon, yet their canopies are changing under northern warming. We assessed recent vegetation trajectories by analysing greening and browning across northern peatlands using a gap-filled, sensor-independent climate data record of leaf area index (LAI) for 2001–2023. title: Mitigating the Impact of Drought on Inland Water Transport: A System Dynamics Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, droughts have disrupted goods transport on Dutch waterways, causing production losses in the hinterland and reputational damage to inland water transport (IWT). As future droughts are expected to be more extreme, the question is how IWT can stay reliable. abstract: Entre os meses de abril e maio de 2024, uma onda de calor (OC) afetou extensas áreas das regiões Sul, Sudeste e Centro-Oeste do Brasil, enquanto o estado do Rio Grande do Sul registrou recordes históricos de precipitação. abstract: Vertical cyclic uplift of single-helix anchors in soft clay can induce stiffness degradation, excess pore-pressure accumulation, and residual displacement. title: Safety and Resilience in Slope Engineering Design for New Buildings under Extreme Rainstorm Climates
abstract: The safety of construction slopes holds significant importance in engineering and architecture, with the lack of resilience against extreme weather conditions being particularly critical. This paper systematically examines the fundamental flaws in traditional design theories regarding the limitations of compression-shear stress paths and the assumption of constant soil parameters. abstract: Abstract. The brittle damage around tunnels in the form of spalling is common in massive crystalline rocks subjected to high in-situ stresses. title: Damage-mechanics-based prediction of natural fracture distribution in tight-sand gas reservoirs using 2d seismic data: Calibration and prediction
abstract: Prediction of natural fracture distribution in tight-sand gas reservoirs remains an industry challenge due to small fault throws. Furthermore, numerous mature oilfields only possess 2D seismic datasets, rendering conventional analytical calculations of natural fractures within tight reservoirs infeasible. abstract: This paper reviews the suitability of carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP)–steel hybrid structures as load-bearing components of dynamic mechanical systems. The literature is evaluated against structural requirements, including load-carrying capacity, fatigue resistance and durability, and motion-related requirements, including inertial properties, vibration and damping. abstract: Strategic freight procurement is the mechanism by which a shipper converts a forecast of future transportation demand into a portfolio of contracted rates before the demand arrives. Our subject here is strategic freight procurement and request-for-quotation management in an enterprise transportation management system, approached as a structured, repeatable auction rather than a clerical sourcing task. abstract: Abstract. Lightning is one of the main sources of NOₓ in the Earth’s atmosphere, yet there is considerable variability in NOₓ production during thunderstorms. This study aimed to diagnose sediment regime transformation in Sutami Reservoir within the Sengguruh-Sutami cascade system, East Java, Indonesia. title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract: Abstract. Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. abstract: Abstract In this study, the axial compression behavior of filament-wound composite pipes reinforced with glass, carbon, and intraply hybrid fibers was systematically investigated through combined experimental and microstructural analyses. abstract: Maintenance tasks scheduling is one of the essential factors in maintenance engineering. This paper focuses on the maintenance task scheduling problem in confined spaces under resource-constrained scenarios (e.g., maintenance task planning during annual inspections in ship engine rooms or offshore drilling platforms), where spatial limitations and multi-resource availability jointly impact maintenance efficiency. abstract: Abstract GRACE/GRACE-FO missions recover gravity field from orbits observed by GPS and variations in inter-satellite distances obtained by the inter-satellite ranging systems. title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria
abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. title: Aqueous‐Phase Processing of Organic Aerosols at the Southern Great Plains: Insights From Integrated Chemical and Microphysical Analyses
abstract: Abstract Aqueous‐phase reactions are hypothesized to be a major pathway for secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation in humid, cloud‐influenced environments, yet direct observational constraints remain limited. Here we investigated aqueous SOA (aqSOA) formation and evolution during the spring 2016 Holistic Interactions of Shallow Clouds, Aerosols, and Land Ecosystems (HI‐SCALE) campaign at the U.S. Department of Energy Southern Great Plains (SGP) site using high‐resolution aerosol mass spectrometer (HR‐AMS) measurements integrated with particle size distribution and meteorological observation

title: Modeling Carbon Dioxide Disposal in a Non-isothermal Viscoelastic Porous Medium
abstract: The paper proposes a mathematical model of carbon dioxide disposal in a non-isothermal viscoelastic porous medium. Following the two-dimensional approach and considering the smallness of the solid phase velocity, the initial system of equations is reduced to the problem of finding the effective pressure and porosity of the medium. Thermal effects caused by gas injection are introduced into the model by the equation for the temperature of the medium. title: Wildfire, Restoration, and Postwildfire Rehabilitation Effects on Wind Erosion in the Great Basin
abstract: Restoration of degraded areas and postdisturbance rehabilitation after wildfire encompass critical approaches for reducing and reversing impacts of wind erosion and sand and dust storms (SDS). However, the broad outcomes of dryland restoration and rehabilitation for wind erosion and SDS remain underexplored. Wind erosion is an emerging issue in the Great Basin of the western United States, exacerbated by invasive annual grasses and associated wildfire. Here, we assess potential wind erosion and SDS responses to wildfire, restoration, and postwildfire rehabilitation treatments at the regional s

title: Atmospheric Aerosol Concentrations and Solar Radiation Attenuation in Urban Environments in Germany
abstract: Purpose: The aim of this study was to investigate the atmospheric aerosol concentrations and solar radiation attenuation in urban environments in Germany. Methodology: The study adopted a desktop research methodology. Desk research refers to secondary data or that which can be collected without fieldwork. Desk research is basically involved in collecting data from existing resources hence it is often considered a low-cost technique as compared to field research, as the main cost is involved in executive’s time, telephone charges and directories. title: Impacts of coal facies on vertical heterogeneity of deep coalbed methane reservoir in the Yulin area of Ordos Basin, North China
abstract: Abstract The vertical heterogeneity of coal is a crucial factor influencing the development of coalbed methane (CBM) and it is significantly influenced by coal facies. Utilizing the theories of coal facies and variation coefficient to clearly classify and quantitatively characterize the vertical coal facies types and heterogeneity of deep 8# coal in the Yulin area of the Ordos Basin based on the submaceral content, coal quality, and physical property tests. title: The electromagnetic characteristics of UXO using the electromagnetic method
abstract: Abstract In UXO clearance operations, reliable detection is a prerequisite for safe and efficient remediation. This paper investigates a transient electromagnetic (TEM) method for UXO detection, including the optimization of a magnetically coupled transmitting source and the analysis of the electromagnetic responses of UXO targets with different orientations and burial depths. title: Melt Production and Volatile Release From Thermochemical Mantle Plumes
abstract: Abstract Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. Here we use thermochemical plume models to compute the melt production and carbon release from compositionally heterogeneous plumes that sample peridotite and eclogite. title: Force-based design of a novel self-centring concentrically braced steel frame validated by nonlinear time-history analysis
abstract: Self-centring concentrically braced frames (SC-CBFs) are intended to limit residual deformation after strong earthquakes, but practical code-oriented procedures for their design remain limited. This study presents a force-based design (FBD) procedure for a horizontally post-tensioned SC-CBF consistent with Eurocode 8 and Eurocode 3. The procedure defines the seismic base shear, brace sizing, allocation of shear resistance between the concentrically braced frame and post-tensioning system, and capacity checks for beams, columns, braces, and strands. A regular four-storey archetype was designed
institutions: Ollscoil na Gaillimhe – University of Galway

title: Circular Economy and Construction Waste Management in Saudi Mega-Projects: Pathways Towards Vision 2030 Sustainability Targets
abstract: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 is accelerating the delivery of large-scale urban, tourism, transport, industrial and infrastructure projects while simultaneously strengthening national ambitions for environmental protection, resource efficiency and waste diversion. The scale of this development creates a strategic challenge: construction and demolition waste cannot be managed only as an end-of-pipe disposal problem. It must be addressed through a circular economy model that prevents waste, preserves material value, enables reuse and high-value recycling, and creates dependable markets for secondar
journal: Global Academic Journal of Economics and Business

title: Dispersión de plumas de contaminación atmosférica por incendios forestales: un caso de estudio en el sur de Argentina
abstract: Forest fires pose significant threats to ecosystems, biodiversity, and human health, highlighting the importance of accurate tracking and assessment of their impact. The sources and levels of wildfire contamination were determined using HYSPLIT simulations and NASA MODIS satellite imagery. The forest fire that started in January 2024 in Los Alerces National Park, located in Chubut Province, Argentina, is presented as a case study. title: Resource Analysis and Screening for Potential CO2 Storage Targets in Low-Porosity Saline Aquifers, Yulin, China
abstract: Abstract The Ordos Basin, a crucial energy base in China, leads the nation in oil, gas, and coal production, consequently leading to high carbon emissions. This establishes it as a key prospective region for implementing CO2 geological storage (CCS) to facilitate regional emissions reductions. However, the basin is predominantly characterized by low-porosity and ultralow-permeability reservoirs, which limit the applicability of current site selection criteria, largely derived from successful international projects involving high-porosity and high-permeability reservoirs. title: Methane Emissions in Melbourne, Australia. Part 2: Improving Prior Estimates Using Synthesis Inversion
abstract: Abstract Urban methane emissions remain highly uncertain due to the complexity of overlapping anthropogenic sources and limitations in current bottom‐up inventories. In this study, we apply a synthesis inversion framework to refine sector‐specific methane emissions for the Melbourne region in Australia, using in situ atmospheric observations and a Bayesian inversion approach. Our method incorporates constrained and unconstrained inversions, observational filtering, and ensemble‐based uncertainty quantification, including both ensemble spread and posterior covariance structure. title: Cross-Comparison of Ground Observations, CAMS Estimates, and Linke-Model Irradiance for Photovoltaic System Design in Sahelian Niger
abstract: Reliable solar-resource inputs are essential for photovoltaic (PV) and hybrid-system design, but temporal matching and measurement traceability require scrutiny where reference records are scarce. This study compares SM206-SOLAR ground observations, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) Radiation Service v4.6 estimates and Linke-model irradiance for Dosso, Niger, in May and August 2021. The CAMS v4.6 dataset documents the coordinates, altitude, UTC intervals and irradiation units. journal: International Journal of Energy and Power Engineering

title: Characterisation and Extension of a Rigid Body Dynamics Solver Coupled with OpenFOAM® for Flight Performance Analysis of Flapping-wing Drones
abstract: The extraordinary aerial agility of hummingbirds and insects continues to inspire the design of flapping-wing drones. To replicate them, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations must be coupled with rigid body dynamics solvers. While OpenFOAM® provides a general articulated-body algorithm (ABA) for these multiphysics simulations, its current implementation is restricted to passive joints and lacks thorough verification for free-flight applications. title: Country-scale forest carbon modeling to support national greenhouse gas inventories in Croatia and Slovakia
abstract: Abstract Forest ecosystems are important carbon sinks and play a crucial role in reaching carbon neutrality. This study presents a reproducible workflow of using the biogeochemical ecosystem model Biome-BGCMuSo to support national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory by including CO 2 emissions and removals from carbon pools lacking explicit carbon stock change (CSC) estimates within the Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) sector. title: Analysis of precipitation trends and extremes in the Upper Capibaribe River, Pernambuco
abstract: Climate change has intensified precipitation variability, especially in semiarid regions such as Northeastern Brazil. This study analyzed rainfall variability and extreme rainfall events between 1986 and 2025 across eight stations in the Upper Capibaribe River sub-basin, Pernambuco. Descriptive statistics, the Rainfall Anomaly Index (RAI), the Mann–Kendall test, and Sen’s Slope estimator were applied. title: Analysis of wind load distribution on various geometrical forms of 3D structures
abstract: Reducing research costs has always been a priority for engineers and researchers. The advent of high-performance computers has enabled extensive use of numerical methods, particularly computational fluid dynamics (CFD), in structural wind analysis. In this study, ANSYS Fluent was used to investigate wind load distribution on eleven three-dimensional geometrical configurations with varying apex shapes and diameter distributions. title: Subwavelength bandgaps and broadband vibration attenuation in symmetry-broken star honeycomb metamaterials
abstract: Abstract Elastic metamaterials can suppress vibration propagation through elastic-wave bandgaps, providing an effective strategy for low-frequency broadband vibration reduction. In this study, the mirror symmetry of a standard star honeycomb (SSH) is progressively broken to develop a single mirror star honeycomb (SMSH) and a chiral star honeycomb (CSH). The bandgap characteristics of the three structures are investigated using Bloch–Floquet theory and the finite element method. title: Numerical Investigation on Repowering Aging Onshore Wind Turbine Foundations Through a Reuse Strategy: An Engineering Case Study
abstract: For the repowering of aging onshore wind foundations, a reuse-oriented strengthening scheme that does not require demolition of the existing foundation is proposed based on the retrofit project of an octagonal extended foundation at a wind farm in Shandong Province, China. Through structural measures such as connecting the foundation ring with high-strength threaded rebars and underpinning the existing foundation with a new foundation, the new and existing foundations are integrated into a composite foundation system with coordinated load-bearing behavior. journal: International Journal of Concrete Structures and Materials

title: Design, Finite Element Analysis, and Experimental Investigation of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer (BFRP) Composite for Oil and Gas Applications
abstract: The pipelines used for transporting oil and gas need to have sufficient strength, durability, and resistance to any form of corrosion. The usual metallic pipes are prone to corrosion and weigh quite a lot. In this research, the use of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composite Pipe has been studied using computer aided design and finite element analysis among others. A BFRP pipe with 200 mm length, 50 mm inner diameter, and 10 mm wall thickness was modeled using orthotropic material property assumptions and studied under an internal pressure of 55 MPa. title: The effect of temperature on fertility: a province-level analysis of monthly total fertility rates in Italy in 2003–2022
abstract: Abstract Long-term climate change has increased the frequency and intensity of high-temperature weather events, which in turn affect human health and wellbeing. Warmer temperatures are reported to affect both reproductive health and behaviors, possibly reducing birth rates. In a low-fertility context, the potential negative impact that climate change might have on fertility is consequential. This study focuses on Italy, a low-fertility country disproportionately affected by climate change, with sharp regional disparities in both climate zones and economic development. title: INVESTIGATION OF ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY VARIATION ON MODEL ROCKET PERFORMANCE
abstract: Atmospheric density is the environmental parameter to which small-scale rocket altitude performance is most sensitive, yet it is routinely treated as a fixed constant in amateur and educational practice. This paper presents a combined analytical, numerical and literature-based investigation of how variation in air density affects model and high-power rocket flight. title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. title: Renewable Energy Use in Small Rural Towns: A Case Study of Thulamela Local Municipality, South Africa
abstract: This manuscript explores the use of renewable energy (RE) in small towns to promote sustainable human settlements, using Thohoyandou as a case study. An exploratory research design underpinned the study. Using a combination of primary and secondary data collection methods, a randomised sample of 125 households in Thohoyandou town was selected, along with 15 purposively selected key informant interviewees. title: Relevance of pesticides for macroinvertebrate communities in agricultural streams – a re-evaluation
abstract: Attributing ecological impairment in agricultural streams to individual stressors is a common challenge in freshwater monitoring because pesticide exposure often co-occurs with habitat degradation, nutrient enrichment, oxygen depletion, and other environmental pressures. The German ‘small water bodies monitoring project’ (‘Kleingewässermonitoring’, KgM) provides an opportunity to examine this challenge using a large-scale field dataset. title: Correlation of conventional histopathology and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in the diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis: doi: 10.7417/CT.2026.2148
abstract: Background: Spinal tuberculosis (STB) is a global epidemic in nations with high tuberculosis burdens, such as India. Mycobacterial culture and acid-fast staining are the primary methods used for the diagnosis of STB. In this study, the aim was to determine the diagnostic accuracy of GeneXpert MTB/RIF over conventional histopathology (HPE) in the diagnosis of STB. Materials and methods: This retrospective study included 64 suspected STB patients who underwent transpedicular biopsy at our hospital. title: From prototypical regimes to observed complex dynamics and CO 2 transport in the Amazonian nocturnal boundary layer
abstract: Abstract. We investigated the characteristics of the nocturnal boundary layer (NBL) above and within the Amazon rainforest canopy during the 2022 dry season. The study aims to determine how NBL dynamics influence nocturnal CO2 and heat exchange across the canopy-atmosphere interface. Utilising observations from the CloudRoots-Amazon22 field campaign conducted at the Amazon Tall Tower Observatory, we distinguished between the strongly and weakly stable regimes to study the effect of radiative cooling and wind shear on CO2 and heat exchange.
