title: Learning Management to Promote Future Skills for Student Teachers: A Case Study of Social Studies Student Teachers at Songkhla Rajabhat University, Thailand
abstract: This mixed-methods case study examined instructional management and future-skill needs in higher-education social studies teacher preparation, developed community-based learning activities for the Social Studies Pedagogy course, and examined changes in six future-skill domains among student teachers. The participants were 30 third-year Social Studies student teachers enrolled at Songkhla Rajabhat University in the first semester of the 2025 academic year. title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. title: Robust Design of a Riprap Basin Outlet
abstract: One of the major causes of hydraulic infrastructure deterioration is scour around the structure and culverts suffer from this at the outlet, resulting in partial or complete collapse of the structure, roadway damage, and increased maintenance costs. Conventional outlet protection systems are commonly designed with a single design discharge, usually the 25- or 50-year return period depending on the size of the channel bed. title: CFD investigation of a novel gabion-based porous medium configuration for energy dissipation in ogee spillway stilling basins
abstract: Ogee spillways which provide very large discharge rates are extensively employed for civil engineering applications, but high velocity flows generated by Ogee spillways can be seriously harmful to downstream structures. This numerical investigation is conducted to assess the potential of adding porous media (uniform gabions and cross shaped gabions, with varying porosities: 30%, 40% and 50%) to the stilling basin at the bottom of ogee spillways to dissipate energy. title: Molecular evolution of oxygenated organic molecules in a cloud-influenced forested mountain environment
abstract: Abstract. Atmospheric oxygenated organic molecules (OOMs) link the oxidation of volatile organic compound to secondary organic aerosol formation, yet their molecular evolution in cloud-influenced forested mountain environments remains poorly constrained. Here, gas-phase OOMs were measured using an iodide-adduct chemical ionization mass spectrometer at a high-altitude forested station in southeastern China during autumn 2023. title: Mapping the Governance Gap: Institutional Capacity as a Missing Dimension of Climate Vulnerability Assessment - Evidence from Greek Local Government
abstract: Climate-vulnerability assessments identify where climatic hazards and socioeconomic sensitivity are concentrated but rarely examine whether the responsible public institutions possess the capacity to respond. This study addresses this governance blind spot by comparing climate-hazard vulnerability with municipal technical-planning capacity across Greece. title: Energy-related industrial CO2 pathways toward carbon neutrality in Shandong, a coal-intensive Chinese province: A structural decarbonization and abatement cost approach
abstract: Industrial decarbonization in coal-intensive provinces is central to China’s dual-carbon goals. However, most provincial scenario studies project future emissions without attributing reductions to transition packages, comparing electrification and hydrogen within one framework, or testing whether cleaner pathways are economically feasible. This study addresses these three gaps. title: Exploration potential of middle jurassic shale gas in the Yabulai Basin, Northwest China
abstract: Abstract The Jurassic continental shale strata are widely distributed across several small- to medium-sized sedimentary basins in northwest China. Currently, shale gas exploration and development in China are primarily concentrated in large basins, while long-term exploration and evaluation of small- and medium-sized basins with unique geological characteristics remain insufficient. title: Three-parameter Kerr soil model: finite element formulation and applications in transient dynamic analyses
abstract: Soil-structure interaction is a topic of paramount importance in civil engineering, as the method of soil modeling directly influences the static and dynamic performance of structures supported by elastic foundations. Simplified models, such as Winkler's, while widely adopted, fail to adequately represent the effects of distributed stiffness and lateral interaction. In this context, multiparameter models, like those proposed by Pasternak and Kerr, offer a more realistic characterization of soil behavior. title: Signs of power: giant ficron handaxes may have played a non-utilitarian role in structuring social groups in MIS 9 Britain
abstract: Giant ficrons are a rare but recurrent sub-type of Acheulean handaxe, that in Britain are predominantly found in assemblages dating to the MIS 9 interglacial. A variety of theories have aimed to explain the striking size and appearance of giant ficrons as reflecting their use in specialised subsistence tasks or non-utilitarian display functions. Despite this, they are typically underrepresented or absent from many studies concerning giant handaxes or Acheulean morphological diversity more broadly. title: Homo Memorabiliaxis: Souvenirs and the Evolution of Autobiographical Memory and Self
abstract: Humans routinely keep souvenirs objects retained for the memories they evoke, yet the evolutionary and cognitive consequences of mnemonic collecting remain unclear. Existing discussions of curated objects concentrate on later prehistory and modern humans and view such objects at the social level, as carriers of shared cultural meaning or as markers of status. Here, we address an earlier time period and locate the phenomenon at the personal rather than the social level. journal: Evolutionary Anthropology Issues News and Reviews

title: Transport and fate of radon: a critical review of mechanisms and environmental influences
abstract: Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas produced from the decay of uranium-238. It poses significant environmental health risks because it can migrate through soil, groundwater, and air before accumulating indoors. This review, based on a critical synthesis of 94 peer-reviewed publications (2009–2025), explores how radon moves and behaves, emphasising diffusion, advection, and dissolution, and the influence of soil properties, groundwater flow, building characteristics, and human activities. title: Collaborative Policy Modeling for Ecotourism Conservation and Development: A Multi-Case Empirical Study Based on Policy Instrument Taxonomy
abstract: The synergistic imbalance between conservation and development remains a core constraint on the sustainable development of ecotourism. Grounded in externality theory, this study constructs a three-dimensional modeling framework that integrates the quantification of positive externalities from ecological conservation, the pricing of negative externalities from tourism development, and the adaptation of policy instruments. title: Design and mechanical performance analysis of re-entrant auxetic structures fabricated using SLA 3D printing: a comparative study
abstract: Auxetic structures, with a negative Poisson’s ratio, have gained significant attention for aerospace and automotive applications due to their superior mechanical performance. In this study, two different Auxetic Structures were used, namely Re–entrant Hexagon (A) and Re-entrant star triangular structure (B). They were designed and fabricated with the use of Stereolithography (SLA) Additive Manufacturing with the use of Standard Photopolymer Resin Material. title: The influence of seasonal microbiological load of a water supply source on the hydraulic characteristics of worn‐out metal networks and the efficiency of their operation
abstract: Assessment of changes in the operational efficiency of water supply systems under the influence of a seasonal microbiological factor in the Astrakhan Oblast. The study included field surveys of sections of metal water supply networks and water intake and water treatment facilities in a number of rural settlements in the Astrakhan Oblast. title: Aerodynamic Characteristics and Wind Load Partitioning in Double-deck Girders: Effects of Inter-deck Clearance Height
abstract: The inter-deck clearance height (IDH), defined as the vertical distance between decks, is a key parameter in the aerodynamic design of double-deck bridges. This parameter governs both global aerodynamic characteristics and the allocation of wind loads across different subcomponents (top/bottom decks, windward/leeward trusses) of the girder, yet its effects remain underexplored. This study examines the effects of IDH using five double-deck girders with varying IDH, combining wind tunnel tests and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations. title: Numerical Investigations of a Novel Offshore Platform Blast Wall Design Using Energy Absorption Devices at Supports
abstract: Abstract Offshore blast walls are critical safety barriers designed to protect personnel and equipment from hydrocarbon explosions. Traditional designs often struggle to simultaneously satisfy code requirements for deflection limits and weld integrity under high-intensity blasts. This study proposes a novel offshore blast wall concept incorporating energy-absorbing support devices comprising PMI foam-filled sliding cores and rotational springs. title: CT image-based experimental and numerical simulation methods for freeze–thaw concrete microstructure
abstract: Freeze–thaw cycling is a primary durability challenge for concrete structures in cold regions. This study presents an integrated experimental and numerical approach to visualize and quantify mesoscale freeze–thaw damage evolution in concrete. Indoor rapid freeze–thaw tests were conducted, combined with computed tomography (CT) scanning for three-dimensional (3D) microstructure reconstruction and finite element (FE) simulation for damage analysis. abstract: Introduction: With the rapid development of China’s highway system, the construction of bridges spanning valleys in mountainous regions has become inevitable. In these areas, the deformation of bridge foundations must be strictly controlled, often through slopes reinforced with anti-slide piles. abstract: Abstract Detachment of authigenic reservoir fines by breakage with consequent migration in rock, straining, and permeability decline has been widely reported for several technological and natural processes. This phenomenon particularly calls for strong attention due to decline in well production and injection rates. This paper presents laboratory corefloods performed in a wide range of flow rates with monitoring of breakthrough fines concentrations and pressure drops across the overall core and its first section. title: Study on barchan dune movement velocity using fiber optic sensing theory and technology: a case study in the Tengger Desert, China
abstract: Abstract Dune movement velocity monitoring is essential to the study of desert ecosystem evolution, the protection of surrounding agriculture, and the prevention of wind erosion. However, traditional monitoring technologies such as field marking, GPS positioning, and image remote sensing suffer from limited accuracy and resistance to interference under harsh desert conditions. abstract: Abstract Melt extraction is a critical process for the formation of eruptible magmas. Magmatic textures and compositions illuminate magma dynamics during the emplacement of a large (2 m diameter) felsic enclave (LFE) within granitic mush in the Aztec Wash pluton (15.7 Ma, NV-USA). The LFE is an ellipsoidal microgranite mass inferred to have been nearly solid when it settled at the top of a crystal-rich zone of the magma body. title: Preloaded and premoistened foundation that overlaps sabkha collapse treatment with construction evaluated by coupled infiltration and consolidation analysis
abstract: Abstract Conventional improvement methods applied to sabkha soil (collapse soil) are time-consuming, lengthening the project schedule. abstract: Foundation selection for a multistorey building on soft ground is governed not only by pile capacity, but also by settlement, load sharing, construction constraints, and cost. title: Numerical evaluation of hydraulic performance of a laboratory-scale Archimedes screw pump
abstract: Archimedes screw pump (ASP) is a type of positive displacement pump for transporting water from lower to upper incline elevations. It is a simple and robust pump widely used for irrigation, flood mitigation, and in wastewater treatment plants. Although ASPs have been used for centuries, there is a lack of literature related to the optimal hydraulic performance and elucidating the underlying flow mechanisms. abstract: Abstract. abstract: We classify within the quasi-geostrophic framework all types of traveling waves in zonal bands of the planetary atmosphere at cloud level according to their wave speeds. abstract: This paper gives a thorough examination of the literature of self-priming centrifugal chemical pumps, focusing on their design, operational principles, and applications in various industries. abstract: Compound climate extremes pose an increasingly severe threat to our societies, ecosystems, and economies under climate change. abstract: Magnetic null points define the magnetic field topology in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres, and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. abstract: Taylor bubble flows with nanoparticle suspensions are regularly encountered in non-isothermal chemical synthesis and microfluidics. title: The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf stabilized three adjacent ice sheets during the last glacial period
abstract: Global ice volume peaked between ~26,500 and 19,000 years ago and resulted in the Laurentide, Innuitian and Greenland ice sheets coalescing in Baffin Bay, a semi-enclosed basin between Greenland and Canada. However, the configuration of their marine terminating margins, which help establish the boundary conditions and sensitivity to processes that govern ice-sheet retreat, remains unclear. abstract: Abstract We quantify the spatial pattern (“fingerprint”) of sea-level rise caused by mass loss from the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets and from glaciers worldwide through 2100. Using ensembles of ice-sheet and glacier mass-balance projections and gravitational, rotational, and deformational sea-level modeling, we calculate normalized sea-level fingerprints and their impacts on Small Island Developing States. title: Plankton Ecology in the Philippines: Diversity, Dynamics, and Ecological Significance Across Tropical Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
abstract: Plankton communities in the Philippines occupy a critical ecological position in one of the world's most biologically diverse marine regions. Situated within the Coral Triangle and traversed by the Western Pacific Warm Pool, Philippine waters support extraordinary phytoplankton and zooplankton assemblages that regulate primary production, mediate carbon fluxes, and sustain the productivity of pelagic and coastal fisheries. title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth's Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. title: Ancient terrestrial forests reborn as modern marine ecosystems under shifting sea levels
abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise and coastal erosion can submerge terrestrial carbon-rich landscapes, yet the ecological fate and climate significance of such relict coastal carbon deposits remain largely unknown. We report the discovery of submerged tropical peat reefs in the shallow coastal waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique; a legacy of ancient coastal forests now transformed into benthic marine habitats. abstract: Abstract Deep-sea corals (DSC) are ecologically important, yet their microbiomes’ composition, structure, and host specificity remain largely unresolved in the South Atlantic, especially for octocorals. Here, we provide a comprehensive characterisation of DSC microbiomes, spanning Hexacorallia (Desmophyllum pertusum, Solenosmilia variabilis) and Octocorallia (Candidella imbricata, three Malacalcyonacea species), collected at ∼710 m depth in the Campos Basin, an active oil- and gas-producing region. title: Integrating Strategic Environmental Assessment into Regional Development Planning for Sustainable Development in Bireuen Regency
abstract: Regional planning in Bireuen has to respond to basic-service needs while also dealing with pressure on watersheds, forested land, and areas exposed to hydro-meteorological hazards. This paper examines how far the 2025-2029 Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is carried into the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (Indonesian term: Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Daerah/RPJMD), rather than remaining a separate compliance document. title: Sustained release of beneficial microorganisms for corals from alginate beads under marine conditions
abstract: AIM: Coral reefs support more than one-third of the global marine biodiversity, but global stressors have negatively impacted their health by disrupting fragile microbial partnerships, leading to widespread mass bleaching events. To address this issue, the use of beneficial microorganisms for coral (BMCs) has been shown to enhance coral resilience. In this study, we evaluated the potential of alginate beads as a delivery method for BMCs underwater. abstract: Abstract. Coastal marine environments are hot spots in the global marine silicon (Si) cycle. Dissolved silicate (DSi) is an essential macronutrient for diatoms, which often dominate primary productivity in temporal coastal seas and constitute a key food source for grazers. Even though benthic release of DSi influences the ecology of coastal marine areas, direct rate measurements of DSi mobilisation remain scarce. Natural radioactivity and elemental associations in coastal sediments of the Sudanese Red Sea
abstract: Background Natural radioactivity in coastal and marine sediments represents an important component of environmental radiation exposure assessment and serves as a valuable indicator of geological provenance, sediment transport processes, and ecological radiological safety. Marine sediments accumulate naturally occurring radionuclides through weathering of terrestrial rocks, fluvial transport, atmospheric deposition, biogenic accumulation, and marine geochemical redistribution. title: Antarctic marine-based ice destabilized when warming outpaces solid-Earth feedbacks
abstract: The Antarctic Ice Sheet is expected to be the largest contributor to sea-level rise over the coming centuries. Previous equilibrium ice-sheet simulations have suggested that this is due to crossing a bifurcation point associated with marine ice-sheet instability. Here we investigate whether sectors vulnerable to this instability can undergo rate-induced tipping, whereby rapid forcing and slow bedrock uplift trigger self-sustained retreat before the bifurcation point is reached. title: Survival and divergence of Arctic endemic cod species during 50,000 years of climate change
abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000-12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod (Arctogadus glacialis) and polar cod (Boreogadus saida), lived at 87-89 °N ~ 48,000-35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. title: Marine Protected Areas for Europe (MPA Europe)
abstract: The MPA Europe project will map the optimal locations for Marine Protected Areas (MPA) in European seas using measures covering the range of biodiversity from species to ecosystems, including habitats. The contribution of these measures to carbon storage will be quantified and mapped. The top 10% and 30% of the area that includes most species, habitats, and ecosystems, and maximises blue carbon benefits, will be prioritised as an MPA network. title: An Ecosystem-Based Marine Spatial Planning Approach for Sustainable Natural Resources Management in the Bangladesh Delta
abstract: Despite the establishment of maritime boundaries with Myanmar (2012) and India (2014), which secured sovereign rights over approximately 118,813 km² of the Bay of Bengal, marine space is still managed on a sector-by-sector basis, and no marine spatial plan has been prepared. This study identifies significant ecological, economic, and cultural areas within Bangladesh's maritime zone, and proposes a framework for the blue economy and develops an ecosystem-based model of marine spatial planning (MSP). abstract: Abstract. To assess the long-term interaction between sea ice conditions and Arctic mixed-phase cloud (MPC) properties, fourteen winter seasons of observations from the North Slope of Alaska are analysed. MPC properties are set into context with sea ice conditions by determining the sea ice sectors which are most relevant to interact with the observed clouds. abstract: This study aims to explore ecological phenomena in Rifqi Farizi’s novel Into the Beneath through the framework of Greg Garrard’s ecocriticism. The research focuses on identifying and analyzing the representation of five key ecological categories: pollution, apocalypse, dwelling, animals, and earth. abstract: Abstract. Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth’s ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. abstract: Sea-level rise may substantially reduce the dry space available on sandy beaches, although its effects depend strongly on local beach characteristics. This study evaluates the residual spatial functionality of five beaches in southern Spain using two normalized indicators: residual available surface area (FA) and residual available beach width (FW). abstract: Abstract Background Plasmodium vivax antimalarial resistance remains an important but understudied challenge in Southeast Asia. Although several molecular polymorphisms have been investigated as potential markers of antimalarial resistance, the available evidence remains scarce and fragmented, particularly regarding their associations with phenotypic drug susceptibility and clinical treatment outcomes. abstract: Coastal geomorphological maps generated in a GIS context in Naples Bay and the Cilento area are presented here to establish a current geomorphological framework for these two sectors of the Eastern Tyrrhenian margin. While sedimentary processes have dominated the geological evolution of the Cilento area, volcanic processes have dominated Naples Bay. abstract: Previous studies show that two promising technologies can increase recruitment probability and survival: (i) helix recesses for entraining coral larvae and (ii) night-time feeding lights for improving subsequent survival. abstract: Southeast Asia has expanded renewable electricity rapidly, yet a rising renewable share does not necessarily indicate an absolute retreat of fossil generation. title: When the lights come on: The hidden carbon cost of a brightening world
abstract: Abstract Nighttime satellite imagery has long served as a proxy for human development, equating light with progress and darkness with poverty. Here, we argue that this framing obscures a critical climate reality: the world's darkest regions, dominated by smallholder agriculture across central Africa, Southeast Asia, and the remote tropics, are simultaneously low‐emission zones and active carbon sinks, a dual function overlooked by Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), national Paris Agreement pledges for greenhouse gas reductions. abstract: This study examines the association between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure and corporate financial performance (FP), and further explores whether organizational slack (OS) moderates this relationship. Using a quantitative approach, with panel data from 278 publicly listed companies across six Southeast Asian countries. title: Baltic Sea sediment bacterial communities show asymmetric and incomplete recovery after reciprocal temperature change translocation
abstract: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. abstract: El artículo aborda la gestión urbana de la recolección de residuos en ciudades turísticas caracterizadas por una marcada variabilidad estacional de la demanda, tomando al Partido de Pinamar, provincia de Buenos Aires, como caso de estudio. El objetivo es desarrollar una propuesta metodológico-operativa para el análisis y la gestión del servicio mediante la integración de variables territoriales, temporales y operativas. abstract: Coastal tourism holds tremendous development potential, yet faces a critical paradox under the experience economy: while demand grows, inadequate tourist experiences increasingly constrain its sustainable development. This study selects Qingdao as a representative coastal destination and integrates online travelogue analysis, affective semantic processing, and GIS techniques to examine tourists’ spatiotemporal trajectories and emotional dynamics, informing improvements in the tourist experience. abstract: Abstract Ocean warming is altering abiotic environments and biotic interactions experienced by marine organisms, where sensitive early developmental windows occur in biologically complex seawater communities. The impact of these interactions on developmental processes and fitness in hosts is not well understood, but likely contingent on the establishment of a host-associated microbiome. title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. abstract: Global climate change and sea-level rise have intensified tropical cyclone–induced wind–surge compound risks, while rapid county-scale risk assessment remains difficult without field investigations. abstract: The coral microbiome is believed to play a crucial role in sustaining corals and enabling adaptation to perturbations. A ubiquitous group of coral-associated bacteria, known as Endozoicomonas, are hypothesized to provide essential metabolites to corals, although detailed dynamics of the interactions between host and microbe are poorly understood. abstract: Abstract The aim of this study is to test whether four marine gastrotrich species shared between the North Sea and the Mediterranean Sea represent single, pan-European taxa or instead comprise hidden, genetically structured lineages. Multi-predatory feeding aggregations in the Norwegian Sea: prevalence and ecological importance
abstract: Multi-predatory feeding aggregations (MPFAs) occur when several predator species concurrently exploit shared, spatially and temporally aggregated prey. Although MPFAs are well described in some marine ecosystems, their prevalence in the Norwegian Sea has historically been underestimated. Here, we synthesize existing biological, acoustic, visual and behavioural evidence to reinterpret classical predator-prey observations through the lens of MPFAs. abstract: Donomulyo Subdistrict in Malang Regency is characterized by complex hill–coastal terrain that is increasingly pressured by tourism development, making it highly prone to landslides. abstract: Associations between fish and benthic habitats are shaped by structural complexity, resource availability, and positioning within the larger seascape. In the remote Gulf of Carpentaria in northern Australia, there is very little scientific information on how fish communities interact with their habitats within a heterogeneous seascape, despite their ecological and cultural value. abstract: Wildfires are a growing environmental and socio-economic threat driven by climate change and land abandonment. abstract: Climate change and other anthropogenic pressures are rapidly reshaping marine ecosystems, altering prey availability and predator interactions. abstract: Abstract Microeukaryotic communities in brackish coastal ecosystems are structured by complex interactions between environmental conditions and habitat heterogeneity. This study examines how moderate salinity levels (ranging from freshwater to salinity 6) and habitat type (water column, sediment, and biofilm) influence microeukaryotic diversity and community composition in shallow coastal waters of the Gulf of Finland, the Baltic Sea. title: Fossil shark teeth record a microscale pathway for ferromanganese oxide nucleation and Li–Ni enrichment in deep-sea biogenic substrates
abstract: Abstract Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are major reservoirs of critical metals considered essential for a low-carbon economy, yet the mechanisms governing their initial formation remain poorly documented. title: Interactions between multi-species marine predator aggregations and the energy landscape
abstract: Multi-species predator aggregations can be found in both coastal and pelagic ecosystems, forming for both foraging and refuging (resting) purposes. The energy landscape represents the power costs required to move through or reside within a habitat. As species may differ in their morphology, buoyancy and length, there may be species-specific heterogeneity in their energy landscapes. Here, we highlight how the energy landscape may influence the small-scale distribution of predators within an aggregation and potentially their ability to forage. title: Marine-Derived Antimitotic Potential of Lombok Fucus vesiculosus: Dose-Dependent Cleavage Arrest in Diadema antillarum Embryos
abstract: Brown macroalgae are increasingly investigated as sources of antiproliferative metabolites, but phenotypic evidence linking crude algal extracts to stage-specific mitotic disruption remains limited. This study re-evaluates an exploratory laboratory experiment examining the effect of an ethanol extract of brown alga identified as Fucus vesiculosus from Lombok coastal waters on early development of the sea urchin Diadema antillarum. title: Multiscale feeding ground fidelity in a migratory marine predator revealed by integrating satellite telemetry and stable isotopes
abstract: Marine megafauna are considered ecosystem sentinels because their distribution and demography reflect variations in prey availability and ocean productivity. Fidelity to feeding areas can therefore serve as an indicator of the long-term ecological importance and productivity of particular regions. However, assessing feeding ground fidelity in vast, open-ocean environments remains challenging, as feeding habitats are spatially diffuse and dynamic, and direct observational data are rare. title: Fungi are overlooked dimethylsulfoniopropionate degraders in marine environments
abstract: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a key marine organosulfur compound, whose microbial catabolism is critical to global sulfur cycling and is the major source of the climate-active gas dimethyl sulfide (DMS). Research has focused on bacterial and algal DMSP catabolism, potentially overlooking the importance of fungi. Here, we vastly extend the known diversity of fungi that cleave DMSP to DMS, showing that many lacked known DMSP lyases, and Pezizomycotina members were most active. title: Evaluating the efficiency of biodiesel production from marine microbial consortium
abstract: A photosynthetic marine microalgae consortium (PMMC) was evaluated as a biodiesel feedstock, cultivated in BG-11 medium prepared with distilled water (PMMCDW) and seawater (PMMCSW), yielding final biomass concentrations of 5.17 g/L and 5.26 g/L, respectively. Chitosan-assisted harvesting was optimized via Response Surface Methodology, yielding peak efficiencies of 96.3% for PMMCDW (pH 5.5, 0.5 mL chitosan, 60 min) and 89.8% for PMMCSW (pH 3, 0.5 mL chitosan, 35 min). title: Public perceptions and (lack of) support for mitigation of artificial light at night in coastal cities
abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is an expanding environmental pressure in urban areas, yet effective mitigation depends on public support. We investigated how residents of two Chilean coastal cities perceive ALAN, its impacts and potential mitigation measures. Respondents demonstrated asymmetric environmental literacy, recognising the societal benefits of lighting while showing limited awareness of its ecological consequences, particularly for coastal-marine ecosystems. title: Different paths, same destination: similar benthic nitrogen cycling sustained by distinct biogeochemical mechanisms in artificialized coastal systems
abstract: Abstract. Human activities are increasingly affecting coastal ecosystems, with shoreline stabilization structures becoming a prevalent response to sea-level rise and extreme climatic events. While these structures aim to protect coastal communities and infrastructures, their effects on ecosystem functioning, and particularly nitrogen cycling and fixed-nitrogen loss processes such as denitrification, remain poorly understood. title: Transoceanic migration of a female tiger shark (Galeocerdo cuvier) demonstrates connectivity in the southern Atlantic
abstract: Abstract The tiger shark is a highly migratory apex predator with distinct populations in the Atlantic and Indo-Pacific regions. Regional analyses in the western Atlantic Ocean have revealed additional genetic differentiation between northern (Caribbean) and southern (Brazilian) populations, particularly in maternally inherited mitochondrial DNA. The eastern Atlantic Ocean, however, remains understudied, leaving connectivity between American and African populations unresolved. title: Evidence for potential top-down control of meso- and micro-copepods during jellyfish blooms revealed by eDNA metabarcoding
abstract: The limitation of traditional survey methods has catalyzed the rapid development and widespread application of eDNA metabarcoding. By collecting water samples from coastal waters off the Shandong Peninsula across the key blooming phase (May and August) of jellyfish, this study reveals the environmental drivers of jellyfish blooms and the potential top-down control exerted by jellyfish on meso- and micro-copepods. title: Surface complexity enhances early invertebrate recruitment on novel substrates for coral reef restoration
abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs are increasingly threatened by climate change and local anthropogenic stressors, prompting the development of artificial substrates for reef restoration. Although substrate material is often considered a key design variable, the relative influence of surface topography on early benthic colonization remains insufficiently resolved. Objective: To evaluate the effects of experimental substrate material and surface topography on early benthic community assembly at Islote Zacatoso reef, Mexican Pacific. title: Bibliometric analysis and visualization of adenomyosis
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This bibliometric analysis systematically evaluated the research landscape, emerging trends, and key focus areas in adenomyosis to guide future research directions. DESIGN: Performance analysis combined with scientific mapping of global adenomyosis research literature. DATA SOURCES: Web of Science Core Collection (1980-2024). title: Population genetic structure and spring−summer spatial distribution of common minke whales (Balaenoptera acutorostrata) in feeding grounds and migratory corridors of the western North Pacific
abstract: Abstract Information on population genetic structure, movement, and distribution is fundamental for effective management of marine species. In the western North Pacific, the common minke whale faces both bycatch and commercial whaling, the latter having resumed in Japanese waters in 2019. In this study, we refined the population genetic structure and spring–summer spatial distribution of this species using 6196 genetic samples collected in feeding grounds and migratory corridors during 1994–2024. title: The near-T2T genome of the feather star Cenometra bella suggests potential evolutionary innovations and coral reef habitat tolerance
abstract: Abstract Background Crinoids are highly conservative echinoderms, retaining ancient features since the early Ordovician, making them classic "living fossils" invaluable for studying evolution and biodiversity. Their evolutionary stability is marked by minimal morphological changes, a sessile lifestyle, and exceptionally slow evolutionary rates, rendering them unique among marine groups. However, they have long lacked high-quality genomic resources, hindering insights into the genomic evolution of early echinoderm lineages. title: GIS-Based Land Suitability Assessment for Cultivation of Bananas and Robusta Coffee in Northern Uganda
abstract: Limited scholarly knowledge exists on land suitability for sustainable crop cultivation in tropical Africa. This study evaluated the physical and economic suitability of land for cultivating bananas (Musa spp) and robusta coffee (Coffea canephora) in northern Uganda. A cross-sectional design sampled 356 households. title: Ecophysiology of the cosmopolitan nitrite-oxidising genus Candidatus Nitromaricola
abstract: The majority of marine nitrite-oxidising bacteria (NOB) belong to three uncultured genera within the Nitrospinaceae family and thus the ecophysiology of these main nitrate producing microorganisms in the ocean remains poorly resolved. Here, we report on the environmental characterization of one of these genera, which we name Candidatus Nitromaricola. A single species within this genus, Candidatus Nitromaricola pontica, comprises >95% of the nitrite-oxidising community in the permanently stratified Black Sea. institutions: Max Planck Institute for Marine Microbiology

title: Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment based on submarine active faults and their possible interactions in the sea of Japan
abstract: Abstract The Sea of Japan coastal areas have experienced tsunami damage caused by submarine active seismic faults. Large uncertainties remain regarding seismic activity of these faults and the following tsunami. Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment (PTRA) enables the evaluation of tsunami risk accounting for such uncertainties. In this study, the tsunami risks of a thermal power plant located on the Sea of Japan coast were evaluated using the PTRA based on submarine active faults, including coupled faults, across the Sea of Japan. institutions: International Research Institute of Disaster Science, Tohoku University

title: Assessment of disinfectant performance against fish-pathogenic bacteria in planktonic and biofilm states
abstract: Disinfecting fish farming equipment and facility surfaces with disinfectant is one of the primary biosafety measures to prevent disease introduction and transmission. However, the actual efficacy of approved disinfectants against fish-pathogenic bacteria and especially their biofilms remain largely undocumented. Six selected disinfectants were evaluated against seven common disease-causing bacteria and their biofilms. title: Marine radar reveals novel group foraging patterns in pelagic seabirds
abstract: Many seabirds are known to frequently feed within multi-specific feeding flocks. These aggregations bring facilitation to prey access as well as potential exacerbated competition. Once a feeding opportunity is found, birds rapidly aggregate to it through processes known as local enhancement. At a larger scale, seabirds may distribute themselves forming patterns such as rakes or clusters, which are thought to increase the probability to cue on other foragers. title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. title: Clinical Outcomes of Partial Injection Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Superficial Non‐ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors (With Video)
abstract: Objectives: Although endoscopic resection is widely performed for superficial non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors (SNADETs), conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (CEMR) may be associated with suboptimal complete resection rates. Partial injection underwater EMR (PI-UEMR) has been proposed to improve the visualization of distal lesion margins and facilitate en bloc resection. title: Reef-scale environmental mosaics shape coral physiological and microbial signatures of resilience
abstract: Abstract Environmental variability shapes coral performance, yet its role in structuring host physiology and microbiome composition across reef habitats remains unresolved. We investigated six geomorphologically distinct sites across Heron Island, southern Great Barrier Reef, as a natural laboratory to test how life-long exposure to distinct environmental regimes influences the holobiont of the coral Pocillopora damicornis. abstract: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). title: Increases in foraging performance of humpback whales in multi-predator feeding aggregations with California sea lions
abstract: Marine predators frequently form ephemeral multi-predator feeding aggregations around dense prey patches, yet the mechanisms and outcomes of these dynamic events remain poorly resolved. We quantified how California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) presence influenced humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) foraging using 46 multi-sensor video tags (mean duration: 7.4 ± 7.1 h) deployed on fish-feeding whales in Monterey Bay, California, USA (2014-2023). abstract: Eutrophication-driven sediment deterioration is a critical issue in enclosed coastal bays. A ceramic material composed of humic organic acids and calcium carbonate mesoscopic crystals has been developed for in-situ sediment remediation, generating high-alkaline environments that promote oxidative degradation of organic matter. title: Changes in species composition of South Georgia seabirds and mammals 1985–2023: decrease in opportunities for local enhancement?
abstract: Seabirds cue into other birds and marine mammals to amplify their foraging success. Consequently, changes to the community (e.g. as the climate warms) can impact foraging success and potentially fitness. For example, flying birds that use groups of seals or penguins as cues might decline if the seal or penguin population declines, owing to fewer opportunities for positive foraging associations with one another. title: Assessment of the Urban Storm Water Drainage System of Kakinada Smart City Using GIS and EPA SWMM under Design Storm
abstract: Rapid urbanization, encroachment on natural drainage channels and intense rainfall have made flooding a recurrent problem in Kakinada Smart City, a low-lying coastal city in Andhra Pradesh, India. This study evaluates the performance of the city's storm water drainage network and proposes modifications to reduce flooding. Intensity–Duration–Frequency (IDF) curves were derived from rainfall records distribution, and design storms were generated with the Alternating Block Method. abstract: ABSTRACT Antibiotic residues, particularly fluoroquinolones, increasingly co‐occur with salinity fluctuations in coastal areas, yet their combined effects on marine bivalves remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the interactive impact of enrofloxacin (ENR; 5 and 500 ng/L) and salinity (30 and 40 PSU) on the marine bivalve Ruditapes philippinarum , using an integrative biomarker approach to assess metabolic, oxidative, and cellular responses. abstract: Environmental changes are extensively reported in the literature, sometimes leading to long-term trends. This study focuses on Arcachon Bay, a coastal lagoon in SW France, which has been the scene of several environmental modifications over the past decades, including a severe decline of seagrass meadows and changes in its physicochemical features. title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission-driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. title: Impact of real‐time digital dashboard on birth outcomes in high‐volume tertiary center: A retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Objective This study evaluates the impact of implementing a real‐time intrapartum digital monitoring dashboard on labor progression and birth outcomes in a high‐resource high‐volume tertiary care delivery ward. Study Design This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a university‐affiliated medical center. title: Polar Seabed Observation Systems reveal winter diel rhythms and environmental drivers of euphausiids in Great Wall Bay, Antarctic Peninsula
abstract: The adaptive diel rhythm strategies of euphausiids during wintertime in the Southern Ocean surrounding the Antarctic continent remain poorly documented. To elucidate this knowledge gap, an in situ benthic observation campaign was conducted via the Polar Seabed Observation Systems (PSOS) in June 2023, targeting the Great Wall Bay (Antarctic Peninsula) to quantify winter diel activity patterns of euphausiids. abstract: Introduction During winter 2025/2026, the Baltic Sea experienced a pronounced basin-wide sea-level depression, with regional sea surface height (SSH) anomalies reaching approximately −60 cm or lower. We examine its atmospheric forcing, associated volume changes and subsequent hydrographic conditions. Methods We combine Copernicus Marine SSH, ERA5 atmospheric fields, Landsort/Landsort–Norra observations, modelled net transport across a Kattegat section, and CTD, Argo and glider measurements. title: Occurrence and Ingestion of Plastic Particles in Marine Fish from Togolese Coast
abstract: The increase in plastic production towards the end of the Second World War, combined with inadequate plastic waste management, has contributed to the contamination of marine ecosystems. The ingestion of plastic particles measuring less than 5 mm, known as microplastics, by marine organisms has been documented. The aim of this study was to demonstrate that plastic particles can ultimately enter the human food supply. title: Vulnerability of Small-Scale Fisheries to Potential Storm Surge in North Borneo Island, Malaysia
abstract: Abstract Small-scale fishers were crucial for providing fresh seafood and contributing to the protein intake of coastal communities. They typically used traditional fishing methods and ventured out to the sea in small boats, often working alone or with a few family members. Despite their vital contribution to the community, small-scale fishers faced numerous challenges and were highly exposed to the effects of climate change. title: York-Tank: A Degradation-Aware and Difficulty-Stratified Stereo Dataset for Underwater Visual SLAM
abstract: Coupled visual degradations in underwater recordings make it difficult to relate simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) performance changes to specific factors and their severity. We present York-Tank, which is a controlled stereo dataset combining dominant-factor sequence design with within-factor severity stratification. title: Blood cockle farming on the east coast of Sumatra: a legal and monopoly analysis
abstract: Blood cockle (Anadara granosa) farming has become one of the most economically important coastal aquaculture activities on the east coast of Sumatra, Indonesia. Despite its significant contribution to local livelihoods, exports, and regional economic growth, the rapid expansion of the industry has generated increasing concerns regarding coastal governance, legal certainty, and market concentration. abstract: Abstract Bacteria of the family Endozoicomonadaceae are widely associated with marine animals, yet their in situ metabolism remains mostly unknown. Genomic studies suggest that members of this family engage in extensive metabolic exchange with their hosts, ranging from nutrient provision in mutualistic sponge and coral symbioses to dependence on host metabolites like lipids in parasitic associations. abstract: Marine actinomycetes represent a promising source of biologically active natural pigments. In the present study, isolate MOE3, recovered from mangrove sediment along the Egyptian Red Sea coast, was provisionally assigned to Streptomyces lateritius based on partial 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, showing approximately 99% sequence similarity to closely related Streptomyces taxa. abstract: Abstract Hydrothermal systems at ultraslow‐spreading ridges are poorly understood, especially where thick sediments overlay detachment faults. The International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 403 obtained the longest sediment record in Atlantic‐Arctic ultraslow‐spreading systems, reaching ∼628 m below the seafloor. title: Revealing potential Atlantic salmon bycatch hotspots from pelagic fisheries landings across the Northeast Atlantic
abstract: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) marine survival has declined markedly over the past five decades, leading to concerns about future population viability. While many studies have explored the impacts of stressors such as climate change and predation, less is known about bycatch from pelagic fisheries targeting finfish species. This study, focused on the first few months of the salmon marine migration period, narrows down the space-time domains where pelagic fisheries bycatch is most likely to occur. abstract: Background: FVKVEVLPQ from Arbacia lixula has previously been studied computationally in triple-negative breast cancer. abstract: Large-scale beach nourishment projects constructed adjacent to port breakwaters may produce spatially contrasting shoreline responses because wave transformation, sediment redistribution, and structural effects act simultaneously. This study presents an empirical analysis of short-term shoreline evolution at a large artificially nourished beach constructed next to the eastern breakwater of the Vistula Spit Channel in the South Baltic Sea. abstract: Coastal cities have shifted from outward expansion to reworking the housing stock they already hold, and renewing aging communities has become harder to manage as a result. abstract: As built-up expansion in the Syrian coastal mountainous areas intensifies, its environmental impacts are becoming increasingly severe. Existing research, however, offers limited quantitative evidence to elucidate the dynamics of this phenomenon. This study addresses this gap by employing mixed-method techniques at the district level of Safita. abstract: Abstract Coral white syndrome (WS) is a widespread condition characterized by tissue loss and skeletal exposure, with multiple bacterial pathogens—particularly Vibrio species—implicated in its etiology. abstract: This qualitative study evaluates Thailand’s Blue Swimming Crab Bank Expansion Project against five international criteria for sustainable community-based conservation: measurable ecological impact, community participation, scientific credibility, knowledge transfer, and policy alignment. title: Effective number of communities reveals extent of biodiversity change – a cross-organism analysis in the Wadden Sea
abstract: Biodiversity changes in ecosystems worldwide, but assessing the true magnitude of this transformation requires the analysis of multiple dimensions of compositional change. abstract: Some conservation programs keep turtles temporarily under human care with the intention of releasing them later to strengthen wild populations. Historically, researchers have questioned whether key survival behaviours might be lost during captive-raising, potentially reducing post-release survivability. Yet no published studies have examined the in-water behaviour of captive-raised turtles in a way that allows comparison with wild conspecifics – an important gap for the critically endangered hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata). title: Liposome supplementation enhances host metabolism in a model symbiotic cnidarian
abstract: Abstract Stable cnidarian–dinoflagellate symbioses provide the trophic foundation of coral reef ecosystems. Understanding nutrient exchange underpinning this symbiosis, and the need for interventions to improve coral health via aquaculture, grow increasingly urgent as reefs face accelerating threats from climate change. Liposomes and lipid nanoparticles, widely used as delivery vehicles in biomedical science, are emerging as promising tools to supplement coral nutrition. abstract: ABSTRACT Peptide bond hydrolysis is essential to biology, yet the kinetic stability of amide bonds makes efficient and selective artificial proteolysis challenging. title: Public willingness to pay for hybrid blue-green infrastructure: Evidence from the Clyde and Forth Estuaries, Scotland
abstract: Nature-based solutions are increasingly recognised as climate-resilient strategies for coastal climate adaptation. This study estimates public willingness to pay (WTP) for the creation of hybrid blue-green infrastructure in place of vacant and derelict land in the Clyde and Forth estuaries, using a contingent valuation method with a payment card format. title: Reimagining the Dead Sea Scrolls: A Position Paper
abstract: The Dead Sea Scrolls are imagined as scrolls and cataloged as manuscripts but consist, for the most part, of scattered and minuscule fragments. In this article, we will propose a new physical object-based ontology that takes the smallest indivisible units, i.e., the physical fragments, as the point of departure. title: Beyond the maximum gradient: a consecutive-threshold criterion for nitracline detection in the Northwestern Indian Ocean
abstract: Depth of the nitracline is an important indicator of the vertical distribution and availability of nitrate in the upper ocean. While the conventional definition of the nitracline as the depth of maximum nitrate gradient (dN/dz) has been widely accepted, this study introduces a complementary consecutive-gradient criterion to detect the onset of a sustained nitrate gradient zone. title: Exploring student biodiversity literacy in Indonesian coastal areas: implications for education for sustainable development
abstract: This study is driven by the degradation of Indonesia's coastal ecosystems, leading to a decline in biodiversity and increase disaster risk for coastal communities. Addressing this issue necessitates the engagement of multiple stakeholders, particularly educational institutions. This study aims to describe the profile of biodiversity literacy of high school students in coastal areas of Sumbawa Island, Indonesia, across cognitive, attitude, and behavioural dimensions and to discuss its relevance to Education for Sustainable Development (ESD). title: Mosques as Community-Based Vertical Evacuation Shelters in Tsunami-Prone Coastal Padang, Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia is among the most tsunami-prone countries in the world due to its location along active subduction zones. In coastal cities such as Padang, extremely short tsunami arrival times, high population exposure, and the limited distribution of purpose-built vertical evacuation shelters reveal a critical gap in socially embedded evacuation planning. This study examines the potential of mosques to serve as community-based vertical tsunami evacuation shelters in coastal Padang, focusing on spatial suitability, social legitimacy, and adaptive reuse within a local disaster risk reduction context

abstract: Abstract Biofouling continues to limit the performance of ultrafiltration membranes for oil–water separation, creating demand for materials that combine high flux, strong selectivity, and built-in antimicrobial activity. abstract: This study examines long-term temperature variability and future climate projections in Hatay Province, located along the Eastern Mediterranean coast of Türkiye. The aim is to evaluate historical temperature trends and assess future warming patterns by integrating homogenized observational records with CMIP6-based climate projections. abstract: Crop growth in relation to management parameters were studied in coastal areas of West Bengal. Resourcesat 2A L3 data was analyzed for vegetation index (NDVI). abstract: This quantitative classroom study examined changes in students' cognitive scores following a four-hour inquiry-based biology intervention using authentic molecular visualization resources (iCn3D and Protein Data Bank structures). abstract: Abstract Coastal internal tides are considered unpredictable: harmonic fits to depth‐varying baroclinic velocity explain little variance. We show the depth‐averaged coastal internal tide is predictable from astronomical forcing. title: Near real-time long-read eDNA sequencing reveals harmful algal bloom dynamics in the Indian River Lagoon
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) are increasingly impacting estuarine ecosystems, yet current microbial surveillance methods often focus on prokaryotic 16S rRNA profiles and overlook eukaryotic bloom-forming species. Here, we applied Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) MinION long-read sequencing targeting the 18S rRNA gene to characterize spatial and seasonal patterns of eukaryotic microbial communities in the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), a biologically diverse 251 km long estuary along Florida’s Atlantic coast. title: Variation patterns and ecological drivers of morphology in different body regions of fishes from the Northwest Pacific Ocean
abstract: Variation in fish body morphology represents an important aspect of phenotypic diversity and plays a fundamental role in understanding fish evolution and ecology. The complex oceanographic conditions of the Northwest Pacific Ocean create diverse selective pressures, making it an ideal system for studying how environmental variability shapes fish body morphology. abstract: Reporting dates do not identify claim payment times. We quantify a reporting-based payment-time assumption's effect on finite-horizon cash ruin in an idealized marine portfolio. title: Diversity and distribution of cryptobenthic fishes and their association with epibenthic fauna in a subtropical estuary
abstract: Abstract Cryptobenthic fishes (CF) are cryptic species that exhibit mimicry with their benthic environment and can be either detritivorous or zoobenthivorous. Few studies have examined the influence of epibenthic macrofauna on CF diversity. This study analyzed the colonization and spatiotemporal succession of CF and macrofauna in fish-specific autonomous reef monitoring structures (FARMS) at Paranaguá Estuarine Complex (Brazil). Farming is the primary mean of rural livelihoods in Bangladesh but agricultural land is slowly declining day by day. abstract: Abstract Genetic monitoring is central to the conservation of threatened species, particularly those with small and isolated populations, as reduced diversity can limit long-term survival and adaptive potential. Islands are ideal for examining these processes due to restricted gene flow and the enhanced effects of genetic drift and inbreeding. The Egyptian vulture ( Neophron percnopterus ), a long-lived species in global decline, serves as a model for examining how insularity shapes genetic diversity and structure. abstract: This study reports a screening-level radiological assessment of drinking water sources – sachet water, tap water, borehole water and river water – across the Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions of Ghana. Activity concentrations of 226 Ra and 228 Ra were measured by high-purity germanium (HPGe) gamma spectrometry in 244 samples collected over one dry and one wet season, and screening-level committed effective doses were estimated for adult consumers. abstract: Small objects in underwater and traffic-sign images often have weak boundaries and low contrast. Downsampling and multi-scale fusion can further weaken the features needed to detect them. abstract: This study evaluated the metal content, fatty acid composition, and health risks of Mediterranean mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis) collected over 8 months from the Kefken coast. As a transition zone between the Black Sea and Marmara Sea, this site is critical for monitoring nutritional quality and regional pollutants. title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China
abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. abstract: The decline of seagrass meadows is a continuing global concern, and seed‐based restoration provides a scalable approach to recovering lost and degraded meadows. title: Chronic exposure to Salton Sea aerosols elicits pulmonary inflammation and shifts in murine lung and fecal microbiome diversity
abstract: Abstract Lung disease is rampant around the Salton Sea, California’s largest inland lake and a major source of airborne particulates. To examine root causes of pulmonary disease, we investigated the exposure impacts of spatiotemporal variation in aerosols collected near the Salton Sea on lung and fecal microbiomes. title: Petroleum fiscal regimes and contractor returns: empirical analysis of the North Sea and Gulf of Guinea
abstract: Petroleum fiscal regimes are institutions through which resource rents, investment risks, public revenues, and domestic economic opportunities are allocated among states, firms, and producing societies. Yet they are often assessed primarily through tax burdens and contractor returns. This study develops a mechanism-based framework that distinguishes direct production-cost effects, cash-flow redistribution, timing-related liquidity effects, and their wider governance and development implications. abstract: Abstract Past variability of oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) provides key insights into future ocean deoxygenation. abstract: Objective: This study aimed to comparatively evaluate the growth performance and total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) removal efficiency of two indigenous marine cyanobacterial isolates, Anabaena spp. and Oscillatoria acuta, under different initial ammonia concentrations, and to identify the most effective isolate for potential application in biological treatment of ammonia-contaminated saline waters. abstract: Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation is widely promoted for rice cultivation to reduce water use and enhance water productivity. title: Functional, communicative, and critical health literacy and stroke prevention behaviors among hypertensive patients in a Bugis Coastal Community, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Health literacy plays an important role in hypertension management and stroke prevention; however, conventional health literacy assessment approaches often overlook sociocultural contexts that shape health-related decision-making in culturally cohesive communities. This study assessed Functional, Communicative, and Critical (FCC) Health Literacy related to stroke prevention among hypertensive patients in a Bugis coastal community in Indonesia using a culturally contextualized approach informed by the Puangrimaggalatung framework. abstract: Abstract Protozoan parasites in the genus Perkinsus proliferate within marine mollusc hosts through schizogony to produce intracellular daughter cells. This proliferation of P. olseni PRA-181 requires glycine betaine (GB) derived from host molluscs. title: Mapping uncertainty. Defining spatial accuracy of WWI historical sources in the Asiago Plateau (NE Italy)
abstract: During World War I (WWI), the landscapes of the Venetian Prealps were extensively transformed by the construction of defensive lines and field fortifications. Historical sources (aerial photographs, military cartography, ground photos, panoramic drawings, and written documents) preserve evidence and memory of these changes and enable the reconstruction of the spatial organization of past military systems through Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The digitization of such sources provides an effective means to locate military features that are no longer visible in the present-day landscape.

abstract: Rapid coastal urbanization increases exposure to multiple hazards while intensifying competition for land essential for safe emergency refuge. This paper proposes a reproducible decision-support framework for planning Disaster Prevention and Relief Accessible Green Spaces (DPRAGS). title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors.

abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are among the most carbon-rich coastal ecosystems, storing substantial amounts of carbon in biomass and sediments. The Gambesi mangrove forest, located on the southern coast of Ternate Island, North Maluku, Indonesia, plays an important ecological role in coastal protection, biodiversity support, and climate change mitigation, yet it faces mounting anthropogenic pressure from land conversion, household waste, and coastal abrasion. abstract: Abstract A new species of Doliocarpus (Dilleniaceae) endemic to the Brazilian Atlantic Forest is described. title: Wetland plant biodiversity in China: a scoping evidence map linking ecosystem services, SDGs, and governance instruments
abstract: Wetlands are biodiversity hotspots and critical nature-based solutions for water purification, climate regulation, and flood and coastal risk reduction, yet they remain among the world’s most threatened ecosystems. This scoping review synthesized 2,482 China-focused studies published between 2001 and 2026 to examine how wetland plant biodiversity supports ecosystem services and informs governance and United Nations. abstract: Oceanographic changes due to carbon dioxide emissions have complex and varied impacts on marine calcifying taxa. title: The geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus Gray, 1838 (Mammalia, Chiroptera) in Guatemala, including the first record of N. lanatus Tejedor, 2005
abstract: We document the first confirmed record of Natalus lanatus from Guatemala, increasing the national bat fauna to 107 species, and present the first country-level synthesis of the geographic and elevational distribution of the genus Natalus . Morphological analyses of N. lanatus ( n = 8) and N. mexicanus ( n = 8) show clear differentiation, with the first two FAMD dimensions explaining 61% of total variance. Voucher-based records further show elevational segregation, with N. lanatus occurring at 731–2,573 m and N. mexicanus from near sea level to 523 m.
institutions: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala

title: Assessment of air pollution toxicity in urban environments in Barcelona, Spain, using a mobile air-liquid interface system
abstract: Toxicity of airborne particles and gases was analyzed using a mobile air-liquid interface (ALI) exposure system at a busy harbor and an urban background site in Barcelona, Spain. Toxic effects were assessed in human A549 cells exposed directly to urban air by measuring lactate dehydrogenase release. Simultaneously, air quality measurements were conducted to monitor particle and gas concentrations. title: Seaweed-derived biostimulants differentially enhance growth, nutritional composition, antioxidant capacity, and sensory quality of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa
abstract: Abstract Seaweed-derived biostimulants offer a promising strategy to enhance the productivity and functional quality of edible seaweeds. This study evaluated the effects of aqueous extracts from Halymenia sp., Halimeda sp., Sargassum sp., Kappaphycus sp., and Gracilaria sp. on the growth, biochemical composition, nutritional quality, antioxidant properties, and sensory acceptance of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa under controlled 35-day laboratory culture conditions. institutions: National Pingtung University of Science and Technology

title: Urban Decay: Fungal Urbanism in Jeff VanderMeer’s Ambergris
abstract: Abstract “Next time you walk through a forest, look down. A city lies under your feet,” writes Anna Tsing. In metaphorizing mycorrhizal networks as cities, Tsing entangles the urban with the fungal to visualize an interstitial city that is typically beneath human notice yet exerts nonhuman agency over the environment. journal: ISLE Interdisciplinary Studies in Literature and Environment

title: Implementasi Radio LoRa dengan Enkripsi Caesar Cipher sebagai Proof-of-Concept Komunikasi Data Sistem Monitoring dan Kendali Latihan Militer
abstract: Penelitian ini membahas implementasi teknologi LoRa dan metode enkripsi Caesar Cipher pada sistem monitoring dan kendali peledakan untuk keperluan latihan militer. Sistem komunikasi radio konvensional yang umum digunakan saat ini memiliki keterbatasan pada jangkauan, rentan terhadap gangguan frekuensi, dan memiliki risiko penyadapan, sehingga diperlukan teknologi alternatif yang andal dan aman. title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. title: Agonistic interactions and vocalizations among Procellariiformes in multi-species feeding aggregations, observed through bird-borne cameras
abstract: Marine predators frequently aggregate at food sources, where interactions can range from cooperative group hunting to interference competition for resources. To investigate interactions at feeding aggregations among procellariiforms, we equipped wandering albatrosses Diomedea exulans with video cameras, collecting 43 hours of footage from 22 individuals. Cameras from eight birds recorded feeding aggregations, capturing a total of 62 minutes of footage (2.7% of observations). title: Phylogenetic Reconstruction of Cephalaspidea Using Multiple Datasets and Inference Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Cephalaspidea is a key group within the Heterobranchia characterized by high species diversity and broad ecological disparity, and it is widely studied in marine ecology and systematics. Previous studies have proposed a preliminary phylogenetic framework for Cephalaspidea using few sanger sequenced phylogenetic markers and transcriptome‐scale datasets. However, relationships among several lineages remain contentious, which may partly reflect sparse sampling of key taxa and differences in topological signal among markers, datasets and analytical assumptions. title: Haplotype tagging sheds light on speciation between two divergent cryptic species of the brown algae Ectocarpus
abstract: Understanding how genome-wide divergence translates to barriers to gene flow is a central question in speciation research, particularly in marine environments where interconnected habitats frequently accommodate cryptic diversity. Using linked-read whole-genome data from the brown alga Ectocarpus, we investigated genome-wide reproductive isolation between two cryptic brown algal species E. siliculosus and E. crouaniorum across replicated hybrid zones in Europe and Chile. title: Delineation of groundwater potential zones in Chalan Beel (inland wetland) for sustainable ecosystem in Lower Atrai River Basin NW Bangladesh
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in sustaining the ecological integrity and water security of the Chalan Beel, the largest inland wetland (5097 km2) in the Lower Atrai River Basin of northwestern Bangladesh. This study delineates groundwater potential zones (GWPZs) using an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) approach. title: Selective Hg2+ Detection Using an Aza-BODIPY-Derived NIR Fluorescence Sensor: Environmental and Biological Applications
abstract: Abstract Mercury contamination in natural environments poses severe threats to ecosystems and human health, emphasizing the urgent need for reliable Hg2+ detection methods. In this work, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent aza-BODIPY derivative (BT) was synthesized as a potential fluorescence sensor. BT exhibited dual colorimetric and “turn-on” NIR fluorometric responses toward Hg2+ in H2O:EtOH (3:7 v/v), achieving a detection limit of 1.7 ppb. The sensor displayed high selectivity through rapid BT–Hg2+ complexation, with reversible sensing enabled by the addition of potassium iodide (KI).

title: FECH negatively regulates protoporphyrin IX accumulation and shell coloration in the dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis
abstract: Shell color in mollusks, shaped by pigment synthesis and deposition, offers a readily observable natural trait. The dwarf surf clam Mulinia lateralis serves as an ideal bivalve model but has a uniform white shell, which limits its utility for genetic studies. In this study, we aimed to explore the feasibility of constructing a shell color‑based endogenous reporter by inducing pigment accumulation. title: Toxicogenetic profiling of an antifungal lawsone silver salt: in silico and in vitro analysis in 2D and 3D mammalian models
abstract: Abstract The development of novel metal-based antifungals requires rigorous characterization of their toxicological mechanisms to ensure patient safety. This study investigated the toxicogenetic profile and cellular interactions of lawsone silver salt (LSS), a compound with established activity against Sporothrix spp. and emerging multidrug-resistant pathogens. Antifungal efficacy was confirmed against planktonic Aspergillus fumigatus , Candida albicans , and C. auris (MIC 1.45–23.2 µM), with significant anti-biofilm activity against C. albicans (185.9 µM) and A. fumigatus (92.9 µM). title: Potential erosion risk assessment of Kanak stream basin (Sivas, Sarkisla) with the ICONA model
abstract: The rapid development of technology following the Industrial Revolution has increased human domination over nature. Erosion, which plays a critical role in the process of natural shaping of the earth, can accelerate over time because of improper utilization of the natural environment by humans. The main objective of this study is to determine the erosion susceptibility of the Kanak Creek Basin, one of the sub-basins in the upper reaches of the Kizilirmak River, using the ICONA model, whose main parameters are slope, lithology, land use and vegetation cover, and Geographic Information Systems (
