title: AN INFORMATION MODEL FOR ACCOUNTING-REGULATORY-OPERATIONAL DATA CONVERGENCE IN US SMALL-CARRIER TRUCKING
abstract: This study aims to conceptualize the distinctive accounting-information environment of American small-carrier trucking, where a single owner-operator or a management team of one or two persons typically manages freight movement, financial recording, tax compliance, and equipment tracking as an integrated activity. The study addresses a gap between accounting-information-system research, which generally treats operational technology and financial recording as separate but periodically integrated layers, and trucking operations research, which typically considers accounting an administrative fun

title: Solar resource assessment and performance forecasting of a utility-scale photovoltaic plant in Bhutan: A high-altitude Himalayan case study
abstract: High-altitude solar photovoltaic (PV) deployment can diversify electricity supply in hydropower-dominated Himalayan regions, particularly during the dry season. This study evaluates the technical feasibility, site suitability, solar resource, and forecast performance of a proposed utility-scale plant at Ladrong, Bhutan. The method integrates GIS terrain screening, slope and aspect classification, horizon and near-shading analysis, grid connectivity, and PVsyst simulation. title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry in Neurobiology: From Imaging to Proteomics
abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has emerged as a versatile approach for probing molecules with high selectivity and minimal perturbation. While applicable to diverse biomolecules, its use in protein studies has proven particularly powerful, especially in neurobiology, where precise molecular tools are essential. A key technology enabling such precision is genetic code expansion (GCE), which allows the incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAAs) bearing bioorthogonal handles into proteins. title: MONDE ·T: A database and interactive webserver for non‐standard amino acids and peptide components in the PDB
abstract: Non-standard amino acids (ncAAs) together with synthetic additions (like caps and linkers) are of wide interest for protein design and pharmaceutical optimization, as they can improve physicochemical properties and possibly reshape protein structure. Their inclusion in experimental structures has not been explored systematically. It remains elusive which components are those most impactful for protein design. institutions: Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology

title: Sistema automatizado para la producción sostenible de Pleurotus sp.
abstract: The cultivation of Pleurotus sp. offers an alternative to take advantage of lignocellulosic residues generated by agricultural activity and, at the same time, obtain a food of nutritional interest. In rural communities, one of the difficulties in maintaining production is the monitoring of variables such as temperature, humidity and CO₂ concentration, particularly when handling is carried out manually. title: Quantification of soil loss by using RUSLE model under different land use and land cover conditions in AKANYARU catchment in Rwanda
abstract: This study quantified annual soil loss across the Akanyaru Catchment (3,402 km², Rwanda) under four land use and land cover types forest, agriculture, residential, and bare soil using the RUSLE model integrated with GIS. The Rainfall erosivity (R) is derived from 20 years of daily rainfall data obtained from the NASA database. The Soil erodibility (K) used is from global soil texture data; slope length and steepness (LS) from a 30 m DEM; and cover management (C) from Landsat 8 NDVI. title: Shake-the-box measurements of vortex shedding and main coherent structures in a rectangular prism bluff body
abstract: This study presents a three-dimensional characterization of the wake behind a rectangular-cylinder bluff body using a time-resolved Tomographic Particle Image Velocimetry (Tomo-PIV) setup. The Shake-the-Box (STB) algorithm was used for Lagrangian particle tracking (LPT), enabling the reconstruction of volumetric velocity and pressure fields. Two chord-to-thickness ratio ( D / H ) orientations of the same geometry were tested: with its short side facing the flow ( D / H = 3 ) and with its long side facing the flow ( D / H = 0.33 ). title: Stable coexistence and transport of lytic phage infections with migrating bacterial hosts
abstract: Bacteriophages (phages), viruses that exclusively infect bacteria, coexist with their bacterial hosts across diverse environments at densities exceeding 10 7 per milliliter in marine surface waters, 10 8 per milliliter in soils, and 10 9 per milliliter in the human gut. In contrast, phage lysis of bacterial populations within well-mixed in vitro environments select for the emergence of phage-resistant bacterial mutants, which, in turn, select for host-range expansion phage mutants and, typically, the collapse of phage populations altogether. title: THERMAL COMFORT MAPPING OF PUBLIC SQUARES USING LANDSCAPE INTERVENTIONS
abstract: Rapid urbanization and rising temperatures had reduced the usability of public squares in tropical megacities, limiting their role as inclusive civic spaces. This study assessed outdoor thermal comfort and tested the effectiveness of landscape interventions in seven renowned public squares in Lagos, Nigeria: Tafawa Balewa Square, Muri Okunola Park, Freedom Park, JJT Park, Gani Fawehinmi Park, Iga Idunganran Palace Square, and Tinubu Square. title: Hydrologic response to changes in land use and variations of physical catchment characteristics
abstract: This study evaluates land-use change and its modeled hydrological response in the study area, which covers 731.41 km 2 of the Genfel watershed. The watershed ranges in altitude from 1764 to 3065 m a.m.l and its mean precipitation and temperature are approximately 597.9 mm and 18.8 °C, respectively. The Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) model was used to simulate watershed hydrological processes, while multi-temporal Landsat imagery from 1987, 2002, and 2017 was classified using supervised classification to assess land-use/land-cover changes. title: Synergistic Co‐Fermentation of Ulva and Waste Activated Sludge for Sustainable Resource Recovery: Mechanistic Insights From Dissolved Organic Matter Transformation and Multi‐Omics Analysis
abstract: Anaerobic fermentation for volatile fatty acids (VFAs) production represents the sustainable and resource-recovery strategy for waste activated sludge (WAS) treatment, yet its efficiency is often hampered by low substrate C/N ratio and limited hydrolysis. Ulva, a macroalga responsible for extensive "green tides" that burden coastal ecosystems and economies, emerges as an ideal co-substrate for WAS anaerobic fermentation due to its high C/N ratio and biodegradability. title: Experimental investigation of transient bed shear stress and scour formation at seawalls under tsunami bore impact using particle image velocimetry (PIV)
abstract: Abstract Tsunami bores generate short-duration, highly turbulent flows that impose intense bed shear stress on coastal structures, often leading to toe scour and structural instability. This study experimentally examines the transient evolution of bed shear stress and scour formation at four seawall geometries (box, curve, slope, and step types) using a dam-break wave testing facility and high-resolution Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV). title: Evaluation of pyocin activity and pyocin-related gene distribution in multidrug- and extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Thailand
abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa remains a major cause of healthcare-associated infections worldwide, with clinical management increasingly compromised by the emergence and dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) lineages. In this study, we evaluated the antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of purified S-type pyocins (AP41, SX1, SX2, G, S5, and M1) against a panel of 29 MDR or XDR clinical P. aeruginosa isolates collected from across Thailand in 2021–2022, integrating phenotypic data with comparative genomic analyses. title: Chemical profiling and multitarget computational screening reveal bioactive phytochemical scaffolds from Echiochilon pauciflorum stocks ex wight
abstract: Echiochilon pauciflorum (Boraginaceae) is an underexplored coastal medicinal plant. We combined GC–MS profiling, multitarget docking, ADMET prediction and cytotoxicity testing to prioritize its constituents. GC–MS analysis of aqueous, methanolic and ethanolic extracts and a hexane-trapped volatile fraction gave 271 peaks; after contaminant screening and grading of library matches, 44 compounds were tentatively identified as plausible plant metabolites, dominated by lupane- and oleanane-type triterpenoids, C13-norisoprenoids, phytosterols and Boraginaceae-type pyrrolizidine alkaloids. title: Assessment of Flood Risks on Power Infrastructure and Renewable Energy Installations in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: This research evaluated the flood hazards that impact power systems and renewable energy setups in the Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area (ONELGA) located in Rivers State, Nigeria. The primary goals included investigating how vulnerable energy infrastructure is to factors such as flood depth, speed, and duration; studying the vital interconnections between energy networks and other crucial services including water provision, healthcare, and transport; and calculating the economic damage and downtime caused by flood effects. title: Impact of Substrate Inhomogeneity and Parabolic Interface on Horizontal Transverse Waves in Sandy Layer
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the dispersion of transverse horizontal surface waves in a sandy layer overlying an inhomogeneous orthotropic half‐space with a parabolic interface irregularity. Two distinct gradient variations of the substrate, namely exponential and quadratic are considered to model different forms of material inhomogeneity. abstract: Anthropogenic CO 2 emissions are a major driver of greenhouse gas accumulation in the atmosphere, whereas natural sources, including volcanic degassing, can locally modify atmospheric composition. Since the onset of renewed bradyseismic activity at Campi Flegrei in 2005, the Solfatara area has released ~ 5,000 tons of CO₂ per day. title: GNSS navigation interference disrupts telemetry tracking of raptors migrating between Europe and Africa
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) interference in war conflict zones can disrupt wildlife tracking for research and conservation efforts. In 2023 and 2024, we tagged Black Kites Milvis migrans in Moldova and Kazakhstan, respectively, with telemetry loggers, tracked them until September 2025 and found that 20 out of the 24 Black Kites had interfered (erroneous) geographical position fixes. abstract: Abstract The formation and evolution of defects and microstructures during the additive manufacturing of metallic materials are closely related to melt pool dynamics under rapid, non-equilibrium conditions. Synchrotron radiation provides a unique tool for the in-situ characterization of metallic additive manufacturing (AM), enabling the visualization of the “black box” phenomena hidden inside the process. title: Spatiotemporal Assessment of Land Use and Land Cover Changes and RUSLE-Based Soil Loss in the Beshilo Watershed, Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia
abstract: Understanding the link between land use dynamics and soil erosion processes is critical for sustainable watershed management in fragile highland environments. This study evaluates spatiotemporal land use and land cover (LULC) changes and associated soil erosion risk in the Beshilo Watershed, Upper Blue Nile Basin, Ethiopia. Multi-temporal Landsat satellite images from 1998, 2012, and 2023 were used to assess land cover transitions, while soil loss was quantified using a GIS-based Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) model. journal: Abyssinia Journal of Engineering and Computing

title: Integrative network pharmacology and genetic evidence identifies NFKB1 as a predicted target of Terpinen-4-ol in psoriasis
abstract: Terpinen-4-ol (T4OL), a tea tree oil component, has anti‑inflammatory effects, but its psoriasis mechanism is unclear. We predicted T4OL targets via SEA, SuperPred, and TargetNet, and identified DEGs from GSE41662. Overlapping targets were subjected to functional enrichment, and PPI network construction. abstract: ABSTRACT Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin. Combining structural with functional imaging requires labeling of myelin with red fluorescence, as many functional sensors, including Ca 2+ indicators and genetically encoded metabolite sensors, fluoresce in the green spectral range. title: Untargeted metabolomic profiling of sweet potato latent virus infected Nicotiana benthamiana
abstract: Viral diseases, the second most significant biotic stress, cause substantial yield loss and quality deterioration in sweet potato, and sweet potato latent virus (SPLV) is one of the dominant viral pathogens infecting sweet potato in China. To investigate SPLV-induced metabolic changes, untargeted LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) was used on Nicotiana benthamiana inoculated with SPLV-infected sweet potato leaf sap. abstract: Despite decades of protecting migrating animals by international treaties, conservation efforts are severely hampered by our limited understanding of large-scale seasonal movements, particularly in cryptic migratory animals like bats. Banding data from a field site on the Latvian coast of the Baltic Sea suggests that some European Nathusius’ bats (Pipistrellus nathusii) move > 2000 km to their wintering range in Spain and France. abstract: Rainwater harvesting in existing university buildings requires an appraisal that connects institutional priorities, feasible retrofits and financial consequences. Selected reviews address system design, research trends and implementation barriers, providing a basis for examining how these considerations inform successive appraisal decisions. abstract: Dual-bell nozzles (DBNs) provide passive altitude compensation by adapting their effective expansion ratio through controlled flow separation and reattachment. abstract: Abstract The lateral line is a mechanosensory system that plays an important role in key fish behaviors such as navigation, prey detection, and schooling. To study the role of the lateral line in these behaviors, researchers often ablate it using aminoglycoside antibiotics such as gentamicin, which are cytotoxic to the sensory hair cells in the lateral line. abstract: This study aims to reveal the development and intellectual structure of global scientific production on the Water Footprint (WF) in industry through bibliometric methods. A total of 3,052 research and review articles published up to 22.12.2025 and indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection database were included in the analysis. title: An analysis of the impact of The Belt and Road Initiative from the perspective of European countries and Hungary
abstract: Global maritime transport routes form the backbone of world trade, as the vast majority of goods are transported by sea from producer to consumer. This research aims to provide a comprehensive overview of global shipping routes affecting Eurasia, their strategic importance, and their role in international trade, with a particular focus on maritime freight transport. abstract: Rice, a principal cereal crop often regarded as a staple food, plays a vital role in the agricultural economy of western Odisha. Cultivation of rice needs various forms of material and energy inputs, making it a resource-intensive process, and hence, its environmental consequences are becoming increasingly significant. abstract: BACKGROUND: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen in livestock and poses a potential public health threat. OBJECTIVE: This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance profiles and molecular characteristics of S. aureus and MRSA isolated from buffalo nasal swabs in the Sylhet and Noakhali districts of Bangladesh. abstract: North American cities are increasingly exposed to climate-related hazards that do not occur in isolation. Extreme heat, drought, flooding, hurricanes, wildfires, wildfire smoke, and sea-level rise interact with aging infrastructure, uneven urbanization, social vulnerability, and fragmented governance systems. title: Direct seeding and turf transplantation can reintroduce native species in grassland degraded by pine plantation
abstract: Abstract Introduction Grasslands worldwide have been extensively converted to exotic tree plantations, resulting in persistent degradation and limited natural recovery after tree removal. In southern Brazil, pine plantations alter soil conditions and create dense litter layers that restrict native plant regeneration, highlighting the need for active restoration. abstract: ABSTRACT Fireflies are semelparous beetles whose immature stages are largely unknown. abstract: Widespread amphibians often show inconsistent species assignments in public databases, complicating accurate range-wide biodiversity mapping and obscuring gaps in taxonomic resolution. abstract: Groundwater contamination from petroleum filling station (PFS) activities poses an increasing environmental and public health challenge in rapidly urbanizing regions where groundwater constitutes a major source of domestic water supply. title: Interventions to address the effects of climate change on human health in sub-Saharan Africa: A scoping review
abstract: Climate change poses disproportionate threats to human health in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet comprehensive evidence on implemented interventions remains under-researched. Understanding the scope and characteristics of existing climate-health interventions is essential for informing policy priorities and action in the region. abstract: Salicornia, a succulent halophyte flourishing in coastal and mangrove ecosystems, holds significant economic and ecological promise. Establishing sustainable cultivation systems requires a profound understanding of its geographical distribution, genetic potential, and the identification of agronomically superior populations. abstract: The Indonesia–Malaysia border region is a dynamic space where cross-border migration creates economic opportunities while increasing the demographic-economic vulnerability of local communities. abstract: Abstract Diclofenac (DIC)-prompted acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated autophagy, all of which contribute to renal impairment. Using a network pharmacology approach followed by experimental validation, this study evaluated the reno-protecting actions of dapagliflozin (DAPA) and montelukast (MON) against DIC-induced AKI in rats, both alone and in combination. abstract: BACKGROUND: The traditional habitat of the Chinese medicinal plant Cistanches Herba (CH) is the deserts of northwestern China. abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA metabarcoding is a powerful monitoring tool for assessing aquatic biodiversity, as well as the sustainability and impacts of fisheries and aquaculture. abstract: Freshwater phytoplankton communities can differ strongly between sampling periods, but the relative importance of seasonal and spatial variation in regulated reservoirs is not fully resolved. Shotgun metagenomics characterized phytoplankton in Xiaolangdi Reservoir, China, at two contrasting endpoints: winter (31 December 2023) and early summer (6 June 2024). title: The Feral Life of Plastic Waste: Third Nature and Speculative Aesthetics
abstract: This article explores the interactions between plastic waste and non-human animals from a non-anthropocentric and future-oriented perspective. However, the absence of implementation guidance limits the scalability and impact of these programs. abstract: Abstract Wildfires wreak havoc on both urban and natural ecosystems and are expected to worsen under future climate conditions. Wildfires have the potential for long-term impacts on the health of downstream reservoirs. This study seeks to compile current literature worldwide regarding impacts of wildfires on reservoir water quality, with a special focus on the implications for harmful algal blooms. abstract: Anthropogenic pressures on freshwater ecosystems have increased metal contamination in riparian zones; however, biological thresholds that distinguish tolerable exposure from ecologically significant accumulation remain poorly defined. This study investigated species-specific thresholds for heavy metal uptake in riparian macrophytes to establish a biologically grounded framework for ecological risk assessment in impacted streams. Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. abstract: Understanding the bioaccumulation and trophic transfer of naturally occurring radionuclides is essential for assessing ecological risk in freshwater systems. abstract: Oil spillage poses profound threats to ecosystems and agricultural systems, particularly in regions where energy extraction coexists with farming communities. title: Running tracks abrasion as a source of microplastics pollution: a long jump sandpit case study
abstract: Modern running tracks and football fields are covered with synthetic surfaces made of polyurethane and rubber blends with an admixture of various materials. We collected sand samples from the long jump sandpits of six elementary school and university sports facilities and examined microplastics (MPs) originating from synthetic surfaces. title: The overlooked role of food and cultural dimensions in recreational fisheries
abstract: Our study examines the diversity of values within a superficially homogeneous recreational fishery and its relationship to angler diversity. We collected data on fishing preferences, behaviors, catch usage, and sociodemographics from 443 shore anglers across 10 cities in the lower Great Lakes. We identified five coherent dimensions, including food, cultural, leisure, challenge/performance, and social-financial centrality, consistent with multidimensional value structuring in recreational fisheries. abstract: Sourcing protein-based biomaterials directly from nature presents persistent challenges in scalability, processing, and batch-to-batch variability. Recombinant engineering has focused largely on spider silks, and hagfish intermediate filament (HIF) proteins remain a comparatively unexplored alternative, with small non-repetitive subunits that have been produced full-length at high yield. title: Radiogenic isotope variability in contemporary mineral dust across the intermountain west of the United States
abstract: Mineral dust is a highly mobile component of Earth’s Critical Zone that influences ecosystem function, soil development, biogeochemical cycling, and environmental archives. Radiogenic isotopes provide a powerful means of characterizing dust because isotope ratios largely preserve source signatures during atmospheric transport. abstract: Abstract The Permian witnessed profound geomagnetic, environmental, and biotic upheavals, yet high-resolution paleomagnetic constraints across critical transitions remain sparse. title: From Ecological States to Trajectories: Revealing Ecological Dynamics Through Environmental Nucleic Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental nucleic acids (eNA) are transforming ecological biomonitoring by enabling sensitive, scalable, and minimally invasive observations across multiple dimensions of ecological systems. Here, we examine how eNA can extend biomonitoring from ecological state assessment toward the inference of ecological trajectories. abstract: Abstract. Inter-array grid optimisation plays a critical role in the technical and economic performance of wind parks and is typically divided into two primary tasks: layout length minimisation and conductor size selection. This work proposes the consideration of three primary tasks, beginning with graph preparation to account for terrain profiles, soft and hard exclusion zones, and export cables. title: Public Perception of Geodiversity in Ubatuba, Brazil: A Step for Geoscience Communication and Geoconservation
abstract: Abstract Understanding public perceptions is essential for planning effective communication strategies to promote geoconservation. However, existing literature often oversimplifies this task, focusing mainly on socioeconomic data and scientific knowledge, while neglecting the influence of numerous other factors that shape perception. title: Tourism urbanization and landscape fragmentation in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain: an integrated analysis of intensity and landscape metrics
abstract: Tourism urbanization prioritizes tourism consumption over traditional residential-focused development, reshaping land use patterns in destination areas. This research examines how tourism urbanization is associated with agricultural landscape change in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain from 1995 to 2020. Using intensity analysis and moving-window landscape metrics, results show that the agricultural landscape in Yilan underwent substantial change over the study period. title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of technological readiness and human resource (HR) digital competence on operational efficiency at Belawan Port, specifically at the Primary Cooperative (Primkop) of Stevedoring Workers (TKBM) Upaya Karya. Digital transformation in the logistics sector demands alignment between technological infrastructure and user capabilities to achieve maximum operational efficiency. abstract: Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. Previous research has leveraged computational approaches to map their extensive diversity. abstract: Abstract The heterogeneity of carbonate reservoirs constitutes a critical control on fluid flow. Nevertheless, most previous studies rely on qualitative characterization and single-scale statistical methods, which hinder multiscale characterization of pore heterogeneity and localized preferential flow. title: Wave-induced drift of pumice: transitions from forward to backward transport
abstract: Floating pumice rafts generated by eruptions of submarine volcanoes can be transported over large distances, yet the role of surface waves in controlling pumice drift remains poorly constrained. Wave-induced transport is often parameterized indirectly in numerical simulations despite limited experimental observations. abstract: The Manila Amendments to the STCW Convention set compliance requirements for seafarers’ maritime communicative competence; however, higher-vocational Maritime English assessment still relies mainly on summative final-term evaluation, with high oral-assessment costs and delayed feedback. abstract: Conservation plans for declining species often rely on contemporary genetic/genomic data to infer historical population structure and evolutionary history of the species. However, modern samples alone may not accurately reflect historical genetic variation, especially after severe population declines or intensive management, and need reference baseline data prior to anthropogenic impact. abstract: During our continued expeditions in the Dinagat Islands, southern Philippines, a new species, Trypethelium flavopigmentosum Taer & Aptroot, was discovered and is herein described. title: Traveler's Palm ( Ravenala spp.) Across Habitats and Its Responses to Disturbance in North‐Eastern Madagascar
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Ravenala (Strelitziaceae) comprises six species of arborescent herbs endemic to Madagascar and iconic to this global biodiversity hotspot. We examined how Ravenala density responds to environmental gradients, land‐use type, accessibility and canopy disturbance. The study was conducted in north‐eastern Madagascar, a region heavily affected by deforestation in recent decades. abstract: The Kura River is a transboundary freshwater system linking upstream, middle-basin and downstream communities, agriculture, infrastructure and ecosystems across the South Caucasus. This study restructures and extends an original educational research project on the ecological problems of the Kura River while preserving its central themes, visual materials, tables and ten-question survey instrument. title: Characterization of the key membrane protein cytochrome Cyc2 from Ghiorsea bivora
abstract: This study reports the heterologous production, purification, and characterization of the cytochrome Cyc2 TAG1 cluster 1 (Cyc2 TAG1_1 ) from Ghiorsea bivora TAG1 in the outer membrane of Escherichia coli BL21. Using a specific gene construct we optimized solubilization and purification protocols to obtain high‐purity enzyme. title: An operational framework to develop and apply mid-range theory for conservation science
abstract: Conservation solutions often lack transferability between contexts, a weakness that stems from a lack of connection between general theories and context-specific research. To address this problem, we propose a methodology for developing middle-range theory in conservation science through the formalised application of an operational conceptual framework. abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth's deep volatile cycle. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. abstract: The cement industry represents a significant source of atmospheric particulate emissions that may contribute to the deposition of trace metals in surrounding soils. This study evaluated the concentrations of zinc (Zn), manganese (Mn), and lead (Pb) in topsoil collected around a cement plant in Branis, Algeria. title: The complete mitochondrial genome and phylogenetic analysis of the zebra turkeyfish Dendrochirus zebra (Cuvier, 1829) (Teleostei: Perciformes)
abstract: Dendrochirus zebra, a reef-dewelling scorpaenid, was sequenced for its complete mitochondrial genome (16,504 bp). abstract: To address the question of how the geological structure and composition of rocks in the Indigirka River basin influence the mineral composition of modern alluvial deposits, samples collected from the lower reaches of the river were analyzed. abstract: Abstract This study examines the role of multinational enterprise (MNE) subsidiaries in facilitating environmental upgrading in value chains, with a specific focus on the salmon aquaculture sector. abstract: Quorum sensing (QS) enables bacterial coordination of group behaviors, yet how enteric pathogens modulate QS during intestinal colonization remains poorly understood. abstract: Despite successive regulatory reforms, entry into enclosed spaces remains one of the deadliest operations in ship management. abstract: Ekosistem mangrove merupakan komunitas tumbuhan yang khas, hidup di wilayah pesisir dan muara sungai yang dipengaruhi oleh pasang surut. abstract: Skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis) is one of Indonesia’s important fishery commodities with high economic value. However, limited information on length-based population characteristics, particularly from small-scale fisheries in Fisheries Management Area (FMA) 573, remains a challenge for evaluating stock utilization and supporting sustainable fisheries management. abstract: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. This narrative review synthesizes 74 documents published between 2008 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, reports of intergovernmental and national agencies, and selected news and NGO records, to examine the emergency response to COVID-19 in Bangladesh, with the European Union as a comparator, and to connect that response to its environmental dimensions. abstract: Senegal, like all other developing countries, faces problems with access to drinking water. This study focused on evaluating the quality of drinking water in the Saraba neighborhood within the commune of Darou Khoudoss in the Thies region. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the structural composition of the raki table by analysing meyhane menus. It aims to identify patterns of menu composition and product diversity in meyhane cuisine and to examine how shared menu structures coexist with regional variation within this widely practised dining format in Türkiye. abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene's largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. abstract: Biodiversity loss, habitat fragmentation and climate change are among the primary environmental pressures affecting species distributions. abstract: Rapid, practical diagnostic approaches are essential for effective fish health management, yet cytological wet mount assessment of internal organs remains underused and inconsistently described in peer-reviewed aquatic veterinary literature. abstract: Temperature-extreme risk is often assessed through trend-based indices, but regional climate-risk planning also requires uncertainty-aware estimates of rare thermal events and their spatial variability. abstract: Geotechnical investigations are widely regarded as a crucial component of the safe, durable and cost-effective construction of structural and highway infrastructure in Nigeria. abstract: Terrestrial multi-species predator feeding aggregations (MPFAs) are characterized by contest competition, but scramble competition is likely more common at MPFAs in pelagic waters. However, empirical investigations are rare. Aerial video was used to estimate abundances of striped marlin and mahi-mahi alongside their attack and capture rates and spatio-temporal positioning as they competed at prey schools. abstract: Abstract Socio-environmental conflicts over natural commons represent a growing challenge for sustainability governance, yet their dynamics remain poorly understood within complex Social-Ecological Systems (SESs). This study examines six emblematic conflicts in the Venice Lagoon (Italy), a complex SES undergoing profound transformations driven by land-use change and the privatisation of natural commons. abstract: Aquatic nitrogen (N) pollution is a global problem, and understanding where best to implement mitigation strategies to reduce transfers from land to water is becoming increasingly urgent. Watershed nutrient budgets, using commonly available census data, can successfully predict riverine export spatially, albeit with variation related to fractional export. abstract: Urban ecological health is increasingly prioritised in Europe, as reflected in the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030, the Nature Restoration Regulation, and the amended Regulation on Environmental-Economic Accounts. Translating these commitments into effective greening policy and planning actions that halt and reverse urban ecological degradation requires standardised, spatially explicit indicators. abstract: Abstract Extreme environments are recognized as valuable reservoirs of microbial diversity and chemical novelty. Adapted to harsh environmental conditions, bacteria isolated from extreme environments exhibit unique biosynthetic capabilities associated with the production of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites. Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains one of the most important neglected tropical diseases, affecting approximately eight million people worldwide. title: Warming effects on population sizes and top–down control are dependent on temperature range
abstract: Rising global temperatures are expected to affect natural ecosystems, but predicting the consequences is challenging given the complexity of ecological communities. Natural communities are complex networks of interacting species, and temperature changes can thus influence species directly and indirectly via changes in their various interactions with other community members within and across trophic levels. abstract: Cartilaginous fish have diverse morphological traits that are essential for understanding their evolutionary history and ecological adaptations. However, the conus arteriosus and its valves, key components of the heart and blood circulation, have been underexplored in phylogenetic and ecomorphological contexts. abstract: Freezing fundamentally alters how minerals transform dissolved phenols in cold environments. As water freezes, solutes are excluded from the crystal lattice and concentrated into microscopic pockets of unfrozen liquid, creating reaction conditions far more extreme than those of bulk solution. Here, we compare catechol oxidation on a key soil manganese oxide under freeze-thaw versus room-temperature conditions. abstract: Plastic pollution is an emerging threat to urban green spaces and forest parks, where recreational activities generate litter that can be redistributed by runoff and fluvial processes. However, the role of small-scale fluvial geomorphology in regulating macroplastic retention within ephemeral stream networks remains poorly understood. This study investigated macroplastic accumulation across four fluvial landforms in five ephemeral streams of Latman Kan Urban Forest Park; a major peri-urban recreational area in Tehran, Iran. abstract: Dam regulation directly affects the intensity of hydraulic exchange and redox conditions in the hyporheic zone by changing river flow and water level, thereby influencing the biogeochemical processes of nitrogen. This study takes the Mojiabao section of the Hun River in Shenyang, China, as the study area. title: Temporal and spatial analysis of precipitation to the identification of extreme climate events in Pará state estimated by CHIRPS
abstract: In recent decades, extreme climate events have been recurrent in the Amazon, causing both intense droughts and prolonged rainy periods, impacting the population and economic sectors. abstract: RepDBmaker is a reproducible Snakemake pipeline designed for the automated construction of large-scale protein sequence databases. It enables the seamless downloading of sequences from different public databases and the integration of user-specified proteomes. The pipeline also performs standardized taxonomic annotations to all compiled sequences and contamination screening in eukaryotic proteomes. abstract: We estimate built-up surface increase within water-related lowlands across Vietnam using Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) estimates, Joint Research Centre surface-water history and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission terrain data accessed through Google Earth Engine. abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is an integral component of fish health and growth performance and therefore represents an important production factor in aquaculture. Antibiotics are a major stressor, not only by disturbing microbial diversity, but also by altering microbial interactions involved in digestion, colonization resistance and functional redundancy. Current risk assessments, however, rely largely on diversity-based evaluations and rarely consider changes in network topology. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Indigenous planning as a vital epistemological and practical framework for disaster risk reduction in the Pacific, centering Hawaiian knowledge systems. abstract: This paper revisits critical climate mobility literature that explores the role of images and visual materials within policy briefs and papers, published about a decade ago, to contrast those findings with present-day policy documents. abstract: Open-conduit volcanoes are characterized by continuous magma supply and persistent degassing, whereas eruptive activity occurs intermittently and is controlled by magma transfer and accumulation processes within the feeding system. abstract: Abstract Bioactive secondary metabolites produced by the haptophyte microalga Prymnesium parvum are key mediators of ichthyotoxicity during harmful algal bloom events. abstract: Disaster, vulnerability and adaptation have been the highly recognized studies in the contemporary globalized environment. The primary purpose of the study is to assess the flood vulnerabilities and adaptation strategies of smallholders in Gaibandha, a northern district of Bangladesh. The primary data of the study were collected from 110 respondents of five villages in Saghata Upazila who had been randomly selected by using survey questionnaire. title: First evidence of a mandibular crest in Brasileodactylus Kellner, 1984 (Pterosauria, Pteranodontoidea, Anhangueridae), with comments on pterosaur headcrests
abstract: Brasileodactylus araripensis Kellner, 1984, is a toothed pterosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin, Brazil. Traditionally regarded as crestless, the species has been central to debates on anhanguerid taxonomy, as most members of the clade possess well-developed sagittal cranial or dentary crests. Here we describe a nearly complete lower jaw (MCT.R.1473) that reveals, for the first time, the presence of a sagittal dentary crest in Brasileodactylus araripensis. title: Caribbean Islands facilitated the colonization of Western Hemisphere barn owls, yet experienced rampant extinction
abstract: Island biodiversity reflects multiple evolutionary roles, encompassing lineages derived from nearby continents, relict taxa and, in limited cases, sources of continental diversity. Reconstructing the biogeographic history and island-mainland diversification dynamics requires an integrated understanding of speciation, extinction and dispersal processes to and from islands. title: The Chemical Effects of Nitrogenous Substances in Two Different Grades of PVDF Used in Offshore Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, two different grades of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) commonly used in offshore applications, one with 3% of dibutyl sebacate (DBS) plasticizer and the other a copolymer containing chlorotrifluoroethylene (CTFE), were subjected to an aging process in contact with a fluid containing hydrocarbons, pyridine, and aniline at high temperature for 90 days. title: Biodegradable mulch films affecting surface runoff, soil erosion, and film fragment loss from farmland
abstract: The use of conventional plastic mulch films is a common agricultural practice that can lead to persistent plastic film fragments entering soil systems. To prevent the accumulation of these fragments, soil-biodegradable mulch films are marketed as alternatives. Unlike conventional plastic mulch, soil-biodegradable mulch films are ploughed into the soil after use, where they biodegrade over time. title: MARKETING STRATEGIES IN TOURISM-LED REAL ESTATE SALES AND DEVELOPMENT: CASE OF GEORGIA
abstract: This article examines the impact of tourism marketing strategies on real estate sales and development in Georgia. It argues that destina­tion marketing influences property markets indirectly but systematically by producing desti­na­tion awareness, place familiarity, repeat visitation, perceived safety, year-round utility, and confidence in the future attractiveness of a location. title: Assessment of the reproductive biology of largetooth silverside Chirostoma arge (Atherinopsidae) in Lake Chapala, Mexico
abstract: Chirostoma arge (Jordan and Snyder, 1899) is a fish endemic to the central plateau of Mexico important for fishing in natural reservoirs such as Lake Chapala. Unfortunately, little is known about this species of the Atherinopsidae family, which is listed as Data Deficient by the IUCN Red List. This study’s objective was to determine the sex ratio, the stage of gonadal maturity in each sex, the spawning season and to estimate the relative condition factor, the minimum standard length and the standard length at first maturity. title: Cation Interactions Governing the Nutritional Status of Serpentine Soils under Red Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) Cultivation
abstract: Serpentine-derived soils are characterized by limiting conditions for plant growth. The combined effects of the physical, chemical, and biological properties of these soils create a stress condition known as the ‘serpentine syndrome’. This study aimed to investigate calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and potassium (K) nutrition in red pepper cultivation on serpentine soils, and to evaluate the relationships among key cation ratios. journal: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology

title: A BRIEF OVERVIEW OF THE PFAS POLLUTION PROBLEM IN THE ENVIRONMENT
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of PFAS contamination in the environment. An analysis of published scientific papers has shown that PFAS are exceptionally resistant to chemical, biological, and photolytic degradation, exhibit significant mobility in water, and can be dispersed across long distances. PFAS are known as «forever chemicals» with half-lives of thousands of years. PFAS contaminate surface water sources and can accumulate in soil and air. title: Conceptual frameworks and learning outcomes for a two-course sequence in energy geographies
abstract: The essay aims to advance the teaching and learning of energy geographies through reflection on 17 years of navigating rapid change in the national and international energy geographies, technologies, economics, and politics. After establishing the institutional and personal research contexts in a large land-grant university, the paper describes a three-part conceptual framework emphasizing energy systems, production of space, and whole-systems approaches. journal: Journal of Geography in Higher Education

title: BIOCHEMICAL RESPONSES OF AQUATIC ORGANISMS TO EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS: IMPLICATIONS FOR ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: The occurrence of emerging environmental contaminants is being observed more frequently in aquatic environments, which can cause biochemical, developmental, endocrine, physiological, and reproductive effects on aquatic species. It is necessary to know the differences between toxicant classes and biological effects types for ecological health evaluation and sustainable environmental management. This study evaluated biochemical responses of aquatic organisms to emerging environmental contaminants by comparing toxicity thresholds across contaminant categories, life stages, and biological endpoint

title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. title: Formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs in the ediacaran dengying formation from the central to Northern Sichuan Basin, SW China
abstract: The microbialites in the Ediacaran Dengying Formation of the Sichuan Basin exhibit significant hydrocarbon potential. Investigating the formation and preservation mechanisms of ultra-deep microbialite-dominated reservoirs is critical for expanding exploration domains. Based on observations of 374 samples from outcrops and cores, thin-section quantification, porosity and permeability testing, and diagenetic sequence reconstruction, this study systematically analyzes reservoir characteristics under different burial conditions and establishes an evolution model for microbialite-dominated reservoi

title: Live and livelihoods in wetland waterlogging: Study from southwest Bangladesh
abstract: Waterlogging is a major hazard that often underestimated even by scientists and policymakers because of its slow onset effects on environment and society. However, it habitually brings miserable sufferings for the communities living around low-lying wetlands, generally called ‘Beel’ in Bangladesh and primarily depending on the natural resources of those wetlands for their livelihoods. title: Reconstructing Eco-Jurisprudence: Qirā'ah Mu'āṣirah fī al-Aḥkām and Systems Theory in Operationalizing Ecological Maqāṣid
abstract: This research explores the global ecological crisis as a structural failure in the relationship between humans, law, and nature, rooted in the anthropocentric paradigm. Although Indonesia possesses rich theological values regarding nature conservation, the eco-theological response has tended to be ethical-spiritual and lacks legal-formal enforcement. This qualitative research with a juridical-normative approach aims to reconstruct the epistemology of Islamic law through Shofiyullah Muzammil's Qira'ah Mu'āṣirah fī al-Ahkām method, synthesized with Jasser Auda's Systems Theory. title: INFLUENCE OF GONADAL MATURATION ON GLYCOSAMINOGLYCAN LEVEL IN Prochilodus brevis SKELETAL MUSCLE
abstract: The role of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) on the sexual maturity of Prochilodus brevis is unknown. In this study evaluated the influence of gonadal maturation on GAGs level in P. brevis skeletal muscle. journal: Revista Brasileira de Engenharia de Pesca

title: Investigating Postseismic Creep in the Laboratory: Testing Dislocation‐Based Models for Transient Creep in the Upper Mantle
abstract: Abstract Studies of postseismic creep often infer a strong reduction in upper‐mantle viscosity after large earthquakes, yet the microphysical mechanism responsible for this behavior remains subject of debate. Here, we present new gas‐medium apparatus experiments at 1100–1200°C on pre‐dried, annealed Åheim dunite (grain size of 400 m) designed to elucidate the microphysical mechanism of transient dislocation creep during postseismic relaxation. title: In Silico Analysis of Nucleotide Diversity of Fish Species in the Daya River
abstract: The current study was designed to assess the nucleotide diversity and genetic structure of selected fish species in the Daya River using an in-silico approach. Genetic diversity is an important measure of population stability, adaptability, and survival, especially in freshwater habitats that are now under increasing human impacts. The nucleotide sequences of the most frequently documented fish species were obtained from the GenBank database, with a primary emphasis on mitochondrial gene segments. journal: American Journal of Science Engineering and Technology

title: Sex differences in turtle vocalizations: social context and behavioural roles
abstract: Abstract Acoustic communication is widespread in animals, yet its function in turtles remains poorly understood. Although turtle signaling has been considered primarily visual and chemical, many species vocalize across life stages. We investigated adult vocalizations in the Midland Painted Turtle ( Chrysemys picta marginata ) to test whether call types and acoustic traits vary across social contexts. title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations
abstract: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: Design of Smart Antifouling Surfaces Using Enzyme-Responsive Surface Topographies
abstract: Biofilm accumulation on polymeric surfaces remains a persistent challenge in biomedical, industrial, and environmental systems. Here, we report an enzyme-responsive antifouling surface that integrates particle-generated topography with biologically activated surface renewal. Microparticles of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) and the chitinase-responsive polymer PHEVD were generated by mechanical abrasion and embedded into poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) to create polymer-composite surfaces with three-dimensionally distributed microparticles. title: Combined sewer overflows attributable to wet weather season contributing to pharmaceutical pollution: A case study in Northern Spain
abstract: The use of combined sewer systems is associated with frequent overflow events and discharges of untreated wastewater containing micropollutants, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of weather-related factors on the presence of pharmaceuticals and illicit substances and assess the related environmental risk. title: The Impact of Business Analytics on Decision-Making Among Small and Medium Enterprises in Andhra Pradesh
abstract: This study assesses how BA adoption influences decision-making in Andhra Pradesh SMEs. The research uses a quantitative descriptive cross-sectional survey method and a structured 25-item questionnaire (Google Forms) administered to owners, managers, and decision-makers in SMEs using convenience and purposive sampling methods to reach an estimated 150 SME respondents. title: Combined effects of heatwaves and pollution on freshwater invertebrates: a scoping review of experimental approaches
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are highly vulnerable to climate change and anthropogenic pollution. Climate change is characterized particularly by an increase in average temperatures, with more intense, longer, and more frequent heatwaves (HWs). While the effects of contaminants are well documented, sometimes in the context of global warming, the impact of HWs, either alone or in combination with pollution, remains poorly studied in freshwater invertebrates. title: Long-term changes in extreme precipitation and their non-stationary teleconnections with ENSO and PDO over Vietnam (1981–2024)
abstract: This study investigates long term spatial trends, interannual variability, and evolving teleconnections of total and extreme precipitation across Vietnam using the climate hazards group InfraRed precipitation with station data (CHIRPS) and 11 expert team on climate change detection and indices (ETCCDI) precipitation indices. The results reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity in precipitation extremes. title: A self-powered wind speed and humidity sensor based on paired flap-type triboelectric nanogenerators with differential humidity responses
abstract: This study reports a self-powered sensor that simultaneously measures wind speed and relative humidity using two triboelectric nanogenerators. The output of conventional triboelectric nanogenerators decreases with increasing ambient humidity. In previous wind sensors, this dependence has been treated as an error to be eliminated. Herein, we used the humidity dependence as a measurement signal. abstract: Background The human oral cavity harbors a diverse microbiota essential for maintaining oral and systemic health. While most resident microorganisms are commensals adapted to specific oral niches, increasing evidence highlights the presence of non-oral bacteria, including Helicobacter pylori, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacteriaceae, Staphylococcus aureus, Acinetobacter baumannii, Enterococcus faecalis and Clostridioides difficile. title: Ephemeral resources promote adaptive sociality in wild guppies
abstract: Sociality can facilitate the discovery of novel resources, yet it can also entail costs, including increased competition, aggression, sexual harassment and disease transmission. Selection should therefore favour social flexibility as a response to changes in resource conditions, allowing individuals to adjust their social associations optimally. abstract: The Niger Delta is known to have hydrochemically impaired shallow aquifers in most places, but the geophysical susceptibility that allows contaminations to occur is not usually quantifiable at the community level. This study integrates six Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) soundings and six Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) traverses across Okerenkoko, Kurutie, and Kunukunuma, three oil-exploration-exposed settlements in the Gbaramatu Kingdom of Warri South-West, Delta State, to quantify aquifer protective capacity using Dar-Zarrouk parameters. title: A UNIQUE GEOSITE OF A LAVA SUBFOSSIL FOREST IN THE GALÁPAGOS
abstract: The Galápagos archipelago is an extraordinary place known for its bio- and geodiversity, especially due to its extensive volcanic origin. Very frequently, a volcanic disaster or hazard may not only destroy parts of its environment, but it may also conserve parts of it. Hereby, in the northern caldera rim of the Sierra Negra volcano on Isabela Island, a remarkabl e discovery was made of a geosite, where lava flows with an age of some 3,000 years enabled the preservation of subfossil structures with more than 80 lava trees and tree moulds along 50 sites in a main area of some 2400 m2 . title: A new zinc bioavailability-based Environmental Quality Standard (EQS) for compliance assessment under the European Union-Water Framework Directive
abstract: Many countries list zinc (Zn) as a River Basin Specific Pollutant (RBSP) under the European Union's Water Framework Directive (WFD). Given the dependency of Zn toxicity to aquatic organisms on local water body conditions, it is essential that the derivation of Environmental Quality Standards (EQS) for Zn incorporates bioavailability. We have updated the Zn EQS by revising and updating the existing ecotoxicity dataset and by including optimized bioavailability models. title: Iturin A disrupts Cryptococcus neoformans membrane integrity, attenuates virulence, and synergizes with amphotericin B
abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans is a major fungal pathogen with severely limited therapeutic options. We evaluated the antifungal activity of the lipopeptide iturin A against eight clinical isolates of C. neoformans . Iturin A exhibited robust anti-cryptococcal activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 12.5 to 25 μg/mL, and demonstrated minimal toxicity in A549 lung epithelial cells and HepG2/C3A liver cells. title: Hydrodynamic resistance on oscillating planar interfacial bodies
abstract: We study the unsteady dynamics of floating planar bodies undergoing lateral oscillations along an air--water interface. Scaling arguments indicate that when the viscous penetration depth and oscillation amplitude are both small compared to the body size, the flow beneath the body can be approximated by an oscillatory Stokes boundary layer, yielding a leading-order description of the hydrodynamic resistance. title: Effects of Pretreatment on the Isotopic Composition of Structural Carbonate in Ray‐Finned Fish Teeth
abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale The carbon and oxygen stable isotope ratios (δ 13 C and δ 18 O) of carbonate contained in fish tooth dentin have the potential to offer insights into environmental and ecological conditions, making them promising targets for analysis in fossil specimens. However, the tooth dentin of extant specimens contains significant amounts of organic matter that can decompose or produce gases that interfere with isotope measurements. title: Soil Physicochemical Alteration Associated with Dolomite Influx Along the India–Bhutan Border
abstract: Abstract Dolomite, a calcium magnesium carbonate mineral, can adversely affect soil properties when present in excessive amounts. The India-Bhutan border region of West Bengal has experienced substantial declines in the quality and yield of fresh tea leaves, potentially associated with dolomite influx from the neighbouring lower Himalayas through recurrent flooding and the use of river water for irrigation. title: Producing a Red List of Ecosystems for the Brazilian Cerrado
abstract: Abstract Land clearance is a key driver of biodiversity loss. This is a particular challenge in the Brazilian Cerrado, the world's most biodiverse savanna biome and a region experiencing a rapid expansion of agriculture. To inform habitat conservation and restoration actions, we used the Red List of Ecosystems (RLE) framework to identify threatened ecosystems within the Cerrado. This biome is divided into 20 ecoregions, and we subdivided each ecoregion into forest, savanna, grassland, and wetland ecosystems. title: Climate drives recent increases in fire activity in aspen ( Populus tremuloides Michx.) forests of the western US
abstract: Background Portions of the western US are experiencing simultaneous increases in wildfire frequency, size and intensity alongside worsening drought conditions. Despite the importance of quaking aspen (Populus tremuloides Michx.) as a keystone species, drivers of wildfire in aspen forests remain relatively understudied compared with neighboring vegetation types. Aims Understanding trends and the drivers of wildfire in aspen forests across the western US is crucial for effective monitoring and management. title: Hydrochemical characteristics and their controls in Jining National High-tech Zone: A land-use perspective
abstract: Groundwater chemistry reflects both natural and anthropogenic processes. In rapidly urbanizing areas where agricultural and construction land coexist, differences in shallow groundwater chemistry remain poorly understood. This study compared hydrochemical characteristics between agricultural and construction land-use types in the Jining National High-tech Zone, China, using geochemical diagrams, ion ratios, mineral saturation indices, and multivariate statistics. title: Mapping Assessment Tools for Nature-Positive Decision-Making
abstract: Background Efforts to support nature-positive decision-making rely on a growing number of assessment tools for Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and Ecosystem Services (ES), yet the available tool landscape remains fragmented and difficult to navigate. Tools differ widely in scope and purpose, and there is limited evidence on how they are recognised and used in practice. title: Wetland vegetation dynamics and its linkage with climatic, hydrological, and land-use/ land cover changes in the Foket floodplain of the Fetam River Watershed, Northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Timely monitoring of wetland changes is vital for effective conservation and management of the landscape. This study, therefore, examines vegetation dynamics and their climatic, hydrological, and land-use drivers in the Foket floodplain wetland, Upper Blue Nile basin, Ethiopia. The LULC analysis was employed based on 1985, 2002, and 2020 cloud-free Landsat images. The maximum likelihood classification algorithm was applied to classify the images into eight LULC classes. title: Real-World Outcomes of the Solitaire™ and React™ Devices from India’s First Multicenter Mechanical Thrombectomy Registry
abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is a low utilization of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in India and lack of a nationwide registry or data. This registry aimed to study the systems of care, functional outcomes, and cost effectiveness of MT treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: Patients were treated with Solitaire™ X and/or React™ catheter as the primary device/s. title: Effects of irradiance and pH on growth, photophysiology, and high-value metabolites production in Chlamydomonas acidophila
abstract: Abstract Acidophilic microalgae represent a promising but underexplored source of bioactive metabolites with potential biotechnological applications. Herein, we evaluated the influence of pH and irradiance on the growth performance, photophysiology, and metabolite profiles of a strain of the acidophile Chlamydomonas acidophila . title: Transcriptomic insights into hydrostatic-pressure-induced triploidy in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) across developmental stages
abstract: Induced triploidy is used in aquaculture to generate functionally sterile stocks and may alter the allocation of resources among growth, maintenance, and reproduction. However, the molecular responses associated with hydrostatic-pressure induction and triploidy remain poorly characterized in large yellow croaker ( Larimichthys crocea ). In this study, fertilized eggs assigned to the induction group were exposed to 7000 PSI hydrostatic pressure for 3 min at 2 min 30 s post-fertilization. Ploidy analysis confirmed triploid status in the pressure-induced groups and diploid status in the controls.

title: Decoupling Amplitude, Energy Input and Contact Time in the Ultrasound‐Assisted Extraction of Ascophyllum nodosum Bioactives
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrasound‐assisted extraction (UAE) is promising for recovering seaweed bioactives, but confounding amplitude/power, energy input, and treatment time complicates mechanistic interpretation and cross‐study comparison. We decoupled amplitude/power from energy input during aqueous UAE of Ascophyllum nodosum , evaluating amplitude, energy input, contact time/mixing, temperature control, and biomass loading. title: Extinguished or overlooked? An examination of lost firefly species of the US and Canada
abstract: Fireflies (Coleoptera: Lampyridae) are iconic indicators of ecosystem health, yet a significant number of North American species face an uncertain future due to increasing threats from habitat loss, light pollution, climate change, and pesticide use. While the most recent assessments have shed light on the conservation status of some US and Canadian species, a considerable knowledge gap remains for 69 species that are categorized as Data Deficient and a further 48 species that have yet to be evaluated. title: Integrated in vitro and in silico evaluation of the antibiofilm activity of Artemisia dracunculus L. against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: This study investigated the antibiofilm and antibacterial potential of Artemisia dracunculus L. extract through integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the disc diffusion method against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus subtilis, and Bacillus licheniformis while antibiofilm activity was determined by crystal violet assay. title: Seismotectonics and structural dynamics of the eastern Sulaiman fold-and-thrust belt, Pakistan
abstract: Structural and kinematic analyses of the eastern Sulaiman Range, based on focal mechanism solutions reveal systematic spatial variations in faulting style. Thrust-dominated deformation characterizes the eastern and western parts of the study area, whereas the central region is dominated by left-lateral strike-slip faulting that is spatially associated with the Kingri fault system. title: Geogenic controls and anthropogenic inputs on the seasonal hydrogeochemical variability of the Paraopeba River basin, Brazil
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the combined effects of geology, land use and land cover, hydrological seasonality, and disturbance history on the hydrogeochemistry of surface waters in the Paraopeba River Basin (PRB), located in Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil, and forming part of the São Francisco River Basin, a region characterized by high lithological complexity and intense anthropogenic pressure. abstract: To unify the decoupled dimensions of scientific rigor and contextual narrative in virtual heritage display, this paper uses the VR project developed for Jingdezhen’s bid for World Cultural Heritage as a case study, and establishes a workflow for the virtual recreation of urban heritage that includes data collection and processing, spatial script, virtual reconstruction, and asset production. title: Preliminary Characterisation of Rhizophora apiculata Fruit Carotenoids by TLC and Zeaxanthin–iNOS Docking
abstract: Rhizophora apiculata fruit potentially contains carotenoid pigments that may contribute to the biological properties of mangrove plants. This study aimed to separate and preliminarily identify carotenoid pigments from R. apiculata fruit and to predict the molecular interaction of zeaxanthin with inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). abstract: Abstract Assessing land use pressure is fundamental to understanding regional sustainability. This study constructs a comprehensive Land Use Pressure Index (L) using remote sensing and socio-economic data from 2000 to 2019 across three dimensions—carbon effects, ecological risks, and landscape stability—with weights objectively determined by the entropy weight method. abstract: Abstract In this study, magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (MIONs) were synthesized using three different. methods: coprecipitation, microwave-assisted synthesis, and hydrothermal synthesis. The resulting nanoparticles were further functionalized with citric acid (CA) and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) to enhance their physicochemical properties and adsorption capabilities. abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic pollution is a long-standing environmental problem because it is highly resistant to natural degradation. This study investigates a poorly studied low-cost biocatalytic approach for the degradation of PET-derived wastewater using esterase-producing bacteria isolated from activated sludge of shrimp waste. title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa modulates Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance
abstract: Abstract This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. The effects of co-culturing with Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ) on Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) virulence and survival under sub-MIC antibiotic exposure were assessed in vitro using 12 bacterial combinations. abstract: Abstract The Spain Species Specialist Group of the IUCN Species Survival Commission, established in 2024, comprises c. 150 specialists in 18 taxonomic working groups. Among its aims is the assessment of the status of Spanish species for the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
abstract: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. title: Topsoil removal increases native forb and grass recovery in a southern Australian urban temperate grassland
abstract: Abstract Introduction Native temperate grasslands are globally threatened, biodiversity‐rich ecosystems. In urban post‐agricultural grasslands, restoration often achieves reestablishment of grass species‐dominated communities, yet associated forb recovery remains limited by non‐native seedbanks and nutrient‐enriched soils. title: Beyond proximity: Green space visitation patterns and physical health outcomes
abstract: Urban green spaces (GS) are increasingly recognized for mitigating health risks linked to urbanization, yet most research emphasizes proximity rather than actual use in Mediterranean cities. This study examines how GS visitation patterns, demographic characteristics, and physical health outcomes interact in Chania, Crete, addressing gaps in GS exposure and chronic disease prevention. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 718 adult residents between June and August 2024. title: Marina Selection Using Weighted Mixed-Variable Axiomatic Design Framework
abstract: Purpose: Marina selection is a complex multi-criteria decision-making problem characterized by heterogeneous data types, inherent uncertainty, and strong dependence on user preferences. Addressing this complexity requires a decision-support framework that can simultaneously accommodate multiple variable representations while preserving theoretical consistency, transparency, and interpretability. title: Heatwave‐Resilient Cuticular Microbiota Protect the Leaf Beetle Plagiodera versicolora From Fungal Infection
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves-extreme thermal events characterized by prolonged supra-optimal temperatures-exert profound impacts on global ecosystem stability and species interactions. While the disruptive effects of thermal stress on host physiology and gut microbiota are well documented, the role of cuticular microbiota in host defense under heatwaves remains poorly characterized. title: Using network modeling to explore the historical evolution of urban systems in the Jiangnan Canal area
abstract: Abstract Canals influence the formation and development of urban systems in adjacent regions, yet the spatial organization of cities within canal regions remains insufficiently examined. Focusing on the Jiangnan Canal area, this study constructs gravity-model-based historical urban networks and applies network analysis to examine structural characteristics and evolutionary patterns, while drawing on historical and geographical contexts to discuss the canal’s potential role in regional urban-system change. title: Divergent Responses of Fungal Communities to Vegetation Structural Complexity in Degraded Roadside Slopes Across Climatic Gradients
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how climate and vegetation structural complexity jointly shape fungal communities is essential for effective roadside slope restoration. To address this, we examined restoration effects on fungal diversity, community composition, and ecological networks across three climatically distinct regions: dry‐hot valley, subalpine, and subtropical. abstract: Abstract The assessment of the morphometric characteristics of the Dzüdza River basin in Nagaland has been critically important for hydrological analysis, flood risk assessment, soil erosion evaluation, and sustainable regional development, owing to its strategic location on the northern fringes of the Himalayas and flanked by hills to the east. title: Condition Matters: Fine-Tuning Ecosystem Service Capacity with Ecosystem Condition
abstract: Ecosystem service (ES) capacity matrices are widely used for ES assessment and mapping due to their operational simplicity. However, standard matrices assign uniform capacity scores to ecosystem types without accounting for local variations in ecosystem condition, leading to systematic assessment errors. title: Warming and predation drive rapid evolution of ecosystem functioning but not functional traits
abstract: Global environmental change can rapidly reshape phenotypic trait distributions through adaptive and neutral processes. Yet, disentangling their relative contributions remains a major challenge, particularly for traits underpinning ecosystem functioning. Using a two‐year mesocosm study, we experimentally evolved Asellus aquaticus under contrasting temperature and predation regimes to test how the joint influence of these global change pressures shape the evolution of traits and ecosystem functioning. abstract: Abstract The CEACAM gene family is among the fastest evolving in vertebrates. It likely originated from an ancestral CEACAM1-like gene encoding an inhibitory receptor. In mammals, CEACAM1 is expressed on epithelial cells and can regulate leukocyte activation. Thus, several bacterial pathogens exploit it for host entry and immune suppression. abstract: As águas subterrâneas são um recurso importante para o abastecimento e o desenvolvimento urbano, o que exige a avaliação de sua vulnerabilidade à contaminação. title: Real-time quantification of fluid flows around bubbles during directional solidification
abstract: Directional solidification of bubbly liquids plays a critical role in shaping the microstructure and properties of many materials, yet the fluid dynamics governing bubble behavior during solidification remain poorly understood. Using cryo-confocal microscopy and particle image velocimetry, we quantify fluid flows around bubbles during solidification of water containing surfactants and tracers. abstract: ABSTRACT How costly are droughts to adults' nutrition in Africa? Do people adapt to recurring droughts? We measure severe droughts using detailed satellite‐based index of greening observed bi‐monthly on a relatively high‐resolution 0.083° grid between 1982 and 2015, that captures persistent and severe deficits in soil moisture relative to grid‐cell and time‐of‐year normal moisture. abstract: This study examines the development of renewable installed capacity in Türkiye over 2000–2025 and screens its agricultural linkages through a criteria-based assessment of applications and a regional Agricultural Renewable Energy Potential Index (AREPI). abstract: Abstract Nitrogen fertilization accelerates soil acidification by stimulating ammonia oxidation, yet the dominant active ammonia oxidizers and their acid-adaptation strategies remain unresolved. abstract: Paleopteran insects (Odonata and Ephemeroptera) occupy a crucial position in insect evolution and are ecologically significant indicators of freshwater ecosystem health. Recent improvement in the number of publicly available genomes and transcriptomes have advanced understanding of genome size evolution, morphological innovation, and ecological responses in these orders. abstract: The transition from mineral extraction to post-mining land use is conventionally structured as a sequential process where recreational functions are introduced after extraction ceases. This study examines the Nanpu 1–3 area in the Bohai Bay Basin using an integrated interpretation of three‐dimensional seismic volumes, coherence and dip‐guided attributes, synthetic seismograms, drilling and wireline‐log records, available core descriptions and test and production summaries.
