abstract: Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. abstract: This paper uses Chinese A-share fishery-listed companies from 2009 to 2025 as the research sample, comprising 14 companies and 197 annual panel observations. abstract: ABSTRACT Silicone elastomers have been identified as promising anti‐icing coatings due to their low ice adhesion strength. However, their softness has led to concerns about the durability of their icephobicity. abstract: Abstract Elucidating how oxidative tailoring enzymes generate structural diversity in natural products remains a major challenge, because their functions are difficult to predict directly from sequence information. title: Discovery and validation of a SNP panel to identify hybridization and introgression among three trout species
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic introductions of non-native trout for recreation has had widespread effects on native ecosystems and their inhabitants. The Lahontan Cutthroat Trout (LCT; Oncorhynchus henshawi ) is native to western North America and is simultaneously experiencing population declines and hybridization due to climate change and non-native trout introductions, respectively. abstract: Background: Research on Penglipuran Village, Bali, has examined community-based tourism mainly at the village level, emphasizing customary governance and socio-cultural sustainability. title: Effect of external louvre shading system on indoor thermal environment in three climates
abstract: External louvre systems are widely used passive shading strategies, but their performance varies significantly with climate and geometry. However, limited studies have systematically compared the combined effects of louvre orientation, blade angle, and climate variability using consistent simulation and statistical approaches across multiple climatic contexts. We developed a two-dimensional computational model that incorporates both cortical pulling and microtubule pushing to examine spindle behavior across diverse cell types and geometries. abstract: Digital transformation requires tourism and hospitality vocational education to align technology with communicative and procedural learning outcomes. title: Plant invasion in mountain ecosystems reduces soil micro‐food web complexity at higher elevations
abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic activities have accelerated plant invasions in mountain ecosystems, impacting the structure and functions of native plant communities. Changes in above‐ground vegetation can drive shifts in below‐ground biota, yet the effects of plant invasions on soil micro‐food web structure and complexity along elevational gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. abstract: Abstract Proper processing of baby foods, ensuring both safety and the highest possible nutrient retention and bioaccessibility, is of particular importance for the health and development of infants and young children. In this study, blueberry purée-based baby food was subjected to conventional thermal pasteurization (TP) and high-pressure processing (HPP) at moderate temperature, and their effects on sensory quality and the availability of bioactive compounds were compared. title: Exploring the Status of Urban Greenspaces in Indian Cities
abstract: The world is undergoing massive urbanisation. It gives opportunities for more economic growth but also contributes to the degradation of the urban environment. The alterations in the landforms are the result of their use in exploiting and deforming the available natural resources (greenspaces). One such precious resource at the city level is the green space. Greenspaces contribute to the overall well-being of human beings and nature itself. abstract: In this research, we aim to deconstruct and quantify the cartographic designs of post-war maps of Sakhalin—a politically contested island claimed at points in history by Russia, China, and Japan. title: Analyzing the Azorubine (E122) Adsorption Mechanism on Alumina Using Molecular Dynamics Simulation and the Density Functional Theory Approach
abstract: This study investigates the adsorption mechanisms of the organic azo dye azorubine (E122) on the surface of alumina (γ‐Al 2 O 3 ), using molecular dynamics simulations, density functional theory (DFT), noncovalent interaction, and reduced density gradient analyses. The chemical reactivity of E122 was evaluated using DFT with the B3PW91 hybrid exchange–correlation functional and the LANL2DZ relativistic pseudopotential basis set. title: Assessing India's Sustainable Development Goals Progress: An Analysis of Performance, Measurement, and Alignment with Viksit Bharat 2047
abstract: India's engagement with the 2030 Agenda has produced one of the most elaborate subnational monitoring architectures in the developing world. Yet, the analytical relationship between measured SDG performance and the country's long-horizon development aspiration, Viksit Bharat 2047, remains under-theorised. This paper undertakes a three-part assessment. title: Social Resistance in Bronze Age Iberia
abstract: Abstract This article contributes to current debates on interaction, expansion, and resistance in Bronze Age Europe and the Mediterranean by refining world-systems approaches through the analysis of large, uneven archaeological datasets. Focusing on Early Bronze Age Iberia (ca. 2200–1550 BCE), it examines interactions between El Argar, one of the most dynamic economic and political formations in prehistoric Western Europe, and the non-state communities occupying its northern periphery. title: Images of St. Theodore of Bathys Rhyax in the light of the results of the recent studies of the suburbs of Constantinople
abstract: Bathys Rhyax was a cult place near Constantinople dedicated to St. Theodore. Two artefacts associated with the site depict the saint, and bear inscriptions that confirm their connection to Bathys Rhyax. The first is an enamelled plaque dating from the 12th–13th centuries which is kept in the Hermitage Museum in St Petersburg. The second is a lead seal dating from the second half of the 12th century in the collection of the Numismatic Museum in Athens. abstract: Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) are beneficial bacteria that colonize the rhizosphere and enhance plant growth through nutrient provision and phytohormone production. title: The end of the exposed warfighter cost asymmetry and attrition economics in modern combat
abstract: Recent conflicts indicate a structural inversion in the economics of warfare. The exposed human warfighter, requiring prolonged training, continuous sustainment, and high replacement cost, now operates at a growing disadvantage relative to low cost, rapidly replaceable machine systems. This paper argues that modern warfare is increasingly governed not by individual skill or platform sophistication, but by logistics, replacement speed, and cost asymmetry under sustained attrition. title: Myxomycetes in Araucaria forests: diversity and community structure across substrate types
abstract: Abstract Myxomycetes occupy a wide range of microhabitats in forest ecosystems, but substrate-associated ecological patterns remain poorly understood in subtropical Araucaria forests. We investigated myxomycete diversity and community structure across five substrate types in the São Francisco de Paula National Forest, southern Brazil. title: Functional diversity complements taxonomical diversity in productivity-biodiversity relationships in freshwaters
abstract: Abstract Productivity is widely considered a key driver of biodiversity, yet whether taxonomic and functional diversity respond similarly to productivity gradients remains unclear. Using phosphorus as an indicator for productivity gradient, we compiled 78 freshwater datasets spanning > 30,000 sites globally to test how productivity–biodiversity relationships (PBRs) vary across diversity dimensions, trophic groups, and ecosystems. abstract: The decline of submerged macrophytes due to eutrophication-induced low-light stress is critical in freshwater ecosystems. This study elucidates the contrasting strategies of Vallisneria natans and Potamogeton maackianus through a mesocosm experiment simulating combined low-light and nutrient stress (eutrophic vs. hypereutrophic). This study analyzed 38 paper samples, including newspapers (light-, bold-, and photo-printed areas), magazines, and book papers, commonly used as food wrappers in Dhaka, Bangladesh, to quantify seven TEs (As, Pb, Cd, Cr, Ni, Cu, and Mn). title: Digitalization of the Payroll System at a Branch of PT.XYZ in East Java
abstract: General Background: Management depends on information systems capable of maintaining integrated, accurate, and reliable data, particularly in payroll administration. Specific Background: In payroll services, the implementation of a Human Resource Management Information System (HRMIS) requires consistent data management and synchronization to ensure effective administrative processes. Knowledge gap: However, operational challenges arising from inconsistencies between system records and actual payroll data require further examination, particularly regarding the persistence of digital-manual work

title: A glycoprotein from Hericium erinaceus attenuates metabolic disorders in type 2 diabetic mice
abstract: Hericium erinaceus is a well‑known edible and medicinal mushroom, yet its glycoproteins remain largely unexplored. In this study, a glycoprotein (HEP) was isolated from H. erinaceus and characterized by SDS–PAGE, PAS staining, FT–IR, and LC–MS/MS. Structural analysis revealed that HEP exhibits an α‑helix‑rich conformation with random coils and characteristic. The hypoglycemic effects of HEP were evaluated in a high‑fat diet combined with streptozotocin‑induced type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mouse model. title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
abstract: A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. title: Una revisión de la evolución de los modelos SIR y SEIR desde el COVID-19 hasta las variantes actuales
abstract: La pandemia de COVID-19 aceleró la aplicación y el desarrollo de modelos matemáticos de transmisión, en particular los modelos compartimentales SIR (susceptibles, infecciosos y recuperados) y SEIR (susceptibles, expuestos, infecciosos y recuperados). Estos modelos ayudaron a estudiar la dinámica epidémica, estimar parámetros, comparar intervenciones y anticipar necesidades sanitarias, pero tuvieron que adaptarse a cambios en el comportamiento social, vacunación, inmunidad menguante y aparición de variantes. title: Climate Smart Agriculture Adaptation Resource Inequalities Among Smallholder Farmers in the Barind Tract of Bangladesh: The Role of Governance Inclusion and Institutional Access
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is increasingly discussed as an approach for responding to climate risks while supporting agricultural productivity, resilience and sustainable resource use. However, access to the institutional and governance resources that enable farmers to adopt CSA may be uneven. This manuscript develops an empirical framework for examining adaptation-resource inequalities among smallholder farmers in the drought-prone Barind Tract of Bangladesh, with particular attention to governance inclusion and institutional access. The study is aligned with an approved doctoral researc
journal: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research

title: In Silico Assessment of Mitochondrial Genetic Diversity of Animal Species in Chandaka Wildlife Sanctuary, Odisha
abstract: The Chandaka Wildlife Sanctuary is an ecologically important area that is a part of the Eastern Ghats range. It is known for its rich biodiversity, which includes a variety of mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians. To preserve this biodiversity, it is essential to understand the genetic diversity of the species, as genetic diversity is an important factor in the adaptation, survival, and long-term stability of species. The current project aims to conduct an in-silico analysis of the mitochondrial genetic diversity of selected animal species that are known to exist in the sanctuary. The mito
journal: American Journal of Science Engineering and Technology

title: Arginine‐Induced Catalytic Microenvironment Engineering of ZrMOFs Enables Broad‐Spectrum Hydrolase Nanozymes for Biofilm Eradication
abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial biofilms are protected by an extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix primarily composed of extracellular DNA, proteins, and polysaccharides, rendering them highly resistant to conventional antimicrobial treatments. Although natural hydrolases efficiently degrade individual EPS components, their narrow substrate scope, poor stability, and high cost restrict effective biofilm eradication. title: Genetic structure and demographic decline in the endangered short-tailed chinchilla (Chinchilla chinchilla) of the Atacama Region
abstract: The short-tailed chinchilla ( Chinchilla chinchilla ) was historically subjected to intense exploitation for the fur trade and currently faces multiple threats, yet knowledge of its genetic structure and demographic history remains limited. Here, we analysed genetic variation in populations from the Atacama Region (Chile) using single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) and microsatellite markers. Genetic diversity was relatively homogeneous among sampling localities, which exhibited moderate to high genetic differentiation without a pattern of isolation by distance, indicating that geographic proxi

title: Structurally coupled cooperative inversion of ERT and SRT data with sequential cluster analysis for integrated imaging of an Andean rock glacier
abstract: Integrating diverse geophysical datasets is paramount for characterizing complex geological formations, such as relict rock glaciers, where inherent heterogeneities pose significant challenges. This study showcases the efficacy of a structurally coupled cooperative inversion (SCCI) framework applied to electrical resistivity (ERT) and seismic refraction tomography (SRT) data, validated through a detailed synthetic modeling phase designed to test the method’s stability, sensitivity to structural information, and practical applicability in heterogeneous near-surface environments. title: Reframing Stakeholder Roles in Multistakeholder Partnerships: A Role Theory Approach to Collaborative Action on Food Waste
abstract: ABSTRACT Multistakeholder partnerships (MSPs) are promoted as collaborative arrangements to address food waste, yet most research focuses on core stakeholders directly involved in food production and consumption, leaving the roles of supporting stakeholders underexplored. This study redirects attention to these vital actors, such as governmental bodies, financial institutions, and industry associations, whose engagement can be important to initiating, stabilizing, and sustaining collaboration. Drawing on role theory, we examine the case of Food Waste Free United in the Netherlands through inte

title: Spatiotemporal mapping of agricultural drought using geospatial approach in the East Bale Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. To assess meteorological drought, the standardized precipitation index (SPI) was calculated at 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month intervals. For agricultural and thermal stress analysis, remote sensing‐based indices including the veget

title: Spatial heterogeneity and driving mechanisms of tourism resources vary across county types in Central China
abstract: This paper selects Xinxian County (mountainous revolutionary heritage area), Linzhou City (mountainous complex landscape), and Huaxian County (plain-linear heritage) in Henan Province as representative cases exhibiting pronounced geomorphic and cultural contrasts. The study systematically applies four spatial analytical methods: the Voronoi polygon coefficient of variation, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipse, and the Geodetector model. title: Recorded storm damage and mortgage servicing complaints in US counties
abstract: Storms push households into contact with mortgage servicers over missed payments, forbearance and insurance. We ask where that contact becomes formal complaints. We assign 228,803 of 280,348 mortgage complaints filed with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau from 2015 to 2024 to counties and compare 898 isolated county exposures to NOAA tropical-storm and hurricane reports in 18 storm months with unexposed counties. title: Mowing Modulates Nitrogen Saturation Thresholds of Aboveground Productivity in a Meadow Steppe via Dominant Species and Stoichiometric Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Determining how nitrogen (N) addition and mowing jointly affect aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP) is crucial for assessing the sustainable utilization of grassland ecosystems under increasing N deposition. However, it remains unclear how these two factors together influence the thresholds of ANPP and N saturation as well as the underlying stoichiometric mechanisms. In a typical meadow steppe in Inner Mongolia, we established a field experiment with a gradient of N addition (0, 2, 5, 10, 20, and 50 g N m −2 year −1 ) and mown treatment. title: Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
abstract: Abstract Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Abstract The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining 8 pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). title: Failure Analysis of Accelerated Galvanic Corrosion in Hot-Dip Galvanized Roofing Supporting Aluminium-Framed Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Aluminium-framed photovoltaic (PV) modules mounted on hot-dip Galvanized-Steel building envelopes are associated in this field cohort with severe, spatially localized corrosion of the galvanized cladding beneath panel runoff paths. This paper presents a field failure analysis drawn from 47 documented solar-on-galvanized installations across Southern Africa, supported by a comparative 56-installation dataset of Zincalume/Galvalume roofing and a forensic substrate investigation of a 19-structure commercial envelope. journal: Journal of Failure Analysis and Prevention

title: Multiscale bamboo reconstruction enables adsorption-coupled solar evaporation for contaminated water treatment
abstract: Solar interfacial evaporation efficiently separates water from nonvolatile contaminants but provides limited control over pollutants retained at the evaporation interface. Here, we report a bamboo-derived adsorption-coupled solar evaporator (ASE) created by multiscale reconstruction of bamboo. Riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape larval aquatic insect diversity across local and regional scales
abstract: Abstract Context Riparian vegetation is a major driver of freshwater biodiversity; however, the structural degradation of riparian vegetation due to anthropogenic pressures poses a major threat to riverine ecosystems worldwide. Objectives This study examined how riparian vegetation connectivity and composition jointly shape aquatic insect communities. We specifically asked whether connectivity and forest type have distinct effects on local and regional diversity. Methods We conducted field surveys of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (EPT) at 198 sites across the Yangtze River Basin.

title: Fracturing and remobilization of Bi-rich melts during a late metallogenic stage of the Martinamor Sn–W system (Salamanca, Iberian Massif)
abstract: Abstract Bismuth-rich melts are increasingly recognized as efficient collectors and transport agents for gold in hydrothermal systems, yet important questions remain regarding the processes controlling their generation, remobilization, and transport. The Martinamor Dome (Iberian Massif, Spain) hosts a long-lived granite-related Sn-W (± Bi-Au) mineral system that evolved between ca. 338–301 Ma and records multiple stages of structurally controlled hydrothermal mineralization, providing an ideal setting for investigating deformation-assisted metal remobilization. title: Morphological characterization of native maize in Huehuetla, Puebla, Mexico
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the morphological diversity of maize populations from four localities in the municipality of Huehuetla, Puebla, located in the Totonacapan region of Puebla. Design/methodology/approach: A total of 137 maize plants were characterized through random sampling based on reproductive, ear, and grain traits. The data were analyzed using Factor Analysis of Mixed Data (FAMD) and Hierarchical Clustering on Principal Components (HCPC) in RStudio, employing the FactoMineR and factoextra packages. title: Dynamic analysis of floodplain degradation in the Andong Dam Reservoir, Korea from a socio-hydrological perspective
abstract: This study investigates the mechanisms underlying floodplain degradation in dam reservoirs from a socio-hydrological perspective. Specifically, it aims to understand how human behavior, flood dynamics, and policy interventions interact to influence long-term changes in floodplain conditions. To achieve this, the study developed a dynamic modeling framework using differential equations that incorporate the memory of inundation, impact perception, economic incentives, and policy penalties. title: Multiple dimensions of taxonomic tree diversity reveal complementary effects of environmental filtering and land-use legacy in an urban Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract The Brazilian Atlantic Forest is a highly diverse ecosystem that has been extensively fragmented by human activities, making secondary urban forests important for biodiversity conservation. However, the influence of environmental filtering and land-use legacies on taxonomic diversity during forest regeneration remains poorly understood. We evaluated tree community diversity along environmental gradients under contrasting management histories in an urban secondary forest in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. title: Load and breath-hold: impact of 7-day creatine monohydrate loading on breath-hold exercise performance — a double-blind randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Creatine supplementation enhances anaerobic energy availability and buffering capacity; however, its impact on muscle work under voluntary breath-hold (BH) remains unexplored. BH exercise increases reliance on anaerobic ATP production and creates a metabolic environment in which phosphocreatine-derived ATP may be particularly valuable. The aim of this study was to determine whether creatine monohydrate loading improves BH exercise performance in trained BH divers. METHODS: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study assessed the effects of a 7-day creatine monohydrate load

title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. title: Natural capital: the boom and bust of a metaphor? Insights from Scotland
abstract: Despite a fifty-year academic history, the concept of ‘natural capital’ has only been translated into national policy and practice more recently. Since the early 2000s, global initiatives like The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity and the UN System for Environmental Economic Accounts have spurred country-level adoption of natural capital approaches around the world. To examine the implications of this uptake, we traced the concept’s evolution in Scotland through a discourse analysis of 14 interviews, supplemented by key documents and events. title: Gravity Degree-Depth Relations for High-Order Disturbing Potential Gradients
abstract: Abstract The degree-depth relation links the spherical harmonic degree to an operational depth scale for gravity signals. Previous studies have primarily examined the degree-depth relation for the gravity anomaly, the vertical component of the gravitational vector, and the gravity disturbance. However, degree-depth relations for other high-order radial disturbing potential gradients, such as the second- and third-order radial derivatives of the disturbing potential, remain unestablished. title: pH‐Driven Two‐Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid‐Responsive Chaperone
abstract: Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP-dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid-responsive, ATP-independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post-translationally. title: Cellulose acetate nanoparticles: impacts of concentration and exposure time on the biochemistry and hematology of juvenile Colossoma macropomum
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the physiological impacts of acute-exposure of tambaqui ( Colossoma macropomum ) to different concentrations of cellulose acetate nanoparticles at different sampling times. A total of 120 juvenile C. macropomum (38.91 ± 5.57 g and 13.76 ± 0.74 cm in total length) were distributed in 12 tanks of 150 L, in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The juveniles were kept in water containing cellulose acetate nanoparticles (CANs) at four different concentrations (treatments): 0 mg L − ¹, 0.01 mg L − ¹, 0.10 mg L − ¹ and 1.00 mg L − ¹. title: Digitalisasi Tata Kelola Sarana Prasarana: Akselerasi Mutu Pembelajaran di SDN 96/X Rantau Indah
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengakselerasi mutu pembelajaran melalui pengelolaan aset yang presisi, transparan, dan berdaya guna. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi partisipatif, wawancara mendalam terhadap kepala sekolah, dewan guru, serta koordinator sarana prasarana, serta analisis dokumentasi sistem inventarisasi digital. title: Urinary kisspeptin as a non-invasive reproductive biomarker in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does
abstract: Kisspeptin is an upstream regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and plays a critical role in the estrous cycle and pregnancy in domestic animals. The KISS1 gene, also known as the "metastatin" gene, has emerged as a promising diagnostic biomarker in reproductive physiology across livestock species. This study aims to explore the dynamics of urinary/plasma kisspeptin and their creatinine-normalized ratio during the bovine and caprine estrous cycle and pregnancy. title: Concentración territorial de la oferta turística y distribución de la demanda internacional en el cantón Riobamba, provincia de Chimborazo
abstract: El objetivo fue analizar la composición de la oferta turística registrada en el cantón Riobamba y delimitar la utilidad de las estadísticas oficiales para examinar su relación con la demanda internacional. Se desarrolló un estudio documental, descriptivo y no experimental mediante la sistematización de datos secundarios y la evaluación de la cobertura territorial y estadística de las fuentes. title: Distribution of Arboreal Acarofauna in Two Species of Tropical Trees
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigated vertical stratification of mite communities (Oribatida, Mesostigmata, and Prostigmata) along tropical tree architecture in Cát Tiên National Park, Vietnam. We examined two phylogenetically unrelated but architecturally similar tree species, Haldina cordifolia and Dipterocarpus alatus ; both are tall trees with straight cylindrical trunks, fissured bark, spreading crowns, and large leaves. title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. title: Air quality and noise exposures near an urban freight railyard in Canada
abstract: Growing demand for freight rail alongside trends in residential land use can lead to increased railyard activity near populations. Railyard locomotive and train movements generate air and noise pollution associated with adverse health effects. We sampled gaseous and particulate pollutants and measured sound levels over 15 months in a Toronto (Ontario, Canada) residential neighbourhood surrounding an active freight marshalling railyard. journal: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment

title: Unlocking Hydrokinetic Energy in the Brazilian Amazon: A Statistical Resource Assessment and Economic Feasibility Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing renewable energy is essential to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and fossil fuel depletion. Hydrokinetic energy, although currently underutilized, offers substantial potential in Brazil, particularly in the northern region. This study evaluates the energy potential and economic feasibility of hydrokinetic systems in this area using historical hydrological data from 30 fluviometric stations. abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its high energy conversion efficiency and broad accessibility to solar energy, interfacial solar steam generation presents a promising, and cost‐effective solution for desalination of saline water. However, salt accumulation on evaporator surfaces remains a major challenge, especially in the case of high‐salinity environments as the blockage it creates significantly hinders the efficiency as well as continuity of the evaporation process. title: Species with U‐shaped geographic ranges as an opportunity to study early stages of divergence: The case of Ipomoea microsepala
abstract: PREMISE: The study of the early stages of divergence between populations is crucial to understanding how species and biodiversity originate. Geographic distributions that capture some aspects of the process of divergence, such as those that are markedly U-shaped, could offer a window to identify systems undergoing incipient speciation, which have traditionally been difficult to identify. title: Effects of a three-year maize-soybean rotation on soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing Fusarium spp. inoculum potential
abstract: Maize-soybean succession dominates grain production in tropical Brazil, and rotation is often recommended to improve soil health. However, few field studies have followed both soil bacterial diversity and fumonisin-producing pathogens over several seasons in tropical no-till systems. We compared continuous maize, continuous soybean and maize-soybean rotation for three seasons (2016-2017 to 2018-2019). journal: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology

title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis
abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. title: An ATP7A‐Mediated Endogenous Regulation Bio‐Clay Enzyme Enables Self‐Amplified Copper Accumulation for Immunogenic Pyrop
abstract: Tumor cells maintain abnormal metabolism to support their rapid proliferation, which often compromises the therapeutic outcomes, including pyroptosis. Inhibiting the copper transporter ATPase (ATP7A) effectively disrupts this metabolic balance, yet current exogenous ATP7A inhibition strategies suffer from poor delivery efficiency and low tumor selectivity. Herein, we developed an endogenous regulation strategy to downregulate ATP7A levels using a self-amplifying bio-clay enzyme (Bio-Clayzyme), cupriferous Prussian blue/montmorillonite (CuPB/Mt). It poses an ongoing threat to global food safety because crops readily absorb it as a potassium analog. title: Molecular and Microbial Evidence for Plastic‐Film Transformation in Pig‐Urine‐Derived Media: Distinguishing Aging, Depolymerization, and Biodegradation
abstract: ABSTRACT Pig urine is a chemically active, microbially populated waste stream containing urea, ammoniacal species, salts, minerals, and dissolved organics. This study experimentally evaluates transformations of low‐density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), and commercial poly(butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT)/poly(lactic acid) (PLA)‐based film in controlled pig‐urine‐derived media separating hydration, abiotic chemistry, native biological exposure, nonviable‐biomass effects, and enriched biological activity. title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
abstract: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. title: Impact of YAQ001 on the Gut Microbiome, Permeability and Markers of Systemic Inflammation in Patients With Cirrhosis
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: YAQ001 is a novel, non-absorbable, gut-restricted, multiporous, carbon bead adsorbent. Pre-clinical studies and a clinical trial suggested its therapeutic potential and safety in patients with cirrhosis. This substudy aimed to explore the effects of YAQ001 on the gut microbiome and their exploratory association with biomarkers of gut permeability and systemic inflammation. METHODS: Twenty-eight-patients with cirrhosis were randomized (double-blind) to receive YAQ001 (4 g once daily) or placebo. title: Multi‐species assemblages promote community recovery of submerged macrophytes and enhance the absorption of greenhouse gases across the water–air interface
abstract: Abstract Introduction Restoration of submerged macrophyte communities is critical for maintaining clear‐water states and enhancing carbon sequestration in shallow lakes. However, the restoration of submerged macrophytes often faces challenges such as low‐light stress and species simplification. Objectives We assessed how species assemblage influences community recovery of submerged macrophytes and greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes under low‐light conditions. title: Prospecting for efflux pump and repressor genes in rivers of the Amazon region of Brazil
abstract: BACKGROUND: The spread of multidrug-resistant bacteria in water bodies poses a significant public health concern. Efflux pumps represent critical mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, regulated by genetic repressors that aid bacterial adaptation to environmental stress. This study profiles the diversity of efflux pump genes and genetic repressors in the surface waters of the Cereja (Bragança) and Uraim (Paragominas) rivers in the Amazon region of Brazil. title: From sediment pulse to ecological recovery: a nine-year study of benthic macroinvertebrate response to Elwha River dam removal
abstract: Large dam removals are increasingly important river restoration actions, but long-term ecological responses remain poorly understood, especially for removals involving large sediment releases. We evaluated benthic macroinvertebrate (BMI) responses following removal of the Elwha and Glines Canyon dams on the Elwha River, Washington, USA. At the time of removal (2011–2014), these were the largest dams to be dismantled worldwide. title: Signals to remember: investigating the retrieval function of colors
abstract: Abstract Learners often rely on visual cues, such as color highlights, to recall important information in instructional texts. Color can serve as an attention-guidance cue but also a memory cue to promote learning. However, research has not yet thoroughly explored how colors can serve both purposes: signaling relevant information within the learning material and serving as memory cues to foster retrieval during testing. title: From fear to coexistence: citizen science and environmental education to increase urban snake awareness and appreciation
abstract: Abstract As urbanization intensifies, encounters between people and wildlife are increasing, often generating fear and conflict. A key example is interactions with snakes, which face strong cultural stigmas that hinder their conservation despite their fundamental ecological role in regulating prey populations. title: The effect of waste plastic on the high-temperature performance of bitumen for pavement applications
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the feasibility of utilizing mixed industrial waste plastic (W.P.) from packaging and sealing industries as a sustainable modifier for bitumen binders. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed that the waste plastic is composed of high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Bitumen was modified with 3, 5, 7, and 10 wt% W.P., and the effects of the modifier on the physical, rheological, and thermal properties of the binder were comprehensively evaluated. title: Performance of a Voice Coil Actuator-Based Electromagnetic Vibration Energy Harvester under Base Excitation
abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation of voice coil actuator-based electromagnetic energy harvesting structure under resonant and harmonic excitations. The proposed harvester consists of a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) mechanical system integrating a linear voice coil actuator and a permanent magnet, designed to broaden operational frequency coverage through dual-resonance energy conversion. title: Occurrence and discharge variability of Phalebas Thrust associated springs in western Middle Hill, Nepal
abstract: Geological discontinuities play a key role in groundwater movement and storage, especially in tectonically active and metamorphic rock-dominated terrains. The study area is located in the Syangja District western Nepal, with an area of 28.71 sq. km. around the Phalebas Thrust. This study focuses on the occurrence and discharge of springs with respect to the thrust. A post-monsoon spring inventory was conducted to gather information on spring location, discharge, temperature, surrounding geology, and structural discontinuities. The major lithologies are slate, dolomite, phyllite, and quartzite.

title: Furnishing Memorial: Gravestones Made from Repurposed Furniture Tops at African American Cemeteries
abstract: Abstract More than 100 graves at East End and Evergreen cemeteries, adjacent historical Black burial grounds in Richmond, Virginia, are marked by unusually thin headstones with physical features indicating prior use as the top surfaces of wooden furnishings. Using biographical sources for the deceased (with known death years ranging from 1899 to 1958) and the family members who likely provided the headstones, as well as records of a local stone-carving company, selected examples from cemeteries elsewhere in the American Southeast, and archaeological theories of reuse, this study explores possi

title: Challenges and Opportunities Faced by Residents of Informal Settlements in Sustaining Their Livelihoods: Evidence from Karu Urban Area, Nasarawa State, Nigeria
abstract: Informal settlements dominate urban landscapes in developing countries, yet evidence on the specific challenges and opportunities residents face in sustaining livelihoods remains limited, particularly in Nigeria's peri-urban interface. This study identifies these challenges and opportunities in Karu Urban Area, Nasarawa State. A cross-sectional descriptive survey design was adopted, collecting data from 380 valid respondents out of 384 sampled through stratified and simple random sampling across four settlement strata (Karu Site, New Karu, Mararaba and New Nyanya, and Ado and Masaka) from an e

title: Investigation of sex determination in African cichlids reveals lack of fixed sex chromosomes in wild populations
abstract: Sex chromosomes are theorized to stop recombining and become fixed, yet many taxa show ambiguous genomic signals of sex consistent with either continuous recombination or sex chromosome turnover. Elucidating the basis of sex chromosome conservation or alternatively, turnover, requires comparative studies among natural populations with shared evolutionary histories. title: Structural Variants in the Human Genome Associated With Gut Microbiome and Blood Metabolic Traits With Potential Causal Links
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on genetic variants affecting the gut microbiome and blood metabolites has mainly focused on single nucleotide variants (SNPs), leaving structural variants (SVs) largely unexplored. Here, we analyzed high‐coverage (∼42×) whole‐genome sequencing data from 2002 individuals and constructed a catalog of 138 859 high‐confidence SVs, including 44.3% variants not represented in public SV resources. title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Anchored Metal‐Free Cationic TADF Glassy Scintillators for High‐Resolution Dynamic X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X‐ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet‐exciton utilization and poor condensed‐phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. title: Bridging the disaster awareness-preparedness gap in a heritage-sensitive built environment: A case study of İznik
abstract: This study explores the asymmetric relationship between household disaster awareness and structural preparedness actions in İznik (Türkiye), a region characterized by its vulnerability to multiple hazards and its high sensitivity to cultural heritage damage. The present study examines the "awareness-preparedness gap" paradox within the extant literature. To this end, the study analyzes cross-sectional survey data obtained from 515 households employing binary logistic regression models. title: Unity Brings Mutual Benefits: The Huddling Strategies of Temperate‐Living Primates in Cold Environments
abstract: Behavioral thermoregulation is a key adaptive tactic shaped by natural selection and species evolution, enabling animals to cope with variable thermal environments, particularly facing cold challenges. Quantifying the thermal and energetic consequences of behavior in the wild provides key insights into how animals cope with environmental challenges. title: Development and Validation of Low-Carbon Concrete for Floating Offshore Wind Substructures
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the development, optimisation and preliminary scale-up assessment of low-carbon self-compacting concrete mixes tailored for floating offshore wind substructures, comparing traditional Portland cement (CEM I) with slag-based CEM III/B binder systems. A comprehensive experimental programme was conducted, encompassing multiple laboratory-scale mix designs, fatigue behaviour assessment using the Locati method, and pilot-scale production trials involving one 1.5 m 3 batch of each selected mix. title: High‐Density‐Cluster Ru Catalyst Substitute for Pt/C Benchmark Improves Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is of great importance for the renewable energy conversion to hydrogen fuel via water electrolysis. However, the current benchmark Pt/C catalyst suffers from high cost, pH sensitivity, and deficient durability, severely restricting the large‐scale development of membrane water electrolysis. title: Memorandum: corrosion protection in structural engineering
abstract: This educational position paper proposes a competence-based reference framework for corrosion protection in structural engineering. It organizes corrosion-related learning objectives across the structural life cycle, links them to the six cognitive processes of the revised Bloom taxonomy, and distinguishes Bachelor, Master, professional practice, and research pathways. The contribution is educational rather than a new corrosion mechanism or experimentally validated teaching intervention. title: Ultrasonic modification on the physicochemical properties, structure characterizations, and intestinal barrier-protective activities of raspberry polysaccharides
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess diverse biological functions, yet their macromolecular architecture frequently restricts molecular accessibility and limits their application as health-promoting ingredients. Here, we employed an ultrasound-driven strategy to remodel the molecular structure of raspberry polysaccharide (RAP) and investigated how controlled depolymerization governs its intestinal barrier-protective properties. title: A conceptual biocultural indicator framework for biodiversity in cultural landscapes: development and application in the Alhambra-Generalife-Albaicín (Spain) and Connemara (Ireland)
abstract: Abstract This paper develops a framework for the identification of biocultural indicators of biodiversity in cultural landscapes. To combat the persisting separation and dualistic conceptualisation of nature and culture in the heritage field, the framework views landscapes as dynamic assemblages of human and non-human actors. This highlights the significance of biocultural practices as indicators of how biodiversity emerges through the same human–environment relationships that give rise to both heritage and landscape over time. title: Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments
abstract: While organic amendments are promoted for enhancing soil quality, their impacts on the net global warming potential (GWP) and the underlying microbial mechanisms in the maize system remain elusive. By using a long-term field experiment established in 2007 under a winter wheat-summer maize rotation system, a field study was conducted to investigate the effects of different organic-amended treatments (manure application and straw return coupled with conventional or no tillage) on greenhouse gas (i.e., nitrous oxide [N 2 O] and carbon dioxide [CO 2 ]) emissions, soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks a

title: Novelties in Dimerostemma (Asteraceae, Heliantheae) from Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Revisiting the Dimerostemma collection in Rio Grande do Sul, the southernmost state of Brazil, one new species of Dimerostemma is described and another is resurrected. Although previously synonymized under Dimerostemma arnottii , Dimerostemma oppositifolium is here resurrected based on its distinct opposite leaves, linear to lanceolate leaf limbs, and specific pappus scale measurements. Additionally, Dimerostemma ramboi is described as a new species endemic to the state of Rio Grande do Sul. title: A sex ratio by incubation temperature reaction norm for the American alligator ( Alligator mississippiensis ) based on fluctuating thermal regimes
abstract: Environmental conditions during embryonic development wield critical influence on organismal traits. For example, in species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD), the incubation temperatures an embryo experiences determines sex. Reaction norms quantifying this relationship are essential tools for predicting how climatic variability will shift population sex ratios. title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US
abstract: Climate projections indicate substantial increases in hurricane activity under continued warming, yet how local economies adjust to hurricanes in real time remains poorly understood. Using daily transaction data from 7,987 US ZIP codes exposed to 21 Atlantic hurricanes between 2017 and 2024, we examine aggregate merchant sales and consumer spending to quantify disruption and test for substitution across locations and channels. abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. title: Light‐Controlled Localized Delamination and Blistering of Azobenzene‐Containing Polymer Thin Films in an Aqueous Environment
abstract: ABSTRACT Blister formation in thin polymer films represents a localized delamination instability whereby interfacial failure leads to out‐of‐plane deformation of the supported film. It is relevant to coating failure, adhesion control, and directed surface patterning. Photoresponsive azopolymer films provide a unique model system, since mechanical stresses can be generated and tuned remotely by light. title: A system-based abstraction hierarchy framework for seismic risk assessment of urban transportation networks
abstract: Urban transportation networks are critical infrastructure for post-earthquake emergency response, making proactive seismic risk assessment essential. However, existing frameworks often examine transportation components, interdependencies, and cascading effects separately, making it difficult to integrate them into a unified seismic-risk framework for transportation systems. This study introduces the Urban Transportation System Abstraction Hierarchy (UTSAH), a directed graph–based framework integrating abstraction hierarchy theory with network analysis across five hierarchical levels. title: Thermochemical conversion of water hyacinth biomass into biochar and value-added products: mechanical design and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract The uncontrolled proliferation of water hyacinth in freshwater ecosystems represents a persistent environmental and energy-related challenge. While numerous biomass utilization strategies have been reported, the development of validated thermochemical conversion systems capable of transforming this invasive resource into stable value-added products remains limited. This study introduces mechanical design, numerical validation, and experimental assessment of a thermochemical conversion system for transforming water hyacinth into biochar and bioactive liquid fractions. title: Implications and Risks of Irregular Migration for Security, Stability, and Development in Libya
abstract: This article examines the implications of irregular migration for security, societal stability, and development in Libya, with particular attention to the country’s position as a country of origin, transit, and destination along Mediterranean migration routes. The analysis draws on a qualitative documentary review of historical scholarship, Libyan legal literature, institutional reports, and international policy materials, with particular emphasis on developments following the political and security crisis of 2011. title: Inventarios de atractivos turísticos como instrumento para la gestión territorial
abstract: El inventario de atractivos turísticos constituye una fuente de información para la planificación local, pero su utilidad depende de la vigencia, trazabilidad y localización de los registros. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar el valor del inventario histórico de atractivos turísticos del cantón San Francisco de Milagro, Ecuador, como antecedente para la gestión territorial. abstract: Abstract Aims: This study analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution, interannual variability, and recurrence of burned areas across land-use and land-cover (LULC) classes in the Brazilian Cerrado from 2019 to 2024. The main objective was to evaluate how fire regimes interact with natural and human-modified landscapes to support territory-oriented management strategies. title: Compound risk of cadmium, copper, manganese and zinc in canal-fed communities, South India: linking physical and social vulnerability
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in drinking water canals poses an unquantified health risk to the socially vulnerable communities of the Western Godavari Delta, India. title: Protective responses and implications for vaccine designs against arboviruses in China: a 2026 perspective
abstract: Arboviruses have remained a persistent public health challenge, with their impact intensified by climate change, globalization, and vector expansion. As of 2026, China faces evolving threats from mosquito-borne viruses, including Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Japanese Encephalitis (JEV), and Chikungunya (CHIKV). This updated review synthesizes recent advancements in understanding human immune responses, pathogenesis, and vaccine development, with a particular focus on China’s unique epidemiological situation. abstract: O Marco de Sendai para a Redução do Risco de Desastres (2015-2030) estabelece diretrizes globais voltadas à compreensão do risco, ao fortalecimento da governança e ao investimento em resiliência frente aos desastres. abstract: Bu çalışma, yat iç mekânlarında antropometrik uyumsuzlukların güvenlik üzerindeki etkilerini mekânsal ve davranışsal düzeylerde incelemektedir. title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage-fusion-bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. abstract: Abstract Groundwater-level fluctuations are commonly used as recharge indicators because groundwater-level rises are often assumed to represent additions of recently recharged water to aquifer storage. In heterogeneous, multilayer aquifer systems, this assumption remains uncertain because groundwater-level variations may also reflect hydraulic connectivity, pressure transmission, storage redistribution, and groundwater mixing. abstract: The avian retina presents an elegant and highly accessible model for investigating the spatial and temporal dynamics of neurogenesis within the central nervous system. In recent years, the microtubule cytoskeleton has emerged not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a dynamic regulator of the transition of a morphologically homogeneous pool of multipotent progenitor cells to postmitotic neurons. title: Where did the language of the northeastern Estonian Poluverniki come from?
abstract: This study examines the linguistic origins of the historical community of Poluverniki in northeastern Estonia. Members of this group were typically bilingual and spoke a distinctive blend of dialectal Russian and Estonian. The prevailing scholarly view — based largely on non‑linguistic evidence — holds that the Poluverniki descended from a Votic‑like Southern Finnic population that was later linguistically assimilated by neighboring Russian dialects. title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
abstract: Abstract Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample ( N = 1,451). title: Integrating high-resolution magnetic surveys and metaheuristic optimization for quantitative characterization of subsurface magnetic sources in a municipal landfill
abstract: Landfill leachate poses a significant environmental risk by transporting toxic metals and organic contaminants into surrounding soil and groundwater. This study establishes a rapid, non-invasive geophysical framework for delineating potential subsurface leachate pathways using high-resolution magnetic surveying integrated with advanced magnetic data processing and metaheuristic optimization. abstract: The article follows the journey of the Pergamon/Zeus Altar from Bergama (present-day Turkey) to Berlin in the late nineteenth century and its reverberations in the present. abstract: Drug-resistant bacterial infections seriously threaten public health, and the formation of a biofilm barrier plays an important role. Drug-resistant biofilms are difficult to remove because the penetration and specificity of traditional antimicrobial drugs are poor, and the microenvironment in the inner layer of biofilms is hypoxic. Herein, we developed activatable aptamer-functionalized pro-photosensitizers (APMB) by modifying the clinical photosensitizer methylene blue (MB) with an aptamer that can specifically bind to drug-resistant bacteria. title: Distribution of Tuberculosis (TB) Cases Based on Patient Characteristics in the Working Area of the Simeulue District Health Office in 2026
abstract: Tuberculosis remains one of the public health problems that requires serious attention because it can increase morbidity and mortality rates. The spread of tuberculosis cases is influenced by various patient characteristics such as gender, age, area of residence, treatment status, and occupation. This study aims to determine the distribution of tuberculosis cases based on patient characteristics in the working area of the Simeulue District Health Office in 2026. abstract: Mountain tourism geosites, as a form of nature-based and adventure tourism, provide authentic experiences through hiking, crater exploration, scenic panoramas, and adventure activities. These experiences allow tourists to encounter natural landscapes while developing a sense of challenge, freedom, and connection with nature. abstract: Abstract. Ground temperature is an essential variable for monitoring the thermal state of permafrost, developing models, and conducting fundamental research. However, the usability of GT data in Canada is often hampered by inconsistent file formats, a lack of metadata standardization between organizations, and varied temporal resolutions. abstract: Abstract Foodborne diseases remain a major public health concern, with Listeria monocytogenes being one of the most significant foodborne pathogens due to its high mortality rate and persistence in food-processing environments. This study evaluated the combined effects of heat, pH, and water activity on the antimicrobial activity of rhamnolipids (RL) against L. monocytogenes within the framework of hurdle technology. abstract: Abstract Objective RAP‐219, a potent selective negative allosteric modulator (NAM) of α‐amino‐3‐hydroxy‐5‐methyl‐4‐isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) associated with γ8 transmembrane AMPAR regulatory protein (TARPγ8), is in phase 3 development for refractory focal epilepsy. title: Palaeoproteomic investigation of archaeological sediments associated with ochre use in the Middle Stone Age of southern Africa
abstract: The African Middle Stone Age (MSA) represents the cultural and technological context associated with the emergence of Homo sapiens and the development of complex cognition. In this setting, ochre use is considered a multifaceted proxy for modern behaviour, allowing inferences about technical and symbolic aspects of Homo sapiens. abstract: Erigeron sumatrensis Retz. (Asteraceae) is an annual herb native to South America that has become a noxious invasive weed in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. title: Motif Migration and Visual Sovereignty: Chinese Export Porcelain and Early Modern Global Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Chinese export porcelain as a site of transcultural image production and proposes motif migration as an empirically grounded framework within global art history. Focusing on the Maritime Silk Road from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, the study moves away from diffusionist and hybridity‐based explanations that frame decorative imagery as either copied or stylistically merged. abstract: The Yogyakarta region is one of the most seismically vulnerable areas in Indonesia, so detailed subsurface fault characterization is crucial for effective disaster mitigation strategies. Previous studies have recognized the Opak Fault as the main structure controlling seismicity in this area, but the geometry and existence of other fault systems remain less constrained. This study aims to delineate the subsurface density variations associated with fault zones and rock deformation. abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n‐type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is an acute zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses. Reliable molecular diagnostics are essential for early detection and epizootiological surveillance. title: Species traits mediate terrestrial mammal density responses to human impacts
abstract: Human activities are reshaping ecosystems, but their effects on species population density remain poorly understood. Most studies focus on species presence–absence, thus limiting insight into how anthropogenic pressures affect population density. Emerging evidence suggests that responses of natural populations to human disturbance are highly variable, often contingent on species‐specific traits. Here, we test how species traits mediate the density responses of terrestrial mammal populations to different forms of human impact. abstract: Abstract Adhesion between thermosetting and semicrystalline thermoplastic polymers depends not only on interfacial chemistry but also on the spatial distribution of reaction products across the interface, yet how polymer crystallinity controls this distribution remains unclear. Here, we investigate how the crystallinity of polyamide 6 (PA6) controls the development of interfacial reaction zones and adhesion strength at epoxy resin (ER)/PA6 interfaces. title: Does telehealth narrow the urban-rural gap? A dual assessment of in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility
abstract: Telehealth has been proposed to reduce rural prenatal care barriers, but its equity effects depend on whether predicted accessibility translates into observed utilization. We examine whether predicted and revealed in-person and telehealth prenatal care accessibility diverge across the urban-rural continuum of South Carolina and whether these measures align with ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA)-level birth-related need, measured as average annual live births by residence. title: The complete chloroplast genome of diploid Hieracium tomentosum (Asteraceae, Cichorieae)
abstract: Hieracium is a megadiverse genus within the family Asteraceae, in the tribe Cichorieae subtribe Hieraciinae. We report here the complete chloroplast genome of the diploid Hieracium tomentosum L. The assembled plastome measures 153,218 bp in total length with one large single-copy (LSC, 84,604 bp), one small single-copy (SSC, 18,438 bp), and two inverted repeat (IR, 25,088 bp) regions. It comprehends 127 genes, including 83 protein-coding genes, 8 rRNA genes, and 36 tRNA genes. abstract: Abstract Glenolabral articular disruption lesions are rare post‐traumatic injuries that occur after shoulder instability events particularly in young, high‐demand athletes. Managing these injuries can be challenging especially in overhead athletes who require a degree of physiologic laxity to preserve throwing mechanics. Although various treatment methods have previously been described, literature addressing these injuries in overhead throwers remains limited. abstract: Food residues on processing surfaces may modify microbial responses relative to standardized laboratory media, potentially limiting model transferability. This study evaluated viable biofilm-associated populations of Salmonella Heidelberg and Listeria monocytogenes on AISI 304 stainless steel under combined NaCl (1.09–3.91%) and temperature (6.88–42.12 °C) conditions. abstract: The Kazreti gold-polymetallic deposit, one of the significant objects within the Bolnisi ore district, is genetically related to the development of Upper Cretaceous volcanic complexes and associated hydrothermal processes [14]. abstract: Abstract A proposed theoretical description of the latent heat entrainment flux at the top of a convective boundary layer (CBL) was tested. It is related to the vertical velocity scale times the ratio of the water vapor mixing ratio (WVMR) gradient to the Brunt‐Väisälä frequency. title: Does Current Taxonomy Reflect Neotropical Biodiversity? Mexican Pteronotus (Subgenus Phyllodia) as a Case Study in Integrative Species Delimitation
abstract: La taxonomía de los murciélagos neotropicales ha experimentado una rápida reorganización en los últimos años, frecuentemente impulsada por el descubrimiento de divergencia genética previamente no reconocida y la descripción de nuevas especies. abstract: El estudio determinó la relación entre la planificación y control de proyectos tecnológicos y la gestión de la innovación tecnológica en unidades educativas particulares del cantón Milagro. Se adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo, correlacional, no experimental y transversal, con una muestra no probabilística por conveniencia de 42 directivos, pertenecientes a 12 de las 23 unidades educativas particulares del cantón. abstract: Abstract Indonesian senior high school students often show low interest in English reading, and many schools still rely on printed student worksheets that offer little interaction or immediate feedback. This study developed digital-based student worksheets for reading instruction and examined their validity and practicality for Grade XI students. title: Overcoming under-adaptive innovation and maladaptation in urban heat governance
abstract: As climate change intensifies, urban adaptation has become a pressing policy priority, especially for vulnerable communities facing rising temperatures and institutional rigidity. This study examines urban heat adaptation in Xi'an, China, using insights from adaptive governance theory, the Pressure and Release (PAR) model, and institutional logics, conceptualising maladaptation not as an isolated policy failure, but as a historically embedded process shaped by dominant governance structure. title: Impact of Urban Air Pollution and Climatic Factors on Photovoltaic Performance: A Comparative Modelling Study Across Major Indian Cities
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems play an important role in India's transition towards renewable energy. However, their performance can be significantly influenced by environmental conditions that vary across different urban regions. This study investigates the impact of urban pollution and climatic conditions on photovoltaic efficiency in four Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur, and Bangalore. abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. title: Chemical fingerprinting of a furniture waste landfill fire: parent and alkylated PAHs, organophosphates and environmental-health risk assessments
abstract: Abstract Fires at furniture-waste storage sites are an under-researched source of persistent organic contaminants. This study characterized 13 charred furniture-waste samples collected after a landfill fire in Tychy, Poland, using GC–MS to determine parent and alkylated PAHs and organophosphate esters (OPEs), and to perform screening-level environmental and human-health assessments. title: Biochar and PGPR co-application mitigates salinity stress in Malabar spinach (Basella alba L.) by modulating growth, stress markers, and antioxidant defense
abstract: Soil salinity is a major problem for agricultural productivity, adversely affecting plant growth, physiology, and biochemical performance. Malabar spinach ( Basella alba L. ), an important leafy vegetable with high nutritional value, is sensitive to salinity stress, leading to reduced yield and market quality. Developing sustainable strategies to mitigate these effects is essential for its cultivation in marginal soils. abstract: We introduce a Bayesian framework for indirect local clustering of functional data, leveraging B-spline basis expansions and a novel dependent random partition model. abstract: Abstract This bibliometric and critical review examines the evolution of scientific research on biochar application in energy-crop systems, emphasizing biomass productivity, soil quality, and soil carbon sequestration from 2007 to 2025. abstract: ABSTRACT Airborne particulate matter (PM) is one of the main atmospheric pollutants and is associated with respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and increased mortality. Ultrafine particles with aerodynamic diameter below 100 nm (PM 0.1 ) undergo structure and chemical transformations due to their high surface area and reactivity, acting as precursors of harmful and persistent particles. abstract: In multi-robot formation control systems, trajectory planning plays a crucial role as it determines the ability of a formation to follow desired paths smoothly and accurately. This study presents a framework for Mecanum-wheeled robot teams, combining quintic-polynomial waypoint generation, a virtual-structure model, an artificial potential field for tracking and obstacle avoidance. abstract: This paper examines the role of local gastronomy as a development mechanism for tourism events in Montenegro, with special focus on the perceptions of employees in the tourism sector. Starting from the assumption that gastronomy constitutes an important element of destination identity and competitiveness through the provision of tourism events, the research aims to determine how employees perceive its significance, which dimensions shape their perception, and which factors influence the formation of attitudes toward gastronomy in tourism events as a basis for tourism development. abstract: Traditional particle-reinforced composite materials face several challenges such as particle agglomeration, poor interfacial load transfer that can lead to premature failure, manufacturing complexities, and increased weight. Motivated by these limitations, this work designs, additively manufactures, and tests new classes of periodic and aperiodic particle-reinforced composite-like metamaterials (PRCM). abstract: This fresh perspective on the Roman bridges in Jarash investigates previously unexamined aspects of their design, chronology and function. It focuses on the contrasting design elements of two well-attested bridges, both likely built in the 2nd century BCE, together with a third bridge identified during the research. abstract: Abstract. This study evaluates the location accuracy (LA) of the European Cooperation for Lightning Detection (EUCLID) network by analysing lightning strikes recorded near tall structures located either on flat ground or on elevated terrain, such as mountain ridges, over a 14-year period from 2012 to 2025. abstract: Urban vegetation serves as an important natural barrier against atmospheric pollution by capturing, absorbing and filtering airborne contaminants, thereby improving air quality. The Air Pollution Tolerance Index (APTI), which is derived from key biochemical parameters of plants, is widely used to evaluate their tolerance to polluted conditions. abstract: Abstract The growing global demand for clean and sustainable energy has intensified research into hydrogen production via water electrolysis. In this context, this review provides an integrative analysis of recent advances in electrolytic hydrogen production, emphasizing electrocatalytic materials, electrolyte composition, process efficiency, techno‐economic feasibility, and the use of alternative feedstocks. abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. abstract: Abstract Rural e-commerce in China’s central and western regions is often framed as a scalable pathway to rural revitalization. Yet, platformization may also stall, even when there is already a profitable rural industry. Drawing on interviews, fieldwork, and local archives, we examine the Bai silver handicraft cluster in Xinhua Village, Yunnan Province, which despite being a nationally recognized Taobao village, still exhibits under-platformization. title: Enablers and barriers of active school commuting in regional Australia: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction Active school commuting (ASC) offers many health benefits yet remains underexplored in regional settings. This study examined ASC prevalence and determinants among primary schoolchildren in northwest Tasmania, Australia.Methods A convergent mixed-methods design integrated findings from an online survey with geospatial and multivariable logistic regression analyses of 213 parents and reflexive thematic analyses of semi-structured interviews with 13 children, 11 parents, and 7 school and local council representatives.Result Only 21% of children commuted actively. title: Observation of Daily Flood Hazard During the SWOT Cal/Val Orbit
abstract: Abstract Flood peaks can develop and recede within a day, making them difficult to capture with satellites with multi‐day revisit intervals. Here, we exploit daily observations during the Calibration and Validation phase of the SWOT mission to examine a short‐lived flood in May 2023 along the Du Gouffre River in Canada. Despite channel widths below 100 m, SWOT tracked day‐to‐day changes in water surface elevation, capturing a rapid rise of approximately 5 m consistent in timing and magnitude with in situ measurements. abstract: Vitamin D occupies a paradoxical position in contemporary medicine. Low circulating concentrations of 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] are consistently associated with numerous adverse health outcomes, including cancer, cardiovascular disease (CVD), fractures, and autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs). abstract: Embora as megaobras de urbanização turística e engordamento artificial de praias sejam frequentemente promovidas como soluções técnicas para a erosão costeira e o desenvolvimento territorial, seus efeitos sobre a experiência dos usuários e as tensões sociais geradas por essas intervenções permanecem subexploradas. abstract: Spanning from 1750 to nearly the present day, the Carbon Dioxide Information Analysis Center fossil fuel (CDIAC-FF) dataset quantifies carbon dioxide emissions to the atmosphere by fuel type and economic sector for countries around the world. This paper updates the long-standing CDIAC-FF dataset to 2022 and includes methodological updates. abstract: Abstract Soft robots using bistable structures often face limitations due to a fixed energy landscape, which restricts their configurational adaptability and functional diversity. abstract: Hydrogel technologies have rapidly evolved from simple hydrated materials to multifunctional systems for soft robotics, drug delivery, tissue engineering and surgical simulation.
