title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal‐Bacteria Interactions
abstract: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions

title: The Evolution, Demise, and Renaissance of Green Spaces in Dar es Salaam: An Explorative Discourse on Influential Factors
abstract: Urban green spaces in African cities are under unprecedented pressure from rapid urbanisation, yet the factors influencing their utilisation remain poorly understood. This paper examines the determinants of green space use in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, one of Africa's fastest-growing metropolitan areas. This study employs a mixed-methods approach across 42 green spaces in three municipalities, drawing on Attention Restoration Theory, Place Attachment Theory, and the Ecological Model of Physical Activity. title: DOE-Driven Synthesis of Bio-based Itaconate Polyester: A Solvent-Free and Catalyst-Free Approach
abstract: Producing polymeric products from renewable raw materials is desirable to reduce reliance on petrochemical-based materials. To date, toxic acrylic monomers and their derivatives are most commonly used in applications such as UV-crosslinked materials. Itaconate compounds are considered as potential “green alternatives” for acrylic compounds because of their similar chemical structure. title: The significance of global identity in shaping individual behaviour and policy support: Focus on plastic purchasing and consumption
abstract: Abstract Background Global identity (GI), a sense of belonging to a global society, is gaining attention as a key factor for promoting pro‐environmental behaviours (PEB) to tackle the global environmental crisis. Among such global predicaments, plastic waste and pollution remain pressing issues. Although prior research has established a link between GI and PEB, the underlying psychological pathways have not been comprehensively explored. title: First record of albinism for the hairy-legged vampire bat, Diphylla ecaudata Spix, 1823 (Mammalia, Chiroptera, Phyllostomidae),and a review of cases of albinism in the Neotropics
abstract: Albinismo é uma anomalia cromática caracterizada pela falta da melanina na pele, pelos e olhos. Há pelo menos 67 espécies de morcegos com registro de albinismo, mas esse número representa apenas 4,5% de todas as espécies do mundo, indicando que é uma anomalia rara. Registros de albinismo em morcegos na região Neotropical são ainda mais raros, enfatizando a importância de se registrar os casos eventuais. journal: Boletim do Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi - Ciências Naturais

title: The role of particle size on the combustion regimes of iron in dust flames
abstract: Unlike gaseous fuels, which are fully characterized by chemical composition, metal fuels also vary in particle size. This paper investigates the effect of particle size on laminar flame propagation in iron particle suspensions with oxygen–argon and oxygen–helium carrier gases. Using a McGill Bunsen-type metal-fuel burner, pure iron flames are stabilized across a broad range of fuel concentrations. title: Feasibility and clinical outcomes of routine point‐of‐care screening for opportunistic infections among people with advanced HIV disease in Guyana
abstract: Abstract Objectives We evaluated the feasibility and outcomes of implementing comprehensive Point‐of‐care (POC) opportunistic infections (OIs) screening among people with Advanced HIV disease (AHD) in Guyana. Methods We conducted a prospective multicentre cohort study across seven sites between February 2024 and March 2025. Adults with suspected AHD, defined as CD4 <200 cells/mm 3 or signs/symptoms suggestive of OIs, were enrolled. title: Infrequent, high-volume rainfall events modulate acorn production for two common oak species in Western North Carolina, USA
abstract: Variations in landscape-scale acorn production have been studied across the Quercus genus to understand its role in ecosystem ecology and forest regeneration. Multiple weather conditions may influence annual acorn production, especially the positive influence of seasonal rainfall. Prior studies have assessed the effects of rainfall measured over monthly and seasonal scales, but have not focused on the potential influence of daily rainfall events (e.g., frequency and volume) on acorn production. abstract: Avicennia marina (Forssk.) Vierh. is an important mangrove plant with high nutritional and medicinal values, featuring saccharides as its primary bioactive compounds. In this study, we successfully isolated a neutral tetrasaccharide (AMO-1) from the fruits of A. marina. title: From Guided-Tour Priorities to Tourist Advocacy: Factors Associated with Value for Money and Intentions to Recommend in South Africa’s Western Cape
abstract: This exploratory study examines whether stated guided-tour priorities and tourist characteristics are associated with value-for-money evaluations and positive recommendations in South Africa’s Western Cape, and whether value adds explanatory information to tourist advocacy. Survey data from 451 participants were analysed using descriptive statistics, bivariate tests, hierarchical binary logistic regression and robustness checks. title: Superpiles: The Impact of Mantle Temperature on Large Low Velocity Provinces
abstract: Abstract Among the most prevalent features in Earth's deep mantle are the Large Low Velocity Provinces (LLVPs), hypothesized to be hotter and compositionally distinct from the surrounding mantle. LLVPs have previously been viewed as either active superplumes rising through the mantle or passive piles shaped by large scale convection. Recent tomography models suggest LLVPs may exhibit a plume‐shaped morphology. Geodynamic experiments offer insights into the formation, characteristics, and evolution of mantle structures. title: Eco Comics in Environmental Education: Bibliometric Mapping and Review of Elementary School Studies
abstract: Eco-comics provide visual narratives for environmental learning, but the scope of the literature and the outcomes assessed in elementary schools remain unclear. This review combines bibliometric mapping of the broader literature with a descriptive synthesis of elementary school studies. Scopus records retrieved on 1 September 2026 were screened with reference to PRISMA 2020; 135 articles were mapped bibliometrically, and six empirical elementary school studies were synthesized descriptively. title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant‐ and fungal‐derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. institutions: The University of Texas at Austin

title: AhR ligands in necrotizing enterocolitis: a provisional evidence map of ligand-specific biology and translational considerations
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains a major cause of gastrointestinal morbidity and mortality in preterm infants, with no targeted mechanism-based therapy. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling is an emerging host-microbe interface because it integrates dietary, microbial, milk-derived, and host-derived ligands that regulate intestinal inflammation, epithelial homeostasis, and barrier integrity. title: First cytogenetic characterization of the southern pygmy perch Nannoperca australis (Teleostei: Percichthyidae): Karyotype, heterochromatin and repetitive DNA organization
abstract: Abstract Chromosome organization and repetitive DNA distribution are important components of genome evolution in teleost fishes but remain poorly characterized in many species of ecological and conservation relevance. We performed a detailed cytogenetic analysis of the southern pygmy perch, Nannoperca australis , a small freshwater species widely used in studies of population structure and evolutionary ecology in southeastern Australia. title: Response-surface optimization of high-performance GO-PET-PEG forward osmosis membranes for bentazone removal
abstract: In this work, a single-layer forward osmosis (FO) nanocomposite membrane was developed and tested for bentazone removal from aqueous systems. Unlike conventional dual-layer thin-film composite membranes, this architecture, incorporating graphene oxide (GO) as a nanofiller and polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a pore-forming agent in a recycled PET matrix, eliminates interfacial defects between layers while simplifying fabrication. title: Phenotypic Antimicrobial Resistance Dynamics Across Varying Clinical Severity Scores of Ovine Footrot Lesions
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is an ancient phenomenon and an increasing global threat affecting animal, human, and environmental health. Its emergence is largely driven by the extensive use of antimicrobials in medicine and agriculture, while bacterial mutations, natural evolution, and horizontal gene transfer further promote the acquisition and spread of resistance genes. title: Working Right Ways: Investigating Health Practitioners' Perspectives of Foot Health and Needs for Providing Good Foot Care With and for First Nations Peoples
abstract: BACKGROUND: History of invasion, ongoing colonisation, and systemic racism excluding First Nations Peoples from healthcare are root causes of health inequalities including disparities in foot health outcomes. Sources of inquiry into current practice, learning, and experience, which may shape reform of providing good foot care with and for First Nations Peoples in the land now known as Australia are health practitioners working in the space. title: Identification of Chaperonin10 as a gene necessary for tolerance to root heat stress in rice
abstract: Due to global warming, crops are exposed to heat stress more frequently. This may reduce yields, hence heat-tolerant varieties are needed. For this, it is important to identify genes governing heat tolerance. In this study we identified a line that is sensitive to high temperature in roots, and through QTL analysis we identified a gene associated with heat tolerance in rice. title: Geologically constrained dynamic evolution and early warning of urban resource-environment carrying capacity: a case study of Jinan, China
abstract: Urban resource environment carrying capacity (RECC) is increasingly challenged by nonlinear interactions among socioeconomic development, resource depletion, and geological environmental degradation. However, existing assessments often neglect the cumulative feedback effects of groundwater depletion and geological responses. This study develops a city-scale system dynamics (SD) model integrating six subsystems (population–economy, land, water resources, ecology, environment, and geological environment) to simulate RECC evolution in Jinan, China, during 2021–2031. title: Ethogram of zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) after exposure to nitrates
abstract: Abstract Nitrate pollution is one of the most widespread forms of contamination, and in high concentrations has adverse effects on aquatic ecosystems. Fish are susceptible to this contaminant and are known to modify their behaviour in a variety of ways when exposed, but most information regarding changes in behaviour pertains only to long‐term or chronic exposure. But in the multiple-receiver WPT system, the power level at the individual load decreases by increasing number of receiver loads. Thus, there is a critical limit to the number of receivers which supposed to be driven with predetermined amount of power for specific input power level. abstract: OBJECTIVES: Despite more than a decade of expanded influenza vaccine access through Medicare, pharmacy-based programs, and community clinics, older African Americans remain vaccinated at markedly lower rates than older White and Asian adults. This study examines why the disparity has persisted and whether U.S. vaccination policy evidence was ever designed to address it. title: A Radiation‐Modulated Frost Index Improves the Representation of Frost Stress and Yield Response in Winter Wheat
abstract: ABSTRACT Late spring frost is a major abiotic stress affecting winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production, yet its impact on yield remains difficult to quantify because crop responses depend not only on the intensity of low‐temperature exposure but also on environmental conditions following frost events. Conventional frost indices are primarily temperature‐based and therefore do not fully capture variability in yield responses under comparable thermal stress conditions. title: Factores asociados a la adopción de tecnologías digitales en UEPS del cantón Santa Rosa
abstract: El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar los factores asociados a la adopción de tecnologías digitales en las Unidades de Economía Popular y Solidaria (UEPS) del cantón Santa Rosa considerando variables como el acceso a recursos tecnológicos, la capacitación, la percepción de beneficios, las barreras percibidas, el apoyo institucional y la cultura organizacional. La investigación se desarrolló bajo un enfoque cuantitativo con diseño no experimental, mediante la aplicación de una encuesta estructurada de escala Likert a una muestra de 150 UEPS. title: Comportamiento leal del consumidor en el contexto de la dermocosmética
abstract: Este estudio analiza los factores que determinan la fidelidad del consumidor en la adquisición de productos de dermocosmética y examina la influencia de la satisfacción generada por la interacción, el entorno de tienda y el resultado de la experiencia de compra en distintos formatos de distribución. Se aplicó una metodología cuantitativa mediante un cuestionario de 60 ítems, estructurado en tres dimensiones de la calidad del servicio, disponiendo de una muestra formada por 313 consumidores. abstract: This study investigated the effect of annealing temperature on the microstructure and electrochemical behavior of commercially pure titanium (CP Ti) subjected to cold rolling and heat treatments between 400 and 900°C. Microstructural characterization and microhardness measurements were performed, along with potentiodynamic polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) tests in artificial saliva following exposure to a fluoridated agent. abstract: Gas drainage boreholes easily suffer hole wall collapse and coal particle blockage under in-situ stress and mining disturbance, drastically lowering gas extraction efficiency. To avoid the drawbacks of traditional dredging technologies, including drainage interruption and borehole wall damage, a gas pulse blockage removal method is proposed to achieve non-contact dredging using transient high-pressure gas. title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract: Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. title: Identifying forest features that increase resiliency of southern‐boundary snowshoe hare populations in Pennsylvania
abstract: Abstract Forest management is a potential tool to increase the resiliency of snowshoe hare ( Lepus americanus ) populations to the negative demographic impacts of low‐snowfall winters. Pennsylvania's forests and landscape differ from those of the core snowshoe hare range, and region‐specific data are needed to optimize forest management for snowshoe hares. We used spatial capture‐recapture to model snowshoe hare population density on 10 forested sites in northwestern Pennsylvania, USA, in winter 2024. abstract: Thin films of α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite) are desirable materials for optoelectronic, sensing, photocatalytic and photoelectrochemical applications. Fe₂O₃ thin film was deposited on glass using hydrothermal method using concentration of FeCl₃.6H₂O 0.25 M at PH 3.0, treated at 160 °C for 4 h and annealed at 500 °C for 5 h. title: Structural control of Fe(II)-based multivalent glycan assemblies enables intramolecular avidity and ultra-high-affinity binding
abstract: Abstract Multivalent glycan recognition depends critically on the spatial organization of saccharides, yet quantitative design rules linking glycan geometry to binding remain poorly defined. Here, we report atomically-precise Fe(II)-based glycoassemblies that enable independent control of glycan valency, spacing, and topology within discrete molecular scaffolds. Using monomeric Griffithsin as a model lectin, we uncover that subtle changes in glycan presentation drive discrete transitions from partial site engagement to high-avidity, multi-site binding, spanning a > 10³-fold range in affinity.

title: Does an Increase in Renewable Energy Production Reduce Net Energy Imports?
abstract: Renewable energy plays a key role in the energy transition to combat climate change and, more recently, has become an important instrument for enhancing energy security. It is generally expected that expanding renewable energy will displace fossil fuel consumption and reduce fossil fuel imports. However, if energy demand grows more rapidly, the relationship between renewable energy expansion and fossil fuel imports becomes less straightforward, often leading to skepticism about the role of renewable energy. abstract: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells. abstract: Biliary ascites is a rare form of ascites resulting from disruption of biliary tract integrity, and spontaneous, non-traumatic, non-iatrogenic perforation of the gallbladder or bile ducts is an exceptionally uncommon cause in adults. We report a 65-year-old man who presented with right upper quadrant pain, jaundice, fever, diarrhea, and progressive abdominal distension following an episode of untreated choledocholithiasis. title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
abstract: Soils are Earth's largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0-90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. title: Risk mapping with community participation: strategies for risk and disaster management
abstract: Risk must be understood as a social construction; public participation is thus essential for the development of integrated plans and policies that are effective and sustainable. This action-research presents participatory mapping carried out in the community of Guarará, municipality of Franco da Rocha, São Paulo, Brazil. abstract: This study presents the implementation and performance evaluation of an Adaptive Inertia-Related Controller (AIRC) designed for the joint-space control of a low-cost robotic manipulator. Addressing the limitations of traditional Proportional-Derivative (PD) controllers, particularly operating in dynamic uncertainty conditions and with low sensor-motor accuracy, the applied AIRC adaptively estimates real-time dynamic model parameters to achieve robust and precise trajectory tracking. abstract: The imperative objective of developing countries is rapid economic growth, and exports are considered an engine of that growth. This study aimed to identify the key targets and mechanisms by which gut microbiota metabolites regulate ATB-DILI. METHODS: Integrative bioinformatics was used to screen for common targets shared by gut microbiota metabolites and ATB-DILI. The target list was refined through protein-protein interaction network and hub gene analyses. title: Stories from ‘Who Cares?’ : Cultivating a Community of Aging Care on the Sunshine Coast, British Columbia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Canada's rapidly aging population poses unique challenges for rural and remote communities such as the Sunshine Coast, British Columbia. METHODS: Qualitative data were gathered from numerous community gatherings and twelve one-on-one interviews. abstract: Ancient Quranic manuscripts constitute an important part of Islamic cultural heritage, preserving the history of Quranic transmission, religious scholarship, and manuscript traditions in the Indonesian archipelago. However, the sustainability of these manuscripts is increasingly threatened by aging materials, environmental conditions, and limited conservation management. abstract: Abstract Glucosinolates (GLS) in Brassicaceae crops are known to suppress soil nitrification. Despite widespread inclusion of Brassicaceae species in pulse crop rotations, their effects on soil nitrification and root nodulation of subsequent pulse crops are poorly understood. abstract: This paper examines Titian’s Bacchus and Ariadne through an iconographic and philosophicalanalysis, employing Friedrich Nietzsche’s concepts of the Apollonian and Dionysian asarticulated in The Birth of Tragedy. abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) refers to disposed electrical and electronic equipment. In Bangladesh, e-waste offers resource potential as well as environmental concern. abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the impact of raw material thermal history (chilled vs. defrosted) and 12-month frozen storage (-18 °C) on the quality of mechanically separated common carp (Cyprinus carpio). abstract: Pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and polyphenols are increasingly detected in aquatic environments, impacting water quality and aquatic life. abstract: Abstract Restoring xylem water transport function after drought is central to plant drought adaptation. Embolism refilling, a key mechanism for recovering water transport capacity, remains debated regarding its generality and mechanistic basis. This review synthesizes four decades of research on xylem embolism refilling, tracing developments from early theoretical constraints and positive-pressure refilling models to phloem-mediated refilling under low tension. abstract: Biochar, as a soil amendment, offers several benefits, including increased soil fertility, carbon (C) sequestration, and improved water-holding capacity in nutrient-poor soils. This study assesses the impact of adding different rates of pine biochar to sandy peach-tree orchard soils on the relative abundance and structure of soil microbial communities (bacteria and fungi) after one year. abstract: Abstract Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. abstract: Systemic risk in critical infrastructure is often analyzed through physical, geographic, and cyber interdependencies. Yet infrastructures are also interdependent through the governing rules that organize human action. These rule-mediated connections are a form of logical interdependency, and breakdowns in rule-governed action can create pathways through which disruption spreads. title: Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth
abstract: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. title: Fabrication of Bifunctional UHMWPE Composites With Self‐Lubricating and Self‐Repairing Capabilities via Core‐Shell MSNs ‐ PFPE @ PEW Particles
abstract: ABSTRACT In mechanical systems, the energy dissipation and wear caused by friction usually lead to the failure of materials during their service life, thereby driving the demand for polymer composite materials with both tribological properties and self‐repairing capabilities. Studying polymer composites with self‐lubrication and self‐repairing functions is an effective approach. title: Biochemical profile of oxidative and antioxidant changes in sheep with clinical pneumonia
abstract: This study characterized systemic oxidative and antioxidant changes in sheep with clinical pneumonia. Twenty sheep diagnosed with clinical pneumonia were compared with 20 individually matched healthy controls. Total antioxidant status (TAS), total oxidant status (TOS), oxidative stress index (OSI), paraoxonase-1 (PON1), arylesterase (ARE), total sialic acid (TSA), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) were assessed. title: Heterogeneity of child and adolescent asthma determinants across urbanization stages: a 21-year global analysis
abstract: Urbanization reshapes environmental exposures, lifestyle, and health systems, yet global evidence on how child and adolescent asthma risk factors evolve across development stages remains limited. Using panel data from 149 countries (2000–2020), this study applied clustering and coupling coordination analysis to identify stage-specific pathways of urbanization and air quality transitions. Generalized additive models were subsequently employed to explore the heterogeneity of asthma determinants across these stages. Four evolution stages were identified: Early Urbanization with Emerging Pollution
institutions: Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research

title: Causal inference in conservation policy: Evaluating the effects of Protected Areas on deforestation and well-being in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: The Peruvian Amazon, one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth, is under increasing pressure from deforestation, threatening both ecological wealth and local livelihoods. Protected Areas (PAs) have emerged as one of the main conservation strategies; however, questions remain regarding their effectiveness in reducing deforestation and their socioeconomic impact. This study evaluates the effects of PAs, their Buffer Zones (BZs), and Regional Conservation Areas (RCAs) on deforestation and household welfare between 2001 and 2023. title: Integrating land-use and climate connectivity to link protected areas at the country level
abstract: Abstract Context Ecological corridors that are high in biodiversity potential and stable under climate change are central to long-term conservation planning. Yet spatial prioritization frameworks rarely integrate land-use resistance and climate stability into a unified approach, limiting their operational value for landscape management and policy. title: To stop or not? Mediterranean migrants differ in both arrival condition and refuelling success after barrier crossing
abstract: Understanding refuelling performance at stopover sites is central to elucidating the migration strategies of passerines, particularly at Mediterranean landfall islands where birds arrive after crossing major ecological barriers. We investigated fuel deposition dynamics and potential flight range in five long‐distance migrant passerines (Great Reed Warbler, Sedge Warbler, Common Nightingale, Wood Warbler and Garden Warbler) using long‐term ringing data (2007–2024) from the Antikythera Bird Observatory, Greece. title: Revision of Neanderthal Activity Zones at Kůlna Cave: Use-Wear Analysis of the Micoquian Lithic Industry
abstract: Abstract Investigating the spatial organisation of Neanderthal sites offers critical insights into their behavioural patterns, adaptive strategies, and site use. Studying how different lithic tools are organised in space and linked to specific functions is therefore essential. Kůlna Cave provides evidence of multiple occupation areas characterised by distinct activity patterns, making it a particularly suitable Neanderthal site for investigating spatial organisation and testing related hypotheses. institutions: Interdisciplinary Center for Archaeology and the Evolution of Human Behaviour

title: Updating the Coordinates of Itera Geodetic Benchmarks Based on the ITRF2020 Global Reference Frame
abstract: The International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF) is a global reference framework essential for maintaining the consistency and precision of positioning results in response to ongoing geodynamic changes. The adoption of ITRF2020 requires updates to geodetic control point coordinates to ensure compliance with international reference standards. This study aims to update the benchmark coordinates at Itera based on the ITRF2020 global reference frame. Observations were conducted using the static GNSS network method constrained to InaCORS and IGS reference stations. Observation data quality was

title: Integrating social science into conservation practice: Evidence from environmental non‐governmental organization publications and practitioner perspectives
abstract: Abstract Social science is critical to conservation success, yet has not become mainstream. To better understand its current state and drivers and barriers to its application, we analyzed 700 peer‐reviewed articles with co‐authors from the 4 largest (“dominant”) international environmental non‐governmental organizations (ENGOs) 1998–2023 and interviewed pairs of scientists and conservation managers at 4 geographically dispersed projects at The Nature Conservancy (TNC). title: Turtle shells, trade-offs, and t -tests: using 3D-printed models to explore morphological evolution and its functional consequences
abstract: Abstract River cooters (Pseudemys concinna) are a novel and compelling system in which to study adaptations and trade-offs in biology teaching labs. This species of turtle lives in the southeastern United States in both fast-moving (lotic) waters lacking predators, and slow-flowing (lentic) waters inhabited by alligators. We used a high-resolution CT scan to create realistic 3D-printed models of P. concinna shells with a range of shell-arching ratios (height/length) published in the literature. title: Beyond the Green Premium: A Discrete Choice Experiment on Tourists’ Multi-Attribute Preferences
abstract: Aimed growing global concern for sustainability, green consumption has become an important topic in tourism research, influencing both industry practices and tourist behavior. Yet tourists’ preferences for green tourism products are inherently complex and context-dependent, requiring trade-offs among multiple attributes such as price, quality, and environmental performance. This study explores tourists’ preferences for green tourism packages and the underlying price-response mechanisms in a multi-attribute context. Based on random utility theory, this study develops a discrete choice experimen
journal: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity
abstract: Abstract The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. title: Gross and Histopathological Charactersation of Pulmonary Abscessation due to Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli in a Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus): A Case Report
abstract: Bacterial lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) can result in severe and fatal diseases in non-human primates (NHPs), and the disease process of pulmonary abscessation in the Collared Mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus), an endangered West and Central African cercopithecid, has been underreported. A gross and histopathological evaluation of a 12-year-old captive female C. torquatus that had a 14-month history of intermittent coughing and that had a polymicrobial co-infection with S. aureus and E. coli is presented. title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
abstract: Abstract Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. title: Thiochromene Analogues as Antiparasitic Chemotype: Synthesis, Antiplasmodial and Antitrypanosomal Profiling, Experimental Validation, and Computational Insights into Trypanothione Reductase Inhibition
abstract: Abstract The emergence of drug resistance and the limited availability of effective therapeutics continue to hinder the treatment of protozoal diseases, highlighting the need for new chemotypes with broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. In the present study, a series of nitro and trifluoromethyl-substituted thiochromene carboxamides, previously identified as antileishmanial agents, were further explored for their broad-spectrum antiparasitic potential. institutions: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

title: Environmental Footprint of Kerala’s Coir Processing Transitions
abstract: This article examines the historical transition of Kerala’s coir industry from traditional retting practices to mechanized production, highlighting the shifting burdens on ecosystems and workers. Retting once imposed severe localized pollution on aquatic systems, with high biochemical oxygen demand and phenolic loading creating anoxic conditions, while mechanization reduced reliance on water bodies but introduced energy intensity, synthetic effluents, and hazardous occupational exposures. title: Protected-area-based nature-based governance and green-blue infrastructure-to-built conversion: spatial regression discontinuity evidence from Kinmen National Park, Taiwan
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) and green-blue infrastructure (GBI) are increasingly promoted for sustainable built environments, yet boundary-based evidence on specific land-conversion mechanisms remains limited. This study evaluates Kinmen National Park, Taiwan, using a spatial regression discontinuity design (Spatial RDD) on 30 m grid cells for 2014–2024. GBI-to-built conversion (G2B) is the primary outcome; strict built-up change, developed-land change, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) change, and GBI fragmentation are contrasting or secondary outcomes. journal: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering

title: The impact of resilience on psychological well-being through emotional intelligence among students at Islamic boarding schools in Kendal Regency
abstract: Psychological well-being is essential for students' positive development, particularly in Islamic boarding schools, where adolescents must adapt to academic demands, religious responsibilities, and communal living. This study aimed to examine the relationship between resilience and psychological well-being through the mediating role of emotional intelligence among Islamic boarding school students in Kendal Regency, Indonesia. A quantitative approach with an ex-post facto design was employed, involving 387 students selected through multistage cluster sampling. Data were collected using the Ryff

title: Mechanical Irreversibility and Strength Overcompensation in a Gypsum Dehydration–Rehydration Cycle
abstract: Abstract Dehydration–rehydration reactions of hydrous minerals modify rock strength, fluid transport, and deformation in reactive geological environments. Although dehydration‐induced weakening is widely studied, the mechanical consequences of subsequent rehydration remain poorly constrained. We combine triaxial compression tests with microstructural and pore‐network analyses of original gypsum, fully dehydrated anhydrite, and rehydrated gypsum. title: Synergistic Regulation of Defect Density and Electronic Structure in Zr‐Metal‐Organic Frameworks via Selective Ligand Pyrolysis for Efficient Photocatalytic Biomass Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising photocatalysts for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion owing to their well‐defined architectures, tunable porosity, and tailorable coordination environments. However, conventional MOF photocatalysts are predominantly employed as components in composite materials, and direct structural modulation of MOFs themselves to boost photocatalytic performance remains challenging. title: Processed manures sustain silage corn yield with amendment‐specific soil and forage response
abstract: Abstract In semiarid western US dairy systems, field evidence remains limited on whether processed manure products can sustain silage corn ( Zea mays L.) productivity and improve soil health. A field experiment conducted in Logan, UT, during 2021–2022 compared compost, vermicompost, Sedron (a thermally and mechanically processed dairy manure), dissolved air flotation, mineral fertilizer, and unfertilized control for their effects on soil chemical properties, silage corn yield, forage quality, and soil health indicators. title: Morphofunctional indices and ontogeny of long bones of the limbs in the frogs
abstract: Anuran limbs offer a valuable model for exploring how selective pressures, developmental constraints, and morphological evolution interact. While previous research has largely focused on total limb length, little is known about ontogenetic changes in the proportions of individual limb bones. This study introduces a novel approach using morphofunctional indices to investigate the functional roles of frog limbs, linking morphology to habitat use and locomotion. We present morphological and ontogenetic data from anurans in northwestern Argentina, emphasizing functionally relevant bone indices. Me

title: Senior elite swimmers were top-10% youths: A Swedish population cohort study
abstract: We evaluated how well swimming performance at ages 13–15 identified future senior elite status (ages 22–25) in a non-selected national cohort. Using the Swedish federation’s Tempus Open database, we followed 8,965 Swedish-developed swimmers born 1995–2001. Each swimmer’s youth performance was summarized as the maximum within-cohort percentile across ages, events, and pool lengths; the resulting top-10%-in-any-cell filter retained approximately 19% of the cohort. title: Petrographic and magnetic fabric evidence for magmatic emplacement and hydrothermal alteration in the Shadan Au porphyry deposit, Eastern Iran
abstract: Magmatic processes and subsequent hydrothermal alterations within porphyry deposits are well-documented through the analysis of mineral chemistry and the magnetic fabrics of their host intrusions. This study integrates structurs, petrography, mineral chemistry, and anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) data to investigate the evolution of magmatic and hydrothermal fabrics in the Shadan porphyry Au-rich deposit, located in northeastern Iran. Fresh quartz monzodioritic intrusions exhibit primary magmatic fabrics characterized by oblate AMS ellipsoids, predominantly aligned with magnetite.

title: Corrosion Resistance of Boronized Carbon Steel in a Galinstan–Refrigerant Two-Phase Agitated System
abstract: Abstract This study experimentally evaluates, for the first time, the corrosion resistance of boronized carbon steel in environments containing liquid Galinstan (GaInSn) and selected organic refrigerants (n-pentane and R1233zd(E)) at 150 °C for up to 80 days. The tests simulated gas–liquid-metal two-phase exposure under pseudodynamic conditions, where the test coupons and corrosive media were mechanically agitated. title: Seismotectonic Controls on the Toba–Samosir Subsurface Environment Revealed by Double-Difference Earthquake Relocation
abstract: North Sumatra is characterized by complex interactions among the Sumatran Fault System, regional subduction, and the volcanotectonic setting of the Toba Caldera, producing heterogeneous shallow crustal seismicity and structurally controlled subsurface environments. This study investigates the seismotectonic and subsurface structural characteristics of North Sumatra using double-difference earthquake relocation, with particular emphasis on the Toba–Samosir region. title: Polyglycine Strands Within a Collagen Triple Helix
abstract: ABSTRACT The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. title: Indoor temperature and office work performance in a temperate climate
abstract: The relationship between indoor temperature and office work performance (OWP) remains contested. Previous laboratory studies, including a controlled experiment in Singapore, report limited or no effects within typical office ranges, but replication across climatic contexts is needed to assess generalizability. The present study was conducted in the temperate climate of the San Francisco Bay Area, closely replicating the Singapore protocol with a 30% larger sample: 75 participants completed four 165-min sessions at 21, 23, 25, and 27°C in a controlled environmental chamber. title: Genomic diversity, population structure, and relatedness of critically endangered Philippine eagles under conservation management
abstract: The critically endangered Philippine eagle ( Pithecophaga jefferyi ) faces severe threats to its population from habitat loss, naturally slow reproduction cycles, and human encroachment. Thus, 38 years ago, the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) was established for the conservation of the endangered Philippine eagle and its rainforest habitat. To support the PEF’s captive-breeding and rehabilitation efforts, this study investigates the genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles of 20 wild-captive and 15 captive-bred individuals under the foundation’s care. title: Prediction of Self‐Starting of a Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Using Static Torque
abstract: ABSTRACT The ability of vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) to self‐start is critical to their performance. There is disagreement in the literature over some of the factors affecting their self‐starting ability and there is very limited information on how the starting azimuthal angle affects self‐starting. We present a series of wind tunnel experiments in which we measure the static torque and self‐starting of a three‐blade VAWT for a range of initial azimuthal angles, which we find to have a very strong effect on the ability to self‐start. title: AN OVERVIEW OF STUDIES ON PLANTS IN ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OVER TWO DECADES (2006–2026)
abstract: While plants are an integral part of terrestrial ecosystems, little attention is given to them in environmental education (EE) research and conservation debates. There is growing awareness of a general lack of plant recognition and appreciation among people that has become a central issue of botanical literacy, contributing to the phenomenon of plant blindness. Despite growing scholarly interest, no comprehensive bibliometric study has yet mapped the intellectual structure, geographical distribution, and thematic development of research focused on plants within the EE domain. title: Drought and Water Stress Analysis in the Kaman Region (Kırşehir, Türkiye) Using Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2A Data
abstract: This study evaluates vegetation dynamics and drought conditions in the semi-arid agricultural landscapes of Kaman (Türkiye) using integrated remote sensing data. NDVI and NDMI derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2, together with land surface temperature (LST) and Sentinel-1 soil moisture, were analyzed to assess vegetation–environment interactions. NDVI time-series analysis revealed a clear seasonal phenological cycle, with peak vegetation growth in spring and a marked decline during summer due to increased temperature and reduced moisture availability. title: The RLR-MAVS-IRF3 axis activates the IFN pathway to restrict Tonate virus (TONV) infection
abstract: Tonate virus (TONV) is a neglected mosquito-borne alphavirus of the Venezuelan equine encephalitis complex associated with febrile illness, encephalitis, and fetal central nervous system abnormalities. Yet, host pathways that sense TONV infection and restrict its replication remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the interaction between TONV and the type I interferon (IFN-I) system in human T98G and A549 cells. title: A taxonomy of reliability indices for cluster‐level constructs measured by multiple individual‐level indicators
abstract: Generalizability theory (GT) provides a variety of intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) to quantify reliability across different conditions of measurement-for example, scale and interrater reliability quantify generalization across items and raters, respectively. In a multilevel modelling (MLM) context, an ICC is often used to quantify the proportion of a subject-level variable's variance that is attributable to cluster-level differences (e.g., between schools or neighbourhoods). title: The complete mitochondrial genomes of Colias lada and Colias wanda (Lepidoptera: Pieridae: Coliadinae) and their phylogenetic analyses
abstract: The complete mitochondrial genomes of two Qinghai-Tibet Plateau butterflies, Colias lada and C. wanda, were assembled from next-generation sequencing data, measuring 15,078 bp and 15,144 bp. Both contain 13 PCGs, 22 tRNAs, 2 rRNAs and one control region. Phylogenetic trees based on the 13 PCGs and 2 rRNAs using ML and BI methods, with high support values, show that C. wanda, C. lada and C. sifanica share a recent common ancestor, and reconstruct the relationships among the Coliadinae genera.

title: DNA Barcoding Validation of Medicinal Ipomoea Species from the Morning Glory Family
abstract: The growing consumption of herbal products has been accompanied by a concerning increase in the use of adulterants during production, which could affect the quality of traditional herbal medicine. DNA barcoding is a powerful method for accurately identifying plants at various taxonomic levels, and for authenticating medicinal plants. In this study, the DNA barcoding regions rbcL and ITS were used to corroborate the botanical classification of commercial seeds from five Ipomoea species and one hybrid, all commonly used as herbal medicines and widely cultivated as ornamentals. title: γ‐Ray Controlled Topological Evolution of Binders for Stable and Activated Li─S Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT γ‐ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent‐free cross‐linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three‐dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. title: Evolution of Peripheral Retinal Perfusion in Sickle Cell Retinopathy During Severe Vaso-Occlusive Crises: A Report of Two Cases
abstract: Sickle cell retinopathy (SCR) is characterized by retinal vaso-occlusion and peripheral ischemia.We describe two patients with homozygous sickle cell disease (HbSS) who presented with extensive peripheral retinal nonperfusion during severe vaso-occlusive crises.Multimodal retinal imaging was performed during the acute phase and after systemic stabilization.Following systemic optimization, including exchange transfusion, follow-up fluorescein angiography demonstrated a reduction in peripheral retinal nonperfusion in both patients without progression of neovascularization.These findings suggest

title: Open Educational Resources as Enabling Conditions for Student Resilience to Failure and Uncertainty
abstract: As today's scientific challenges become increasingly complex and interdisciplinary, future researchers in the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) need both disciplinary skills and adaptive resilience to persevere and cope productively with failure. We argue that Open Educational Resources (OER) provide the enabling conditions for this resilience. title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. title: Evaluation of sustainability of lubricants by life cycle assessment and carbon footprint measurement
abstract: The global increasing awareness of sustainability has greatly affected the traditional lubricant market. The goals to reduce environmental pollution have increased the use of biolubricants rather petroleum based ones significantly due to several harmful impacts of the later including non-biodegradability, higher carbon emissions and bio-toxic wastes. In this review, a comparative analysis of biolubricants (soybean and rapeseed oils lubricants) with mineral and synthetic lubricants was performed with respect to their life cycle assessment (LCA) and carbon footprint (CFP) measurement. title: Structural basis of antigenic drift in FMDV O/Cathay topotype variants revealed by porcine-derived single B-cell neutralizing antibodies
abstract: The porcinophilic O/Cathay topotype variants of foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) continuously accumulated mutations over time and produced antigenic drift, leading to diminished serum neutralization and compromised vaccine efficacy. However, the structural basis underlying this divergence remains poorly defined. Herein, we observed that the newly emerging O/Cathay variants in China exhibited marked neutralization escape from porcine immune sera. title: Comparative biomass carbon storage, CO2 mitigation potential and green economy valuation of polyculture and monoculture plantations under the Jan Van Yojna social forestry scheme in semi-humid tropical Jharkhand India
abstract: Tropical forest plantations under community-based schemes represent an underexplored yet critical nexus between land-use policy, climate change mitigation, and green economy valuation. This study provides the first quantitative assessment of biomass carbon storage, CO 2 mitigation potential, and carbon credit value for two contrasting Jan Van Yojna (JVY) plantation sites in the semi-humid tropical region of Ranchi district, Jharkhand, India: a seven-species polyculture stand at BUDMU (652 trees, 2.2 acres) and a monoculture Tectona grandis stand at ANGADA (500 trees, 2.0 acres), both establish

title: Comparative Study of Moses in the Qur’an and the Bible: Narrative Differences, Theological Construction, and Historical Context
abstract: This article compares the narratives of Moses in the Qur'an and the Bible and explores ‘thinking beyond the narratives.’ Existing comparative studies often focus only on identifying similarities and differences. This research aims to address this gap by asking why such variations and similarities exist and what their theological implications are. Using a qualitative, critical-comparative analysis method that combines narratological, comparative theological, and historical-critical approaches, this study examines key episodes, such as the Golden Calf incident and the drowning of Pharaoh. title: Field evaluation of Bacillus -based consortium biofertilizer for rhizosphere zinc availability, grain biofortification and paddy yield
abstract: The zinc (Zn) deficiency in submerged rice limits productivity and nutritional quality. This study evaluated the potential of zinc-solubilizing plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to enhance Zn availability and uptake in rice under submerged conditions. Field experiments were conducted over two years using five Bacillus-based biofertilizer formulations: three single-strain inoculants (B. megaterium AN24 as BF-1, B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-2, B. megaterium AN31 as BF-3) and two combined formulations (B. megaterium AN24 + B. aryabhattai AN30 as BF-4, B. megaterium AN24 + B. megaterium AN3

title: Charge-Driven Engineering of Titanium Implants with Chitosan and Poly- l -Lysine for Dual Antiadhesive and Anticorrosive Functionality
abstract: Abstract Peri-implant infections remain a major cause of implant failure, motivating the development of multifunctional titanium surfaces capable of preventing bacterial colonization while preserving implant performance. Herein, a chitosan/poly-l-lysine (CH-PLL) bilayer coating was engineered on hydroxyl-rich titanium surfaces generated by hydrothermal treatment (HT) or plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO). title: Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov.: a novel candidate for plant growth-promoting actinomycete from bare soil developing on Miocene lacustrine sediment of the Sokolov Coal Basin, Czech Republic
abstract: Abstract A novel actinomycete, designated as BCCO 10_0861 T , was isolated from overburden Miocene clay sediments undergoing primary succession in Northwest Czechia and characterized by the polyphasic approach. title: Irrigation-driven modulation of growth and stress resilience in cork oak (Quercus suber L.) seedlings in nursery environments
abstract: Cork oak (Quercus suber L.) is a keystone species of Mediterranean forestry, increasingly threatened by prolonged droughts and anthropogenic pressures. Improving nursery seedling quality is therefore essential for successful reforestation. This study evaluates the effects of three irrigation regimes (i) daily manual watering (IN), (ii) irrigation triggered when soil moisture falls below 30% (IB), and (iii) irrigation at field capacity based on daily container weight loss (IC), and two container types (rigid pots: 2000 cm³; alveolate trays: 500 cm³ per cell) on the morphological development of

title: Clonality in European black poplar conservation units using genomics
abstract: Aim of study: We performed a fine scale characterization of two European black poplar (Populus nigra) in situ conservation units, using a large sample of individuals and a comprehensive set of genetic markers. This information is pivotal to understand the population dynamics of the units for implementing conservation and management plans. Area of study: We studied two populations with distinct environments and management practices in Spain and Austria. Material and methods: We genotyped 500 adults and 250 juveniles within each population using 13K single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers.

abstract: The rapid growth of aquaculture has led to the prevalence of infectious diseases and antibiotic resistance. Therefore, new sustainable strategies are required to prevent this situation from growing. The present study evaluated the effect of ethanolic leaf extracts of Cinnamomum tamala (CTE) and Cinnamomum camphora (CCE) against Aeromonas salmonicida . title: Measuring circular economy performance in the EU: evidence from an FAHP-weighted composite index
abstract: Assessing circular economy (CE) performance across EU countries remains challenging due to the scarcity of country-level composite measures and uncertainty surrounding indicator importance. This study develops a circular economy index aligned with the EU Circular Economy Monitoring Framework. Expert judgments (n = 7) were collected through pairwise comparisons and translated into pillar and indicator weights using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP). abstract: The growing demand for sustainable bioinputs has driven the production of microbial biosurfactants from low-cost substrates. This study evaluated the biosurfactant production by the strain Bacillus licheniformis UCP 1014 utilizing crude glycerol and corn steep liquor as agroindustrial as substrates, using Rotatable Central Composite Design (RCCD). title: Reduction of off-flavour formation and improved α-oligoglucoside utilization enable use of Saccharomyces eubayanus as a novel lager brewing yeast
abstract: Lager beer, made by fermentation of barley malt using the hybrid yeast Saccharomyces pastorianus, is extremely popular worldwide. The low genetic variation of S. pastorianus strains limits the scope of development for novel lager beer types. The wild ancestor Saccharomyces eubayanus has potential for lager brewing, but its application is constrained by formation of phenolic off-flavours (POF+ phenotype) and limited uptake of the wort α-oligoglucosides maltose and maltotriose. title: A pH-stimulated responsive micro-drug delivery system loaded with gastrodin that improves type 2 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly increasing global metabolic disease. The development of effective oral hypoglycemic agents, primarily derived from natural compounds, remains a significant challenge. In this study, we developed pH-responsive sodium alginate (SA) microspheres combined with low methoxy pectin (LMP) that are loaded with gastrodin (Gas) (denoted as Gas@MPs) and successfully delivered Gas to the gut for controlled release. title: Hidden in the deadwood: Taxonomically curated barcode library reveals deep genetic divergence in Eurasian saproxylic beetles
abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. While European DNA barcode reference databases have expanded in recent years, they remain dominated by western and northern populations, leaving Central and Eastern European taxa heavily underrepresented. title: Upcycling Industrial Lignin Into Cationic Hydrogels With Potential for Sustainable Plant Protection
abstract: Bio-based antimicrobial materials are increasingly explored as sustainable alternatives for plant pathogen control. Here, we report a circular economy approach in which industrial kraft lignin was upcycled into cationic lignin (CL) and physically embedded within chitosan-genipin (CH-GPN) hydrogels to form CH-GPN-CL. These bioactive materials were evaluated for the in vitro inhibition of the plant pathogen Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000. title: Biotechnological potential of aquatic hyphomycetes: a review
abstract: Aquatic hyphomycetes are an ecological group of anamorphic fungi that play an essential role in decomposing plant substrates in lotic environments. This narrative review compiled studies highlighting the biotechnological potential of this group, contributing to the understanding of its applications and perspectives. The analysis emphasizes aquatic hyphomycetes as significant producers of metabolites with applications across various sectors, including industrial, agricultural, environmental, and health sectors. Notably, these organisms degrade lignocellulosic compounds and produce antimicrobial

title: Network centrality position shapes urban innovation capacities: evidence from China’s interlocking corporate network
abstract: Understanding how cities function as innovation incubators within increasingly interconnected economies is crucial for sustainable development. This study investigates how a city’s centrality within an enterprise-derived network shapes its technological innovation capabilities and underlying mechanisms. We construct an interlocking network model based on extensive corporate linkage data for Chinese cities. title: Assessing the metabolic rate in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, Progressive Muscular Atrophy, and Primary Lateral Sclerosis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether resting energy expenditure (REE) differs between patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), progressive muscular atrophy (PMA), and primary lateral sclerosis (PLS). METHODS: Patients with ALS, PMA, and PLS were enrolled between 2017 and 2021 in a prospective cross-sectional study. REE was measured by indirect calorimetry. Body composition was assessed using air displacement plethysmography and used to calculate predicted resting energy expenditure (pREE). journal: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and Frontotemporal Degeneration

title: The Symbolic World: A Brief Analysis of Simulacra in White Noise
abstract: This paper takes Baudrillard’s theory of simulacra and hyperreality as its core framework to analyze White Noise, a classic of postmodern literature by Don DeLillo, aiming to reveal how simulacra permeate and reshape the lifestyle and individual cognition of postmodern society as depicted in the novel. White Noise presents a world of simulacra dominated by symbols, where the real is replaced by simulacra and individuals lose themselves in the carnival of symbols, and in doing so, they forfeit their subjectivity and genuine emotional connections.
journal: Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences Studies

title: Postfire soil convergence toward an unburned reference varies with fire severity and soil depth
abstract: Abstract Background Wildfire effects on soil can differ among soil properties, soil depths, and fire-severity classes, yet their longer-term trajectories remain poorly resolved in subtropical pine plantations. We evaluated temporal convergence of burned soils toward an unburned reference following an April 2022 wildfire in a Pinus massoniana plantation in central China. abstract: Abstract The Raman spectrum of lawsonite is characterized in situ at high temperatures through its dehydration temperature under vacuum. The structural reorganization associated with dehydration appears to initiate in the Si and Al-dominated layer of the structure, and proceeds between 525–550 and 725 °C. abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. title: Low Threshold Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers Based on CsPbI 3 Thin Films
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskites are attractive gain media for compact coherent light sources. Although the all‐inorganic CsPbI 3 is a particularly promising representative, low‐threshold laser operation remains challenging in CsPbI 3 thin films due to phase instability and difficulties in preparing high‐quality thin films within low‐loss optical resonators. Here, we demonstrate the first vertical‐cavity surface‐emitting lasers (VCSELs) based on CsPbI 3 thin films. title: Design and performance analysis of reset-based active disturbance rejection control
abstract: To address the inherent trade-off between transient performance and noise robustness of the traditional linear extended state observer (LESO) within the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) framework, a novel reset extended state observer (RESO) scheme is proposed. Its core idea is to introduce a state correction mechanism regulated by the reset gain matrix into the LESO, which can maintain structural simplicity to the greatest extent. title: SCIN Overexpression Attenuates LPS-Induced Apoptosis and Differentially Modulates EGFR Abundance and Phosphorylation in Human Oral Keratinocytes
abstract: Background: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory and immune-mediated oral mucosal disease characterized by epithelial damage, basal cell degeneration, and recurrent lesions. However, the molecular mechanisms responsible for keratinocyte injury and apoptosis during OLP progression remain incompletely understood. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain. METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. title: Green synthesis and characterization of Bi₂O₃ nanoparticles using Cuminum cyminum seed for antimicrobial and cytotoxic evaluation
abstract: Green synthesis provides an alternative to traditional chemical processes of nanomaterials preparation, which is cost-effective and environmentally benign. This paper has demonstrated synthesis of bismuth oxide nanoparticles (Bi 2 O 3 NPs) using Cuminum cyminum seed extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent of bismuth nitrate precursor. title: Mechanisms of Sensitisation and Development of Hand Allergic Dermatitis Induced by Occupational Allergens
abstract: Introduction: Due to the frequent exposure to chemical, biological and physical agents, occupational allergic dermatitis of the hands is a major health issue. Various types of dermatitis can present with the same symptoms. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the immunopathogenesis processes that lead to occupational allergic hand dermatitis and to diagnose such conditions. title: Waterborne eDNA metabarcoding of the upper Llano River watershed (Texas, USA) detects regionally unreported green plant taxa
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) represents a promising preliminary tool for efficiently assessing biological diversity in locales where conducting intensive field surveys is logistically challenging, as in the case of west-central Texas. Its utility for characterizing biodiversity across broad spatial scales is amplified in lotic systems, which can transport eDNA several kilometers from its source and often contain signals from both aquatic and nearby terrestrial organisms. abstract: Identifying seismogenic faults, their geometries, and associated slip rates is essential for assessing seismic hazard estimates. During earthquake sequences, complex fault systems are often activated, involving the rupture of multiple segments. Identifying these fault segments remains a challenging task. This study proposes a quantitative, statistically based workflow using a cluster analysis to identify the number and dimensions of fault segments based on earthquake hypocenter distributions, an approach particularly suitable for aftershock sequences. abstract: Abstract Insecticides targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are used because of their high neuroactive efficacy. However, they can also exert substantial toxic pressure on nontarget aquatic invertebrates. A previous study suggested that irreversible receptor binding is the main driver of thiacloprid bioaccumulation. title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. abstract: Abstract Fractional nonlinear evolution equations serve as a fundamental model to capture complex phenomena with memory effects, anomalous dispersion and long-range interaction. abstract: Abstract Background Weight regain affects most individuals attempting to treat obesity and its comorbidities, and it is associated with increased risk of metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. title: Collective future thinking over the Russia-Ukraine war: Cross-national perspectives from Poland and Türkiye
abstract: Collective future thinking involves individuals’ imagining the future of the group they feel they belong to. In the present study, we examine how individuals from Türkiye and Poland, two countries with different sociocultural and geopolitical contexts, simulate the future of their own country and that of Russia and Ukraine in the context of the Russia-Ukraine War. Participants ( N = 152) reported two future events that they expected to occur in Russia, Ukraine, and their own countries. abstract: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is widely used in tropical agriculture, yet its effects on non-target ectothermic vertebrates remain poorly understood. This study assessed the subchronic toxicological impact of 2,4-D on the liver and kidneys of Tropidurus torquatus, a neotropical lizard commonly found in agricultural areas. Seventeen adult males were divided into control (n = 9) and treatment (n = 8) groups. abstract: In 2015, the United Nations adopted the elimination of open defecation as Sustainable Development Goal 6.2. abstract: As part of the global effort to replace petroleum-based materials with sustainable alternatives, there is growing interest in enhancing the toughness of biological materials for durable textile applications. Functional composites derived from renewable sources, such as fungal hyphae, have attracted widespread attention. abstract: Background: Contemporary discussions of synodality frequently emphasize participation, discernment, governance, and ecclesial structures, while the Christological foundation that gives synodality its inner form is less often made explicit. abstract: Friction Stir Welding (FSW) is widely validated as a solid-state joining process that has gained significant attention for the welding of aluminum alloys in aerospace and automotive applications. abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Grasslands are biodiversity-rich ecosystems in which plant functional diversity strongly influences ecosystem functioning. Silicon (Si) and calcium (Ca) are often overlooked in trait-based frameworks despite their roles in plant physiology, stress tolerance and nutrient dynamics. This study investigates how leaf Si and Ca vary among plant functional groups, how they relate to soil Si and Ca availability, and whether they are associated with specific leaf area (SLA). title: Environmental risk, natural disasters, and economic growth management in Indonesia: A satellite-based analysis
abstract: This study examines how environmental risk and natural disasters affect economic performance in a disaster-prone emerging economy. It focuses on the short-run and long-run impacts of flood exposure, forest loss, and spatial economic expansion on Indonesia’s economic growth, with implications for investment stability and growth management. abstract: The preparation and preservation of animal specimens constitute important tools for the teaching of zoology, comparative anatomy, morphology and ichthyology. abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the internal fit at the implant-abutment interface of zirconia and cobalt-chromium abutments fabricated using different techniques by micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). title: Design and fabrication of functionally graded 3D polymeric scaffolds for simultaneous cell support and localized MicroRNA delivery
abstract: Scaffolds have proven useful as matrices for cell culture, tissue ingrowth, organ formation, mechanical support, drug screening platforms, and localized delivery systems. Their performance depends on multiple structural and material properties that determine their suitability for specific applications. In this study, we developed a multifunctional scaffold designed to provide both cell culture support and gradual microRNA (miRNA, miR) delivery. title: Fabrication of High‐Performance Sustainable Packaging Composites via Blending of Recycled Polypropylene With Surface‐Functionalized Rice Husk‐Derived Nanosilica and Phthalate‐Modified Starch
abstract: ABSTRACT Polypropylene is extensively used as a packaging material, creating a huge amount of waste after use. This work highlights the use of recycled polypropylene (rPP), starch phthalate, and modified nanosilica to produce sustainable packaging material. Both starch and nanosilica are functionalized to improve overall compatibility by increasing dispersion within the rPP matrix. Among the formulations, the optimal composition was 8:0.6:32 (starch/starch phthalate:nanosilica:rPP:PMS3). title: Ontogenic configuration of stelar development in root orders of climbing Apocynaceae species, Vincetoxicum capparidifolium (Wight & Arn.) Kuntze
abstract: Root systems demonstrate peculiar anatomical plasticity, with structural traits altering predictably across root orders to optimize water uptake, transport proficiency, and mechanical assistance. This is the first comprehensive study to elucidate the anatomical structure and hydraulic specialization across five successive root orders of Vincetoxicum capparidifolium (Wight & Arn.) title: Crystallization-mediated twisting of supramolecular nanoribbons from plant-derived triterpenes
abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). title: A modeling framework for predicting resistance to cell wall-inhibiting antibiotics and rational identification of antibiotic combinations in S. aureus
abstract: The microbial cell wall is a key target for many antibiotics owing to its conserved essentiality across the bacterial kingdom. Modifications of this cellular component, whether structural, chemical, or organizational, are frequently found in antibiotic-resistant isolates. We develop an ODE (Ordinary Differential Equation) model of the peptidoglycan biosynthesis pathway (PGNet), integrate it with transcriptome data from vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus (VISA), and characterize its cell wall in terms of total peptidoglycan content and degree-of-crosslinking. title: Atlas‐Guided CD55‐Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement–Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds
abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single-cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic-wound single-cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement-regulatory and reparative features. title: Temporal dynamics and species-specific responses to biotic and abiotic drivers shape seedling establishment in a subtropical forest
abstract: Abstract Seedling establishment is a critical demographic bottleneck for species regeneration and diversity maintenance in forests, yet the temporal contributions of biotic and abiotic factors remain poorly understood. This is because most previous studies focused disproportionately on biotic factors or limited abiotic factors and used observational data lacking standardized baselines for seedling age. title: Unexpected Inter‐Annual Variability in Methane Emissions From Western Siberia’s Oil and Gas Sector
abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) emissions from the oil and gas (O&G) sector are a major source of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions. Russia is a leading CH 4 emitter, with the O&G sector accounting for approximately 80% of its total fossil fuel‐derived CH 4 emissions. However, long‐term emission trends remain unclear due to significant discrepancies between bottom‐up inventories and atmospheric model estimates. abstract: As transformações ambientais que ocorrem no meio ambiente pressionam os ecossistemas florestais de forma a ocasionar o desequilíbrio nas suas funções ecológicas, além de contribuir para a perda desses ecossistemas. title: Knowledge governance and organizational learning capacity in village cooperatives: the role of institutional mechanisms
abstract: Village cooperatives are expected to support rural economic development, yet their institutional and economic performance often depends on more than formal establishment, capital provision, or policy support. This study examines how knowledge governance contributes to institutional effectiveness and local economic capability in village cooperatives through institutional mechanisms and organizational learning capacity. title: Co‐Infection of Aeromonas veronii and Citrobacter braakii in Yellow Catfish ( Tachysurus fulvidraco )
abstract: Recently, a disease outbreak was observed in farmed yellow catfish (Tachysurus fulvidraco) in Tianjin, China. Naturally infected fish exhibited surface haemorrhages, abdominal distension, anal redness, and hemorrhagic ascites. Histopathological examination revealed systemic lesions in the stomach, intestine, liver, and spleen. Two Gram-negative bacterial isolates, designated PFL and PFS, were isolated from the liver and spleen of diseased fish, respectively.
