title: Responses of soil characteristics and bacterial communities to agricultural irrigation with different treatment levels of wastewater
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of domestic wastewater treated at different treatment levels on the biochemical characteristics of irrigated soils. Raw domestic wastewater was subjected to four treatment processes: (1) grit sedimentation; (2) grit sedimentation combined with ultrafiltration (UF); (3) grit sedimentation combined with anaerobic activated sludge treatment followed by UF; and (4) grit sedimentation combined with aerobic activated sludge treatment followed by UF. title: An integrated multilayer environmental impact assessment framework for accelerating sustainable energy infrastructure permitting
abstract: The deployment of sustainable energy infrastructure in the European Union is now limited less by technology costs than by the duration and unpredictability of permitting. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), the main authorization instrument for energy projects, evaluates the impacts of a proposal. title: Understanding Phosphorus Dynamics in Martian and Lunar Regolith Simulants: Insights for Space Agriculture
abstract: Abstract Phosphorus (P) is a vital nutrient for plant growth and development, making it essential for sustaining agriculture as human colonies are established in space. However, there is limited knowledge of native P forms and of the interaction between applied P and the lunar or Martian regolith. This highlights the need to examine how this essential nutrient interacts with the regolith for sustainable P management. abstract: Abstract The antibiotic resistance of pathogenic microorganisms due to the irresponsible use in healthcare and agricultural practices is one of the global threats for the human, especially immune-compromised patients. Thus, searching for a novel compounds from fungi with unique affinity to combat the drug-resistant microorganisms was the objective. Talaromyces purpurogenus # PZ292970.1, an endophyte of palm tree Elaeis guineensis , has the highest productivity of azaphilone pigment (25.5 AU410/ml), with a strong activity against E. coli (MIC value 6.8 µg/ml), S. aureus and C. albicans (MIC val

title: Elevated CO 2 drives nonlinear trait responses and reshapes growth‐virulence trade‐offs in a plant pathogen
abstract: Summary Atmospheric CO 2 is rising at unprecedented rates. While its physiological effects on plants are well‐documented, the direct evolutionary impact on plant pathogens remains unknown. We investigated how CO 2 interacts with other abiotic factors to shape the evolutionary potential of pathogens. We combined controlled CO 2 gradient experiments with quantitative genetics to assess the interactive effects of CO 2 , temperature and geography on Phytophthora infestans . title: Limestone reaction and crop yield in sandy soil of Bahia’s Cerrado, Brazil
abstract: Soil amendment is an essential step toward the introduction or maintenance of intensified agricultural production systems. The aim of the present research is to assess lime’s response to crops rotation and sandy soil yield in Bahia’s Cerrado region, Brazil, under controlled conditions. The experiment was conducted at completely randomized design with four replications. The crops were grown in pots filled with 20 kg of Oxisol (14% of clay). title: Screening and characterization of endophytic bacterial isolates associated with Echinops kebericho M. and Lepidium sativum L. and evaluation of their potential role
abstract: Endophytic bacteria (EB) associated with medicinal plants contribute to plant growth by enhancing nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and phytohormone production. This study aimed to isolate and characterize potential endophytic bacterial isolates (EBIs) from Echinops kebericho Mesfin and Lepidium sativum L., two traditional Ethiopian medicinal plants, and to evaluate their ability to utilize various growth substrates. title: Ionization Structure and Metal Enrichment of the Galactic Center Minispiral Observed with JWST
abstract: Abstract Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) is the nearest quiescent supermassive black hole, and its proximity offers a unique opportunity to study its surrounding fuel supply. We leverage extensive spatial and spectroscopic information provided by the JWST/MIRI Medium Resolution Spectrograph instrument to disentangle mid-infrared ionized gas structures in the central 0.1 pc of the Galaxy. The Galactic Minispiral’s Bar and Northern Arm are revealed by their distinct morphological and kinematic signatures. title: Individual Resilience as Human Capital Stock: Neighborhood Social Capital, Environmental Perceptions, and Dynamic Pathways Across COVID-19 Phases
abstract: Abstract This study, grounded in the social ecological theories, investigates how the pathways linking neighborhood relationships, perceived environmental quality (PEQ), and individual resilience (IR) differed between the COVID-19 pandemic and the post-pandemic period. The empirical focus is on Chinese international students (CIS) in the UK, who experienced a unique form of “double exclusion” during the pandemic. title: Crash-loaded roll-formed multi-chamber steel sheet structures – algorithmic optimisation, manufacturing and testing
abstract: The usage of high-strength steel sheet metals in crash absorbing structures can favour efficient and lightweight designs. For multi-chamber structures made of sheet metals, roll forming is one of the most notable manufacturing methods regarding mass production. The Graph and Heuristic based Topology optimisation is a well-established software tool to optimise crash-loaded multi-chamber structures. title: Core–Shell Upconversion Platform Based on an Amino-Functionalized ZIF-8 with a Covalently Anchored Ruthenium Nitrosyl Complex for Controlled Release of Nitric Oxide in Biological Media
abstract: Abstract The development of nitric oxide (NO) donor agents capable of controlled NO release upon light irradiation in the biological window is relevant for phototherapies. The cis-[Ru(dc-bpy)2(SO3)(NO)]+ complex (dc-bpy = 2,2′-dicarboxybipyridine) is synthesized and anchored onto a NaYF4:Yb,Tm@ZIF-8-NH2 nanoplatform. The isolated complex presents high stability under basic conditions (pH 9) and an absorption band in the visible region up to 405 nm. A core–shell platform of upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) coated with ZIF-8 is synthesized and functionalized with amino groups (UCNP-ZIF-8-NH2).

title: Pressure-Induced Modulation of Electronic, Elastic, and Optical Traits in Hexagonal La₂O₃ for Advanced Solid-state Battery Cathode Frameworks
abstract: In this study, we systematically investigate the composition-dependent elastic, mechanical, and thermophysical properties of the hexagonal close-packed (HCP) structured rare-earth metal chalcogenide, lanthanum oxide La2O3, at a constant temperature of 300 K. Atomistic simulations were executed across a hydrostatic pressure range of 0–100 GPa using the well-established Lennard-Jones (L-J) interatomic potential model. title: Unlocking the potential of melon seed protein: enzymatic hydrolysis and functional characterization of protein hydrolysates
abstract: Melon seeds are a protein-rich byproduct that remains underutilized. This study investigated the production and functional properties of protein hydrolysates from melon seed protein using six proteases: papain, bromelain, neutral protease, alkaline protease, pepsin, and trypsin. The hydrolysates were evaluated for antioxidant activities and α-amylase inhibition. title: An antimicrobial cyclic peptide with multitarget efficacy for acne
abstract: Abstract Acne vulgaris is a complex inflammatory disorder, and current treatment options are often limited by antibiotic resistance and cutaneous irritation, underscoring the urgent need for safer multi-target therapeutic alternatives. In this study, a novel antimicrobial cyclic peptide (AMCP) was systematically evaluated for its multidimensional anti-acne efficacy, and a penetration enhancer was developed for improving the transdermal penetration. title: Activating pedagogies for sustainable futures: ‘walking with’ the Maramataka over time
abstract: The aim of this study was to understand what, why and how pedagogies for sustainable futures might be activated through encounters with waterways over Indigenous time-space coordinates. ‘Walking-with’ learners of different age groups at key phases of the Māori lunar system (maramataka) – a chronotopic analysis charts the impact of pedagogies in activating sustainable responses by learners over time. abstract: Abstract The Weberian apparatus is an innovation serving as the primary sound-conduction path for otophysan fishes. In this study, we investigate how North American catfishes (Ictaluridae) how this system varies across diverse ecological landscapes. By leveraging CT scanning and geometric morphometrics on 136 specimens across 47 species, we mapped the evolutionary trajectories of three critical components: the scaphium, tripus, and peripheral structures including the associated vertebrae and ligament insertions. title: Bacterial cellulose biosynthesis using native microorganisms from a mixture of non-centrifugal sugars and apple juice
abstract: Bacterial cellulose (BC) is a biopolymer with numerous potential applications, although it is associated with considerable production costs of conventional culture media. In this study, BC biosynthesis was investigated using native microorganisms from a mixture of non-centrifugal sugars (NCS) and apple juice as a low-cost alternative substrate. Sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene identified Acetobacter persici and Bacillus sp. among principal species associated with cellulose biosynthesis. title: MyD88 sustains a metastasis-competent cell state by promoting integrin-mediated adhesion in melanoma
abstract: Abstract Background Metastatic dissemination remains a major challenge in melanoma, as environmental cues can reshape tumor cell plasticity and promote transient states that enable invasion and colonization of distant organs. However, the tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms that integrate these external signals and sustain metastatic competence remain incompletely understood. title: Dual-mode (light/dark) active nanocellulose–MOF–carbon dot filters for airborne bacterial suppression in hospital environments
abstract: Airborne microbial contamination in hospitals is a major driver of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). So far, most commercial air filters capture microorganisms but do not inactivate them, and they rely on non-biodegradable polymers. title: A Six‐Year Multisite Monitoring Network Reveals a Regionally Structured Hierarchy of Incidence Among Cotton Bollworms in Benin
abstract: ABSTRACT Cotton bollworms are a major constraint to cotton production in Benin despite insecticide use, yet their spatio‐temporal distribution remains poorly characterised. Cotton pest management still relies on calendar‐based programmes that do not account for local variability in pest pressure. title: An integrated framework for characterising livestock systems and assessing ruminant performance across heterogeneous production environments: Evidence from Nigeria
abstract: Globally, livestock production systems (LPS) are crucial for supporting livelihoods and ensuring food security. This study developed and applied an integrated livestock production zone (LPZ) framework to characterise (LPS) and evaluate ruminant performance across Nigeria’s diverse agroecological environments. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining expert consultations, a literature review, and a participatory on-farm survey across 12 states with 1,404 participants. title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
abstract: Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS 2 microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. title: Association between maternal traumatic stress related to Great East Japan Earthquake and behavioral problems in offspring
abstract: Background: : Women who experienced the Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) and subsequently became pregnant may have children who are more likely to exhibit emotional and behavioral problems. However, few longitudinal studies have investigated the developmental outcomes among children born to mothers who experienced natural disasters before pregnancy and continued to experience stress symptoms thereafter. abstract: This study optimized ultrasound-assisted deep eutectic solvent (DES) extraction of total flavonoids from Houttuynia cordata Thunb. and evaluated their in vitro antioxidant and antibacterial activities. Among eight screened DESs, choline chloride–lactic acid (1:1, 30% water) was selected as the optimal solvent. title: Robustness of oxygen metrics to sampling frequency in a stratified lake
abstract: Abstract Long-term lake monitoring often relies on monthly dissolved oxygen profiles, but the robustness of derived oxygen metrics to this temporal resolution is uncertain. We compared three years (2022–2024) of hourly sensor observations (high-frequency (HF)) with approximately monthly discrete profiles (low-frequency (LF)) from a small, dimictic subalpine lake. title: Subsurface volumetric estimates of ultramafic and mafic rocks in the Livengood Terrane, Central Alaska: implications for carbon mineralization
abstract: Abstract Mafic and ultramafic rocks are sources of critical minerals and also provide a medium to securely store CO 2 . The objective of this study is to delineate the geometry and assess the volumes of ultramafic rocks in the Livengood Terrane in central Alaska using high-resolution aeromagnetic, petrophysical, and borehole datasets. We analyzed magnetic anomalies using 3D inversion using constraints from previous outcrop and petrophysical data. title: Evaluating the multi-scale performance and mechanical behavior of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) mixtures incorporating waste-derived oils and vacuum bottom rejuvenators
abstract: Maximizing the utilization of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) while maintaining long-term fatigue durability is essential for sustainable pavement infrastructure. To address this challenge, this study aims to establish a multi-scale framework for evaluating and optimizing rejuvenator performance in high-RAP mixtures. Accordingly, the efficacy of three distinct rejuvenators—Waste Engine Oil (WEO), Lubricant Oil (LU), and Vacuum Bottom (VB)—was investigated in restoring the chemical and mechanical properties of bitumens and mixtures incorporating 30%, 45%, and 60% RAP. title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of triiodothyroacetic acid (Triac) in patients with resistance to thyroid hormone β (RTHβ): a multicentre, international, retrospective cohort study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disease features in resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ), caused by THRB mutations, arise from insensitivity to thyroid hormone in tissues expressing thyroid hormone receptor (TR)β and from lifelong thyrotoxic effects in TRα1-expressing tissues, posing substantial cardiovascular morbidity/mortality. The T3-analogue triiodothyroacetic acid (Triac) holds potential as an effective treatment. title: Impact of Pulsed CO2 Electrolysis on Surface Structures and Product Distribution for Oxide-Derived Cu
abstract: Abstract Using potential pulses in Cu-catalyzed CO2 electroreduction (CO2RR) has recently shown great promise in steering product selectivity. However, the effect of these pulses on the catalyst structure and, therefore, the formation of C1 and C2 products remain unclear. Herein, we altered the applied potential of the anodic pulse and varied the duration of the cathodic CO2RR pulse to investigate the effect of both the oxidation state and restructuring of an oxide-derived Cu nanoparticle catalyst on the CO2RR. title: Long-term retrospective analysis of cattle ectoparasite records in and around Gondar, Northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Background Cattle ectoparasites are important constraints to livestock production in Ethiopia, causing economic losses through reduced productivity, deterioration of hide and skin quality, disease transmission, and increased treatment costs. However, information derived from long-term veterinary clinic records remains limited in northwestern Ethiopia. title: Short‐Term Weather Variability Alters Plant Carbon Balance in Arctic Tundra Species
abstract: ABSTRACT Increasing weather variability is an aspect of global change with poorly understood impacts on organisms and ecosystems. Model predictions have shown that weather variability can diminish physiological performance, but empirical corroboration remains limited. Here, we explore the effects of short‐term variation in temperature and light on plant physiological functioning and the resulting leaf carbon balance. title: Navigating Complexity Through Mixed Methods Research: Insights from a Large-Scale Interdisciplinary Environmental Study of Biodiversity and Human Wellbeing
abstract: This paper explores the challenge of navigating complexity within mixed methods research process, drawing on a large-scale interdisciplinary environmental project exploring the wellbeing dimensions of human interaction with woodland biodiversity. Reflecting on the design and implementation of a multiphase mixed methods project involving over 9,000 participants, we examine how complexity emerged through the phenomenon under investigation, the structure of the research design, and the collaborations through which knowledge was produced. title: Environmental Determinants of Mental Health: a multilevel theoretical framework for understanding mental health and wellbeing
abstract: The present paper develops Author’s concept of Environmental Determinants of Mental Health for 2025 into a Multilevel Pathways Framework for the Environmental Determinants of Mental Health. The framework explains how natural, built, social and digital environmental conditions may influence mental health and wellbeing through environmental encounters, direct exposure, appraisal, access or avoidance, and biopsychosocial mechanisms. title: Interactions between lactobacillus and yeast: A recent update
abstract: Abstract Lactobacillus and yeast are microorganisms widely distributed in nature. Their interactions significantly impact fermentation processes, human health, and medical care. However, there is a lack of a systematic summary of the characteristics of these interactions, and the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain unclear. This review systematically summarizes the characteristics of Lactobacillus and yeast interactions, highlighting both mutualistic symbiosis and antagonistic effects. abstract: Abstract NiMoS hydrodesulfurization (HDS) catalysts were synthesized through an inorganic–organic dual modification strategy with molybdenum‐based polyoxometalates (POMs) as precursors. title: TRANSFORMING THE DARK TOURISM POTENTIAL IN AZERBAIJAN INTO SUSTAINABLE TOURISM REVENUE
abstract: This study examines how Azerbaijan’s dark tourism potential can be transformed into sustainable tourism revenue by identifying key strategic and institutional factors. Dark tourism, encompassing sites related to genocide, armed conflicts, and historical tragedies, represents a growing niche with significant cultural, educational, and economic implications. abstract: Allura Red AC (AR) is a synthetic anionic dye commonly used as a coloring agent in food and beverages. The extensive use and subsequent discharge of this dye as an industrial effluent raises significant health and environmental concerns. In this research, oxidized graphene-like carbon nanoparticles (Ox-CNPs) were evaluated for their potential in adsorption of AR. abstract: RIG-I and MDA5 are cytosolic RNA sensors that recognize distinct viral ligands in mammals, yet RIG-I has been independently lost from multiple teleost lineages. How RIG-I-deficient vertebrates preserve recognition of RIG-I-associated viral RNA remains poorly understood. abstract: This article examines archaic words in T. Qayıpbergenov’s novel The Karakalpak Epic, focusing on their historical origins, semantic features, and functions in the literary text. The study is based on the three books of the trilogy and applies continuous sampling together with etymological, comparative-historical, descriptive-semantic, and contextual analysis. abstract: In this exclusive interview for BIG_Review, Art & Borders Editor Elisa Ganivet speaks with Nico Alexandroff about his work as a spatial researcher at Border Forensics. abstract: Climate variability and environmental stressors, including erratic rainfall, recurrent drought, and soil degradation, increasingly threaten the sustainability of smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia, where rain-fed farming remains the main source of livelihood and food security. Although climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted as a strategy to increase productivity, build resilience, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, evidence on its effects at the local level remains limited. abstract: This research arises from the painful reality of disappearances in Mexico. The country is experiencing an accelerated increase in such problem and has been unable to respond promptly and effectively to the needs of disappeared persons’ relatives, who are indirect victims. abstract: Since the seminal studies of Stam, Hutcheon, and Sánchez Noriega, research on novels adapted into films has focused on the transpositions between page and screen. This proposal examines an intermediate step: the adaptation of a novel into a screenplay. It aims to show that screenwriting is a genre whose dominant function is enactment and embodiment. abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a significant global health threat, particularly in hyper-endemic regions like Vietnam, where the co-circulation of multiple serotypes and genotypes complicates disease control. abstract: Abstract Background Under the EU Nitrates Directive, Member States are required to adopt suitable measures to comply with the limit value of 50 mg NO 3 l −1 in groundwater. abstract: ABSTRACT Here, we review solid‐state NMR investigations of a variety of peptaibols in phospholipid bilayer environments. abstract: Increasing urbanization and water scarcity have intensified the need for advanced wastewater treatment technologies capable of producing high-quality effluent suitable for reuse. This study investigates the performance of an integrated Media Filtration–Membrane Bioreactor (MF–MBR) system for domestic wastewater treatment under conditions representative of Indian municipal wastewater. abstract: Himalayan soils are highly susceptible to the impacts of climate change and land-use shifts. Soil organic carbon (SOC) and the carbon management index (CMI) are key measures of soil health in response to land use changes. This study assessed total organic carbon (TOC), carbon fractions, carbon pool index (CPI), CMI, and physicochemical properties in forest and agricultural land-use systems in the temperate western Himalayas. abstract: Similar to worldwide trends in the nursing profession, in the Maldives, male nurses' participation in the workforce continues to be shaped by gender dynamics and is often affected by meaningful opportunities and distinct challenges. This study aimed to gain a deeper understanding of why men choose nursing, their working experiences, and career trajectories, offering insights into the challenges and opportunities they encounter. abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. abstract: Abstract The widespread use of antibiotics has resulted in their frequent occurrence in aquatic environments, raising ecological concerns; however, conducting precise monitoring and tracing of a broad spectrum of antibiotics concurrently in complex river networks at the watershed scale still faces significant challenges. This study investigates the laminar burning velocities (LBVs) and flame instabilities of DMC/NH 3 /air mixtures at 393 K and 1–4 atm, over equivalence ratios of 0.7–1.5 and NH 3 mole fractions of 0–40%. abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the short-term effects of incorporating aquatic macrophyte biomass on chemical and biological indicators of degraded pasture soil under controlled conditions, assessing its potential to support soil restoration. abstract: From 1931 to 1945, Japanese wartime photography was determined by a censorship system that shaped what could and could not be seen. abstract: This research explores the mobilization of informal social capital as a mechanism for circumventing institutional barriers to export among Moroccan women entrepreneurs. abstract: ABSTRACT Heterochrony, defined as evolutionary changes in developmental timing, is a key mechanism underlying morphological diversification across taxa. abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. abstract: The International Conference on Phenomena in Ionized Gases (ICPIG) is one of the longestrunning and most influential international conferences in plasma physics. abstract: Multifamily housing is common in urban areas, and neighbor noise is a frequent problem. abstract: The loose equilibrium (LE) hypothesis predicts that biotic assemblages will exhibit modest change from year-to-year but will not follow directed trajectories away from a stable baseline over longer periods of time. Using 8 years (2016–2023) of data from 21 National Ecological Observatory Network streams, we test the LE hypothesis for benthic insect assemblages. abstract: Transforming animal manure from an environmental liability into a renewable biohydrogen resource represents a promising strategy for simultaneously addressing waste management and clean energy production. A narrative comparative review was conducted based on the critical synthesis of 130 peer-reviewed publications. abstract: Exosomes are central mediators of intercellular communication in the tumor microenvironment, transferring proteins, lipids, metabolites, and nucleic acids that regulate cancer progression. abstract: This study investigates the interplay between the Big Five personality traits, Environmental Factors, and pro-environmental behavior (PEB) using an integrated approach that combines Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) and Fuzzy Multi-Criteria Decision Making (FMCDM). abstract: While pet ownership is increasingly recognized as a vital contributor to human well-being, the specific behavioral and psychological mechanisms linking pet-related activities to owner happiness remain underexplored. abstract: Abstract Suspended sediment dynamics in small agricultural catchments are shaped by the interaction of overland and subsurface flow processes, yet no event-scale, flow pathway-specific comparisons of seasonal discharge (Q)–suspended sediment concentration (SSC) relationships within a single catchment exist. abstract: The escalation of the Iran conflict, which threatens global energy supply through the Strait of Hormuz, raises the question of how energy sector stocks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) respond to such geopolitical risk. abstract: ABSTRACT Yellow is an established color category despite being generated by a mixture of primaries on RGB displays. abstract: ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) is a key enzyme in cellular metabolism that catalyses the cleavage of citrate to produce acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA), thereby bridging energy metabolism and epigenetic regulation. abstract: Abstract In the irrigated arid regions of Iraq, soil degradation and severe evaporative demand constrain legume productivity. abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive agriculture relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers, which contribute to green‐house gas emissions and to the degradation of soil quality and microbial biodiversity. title: Flight dynamics and optimal control of unpowered avian landings
abstract: Abstract Most birds can transition from aerial to terrestrial locomotion in complex environments. However, to touchdown at safe speeds is challenging as low speeds result in poor aerodynamic control authority, especially in unpowered flight, and how birds manage this is not well understood. Through exploration of the dynamics, we provide an analytical optimal control strategy that minimizes touchdown speed and show that zero touchdown speed is physically possible in unpowered flight. journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences

title: From Approval to Occupancy: Regulatory Translation of Water-System Requirements in Lagos High-Rise Housing
abstract: High-rise residential buildings in Lagos rely heavily on water stored, pumped, and distributed within the building, because public supply is limited. Whether they deliver adequate pressure and continuous supply depends on design decisions that regulation could check. This study examined how far Lagos regulatory instruments translate the technical requirements of building water systems into criteria that can be assessed and verified. A qualitative document analysis was conducted on seven instruments: the National Building Code 2006, the 2019 Lagos planning permit and building-control regulation
journal: International Journal of Environmental Sciences Development & Sustainability

title: An assessment of the sensory attributes and the consumer acceptance of new experimental and commercial spekboom products
abstract: Spekboom (Portulacaria afra), a succulent viewed as both environmentally and socioeconomically acceptable, remains underutilized. This study investigated the culinary potential and consumer acceptability of spekboom across diverse flavour profiles and textures. A sensory assessment was done using Just-About-Right analysis and overall liking of new experimental (relish, pickle, lemon curd, and salad sprinkle) and commercial (preserve, chutney, pickle, and chicken spice) spekboom products, followed by a consumer survey to evaluate drivers of adoption and willingness to try spekboom-based product

title: Shaping biodiversity from within: How experts' perceptions of values, rules and knowledges influence biodiversity assessment
abstract: Abstract While biodiversity conservation has had its local success, worldwide biodiversity loss continues rapidly. Despite the push towards more inclusive and equitable approaches, conservation practices often reinforce existing conceptualizations of biodiversity, excluding other ways of knowing and valuing nature. This paper explores the process of assessing biodiversity among a group of habitat experts. Our study contributes to the literature with empirical understanding of the tension between objective and more pluralistic, relational understandings of biodiversity among a group of experts.

title: Thermophilic Adaptation of a Minimal Hammerhead Ribozyme Comes with a Functional Penalty
abstract: Life has adapted to extreme environments, such as elevated pH, extreme temperatures, and environments with a lack of oxygen. The biomolecules made by organisms that live in extreme environments must adapt to remain folded and functional. Recent computational studies have shown that rRNA, tRNA, and certain mRNAs adapt in thermophilic organisms through an increased GC content. However, few previous studies have assessed the efficiency of adapted thermophilic RNAs. title: Polylactic co-glycolic acid (PLGA)-based nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract: A potential therapeutic strategy against oxidative stress and diabetes in rat model
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. Persea americana seed extract (PSE) has antidiabetic potential but suffers from non-specific distribution and poor bioavailability, thus limiting its clinical application. title: Seed persistence of nine weed species in silage, manure, and slurry and implications for dispersal through organic fertilizers
abstract: Weed seed contamination of cattle feed can contribute to weed dispersal within crop–livestock systems when viable seeds survive digestion and are returned to fields through manure or slurry applications. However, the persistence of weed seeds from feed preservation to waste recycling remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the viability of common agricultural weed seeds after exposure to silage fermentation, simulated rumen digestion, and storage in cattle manure and slurry. Seeds of nine weed species ( Abutilon theophrasti , Alopecurus myosuroides , Amaranthus retroflexus , Av

title: Materials and technological choices in ceramic production of Medieval Almería (al-Andalus): clays, glazes and colorants
abstract: Abstract This article presents the archaeometric characterisation of a collection of medieval pottery (11th–12th centuries) from two documented pottery workshops in the city of Almería. The study focuses on common pottery used for cooking, tableware, water storage, as well as pottery associated with production processes. This type of material is widely represented in the archaeological record, but is rarely characterised from a technological and compositional perspectives. title: Isolation, Characterization, and Phytotoxic Activity of Streptomyces spp. from Diseased Potato Scab Tubers
abstract: Abstract Biological herbicides serve as highly efficient and eco-friendly weed control agents, which typically consist of natural secondary metabolites, such as phytotoxic metabolites produced by Streptomyces sp. However, the isolation of phytotoxic compounds from pathogenic Streptomyces strains has been insufficiently investigated. Here, a total of 50 strains of the Streptomyces genus were isolated from the potato tubers with typical common scab (CS) symptoms using the culture-dependent method. title: Management of Road Infrastructure Project in Cebu City: Monitoring and Evaluation Standard Policy
abstract: The consequential measurement of conveyor infrastructure is the associated roads that provides linkages to neighboring cities and municipalities. A good road transport at the city level is crucial in the movement of constituents and conveyor of goods with low of occurrence costs. Good city road infrastructure is associated not only with the economic growth but also contributory with poverty reduction as stated by various studies. title: Eco-friendly biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles by saprophytic Fusarium solani as a sustainable therapeutic approach for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus wound infections
abstract: The rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has prompted the exploration of novel, naturally sourced therapeutic alternatives. Here, the saprophytic fungus Fusarium solani was used to biosynthesize silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), which were characterized by UV-visible spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). title: Desafíos y oportunidades en los procesos de construcción y gestión de datos: Aportes para una estrategia sanitaria en la provincia de Buenos Aires (2024-2025)
abstract: Los instrumentos estructurados de registro son centrales para la gestión sanitaria, pero su diseño y las condiciones organizacionales que lo rodean inciden fuertemente en la calidad de los datos producidos. Este artículo presenta una investigación cualitativa documental, de diseño flexible, sobre los procesos de construcción y reporte de datos cuantitativos en salud, realizada en tres municipios del conurbano bonaerense y dos direcciones del Ministerio de Salud de la provincia de Buenos Aires (julio 2024-marzo 2025). title: Behavioural and brain volumetric changes associated with problematic substance use through the lifespan
abstract: Abstract Addiction stands as a critical public health concern, contributing substantially to morbidity, mortality and societal burden worldwide. It can be conceptualized along a developmental continuum, from risky substance use in adolescence to compulsive use and addiction in adulthood, yet the neural changes underlying this continuum remain poorly understood. Here we show age-specific brain structural trajectories along this continuum by harmonizing multimodal data across large population cohorts spanning adolescence to late adulthood. title: Population structure of the last Tomares nogelii (Lepidoptera, Lycaenidae) population in the European Union—A capture‐mark‐recapture study
abstract: Abstract Effective conservation of highly specialized butterflies in fragmented landscapes requires quantitative estimates of population size, turnover and functional connectivity. Here, we present the first capture–mark–recapture (CMR) survey of the last known metapopulation of Tomares nogelii dobrogensis , a locally monophagous Lycaenid, in northern Dobrogea, Romania. From May to July 2025, six spatially separated colonies were surveyed, recording 832 capture events (638 first captures and 194 recaptures). title: Respostas fisiológicas, crescimento e qualidade de hastes florais de espécies de Heliconia tratadas com ácido salicílico e caulim sob condições de pleno sol no semiárido
abstract: Tropical floriculture is an economically relevant activity, particularly for family farming, because of the high added value of cut flowers and the potential for rapid financial returns. Among tropical ornamentals, Heliconia species are valued for their diversity of colors and forms. However, cultivation under full-sun conditions in semi-arid regions exposes plants to high solar irradiance, which may constrain physiological performance and growth. title: Ecological impact of steeplebush (Spiraea tomentosa L.) invasion on mite communities (Acari, Mesostigmata) in wet meadow ecosystems
abstract: Invasive plants are species introduced outside their natural range and often cause ecological or economic harm. By modifying litter quality, root architecture, and soil chemistry, invasive plants can alter many soil processes, including nutrient cycling and edaphic activity. The main aim of our study was to provide the first assessment in Poland of the ecological impact of Spiraea tomentosa L. invasion on the abundance, diversity, and species richness of soil Mesotigmata (Gamasida; Gamasina and Uropodnia) mite communities in wet meadow ecosystems, thereby offering novel insights into the below

title: Stochastic Resonance and Library Space Design: Rethinking Silent Policy Through Cognitive Psychology
abstract: This study explored the integration of cognitive psychology into library space design, specifically examining how stochastic resonance where background noise enhances cognitive performance can inform acoustic zoning policies in academic libraries. Anchored in Ranganathan’s principles and the shifting demands of emotionally responsive users, the research critiqued the traditional silent library model. title: Localizing Early Numeracy Policy in Decentralized ECE Systems: Evidence from Indonesia
abstract: Early numeracy is central to school readiness and educational equity, yet national policies may be implemented unevenly across geographically and institutionally diverse early childhood education (ECE) settings. This study examined the implementation of Indonesia's 2024 early literacy-numeracy policy in urban, rural, and remote settings in West Nusa Tenggara and explored the feasibility of the LENTAS (Locally Contextualized Early Numeracy with Technology Support) model. title: Development of Interactive Media Learning for Flood Risk Education: Enhancing Flood Knowledge in Tha Than, Eastern Thailand
abstract: This study developed and evaluated interactive digital learning media that translate local flood evidence from Tha Than Subdistrict, Chachoengsao Province, Thailand, into flood risk education. A research and development design were used with two objectives: (1) to design and develop the media from local flood evidence and to evaluate their quality and efficiency (E₁/E₂), and (2) to compare flood knowledge before and after use of the media. title: Demarcating and negotiating borders: Stancetaking and identity construction in Polish online discourse about Russia's war in Ukraine
abstract: This study investigates discursive borderwork in online communication about the war in Ukraine. It examines how borders are drawn through the dynamics of nomination and stancetaking and their relationship to identity construction at both the micro scale of individual references and the macro scale of single comments and interactional exchanges. The analysis draws on user-generated content from Polish internet forums collected between April and September 2022. title: Dietary nanoencapsulated A-Ghrelin improves growth performance and health status in juvenile Siberian sturgeon
abstract: This study evaluated a novel multi-functional feed supplement for juvenile Siberian sturgeon ( Acipenser baerii ), combining an acetylated ghrelin analog (A-Ghrelin) with a chitosan-alginate-iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) nanoparticle delivery system. Over 60 days, 240 fish (initial weight: 8.5 ± 0.9 g) were assigned to eight diets ( n = 3 tanks/treatment). title: Molecular, agro-morphological, and phytochemical analysis of goldenrod (Solidago spp.) genotypes grown under two contrasting climates
abstract: Solidago , belonging to the Asteraceae family, is used as an herbal medicine and possess diuretic, anti-microbial, cytotoxic, anti-inflammatory, gastroprotective and immunobiological properties. However, the extent to which genetic differences among wild and cultivated Solidago materials contribute to variation in agronomic performance and phytochemical quality under contrasting environmental conditions remains insufficiently understood. title: When Geography Dilutes Accountability: Managerial Discretion and Fiscal Expansion in Local Government
abstract: Democratic accountability assumes that the citizens who bear the costs of government decisions can sanction the officials who make them. We identify a structural break in this assumption. When a city funds itself through taxes that fall partly on nonresidents (highway travelers, commuters, and regional shoppers who cannot vote in local elections) the electoral link between bearing costs and imposing sanctions weakens. title: What are pulsar companions made of? Using gravitational tides to probe their compositions
abstract: Low eccentricity, short orbital period pulsar companions may provide a probe to study novel dense and stable exoplanet internal compositions due to the potentially significant orbital evolution they experience caused by strong gravitational tides. We model the tidal characteristics such as apsidal motion constants, orbital precession, and tidal deformability for a variety of equations of state to be compared with values recovered via pulsar timing for a sample of four systems: PSR J1719-1438b, PSR J0636+5128b, PSR J2322+2650b, and PSR J1807-2459A b. title: Radiocarbon dating of wooden beams at Herodium palace-fortress: Modeling tree-felling events and their implications on site chronology
abstract: The site of Herodium is best known for its impressive, well-preserved palace fortress, built by Herod the Great, towards the end of the 1st century BC. The site's conical shape, artificially created to transform it into Herod's monumental burial complex, is clearly seen from afar. The impressive preservation of wooden beams and posts at the site has allowed for a rigorous radiocarbon study of the beams' felling dates and their potential implications for the timing of construction activities at the site. title: Molecular mechanisms of boron in animal nutrition: from cellular signalling to systemic metabolic regulation
abstract: Boron is essential for higher plants and biologically active in animals, although its essentiality in mammals remains unproven because no boron-dependent enzyme, cofactor, or consistent deficiency syndrome has been established. This review critically examines the biochemical, cellular, and physiological roles of boron in animal nutrition, emphasizing chemical speciation, dose dependence, and mechanistic uncertainty. title: Confucian ethics and the narrative construction of sustainability and food safety: a case study of ‘ A Bite of China ’
abstract: As public concern about food crises has risen, China faces the challenge of rebuilding confidence in its domestic food supply chains. In response, state media has intentionally utilised culturally rich, visually appealing storylines to reframe food governance through traditional ethical ideals and ecological sustainability. This study examines how Confucian ethics are incorporated into the Chinese food documentary ‘A Bite of China’ and how the series constructs narratives of food safety and sustainability. title: Epidemic dynamics of wheat stripe rust under climate change and lagging human-led disease management
abstract: Abstract Wheat stripe rust poses substantial challenges to food security in China, and elucidating its epidemic patterns provides a scientific basis for disease management. To investigate the factors underlying its widespread 2020 outbreak and the associated inoculum transmission dynamics, 645 Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici samples were collected from 15 provinces across China in this study. title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). title: Constraining Fault Kinematics and India‐Tarim Convergence Partitioning in Southwestern Tibet With Geodetic Block Modeling
abstract: Abstract How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. In this study, we derive high‐resolution velocity fields for the southwestern Tibetan Plateau using both GNSS and InSAR observations. title: Effect of substituting maize with newly released sorghum varieties on laying performance and egg quality of bovans brown
abstract: Rising maize prices and increasing competition caused by rising human food demand are forcing poultry producers to seek alternative energy sources. Newly released grain sorghum varieties in western Ethiopia may serve as a viable substitute, but their effects on laying hen performance and profitability need assessment. title: Development Pathways and Financial Value in Premier League Football: Comparing Integrated Multi-Club Networks and Non-Integrated Clubs
abstract: Integrated multi-club ownership networks have expanded rapidly in European football, yet empirical research comparing the financial returns of their youth development with traditional single-club structures remains limited. This study compares two non-integrated clubs (Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur) with two integrated networks (Manchester City, Brighton & Hove Albion). title: Burned habitats facilitate predation and lead to long‐term reductions in prey success
abstract: Intensifying wildfire regimes under global change are expected to shift species interactions through changes in habitat structure and composition, vegetation productivity, and sensory cues. Yet there is little evidence of how burn-induced changes in habitat composition and structure modify predator-prey relationships. We investigated how wildfires influence relationships between mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and cougars (Puma concolor) in the US Intermountain West using high-resolution telemetry data, kill site locations, and annual measures of mule deer fawn production. title: Vanishing Borders: Ethnicity and Trade Costs at the Origin of the Yugoslav Market
abstract: This article uses the creation of a paradigmatic multi-ethnic state, Yugoslavia, in 1918, and a novel large dataset of grain prices to examine the effect of ethnicity on trade costs when borders changed. Controlling for transport costs and import tariffs, we find a large but transitory border effect. Ethno-religious differences initially significantly increased price gaps, but their negative influence vanished over time as well. abstract: BACKGROUND: Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life of individuals with serious, progressive illnesses. Therapeutic patient education is a key approach for enhancing patient autonomy and empowerment. However, structured educational interventions for patients receiving palliative care remain poorly documented in the literature, in contrast to the growing body of evidence regarding education for caregivers and healthcare professionals. abstract: This article investigates the motivational grammars of villains in Hollywood superhero films through the lens of Schwartz’s Theory of Basic Human Values. title: The soybean agribusiness and dismantling of local economies: Socioeconomic impact and conflict in the Cerrado biome of Piauí (Brazil, 1996-2022)
abstract: This article examines how agribusiness expansion has reshaped local economies in the Cerrado biome of the Matopiba region (Brazil) by comparing the socioeconomic impacts and environmental conflicts associated with two agricultural production models: diversified farming and soybean monoculture. Drawing from discussions concerning peasant economies and the distinction between ‘substantive’ and ‘formal economy’, the study integrates documentary, qualitative, and quantitative data (1996–2022) on vegetation extraction, agricultural production, deforestation, wage labour, land use, and conflicts. title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
abstract: Abstract Climate change mitigation reshapes the distribution of economic assets in the low-carbon transition. Here we quantify climate-related assets for 169 countries across four dimensions: fossil fuel production, climate change damages, renewable energy potential and land carbon sequestration capacity. abstract: Abstract Mechanically responsive organic crystals are attracting increasing attention as soft actuators. title: The spillover effects and mechanisms of typhoon disasters on stock volatility: considering the heterogeneity of financial enterprises and non-financial enterprises
abstract: Extreme meteorological events, such as typhoons, constitute severe external shocks that significantly impact macroeconomic operations and fundamental corporate activities. Grounded in stakeholder theory, this study employs a two way fixed effects difference in differences model alongside the VaR-BEKK-MVGARCH-DUMMY-T framework. title: Combined application of biochar and silicon on physiological and antioxidant defense mechanism of wheat against plastic induced stress
abstract: The exponential rise in plastic waste has become a major problem for the environment and public health because of its high stability, non-biodegradable nature and long-term persistence. This investigation analyzed the effects of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) on wheat plants and the alleviation of its adverse effects using jackfruit shell biochar (JSBC) and potassium silicate (Si). While group coaching is increasingly recognized as a developmental modality to foster growth in complex work environments, gaps remain in understanding how group coaching supports women who face imposter syndrome or how effective this modality is for women anesthesiologists. abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen reduction systems (ORS) are protection systems, with a design protection objective to limit fire spread beyond the point of ignition. abstract: BACKGROUND: The emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) uropathogenic Escherichia coli and the increasing prevalence of biofilm-associated infections have created an urgent need for new antimicrobial strategies. abstract: The role of different host species in the circulation dynamics of tick-borne pathogens (TBPs) in northern ecosystems remains insufficiently characterized, despite the widespread distribution of these pathogens in European wildlife. In particular, the contribution of medium-sized mammals, including non-native species, to TBP circulation is poorly understood. title: How much would egg and duckling predation need to be reduced to reverse declines of ground-nesting waterfowl in Finland? A demographic scenario analysis
abstract: Abstract Populations of water- and wetland-associated birds have declined globally due to multiple pressures, including habitat loss, climate change, and predation. Ground-nesting waterfowl are particularly vulnerable to predators, and the spread of invasive mammalian predators like raccoon dogs ( Nyctereutes procyonoides ) has intensified this threat in parts of Northern Europe. Predator removal has previously been implemented to support waterfowl populations, with mixed outcomes across studies. title: Influence of functional traits and trait syndromes on the vulnerability of amphibians and reptiles in the tropical dry forest of Oaxaca, Mexico
abstract: Abstract Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, yet their biodiversity remains understudied compared to humid tropical forests. We integrated functional trait ecology with environmental vulnerability assessments to evaluate multi‑causal disturbances affecting amphibians and reptiles in Oaxaca, Mexico, a hotspot of endemism and biodiversity loss. Environmental Vulnerability Scores (EVS) were constructed for the complete herpetofaunal assemblage and compared against international (IUCN) and national (NOM‑059) classifications. title: Newly planted woodlands improve connectivity for woodland fauna, flora and fungi
abstract: Abstract Context Young planted woodlands may only support a small proportion of the biodiversity found in mature woodlands but may play an important role in promoting species movements and enhancing biodiversity due to their emerging structural similarities. Objectives We assessed whether recently planted woodlands increase connectivity between mature woodland patches relative to agricultural fields, and whether responses vary across active (small mammals, ground invertebrates) and passive (plants, fungi) dispersers. title: Genomic prediction of single cross families of perennial ryegrass under two nitrogen managements
abstract: Abstract The performance of a single cross is determined by the additive effects of the parents and their interactions, which can be estimated through general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA). With genome‐wide marker information, it is possible to predict GCA for new parents and the genetic value of unrealized crosses. Several studies in crops such as maize ( Zea mays L.) and rice ( Oryza sativa L.) have demonstrated the potential of genomic prediction for single‐cross performance. title: Politicizing Facts in Canadian Parliament: A Comparative Analysis of the 35th and 42nd Parliament
abstract: Abstract Contemporary political controversies often seem to centre on issues that can be verified empirically. This article investigates the hypothesis that right-wing populism increases such contestation—which I call the politicization of facts—by a comparison of parliamentary debates on 44 bills in the Canadian parliament spanning two time periods (1994–1997 and 2015–2019) and two subjects (the environment and crime). title: Prokaryotic assemblages in bromeliad phytotelmata reflect shared and host-specific patterns in campos rupestres
abstract: Abstract Bromeliads play a key ecological role in many Brazilian ecosystems, particularly in campos rupestres (Brazilian rupestrian grasslands) , but face increasing threats from mining and extractive activities in the Iron Quadrangle region of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Their water-filled leaf axils, or phytotelmata, host diverse microbial communities that may influence host fitness, although the ecological drivers shaping these communities remain poorly understood, especially in endangered campo rupestre ferruginoso (ferruginous rupestrian grasslands). title: Legume Residue Configuration Modulates Topsoil Moisture and Greenhouse Gas Emissions Under Contrasting Wetting Regimes in a No‐Till Fallow
abstract: ABSTRACT Crop residues provide agronomic and environmental benefits under no‐till systems, but decomposition can increase greenhouse gas emissions, particularly from legume residues. Rainfall events influence soil moisture and microbial activity, yet relatively little is known about how surface residue configurations modify greenhouse gas responses under contrasting wetting regimes. This study evaluated how standing, mulched, and removed mung bean ( Vigna radiata (L.) R. title: Supercapacitive decoupled electrolyzer towards enhanced green hydrogen production
abstract: Green hydrogen production through renewable-powered water splitting is pivotal for achieving net-zero carbon emissions. However, its large-scale adoption remains challenged by high energy demands, system complexity, and the need for flexible integration with intermittent renewable energy sources. Decoupled water electrolysis, in which hydrogen and oxygen are produced in temporally separate steps, provides a promising route for membrane-free and inherently safer operation. title: A 4-D spatio-temporal misfit function for waveform inversion of Distributed Acoustic Sensing data
abstract: Summary Standard Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) objective functions often struggle to resolve deep structures when data are dominated by localised near-surface scattering. To address this, we develop a 4-D time-frequency-space-wavenumber (TFXK) objective function that explicitly enforces spatial coherence, leveraging the dense sampling of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS). title: Reconstructed functional diversity and food-web structure reveal mammalian community shifts through the Oligo-Miocene in Oregon
abstract: Abstract Understanding how ecological communities respond to environmental change over long timescales is essential for predicting modern ecosystem dynamics. Here, we reconstructed functional community composition and trophic network structure of seven mammal communities from the eastern region of Oregon. We focused on fossil localities that span the past 32 million years. We used diet and body mass to reconstruct community functional diversity and evaluated community differences using correspondence analysis and Fisher’s exact tests. title: Provenance and environment jointly shape early regeneration in fir and beech: evidence from distributed participatory trials across Europe
abstract: Summary Forest regeneration is shaped by strong demographic filters during germination and early establishment, yet the relative contributions of seed provenance and environment remain poorly understood under natural conditions. We combined climate‐chamber trials with a continental‐scale, field‐based citizen science seed‐sowing experiment to quantify germination, early phenological development, and 3‐yr postgermination survival of fir ( Abies spp.) and beech ( Fagus spp.) provenances across Europe. title: Reprogramming tumor cells with LCOR mRNA nanotherapy to enhance immunotherapy
abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) are often considered undruggable due to their structural complexity. mRNA technologies can overcome this therapeutic limitation by enabling dynamic protein replacement therapies. Here, we explore the TF activity of LCOR (Ligand-dependent corepressor), which suppresses tumor growth, at least in part by inducing the antigen presentation machinery (APM) in tumor cells and constraining cellular plasticity. title: THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE VARIABILITY ON MILK PRODUCTION AMONG DAIRY FARMERS IN RWANDA, CASE STUDY ON SELECTED COOPERATIVES IN GICUMBI DISTRICT
abstract: In Rwanda, smallholder dairy farmers are increasingly experiencing the effects of changing weather patterns, which influence pasture availability, water resources, and milk production. Gicumbi District, known for its dairy farming potential, has experienced noticeable fluctuations in rainfall and temperature, yet limited empirical evidence existed on how these climatic changes affect milk production among dairy farmers. title: Niches in cancer: from primary tumors to metastatic disease
abstract: Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant-cell behavior. These local environments sustain stem-like states, regulate immune surveillance and vascular remodeling, and influence dissemination and treatment response. title: Mechanism and field application of CO₂ phase‑change fracturing for gas extraction in low‑permeability coal seams
abstract: To address the inefficient gas extraction problem of high‑gas low‑permeability coal seams in Guizhou Province, this study investigates the permeability‑enhancing mechanism and field performance of liquid CO₂ phase‑change fracturing, taking local anthracite and bituminous coal as research objects. Relying on the special thermophysical properties of liquid CO₂, phase‑change shock loading creates multi‑zone fracturing in coal mass; meanwhile, CO₂ can displace adsorbed methane to improve seam permeability. title: REIMAGINING CLIMATE JUSTICE THROUGH THE LENS OF GREEN SOCIAL WORK: AN INTEGRATED CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK
abstract: Climate justice scholarship has converged on a trivalent model of distributive, procedural and recognition justice, yet this model remains largely anthropocentric, vulnerable to technocratic and market-based capture, and silent on both the epistemic marginalisation of Indigenous and Global South knowledge and the structural drivers of the crisis. Green Social Work, grounded in eco-social theory, links environmental and social justice, but its implications for the conceptual architecture of climate justice have not been systematically mapped. title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
abstract: Community question-answering (cQA) platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer “best” or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. title: Ascending infection of Gardnerella spp. and compartmentalized inflammatory response in fetal–maternal interface organ‐on‐chip model
abstract: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality worldwide, with ascending infection and inflammation at the fetal-maternal interface recognized as major contributors to its pathophysiology. Gardnerella spp., key species associated with bacterial vaginosis, have been implicated in adverse pregnancy outcomes; however, the mechanisms underlying their ability to ascend and trigger inflammatory responses remain poorly understood. title: Beyond degrees Celsius: Mapping competing justice scenarios in Australia's energy transition
abstract: The energy transition is routinely framed as a technical challenge. But transitions are socio-political undertakings. The struggle over what counts as a “just transition” is a struggle over what a liveable future should look like. Facts alone cannot settle this dilemma because the struggle rests on competing ideas about what a just transition is for . Detailed economic and physical scenarios map climate trajectories, but no comparable map exists of the internal rationales behind the transition narratives. Social science should fill that gap. title: The opioid crisis in different contexts around the world: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Aim This scoping review examined how peer-reviewed literature conceptualizes and contextualizes opioid-related harms worldwide, with attention to regulatory environments, opioid types, including prescribed and illicit opioids, and population-level consequences. Subject and methods This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards. Systematic searches were conducted in LILACS, Scopus, Embase, and MEDLINE up to January 2026. title: Updated facility‐level inventory and LCIA of the public electricity grid in Ontario, Canada
abstract: Abstract As the composition of Ontario's electricity grid will change over time, it is important to have a comprehensive understanding of the environmental impacts of Ontario's electricity grid as it stands today. However, publicly available information on impacts of Ontario's electricity grid is available only in aggregate from government sources. title: All-trans retinoic acid in solid-tumour immunity: context-dependent signalling, cellular states, and combination therapy
abstract: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) influences several processes relevant to cancer immunotherapy, yet its effects in solid tumours range from relief of myeloid suppression to reinforcement of immune tolerance. This divergence reflects the source and duration of retinoid exposure, the molecular state of responding cells and the phase of treatment. title: Improving the efficiency of helitack crew deployment through spatial optimization
abstract: Background Improving the deployment of helitack crews is crucial for limiting the growth of newly ignited wildfires. Aims We evaluated whether an optimization model could improve deployment in areas where high-intensity fires could occur compared with the current heuristic approach. Methods The model maximized coverage of areas with high potential intensity values using a fixed number of deployment sites. abstract: Multifunctional and environmentally friendly hydrogel materials were developed through the reaction of chemically crosslinking biocompatible polymers and natural crosslinkers present in grape pomace, a waste product left over during the wine making process. title: From molecular advances to limited clinical impact: The persistent gap in chromoblastomycosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chromoblastomycosis (CBM) is a chronic implantation mycosis of considerable morbidity, first described more than a century ago, predominantly affecting rural populations in tropical and subtropical regions. Although historically associated with impoverished settings, an increasing number of cases have been reported in both endemic and non-endemic areas, including high-income countries, reflecting an underrecognized epidemiological landscape. title: Balanced phosphorus supply and foliar Zn-EDTA improve nutrient acquisition, physiological Zn function, and potential seed Zn bioavailability in blackgram grown on Zn-deficient soil
abstract: Phosphorus (P) - zinc (Zn) interactions regulate nutrient acquisition, physiological function, productivity, and seed nutritional quality. title: Land fragmentation, tenure insecurity, and irrigation water management in Egypt: a hybrid review and sensitivity analysis
abstract: Egypt has one of the tightest water budgets in the world, while its farmland has been divided into ever-smaller holdings for a century. This paper connects these two issues by pairing a structured literature review with a transparent sensitivity analysis based on Egyptian census data and Nile Delta field studies. It asks how holding size and tenure affect irrigation water application, and how much of the excess consolidation might recover. title: Lightweight CNT Fabric Current Collectors Enabling Silicon Anodes in High-Capacity Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) require metallic current collectors such as copper for anodes and aluminum for cathodes, adding significant weight without contributing to the capacity. This is especially problematic for Si-dominant anodes, with mass loadings lower than 2 mg cm–2. Here, copper is replaced with lightweight, non-woven carbon nanotube fabrics (CNTfs) combined with high-capacity Si/PPAN active material to form a self-standing composite anode. title: Sustainable valorization of tea waste for promoting plant growth, secondary metabolites production and environmental sustainability in tea cultivation
abstract: Abstract Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze, represents a commercially significant crop, primarily recognized for its pharmacologically active secondary metabolites, including catechins and caffeine. However, excessive reliance on agrochemicals threatens both soil fertility and the biochemical quality of tea leaves, underscoring the urgent need for sustainable agronomic alternatives. title: Quantitative Fracture Analysis of All‐Polymer Active Layers for Intrinsically Stretchable Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Comprehensive Summary Stretchy organic solar cells require active layers that can not only tolerate large tensile deformation but also resist crack propagation after damage initiation. However, conventional mechanical descriptors such as crack‐onset strain and fracture strain provide limited information on how cracks evolve and dissipate energy in deformable photovoltaic films. title: The actual sky of Van Gogh’s Starry Night: a multidisciplinary reconstruction
abstract: The Starry Night : whether its sky represents spontaneous fantasy or a realist depiction has gone unanswered for over a century. Earlier astronomical readings, constrained by the conventional June dating, reached mutually exclusive conclusions, and the painting’s celestial arrangement was never quantitatively tested. title: Predicting connectivity from movement trajectories and step selection
abstract: Predicting and mapping connectivity are essential for ecology and conservation in the face of environmental change. Yet connectivity modeling is challenging because it requires understanding how organisms successfully move across complex landscapes. GPS tracking increasingly produces detailed data on movement trajectories and fine‐scale resource selection, yet it remains unclear how to reliably link such data to connectivity models without relying on individual‐based simulations. title: Green synthesized silver nanoparticles from floral waste of Tagetes patula for mitigation of Meloidogyne incognita stress in tomato plants
abstract: Meloidogyne incognita ( M. incognita ) is a destructive plant parasitic nematode causing severe crop losses worldwide. This study aims to evaluate the potential of Tagetes patula - mediated silver nanoparticles (TP@Ag NPs) as an eco-friendly nematicidal and plant growth-promoting agent against M. incognita infection in Solanum lycopersicum L. seedlings. abstract: Reconstructing the dietary and habitat preferences of extinct taxa is essential to understand the selective pressures that drive morphological and behavioral evolution, which provides a necessary framework for understanding macroevolutionary patterns and how extinct lineages navigated ecological shifts across time and space. This study examines the degree to which environmental changes influence dietary intake by analysing dental microwear in Heteroxerus rubricati , an extinct xerine squirrel from the Middle Miocene (Aragonian) of the Iberian Peninsula. abstract: Background: Skin cancer is a major public health problem worldwide. abstract: Abstract Adverse meteorological conditions often force farmers to plant maize ( Zea mays L.) outside its optimal planting window. Early or delayed planting can significantly influence crop phenology, yield, and disease severity. This study evaluated two contrasting cultivars, PAN4R-872BR (early-maturing and NLB-susceptible) and DKC75-65BR (medium-maturing and NLB-resistant), across multiple planting dates and assessed the effect of planting date on Northern Leaf Blight (NLB) severity. title: Contrasting CH 4 flux responses to distinct drought regimes and nitrogen enrichment in a temperate steppe
abstract: Summary Drought and nitrogen (N) deposition alter greenhouse gas fluxes, but how distinct drought scenarios interact with N enrichment to regulate the methane (CH 4 ) sink remains poorly understood. We conducted a 4‐yr field experiment in a temperate steppe to examine CH 4 fluxes under three drought regimes – early‐season intense drought (ID), mid‐season chronic drought (CD), and mid‐season reduced rainfall frequency (RF) – and N addition. title: Parents’ perspectives and roles in influencing 10–12-year-old children’s fruit and vegetable consumption: a qualitative study in Sweden
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parents play a central role in shaping children's health behaviours and dietary habits. Previous research has provided insight into parents' feeding practices, especially regarding preschoolers. Less is known about how parents of 10-12-year-old children, whose fruit and vegetable (F&V) intake is particularly low relative to recommendations, perceive F&V and translate their intentions regarding F&V into everyday practices. title: Processing and functional valorisation of Aronia melanocarpa pomace: a critical assessment of extraction technologies and industrial implementation barriers
abstract: Chokeberry ( Aronia melanocarpa ) pomace is a major by-product of juice production and represents a rich source of polyphenols, dietary fibre, and functional compounds. Despite its high nutritional and technological potential, its industrial utilisation remains limited. This study provides a critical and application-oriented review of processing, extraction, and valorisation strategies for chokeberry pomace, with particular emphasis on technological performance, stability of bioactive compounds, and food-related applications. title: Combining ability and gene action studies for different horticultural traits in pink brinjal (Solanum melongena L.)
abstract: Pink brinjal ( Solanum melongena L.) is a highly preferred and extensively cultivated vegetable crop in Jammu and Kashmir, yet its genetic improvement has been constrained by the limited availability of high-yielding cultivars and the paucity of genetic information for parental selection. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of combining ability and gene action in elite pink brinjal germplasm, generating a strategic framework for hybrid breeding in the specialized market segment. abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Water Use Efficiency (WUE) is widely used to describe carbon-water coupling, but its meaning varies among disciplines, measurement approaches and spatial and temporal scales. title: Physical Characterization of Volcanic Aquifer Systems in the Southwestern Ethiopian Highlands: A Case of the Gilgel Gibe Catchment
abstract: Volcanic aquifers are globally important groundwater resources, but their pronounced heterogeneity arising from lava emplacement, volcanic facies, structural features, and differential weathering makes hydrogeological characterization challenging. In many developing regions, limited field data further constrain aquifer characterization, increasing uncertainty in groundwater development and management. abstract: The cGAS–STING pathway is composed of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) and the stimulator of interferon genes (STING). It plays a critical role in detecting DNA damage and activating the innate immune system for pathogen defense. The pathway has been extensively studied for its potential in cancer therapy, aiming to enhance anti-tumor immunity. title: Therapeutic and Biomedical Applications of Dopamine‐Derived Scaffolds: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Dopamine, a pivotal catecholamine, serves as a versatile scaffold in drug design due to its unique pharmacological profile and chemical reactivity. This review integrates evidence on the therapeutic applications of dopamine-derived compounds, ranging from their established roles in treating neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease to emerging innovations in enzyme inhibition, gene delivery, and tissue engineering. title: The transition towards CSA as a relational model: shaping relational processes between farmers and governments, agri-food corporations and the financial sector
abstract: Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) can enhance the mitigation and adaptation capacity of the sector. Yet progress towards CSA remains slow. Durable and scalable transformation requires more than technological adoption or changes in farmers’ capabilities; it depends on the relationships through which actors coordinate resources, interests, and institutional conditions. abstract: Study region : Geum River Basin, South Korea, a structurally heterogeneous watershed with 14 agricultural, 12 domestic/industrial intake, and 3 hydropower stakeholders. The basin has the highest agricultural water demand among South Korea’s six major river basins, with precipitation concentrated in the summer monsoon season, making dam operations critical for balancing competing water demands during irrigation. title: Experimental enhancement of a double-slope solar still using external reflectors and nano-coated absorber plates for solar desalination
abstract: Freshwater scarcity, particularly in arid and off-grid regions, demands efficient and low-cost desalination technologies. abstract: The use of Rubberized Geopolymer Concrete (RGC) represents a sustainable solution that can reduce reliance on Portland cement and make use of the potential uses of waste-tire rubber in construction. This review paper critically evaluates the constituent materials, design parameters, rubber pretreatment, fresh and hardened properties, durability, microstructure, and performance-enhancement measures of RGC.
