abstract: Abstract The olive oil industry generates a significant amount of by-products during harvesting and oil extraction, creating environmental challenges while offering opportunities for valorization within livestock production systems. This review provides a structured synthesis of current knowledge on chemical composition, nutritional characteristics, bioactive properties, processing strategies, and feeding applications of major olive oil by-products, including olive pomace, olive cake, olive leaves, and olive mill wastewater. abstract: Hamlet, staged in Moscow on 8 January 1912, is one of the most celebrated and extensively studied theatrical productions of the twentieth century, as it brought together the co-director of the Moscow Art Theatre, Konstantin Sergeevich Stanislavsky, and the English director Edward Gordon Craig. abstract: Abstract Quantum computer hardware is predicted to scale over hundreds of thousands of qubits coming online in the next decade. abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. Vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and ocean sensing all depend on recognizing underwater signals, but to our knowledge LALMs have not been systematically evaluated on them. abstract: Cylindrical or spherical windows often appear in experiments and real applications. Measuring through those windows requires projecting 3D points to pixels, which is different to compute due to refraction. abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). title: Field Response of the Orbital Moment Probed by Integrated Magnetic Circular Dichroism
abstract: Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) is an optical probe of orbital time reversal symmetry breaking. Although frequency integrated MCD is related to the self-rotation contribution to orbital magnetization at zero field, its magnetic response generally differs from the thermodynamic orbital susceptibility. Here, we define the MCD susceptibility and derive general expressions for multiband systems using an electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariant approach. abstract: The near-field evolution of chemically reactive pollutants in the exhaust plume of a 270 m crude oil tanker is investigated using a high-fidelity Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) framework coupled with a Conditional Moment Closure (CMC) turbulence-chemistry interaction model and the CBM-IV atmospheric chemistry scheme. title: Hydrodynamics and propulsive efficiency of stern-sculling propulsion
abstract: Stern-sculling is a traditional form of human-powered boat propulsion in which a single oar is oscillated laterally at the stern. In this study, we investigate this propulsion technique from a hydrodynamic perspective by continuously measuring the oar kinematics, the boat motion, and the forces acting on the oar across a broad range of boat speeds. abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. title: Existence of Minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah Model via Covariance Floors on the Value Distribution
abstract: The Gaussian Mumford-Shah model segments an image into regions by minimizing a continuous multivariate Gaussian negative log-likelihood term plus a perimeter penalty. It is used for scalar- and vector-valued images, in particular hyperspectral images, but the existence of a minimizer in general is not guaranteed. abstract: We propose a protocol to prepare and probe dark states in a single-molecule electron spin resonance based on atomic force microscopy (ESR-AFM), thus extending existing techniques developed to address Rabi oscillations. To this end, we simulate in analogy to atomic physics the coherent manipulation of a three-level system in the V-configuration using a multifrequency magnetic field. title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,λ)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. title: Sensory Comfort Across Multisensory XR Prototypes for Autistic Adults
abstract: Multisensory XR may support informal learning for autistic adults, but sensory-friendly design often emphasizes reducing input. We conducted a mixed-methods, counterbalanced within-subjects study with 20 Chinese autistic adults who evaluated five complete XR configurations presenting the same popular-science content. Comfort differed substantially across the configurations (Friedman chi-square(4) = 46.39, p < .001, Kendall's W = .58). abstract: Lithium-rich cathodes boast a large specific capacity due to the presence of excess lithium per transition metal. abstract: Topological insulators lie outside the standard Landau paradigm: Instead of being characterized by local order parameters and spontaneous symmetry breaking, their defining properties are encoded in the global structure of their quantum states and manifested as robust boundary states. abstract: By employing SWAP Monte Carlo moves during slow Lubachevsky-Stillinger-like particle growth, we generate well-thermalized disordered jammed ellipse packings for a wide range of particle aspect ratios $α$ and maximum/minimum particle-diameter ratios $λ$. abstract: Silicon-on-insulator is mostly the main driving material system for the field of silicon photonics, including PICs, due to high index contrast and compatibility with current semiconductor manufacturing processes [1]. abstract: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. abstract: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. abstract: Future lunar surface missions require reliable positioning for autonomous rover operations. Lunar navigation satellite systems may provide limited vertical positioning accuracy due to satellite availability and observation geometry, particularly during early deployment. title: Spaceflight-associated Motion Sickness in Commercial Crew Astronauts
abstract: Spaceflight-associated motion sickness, including space motion sickness (SMS) and terrestrial readaptation motion sickness (TRMS), has presented as the most operationally limiting effect on the human in the days following a gravity transition. Published data suggest that astronaut head movements provoke symptoms, but those studies rarely controlled for them. abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. abstract: Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) operate from colocation facilities that draw power from regional grids and store limited backup fuel. abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) updates for Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) allow engineers to modify their software wirelessly. In the automotive domain, they enable manufacturers to update software without physical access to the vehicle. However, OTA updates can generate a large number of possible software configurations. abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. abstract: Marine fishery and aquaculture processing generate substantial volumes of biological byproducts—fish skin, bone, scales, and viscera—that remain underutilized as feedstocks for higher-value bio-based materials. abstract: Humanoid robotic arms must manage uncertain contact during grasping, assembly, transport, and physical human-robot interaction. title: Ireland & the Ocean: a decade dive review into Ocean Literacy
abstract: Human and natural systems are deeply interconnected, influencing one another for centuries. In recent decades, the protection of the marine environment has gained prominence, particularly following several reports linking climate change, biodiversity loss and ocean pollution to human health. Ocean Literacy (OL), a framework that promotes education for sustainable development (ESD) focused on the ocean, is emerging as a strategic bridge between education, sustainability, and public policy. abstract: The objective was to diagnose the orientation of quality management in higher education institutions. abstract: We read with great interest the report describing the first robotic totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass (TECAB) in Southeast Asia. While this achievement deserves recognition, we believe several aspects-including revascularization strategy, prolonged operative and recovery times, and the lack of intraoperative transit-time flow measurement-require further clarification to accurately interpret the clinical significance of this pioneering experience.

abstract: In this introduction to the special issue, we define and explore the concept of national narratives in East and Southeast Asia. abstract: The Philippines was briefly the world's largest market for non-fungible token (NFT) ownership, driven by the play-to-earn game Axie Infinity during the pandemic, with Vietnam and Thailand close behind. abstract: This study investigated stakeholder perspectives on government-led quality assurance in higher education institutions in Nangarhar Province, including perceptions of government support, implementation challenges, and quality improvement needs. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract Marine social-ecological systems (SES) face unprecedented pressures, demanding approaches designed to create more sustainable interactions within and between those systems. abstract: Disaster outcomes in rural Indonesia are shaped not only by the intensity of hazards but also by the social relationships through which communities communicate, cooperate, and access resources. This integrative review examined how community social capital contributes to disaster resilience in rural Indonesia and under what conditions it fails to do so. abstract: Chronic lung infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major complication of cystic fibrosis (CF), contributing to lung function decline and increased morbidity and mortality. title: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR LIFECYCLE SAFETY MANAGEMENT AND ASSURANCE OF RECHARGEABLE LITHIUM BATTERIES FOR MILITARY APPLICATIONS: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF INDUSTRIAL, MILITARY, AND SPACE SAFETY DOCUMENTS
abstract: Rechargeable lithium batteries are used across diverse military platforms, where safety management must address not only battery design and testing but also operational conditions, handling, incident response, and end - of - use management. This study conducted a structured comparative document analysis of 14 industrial, military, space, and operational safety documents to develop an integrated lifecycle safety management and assurance framework for military battery applications. title: On the Distribution of Spatial Polarization Indices
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper develops a statistical framework for inference on recently developed spatial polarization indices and clarifies their relationship to spatial inequality and dependence. abstract: This paper presents a case study of the entrepreneur and landowner Anton Kajfež and his successors, owners of one of the largest companies in Kočevje and Lower Carniola before World War I and during the interwar period. The company focused primarily on the timber and wine trade and became a significant shareholder in many regional companies and banks. title: Extreme drought stress diminished soil carbon sequestration and restructured microbial communities at the Dajiuhu subalpine peatland, Central China
abstract: Peatlands store approximately 30% of global terrestrial soil carbon, yet how subalpine peatlands respond to extreme drought remains poorly understood. title: Educating for a climate-changed future in India: diagnosing a mandate-without-mechanism condition
abstract: India’s constitutional provisions, Supreme Court directives, and National Curriculum Framework make its formal commitment to climate change education unusually explicit, yet classroom implementation remains uneven. This article combines analysis of India’s multilevel policy architecture with a structured review of 72 empirical studies published from 2007 to 2026. abstract: Background: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and post-EIA monitoring generate substantial biodiversity information through ecological surveys conducted before, during and after development projects. In the Republic of Korea, these records have accumulated in individual assessment reports, but their reuse has been limited because occurrence information is dispersed across documents and is not generally available in a structured format. title: From Facebook to political actions: nationalism, patriotism, and participation in Vietnam’s digital sphere
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between three types of social media use and four dimensions of political participation on Facebook. abstract: Blue supergiants are crucial to understanding the evolution of massive stars. However, their formation, mass loss, and pulsational properties remain poorly understood. Although distinguishing between pre- and post-red supergiant (RSG) phases is challenging, stellar pulsations provide valuable constraints on their masses and evolutionary status. abstract: Cyanobacteria are emerging as multifunctional components of sustainable agroecosystems, with the potential to influence nutrient cycling, soil structure, plant-associated microbiomes, and crop responses to environmental stress. This review integrates current knowledge of the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these effects, emphasizing nitrogen fixation, nutrient mobilization, phytohormone biosynthesis, extracellular polymeric substances, biocontrol-related metabolites, and stress mitigation. title: The Active Archive: Haptic Reconstruction in Albertina Carri's Los Rubios (2003)
abstract: The fragility of memory beyond any specific context is a biological and universal bodily process. That is the initial reflection behind Albertina Carri’s 2003 Los Rubios, a film that, through its retelling of autobiographical events from the Argentinian Dirty War, breaks documentary conventions and maximises the audiovisual medium to portray an erased history. abstract: Popular discourses on the drivers of child trafficking and migration are dominated by notions of household poverty and economic hardship. abstract: Liquid smoke derived from lignocellulosic biomass has attracted increasing attention as a natural preservative due to its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties. abstract: Abstract Cosmopolitanism is most widely understood as a political position that, based on a shared status of citizens of the world ( kosmopolitês ), all human beings are equal. abstract: Abstract We investigate whether observers on rocky habitable-zone (HZ) planets in known multi-planet systems could recognise the apparent retrograde motion of neighbouring planets. abstract: La malnutrición es frecuente en niños críticamente enfermos y se asocia con mayor morbimortalidad, infecciones, ventilación mecánica prolongada y mayor estadía hospitalaria. abstract: BACKGROUND: Schistosomiasis is one of the most prevalent neglected tropical diseases in sub-Saharan Africa, causing substantial morbidity and millions of disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Although the WHO aims to eliminate schistosomiasis as a public health problem in several countries by 2030, current epidemiological data on schistosomiasis in Zambia are insufficient to adequately characterize transmission patterns, identify priority intervention areas, and inform the planning and evaluation of control programmes. title: From Tito's Yugoslavia to the Bolivarian republic: A history of diplomatic, economic, military, and non-aligned-movement-mediated relations between Serbia and Venezuela (1950- 2026)
abstract: Serbia and Venezuela maintain one of the oldest formally established relationships between Southeast Europe and Latin America — dating, by the Serbian foreign ministry's own record, to 13 April 1882 — yet no dedicated peer-reviewed study of the dyad exists in any lan- guage, a gap this review both documents and begins to fill (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, 2026; Simić, 2024). title: From the Authoritarian Playbook: Academic Freedom and the Politics of Self-Censorship in Florida
abstract: Between 2021 and 2023, the State of Florida enacted numerous bills and took administrative actions interfering with university autonomy and academic freedom amid a combative political discourse vilifying universities as too “woke.” Defenders of these interventions have argued that academic teaching and research content have not been censored. title: Ferroptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms, tumour microenvironment, therapeutic resistance, and clinical translation
abstract: Ferroptosis is a distinct form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and oxidative membrane damage, and it differs fundamentally from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in its molecular mechanisms and execution pathways. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis plays a pivotal role in cancer biology by regulating tumour initiation, progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). title: Singing Homer : Modern Greek songs, digital literacy, and the experiential reception of the epics in secondary education
abstract: Abstract This article reports on Singing Homer , a two-year cultural project (2021–2023) in a Greek lower-secondary school that engaged students with the Iliad and the Odyssey through modern Greek songs. The project addressed persistent challenges in teaching Homer – linguistic difficulty, cultural distance, and questions of curricular relevance – by introducing music as a medium of reception and reinterpretation, through which students connected modern musical narratives with Homeric figures and themes. abstract: Abstract Why do some regions achieve higher levels of economic development while others do not? This paper introduces the Agglomeration-Clustering-Knowledge Spillovers (AC-KS) model, a conceptual framework for better understanding the nature of such differences. We argue that the missing piece of this puzzle is the process by which localized anchors ignite dynamic triangular forces between agglomeration, clustering, and knowledge spillovers, setting in motion a life cycle of first- and second-generation knowledge spillover effects. title: "Aragwadhadi Avaleha as a Virechaka Yoga: a Comprehensive Review"
abstract: Virechana Karma (therapeutic purgation) represents one of the principal bio-purification procedures (Panchakarma) in Ayurvedic medicine, specifically designed to eliminate vitiated Pitta dosha and associated morbid substances through the anal route.Aragwadhadi Avaleha, a classical Ayurvedic formulation documented in the Charaka Samhita Kalpa Sthana, stands as a significant Virechaka Yoga (purgative preparation) that combines three potent ingredients: Aragwadha (Cassia fistula Linn.), Trivrut (Operculina turpethum Linn.), and Guda (jaggery).This comprehensive review aims to systematically analy

title: Comparative physicochemical and mineral profiling of multifloral honeys from Apis mellifera in Himachal Pradesh, India: implications for export and GI tagging
abstract: This study examined the physicochemical, mineral, and bacterial profiles of multifloral honeys from Apis mellifera L. collected from different agro-climatic zones of Himachal Pradesh, India. Of the total honey samples, 26 were identified as multifloral based on melissopalynological analysis. title: Combined effects of board and audit committee characteristics on earnings management in listed manufacturing firms
abstract: The credibility of financial reporting may be undermined when managers use accounting discretion to alter reported earnings, with possible consequences for investors’ confidence. This study investigates the individual and joint relationships between board and audit committee attributes and earnings management for 49 manufacturing companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) from 2012 to 2024. title: Estudio de factibilidad para la implementación de un Disney Caribe en Punta Cana, República Dominicana
abstract: Este artículo analiza la viabilidad de establecer un parque temático de Disney en Punta Cana, bajo el concepto de “Disney Caribe”. A través de un enfoque cualitativo con revisión documental y análisis contextual, se exploran los factores económicos, sociales, turísticos y medioambientales que influyen en la ejecución del proyecto. El estudio considera la infraestructura disponible en la región, el crecimiento del turismo, el posicionamiento internacional de la marca Disney, y las condiciones para la inversión extranjera en República Dominicana. title: Azolla as an Extra Supplement to Maintain Milk Quantity of Dairy Cows During Winter
abstract: The climate of Koraput district in Odisha supports the growth of different types of green plants, with moderate temperatures, good rainfall, and varied landforms. Azolla pinnata, a small water fern that grows well between 20°C and 30°C, is easily found in this area and can be used as a low-cost protein source for dairy animals. During the winter season (November to February), the lower temperatures usually reduce how much cows eat and graze, which can lead to a drop in milk production and financial difficulties for small farmers. title: Service Shitshows Delivery Prevention: Live-Action Role-Playing (LARP) Bad Service
abstract: Frontline service workers and/or their supervisors delivering clearly inaccurate, bad, and/or unlawful service to customers or other “persons of interest” (POI) that causally precedes negative outcomes is one category of shitshow service-failure performance. The study presents both case studies and findings from national data showing that shitshow service enactments by performing professional public servants (PPSs) occur daily and more frequently in the U.S. than in other economically developed nations. title: The British general strike of 1926 in its global and temporal contexts
abstract: Historians routinely put the 1926 British General Strike into a British historical context stretching back to the First World War and before. More rarely historians look forward to the consequences of the Strike and to how it has been remembered. This article puts the British Strike into an international context and considers its consequences and the memory of it into the twenty-first century. title: EXPORT PROCESSING ZONES IN NIGERIA: PERSPECTIVES AND CHALLENGES
abstract: An Export Processing Zone also known as Free Trade Zone is a designated geographical area established by a government for businesses to operate. Several of such zones are usually established in different parts of a country. Mostly, the businesses that operate in the zones are private sector driven and are mainly aimed to promote export-oriented industrialization, facilitate technology transfer and attract foreign direct investments. journal: Journal of Jurisprudence, International Law and Contemporary Legal Issues

title: Islamic entrepreneurship opportunities in Lamongan Regency: Integrating local economic potential, business-enabling conditions, and business performance
abstract: The agricultural, fisheries, trade, and manufacturing sectors make Lamongan Regency a relevant setting for examining Islamic entrepreneurship opportunities. This study aims to map these opportunities by connecting the regional economic structure, business-enabling conditions, and evidence of practices related to Sharia principles. abstract: This study seeks to analyze how the role of sarong Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) is done to encourage economic growth in the area in Gresik City. Besides being economic units that create employment and income, Sarong MSMEs also play a role in improving women empowerment, community involvement and maintain local cultural identity. title: Anatomical characterization of Dalbergia ruddae and its analysis as tonewood
abstract: Dalbergia ruddae wood is highly valued in Mexico for the manufacture of musical instruments. However, the lack of information on its anatomical structure makes its identification difficult. The identification of Dalbergia woods is highly complex due to the similarity between species. Some Dalbergia species are in danger of extinction. title: Asking Questions Aloud: A Case for Interrogative Transmission
abstract: Abstract I argue that questions can be transmitted through asking just as beliefs are transmitted through testimony. Just as we rely on testifiers to assert only when their epistemic position is good enough, so (I argue) we rely on queriers to ask questions only if they are in a position to know that the question is sound, which guarantees that the asked question has an answer. title: High prevalence and diversity of mesophilic bacteria detected in pre-enrichment raw milk from Ecuador using two multiplex TaqMan qPCR assays
abstract: The consumption of raw cow’s milk remains common and traditional in Ecuador, especially due to its sale in informal markets, despite its recognized potential to act as a vehicle for multiple zoonotic pathogens and chemical substances. title: Pharmacokinetic diversity of baloxavir marboxil across rare avian species
abstract: High pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) poses a serious threat to captive rare birds. Because effective countermeasures are limited, the use of human antiviral drugs to treat HPAIV infections in captive rare birds has been considered. Although the human antiviral drug, baloxavir marboxil (BXM), is not approved for the treatment of influenza virus infection in birds, previous studies demonstrated the antiviral efficacy of BXM in experimental avian models. abstract: Abstract. Quantifying long-term soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics in croplands is critical to evaluate their climate mitigation potential. We assessed SOC stock changes over 21 years at the BE-Lon ICOS cropland (Belgium) by comparing decadal soil inventories, RothC model simulations, and eddy covariance (EC) flux measurements, supported by comprehensive uncertainty propagation. title: Shared household environment structures the gut microbiota in a large family cohort with central areolar choroidal dystrophy
abstract: Central areolar choroidal dystrophy (CACD) is a rare monogenic hereditary retinal dystrophy characterised by progressive retinal pigment epithelium and choriocapillaris atrophy, photoreceptor loss, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiota can modulate systemic inflammatory responses and may influence ocular health through the gut-eye axis. abstract: Abstract Biological sulfate reduction combined with chemical precipitation of metal sulfides is an good alternative to mitigate environmental impacts of acid mine drainage (AMD) and to recover base metals. This process requires a consistent supply of electron donors, and this study investigated the use of Brewery Spent Grain (BSG) as a slow-release electron donor (SRED) to sustain sulfate reduction and enhance metal sulfide precipitation as settling particles. title: Wealth Creation and Entrepreneurial Performance of Pig Farmers in South-South, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the influence of respective factors of wealth creation on designated measures of entrepreneurial performance of pig farmers in South-South, Nigeria. Specifically, it established a nexus between financial capital and market share; human capital and turnover; social capital and customer satisfaction; and intellectual capital and customer loyalty; respectively. abstract: Introduction. Besides being a place for lifting weights, the gym is an interesting environment to explore how certain individuals performing routine activities engage with information. This paper investigated Cordilleran gym users’ interaction with information sources in pursuit of their fitness goals. Method. abstract: Digital transformation is a vital part of a state’s political agenda, aiming not only to accelerate economic growth and promote sustainable social development but also to change the image of a state in the context of soft power enhancement. In this regard, a notable example of governmental intention to reinforce its soft power is Japan. abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). abstract: Retrofitting homes in the United Kingdom is a critical component of achieving the country's net-zero carbon emissions target by 2050 and a contribution to climate change mitigation. This is particularly pressing as the country is home to some of the least energy-efficient housing in Europe. Retrofitting measures are scarcely adopted in the private rented sector that faces greater challenges than social or owner-occupied housing. abstract: The article conducts an interpretative review of contemporary scientific literature (2000–2026) to analyse the environmental aspects of conventional funeral practices and introduces sustainable burial cemetery models such as green cemetery and conservation burial grounds. abstract: Global dry land agricultural systems face intensifying structural and climatic pressures, demanding innovative soil management paradigms to sustain crop productivity and preserve scarce hydrological and nutritional resources. Conventional tillage (CT) practices, characterized by intensive mechanical soil inversion, accelerate the oxidation of soil organic matter, disrupt macro-pore continuity, and generate high subsoil bulk density that limits water permeability and exacerbates terminal drought vulnerability. abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. title: Deficit Irrigation Affects Tuber Mineral Composition of Four Potato Genotypes
abstract: Abstract Deficit irrigation (DI) is a sustainable approach to optimize water use while maintaining yield and quality of potato tubers, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions like the Mediterranean. This study assessed the impact of DI on the macro- (Ca, K, P, N, Mg) and micromineral (Cu, Fe, Mn, Na, Zn) element composition of four ‘early’ potato genotypes (G) across two growing seasons (S) in southern Italy. abstract: As urban temperatures rise from climate change, the burden of heat exposure is likely to be unequally distributed across neighborhoods. Prior research shows that heat varies based on neighborhood racial/ethnic composition, with people of color experiencing higher temperatures relative to Whites. Yet, previous studies of neighborhood racial/ethnic diversity and heat have been largely aspatial. abstract: This study investigates the complex, interconnected relationships between green foreign direct investment (FDI), governance quality, and infrastructure development in three major emerging African economies, such as South Africa, Egypt, and Nigeria from 2008 to 2023. abstract: Small exoplanets on close-in orbits are exposed to high levels of stellar irradiation, which can effectively remove low-mass primordial H/He envelopes through atmospheric escape. abstract: The Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-based Life-course and Environmental Research (SIMPLER) is a national research infrastructure that provides longitudinal data and biological samples to investigate how dietary, lifestyle, environmental, and genetic factors influence health and disease across the life course. SIMPLER integrates two population-based prospective cohorts: the Swedish Mammography Cohort and the Cohort of Swedish Men. abstract: This study addresses the design and simulation of a low-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance spectrometer prototype based on a modular Halbach array of permanent magnets. The objective was to develop a low-cost system with high magnetic-field homogeneity for teaching and research purposes at the Costa Rica Institute of Technology. abstract: This At-Issue examines the life and times of Floribert Bwana Chui, a young Catholic customs officer from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) who was killed for refusing to accept a bribe and allow the smuggling of spoilt foodstuff. Later beatified as a martyr by the Catholic Church—having fulfilled the church’s stipulations thereof—few, if any, have considered his beatification as something more than a notable spiritual event: as a symbolically strategic move by the Catholic Church. Using a unique dataset that provides complete histories of actual transactions in the real estate market, this study documents a seller‐buyer valuation gap consistent with an endowment effect among real estate owners, regardless of gender or experience. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how the qualification of assurors in sustainability and environmental reporting assurance (SERA) is constructed and why it remains fiercely contested. abstract: The ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) is the major machinery for intracellular protein degradation, playing an indispensable role in maintaining proteostasis across all tissues. abstract: ZnO nanorods (ZnO NRs) are some of the most significant one-dimensional oxide nanostructures because they have a broad direct band gap, a high exciton binding energy, are chemically stable, have a massive surface area, and are piezoelectric. abstract: Reconstruction of 3D structures using under-ice AUV video footage has been inaccurate, although it is not certain whether this is due to shortcomings in the methods or an inherent deficiency of the capture system. We test four different models for reconstruction on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video (Icefin, Kamb Ice Stream): classical feature matching SfM, differentiable photometric splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model. All four fail, each in a distinct way: near-total registration yielding almost no structure, geometrically broken output despi

title: Intrinsic Vectorial Gradiometry via Quantum Control of a Spin-based Sensor
The grounded spirituality of mathematics
abstract: We propose that mathematics is done largely as a means of both coping with and celebrating our physicality in the natural world. Inspired by David Abram's "Becoming Animal", we suggest that -- in opposition to the popular image of an otherworldy Platonic realm-- the spiritual component of doing mathematics is grounded on and in the Earth. We explore this as a means of questioning the widespread adoption of AI in the workflows of research mathematics.

title: VulnBump: A Benchmark for Fixing Vulnerable Dependencies in Real Projects While Keeping the Build and Tests Green
abstract: Software composition analysis (SCA) tools report far more vulnerable dependencies than teams fix: in Snyk Open Source production data, 94% of vulnerability findings have a known fixed version, yet only about 10% are resolved. Agentic coding tools could close this gap, but no benchmark evaluates them on vulnerability-driven upgrades in real, runnable projects across ecosystems, verified independently of the agent. We present VulnBump: 307 upgrade tasks covering 2,066 fixable vulnerabilities in 43 repositories across six package managers, matched to Snyk Open Source production vulnerability dist

title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. title: The Missile and the Toll: Two-Way Flow Through the Strait of Hormuz
abstract: Tolls for safe passage and attacks on shipping are usually treated as mutually exclusive: either ships pay or attacks happen. We argue they are complementary. In a Stackelberg escalation game for the Strait of Hormuz, the enforcer chooses an attack intensity and a toll schedule; the response is to pay, cross exposed, wait, reroute, or exit. Attacks create the willingness to pay; tolls harvest it. The model predicts asymmetry across trade forms: a toll where the cargo owner can pay and the vessel owner will consent, and none where either fails. title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate
abstract: Descriptions of how people use AI are becoming training data for the next generation of models. We ask whether what a model reads about its users changes how it treats people. Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning, we train Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora built from the same 1,625 real-world usage scenarios. The corpora differ only in the predominant motive they attribute to users of AI chatbots: helping others (prosocial), exploiting others (antisocial), legitimate self-advancement, or task completion. Finetuning shifts the models' stated beliefs about users, how true those belief

title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring
abstract: Remote wildlife monitoring increasingly depends on high-fidelity cameras and sensors deployed far from grid power and terrestrial networks. Low Earth orbit satellite links can provide connectivity in these settings, but their high power draw and variable bandwidth, combined with intermittent on-site solar harvesting, make continuous backhaul infeasible. Current systems therefore filter at the edge, with motion triggers that waste limited energy and bandwidth on environmental artifacts, or fixed vision models that cannot follow evolving expert objectives. We present \textsc{ATLAS}, an expert-gu

title: The Curse of Knowledge in Role-Playing Language Models
abstract: Role-playing language models speak as characters in games and agent simulations, where the system records what each character can hear, see and understand. We test whether characters respect these boundaries in 480 scenes, each with a counterfactual twin that changes only the hidden fact, so mentions of the twin's fact measure guessing. Across 11 open-weight models, characters use content from speech they cannot understand or hear at 67 and 72 percentage points (pp) above this baseline, although most models correctly state what the character perceives. title: ABench: Adversarily Benchmarking Large Language Models across Taxonomized Values
abstract: Ensuring the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) with diverse cultural values is critical for their safe global deployment. However, existing alignment benchmarks are predominantly English-centric or confined to simple discriminative tasks. Moreover, they often fail to effectively evaluate model robustness against complex, adversarial inductions within specific cultural contexts. To address these limitations, we propose ABench, a fine-grained, handcrafted benchmark specifically tailored to taxonomized values in Chinese. title: Detection and Statistics of large-scale Sector Boundary Crossings in the Solar Wind: The SBCross Catalog
abstract: Heliospheric sector boundary crossings (SBCs), composed of the Heliospheric Current Sheet (HCS), Heliospheric Plasma Sheet (HPS), and surrounding plasma halo, represent fundamental structures in the solar wind that influence interplanetary dynamics and space weather. We present the \textsc{SBCross} catalog, an automated, publicly available database containing 1,076 SBC events derived from in-situ observations spanning more than 30 years (1995--2026), covering Solar Cycles 23 and 24 alongside the rising and maximum phases of Solar Cycle 25. By combining interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) and 2

title: Sociotechnical Aspects of Tor Relay Rejection
abstract: In 2019, the Tor Project enforced an end-of-life (EoL) policy for Tor versions, leading to the rejection of outdated relays, amounting to a notable fraction of consensus weight. While this policy aids network maintenance, reduces backporting efforts, and shortens vulnerability exposure, its sociotechnical implications remain unstudied.

title: Action-Quantized Scar Multiplets and Dissipative Cat States from Fractal Period-Locking in the Open Quantum Baker Map
abstract: We open the quantum baker map with a position window of width $w$ and center $q_c$. Classical pruning tiles the $(q_c,w)$ plane into diamonds where the $T$ leading resonances form root-of-unity multiplets. At $w=1/2$ one periodic orbit survives for almost every $q_c$, and the multiplets are quantized without free parameters: their modulus $2^{-1/2}$ saturates the pressure bound and their phase is the orbit action. They form cycling multicomponent cat states, and the opening becomes one mid-circuit measurement, enabling spectroscopy with $\sim10^2$ shots on quantum processors.

title: Which Knowledge Should LLMs Trust? Uncovering a Generalizable Steering Direction Across Knowledge Conflicts
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently encounter conflicts between internal parametric knowledge and external contextual knowledge, yet the mechanisms governing this selection remain unclear. We show that the choice between context and parametric knowledge is linearly represented and can be controlled along a single direction in the model's residual stream. We first demonstrate that this direction generalizes across factual-conflict settings, including context formats, knowledge categories, and datasets, while consistently shifting behavior between parametric and contextual answers. title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
abstract: Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution. We present RiseHarness, a framework for iteratively improving agent harnesses with model weights fixed. It focuses on flipping tasks with both successful and failed runs under the same configuration, using successful runs as references for failure analysis. RiseHarness combines agent trajectories with internal harness traces from a runtime monitor to examine how model actions interact with

title: SteerSearch: Interactive Search Reasoning with Mid-Response Steering
abstract: Search-augmented language models increasingly serve as long-horizon research agents, yet most open training methods assume a fixed user goal throughout search. We study mid-response steering, where users redirect a model during ongoing reasoning or retrieval. We identify answer-target anchoring, a failure mode in which fixed-query search agents retrieve evidence for the updated request but still answer an earlier question. We introduce SteerSearch, an RL framework that trains on interactive search trajectories with injected interventions to enable context-preserving target reassignment, and St

title: Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models increasingly use multi-step search to solve knowledge-intensive tasks, yet existing systems typically expose retrieval through fixed pipelines or collections of atomic tools. We introduce Retrieval Program Learning (RPL), a programmable search framework that allows a policy to compose search primitives into executable programs with local state and control flow. This enables adaptive search that can retrieve broadly, process intermediate results, and selectively construct model context without tying retrieval breadth to context consumption. title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
abstract: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. However, prior work largely treats PI as a fixed design choice, leaving the effects of its content and construction poorly understood. This challenge is particularly important in multi-turn agentic settings, where trajectories contain actions, observations, and reasoning that can be transformed into PI in many ways. We systematically evaluate 16 PI configurations across three multi-turn agentic benchmarks and three student models that vary in scale

title: A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation
abstract: Ionizing radiation produces correlated errors in superconducting qubits, posing some challenges to quantum error correction. In addition, it causes background events in other superconducting cryogenic devices, such as kinetic inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Cosmic muons are a component of this background that can only be partly shielded against at ground level, but can be tagged by an independent detector inside the cryostat, so that the affected data can be vetoed, or the muon tags incorporated into error correction. title: A duality principle for the neighbourhood of manifolds and applications to counting rational points near curves
abstract: In this paper, we establish a duality principle relating the count of rationals near a manifold to a sparse counting problem for the dual. As applications, we give a short, self-contained proof of sharp bounds for planar curves under minimal regularity conditions and similarly, sharp upper bounds for non- degenerate space curves, again under minimal curvature conditions. title: Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Imagination
abstract: Predicting cost in a multi-agent world model moves most constrained policy updates into imagination: the stronger model-free baseline needs $10$ to $20$ times CA-MAMBA's interactions on the median SMAC configuration, and CA-MAMBA earns $2.8$ to $12$ times the baselines' MAMuJoCo reward at equal budget. In controlled tests on one task per benchmark, pricing the model's cost advantages at parity more than halves a cost-blind learner's cost and meets a tight continuous-control limit the learned multiplier misses, suggesting the model's cost estimates are not the bottleneck.

title: A design concept for the High Resolution Imager on the Habitable Worlds Observatory
abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will be NASA's next flagship astrophysics mission, designed to search for signs of life on planets around nearby stars and conduct transformational science across astrophysics. Its High Resolution Imager (HRI) is not only the observatory's main imaging camera, but also provides grism spectroscopy and sub-microarcsecond astrometry, as well as the observatory's fine guidance, wavefront sensing and pupil imaging. title: ENSO-Flavor Differences in Indonesian Marine Heatwaves: Satellite SST, Physical Covariates, and Coral Habitat Suitability
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the Indonesian Seas develop within a long-term rise in sea surface temperature and strong interannual climate variability. We analyze daily NOAA Optimum Interpolation Sea Surface Temperature version 2.1 for 1982–2022 and compare five Eastern-Pacific (EP) with five Central-Pacific (CP) El Niño events. MHWs are detected against a fixed 1982–2011 baseline, and each event is represented by the common 1 July–30 June window spanning its developing and decaying phases. title: Phenology of spring phytoplankton bloom in the marine waters around Kamchatka
abstract: Timing and other phenological parameters of the spring phytoplankton bloom in the waters around Kamchatka are determined on long-term satellite-derived data for chlorophyll a concentration obtained in 1998–2024. Three methods of the timing determining are compared, as the biomass threshold, the cumulative biomass threshold, and the maximum biomass growth rate; finally, a modified threshold method is proposed, more suitable for the study area. title: Microbial deamination of peptides and proteins as a source of persistent marine dissolved organic matter
abstract: Abstract Refractory dissolved organic nitrogen is a major component of the ocean's nitrogen pool, yet the mechanisms producing and preserving it remain poorly understood. Here, we show that deaminated peptides (DAPs), derived from microbial processing of proteinaceous material, are ubiquitous across oxygenated marine environments—from productive coastal waters to the oligotrophic ocean—and persist from surface to bathypelagic depths. Improved recovery of sub-ice shelf bathymetry from gravity data using an isostatic correction: a case study from the Dotson and Crosson ice shelves, West Antarctica
abstract: Abstract. Bathymetry beneath ice shelves is challenging to observe yet is vitally important for modelling how ice sheets will evolve into the future. An alternative to direct observation of bathymetry is to invert airborne gravity data for the bathymetric signal. Appropriate gravity data can be collected via remote sensing above the ice shelf and be used to provide an initial estimate of sub-ice-shelf bathymetry, typically at wavelengths of ~5 km and above. title: Species-specific phenological indicators reveal topographic–climatic associations with evergreen-tree phenology in subtropical hilly regions
abstract: Evergreen-tree phenology is an important ecological indicator of forest responses to climate change and local environmental heterogeneity. In subtropical hilly regions, frequent cloudy and rainy conditions, complex terrain, and weak seasonal greenness signals hinder species-level phenological retrieval and interpretation. Here, we evaluated the ecological indicator value of the start of season (SOS), end of season (EOS), and length of season (LOS) for eight representative evergreen tree species in Xiamen, Fujian Province, China. Development of a Towing System Design Program Based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual
abstract: Marine towing is required for transporting ships and floating structures and for salvage operations of damaged vessels. Safe towing operations require the estimation of towing resistance, selection of an appropriate tug and towing equipment, and verification of the towing system. However, the design procedure based on the U.S. Navy Towing Manual involves repeated manual calculations using tables, curves, and empirical criteria, which can be time-consuming and prone to reading errors. title: Feasibility of Wearable Heart Rate Variability Monitoring During a Military Closed-Circuit Rebreather Dive: An Exploratory Case Report
abstract: Background: Heart rate variability (HRV) monitoring during real-world closed-circuit rebreather (CCR) diving remains methodologically challenging. This exploratory case report describes phase-related HRV variations obtained from a wearable device during a military CCR dive. Methods: A trained male military diver underwent continuous monitoring with a RootiRx® single-lead wearable device placed in a custom waterproof enclosure. Three consecutive 20 min segments were analyzed: pre-dive, CCR dive, and immediate post-dive. The post-dive segment was not acquired under standardized resting condition
journal: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology

title: Arbitraje de emergencia: bases teóricas y diseño procedimental en los reglamentos arbitrales peruanos
abstract: Emergency arbitration is consolidated in international commercial arbitration practice. In the Peruvian legal system, given the absence of comprehensive legislative development, arbitral institutions have driven the development of this mechanism through special provisions in their rules. This article analyzes its theoretical foundations and procedural framework based on a representative sample of Peruvian institutional arbitration rules. title: A new piece in the puzzle: The palaeoecological significance of bryozoans over 7000 years in Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan)
abstract: ABSTRACT Submarine caves are cryptic, climatically sensitive habitats with long‐term ecological dynamics that are poorly understood. We present the first palaeoecological analysis of bryozoans from Daidokutsu Cave (Okinawa, Japan), based on a sediment core spanning approximately the last 7000 years. title: Drought Trends in Türkiye Under Global Warming Conditions
abstract: The methods used in monitoring the increasing drought are vitally significant. In order to determine and monitor drought, many scientific studies have been carried out in our country, especially using the standardized precipitation index (SPI). However, due to increasing temperatures and evaporation, there is a need for studies showing the spatio-temporal change of drought at the country scale according to the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI), which also takes evaporation into account. title: Rainfall Trends in Northern Algeria (1901–2024): Spatial Heterogeneity, Temporal Asynchrony, and Implications for Cereal Production
abstract: Abstract Northern Algeria is a transitional zone between the Mediterranean and the Sahara, yet the spatiotemporal structure of its long-term precipitation trends remains poorly studied. This study analyses 124 years of monthly precipitation data (1901-2024) extracted from the CRU-TS4.09 gridded dataset (0.5°×0.5°) at 50 stations distributed across the region. title: Generalized parton distributions of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model: Sum over all quark states at nonzero skewness and momentum transfer
abstract: We compute the combinations $E_M=H^{u+d}+E^{u+d}$ and $H_E=H^{u-d}+tE^{u-d}/(4M_N^2)$ of unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model at nonzero skewness $ξ$ and nonzero momentum transfer $t$. title: Super Warm Early Eocene Simulations With HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL
abstract: Abstract The early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO; 53.3–49.1 million years ago) represents the period of greatest sustained warmth in the Cenozoic (last 66 million years), with proxy‐data indicating global‐mean temperatures 10–16°C above preindustrial and atmospheric concentrations of 1,200–2,500 ppmv. This extreme greenhouse climate provides insights into Earth's climate sensitivity and feedback mechanisms and offers a stress‐test for evaluating climate models under vastly different boundary conditions. Here we present the first application of the HadGEM3‐GC31‐LL model to the super‐warm EECO.

title: Isobaric Crystallization of Aqueous Magnesium Chloride Solutions at Icy Moon Conditions
abstract: Abstract Subsurface oceans inside icy moons are expected to contain dissolved salts whose crystallization controls the mineralogy of their hydrospheres and potentially their surfaces. Here, we use in situ neutron diffraction to investigate the isobaric crystallization of a nearly saturated MgCl2/D2O solution between ambient pressure and 0.4 GPa. title: Gen-EBM: An energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that strongly depend on the underlying climate feedbacks. We present the Geneva energy balance model (Gen-EBM), a new 1D latitudinal EBM designed for the rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. title: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse
abstract: Abstract Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes undergo gravothermal evolution whose late-time behaviour is central to predictions for dense substructure and black-hole seed formation. We revisit the calibration of this evolution using a new spherical Direct Simulation Monte Carlo code, SphDSMC, which follows spherically symmetric SIDM systems without force softening and to substantially higher central densities than standard N-body simulations. title: Educating character, difference and the “great questions” curriculum
abstract: Purpose This article examines difference in interdisciplinary character education programs in higher, secondary and elementary education. Such successful “classical education” curricula focus on “Great Books” or “classics,” but their canon-based approaches have drawn criticism for difficulties with incorporating difference. The innovative, inquiry-driven “Great Questions” curriculum of Villanova University's Humanities major represents a “classical” approach that remains grounded within its formative Augustinian tradition while reflectively opening to noncanonical texts. title: Sai số nội suy hình học và khoảng cách tuyến trong khảo sát địa hình đáy
abstract: Khảo sát địa hình đáy là cơ sở quan trọng cho thiết kế và khai thác các công trình hàng hải. Tuy nhiên, độ chính xác của mô hình địa hình đáy không chỉ phụ thuộc vào sai số đo tại điểm mà còn chịu ảnh hưởng của sai số nội suy giữa các tuyến khảo sát, trong khi mối quan hệ này chưa được lượng hóa đầy đủ. title: Campo de Dalías and the “Almeria miracle”: a cautionary tale of the value of water in agriculture
abstract: Abstract Renowned for having one of the highest concentrations of greenhouses in the world, Campo de Dalías, located in the southeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in the southwest of the province of Almeria in Spain, offers a compelling case for understanding the evolution of how water has been valued and managed in agriculture. The region’s trajectory, from the discovery of groundwater in the 1940s, through its subsequent overexploitation, degradation, and eventual depletion, ultimately led to the adoption of water-efficient practices and the use of desalinated water for irrigation today. abstract: A recent study suggests that the precipitation records of the western Qaidam Basin during the middle Piacenzian warm period (mPWP, 3.264–3.025 Ma) are broadly consistent with those of the monsoon-influenced regions, and are highly sensitive to 20 kyr precessional cycles, implying that the East Asian summer monsoon (EASM) precipitation intensified and penetrated farther westward into the Asian interior during this warm interval. title: Reproduction and prevalence of Probopyrus pandalicola (Isopoda, Bopyridae) in Yucatán, southeastern Mexico
abstract: This study provides data on size at sexual maturity, fecundity, embryo size, brood loss, and prevalence of the isopod Probopyrus pandalicola, parasite of Palaemon mundusnovus, at Sisal, Yucatán, Mexico. title: Brief communication: Mass balance of glaciers in the Eastern Hindu Kush from 1979 to 2002 using KH-9 panoramic and SPOT-5 stereo imagery
abstract: Abstract. Glaciers exhibit region-specific mass loss patterns in response to ongoing climate change. In this study, we provide a geodetic mass balance assessment for glaciers within the Hindu Kush region spanning the period 1979–2002, utilizing KH-9 panoramic imagery and SPOT-5 stereo satellite imagery. Our analysis reveals a moderate mass loss of −0.13 ± 0.12 m w.e. a−1, a rate similar to post-2000 observations given their uncertainties. title: eDNA metabarcoding reveals invertebrate diversity in the blackwater pools of southeast Queensland peatlands
abstract: Despite harbouring a disproportionate diversity of rare and endemic species, the pyrophilic peatlands of southeast Queensland remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding their invertebrate communities. In the physically and chemically extreme blackwater pools, meiofaunal assemblages likely form critical trophic links but have never been described due to their small size and low public profile. abstract: Groundwater occurrence in Walajabad block, Tamil Nadu, is influenced by variations in geological formations and subsurface conditions, making detailed characterization important for groundwater exploration and management. This research explores the groundwater characteristics and subsurface resistivity patterns for this block. In this study, 110 vertical electrical sounding (VES) points were conducted using the Schlumberger electrode array to investigate the subsurface resistivity distribution and groundwater conditions. title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. abstract: Abstract. Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the most dominant precursor of ozone-depleting substances and the third most important anthropogenic greenhouse gas, with agriculture contributing the largest share of emissions (56 %). Over the past two decades, airborne in-situ measurements have become increasingly important for studying emission and transport of N2O in the atmosphere, also driven by the development of more precise and simultaneously faster Quantum Cascade Laser (QCL)-based spectrometers. title: 3D crustal seismic structure of southern mainland Portugal from combined local earthquake and active source tomography
abstract: Summary We present P- and S-wave seismic tomographic models for southern mainland Portugal, specifically for the region south of the 39° N parallel. These models were obtained using local seismicity and wide-angle refracted and reflected seismic profiles, considering a spatial resolution of approximately 10 km in latitude and longitude, and 3 km in depth, the highest spatial resolution so far compared to previous models of similar or broader regional scope. The aim is to improve the understanding of continental seismicity and to correlate seismic heterogeneities with crustal tectonic structure

title: Seasonal and Spatial Patterns in Water Quality and in Situ Responses of Daphnia Magna along River Kaduna, Nigeria
abstract: Variations in biochemical oxygen demand and dissolve oxygen affect aquatic organisms and have the potential to disrupt the ecological equilibrium of aquatic ecosystems. This study examined the effects of these environmental factors on the growth, reproduction and survival response of Daphnia magna at various sampling sites with differing levels of pollution in the River Kaduna, Nigeria, during both the dry and wet seasons. The physicochemical changes and the structure and dynamics of the D. magna community were monitored bi-monthly. In situ bioassays involving D. magna were conducted twice at

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Virgin and Recycled Polypropylene Kitchenware in the UK: Impacts of Domestic Recycling, International Supply Chains, and Consumer Use
abstract: This study evaluates the cradle-to-grave environmental performance of polypropylene (PP) kitchenware in the United Kingdom (UK), addressing critical gaps in understanding how material choices, global supply chains, domestic recycling, and consumer use-phase practices interact. Four scenarios were assessed using life cycle assessment (LCA) modelling: virgin PP (vPP) manufactured in China and Germany, recycled PP (rPP) produced in the UK, and a 50:50 vPP–rPP blend. Environmental impacts evaluated using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H) and IPCC 2021 GWP100 showed that under the modelled scenarios, UK

title: MONKI: a three-dimensional Monte Carlo simulator for transfer of polarised light in planetary atmospheres
abstract: Abstract. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool for characterising planetary atmospheres and surfaces. For the design and operation of spectro(polari)metric instrumentation, numerically simulated signals of the measured radiation are essential. Here we present MONKI (Monte Carlo KNMI), an efficient and accurate radiative transfer code written in Fortran, based on the Monte Carlo method. MONKI computes both total and polarised radiances reflected and transmitted by a planetary atmosphere, fully accounting for the polarisation of light in all orders of scattering. title: A dual role of precipitation amount and temperature determines precipitation isotopic trends in Southeast Alaska
abstract: Southeast Alaska is one of the wettest places in the world, with some locations within the region receiving upwards of 6 metres of precipitation annually. Given the region's abundant precipitation, it is important to understand the mechanisms controlling the hydrologic cycle to better constrain past and future trends in climate. Accomplishing this requires the evaluation of isotopes in precipitation, as this is key to untangling the many drivers of the water cycle. However, there has never been a precipitation isotope study conducted in Southeast Alaska, vastly limiting our understanding of th
journal: Isotopes in Environmental and Health Studies

title: In-flight receiver calibration of the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) by passive Earth observations
abstract: Abstract. Post-launch characterization of the receiver telescope of the laser altimeter is essential for achieving precise georeferenced planetary measurements and for radiometric calibration to passively measure surface reflectance. For the Ganymede Laser Altimeter (GALA) aboard the Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice), such in-flight calibration was originally planned during a lunar flyby but could not be performed due to an unexpected reboot of the instrument. Institute for Space Astrophysics and Planetology

title: Entanglement and apparent thermality in simulated black holes
abstract: We investigate the apparent thermality of Hawking radiation in the semi-classical limit of quantum black holes using the mean-field limit of a chiral spin-chain simulator, which models fermions propagating on a black hole space-time in the continuum. In this free-theory regime, no genuine thermalisation occurs. Nevertheless, we show that a bipartition across the event horizon yields a reduced density matrix whose mode occupations follow an apparent thermal Fermi-Dirac distribution. title: Integrating a global glacier model into local hydrological modeling: Impacts on melt contributions
abstract: Abstract. Snow and glacier meltwater are critical water resources for mountain regions, yet their accurate representation in hydrological models remains challenging. As climate change alters the timing and magnitude of melt contributions, accurate partitioning between snow and glacier sources becomes increasingly important. To address this challenge, this study couples the hydrological model HBV (as implemented in the Raven modeling framework) with the Global Glacier Evolution Model GloGEM and integrates a snow redistribution scheme for application across 14 glaciated headwater catchments in S
institutions: Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research
Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research

title: Flyway-scale migration phenology identifies mismatches between migration timing and European hunting regulations
abstract: The study of bird migration timing is pivotal for the identification of the onset of pre-breeding migration, when, according to the European regulatory framework, the hunting seasons should end following Article 7.4 of the EU Birds Directive. Member States may use different data sources, including citizen science platforms, to determine this onset. Here, we used data from eBird, a citizen science platform, to describe the timing of pre- and post-breeding migration of the Song Thrush (Turdus philomelos) across the Western Palearctic. For EU Member States, we compared the onset dates of pre-bree
institutions: Istituto Superiore per la Protezione e la Ricerca Ambientale
Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior

title: Metastable and Stable States in Covalent Organic Frameworks Controlled by Synthetic Selection Pressure
abstract: The synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has long followed a thermodynamics-driven approach, aiming to obtain highly ordered stable crystalline materials while overlooking metastable structures with unique dynamic characteristics. Inspired by the biological concept of "selection pressure," we propose that the harshness of synthetic conditions serves as a key selection pressure governing the final state of COFs. title: Early disaster response to extreme heat in modern Shanghai, 1873–1949: limited preparedness and unequal protection
abstract: As extreme heat has become one of the most deadly climate risks in cities today, a fundamental question is rarely asked: where does a city’s heat-disaster response capacity actually come from? Taking Shanghai from 1873 to 1949 as a case study, this study reconstructs summer extreme heat events by integrating Xujiahui Observatory temperature observations with modern newspapers and municipal archives. Focusing on three representative years (1894, 1934, and 1942), this study compares how heat shocks were transformed into social impacts and governance responses under different institutional contex

title: Chromium Removal from Wastewater Using Phosphorylated Fish Bone Char
abstract: Hexavalent chromium is a toxic and highly leachable contaminant associated with several environmental hazards. A phosphoric acid-functionalized fish bone char has been synthesized by chemical impregnation and researched for the treatment of hexavalent chromium from water. The surface area of the synthesized material is found to be 19.79 m2/g by nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherm having pore volume and diameter of 0.049 cm3/g and 13.7–14.9 nm, respectively. journal: American Journal of Pure and Applied Biosciences

title: Análise integrada do comportamento não estacionário de fenómenos hidrológicos extremos: caso de estudo da bacia hidrográfica do rio Muriaé (sudeste do Brasil)
abstract: O estudo analisou o comportamento não estacionário de eventos hidrológicos extremos na bacia do rio Muriaé (8,126 km2, sudeste do Brasil), uma região propensa a inundações fluviais. Foi utilizada uma metodologia que combina a técnica das séries de picos acima de um limiar, POT (do inglês Peaks Over Threshold), e a estimativa da taxa de ocorrência por Kernel (KORE). Comparativamente à série de máximos anuais, a POT permite selecionar múltiplos eventos extremos por ano, resultando em amostras com maior número de elementos, logo, mais representativas do fenómeno em estudo. title: Rotation Age Results of Low Planting Density Effects in Loblolly Pine (Pinus taeda L.)
abstract: Abstract Planting density is the most important management decision made by a forester when establishing a loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L.) plantation. Traditionally, planting densities were often chosen with the assumption that at least one mid-rotation thinning operation would provide intermediate cash flow(s) while also accelerating the growth of residual trees to more quickly provide solid wood products at future thinnings and final harvest. Recently, closures of pulpwood processing facilities throughout the southeastern USA have led to growers considering low planting density, no-thin mana

title: Free-surface effects on the energy-harvesting performance of a fully passive flapping foil
abstract: Fully passive flapping-foil energy harvesters offer structural simplicity and require no external actuation, but their self-excited motion and power extraction may be strongly affected by a deformable free surface during near-surface operation. This study aims to quantify how submergence depth affects energy-harvesting efficiency and to elucidate the associated changes in free-surface deformation, vortex evolution, load–motion phase coordination, and foil-surface pressure fluctuations. To this end, a two-dimensional numerical investigation is conducted on a fully passive NACA0015 flapping foil
journal: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development

title: VPP-Driven Sail and Foil Trim Optimization for the Olympic NACRA 17 Foiling Catamaran
abstract: Abstract The Nacra-17 is the current Olympic catamaran sailed in the Olympic Games since 2016 by a mixed crew. Over the years, the boat has undergone some changes. The initial design of the boat featured a set of appendages that only rarely allowed the boat to foil. Today, Nacra-17 features semi-L-shaped daggerboards and T-rudders, all of them independently trimmable. This allows the boat to foil at wind speeds of 9 kn and below on an upwind tack and even earlier on a downwind tack. title: Fine-scale spatial variability of winter CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes in Arctic tundra derived from snowpack gradient measurements
abstract: Abstract. Winter carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) fluxes from soils under seasonal snowpacks make non-negligible, yet poorly constrained contributions to annual carbon budgets across Arctic regions. Quantifying these fluxes and their spatial variance will better constrain uncertainties in simulations of winter carbon fluxes from terrestrial biosphere models. We address this gap by measuring and identifying patterns and spatial variability in CO2 and CH4 soil-atmosphere fluxes through late winter snowpacks at an upland tundra site in the western Canadian Arctic. title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: ABSTRACT Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry – or ‘mountain’ – supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: An analytical model for rotors in confined flow across operating regimes
abstract: Rotors operating in confined flows, or blockage, are commonly encountered in wind and water tunnels, as well as in shallow or dense deployments of hydrokinetic turbines. Confinement induces a streamwise pressure gradient in the channel, modifying the rotor induction, thrust and power. To account for these effects, physics-based or empirical blockage corrections are used as a transfer function between the dynamics of an object operating in confined and unconfined settings. title: Flow Dynamics with Jet-induced Vortex Control in a Slotted Vertical-axis Wind Turbine
abstract: This study investigates the aerodynamic impact of passive blade slots on the unsteady flow dynamics of a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) operating at low tip speed ratios. A two-dimensional URANS-based numerical investigation using the k–ω SST turbulence model was performed to analyze the creation of slot-induced internal jets and their interaction with the surrounding flow field. title: Analysis of a Textile Company’s Performance Based on Selected Sustainability Indicators Using The MPSI and ARTASI Methods
abstract: The textile industry, which plays a vital role in countries’ economic development, contributes to numerous environmental, economic, and social problems because of its extensive use of chemicals and high consumption of water and energy during production. For the industry to keep pace with current changes, it is increasingly important that it adopt sustainable practices in its production and consumption processes. title: The Use of Styrofoam as an Innovative Building Component in Calabar, Cross River State: Implications for Sustainable Architectural Practice
abstract: The persistent housing deficit, indoor thermal discomfort, and rising energy demand in Nigeria’s humid-tropical climate have triggered a search for innovative building components that advance energy efficiency and sustainability in the construction industry. In Calabar, Cross River State, where rapid urbanization and informal construction patterns coexist with climatic vulnerability, the adoption of expanded polystyrene (EPS), commonly known as Styrofoam, as an architectural component remains under-explored, particularly in walling, insulation, and prefabricated systems.
