title: Improved desalination by polymer grafting
abstract: Freshwater scarcity demands desalination technologies that are efficient, scalable, and sustainable. Capacitive deionisation (CDI) is promising but remains limited by inefficient ion adsorption and poor charge utilisation. Here, we show that suitably chosen polyampholytic block copolymer grafting can substantially enhance CDI performance, via a combination of dipolar response and steric effects. title: Beyond the trail: how tourist access shapes mammal activity in a highly visited national park in Costa Rica
abstract: Introduction: Ecotourism can alter wildlife behavior without affecting species diversity, but this is a poorly known subject. Objective: To evaluate the influence of tourist access on medium- and large-bodied mammals in Manuel Antonio National Park, Costa Rica. Methods: From April 2021 to August 2022, camera traps monitored mammals along public trails during periods of restricted and unrestricted tourist access associated with COVID-19 policies and weekly closures. title: 10-kHz coherent anti-stokes Raman spectroscopy thermometry in an arc heater
abstract: Abstract The complexity of high-temperature non-equilibrium flow leads to significant limitations of existing computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models.To further refine these models, there is a pressing need to acquire ro-vibrational temperature data in non-equilibrium flows, which serves to characterize the molecular population distribution. title: Air pollution, urbanization, and health in emerging countries: A Kuznets curve analysis of noncommunicable diseases and infant mortality
abstract: The harmful health effects of environmental pollution on the general public have been a subject of urgent concern for scholars and health experts. The study investigated the effects of pollution on health outcomes in seven selected emerging nations. The countries include Mexico, Indonesia, India, Turkey, China, South Africa, and Brazil. The study drew data from the World Bank Indicators and World Health Organization databases covering 2000–2018. After testing heterogeneity among variables, the study used two-stage least squares (2SLS) regression and ordinary least squares as a robustness check

title: Rural place leadership across the Anglo-Scottish border: analysing the evolution, resilience and success of the Borderlands partnership
abstract: This paper explores the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership, a cross-border initiative seeking to address common challenges in the Anglo-Scottish rural periphery. Utilising a path-tracing methodology, a timeline was constructed to identify key events in the evolution of the Borderlands Partnership which created opportunity spaces for institutional entrepreneurship and generative place leadership. title: Effect of RANDALLfoils on the fluid dynamics of rowing
abstract: Abstract Rowing-blade attachments have the potential to modify blade-fluid interactions during the rowing stroke, however these effects remain difficult to isolate in on-water rowing. This study experimentally investigates the RANDALLfoil, a blade attachment designed to alter the flow around a rowing blade, using 1:4 scaled rowing motions. Force and torque measurements are collected for a standard blade and a RANDALLfoil blade, and two-dimensional particle image velocimetry (PIV) is used to relate the measured loading to leading-edge vortex (LEV) development. title: Gravity-Thermal Coupling Response of a 1m Off-Axis Primary Mirror for AIMS Telescope
abstract: Abstract This paper takes the 1-meter off-axis primary mirror of the AIMS solar telescope as the research object, and adopts the finite element method to analyze its gravity-thermal coupling deformation characteristics under seven elevation angles and three temperature conditions. The results show that the worst surface figure of the primary mirror occurs at −15◦C and 0 ◦ elevation, with an RMS surface accuracy of λ/112.9 (@ 632.8 nm, corresponding to PV = λ/16.4). title: Patterns of variation and taxonomy of the Zygaena fraxini-group in Iran with a focus on Zygaena rosinae Korb 1903 and Zygaena escalerai Poujade 1900 (Lepidoptera: Zygaenidae)
abstract: Species of the genus Zygaena exhibit remarkable morphological diversity in Iran, which historically led to the description of numerous species and subspecies in the region. One of these lineages, the fraxini-group, currently comprises nine species and 36 subspecies, largely delimited based on external morphology, biology and distributional data. Here, we reassess species and subspecies boundaries within this group using an integrative taxonomic approach combining DNA barcoding, internal morphology and species distribution modelling (SDM). Exploring Reverse Logistics: A TRLI-S-B Model Analysis Based on Information, Emotion and Perceived Uncertainty
abstract: This study examines how reverse logistics shapes recycling intentions by proposing a theoretical framework grounded in the TRLI-SOR model. The framework characterizes the reverse logistics information environment through four core antecedents: information authority, information conflict, information overload, and information complexity. Perceived uncertainty is specified as the central mediating mechanism, and worry is incorporated as the key emotional response. title: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
abstract: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. Here, we introduce a climate-feedback into an IO system via the crop sector to illustrate the potential couplings between climate change and material and economic flows. title: Recharge Performance of Pond-Based Managed Aquifer Recharge in the Ramganga Basin
abstract: Groundwater underpins India's water and food security but faces growing stress from overexploitation and climate change. This study evaluates the hydrologic performance of small-scale, pond-based Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) interventions implemented under government development programs, in the context of India's plan to construct 14 million additional recharge structures. Focusing on the groundwater-stressed Ramganga basin, the study draws on three years of participatory monitoring of 23 recharge structures. title: Prenatal microplastic exposure-induced testicular developmental toxicity and its long-term hazards in male rat offspring
abstract: The pervasive environmental presence of microplastics (MPs) raises concerns regarding their potential impacts on reproductive health, particularly in the context of prenatal exposure. This study aimed to establish a polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) exposure model in pregnant rats and to investigate the subsequent effects on the growth, hormonal profiles, steroidogenic enzyme expression, and testicular histology of male offspring from birth to adulthood. title: Association of Long-Term Residentially Assigned Speciated Atmospheric Mercury Emission Flux with All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality
abstract: Abstract Mercury (Hg) is a persistent global pollutant, but population evidence on residentially assigned species-specific atmospheric Hg emission flux and mortality is limited. We analyzed UK Biobank cohorts for all-cause/other-cause (N = 322,666), cardiovascular disease (N = 344,333), and cancer mortality (N = 381,432). Annual EDGAR v8.1 fluxes of total Hg, gaseous elemental Hg (Hg0), gaseous oxidized Hg (Hg2+), and particle-bound Hg (Hg–P) were assigned to geocoded residences. title: Careless Assemblages: Examining Care and Violence After Men’s Unwanted Sexual Experiences
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper develops careless assemblages as a concept to explore the failures to care for men after sexual violence and abuse. We draw upon data from the Men's Unwanted Sexual Experience (MUSE) project, which included semi‐structured interviews and arts‐based workshops with 40 self‐identifying men in Northeast and Southeast England. We show how failures to care for men who are survivors are more than an absence, but an assemblage of gendered discourses, institutional procedures and public interactions that continue harm and violence by disabling men from accessing support. title: Techno-economic comparison of fossil, renewable-carbon and recycling pathways for polypropylene
abstract: Polypropylene production relies predominantly on fossil resources for process energy and carbon feedstock. This study compares fossil primary production, renewable-carbon primary routes based on biomass, renewable hydrocarbons, or CO2 and hydrogen, and recycling pathways under German industrial cost conditions within the European carbon-pricing framework. Literature-based process data are harmonised to a functional unit of 1 tonne of polypropylene pellets at the plant gate. title: Renewable electricity surplus exchanges through the Italy–Tunisia ELMED interconnection: an exploratory market coupling analysis
abstract: Abstract The Mediterranean region is emerging as a strategic area for energy transition, where cross-border electricity interconnections can play a key role in integrating renewable energy resources and strengthening Euro-Mediterranean cooperation. In this context, the ELMED interconnection between Italy and Tunisia serves as a significant case study for analyzing how cross-border electricity exchanges can facilitate the integration of renewable energy surpluses between power systems with different demand profiles and resource availability. title: Influence of nanoscale effects and gradient pore-structure characteristics on the permeability of nanofiltration membranes
abstract: Abstract Understanding the coupled influence of nanoscale interfacial effects and pore structure is essential for clarifying water-transport mechanisms in nanofiltration (NF) membranes. Previous studies have mainly examined either nanoscale transport effects, such as wall slip and interfacial viscosity variation, or membrane structural parameters independently, while their combined effects on membrane permeability remain insufficiently understood. title: Environmental Perception and Intelligent Navigation for Autonomous Delivery Robots in Complex Scenarios
abstract: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) face perception and navigation challenges in complex scenarios. When operating in real world urban environments, ADRs have trouble negotiating upturned streets, uneven terrain, and moving obstacles. This review covers three key areas: environmental perception, navigation techniques, and mechanical adaptability of delivery vehicles. The reviewed studies show that navigation has evolved beyond avoiding obstacles, to its current state of considering whether the ground can be traversed. title: Ecotheological Interpretation of the Story of the People of Saba’ (Q.S. Saba’ [34]: 15–17) to Minimize the Food Waste Crisis in Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to examine the ecotheological interpretation of the story of the Saba’ people in Q.S. Saba’ [34]: 15–17 to minimize the food waste crisis in Indonesia. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, drawing primary sources from the Qur’an (particularly Q.S. Saba’ [34]: 15–17), supported by verses addressing tabdhīr (wastefulness), isrāf (excessiveness), resource reuse, and the prohibition of environmental degradation. institutions: Sunan Gunung Djati State Islamic University Bandung

title: Thermal resilience under climate extremes: simulation-based assessment of heatwave impacts in informal buildings in Cairo
abstract: Abstract Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves. Informal settlements are particularly vulnerable to heat stress due to inadequate housing conditions and socioeconomic constraints. In Egypt, informal housing accounts for 38.6% of the national housing stock, yet the risk of indoor heat stress remains underexplored. This study proposes a quantitative method to identify and classify heatwaves in Cairo and assess their impact on indoor overheating and heat-stress risk. Heatwave characteristics were analyzed for historical (2010–2024) and futur
journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science

title: Ergonomic design of rock-climbing clothing: beyond static anthropometry to movement-informed design
abstract: Conventional garment design typically relies on static anthropometric measurements, which may not adequately account for changes in body dimensions and posture during highly dynamic activities such as rock climbing. This study investigates how climbing-specific movement analysis and dynamic anthropometry can inform ergonomic design of rock-climbing clothing. It combines a review of relevant research with observational and movement analysis of climbers using the Xsens motion-capture system to examine relationships between dynamic body dimensions and garment pattern requirements. title: Apparent ecological network expansion masks structural reorganization and corridor vulnerability in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration
abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization is reorganizing landscape connectivity, yet whether increases in ecological sources or corridors actually represent stronger regional networks remains unclear. Using three representative time slices (2013, 2018, and 2023) in the Central Plains Urban Agglomeration, China, we integrated InVEST–MSPA, Conefor, circuit theory, complex-network analysis, Louvain community detection, and edge collective influence (ECI) to examine stage-specific network reorganization and corridor vulnerability. title: An improved yaw attitude model for GPS Block IIF satellites during eclipse seasons
abstract: Abstract This study improves the operational eclipse-season yaw attitude model for Global Positioning System (GPS) Block IIF satellites by using Reverse Kinematic Precise Point Positioning (RKPPP) yaw estimates as an observation-driven reference. Using a 7.5-year global GPS tracking dataset, we reconstruct yaw attitude time series over eclipse season maneuvers and compare them with the current operational attitude model. title: Complex-valued modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation
abstract: Motivated by the introduction of the Zakharov-Kuznetsov equation as a higher dimensional generalization of the Korteweg-de Vries equation, in this paper we introduce the modified Zakharov-Kuznetsov (mZK) equation as a 2-dimensional generalization of the complex-valued modified Korteweg-de Vries equation. We initiate the mathematical analysis of the mZK equation on $ \mathbb{T}^2 $ by proving a local well-posedness result in Sobolev spaces and by establishing a failure of uniform continuity. We also note that the real-valued version of the mZK equation has physical significance.

title: Global Fujita–Kato Solutions of the Incompressible Inhomogeneous Magnetohydrodynamic Equations

title: Unwilling to leave, unable to stay: mechanism of plasticity in site fidelity as a rewarding tactic in changing environments
abstract: Abstract Context Home-ranging is common among animal species, as site fidelity facilitates cognitive map development and promotes efficient habitat use. The adaptive value of site fidelity, however, should decline as habitat conditions change, yet empirical evidence remains limited, especially for wide-ranging species. Objectives We investigated how fire and forest harvesting affect home-range stability in boreal caribou, a species typically exhibiting strong site fidelity. title: Enhanced growth and yield of chia (Salvia hispanica L.) through phosphorus-induced soil property improvements
abstract: A field experiment was conducted from November 2022 to February 2023 at Boda Upazila, Panchagarh District, located in Agroecological Zone 1 (AEZ-1) of Bangladesh.The objective was to examine the effects of different phosphorus (P) levels on the growth and yield of chia plants (Salvia hispanica).The trial included six levels of phosphorus, designated as T0 (0 kg ha⁻¹), T1 (20 kg ha⁻¹), T2 (40 kg ha⁻¹), T3 (60 kg ha⁻¹), T4 (80 kg ha⁻¹), and T5 (100 kg ha⁻¹), using Triple Superphosphate (TSP) as the phosphorus source.The treatments were organized in a Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with

title: From forest to farmland: seasonal habitat suitability and risk areas of human–elephant conflict in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) of Thailand
abstract: The Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) is currently undergoing drastic economic income development and some of the most rapid landuse changes in Thailand. This area is also amongst the highest for human–elephant conflict (HEC) especially around the Eastern Forest Complex (EFCOM). Studies regarding ecological risks to the wild Asian elephant ( Elephas maximus ) and the population’s impact on human well-being in the area are limited. Despite their potential in optical switching, communications, and signal processing, achieving large optical modulation while maintaining low optical loss and strong field confinement remains a major challenge. title: Performance degradation and failure mechanisms of pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid sucker rods after long-term downhole service
abstract: Pultruded carbon/glass-fiber hybrid composite rods are increasingly used as sucker rods, yet the relationship between degradation accumulated during long-term downhole service and subsequent longitudinal splitting during retrieval and drum winding remains insufficiently understood, particularly for rods containing a carbon/glass hybrid transition region. This study compared five specimens sectioned from a pristine 22 mm-diameter parent rod with five specimens sectioned from a service-aged parent rod retrieved after 435 days of actual downhole service. title: Beyond wind-sector management: optimal wind farm operational planning for balancing fatigue damage and extending lifetime
abstract: Abstract. We present an optimization framework for long‑term wind farm operation that balances fatigue loads and energy yield to extend turbine and farm lifetime. The approach plans per‑turbine derating setpoints for discrete wind conditions using an engineering wake model and surrogate models for power and damage. We formulate the problem as a nonlinear program and solve it either for the full farm in a single run or iteratively per turbine. title: Confining density functional approach to the QCD phase diagram at low temperatures and thermal twin stars
abstract: Abstract We present a density functional-based equation of state for warm, dense nuclear matter with a transition to deconfined quark matter for applications to simulations of supernova explosions and neutron star mergers, but also for the cosmological evolution of Q-balls. For the quark matter equation of state, we employ a recently developed confining density functional approach while nuclear matter is described within a relativistic density functional model of the DD2 class. title: Distributed Observation Scheduling and Sensor Fusion For Large Agile Constellations
abstract: With the rapid increase in interest towards large scale earth observing satellite constellations, the problem of properly commanding and utilizing these systems has become increasingly relevant. This work focuses on a complete distributed approach to this problem, incorporating an observation task allocation and scheduling algorithm in addition to a sensor data fusion algorithm for end-to-end target coverage and processing. title: The Limits of Tidal Circularization and Atmospheric Escape for Mini-Neptunes and Super-Earths: The Case of TOI-2257 b
abstract: With a 35-day orbital period and $\sim$0.5 eccentricity, TOI-2257 b occupies a sparsely populated corner of transiting mini-Neptune parameter space and may lie near the orbital distance at which tidal and atmospheric escape process become negligible. To test this hypothesis, we performed simulations of the combined stellar, tidal, and atmospheric evolution and confirmed that TOI-2257 b does lie near this boundary, regardless of whether it formed with or without a primordial hydrogen envelope. title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. title: Dual Reverse Time Migration: Efficient Least-squares Imaging with Multiple Scattering in Dual Space
abstract: Least-squares reverse time migration (LSRTM) estimates a broadband reflectivity image by iteratively minimizing the data misfit. Despite its superior imaging performance over conventional reverse time migration (RTM), LSRTM is fundamentally limited by the first-order Born approximation and incurs a high computational cost due to the iterative solution of a source-dependent model-space Hessian. title: Fully Automated Wannier Disentanglement via Projectability Selection in Gaussian and Augmented Plane-Wave Frameworks
abstract: Constructing the frozen manifold for entangled bands requires balancing exact reproduction of the target bands with sufficient variational freedom to build a well-localized subspace from the broader Bloch pool. We present a workflow that systematically determines the energy ceiling for a target number of selected Wannier projections, freezing every Bloch state below this threshold across the sampled k-mesh. title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
abstract: We consider the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the recent 248 keV event observed by LZ and identify different experiments that could test it. Details of the underlying model and the ability of complementary experiments to test it depend significantly on the high-velocity tail of the dark matter distribution. We consider several example velocity distributions motivated by the impact of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) in order to map out the effects of this dependence. title: One-Bit Coherent Distributed Radar Detection in Clutter via Velocity-Plane Search: Vanishing Loss and EEC-Calibrated Thresholding
abstract: Coherent distributed radar architectures enhance the detectability of low-reflectivity targets. However, conventional coherent processing generally entails prohibitively large volumes of inter-station data exchange, thereby motivating the adoption of one-bit quantization strategies. In this work, we investigate a clutter-dominated regime in which the interference is driven by a dense ensemble of weak scatterers. title: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method for the shallow water equations on Cartesian grids: mass conservation and wetting and drying over variable topography
abstract: A ghost-cell immersed boundary method is proposed for the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a variable bed (topography), solved with an explicit Godunov-type finite volume scheme (unsplit second-order MUSCL, HLLC flux, hydrostatic reconstruction) on Cartesian grids. Ghost-cell methods leak mass through the wall. To find a robust and conservative treatment, eight constructions of the ghost values and a cut-cell form of the continuity equation were applied to seven test problems, which include wetting and drying on sloping beds and a laboratory dam break. title: Global stability and sharp decay for the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations without thermal diffusion
abstract: We study the two-dimensional non-rotating primitive equations with positive horizontal and vertical viscosity and without thermal diffusion. Our main results are fourfold. First, for every integer \(s\ge4\), we prove that sufficiently small, compatible, doubly periodic \(H^s\) perturbations of a stably stratified rest state with an affine temperature profile generate unique global strong solutions; the horizontal velocity and temperature remain uniformly small at the initial Sobolev order despite the derivative loss in the full diagnostic vertical velocity, and strict stratification persists.

title: Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
abstract: We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. title: WALTzER: Wide-band Atmospheric Laboratory for Transiting Exoplanet Research
abstract: Understanding the origin and evolution of planetary atmospheres, and the connection between their lower and upper atmospheric layers, remains a fundamental challenge in exoplanet science. Addressing these questions requires observations spanning a broad wavelength range, from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared, together with the ability to simultaneously characterise planetary and stellar variability. title: Deterministic Shift Equivalence Testing for Sparse Polynomials
abstract: We study the shift equivalence testing problem for high-degree sparse multivariate polynomials. title: Heterogeneity among and competition between life stages together extend the stability boundary of complex ecological communities
abstract: Classical models of pairwise species interactions consistently predict that large, complex communities are inherently unstable, yet the observed persistence of diverse communities highlights a central contradiction in theoretical ecology. While foundational frameworks often model species as homogeneous populations, one theoretical resolution lies in including internal species structure. title: Topographically Forced Stationary Waves Can Explain the Near-Surface Zonal Winds Observed by Huygens on Titan
abstract: Titan's equatorial superrotation is associated with climatological retrograde (westward) near-surface winds at low latitudes, as consistently simulated by Titan general circulation models. However, the Huygens probe measured prograde (eastward) near-surface winds, contrary to the expected circulation. We investigate whether these observations reflect localized forcing by large-scale topography, using paired three-dimensional dry simulations with and without topography in the Titan Atmospheric Model. title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
abstract: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$σ$-meson interpolating operators. The analysis is performed using three gauge ensembles, including one ensemble simulated with two degenerate light, a strange, and a charm quark with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical value. title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
abstract: Cloud droplets respond to turbulent motion with finite inertia and settle under gravity, while condensation and evaporation change their sizes. The nonuniform accumulation of cloud droplets in turbulent flows, known as preferential concentration, has attracted sustained interest because it affects droplet collision and coalescence rates. We develop an analytical theory that quantifies the coupled effects of droplet inertia, gravitational settling, and phase change on concentration changes. title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension.

abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
abstract: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. abstract: We study a generalized Gross-Pitaevskii equation arising in the mean-field description of exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensates. title: A Fully Discrete, Mass-Conservative Adaptive Discontinuous Spectral-Element Method for the One-Dimensional Richards Equation in Mixed Form
abstract: We present and analyze a spatially and temporally adaptive high-order method for the one-dimensional Richards equation describing vertical water transport in unsaturated soil, with an emphasis on resolving sharp wetting fronts while satisfying a fully discrete water mass balance. The spatial discretization uses an arbitrary-order local discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element formulation with collocated Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature, and the time integration is based on a high-order Rosenbrock-Wanner method. title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
abstract: Birkhoff pseudospectral methods replace the differentiation matrices of classical transcriptions with integration operators whose conditioning does not deteriorate with polynomial order. This paper presents theoretical and computational advancements toward their practical use in aerospace optimal control. abstract: In the case of the totally degenerate split degenerations given by fibered powers of Tate curves over $\mathbf{Z}[[q^{1/w}]]$, this article proves a Fourier expansion principle that applies to higher coherent (equivariant) cohomology classes of rigidified line bundles on the $\mathbf{Z}((q^{1/w}))$-fiber. We do not require any ampleness hypotheses. title: Optimal Gating for Dead-Time-Constrained Single-Photon Detectors
abstract: We develop a Fisher-information framework for optimizing single-photon detector gating in periodic experiments, in contrast to previous more empirical or heuristic gating choices. After each photon detection, such a detector is insensitive for a dead time, so that an early background detection can obscure a later signal. title: KNO scaling violation: the role of the fragmentation region
abstract: This work is motivated by two independent considerations. The first is that KNO scaling is observed in the central rapidity region ($|η|<0.5$, for example) and violated when the fragmentation region is included ($|η|<3.4$, for example). The second is that, in the CGC framework, the $k_T$-factorization formalism is more appropriate to describe particle production in the central region and the hybrid formalism is more appropriate for the fragmentation region. title: Multi-time-stepping splitting scheme with mass lumping for the multiscale wave equation
abstract: Efficient simulation of wave propagation in high-contrast media is challenging because standard explicit schemes are subject to severe time-step restrictions induced by fine spatial scales and fast multiscale modes, whereas fully implicit schemes require costly globally coupled solves. In this work, we develop a mass-lumped multi-time-stepping partially explicit splitting method for multiscale wave equations. title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
abstract: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $Δ(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $Δ$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $Δ$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. title: RadGeoLoc: Radar Geolocalization via Particle Filtering
abstract: In real-time autonomous field applications, GNSS is often unreliable and inaccurate. A possible solution is localizing against a prebuilt map like a satellite image, as it is georeferenced and already surveyed. In this work, we localize a spinning radar measurement against overhead RGB imagery with a learned observation model. abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. title: Information geometry of DGLAP evolution
abstract: Quark and gluon splittings shift proton momentum toward smaller fractions with increasing resolution. Momentum conservation makes the summed momentum-weighted quark and gluon densities, when nonnegative, a probability distribution. We apply information geometry, the geometry of probability distributions, to this probabilistic form of Dokshitzer-Gribov-Lipatov-Altarelli-Parisi evolution. abstract: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity $v_w\to 1$. We generalize this treatment to arbitrary $v_w< 1$, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. abstract: Neutron stars constrain dark matter that is present inside them, through their maximum mass and the tidal deformability. abstract: Neutrinos and muons produced in the forward direction of LHC collisions and detected by the FASER and SND@LHC experiments enable a comprehensive deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) programme, covering both neutral and charged currents, at TeV energies. This programme aims to provide stringent constraints on proton and nuclear structure as well as on hadron fragmentation, and to offer novel insight into neutrino interactions at the highest energies achieved in a laboratory. abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. title: Modelo de gestão de dados marinhos FAIR com articulação IODE no Panamá
abstract: Marine data management in developing countries faces structural challenges such as institutional fragmentation, lack of regulatory frameworks, and capacity limitations, hindering the adoption of FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). This study, with a qualitative approach complemented by a descriptive quantitative component, aimed to design a national marine data network model based on FAIR principles for Panama, articulated within the framework of the IOC-UNESCO IODE programme and OBIS. title: Chinese Botany at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair
abstract: This article examines the Chinese botanical exhibits at the 1873 Vienna World’s Fair as part of global knowledge formation within Austro-Hungarian Empire. It argues that these exhibits were not static displays but dynamic objects mediating trade, science, and imperial representation. Drawing on customs records, diplomatic correspondence, exhibition catalogues, and contemporary reports, the study traces their trajectory from collection across treaty ports and Southeast Asia to exhibition and reception in Vienna. abstract: This research analyzes the dynamics of halal tourism and the implementation of Islamic values in key Southeast Asian destinations, namely Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand. This research uses a qualitative approach to explore how Islamic values, such as halalness, sustainability, and inclusiveness, are implemented in halal tourism policies and practices. abstract: This study examined the legal and ethical challenges associated with genomic data sharing in Nigeria with focused on issues of consent, privacy, data ownership and international collaboration. abstract: Abstract Background Environmental metadata is essential for using metagenomic and microbiome data to gain relevant biological insights like relations between the environment and microbial communities, genome content and protein-level adaptations. abstract: Abstract The semi-enclosed Baltic Sea is a comparatively young brackish ecosystem characterised by strong environmental gradients that can shape genetic diversity and demographic history in marine species. The amphi-Atlantic bivalve Arctica islandica (Linnaeus 1767) inhabits the southwestern Baltic Sea, where populations experience environmental conditions distinct from fully marine habitats. abstract: Adolescents’ environmental responsibility is shaped by both individual and contextual factors, including life goal orientation and family communication processes. The present study examined the associations between parent–child civic communication, intrinsic and extrinsic life goals, and environmental responsibility toward the sea among Italian adolescents. abstract: Marine biodiversity is adversely affected by many human activities and their pressures. As such, there is the need for a cause-consequence-response method to objectively address the risks associated with those adverse changes. abstract: La Generación Aumentada por Recuperación (RAG) es una metodología que permite reducir las alucinaciones en modelos de lenguaje aplicados a bases de datos especializadas. Systems need to be able to handle requests that are worded differently but mean the same thing, to make sure routing is consistent, caching can be reused, latency is reduced, reliability is ensured, and governance is supported. journal: International Journal of Computer Trends and Technology

title: Climate Litigation and Constitutional Courts: Advancing Intergenerational Environmental Rights Through Constitutional Adjudication
abstract: Climate change has intensified the need for legal frameworks that recognise environmental protection as an essential component of constitutional governance. In recent years, climate litigation has emerged as a significant pathway through which constitutional courts interpret and enforce environmental rights, particularly in relation to future generations. This paper examines how constitutional adjudication has contributed to the development of intergenerational environmental rights within environmental constitutionalism. title: In Hot Water? The Macroeconomic Impacts of El Niño
abstract: Despite their potentially major impacts, little is known about how El Niño impact the U.S. economy. El Niños are distinct from other commonly studied weather shocks because they are a global phenomenon, unfold over a period of months, can be forecast months in advance, are relatively infrequent, and have very different effects on weather outcomes depending on the time of year and region. These features make traditional analytical methods ill-suited to studying the economic impacts of El Niño events. In this paper I use a new approach to estimating the impulse response functions of El Niños. I

title: Economic Policies toward Taiwan’s Indigenous Peoples, 1684–1874
abstract: This article examines economic policies toward Taiwan’s Indigenous peoples during the early Qing period (1684–1874) through documentary analysis. Major policies included the tongshi system, the Aboriginal Affairs Subprefect, restrictions on reclamation, acculturation and education, and tax reductions. These measures aimed to maintain social order, regulate Indigenous–Han relations, protect Indigenous livelihoods, and facilitate economic development. abstract: Nigeria is blessed with abundant petroleum and other natural resources such as oil and gas, yet the citizens are energy poor. Nigeria’s petroleum concern could be expressed in a paradoxical state. That is energy poverty in the midst of energy wealth. Generally speaking, Nigeria’s economy is monocultural where almost every economic activity revolves around oil and gas. Petroleum oil accounts for about 80% of government revenues, including export and foreign exchange earnings and 70% of electricity generation. title: Beyond Biomass: Relationship Between Biofilm Architecture, Viable Bacterial Burden, and Antibiotic Survival in Clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates
abstract: Crystal violet (CV) staining is widely used to classify clinical isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae as non-adherent, weak, moderate, or strong biofilm producers. However, a measurement of total adherent biomass does not necessarily indicate the number of viable bacteria present within a biofilm or the capacity of those bacteria to survive antimicrobial exposure. This study examined the relationships among CV biomass, three-dimensional biofilm architecture, viable sessile burden, and antibiotic survival in a panel of 60 non-duplicate clinical K. pneumoniae isolates. title: A Curated Library Collection: Pacific Records and the Australian Joint Copying Project, 1939–54
abstract: This article examines the identification and acquisition of documents for the Australian Joint Copying Project (AJCP) from 1939 to 1954. It argues that the AJCP’s evolving scope reflected Australia’s shifting geopolitical identity and intellectual ambitions in the Pacific. Initially shaped by librarians’ efforts to address a national shortage of research materials, the AJCP expanded after World War II with the involvement of the Australian National University’s Research School of Pacific Studies. Drawing on administrative records and policy manuscripts held at the National Library of Australia

title: Seismological Constraints on Subduction and Suture Zone Architecture in the Central African Copperbelt
abstract: Summary Central Africa marks a major collisional zone of the Pan-African Orogeny, involving convergence of the Congo and Kalahari plates during Gondwana assembly (~600–500 Ma). This collision formed the Lufilian Belt and one of the world’s most significant metallogenic provinces—the Central African Copperbelt. However, the deep lithospheric architecture underpinning this mineral-rich region remains poorly understood. title: Integrated Waste Treatment Facility In Payakumbuh: Performance Evaluation and Technology Selection Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis
abstract: The collapse of the Payakumbuh regional landfill in December 2023 left the city without a final disposal site, so the integrated waste treatment facility (TPST) commissioned in January 2025 now carries most of the municipal waste load. This study measured the facility's performance, traced its material flows, and identified the most suitable technology combination for its expansion. title: Time waits for no one: a long-term study of the dynamics of nematode metacommunities in newly formed ponds
abstract: Abstract Understanding how ecological communities assemble through time requires integrating temporal dynamics with species’ life-history and functional traits. Here, we investigated long-term dynamics of nematode communities inhabiting the sediment of eight newly created ponds. We measured abundance, species richness, and community composition monthly over 3 years in all ponds and over 10 years in one pond, representing approximately 10–100 generations for most free-living nematode species. abstract: Bamboo-Based Headwater Conservation and Its Utilization as Alternative Energy in Facing Energy Crises and Military Threats. Bamboo management may connect headwater protection with local energy diversification, provided that biomass extraction does not undermine soil cover and ecological functions. This article examines the evidence supporting this connection through a focused narrative review of eleven journal articles published between 2020 and 2026. title: Faculty Perceptions of Shared Governance and Collaborative Work Environment in a University Setting: Evidence from Xiamen, China
abstract: University governance in China has undergone a gradual but discernible shift from centralized, top-down administration toward more participatory and collaborative arrangements. Drawing on Emerson, Nabatchi, and Balogh’s (2012) collaborative governance framework, this study examines how faculty members at a comprehensive university in Xiamen, China, perceive shared leadership and the collaborative work environment. title: Chasing Bubbles: Toward a Standardized Approach for Quantifying Methane Ebullition Using Bubble Traps in Streams and Rivers
abstract: Abstract Ebullition transports large quantities of the potent greenhouse gas methane (CH4) from stream sediments into the atmosphere. However, the use of different sampling designs complicates comparisons of CH4 emissions estimates between studies. Here, we present the first systematic review of sampling designs used in the past for assessing fluvial CH4 ebullition rates. In addition, we conducted field experiments to estimate the optimal number of bubble traps and the length of the sampling period, and to assess uncertainties in determining CH4 content in the emitted bubbles. title: Come a long way: The global historian’s craft, twenty years on
abstract: Abstract Twenty years after the founding of the Journal of Global History , this anniversary article takes stock of global history: its trajectory, its markers of disciplinary maturity, its political sense of purpose, and the difficulties and limits of the enterprise. Concerns after 2016 that global history might lose its relevance in a changing political climate have, thus far, not been borne out. abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh harga dan fasilitas terhadap keputusan wisatawan dalam memilih paket wisata pada PT Holiday Trip Tour and Travel. title: Building and Sustaining: The Unfinished Medina-Mecca Extension of the Ottoman Hijaz Telegraph Line (1900-1904)
abstract: The Salt-Medina-Mecca telegraph project began in 1900 with the aim of building a continuous overland connection under Ottoman administrative control and reducing reliance on the foreign submarine cable via Jeddah. However, the project was stalled before completion and this article examines why work on the Medina-Mecca extension initially stalled and why it remained unfinished. Drawing chiefly on official Ottoman records, the study uses the Salt-Medina line, completed in 1901, as a comparative baseline. title: The Operational Politics of "Untitled"
abstract: “Untitled” is ubiquitous in modern and contemporary art, yet scholarship has treated it as a homogeneous category signifying openness or resistance. This article argues that “Untitled” functions not as the absence of naming but as an active operational strategy that redistributes naming authority across the art world. Drawing on case studies of four modern and contemporary artists, the analysis identifies three interlocking mechanisms: semantic resistance, perceptual intensification, and institutional recoding. title: QUANTUM-RESONANT ENERGY COUPLING IN AGRICULTURE (QREC-AGRI): A FALSIFIABLE MULTISCALE FRAMEWORK FOR TESTING NON-CONTACT EFFECTS IN PLANT-SOIL-WATER SYSTEMS
abstract: Agriculture increasingly requires interventions that improve yield stability, resource-use efficiency and stress resilience without proportionally increasing chemical or energetic inputs. Quantum-Resonant Energy Coupling for Agriculture (QREC-Agri) is a proposed remote, non-contact intervention whose initiating physical mechanism is presently unresolved. Rather than infer mechanism from outcome, this article develops a falsifiable framework that separates four evidentiary layers: agronomic efficacy, biological mediation, physical coupling and quantum-mechanistic attribution. title: Climate-Resilient Inclusive Banking in State-Owned Commercial Banks: a Five-Level Governance Model for Bangladesh
abstract: Purpose: Bangladesh needs its banks to finance climate adaptation while protecting both vulnerable borrowers and bank balance sheets from physical and transition risks. State-owned commercial banks (SOCBs) have national reach and public mandates, yet they carry some of the weakest asset quality in the system. This paper asks how SOCBs can integrate climate risk management with inclusive lending without excluding the communities most exposed to climate hazards. title: Asymmetrical governance and territorial welfare allocation in Bangladesh
abstract: This study examines how Social Safety Net Programs (SSNPs) in Bangladesh generate spatially differentiated welfare outcomes within a unitary governance system. It conceptualizes these patterns as programmatic asymmetry, where welfare resources are unevenly distributed based on regional variations in poverty, vulnerability, and demographic conditions. Using qualitative secondary analysis of government data, HIES, and existing literature, the study evaluates allocation patterns, primarily through the Employment Generation Programme for the Poorest (EGPP). title: Better data for better public health decision-making: perspectives on quantifying the intended and unintended impacts of public service modifications
abstract: Public services such as healthcare, schools, and transport constitute the infrastructure essential for a functioning and productive society. These services may undergo planned modifications because of interventions intended to manage societal challenges, or experience unplanned disruptions resulting from external shocks. For instance, schools might be closed to mitigate the spread of an infectious disease, or when an external shock, such as a heatwave, renders their continued operation infeasible. title: An Analysis on the Absence of Chinese Wildlife Conservation Legislation Through the Bear Bile Case and the Comparative Perspective of Canada’s Legal Practice
abstract: This article examines the ethical deficiencies in Chinese wildlife conservation legislation through a critical analysis of the controversial bear bile farming case. By investigating China's current wildlife protection legal framework and its practical implementation, the research reveals a profound disconnect between legislation and effective wildlife conservation. The study identifies three major ethical absences in Chinese wildlife protection laws: the concept of sustainability, the principle of public participation, and animal welfare considerations. title: From Farm to Table Measuring Host Communities’ Relationship with the Plant World in Instagram Tourism Reels
abstract: Regenerative tourism claims to move beyond sustainability by restoring ecosystems and communities, but whether its communication enacts that claim has not been measured. The article annotates ten Instagram reels and captions from five regenerative, sustainable and neoliberal accounts, across 34 nodes and 261 values, yielding 1,737 multimodal and 565 linguistic annotations. title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). title: Scribbles near Shaukiwan: Squatter Formalization and Everyday Colonial Relations in Late Nineteenth-Century Hong Kong
abstract: Scholars have identified colonial land reforms, beginning in 1890s Squatter Board and culminating in the 1900s New Territories Land Court, as “momentous” and “revolutionary” transformations in the history of Hong Kong and, indeed, China. But what did this transformation look like on the ground, during the mundane encounters between colonial officials and squatting residents? abstract: This article offers a legal-criminological analysis of the Chinese public security system. It examines the normative, institutional, and technological foundations underpinning crime prevention in China, highlighting the integration of criminal law with broader policies and mechanisms of social supervision. The study explores how this framework enables early intervention against criminal behaviour while prioritising the collective interest. title: A review of country ambition in targeting important areas for biodiversity under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
abstract: Targets 1 and 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) require actions to focus on areas of importance for biodiversity-a prerequisite for reversing biodiversity loss and halting human-induced extinctions as set out in the Mission and Goals of the KMGBF. There is a need to review progress on how countries are aiming to identify and conserve such areas of importance. abstract: The booming fast fashion industry fuels a throwaway consumer culture that has negative environmental impacts. Sustainability branding of fast fashion is like solving a paradox. title: Navigating Traditions and Modernity: Gender Dynamics in Opobo Kingdom, 1870 – 2022
abstract: This paper explores the gender dynamics within the Opobo Kingdom of Rivers State, Nigeria, from its founding in 1870 to 2022 focusing on the diverse roles and contributions of women from the pre-colonial period to the post-colonial era. It critically examines how women have navigated the intersecting forces of tradition, modernity, and socio-political structures to serve as agents of change. title: Revisiting Prime Minister John Curtin’s house as an intimate Australian domicile
abstract: John Curtin was the Prime Minister of Australia during WWII and died in office in 1945. In the early-1920s he designed a modest family home in Western Australia with a wide verandah so he could rehearse speeches and recite poetry while perambulating its perimeter. It was a seaside respite far away from the slings and arrows of political and public life in the capital of Canberra. This study reexamines a seemingly ordinary house with extraordinary historical associations to unpick how national narratives and personal domestic materialities collide in the domicile. abstract: The aim of this study is to compare football agent activities in Türkiye and England within financial, administrative, and legal contexts. The study employs a qualitative research design, utilizing document analysis, purposive sampling for data collection, and content analysis methods. The documents collected as raw data include football agent regulations, lists of licensed football agents, agent payments, and agent payment reports publicly shared by the Turkish Football Federation and the English Football Association. abstract: This research investigates the interplay of Islamic environmental ethics, environmental awareness, and the practice of green banking services in Bangladesh from a moral perspective of Maqasid al-Shariah. title: Across North America: Reginald Arthur Lorrain and the Making of a Missionary
abstract: This article examines the North American years (1899–1902) of Reginald Arthur Lorrain, an Englishman who subsequently served for several decades as a Christian missionary among the Maras of the Indo-Burma borderland. Drawing on Lorrain’s unpublished personal diary, the study traces his passage through the agricultural, industrial, and itinerant-labour economies of Manitoba, Ontario, and the southern United States, and argues that the hardship, physical risk, and social marginality he encountered there constituted a formative, if unintended, preparation for his later missionary vocation. abstract: ABSTRACT Anaerobic speed reserve (ASR) and critical speed (CS) offer practical, performance‐based estimates of physiological tolerances, and can be derived from maximal aerobic speed (MAS) and maximal sprint speed (MSS) in swimming. title: Reproducing Historic Inorganic Compounds: Reference Materials for Identifying Compounds in the Clemens‐Winkler Collection (Part 3)
abstract: The Clemens‐Winkler collection is a significant 19 th ‐century archive of inorganic chemical specimens, offering insights into the scientific practices of its era. As part of a digitization project, this study uses nondestructive analytical techniques—synchrotron‐based X‐ray diffraction (XRD) and X‐ray fluorescence (XRF) at the P21.2 beamline of PETRA III, as well as laboratory Raman spectroscopy and handheld XRF—to characterize historical samples without opening or damaging their sealed containers. title: The Many Routes to the Ubiquitous Bradley–Terry Model
abstract: The rating of items based on pairwise comparisons has been a topic of statistical investigation for many decades. Numerous approaches have been proposed. One of the best known is the Bradley–Terry model. This paper seeks to assemble and explain a variety of motivations for its use. Some are based on principles or on maximizing an objective function; others are derived from well-known statistical models, or stylized game scenarios. They include both examples well-known in the literature as well as what are believed to be novel presentations.

title: Climate Justice in Sub‐Saharan Africa: Unequal Burdens and Pathways to Socially Just Adaptation
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change in Sub‐Saharan Africa is often framed through vulnerability, resilience, and adaptation, yet these concepts alone do not fully explain the unequal social, economic, and political conditions shaping climate harm. This review examines climate change through a climate justice lens, focusing on unequal burdens, household welfare losses, fiscal constraints, adaptation finance, gendered inequalities, and pathways to socially just adaptation. title: The Social and Economic History of Cattle Breeding in Thrace in the Early Republican Period (1923- 1950)
abstract: This study focuses on the socio-economic history of cattle breeding in Thrace from the mid-1920s to the late 1940s. title: Spiritual Tourism Without Staging the Sacred: Evidence from Tanjung Puting
abstract: Spiritual tourism increasingly encompasses contemplative encounters with nature and culture, yet the development of spiritually themed products in protected-area destinations raises questions about cultural authority, conservation, and commercialisation. This study explores whether an ecotourism destination in Tanjung Puting, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, could support a community-sensitive spiritual tourism offer without transforming sacred practices into visitor performances. abstract: This article is a result of the first year of the educational project under the National Program "Education with Science", implemented at the Faculty of Biology at Sofia University "St. Kliment Ohridski". The project aims to create a sustainable connection between the academic community, school teachers and students, introducing modern scientific achievements and research approaches into school education. title: Access to and control over water security: The perspective of gender equality in Lao PDR
abstract: Climate change and water-related disasters significantly affect water security and livelihoods, particularly in vulnerable communities. In Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), women often bear the burden of domestic water collection, yet their role in water governance remains limited. The objective of this study was to examine gendered dimensions of access to water security and participation in water-related decision-making across household, community, and institutional levels in Lao PDR. title: Modern pollen rain of an upland area: implications of pollen dispersal for interpreting palaeoenvironmental records
abstract: A long‐term perspective on landscape evolution is critical for understanding past land‐use activity, land cover–climate feedbacks and, notably, for establishing a factual basis for conservation. Fossil pollen analysis provides a means to achieve this. Biases pertaining to pollen productivity, pollination processes and basin size, however, mean there is not a one‐to‐one relationship between pollen and plant presence. Upland pollen recruitment is poorly understood, and existing studies of pollen dispersal have yielded conflicting results, making interpreting past landscape character challenging.

title: Designing Culturally Grounded Mindful Learning for Social Moderation in Elementary Schools: A Qualitative Needs Analysis in a Pandalungan Context
abstract: Elementary classrooms are formative social spaces in which children learn how to interpret difference, regulate responses, participate fairly, and handle disagreement. This qualitative needs analysis examined how culturally grounded mindful learning could be designed to support social moderation in upper-grade elementary classrooms in Jember, East Java, Indonesia. title: Between the Mosque’s Call and the Temple’s Bell: The Making of Bengal’s Syncretic Literature across a Thousand Years
abstract: This essay argues that Bengali literature emerged from a continuous process of religious and cultural interweaving, shaped by Bengal’s multi-ethnic origins and centuries-long Hindu–Muslim coexistence. abstract: Abstract Shipboard hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs) are increasingly deployed to integrate advanced propulsion systems and pulsed power loads while maintaining high power quality and reliability. However, rapid load fluctuations can induce severe transient disturbances that threaten system stability. This paper proposes a system-level coordinated control strategy for an Active Front-End (AFE) converter and a Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) to enhance transient stability and power quality in shipboard hybrid AC/DC MGs. abstract: This article examines the need to transform Indonesia’s regional regulation-making from a predominantly formal and documentary process into a smart, participatory, data-driven, and accountable model of local law-making. title: Pengaruh Work Life Balance dan Motivasi Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan pada Wedding Planner by Riska
abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of work-life balance and work motivation on employee performance at Wedding Planner by Riska. The study was motivated by the high work demands in the wedding service industry, which may affect employees’ work-life balance, work motivation, and overall performance. A quantitative research method was employed, with data collected through questionnaires. The population consisted of 53 employees, all of whom were selected as respondents using a saturated sampling technique. abstract: The study evaluated the perceived effects of implementing single-use plastic regulations on micro fish vendors in the Island Garden City of Samal. It used a quantitative descriptive-comparative study design to examine the vendors' demographic characteristics and their perceptions of the regulation's impact on their business operations. The study also found no differences in perceived impact among vendors when divided into groups by age, gender, and educational attainment. While governments and wellknown political leaders are usually the focus of the traditional political perspective, nontraditional players like online-based civil society organisations are becoming more and more important in environmental politics at all levels. This study aims to examine the potential of traditional markets to improve community economic welfare from an Islamic economic perspective. abstract: Background Western US forests face rising high-severity fire risk motivating increased investment in forest management. abstract: The tokenisation of intellectual-property-related financial claims on distributed ledger technology (DLT) promises fractional investment, programmable licensing, faster settlement and improved traceability. Yet the same ledger architecture that can make regulatory information more accessible may also create a new confidentiality problem for IP-intensive issuers. This paper interrogates the normative and policy dimensions of road infrastructure provision in Ghana by reframing it as both a government obligation and a welfare good. abstract: Employee’s positive organizational behavior (POB) can be beneficial to individuals at work and organizations, promoting individual and organizational performances. abstract: Rivers State, located in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, possesses a rich cultural heritage that holds immense potential for tourism development. abstract: In recent years, the consumption patterns of live music in India have broken out of conventional metropolitan hubs and found an eager, mobile audience across smaller towns, rural valleys, and scenic regional getaways. abstract: This paper examines the strategy of da'wah in empowering the community by thematically examining the verses of the Qur'an. abstract: The fashion industry is widely recognized as one of the most environmentally harmful industries, prompting increasing attention to technological and circular solutions promoted as pathways toward sustainability. abstract: This article analyzes one of the most relevant topics in Arbitration, which is procedural and evidentiary freedom and its direct relationship with Soft Law (Best Practices). It is a particularly significant issue in Peru, since the vast majority of local ‘arbitration experts’ resort to the Civil Procedure Code, which significantly undermines the practice of arbitration.

abstract: In July 2026, the unexpected mass crossing of migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta sparked bitter controversy in the European Union (EU) and exposed once again the lack of European solidarity in the field of migration. At the same time, member states were perfectly ready to help each other fight the devastating bushfires that raged around the Mediterranean. title: Legal Pluralism and Building Permit Enforcement in Tanzania: Contradictions of the Dual Land Tenure System
abstract: Tanzania operates a dual land tenure system. It recognises granted and customary rights of occupancy. The statute treats the two forms as equal, as set out in section 18(1) of the Village Land Act. The Constitution and the Court of Appeal confirm that customary rights are property. Yet building permit enforcement is built around granted title. A landholder in a declared planning area must obtain a permit before development. abstract: Climate policy increasingly recognises that unequal social relations shape climate risk, yet this recognition has not consistently changed budgets, eligibility rules, or outcomes. This article examines where near-universal gender commitments weaken and what determines the scale of that loss. abstract: This article draws upon research undertaken in two rural communities in Malaysia under the program My Village My Future, a community-based entrepreneurship program initiated by the government to develop rural areas. Little is known about the success of rural community-based entrepreneurship. The paper uses various community-based entrepreneurship models to explore rural community-based entrepreneurship's roots, challenges, and issues. abstract: Indonesia’s food security governance faces a structural paradox: a 2025 budget allocation of IDR 155.5 trillion coexists with 23.28 million undernourished citizens and a 13-year absence of a National Food Plan. This study argues that data infrastructure fragmentation is the principal structural barrier underlying this paradox. abstract: This paper examines Michel Foucault´s most relevant theoretical and methodological contributions to contemporary approaches of political discourse analysis within the French tradition. It specifically assessed the influence of income creation, community-based tourism activities, and ecotourism activities on wildlife conservation. abstract: The Nigerian Civil War, which ranged from 1967 to 1970, stands as a pivotal moment in the nation's history, marked by intense ethnic tensions and a profound struggle for control over resources and power. title: LEXICAL-SEMANTIC FEATURES OF ENGLISH AND UZBEK TRADE TERMS
abstract: The article is devoted to the lexical-semantic features of trade terms in English and Uzbek languages. Trade terminology is one of the oldest and most dynamic layers of economic vocabulary in both languages. The study covers polysemy, synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy and homonymy, as well as semantic changes and borrowings. The article material consists of English trade terms and their Uzbek equivalents drawn from explanatory and bilingual dictionaries, legal and normative documents and commercial texts. abstract: This study assessed the preparedness of public primary schools for climate-responsive disaster planning in Port Harcourt City Local Government Area of Rivers State. abstract: This paper evaluates the demographic effects of two major earthquakes – L’Aquila 2009 and Central Italy 2016 – that struck a large area in Central and Southern Italy. abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance is shaped by biosocial and microbiological processes, yet sex and gender have not been systematically framed across the three domains (infection, antibiotic selection and transmission) that lead to drug-resistant infection. title: OPTIMIZATION OF TOURIST ROUTES IN BATAM CITY USING INTEGER LINEAR PROGRAMMING WITH DESTINATION CATEGORY CONSTRAINTS
abstract: Tourist route planning plays an important role in improving travel efficiency and visitor experience in urban tourism areas. Batam City offers numerous tourist destinations with diverse characteristics, making route planning under realistic constraints a challenging task. Classical Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) models assume that all destinations must be visited, which is often impractical in real-world tourism scenarios. Therefore, this study proposes an optimization model for tourist route planning in Batam City using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) with destination category constraints.

The study analysed that indeterminacy and its effects on exceptionality, proportionality and legal certainty. The research was qualitative, legal-dogmatic and documentary, reviewing norms, constitutional case law, inter-American standards, comparative law and recent Latin American scholarship. title: IMPACT OF COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION ON PERFORMANCE OF DRYLAND RESTORATION INITIATIVES: A CASE STUDY OF COMBIO AND TREPA PROJECTS IN RWAMAGANA DISTRICT, EASTERN RWANDA
abstract: This study examined the impact of community participation on the performance of dryland restoration initiatives implemented under the TREPA and COMBIO projects in Rwamagana District, Rwanda, since 2022. Despite increasing investments in dryland restoration, limited empirical evidence existed regarding how different levels and forms of community participation influence restoration outcomes in Rwanda. abstract: Labour, which is the totality of the relationship between employers and employees, including service conditions is very crucial to national development. Consequently, when labour relationship are not effectively managed, with respect to the university system, it disrupts academic activities. The fundamental objective of this paper is to evaluate the management of labour dispute, with particular reference to the Nigerian university system. abstract: This article takes a critical-analytical approach to assess the need to humanize the sciences for peace, security and sustainable development in a technology-based global society.Arising from the linkage between the sciences and the global challenge of insecurity, this paper emphasizes the relevance of humanistic approaches and methods to the sciences in light of the skills and invaluable insights of the humanities, which can help to proffer both ethical and value-laden creative solutions to myriad problems facing humanity in a globalized world.This paper considers the importance of humanizing

title: "Wondrous Emanations of a Transcendently Transfigured Sublimity and Profundity": The Reception of Beethoven's Last Three Piano Sonatas in the Nineteenth and Early Twentieth Centuries
abstract: Ludwig van Beethoven’s last three piano sonatas, Opp. 109, 110, and 111, have captured the imaginations of critics from the nineteenth century to the present. As “late” works penned towards the end of the composer’s life, these sonatas have often been read as infused with existential or transcendental meaning, frequently aligned with Beethoven’s own experiences. title: Legal Pluralism and Customary Forest Governance: Customary Community-Based Zoning and Institutional Adaptation in Yongsu Desoyo, Papua
abstract: Customary forest governance in Papua reflected the complex dynamics of legal pluralism, where state and customary law interacted in the management of community living spaces. This research aimed to analyze the governance of the indigenous forest by the Yongsu Desoyo community through a traditional zoning system consisting of sena, buso, and sasena as cultivation land, utilization zone, and sacred zone. title: Regulatory Gaps Facing Indonesian Village-Owned Enterprises in Cross-Border Digital Trade and Insights from Malaysia
abstract: Background: Government Regulation No. 11 of 2021 grants Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) legal entity status without any territorial limit on their markets. Yet official data record only 22 exporting BUMDes out of about 66,000, and none is identified as trading through cross-border e-commerce platforms, revealing a gap between formal legal capacity and actual participation. title: An unexpected source of methane by a power plant
abstract: Abstract The ICOS atmospheric monitoring station at Saclay, southwest of Paris, continuously measures atmospheric CO₂, CH₄, and other trace gases for more than a decade, providing insight into processes acting from local to global scales. During winter under north-westerly winds, the station repeatedly records large methane enhancements that can be traced to the plume of a nearby complex of power plants located a few hundred metres from the site. title: Research on the flow of agricultural subsidies and the stability of transfer contracts: with a discussion on its impact on investment
abstract: Contractual stability in land management is crucial for incentivizing long-term investment, enhancing productivity, and promoting sustainable agricultural development. However, contractual instability remains a prominent issue in China’s land leasing market reform, and its causes and impacts require systematic analysis. abstract: The question of methodology in the emerging field of intercultural studies interested my graduate advisors at UCSB, whose formative influences were indispensable for my intellectual development. Raimon Panikkar’s complex thought stood on the oneness of epistemology and ontology (you “become” what you “know.”) He also directed my attention to the philosophy of Nishida Kitarō. Ninian Smart heralded his own approach to the philosophical study of religion. title: A africanofobia enraizada: esquerda acadêmica — discursos, práticas e contradições
abstract: A partir de uma abordagem qualitativa, método de pesquisa memorial, observação participante e análise documental, este artigo faz uma análise crítica sobre a relação entre os estudantes africanos e a esquerda acadêmica brasileira. O texto problematiza os múltiplos aspectos do processo de formação, que vão desde o acolhimento, integração e permanência – mas também as implicações ideológico-epistemológicas que marcam o processo como um todo. title: Sustainable Smiles: Modifying Mothers' Behavior Towards Eco-Friendly Oral Health Care and Radiology for Managing Children's Anxiety and Promoting Their Well-being
abstract: Background: Traditional pediatric dentistry and conventional dental radiography contribute to environmental waste and trigger severe dental anxiety in children.Modifying maternal behavioral patterns toward sustainability and modern green radiology could offer a dual solution for environmental conservation and pediatric psychological well-being.Aim: This study evaluated the effectiveness of an educational intervention in modifying mothers' behaviors toward eco-friendly oral health care and radiology, managing children's anxiety, and promoting their well-being.Subjects and Methods: A quasi-exper

title: Mating preference evolution has sex-opposite effects on species persistence under reproductive interference
abstract: Reproductive interference, where interspecific mating activities have negative effects on reproductive output, can impact the expansion of one species' range into that of a related competitor. Theory to date suggests that if species recognition mechanisms evolve rapidly enough, the attenuation of reproductive interference may allow range expansions to proceed (a form of evolutionary rescue). title: Convergence, Competition or Complementarity? EU-Member States Cooperation on Mobility and Returns
abstract: European Union (EU) external migration governance in the Southern Neighbourhood is shaped by variable patterns of interaction between the EU and its Member States (MS). Dynamics of competition, convergence and complementarity coexist across cooperation on legal mobility and returns, producing distinct configurations of external migration governance and shaping the EU’s bargaining power with third countries. title: La noción de riesgo existencial y sus problemas
abstract: The notion of existential risk, in the sense of a natural or artificial factor that could endanger the existence of our species, is beginning to be widely used in discussions about the future of humanity. This usage can be useful in raising awareness of the dangers that threaten our species if we do not take appropriate measures in time, particularly about the impact of new technologies on the environment and human societies. title: In the Footsteps of Trebellius Maximus: Finding the Rossett Roman Villa and its Implications
abstract: Abstract The discovery of a lead ingot near Wrexham in 2019 prompted an investigation into Roman activity in the surrounding area, leading to the identification of the first structurally attested Roman villa rustica in north Wales. In a region where evidence for rural settlement and agriculture has long been eclipsed by military and industrial remains, this find raises new questions about everyday life under Roman rule.
