abstract: This paper doctrinally examined oil and gas exploitation and the energy security rights of host communities in Nigeria, exposing a trajectory of resource abundance and national wealth, but a paradox of a population in abject want, environmental degradation, economic emasculation and deliberate domestic energy unavailability and unaffordability, resulting in grinding energy poverty. title: The Utilitarian Construction: A Reflection on the Formation of the Logistics Sector SOE Holding Company
abstract: This study analyzes the application of utilitarianism as a philosophical foundation in the establishment of a State-Owned Enterprises (SOE) holding company in Indonesia’s logistics sector, with PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) as the parent company. This policy is based on Law Number 1 of 2025 concerning SOEs, which authorizes the state to establish operational holdings to enhance efficiency and national economic utility. title: CLIMATE-DRIVEN BORDER FLUX AND THE POLITICS OF HUMANITARIAN-REFUGEE DIPLOMACY
abstract: This paper discusses the interplay of climate-induced mobility, border dynamics, and politics of humanitarian-refugee diplomacy in the modern international system. It states that climate change has become one of the key factors leading to displacement, transforming the migration patterns and imposing more and more pressure on the existing system of governance. title: El delito casi impune: protección penal de los recursos del patrimonio genético en Ecuador
abstract: The study analysed the criminal offence of unauthorised access to genetic resources of the national heritage, set out in Article 248(1) of the Comprehensive Organic Criminal Code, in its doctrinal, multilevel legal and applied dimensions. The aim was to determine the causes of its punitive ineffectiveness and to assess its consistency with the biocentric paradigm of the Constitution. title: Social Sciences as a Pathway to Equitable Environmental Governance and Climate Action
abstract: Global environmental challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, pollution, and resource depletion pose existential threats to ecosystems and human well-being. While the natural sciences provide crucial data on the scope and mechanisms of these issues, addressing them effectively requires an understanding of the human dimensions that underlie environmental degradation. Social science plays a vital role in interpreting the behavioral, cultural, political, and economic drivers of environmental change, offering tools and frameworks for creating sustainable solutions. title: From policy to practice: Healthcare providers' experiences in implementing vaccination strategies in Mozambique
abstract: Introduction: Achieving full immunization coverage remains a persistent challenge in many low- and middle-income countries, leaving children vulnerable to preventable diseases. In Mozambique, only 38% of children aged 12–23 months have received the basic antigens, and even fewer have completed the national immunization schedule. This downward trend signals widening gaps in access to and utilization of immunization services. title: Think like a ship: business ecosystems and human well-being
abstract: The ecosystem concept, borrowed from natural sciences, helps social scientists study organizations, economic regions, and the complex relationships between organizations and people. However, these discussions often fail to consider the normative aspects and values inherent in social systems. Meanwhile, the ecosystem services concept, developed within the natural sciences, assesses how ecological systems contribute to human well-being, enhancing their perceived, experienced, and economic value to society. title: Virtue of Care and Ethics of Virtue
abstract: There are two characteristics shared by Virtue Ethics and the Ethics of Care: a distance from deontology and consequentialism on one hand; the importance of the emotional and affective dimensions in moral discourse on the other. Nonetheless, it seems that the two theories diverge regarding the central focus of moral life: the role of the agent’s character (virtues), relationality and responsibility for others (care). title: The Expansion and Constraints of Extraterritorial Jurisdiction: From the Perspective of International Law
abstract: Against the backdrop of globalization, the extraterritorial exercise of state legal authority has shown a noticeable trend of expansion. As the concept of state authority evolves from absolute territoriality to a functional and instrumentalized framework, nations are extending their regulatory reach outward to safeguard core objectives such as national security, economic interests, and value systems. title: Closed-loop upcycling of residual lithium in LiFePO4 into tunable thin lithium metal electrodes
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. title: Book Forum on Omer Bartov's Israel: What Went Wrong?
abstract: This book forum discusses Omer Bartov’s latest book on the roots of contemporary Israeli politics. In particular, it examines Zionism and its transformation—from what Bartov presents as an initially emancipatory ideology for some of its adherents into the ethnonationalist state ideology that, in his account, underpins Israel’s genocidal policies today. The forum features three critical responses to the book, by Jakub Záhora, Pavel Barša, and Hanna Pfeifer, followed by a response from Bartov. title: Markets, Power and Social Order: Rethinking the Political Economy of Pre-colonial Igbo Land
abstract: The political economy of pre-colonial African societies cannot be understood apart from the institutions through which production, exchange, authority and social relationships were organized. Pre-colonial Igbo Land has long been characterized as a "stateless" or decentralized society, and existing interpretations of its political economy have often emphasized dispersed political organization, subsistence production, long-distance trade and the absence of centralized state structures. abstract: Objectives Cochrane South Africa (CSA) is a Cochrane geographic group established in 1997, aiming to advance the skills and awareness of evidence-based healthcare (EBHC) nationally and regionally through a comprehensive training programme. This project aimed to evaluate the training delivered by CSA from 2021 to 2022. Design We applied the Kirkpatrick model to evaluate the training offered, using a mixed-methods study design that comprised pretraining and post-training online questionnaires and interviews. title: Lionardo Salviati, Tacitism and the People of Florence
abstract: This article explores Lionardo Salviati’s Discorso sopra le prime parole di Cornelio Tacito, a brief commentary on the beginning of Tacitus’ Annales published in 1582. While it is widely recognised as one of the first examples of political commentary on the Roman historian, its content has only received scant attention. Moreover, the few interpretations that do exist all agree that Salviati presents a fairly straight-forward defence of the Medicean dynastic monarchy under which it was written. title: A Phase 2 Trial Evaluating the Immunogenicity and Safety of an mRNA-Based Seasonal Influenza Vaccine Candidate Encoding Hemagglutinin and Neuraminidase
abstract: Influenza vaccines targeting both hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) might offer broader protection than current vaccines, which primarily target HA. This randomized phase 2 study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of an investigational mRNA-based trivalent seasonal influenza vaccine encoding HA and NA from A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria (FLUm3HA-3NA). title: ‘SERIOUS, IMPORTANT, OVERCROWDED’: THE REPLICAS IN THE MINOAN ROOM AT THE 1936 BURLINGTON HOUSE EXHIBITION
abstract: In 1936, 36 years after Sir Arthur Evans first broke soil at the site of Knossos, a retrospective exhibition dedicated to 50 years of British archaeological work in Greece was staged in the Royal Academy at Burlington House in London. Evans displayed his work on the Minoans in a dedicated room, in what would be one of his final major museum exhibitions. This article examines Evans’ heavy use of replicas in his Minoan Room. title: Resource Rents And Institutional Quality: Exploring Global Corruption's Paradox
abstract: This study explores the complex relationship between natural resource rents, institutional quality, and corruption, stemming from the "natural resource curse" paradox. Employing a fixed-effects methodology with data from 175 countries, the research reveals that the interaction between natural resource rents and institutional quality significantly escalates corruption. A noteworthy finding is that while institutional quality is generally presumed to mitigate corruption, in the context of natural resource rents over the past two decades, it has paradoxically exacerbated corrupt practices. title: Construction of Evaluation Indicators for Sustainable Practices in Agricultural Microbusinesses
abstract: Global society faces the critical challenges of eradicating poverty, ensuring food security, and addressing environmental degradation. In this context, agricultural microbusinesses emerge as essential actors in productive dynamics, contributing significantly to food sovereignty and economic transformation. In Latin America, family farming supplies 53% of global food demand, accounts for 7.92% of GDP, and employs one-fifth of the economically active population. title: Law after empire
abstract: This paper examines how legal knowledge circulates in post-colonial contexts, arguing that the authority of law after empire is produced through the movement of people, institutions, and epistemic practices along old and new imperial routes. Drawing on comparative research on three regional courts, the Caribbean Court of Justice, the now-defunct Central American Court of Justice, and the East African Court of Justice, it reframes post-colonial legality not as a story of transplantation or dependency, but as a process of circulation and translation. title: Consumer Decision‐Making Styles Across Product Involvement Levels: A Mixed‐Methods Study of Online Flash Sale Events
abstract: ABSTRACT Online flash sale events create urgency, scarcity and deep‐discount conditions, yet little is known about how consumer decision‐making styles vary across product involvement levels and how they are associated with situational involvement. title: A Typological Analysis of Rural Youth Deliberative Participation and Its Generative Logic: A Case Study of D Village, H Province
abstract: Rural youth participation in deliberative consultation has the potential to revitalize grassroots good governance; however, insufficient participation remains a persistent challenge. Based on fieldwork in townships in North China, this qualitative study employs Coleman’s rational choice theory as an analytical framework. It reveals that youth’s decisions to engage in deliberative consultation are shaped by both structural factors and individual endowments. title: Voices of Displacement: Representing Sri Lankan Refugees in Media
abstract: In recent years, mass media has played a crucial role in shedding light on contemporary socio-political issues across the world. Many filmmakers address pressing social concerns through cinema, creating awareness among audiences and encouraging public discourse. Such representations often help draw attention to the problems faced by victims and vulnerable communities, thereby fostering empathy and understanding. title: La cabaña del tío Tom: análisis traductológico de una adaptación al español dirigida a un público juvenil
abstract: La obra Uncle Tom’s Cabin de Harriet Beecher Stowe es un clásico de la literatura publicado en 1852 que denuncia la situación racista que vivían las personas de color estadounidenses, quienes, por su etnia, estaban sometidas al esclavismo de la época. La relevancia de la obra fue tal que incluso se consideró uno de los detonantes de la Guerra de Secesión y, rápidamente, empezó a traducirse a cientos de idiomas, siendo uno de ellos el español. title: Effectiveness of a structured educational program on knowledge about medication errors and stress of conscience among psychiatric nurses
abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication errors are a persistent threat to patient safety in psychiatric settings, where complex pharmacotherapy and ethical conscience heighten nurses' stress of conscience. AIM: This study evaluated the effectiveness of a structured educational program on knowledge about medication errors and stress of conscience among psychiatric nurses. METHODS: A one-group pre-post quasi-experimental design was implemented with 89 nurses from Assiut University Psychiatric Hospital and at Assiut Mental Health Hospital (Ministry of Health hospital), Egypt. title: Assessing Extension Workers’ Opinions on Participatory Training in Sudan
abstract: This study examined the opinions of extension workers on participatory training in the Sudanese states of Gezira, Sinnar, and Gedarif. Data were collected from a sample of 205 extension workers using structured questionnaires, supported by secondary sources. The results show that the availability of training opportunities for extension workers was limited, and more frequent training sessions were required. title: Cultured Mining Governance in the Perspective of Siyasah Dusturiyah: Evidence from Sand Mining in Boyolali Regency
abstract: Mining activities in Boyolali Regency provide economic benefits but also generate socio-environmental and governance challenges. This study examines sand and rock mining governance through the perspective of Siyasah Dusturiyah and proposes a governance model based on prophetic values. Using a socio-legal approach, the study analyzes mining practices in Cepogo, Musuk, and Selo District through field findings, legal analysis, and environmental data. title: Ambition without alignment: Pollinators in the EU Nature Restoration Law
abstract: Abstract Pollinators are essential for life on Earth. They enable the reproduction of most flowering plants and support biodiversity as well as food systems. However, their numbers are in great decline. Research finds a continuing decrease in pollinating insects each year. This article reviews whether EU Law is fit to address this challenge. First, this paper analyses the norms in the EU Nature Restoration Law (NRL) and the Delegated Regulation, finding that the NRL demands wide‐scale system change to comply with the targets set out. title: Revisión y discusión del conocimiento de la Garza Cucharona (Cochlearius cochlearius) en Argentina
abstract: En Argentina, la Garza Cucharona (Cochlearius cochlearius) ha sido históricamente considerada una especie ocasional o extremadamente rara. A partir de una recopilación de información y de consultas a personas, confirmamos su nidificación en tres provincias del nordeste del país: Formosa, Chaco y Misiones. title: The conditions for digital integration: A comparative case study of three TVET colleges in KwaZulu-Natal
abstract: Digital technology has spread unevenly through South Africa’s public technical and vocational education and training (TVET) colleges. This article examines what determines whether the technology available to a college becomes part of everyday teaching. It reports on a comparative study of three public TVET colleges in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN), ranging from a well-connected urban college to a dispersed rural college, drawing on interviews with managers, institutional documents and three complementary theoretical perspectives. title: Sugarcane farming practices and household income levels nexus: A case of Ndhiwa Sub-County, Homa Bay County, Kenya
abstract: Sugarcane farming is the main economic activity in Ndhiwa sub County. While the activity remains an important source of rural livelihoods, there is limited research with regards to the contribution of sugarcane farming to household income. While its contribution to rural incomes is significant, limited empirical evidence exists on how different dimensions of sugarcane production including land allocation, farming practices, labor structures, payment systems, and value chain participation affect household income. title: Rilvegostomig Plus Trastuzumab-Deruxtecan for Early-Stage Breast Cancer

abstract: Federalism has long been celebrated for its ability to foster policy innovation, transforming states into “laboratories of democracy.” Yet, federalism discourse has largely neglected Indian tribes, the third sovereign in the American constitutional order. Tribes regularly implement novel policies. However, tribal policy innovation is hindered by uncertainty over whether tribes or states govern Indian country activities. abstract: The origin and evolution of land plants precipitated fundamental changes to the Earth system and enabled the diversification of life on land. abstract: Abstract This article reviews the life and contributions of Ernest S. Keeping (1895–1984), a British‐born physicist who became a mathematics professor at the University of Alberta in 1929. He played a pivotal role in shaping the university's Mathematics Department, serving as its head from 1954 to 1961, and continuing to teach until 1970, nine years after his official retirement. title: Blue-eyed bargains: Nazi-era acquisitions at the museum of far eastern antiquities in Sweden
abstract: This article examines the provenance of cultural objects acquired by the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities in Stockholm during the National Socialist era. Taking the 1937 acquisition of two Chinese bronze tripods from Josef Plaut as its point of departure, the study investigates the circumstances of the sale in relation to the Washington Principles and the Terezín Declaration. The analysis subsequently expands to the museum’s acquisition practices between 1933 and 1938. This process identifies a further case involving the 1934 acquisition of books and journals from the scholar Alfred Salmony.

abstract: Human-bear interactions with Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus) are increasing in Japan. abstract: Abstract This article presents two interconnected arguments. First, a method other than the doctrinal method is needed to study EU constitutional law. Using the ruling in Commission v Hungary as the central example, the article demonstrates that EU constitutional law is not just legal but also political in nature. Following Martin Loughlin, the article therefore argues that the method of EU constitutional law is ‘the method of prudence’. title: Does power-sharing facilitate memory-sharing? Bosnian Croat narratives in post-war Bosnia and Herzegovina
abstract: This study examines how Bosnian Croat wartime narratives intersect with perspectives on post-war power-sharing in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Drawing on media, NGO reports and semi-elite interviews, it shows that despite shared wartime narratives, particularly those depicting Serbs as aggressors, competition within the consociational system has led to narrative divergence between Bosnian Croats and Bosniaks. abstract: The production of cultured meat is gaining regulatory approval in countries worldwide, with the global market being estimated to grow substantially over the next few years. However, its recognition as an effective technology in tackling issues concerning human health, the environment, and animal welfare has been received with mixed feelings across different countries. abstract: El presente artículo versa sobre el escritor inglés John Gay, considerado en su país como uno de los mejores poetas burlescos y satíricos de su época; más concretamente de su obra The Fables, que consta de sesenta y ocho fábulas: cincuenta publicadas en 1727, a las que se añadieron dieciocho en 1738. abstract: Abstract Tropical landscapes are largely shaped by the daily decisions of smallholder farmers. Public institutions and private companies increasingly aim to shape agricultural landscapes by influencing farmer decisions. Farmer land-use decision-making is complex and highly dynamic, especially in tropical smallholder systems. title: Strengthening the Paris Agreement Through Collective Decisions: Achievements and Limitations
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its bottom‐up architecture, the Paris Agreement succeeded in securing broad participation but remained vulnerable to challenges concerning both the adequacy of national mitigation commitments and their implementation. This paper assesses the extent to which Parties to the Paris Agreement have succeeded in ensuring the effective functioning of the Paris framework through their collective decisions. It analyses two dimensions: the operationalisation of the Paris mechanisms and rules and the coordination of national efforts in the areas of mitigation pathways and climate finance.

title: When and How Do Women Directors Matter for Corporate Sustainability? The French Case
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines when and how board gender diversity matters for corporate sustainability. Using a sample of French listed firms over 2006–2024, we combine dynamic system GMM estimations with difference‐in‐differences tests around France's phased board gender quotas. The results show that greater female board representation is associated with stronger ESG performance, but that this relationship is highly contingent. title: A Paired RGB-Sonar Dataset for Fish Monitoring with Consumer Sonar
abstract: Imaging sonar enables underwater observation in conditions where optical imaging is ineffective due to darkness and turbid water. However, imaging-sonar systems previously used for ecological monitoring have typically been expensive, limiting their accessibility. Consumer forward-looking sonar has the potential to make fish monitoring more accessible, but its noisy imagery makes annotation and the development of automated methods challenging. title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
abstract: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. The total number of dipoles in the set of Fermi seas forming the two-dimensional ground state equals the number of electrons in the system and the density of states at the Fermi level is that of a two-dimensional Fermi gas. title: Disjoint in Name Only: Illusory Resilience in the Internet
abstract: Internet path diversity is usually verified at the logical layer: two alternatives may share no AS or IP link yet traverse the same facility, conduit, or submarine landing zone. We call this gap illusory resilience and define the Illusory Resilience Index (IRI) as the latent hazard-weighted physical overlap of a logically disjoint path pair. To detect such hidden exposure without carrier underlay maps, we audit three public signals: correlated BGP withdrawals during documented physical incidents, operator interconnection-footprint overlap, and shared submarine landing zones. title: The World as Viewed by 136 Countries: An Open, Curated, Annotated, and Multilingual Dataset of 118 Million State Media Articles
abstract: State media outlets often project their governments' narratives to target both domestic and foreign audiences. Because this content is plentiful and free to access, it appears widely in the web corpora that large language models (LLMs) are trained on and that retrieval systems draw from. However, the prevalence of state media in these corpora and its potential influence on LLM outputs remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce WorldStateMedia, an open dataset of 118 million state media articles from 136 countries in 114 languages. We extract these articles from existing pretraining

title: BiNar: Bitstream Native Restorer for Bitstream-corrupted Image Restoration
abstract: Bitstream-corrupted image restoration (BCIR) aims to reconstruct faithful images from corrupted compressed bitstreams. However, corruption occurs in bitstream-domain may lead to unpredictable error propagation and distortion amplification in pixel-domain, and even result in complete undecodability by standard decoders, posing significant challenge to existing image restoration paradigms. To address this challenge, we propose Bitstream Native Restorer (BiNar), a generative restoration framework that leverages fine-grained bitstream-native semantics to guide bitstream-corrupted image restoration

title: CT25: the new generation of CTEQ-TEA PDFs
abstract: This contribution reviews CT25, a new generation of CTEQ--TEA parton distribution functions (PDFs) for precision QCD. With its first member sets released in 2025, the CT25 family addresses common uses of parton distributions in diverse contexts. We describe the CTEQ--TEA Parton Cloud, an online database of exploratory global fits to precision QCD measurements, from which we select PDF solutions for general- and special-purpose calculations. title: Linear Twisting Sidewinding Gaits for Twistable Snake Robot Motion Planning on Complex Terrains
abstract: Sidewinding is an efficient gait for snake robots to locomote on various terrains, by undulating the backbone curve and shifting the contact segments along it. However, relying solely on undulatory motion limits the locomotive capability of snake robots, and combining it with twisting motion can improve their speed and robustness. This hypothesis has recently been verified by the rolling vector approach, which locomotes the robot like a differential-drive car. abstract: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. title: Can LLM Agents Resolve Service Failures? Simulating Multi-Turn Complaint Handling under Information Asymmetry
abstract: LLM agents are widely adopted in service chatbots for rule-guided support and information access, yet emotionally demanding complaint handling still relies heavily on human agents. We introduce ServiceBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark dedicated to complaint handling, with 2,500 scenarios spanning 184 complaint categories and five service industries. We propose Asymmetric Progressive Complaint Simulation (APCS) to simulate realistic complaint handling, together with a justice-based evaluation framework. title: Eurasian Basin Transect 2026 Cruise Report
abstract: The Eurasian Basin Transect 2026 cruise (EBT2026; ID 2026007011) was conducted 23 July–10 September 2026. title: Deep-water Pycnogonids (Arthropoda, Pycnogonida) from the Indian Ocean Territories, north-western Australia collected by RV Investigator expeditions to the Australian Christmas Island and Cocos (Keeling) Islands Territories
abstract: Six species of Pycnogonida belonging to five genera were collected by CSIRO research vessel RV Investigator expeditions to the Australian Christmas Island and Cocos (Keeling) Islands territories to the north-west of the Australian mainland. The small collection consists of four species new to science, one known deep-water species and one subadult form that remains unidentified. Specimens were gathered from the seafloor using sleds and nets at depths ranging from 328 m to 2435 m.

abstract: Historically, Pachycheles sculptus was considered a widely distributed species in Chinese waters with significant morphological plasticity. abstract: During 2013 (Gulf of Aqaba) and 2020/2022 (Oman), extensive sampling efforts were conducted, covering two areas of the northwestern Indian ocean. In these expeditions numerous specimens of squat lobsters belonging to the genus Galathea (Galatheidae) were collected. The study of these specimens integrating molecular and morphological data revealed the presence of five new species. Here, we describe and illustrate these new species. Molecular data from mitochondrial and nuclear markers were also included to support the taxonomic status of the species.

title: Historic diversity of pelagic copepods across the Arabian Gulf
abstract: The Arabian Gulf (hereafter “Gulf”) is a young ocean basin noted for its low biodiversity for many marine organisms. Natural and anthropogenic factors, such as shallow depth, high water temperatures, high salinity, and rapid urbanization and industrialization of coastal areas, are considered as stressors on biodiversity of the Gulf. It is important to investigate the broader distributional patterns of key organisms in the basin to understand how those communities might change over time. Shallow magma storage and degassing at Brothers volcano, Kermadec arc: implications for submarine hydrothermal processes and seafloor mineralisation
abstract: Magmas degas volatiles and metals into submarine arc-related hydrothermal systems, but the nature of this process and its role in seafloor massive sulfide (SMS) mineralisation are poorly understood, particularly in submarine arcs hosting Cu–Au-rich deposits. To address this, we studied glassy melt inclusions (MIs) and matrix glasses from Brothers submarine volcano in the Kermadec arc, where there is strong evidence for magmatic involvement in hydrothermal processes and Cu-Au-rich mineralisation. title: Resources of mesopelagic fish in the Far Eastern Seas and adjacent Pacific waters of Russia: untapped potential for domestic fisheries
abstract: Based on the authors’ personal experience, archival data, and literature sources, a brief overview for status of the mesopelagic fish stocks in the Far Eastern Seas of Russia and adjacent waters of the Pacific Ocean is presented. Unexploited biomass of the midwater species, as a biotopic group, amounts to 50[.] 10[6] to 80[.] 10[6] t that constitutes a substantial resource base for the national fishing industry. title: Performance of Acropora species on the Great Barrier Reef's first coral tree nursery
abstract: Abstract Introduction The worldwide decline of coral reefs has led to the proliferation of local‐scale coral restoration projects. Active restoration using in‐water coral tree nurseries and outplanting of coral fragments is relatively new on the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) and complements traditional, passive approaches to reef protection. However, given the infancy of these methods, few studies have measured the effectiveness of coral restoration techniques, including coral nursery systems. Life at the edge: Planktic foraminiferal distribution through the California Current Oxygen Minimum Zone
abstract: Abstract Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs) are expanding globally, reshaping marine ecosystems, and creating physiologically challenging conditions for many marine organisms. Vulnerable communities will likely shift toward taxa adapted to low-oxygen conditions. Such adaptations are rare in eukaryotes, but some foraminiferal taxa can survive, and even calcify, in severely oxygen-depleted environments. abstract: Background. Imut Jongor Beach in Mundu District, Cirebon Regency, is a marine tourism destination that is still in the development stage and has great potential to support the growth of community-based tourism. However, the management of this destination still faces various limitations, especially in terms of facilities, institutions, and the development of tourist attractions. Purpose. title: Intelligent Cruise Cabin Layout Design based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This study focuses on the layout optimization of passenger spaces on cruise ships and proposes a reinforcement learning-based method for compartment arrangement in digital ship design. Traditional layout planning relies mainly on manual experience and repeated adjustments, making it difficult to respond efficiently to changes in deck boundaries, structural conditions, and functional requirements. title: Onshore Power Supply Readiness in Adriatic–Ionian Ports: A Multiple-Case Assessment and Typology for Marine Spatial Planning and Port Governance
abstract: The onshore power supply (OPS) eliminates ship emissions at berth, yet feasibility is site-specific, and most evidence concerns large Northern European and Asian ports. This multiple-case study assesses OPS readiness at six ports of the Adriatic–Ionian macro-region (Ancona, Ploče, Durrës, Volos, the river port of Belgrade, and the lake port of Ohrid) covering ferry, cruise, cargo, and tourism in the European Union (EU) and non-EU jurisdictions. title: A New Species of Damselfish (Teleostei: Pomacentridae: Pomacentrus) from Madagascar, with an Updated Phylogeny for the Species-Rich Genus Pomacentrus
abstract: Herein we present a phylogenetic analysis of the species-rich pomacentrid genus Pomacentrus, based on the analysis of sequence data from eight nuclear and mitochondrial loci, and describe a new species from inshore reef habitats in Madagascar. Pomacentrus maintivombona, new species, is described based primarily on specimens collected during an expedition to survey marine fishes on shallow fringing reefs and rocky habitats spanning the Masoala Peninsula in northeastern Madagascar. abstract: Set in 1847 during the peak of the North Atlantic whaling industry, The Leviathan's Reckoning presents a poignant narrative of human greed, moral tension, and nature's retribution. Driven by an insatiable hunger for whale oil profit, Captain Fred Winston of the brig Sea Serpent ignores an elderly fisherman's stern warnings regarding the cursed waters of Death Valley, going so far as ordering the innocent man's demise to protect his commercial interests. title: Morphological description of Nauplius stages I and III, and Protozoea from stages I to III of Metapenaeus stebbingi Nobili, 1904 (Crustacea, Decapoda, Penaeidae)
abstract: Metapenaeus stebbingi Nobili, 1904 is an Indo-Pacific shrimp species. Larvae of M. stebbingi were obtained from eggs that hatched four days after spawning from gravid females captured from incidental fishery. The naupliar and protozoeal phases were reared for six days under controlled laboratory conditions at a room temperature of 30 °C, with seawater maintained at 29 °C, a salinity of 37‰, and pH 7.9. title: MARITIME ECONOMIC GOVERNANCE UNDER THE NGUYEN DYNASTY, VIETNAM: FROM TRADE SECURITY TO MARINE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT
abstract: This article examines the mechanisms employed by the Nguyen Dynasty to regulate and protect maritime economic activities between 1802 and 1858, focusing on two principal areas: maritime trade security and marine resource management. title: Species of the genus Gibberula Swainson, 1840 (Gastropoda: Cystiscidae) from Namibia
abstract: The marine gastropod fauna off Namibia (SW Africa) has hardly been explored. The current study on species of the genus Gibberula Swainson, 1840 is part of an inventory of marine gastropods from Namibia. Four species are described as new, all endemic to Namibia: Gibberula oshishani sp. nov., G. evukule sp. nov., G. ehodhi sp. nov., and G. heyali sp. nov. One additional species was also known from South Africa: G. cf. bensoni (Reeve, 1865). None of the species known from Angola was found in Namibia. title: Sandy Turbidity Current Acts as a Rusty Carbon Pump at the Shelf Edge
abstract: Abstract Sandy turbidity currents (STCs) efficiently sequester organic carbon (OC) through rapid burial. Yet our understanding of OC preservation within STC deposits remains far less constrained, especially considering STC deposits as an inferred major sink for iron‐bound OC (Fe‐OC), a long‐term stabilized form of OC. Dynamic UAV-based search operations using probabilistic diffusion modeling of Man Overboard incident victims
abstract: More than 70% of the people that fell overboard cruise ships in the period 2010–2019 lost their lives (CLIA, 2025) . This paper presents a strategy for reliably predicting the area a person may be in after a man overboard incident, and describes in detail the search methods to find them utilizing UAV technology. abstract: This paper presents a benchmark study of linear wave-induced motions and global loads, organised by the MARSTRUCT Virtual Institute with the objective of quantifying the hydrodynamic modelling uncertainty and its consequences for extreme load prediction across different hull forms. This is a follow-up to a benchmark study Parunov et al. title: New records and new species of Amphipoda (Crustacea) collected in the South-West of French Atlantic Coast
abstract: Exploration of mainly circalittoral rocky habitats in the South-West of the French Atlantic coast during the CIRCATAX project revealed four new species and five new records of amphipods. Lepidepecreum antennatum sp. nov., Iphimedia jeanneae sp. nov., Hornellia (Metaceradocus) serrata sp. nov. and Gammaropsis sorbei sp. nov. are herein described. Hornellia (Metaceradocus) serrata represents the first record of the Hornellidae family in European waters. title: Bioprospecting perchlorate-reducing bacteria: report of the genera Psychrobacter, Planococcus, Carnobacterium, and Paeniglutamicibacter isolated in Cierva Point, Antarctica, and its contribution to SDG 3
abstract: Abstract Perchlorate (ClO 4 − ) is a global contaminant that has been detected in various environmental matrices. ClO 4 − is considered an emerging pollutant because of its potent endocrine-disrupting effects, which impairs iodine uptake in the thyroid gland, and its high toxicity and persistence. Therefore, the development of technologies for its reduction in ecosystems is imperative; bioremediation is a promising technology for ClO 4 − reduction. title: Stone to Lead: The Anchor from the Dor L2 Cargo and the Chronology of Composite Anchors from the 7th‒4th Centuries BCE
abstract: Abstract A wood and lead anchor stock found in underwater excavations at the Dor Lagoon belongs to a cargo of amphorae and iron blooms, designated as the Dor L2 site, dated to the late 7th‒early 6th centuries Before Current Era (BCE). This anchor is contemporary with the earliest composite wooden anchors found in the Mediterranean, such as those from Mazarrón 2 and Karaburun. This article provides detailed typological and technological analyses of the anchor stock from Dor, as well as further insights stemming from a reevaluation of the chrono-typology of composite anchors in the Mediterranean

title: New Ocinaropsis from West Africa (Lepidoptera, Lasiocampidae)
abstract: The second species of the African genus Ocinaropsis Aurivillius, 1905, Ocinaropsis tinubu sp. n., is described from West Africa. It occurs in the West Sudanian savanna ecoregion, spanning from eastern Senegal to northern Ghana, and the Guinean forest-savanna ecoregion in northern Nigeria. The type species of the genus, Ocinaropsis obscura Aurivillius, 1905, is reportedly found in the KwaZulu-Natal–Cape coastal forests ecoregion in South Africa and the Maputaland coastal forests and woodlands ecoregion in southern Mozambique, over 4500 km away from the new species. abstract: Abstract This article recentres East Africa in the global history of cowrie shells by tracing the trajectories of Monetaria annulus —the East African cowrie species—across interconnected monetary arenas in the nineteenth century. Situating African monetary history within transoceanic processes, it argues that the ‘great cowrie inflation’ in West Africa was closely tied to the reorganization of procurement networks, labour regimes, and commercial infrastructures in the Western Indian Ocean. title: Moving-Window Weighted Least Squares with Edge Optimization for Schuler Oscillation Suppression in Inertial Navigation Systems
abstract: To address the reliance of damping-network-based Schuler oscillation suppression on external aids in pure inertial navigation systems, as well as the edge effects and low computational efficiency of time–frequency transform methods, this paper proposes a moving-window weighted least-squares edge optimization (MWLS-EO) algorithm. title: Locomotion and hunting strategies of large vertebrate predators in pelagic waters
abstract: Many of the key dynamics that shape predator-prey interactions are governed by the physical and physiological principles which determine how animals move and perform in their environments. This opinion paper outlines the foundations underlying marine vertebrate predator-prey encounters within the context of pelagic habitats. Variables, such as maximum swimming speed, acceleration and manoeuvrability, play crucial roles in dictating the outcome of predator-prey encounters. title: Physics-anchored residual learning for ship fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emission prediction
abstract: Predicting the fuel, and hence the energy, that a ship needs under given operating and environmental conditions underpins voyage optimisation, performance monitoring and regulatory emission accounting. Resistance-based models are transparent but inaccurate in service; black-box learners fit the training distribution but extrapolate poorly and offer no physical insight. abstract: Abstract Background The purpose of this paper is to examine the scale and importance of Indigenous cultural burning in precolonial times on the Central California Coast. We begin by reviewing recent advances that help us understand past human–environment interactions and facilitate the detection of ancient cultural burning by Tribes in Western North America. abstract: The aim of present study is to investigate the attitudes and behaviors of university students in Northern Greece regarding their vacations in Greece in the summer of 2024. Their vacations concerned water sports tourism summer destination; the product "sun and sea", examining their experiences in Greece, through the evaluation of the quality of services offered by tourist destinations, the Environmental Sustainability of the tourist destination and how these factors influence the future intentions of the respondents for repurchase. Multiyear dual-isotope fingerprinting at South Asian receptor sites constrains carbon monoxide sources and enhanced oxidation
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is an indirect short-lived climate forcer with uncertainties both in sources and its role in atmospheric oxidation. Based on nine winter-long dual-isotope campaigns at two South Asian receptor sites intercepting the continental outflow, we quantified CO source contributions and emission–sink dynamics. title: Beyond the Ship: A 4M Framework Analysis of Safety Risks and Tour Guide Preparedness in Shore Excursion
abstract: Safety incidents during shore excursions can disrupt cruise itineraries and threaten tourist well-being. This study examines incident-related factors and tour guide preparedness at Company A, a destination management company operating in Bali. A qualitative descriptive design combined content analysis of 45 incident reports from 2025 with semi-structured interviews with 12 purposively selected guides who had handled or witnessed incidents. title: Evaluating changes in China’s Grand Canal’s cultural landscape over the past 20 years based on collective memory: The Yangzhou section as an example
abstract: The Grand Canal of China is a giant linear cultural heritage. Within its protected area, in addition to the registered heritage sites, there are a large number of everyday cultural landscapes closely related to residents’ daily lives. Over the past two decades, with the continuous advancement of spatial development, conservation, and utilization along the Grand Canal, these cultural landscapes within the protected area have undergone various changes. abstract: This study presents an integrated hydrodynamic-structural analysis of a Tension-Leg Platform (TLP) Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT) using an ANSYS AQWA–Static Structural workflow. title: Cosmetic powder of 2000-years old Jetyasar culture. A complex analytical study
abstract: Jetyasar was a significant archaeological culture in the Eastern Aral Sea region, flourishing from the late 1st millennium BC to the 8th century AD. Highly likely it appeared as a result of contacts of oasis agriculturists and steppe nomads. Here, we report the first results of an analytic examination of chalk pieces from excavations of two female burials of the 2nd–4th centuries AD from the Eastern Aral region (Kazakhstan). title: Biostratigraphy of the Famennian Makarovian Regional Substage (Devonian, South Urals)
abstract: The paper presents a bed-by-bed description and paleontological characteristics of the carbonate deposits within the stratotype area of the Makarovian Regional Substage (Famennian), including Cheiloceras ammonoid and Zilimia polonica brachiopod beds. The authors have studied two sections located along the Sikasya and Ryauzyak river valleys on the western slope of the South Urals. In the stratotype area, the Makarovian is composed entirely of polymictic bioclastic limestone. The rocks contain a diverse assemblage of fossils, primarily comprising brachiopod, ammonoid, foraminifera, and ostracod

title: Exploring supply chain management challenges in food provisioning on maritime training vessels: post-consumer food waste and the potential role of digitalisation
abstract: Achieving sustainable consumption at sea requires understanding the organisational mechanisms that shape food provisioning under uncertainty. Using a mixed-methods case study of a maritime training vessel, this study combines semi-structured interviews with key provisioning stakeholders and an exploratory survey of student–cadets to examine the organisational mechanisms generating plate waste and the potential contribution of digitalisation to more sustainable provisioning. title: Features of walleye pollock eggs distribution off the southern Kuril Islands
abstract: Spatial distribution of walleye pollock eggs at the southern Kuril Islands is analyzed and the patterns are classified on the data of ichthyoplankton surveys conducted from 2000 to 2022. title: Molecular and morphological identification of yellow tonguefish ( Symphurus williamsi ) and darkcheek tonguefish ( Symphurus chabanaudi ) at the southern and entrance to the Gulf of California
abstract: The genus Symphurus is a group of demersal fish with high diversity and taxonomic challenges during their early development. This study addressed the morphological and molecular identification of Symphurus larvae in La Bahía de la Paz and the entrance to the Gulf of California. Zooplankton samples were collected during the day and night at 58 stations in October 2022. title: Clave actualizada para la identificación de los Syllidae (Annelida) del área íbero-balear
abstract: Tras 23 años de su publicación, la monografía sobre la familia Syllidae (Annelida) de la serie de Fauna Ibérica, ha quedado anticuada en lo referente al número de especies y a la nomenclatura, ya que se han encontrado más especies en el ámbito de la península Ibérica y Baleares y ha habido numerosos cambios en su sistemática. title: European Exploration Innovations: The Role of Afro-Asian Technology and Ideas in European Exploration, 1400–1700
abstract: This paper revisits the formation of the European Age of Exploration by re-examining the claim of an “independent Western breakthrough.” Taking European overseas expansion from 1400 to 1700 as its main thread, the paper argues that Europe’s maritime capabilities did not emerge out of nowhere, but gradually developed through the absorption of mathematical knowledge, astronomical observations, navigational instruments, shipbuilding experience, and gunpowder technologies from Asia and Africa. title: Fracture and Calving Front Evolution: A Case Study of Fimbul Ice Shelf, Antarctica
abstract: ABSTRACT This study combines historical records, satellite remote sensing data, and inverse modelling to investigate crack formation and calving front evolution of the Fimbul Ice Shelf, Antarctica. title: The Effect of Maritime Safety Training and the Availability of Safety Equipment on Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and the Performance of Evergreen Container Ship Crews at Tanjung Emas Port, Semarang
abstract: This study examines the effects of maritime safety training and the availability of safety equipment on occupational health and safety (OHS) and ship crew performance aboard Evergreen container ships at Tanjung Emas Port, Semarang. A quantitative, descriptive-associative approach was employed using multiple regression and correlation analyses to assess the relationships among the research variables. title: Phinisi as Living Maritime Heritage: Integration of Cultural Preservation and Sustainable Tourism in Tana Beru, South Sulawesi
abstract: Phinisi is a traditional sailing vessel and a living maritime heritage associated with the boatbuilding communities of South Sulawesi, Indonesia. Its growing use in tourism creates opportunities to communicate maritime knowledge and support livelihoods, while also raising questions about cultural authenticity, community participation, and the continuity of traditional skills. This qualitative case study examines how Phinisi is maintained as living heritage and how its use in tourism intersects with cultural preservation and sustainable tourism in Tana Beru. title: Evaluation of Seed Viability and Quality for Santigi (Pemphis acidula J.R. Forst and G. Forst) Conservation: Assessing the Effect of Chemical and Physical Scarification
abstract: Pemphis acidula J.R.Forst. and G. Forst. or santigi is a plant native to Indonesia, widely recognized for its high economic value. Although listed as Least Concern by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), its existence in the wild is increasingly threatened by land degradation, climate change, and it suffers from low natural seed germination rates. This study aimed to evaluate the seed viability and quality of P. acidula and assess the effectiveness of chemical and physical scarification techniques on the viability of santigi seeds. title: From Colonial to Educational: Dialogic Imagination of Matthew 28:19-20 and the Story of Apapuhang in Sangihe
abstract: This article addresses the issue of how the Christian mission in Indonesia is understood, specifically, the tendency to equate the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20) with "Christianization". This perception is linked to a colonial legacy that has shaped biblical interpretation and potentially hinders religious moderation and interfaith peace. The study aims to reinterpret Matthew 28:19-20 from the perspective of the Sangihe people by engaging in a dialogue with the “Apapuhang” folktale. title: Management Can Make Shark Fisheries Sustainable: Evidence From Long‐Term Surveys
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable management of shark fisheries is challenging because sharks are highly vulnerable to fishing mortality. By analysing data from three independent scientific surveys between the early 1970s and late 2000s across three fishing regions in southern Australia, we show that conservative fisheries management following severe depletion facilitated full stock recovery of the gummy shark ( Mustelus antarcticus ), a species of moderate biological productivity. title: Analytical Review of Natural Hydrogen Sources and Occurrence for Sustainable Hydrogen Future in Indonesia
abstract: One transformative, inexpensive (~$0.5-1/kg), and low-carbon energy source is natural hydrogen produced by serpentinization and other geochemical processes. Global data on its accumulation, migration, and geological mechanisms have been collected in the present study. Temperature, pressure, and mineralogy all affect the rate at which hydrogen is generated. title: Human Plunder: Slaving Raids, Economic Warfare, and Mercantilism in the French Caribbean, 1665-1713
abstract: Abstract Between 1665 and 1713, at a time of almost perpetual warfare in Europe, privateers frequently assaulted and seized enslaved people from rival colonies all over the Caribbean. Following mercantilistic principles, the French in particular sought to increase the labour force in their colonies while undermining their enemies’ plantation economies. Of the about 14,000 to 16,000 slaves captured in inter-colonial raids, more than 10,000 were forcibly taken to French colonies. These raids not only came at a high human cost but also led to shifting economic fortunes in the Caribbean.

title: The Phantom Naturalist: What do we know about the nineteenth-century natural history collector Alfred Crossley?
abstract: Born in Halifax, UK, in 1839, and shipwrecked on Madagascar as a youth, Alfred Crossley had returned to the island by 1869 and in the ensuing eight years made hugely important collections of mammals, birds, butterflies, and other natural history specimens. Many of these are now in major museums in the UK and Europe (including numerous holotypes), but unknown quantities went to private collectors and are now lost. Unfortunately, Crossley’s original documentation has also disappeared; and apart from his collections themselves he left few traces of his journeyings, which included Cameroon and Mau

title: Origami‐Inspired Morphing Fuselage for Agile Fixed‐Wing Flight
abstract: Body morphing is widely used in nature for agile locomotion; yet, despite significant interest in morphing wings, aerial robotics has not explored a morphing fuselage to control flight. Current winged aerial robots rely on complex control systems with multiple control surfaces, yet cannot adapt their body shape. title: Ruth Stephan’s Andean Journey: The Peña Pancho Fierro and Transnational Indigenism in The Tiger’s Eye Magazine
abstract: In 1946, shortly after World War II, U.S. poet Ruth Stephan travelled to Peru seeking artistic direction. In Lima, she joined the indigenist avant-garde of the Peña Pancho Fierro, led by Alicia and Celia Bustamante and José María Arguedas. This encounter reshaped her understanding of indigenous culture and informed her little magazine The Tiger’s Eye (1947– 1949), which placed pre-Columbian and contemporary indigenous art alongside Abstract Expressionism and Surrealism. journal: Mistral | Journal of Latin American Women s Intellectual & Cultural History

title: Rediscovery of Sphagnum perichaetiale and S. trinitense (Sphagnaceae) in Puerto Rico
abstract: Two Sphagnum species thought to be extinct in Puerto Rico were rediscovered. The current distribution range of these species is substantially reduced compared to the historical distribution based on herbarium records. We contribute notes on S. perichaetiale and S. trinitense distribution, habitat, and a checklist of associated plant species. A key to the three extant Sphagnum species found in Puerto Rico is presented along with suggestions for conservation efforts to preserve S. perichaetiale and S. trinitense. title: ECOCRITICAL AND ECOTOURISM ANALYSIS OF EBIET SONGS
abstract: This study examines the ecocritical dimension and the potential of ecotourism in the lyrics of Ebiet G. Ade, an Indonesian musician known for his sensitivity to humanitarian and environmental issues. Using an ecocritical approach, this study aims to explore how Ebiet's songs represent the ecological crisis, the relationship between humans and nature, and spiritual reflections on natural disasters that occur in Indonesia. Furthermore, ecotourism values such as environmental conservation, local wisdom, and community education are also identified in the messages of his lyrics. Data were collected

title: Natural resource management strategies of nature-based tourism firms
abstract: This study examines how dependence on natural resources and ecosystem services shapes the strategic behaviour of nature-based tourism firms operating in changing environments alongside competing land uses. The study draws on resource-based theory, the natural resource–based view, and the natural resource dependence perspective. It uses semi-structured interviews with 25 micro and small firms in two UNESCO biosphere reserves in Finland to identify a classification of socio-ecological uncertainties differentiated by geographic scale and firm controllability and six strategic approaches organised

title: The social life of viruses: a queer sort of science
abstract: A burgeoning microbiology field, sociovirology is the study of how viruses interact with one another and the effects such interactions have on social evolution. Challenging dominant narratives that viruses are individualistic pathogens, sociovirologists explore the social interaction of viruses through the language of cooperation, altruism, and cheating, social concepts with biological definitions. Viruses cannot self-replicate-they must rely on living cells to reproduce-and thus are commonly believed to be biologically nonliving. By focusing on virus-virus interaction and evolution, socioviro
journal: History & Philosophy of the Life Sciences

title: Human and climate-environment interactions in Pyrenean landscapes: a Lateglacial-Holocene multiproxy reconstruction
abstract: Abstract. Mountain ecosystems present a complex challenge in disentangling the drivers of their long-term transformation. The subalpine belt of the Pyrenees, once forested, is now characterised by a mosaic of forest patches and open landscapes, and represents a key region in herding practices. However, the relative contributions of climate and human activity in driving its change remain intensely contested. title: The World of Action: On the Aesthetic Style of Moby-Dick and Melville’s Anxiety of Modernity
abstract: With its unique ''anti-form'' aesthetic style, Moby-Dick constructs ''the world of action.'' This literary phenomenon is manifested not only in the novel’s integration and innovation of diverse genres—scientific knowledge, drama, opera, political critique, and philosophical essay—but also in its demonstration of Melville’s profound reflection on the pursuit of certainty through an argument for abundance. The formation of this aesthetic style is rooted in multiple anxieties embedded in the modernization of nineteenth-century America dominated by ''action'': interpretive anxiety in confrontation
journal: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences

title: Digging Market Garden: Wellbeing Impacts on Military Volunteers of Participation in Archaeological Excavations Commemorating the Eightieth Anniversary of the Battle of Arnhem
abstract: This article focuses on the social outcomes of archaeological fieldwork. It describes fieldwork conducted as part of Digging Market Garden (DMG), a project exploring the material traces associated with preparations in South Lincolnshire for Operation Market Garden during World War II. The fieldwork took place in 2024 at Fulbeck Manor. Fieldwork volunteers were serving and veteran armed forces personnel and their families. DMG worked closely with two charities that support trauma recovery and mental well-being amongst these groups through archaeology, Wings to the Past and Operation Nightingale

title: Optimal growth temperature is not an adequate proxy of microbial cold adaptation
abstract: Abstract Microbial thermal adaptation is commonly characterized using the minimum (Tmin), optimum (Topt), and maximum (Tmax) temperatures that define the thermal growth range of microorganisms; with Topt been frequently used to compare microbial thermal characteristics. Although previous studies have shown that Tmin and Topt reflect distinct aspects of microbial thermal physiology, the generality and quantitative limits of this relationship across microbial diversity have not been systematically evaluated. title: Castles in the Air: Sectarian Puritanism, the Revolutionary Caribbean and the Forgotten Colony of New Warwick, Trinidad
abstract: Abstract This article examines an overlooked attempt to colonize the island of Trinidad during the English Revolution of the 1640s. This project was engineered by a consortium of radical puritans, seeking to create a protected enclave in the New World for separatists, anabaptists and other sectaries. ‘New Warwick’, as the colony was called, quickly collapsed, but reconstructing the Trinidad enterprise allows for the examination of important developments in the history of the English Atlantic, including the rise of religious divisions in parliament's civil‐war armies; the interplay between the

title: The Elateridae (coleoptera: Polyphaga: Elateroidea) of the Indian Subcontinent: Zoogeography, Diversity, and Natural History
abstract: The Elateridae (Insecta: Coleoptera) includes more than 700 genera and 14,000 species globally. Its wide distribution throughout the world, elusive systematics, and enigmatic biology have attracted considerable attention in terms of classification, phylogenomics, behaviour, ecology, management, and paedomorphic lineages. The Elateridae has undergone substantial restructuring with respect to placements of taxa in its classification. title: Diet behavior of whitefish Coregonus lavaretus Linnaeus, 1758 in Lake Sevan (Armenia)
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the diet and behavior of the whitefish. Studies of the Lake Sevan whitefish Coregonus lavaretus Linnaeus, 1758 population were conducted in 2023–2024. A total of 300 whitefish were collected during the three seasons, reaching 100 specimens per season. Whitefish of various ages were used for the analysis. The whitefish ranged in age from 1+ to 6+. Analysis of the trophic structure revealed a significant shift in the whitefish's diet. title: Two New Funerary Altars with Figural Niches from Patara: An Assessment of Local Production and Reuse
abstract: This study focuses on two inscribed funerary altars with figural niches recovered in the vicinity of the City Gate during the 2025 excavations at Patara. The monuments are examined through typological, comparative, architectural, stylistic and epigraphic analysis. Their place within the Lycian tradition of altars with figural niches and the processes of their reuse are also discussed. The study demonstrates that economic factors played as decisive a role as burial customs in the distribution of altars with figural niches. The Ye’kwana are a Carib people of indigenous speech whose current population is estimated to be around 7,000 people distributed in villages that are located in Venezuela and Brazil. abstract: Schistidium deguchianum Ochyra & Bedn.-Ochyra, an endemic Andean species previously known only from its locus classicus in Urubamba Province (Cusco Region, Peru), is reported here from a second locality in Peru. The species was discovered in Jauja Province (Junín Region), approximately 400 km northwest of the type locality, where it was collected in 1977 by Pirkko and Eberhard Hegewald and misidentified as S. cinclidodonteum (Müll.Hal.) title: Transforming the Panama Canal from Transportation Infrastructure into a Tourist Destination: Opportunities, Challenges, and Sustainability Implications
abstract: This research examines the transformation of the Panama Canal from functional transportation infrastructure into a significant tourist destination while maintaining operational integrity. Employing descriptive and analytical methodologies, the study analyses visitor statistics, economic impacts, infrastructure investments, and sustainability challenges across recent years. Findings reveal substantial growth in visitor numbers and demonstrate that canal tourism consistently contributes to a significant proportion of national tourism revenues. title: Late antique and early byzantine cisterns and tanks in the eastern Mediterranean: state of the art
abstract: Abstract Water, a fundamental prerequisite for life, has increasingly become a strategic resource in recent decades. Consequently, research into ancient water management technologies is gaining renewed relevance. This article inaugurates a series of studies focused on water collection systems in cisterns/tanks across the eastern Mediterranean. It offers an overview of current research trends, evaluates the state of the source material, and highlights the strengths and limitations of existing scholarship. title: A review of the southern African spider beetle genus Scaleptinus Borowski, 2006 (Coleoptera: Ptinidae: Ptininae) and notes on their unusual male genitalia
abstract: The spider beetle genus Scaleptinus Borowski, 2006 (Coleoptera: Ptinidae: Ptininae) was created to reclassify two morphologically distinct, scale-covered species of Ptinus known from the arid western regions of Namibia and South Africa. In this same publication, two new species, S. beardae and S. similis, were each described from single male specimens. Morphological examination reveals that S. beardae is within the range of morphological variation seen in S. squamulosus and is here proposed as a junior synonym. title: The (moving) elephant in the room: A literature review on the impact of tourism on local residents’ mobility
abstract: Tourism is fundamentally a mobility phenomenon, yet its impacts on everyday mobility and transportation behaviors of residents remain neglected in both tourism and transportation research. This literature review examines how visitor impacts on residents’ everyday movement are conceptualized, measured, and analyzed in empirical research. Following PRISMA guidelines, it identifies 11 articles that capture perceptions of locals about tourism’s influence on their day-to-day mobility patterns. title: The Influence of Body Growth Rates and Climatic Parameters on Gametogenesis of Pithecopus gonzagai (Anura, Phyllomedusidae) in Two Brazilian Domains
abstract: This study evaluated the influence of body condition indices and climatic parameters on gametogenesis in Pithecopus gonzagai from two Brazilian morphoclimatic domains. Individuals were sampled monthly at the Tapacurá Ecological Station (Atlantic Forest) and the Olho D'Água da Bica Forest Garden (Caatinga). Body condition was assessed using the condition factor (K1) and gonadosomatic, hepatosomatic, and liposomatic indices calculated from body and tissue masses. title: Development's Race Problem: Post‐Black Lives Matter Erasures, Palestine and the Politics of Publishing
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite efforts by critical scholars of development to centre race in their analysis, Development Studies remains entangled in its racist history and contemporary imperialism. New troubling forms of oppression and control within the discipline's approach to race have emerged, marking the post‐Black Lives Matter era as a point of transition between old and new erasures of race. We argue that although race is no longer ignored, the discursive and material boundaries within which it can be discussed have been erected through silencing, censorship, regulation and appropriation. abstract: Conversations about student debt frequently target attendees of four-year and professional institutions, since higher-cost institutions are more likely to lead to high levels of debt. While some research has focused on financial aid and college funding at community colleges, we have comparatively limited scholarship regarding conceptualizations of student debt. title: Fish helminth fauna of the Debed River of the Lori Region of Armenia
abstract: The study of the fish helminth fauna of the Debed Rive rand the detection of fish infection by helminths. The material was collected in 2023. A total of 92 individuals of 4 fish species from the Debed River were examined. Helminthological examination of fish, collection and cameral processing of helminths were carried out according to generally accepted methods. title: Managing the Low-Carbon Transition of Tourism in Vietnam: Policy Progress, Practice and Governance Gaps
abstract: Vietnam has placed green growth and net-zero emissions by 2050 at the centre of its tourism policy, while also setting some of the most ambitious volume targets in Southeast Asia. In 2025 the country received 21.2 million international arrivals, 84.3% of them by air, and new policy now aims for 45 to 50 million international and 160 million domestic visitors by 2030. This paper asks whether the way green tourism is currently managed in Vietnam is capable of reconciling these two goals. title: Predominance of Externally Mixed Black Carbon Over the Tibetan Plateau During the Asian Summer Monsoon
abstract: Abstract The mixing state of black carbon (BC) strongly influences its lifetime and radiative forcing over the Tibetan Plateau (TP). Previous observations, mostly conducted during the non‐monsoon season, suggested that thickly coated BC dominates due to long‐range transport from South Asia. Here we report near‐surface BC mixing state measurements during the 2021–2023 summer monsoons at seven sites across the central–southern TP. title: Disney's Location Strategy in China: Balancing Global Brand Identity and Local Adaptation
abstract: Multinational companies face a persistent tension between maintaining a consistent global brand identity and adapting to local consumer preferences. Disney's long-term presence in China provides a useful observation sample for examining this issue. Since the opening of Shanghai Disneyland in 2016, Disney has accumulated substantial operational experience in the Chinese market. This article examines how Disney has adapted to the Chinese market while maintaining its core brand identity. title: Hierarchies of alcohol – pulque and beer in Mexican society (c. 1500 to 1940)
abstract: Abstract While Mexico today is often characterised as ‘tequila country’, the most important alcoholic beverage both during the pre-colonial and the Spanish era was pulque, the fermented sap of the agave plant. In addition to holding ritual significance, pulque served a pragmatic purpose: it is nutritious, can replace food and water, and features high microbial diversity. This paper explores how – under colonial rule – pulque was characterized as ‘low-class’, but also became an important revenue source. title: The Afterlife Dopo Dante: Translating the Topography of Inferno and Purgatorio for the Twenty-First Century
abstract: This article explores the translation of topography in twenty-first century translations of Dante’s Divina Commedia. Extensive research has already been done on topography in the Commedia source text, cataloguing place names, examining the metaphorical significance of place, and comparing Dante’s worldview to his medieval contemporaries. However, there has been minimal close textual comparative analysis of how topography is translated into English. title: The JUICE Lunar–Earth gravity assist from trajectory design, navigation and spacecraft operations perspective
abstract: Abstract. This paper describes the world’s first-ever Lunar–Earth Gravity Assist (LEGA) performed by ESA’s JUICE spacecraft on 19–20 August 2024 from trajectory design, navigation and spacecraft operations point of view. This double flyby – Moon first, Earth second – enabled a large Delta-V gain while minimizing propellant use, redirecting JUICE toward its next destination: Venus (August 2025) and ultimately Jupiter (2031). title: Simulation and analysis of strongly asymmetric swirl distortion flow fields
abstract: Abstract Driven by the growing demand for stealth and super-maneuverability in modern advanced aircraft, multi-bend inlets such as S-shaped and buried inlets have been widely adopted. While enhancing performance, the swirl distortion induced by such inlets severely restricts engine performance and operational stability. title: The Land Is Speaking
abstract: Alex Stark discusses Peruvian wisdom, feng shui, architecture, healing, community, and the reciprocal relationship between people and the land.

title: CRIMEAN TATAR FOLK INSTRUMENTAL MUSIC
abstract: This article discusses the unique musical heritage of the Crimean people, its melodic, stylistic and intonational properties. It examines the historical background to the emergence of folk samples and proposes a classification of traditional musical instruments. Furthermore, an analysis of a number of Crimean Tatar instrumental melodies is provided, including the sections: “Toy merasimi avalari”, “ Dolular”, “Ag‘ir avalar ve xaytarmalar”, “Cheshit oyun avalar”, “Qonushma ve eglenje avalar”. title: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation sustains carbon sinks under warming Tibetan permafrost region
abstract: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) by legumes is a major natural source of reactive nitrogen that supports ecosystem functioning and carbon sequestration. Warming across the Tibetan Plateau alpine permafrost region may trigger substantial shifts in vegetation composition and distribution, yet the consequences for ecosystem nitrogen inputs remain poorly understood. Here, using 1047 plant samples from 323 plots across the Tibetan Plateau and 15N natural-abundance techniques, we quantify legume and non-legume nitrogen sources and regional aboveground SNF rates. title: The Camel in Nabataean Society: Archaeological and Historical Perspectives
abstract: Camels have been companions to humans since ancient civilizations, being a preferred animal because of their multipurpose nature. They were commonly used for long-distance transportation, favored over other animals like horses and donkeys due to their patience and ability to endure long journeys through harsh deserts with minimal water. In ancient times, people across the Middle East and Arabian societies relied on camels for overland trade and daily life. journal: International journal of civilizations studies & tolerance sciences.

title: ESCALATION AND NUCLEAR NON-PROLIFERATION CHALLENGES IN THE KASHMIR REGION
abstract: The Kashmir region remains an epicenter of strategic instability in South Asia, with the conflict sustained by India and Pakistan’s decision not to align with international nuclear non-proliferation norms. The study examines regional strategic stability in the India–Pakistan dyad, with particular reference to the Kashmir region as its main dependent variable. Strategic stability is understood in terms of the predictability and resilience of the bilateral security balance in conditions of recurrent escalation risk. title: Edmund Blunden and Places in Hong Kong
abstract: Despite working as Professor of English at The University of Hong Kong for over a decade (1953–1964), Blunden’s time in Hong Kong has been little documented. This article aims to fill the critical gap by tracing Blunden’s footsteps in Hong Kong through exploring previously undiscussed archival materials mainly in overseas archives, supplemented by oral history interviews, contemporary accounts and analysis of Blunden’s works as well as secondary literature, bringing together archival research, literary biography, and historical investigation. title: THE LATE IRON AGE IN THE LAKE VAN BASIN IN THE LIGHT OF THE LATEST DATA
abstract: After the fall of the Kingdom of Urartu, which is the central power of Eastern Anatolia, in scientific studies conducted in the Lake Van Basin, the findings referred to as the “reddish ware group,” produced in imitation of Urartian bright red burnished pottery, have been encountered. It has also been shown that there are differences in the typology of spouted containers, tankards, and pottery not found in the Urartu ceramic workshop. title: When Place Becomes Prop: Public Art, Private Selves, and the Aesthetic of Spectacle
abstract: This reflective essay explores the evolving relationship between public art, personal identity, and spatial experience through an encounter with Chris Burden’s Urban Light installation in Los Angeles. Blending personal narrative with cultural theory, the piece examines how public spaces like Urban Light are increasingly transformed into backdrops for self-performance and digital self-branding. title: Pre-Colonial Trade in a Border Region: A Case Study of Illela-Konni Trade Relations, 1700-1900 A.D
abstract: This paper examines Illela and Konni trade relations from 1700 to 1900 and argued that the relations are influenced by geographical and historical factors. The objective of the paper is to analyse how these factors shaped trade between the two towns. Through a critical analysis of oral interviews, archival records, travellers' accounts, and relevant secondary literature, the paper found out that variations in climate, soil, vegetation and resource endowments created patterns of comparative production that encouraged sustained exchange in grains and livestock which in turn developed the trade.

title: How reason found its common sense in Latin Aristotelianism: Commentary practice and the problem of universality in latin aristotelianism
abstract: Argument A history of “common sense” concerns as much the epistemological concept as the very architecture of human rational judgment. The historian of medieval philosophy Étienne Gilson (1884–1978) cast nineteenth-century Jesuit appeals to common sense as a costly defense against the Cartesian problem of certainty: when intellectual first principles are fused with sensus communis , metaphysical realism is at risk. title: La institucionalización de la vacunación en España: de la viruela al Calendario Nacional de Vacunación (1803-1975)
abstract: La vacunación ha desempeñado un papel central en la construcción histórica de la Salud Pública en España y en la progresiva institucionalización de la intervención sanitaria del Estado. Desde finales del siglo XVIII, la lucha contra la viruela actuó como motor de una política preventiva cada vez más sistemática, que evolucionó desde la inoculación variolosa hacia la vacunación jenneriana y su regulación administrativa. abstract: Abstract Introduction Evidence on how issues related to LGBTQI+ are prioritized in national policy processes is limited despite increasing global attention to LGBTQI+ rights. abstract: Abstract Background: Empathy is essential for healthcare professionals, enhancing patient-physician relationships, clinical outcomes, and patient adherence while reducing medical errors. abstract: This article examines the European Union’s collective securitization of Russia across two critical junctures: the 2014 annexation of Crimea and the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Why did the EU, long energy-dependent and internally divided, adopt substantial but fragmented measures that changed little in 2014, yet achieve unprecedented unity, scope, and institutionalization after 2022? abstract: Vaccinium myrtillus has commonly been recognized as encompassing plants from Eurasia, Japan, and North America. Published molecularbased phylogenetic data, however, suggest that V. myrtillus is not monophyletic and might best be divided into distinct taxonomic entities. Submerged paleolandscapes in the eastern North Sea offer an archive of past environmental changes due to sea level rise and coastal retreat. abstract: Understanding rising atmospheric CO2 effects on the chemistry of the world’s ecosystems remains nascent. abstract: Climate change and marine degradation are ecological pressures that are increasingly affecting the lives of coastal communities, including the social conditions and well-being of children.
