abstract: Eutrophication is a phenomenon characterized by increased nutrient levels that has far-reaching impacts on the structure and function of aquatic ecosystems, particularly through changes in trophic dynamics and plankton-based food webs. abstract: Ocean ecosystems have played a crucial role in people's lives around the world for millennia. abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) and tropical cyclones (TCs) are ocean–atmosphere extremes that can occur during the same season under a warming climate. abstract: Abstract Isopods of the family Cymothoidae Leach, 1814 are frequently found as fish parasites in continental and marine environments, distributed in tropical and subtropical environments. abstract: Coastal sedimentary archives offer key insights into past severe storms and related flooding, contributing to a better understanding of long-term coastal hazard histories. abstract: This paper demystifies the popular perception that Kerala’s coastal communities have retained their traditional fishing culture (Kerala Tourism Citation2022), often romanticised in digital archives, using Vypeen Island as a case study. title: Assessing and quantifying variations in the functioning of marine food webs across scales
abstract: The mismatch between the scale of ecological processes and management decisions represents a significant challenge in marine conservation. This misalignment can result in ineffective conservation measures and compromise the sustainability of marine ecosystems. The large spatial resolution commonly used to analyze food webs may obscure key ecological processes and their functioning, leading to inaccurate conclusions with important consequences for management and governance. title: Atlas of pollen and spores from forests and wetlands in the mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain, USA
abstract: This atlas includes descriptions and illustrations of pollen and spores from plant species found in the mid-Atlantic Coastal Plain of the United States of America, with a focus on taxa that grow in or near riparian wetlands. It includes light micrographs and detailed descriptions of 141 species spanning 105 genera and 68 families of plants. This atlas was compiled to facilitate the identification of palynomorphs from sedimentary archives in the mid-Atlantic region. It includes both wetland taxa and those from surrounding uplands that may be deposited in wetland sediments.

title: How natural dynamic pH conditions could affect compounds mediating marine diatom-bacteria interactions: a chemical theoretical perspective
abstract: Abstract Life in marine diatom-bacteria communities is coordinated through a multitude of chemically-mediated interactions in a highly dynamic environment. Respiration and photosynthesis create steep gradients and large fluctuations in abiotic conditions on diel timescales. But how sensitive biomolecules involved in microbial interactions are to such dynamic microscale environmental impacts has not been assessed so far. title: The Potential For The Development Of Halal Tourism At The Marine Tourism Park In The South Jawai Subdistrict, Sambas Regency
abstract: Halal tourism development has emerged as a strategic catalyst for enhancing regional economic diversification rooted in Islamic values. This study aims to analyse the empirical conditions, evaluate the potential for halal tourism development, and identify the driving and inhibiting factors at Taman Wisata Bahari, Jawai Laut Village, South Jawai District, Sambas Regency. Employing a qualitative descriptive field research approach, data were gathered through in-depth interviews with site managers, local vendors and tourists, complemented by participatory observation and documentation. title: Turbulent mixing by non-breaking surface waves in the ocean: theory, observation and modeling
abstract: Most ocean general-circulation models face the persistent challenge that the simulated summer ocean mixed layers are too shallow, indicating a lack of mixing; climate models coupled to them simulate too hot sea-surface temperatures (SSTs). Global wind energy input to the oceans supplies a great amount of energy to the surface waves. title: Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Data Processing and Analysis Model for Seaport Based Surveillance in Maritime Narcotics. 'A Case Dar Es Salaam Sea Port'
abstract: This study presents the design and evaluation of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based facial recognition system that utilizes a police photo archive for real-time suspect identification at maritime seaports. The system processes real-time images captured by UAVs and compares them against a curated database of 669 known suspects. A total of 2,355 UAV-captured images from Ununio and Kigamboni seaports were used to evaluate the system. title: Animal indicators of climate stress in Mediterranean marine protected areas: evidence limits and monitoring design
abstract: Animal observations can reveal ecological change in marine protected areas, but their conservation importance and their ability to diagnose climatic causes are different properties. This critical narrative synthesis examines how those two properties differ across four observation classes: benthic condition, coastal fish composition, seabird reproduction and unusual animal occurrences. title: “Pathways Strewn with Ocean Waves and Thorns”: Grassroots Multiculturalism and the Trojan Horse Coffeehouse in 1970s Toronto
abstract: In 1972, as Toronto’s cultural landscape was being reshaped by postwar immigration and countercultural movements, poet Gwendolyn MacEwen and musician Nikos Tsingos opened the Trojan Horse at 179 Danforth Avenue. This boîte became an unexpected hub where political exiles, artists, and activists forged connections across cultural boundaries. title: Geochemical fingerprints of modern and relict sands along the Northern Adriatic coast: tracing natural processes and anthropogenic sediment redistribution
abstract: Elemental geochemistry provides an effective tool for reconstructing sediment provenance and tracing the evolution of coastal depositional systems. This study investigates the geochemical composition of relict sands, Holocene beach-ridge deposits and modern beach sediments along the Emilia–Romagna coast (Northern Adriatic Sea) using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyses and selected elemental ratios. title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. title: Early to Mid‐Holocene molluscan community dynamics in Billefjorden, central Svalbard: the interplay of local geomorphology and regional climate
abstract: The postglacial evolution of High Arctic coastal environments is recorded in the rich fossiliferous archives of raised marine terraces. This study employs a multi‐proxy approach combining molluscan community analysis, taphonomy and sedimentology to reconstruct the Early to Mid‐Holocene environmental dynamics of the Mimerdalen embayment in the Billefjorden area of central Svalbard. Our results indicate that local benthic succession was driven by a complex interplay of glacio‐isostatic rebound and fluctuating sediment supply rather than simple climatic warming. title: High-Resolution Study of the Magnetic Properties in Marine Sediments Based on Diamond NV Center Magnetometry
abstract: Magnetostratigraphic dating has been widely employed for the study of marine sediments, including ferromanganese nodules (MFNs) and ferromanganese crusts (MFCs), using high-resolution rock magnetic microscopy (RMM) techniques. However, these sediments accumulate at extremely slow rates of millimeters per million year (mm/Ma), while previously employed scanning SQUID microscopes (SSM) and Hall probe microscope are limited to sub-millimeter spatial resolution. title: Physicochemical characteristics of Nigerian estuaries and their patterns, drivers, and implications for environmental management
abstract: Estuaries are dynamic coastal ecosystems that provide essential ecological, biogeochemical, and socio-economic services. Despite their importance, Nigerian estuaries remain underrepresented in global scientific literature, with existing studies fragmented and spatially uneven. This study systematically reviewed the physicochemical characteristics of surface waters and sediments in selected Nigerian estuaries, including Lagos Lagoon, Awoye, Bonny River, Imo River, and Qua Iboe River. title: Entrepreneurial Practices: Bapandai-pandai in Minangkabau Coastal Communities
abstract: Women in Jorong Pasia Tiku, a coastal village in West Sumatra, run small enterprises but rarely try to grow them. This study asks why, and what that choice reveals about how Minangkabau women act within their gender relations and coastal livelihoods. Research on women’s entrepreneurship usually tracks income, growth, and digital adoption. Little of it examines how household roles and local social structures shape women’s economic decisions in coastal communities. Giddens’s structuration theory frames the analysis. A feminist qualitative design guided data collection through in-depth interviews

abstract: ABSTRACT Northern Borneo provides a key archive of how convergent‑margin processes and drainage reorganization shaped the southern South China Sea margin from the Paleogene to the Neogene. This study integrates whole‑rock major–trace element data from Rajang–Crocker and Neogene successions in Sabah with detrital zircon U–Pb age spectra to reconstruct source‑to‑sink evolution and to evaluate the relative contribution of first‑cycle and recycled sediment sources. title: Leaning left: how turn bias and habitat complexity shape spatial cognition in a coral-reef fish
abstract: In coral reef ecosystems, anthropogenic change is rapidly altering habitat structure, but the consequences for fish cognition remain poorly understood. We tested whether structural habitat complexity influences spatial learning and strategy use in the humbug damselfish (Dascyllus aruanus). Juveniles were reared in aquaria containing either high- or low-complexity coral structures and trained in a T-maze task, requiring the use of egocentric (turn-based) and/or allocentric (landmark-based) strategies to locate a reward. title: Measuring the nutritional benefits of fisheries adaptations in the Pacific Islands region
abstract: Fish are an important source of dietary protein 1 and essential nutrients 2 . However, efforts to sustain these benefits across the global south are increasingly challenged by population growth, habitat degradation and climate change 3 , 4 , 5 . These pressures are particularly acute in several Pacific Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where gaps have emerged between the recommended level of fish consumption needed for good nutrition and the supply of fish from coral reefs and other coastal habitats 6 , 7 , 8 ̶ the source of most fish consumed in the region 8 , 9 , 10 . abstract: The cone penetration test (CPT) is widely used in offshore geotechnical engineering, with growing interest in directly deriving soil responses such as p–y curves for monopiles, to reduce the need for advanced laboratory testing. This requires reliable relationships between the CPT response and the underlying soil stress–strain behaviour. title: Ibn Khaldûn as a Colonial Archive: Toward an Epistemic Decolonization
abstract: Abstract This article examines Ibn Khaldûn not as a stable, timeless precursor of modern social science but as a figure constituted through colonial translation and reception. Focusing on nineteenth- and twentieth-century French and English translations of the Muqaddimah , it argues that Ibn Khaldûn emerged in modern scholarship as a colonial archive—a site where translation, race, and epistemic authority intersected to produce new forms of historical and sociological knowledge. title: Temporal trends of dengue exposure among children in coastal Kenya
abstract: Abstract Background Serosurveys suggest widespread dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Africa but there is limited information on the temporal patterns of exposure. Methods Using repeated cross-sectional serosurvey data, we estimated the prevalence and incidence of DENV infections in coastal Kenya over 20 years (1998–2018). abstract: ABSTRACT Compound‐specific stable isotope analysis (CSIA) has been widely applied to modern and archaeological samples of animal and human body tissues to evaluate food habits and/or physiological conditions. However, these techniques have rarely been applied to aquatic mammals, for which further study is required to evaluate their utility. abstract: From protected area coverage to conservation outcomes A new Scandinavian assessment shows where current marine area-based protection is too weak and how site-level evidence can guide stronger marine protection. title: DNA-Based Diet Analysis in a Coastal Population of Turtle Doves in the Netherlands
abstract: Detailed information on local diet composition can be important in efforts to conserve migratory birds. We determined the diet of Turtle Doves Streptopelia turtur in a coastal dune population in The Netherlands, where this species is in steep decline. We collected fresh droppings in the field and determined the plant species therein using metabarcoding and next generation DNA sequencing. abstract: Forty-one isolates of the genus Aurantiochytrium were cultured from 32 samples collected from the Red Sea mangroves, Egypt. While several potentially toxic species of Pseudo-nitzschia have been reported in Turkish coastal waters, toxicity studies have remained localized to the Sea of Marmara. title: Understanding Safety of Navigation Deficiencies Leading to Vessel Detention: A Data-Driven Analysis of Black Sea Memorandum of Understanding Inspections
abstract: Preventing safety of navigation (SN) deficiencies is of critical importance in waterborne transport since the SN Code constitutes one of the most recurrent deficiency categories that serve as a basis for detention under port state controls (PSC). In pursuit of this objective, this study initially delineates and critically evaluates the interdependencies between a spectrum of influential determinants and deficiency types, as well as their respective contributions to detention occurrences attributable to the SN code. title: Impacto de la variabilidad pluviométrica en el balance hídrico de los acuíferos costeros en la costa sur de Artemisa y Mayabeque, Cuba
abstract: The assessment of groundwater availability and dynamics in coastal karst regions requires an integrated analysis of climate variability and the hydrogeological response of the aquifer system. This study analyzes precipitation behavior and its impact on the water balance of the sub-aquifers on the southern coast of Artemisa and Mayabeque provinces, Cuba, during the 2009-2024 period. title: Microbial niche partitioning explains N 2 O distributions and cycling in marine oxygen minimum zones
abstract: Oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) are marine hotspots for cycling and emission of the powerful greenhouse gas nitrous oxide (N 2 O). Steep redox gradients host diverse microbial communities that produce and consume N 2 O, generating a characteristic vertical distribution, with low concentrations in anoxic cores and supersaturated accumulation in surrounding oxyclines. abstract: ABSTRACT Direct seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically hampered by chloride‐induced competitive oxidation, corrosion, and active‐site poisoning, driving the urgent need for highly active and chlorine‐tolerant electrocatalysts. Herein, a surface‐engineered electrocatalyst comprising osmium nanoparticles (Os NPs) anchored onto CoFe layered double hydroxide (Os/CoFe LDH) was prepared. title: A Novel Sea Anemone Peptide Ed-79 Blocks Shaker Kv Channels and Exhibits Insecticidal Activity
abstract: The escalating resistance of agricultural pests to conventional chemical insecticides has created an urgent need for eco-friendly biological alternatives with novel modes of action. Sea anemone venoms are rich in structurally stable and target-specific ion channel-modulating peptides, representing a promising source of new insecticidal molecules. abstract: ABSTRACT Successive waves of extraction in the Caribbean—from plantation monocultures to oil and gas—have reshaped overlapping agrarian, coastal and marine environments, undermining the socio‐ecological foundations of small‐scale fisher livelihoods and generating ongoing conflict between the state, energy sector and fishing communities. Yet despite the importance of fishing to post‐colonial island economies, these tensions are rarely examined through a post‐plantation lens. abstract: Asian outflow represents 50% of global anthropogenic mercury emissions, but the atmospheric oxidation pathways controlling its deposition to the adjacent Pacific Ocean remain poorly constrained. abstract: The tectonic evolution of the Tethyan oceans and the subsequent accretion of East Asian blocks to Eurasia are central to deciphering the geodynamic assembly of the Asian continent. However, the precise paleogeographic configuration of these continental fragments along the northeastern Gondwanan margin remains a subject of intense debate, obscuring our understanding of the episodic lifecycles of the Proto-, Paleo-, and Neo-Tethys oceans and the sequence of Gondwanan fragmentation. title: STYLISTIC POTENTIAL OF PROVERBS CONTAINING HYDRONYMIC COMPONENTS IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK
abstract: This article investigates the stylistic potential of English and Uzbek proverbs containing hydronymic components and water-related lexical elements. Particular attention is paid to the role of river, sea, ocean, and water imagery in the formation of figurative meanings, the expression of cultural values, and the achievement of communicative effects. This paper develops an improved polarization-sensitive semi-analytic Monte Carlo (SMC) method for vertically stratified water. abstract: This study estimates comparative upper bounds on pressure-retarded osmosis (PRO) power and specific energy for five Japanese river estuaries and desalination-brine scenarios. abstract: The article examines oneiric modality as a stylistic dominant in Neil Gaiman’s novel “The Ocean at the End of the Lane”. title: Comparison of affordability and availability of antidepressants in China from 2019 to 2022: evidence from national procurement database
abstract: Background: Depression is a widespread mental disorder imposing significant societal burdens. The COVID-19 pandemic exacerbated its prevalence, emphasizing the need for improved access to affordable and effective treatments. This study aims to examine the trends of antidepressant availability and affordability in China from 2019 to 2022 and the role of the National Volume-Based Procurement (NVBP) policy. abstract: Accurate data-driven identification and long-term forecasting of surface ship motions in realistic ocean environments are essential for advanced autonomous navigation and predictive control systems. However, robust system identification in such conditions remains challenging due to high-frequency wave-induced disturbances, which contaminate measured signals and may contribute to error accumulation in recursive forecasting. title: Hydrogen and Helium Dissolution, Outgassing, and Loss in Evolving Sub-Neptune Magma Oceans: Examining Demographic Features and Radius Evolution
abstract: Abstract Sub-Neptunes’ molten interiors are expected to accommodate large quantities of volatiles, potentially altering their radius evolution. title: Understanding how local public policies influence blue food systems. The case of Barcelona
abstract: Abstract Cities are increasingly important actors in food governance, yet their role in blue food systems remains poorly understood, particularly because they generally lack authority over fisheries management. This study examines how municipal policies shaped Barcelona’s blue food system between 1940 and 2023 and asks how local governments influence seafood provisioning through powers exercised beyond production. abstract: This world literature review presents the current systematics, ecology and toxicology of snakes of the subfamily Hydrophiinae – a genetic clade including the most toxic Australian terrestrial elapids and sea snakes. The spatial distribution and occurrence of snakes of the Elapidae family, tied to the climatic zones and landscapes of the continent, are considered. abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the long‐term corrosion of copper canisters in a deep geological disposal repository, focusing on the environmental transition from oxic to anoxic conditions. abstract: Despite the extensive German archival evidence, there is still some historical opinion that Germany did not constitute a threat to Australia in 1914. abstract: The increasing scarcity of natural aggregates, coupled with the growing environmental burden associated with municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) residues, poses a dual challenge for sustainable urban construction. abstract: Holothuria scabra, commonly known as sandfish, is a highly valued sea cucumber species distributed in tropical marine waters, including Indonesia. This study aimed to genetically identify H. scabra populations from Buaya Island (Alor) and Seraya Island (Labuan Bajo) using DNA barcoding of the Cytochrome Oxidase I (COI) gene. abstract: Soil arthropods constitute a structurally and functionally important component of West Bengal’s below-ground biodiversity, yet their diversity is considerably less documented than above-ground agricultural pests. abstract: Abstract Histories of protest in the Highlands and Islands have been largely limited to the study of dramatic and large-scale events driven by issues of possession of and access to land after 1850. abstract: This article examines how idiomatic and figurative language constructs environmental meaning in the works of the American writer Ernest Hemingway and the Uzbek novelist Tog'ay Murod. abstract: Trilobites exhibiting injuries are ideal palaeontological archives for Palaeozoic predator-prey interactions. abstract: Sand dunes along the coastal plain of Mandatory Palestine (1920–1948) went through dramatic legal and economic changes under British rule. This terrain accounted for a disproportionate share of the state domains the British Palestine government leased to Zionist companies and far exceeded the amount of similar lands allotted to Palestinians. abstract: As a historic cradle of civilization, the Middle East (ME) was once a pioneer in urbanization and human advancement, yet today the region struggles with disparities in genomic medicine. abstract: Terrestrial megafauna (animals >1,000 kg) have substantial impacts on ecosystems while alive; yet, we know little about the impacts of these ecosystem engineers after they die. abstract: This article examines the monumentalisation of World War I in the Isonzo/Soča region (today divided between Italy and Slovenia), promoted by the Italian government and local authorities during the interwar period. abstract: As scholarly publishing becomes increasingly commodified, market-oriented definitions of excellence are reshaping the organization and hierarchization of scientific knowledge. abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are among the most threatened globally, yet practical guidance for implementing targeted freshwater protected areas remains limited. Analytical and descriptive in nature, the study employs a qualitative methodology based on a literature review and theoretical-conceptual analysis guided by Buzan and Wæver’s Regional Security Complex Theory. title: A Study of Artistic Training for Chinese Women at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Lyon (1921–1946)
abstract: During the early twentieth century, increasing numbers of Chinese students travelled to France to pursue artistic education. Among the institutions that received these students, the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Paris has attracted substantial scholarly attention, while the contribution of the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts de Lyon has been investigated less extensively. In 1921, the Franco-Chinese Institute of Lyon was established, serving as a bridge that enabled eight Chinese female students to receive training at the École des Beaux-Arts de Lyon. title: The geotourism potential of geosites and archaeo-paleontological landscape in the Gulf of Zula–Danakil corridor, Eritrea
abstract: The Gulf of Zula–Danakil corridor of Eritrea represents a unique “rift–reef–refugium” setting exceptionally rich in geological attractions (such as volcanic cones, hot springs and reef beds) and archaeo-paleontological heritage. The region boasts globally important Stone Age sites like the 125,000-year-old artifact-bearing reef at Abdur, the 1.0-million-year-old Homo erectus cranium from Buia, Asfet, and the ancient port of Adulis, offering insights into human evolution, dispersal, and ancient maritime history. abstract: This study aims to analyze the readiness of the tourism sector's carrying capacity in Majene Regency and evaluate the reliability of a spatial-based Smart Tourism application in supporting digital tourism governance transformation. Using an exploratory analytical descriptive approach, primary data was collected through cross-sector Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) involving local government elements, destination managers, business actors, and the community, then analyzed using thematic methods. title: Revising the Cambro-Ordovician depositional margin of Gondwana in eastern Australia: geochronology constraints on the Girilambone Group, central NSW
abstract: Cambrian deposition along eastern Gondwana extends from the western Koonenberry and Loch Lilly–Kars belts to the eastern Saint Arnaud and Warrata groups (and other covered Thomson Orogen units). Farther east, the Lachlan Orogen’s Ordovician depositional system comprises turbidite packages of the Adaminaby, Castlemaine and Girilambone groups. title: Plasma-Enhanced Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP) with Self-Cleaning Electrode for Scalable Remediation of Particulate Matter in Large Diesel Engines
abstract: Abstract We have demonstrated a fundamentally new pollution control device that integrates a plasma-enhanced electrostatic precipitator (PE-ESP) with a self-cleaning electrode. In the PE-ESP, high-voltage (20 kV) nanosecond (20 ns) pulses generate a transient plasma that produces ion densities approximately 6 orders of magnitude higher than those created by a conventional DC corona. This plasma enhancement increases the particle charging efficiency and allows electrostatic precipitators to be designed much more compactly, making them suitable for mobile sources. title: Cataloging the alien flora of Portugal: New findings and updates
abstract: During recent fieldwork in Portugal – mainly in the regions of Estremadura and Ribatejo in the autumn of 2024, but also earlier and elsewhere in the country – many interesting non-indigenous taxa were recorded. The following 25 taxa were not yet known from Portugal: Amaranthus blitum subsp. pseudogracilis, Amaranthus palmeri, Bassia indica, Cardiospermum grandiflorum, Casuarina cunninghamiana, Chloris gayana, Crepis bursifolia, Cyperus papyrus, Elatine ambigua, Eleocharis obtusa, Eragrostis mexicana, E. pectinacea, Guizotia abyssinica, G. schimperi, Hedera algeriensis, Hydrocotyle bowlesioides

title: Improvised care: Jewish refugee medicine and public health in wartime Shanghai, 1938–1945
abstract: Between 1938 and 1941, nearly 20,000 Jewish refugees fleeing Nazi persecution arrived in wartime Shanghai, a city already destabilized by the Sino-Japanese War (1937-1945), mass displacement, and fragmented governance. Their arrival exposed the limits of Shanghai's overstretched public health system while also generating new forms of medical organisation, refugee self-governance, and intercultural collaboration. title: Two centuries of Colombian paleontology
abstract: Paleontological research on Colombian material has been conducted since 1838. Here, we compiled a database of all published articles through May 2025 to assess temporal trends and changes in Colombian paleontological research. We identified 842 paleontological articles, most of which were published after 1960. Starting in 2000, publications increased significantly, alongside a shift in authorship and research topics. abstract: This work aims to establish the importance of improving nursing performance in guiding older adults in the use of Information and Communication Technologies. A literature review was carried out in databases such as Scielo, Pubmed, and Medline, covering the period from 2019 to 2024, in both Spanish and English. abstract: Abstract Datasets derived from mixed‐template DNA amplification and sequencing (‘metabarcoding’) are common in environmental DNA (eDNA), microbiome or microbial ecology analyses. Such metabarcoding data have been broadly used to inform estimates of biodiversity, distribution and abundance across a wide range of species and habitats. Generally, data from metabarcoding consist of a table of read‐counts assigned to each of a set of taxa or sequence variants. abstract: The lexical accuracy of teachers' discourse can facilitate or hinder the comprehension of academic messages. The objective was to analyze how the use of clear, precise and simple language by teachers affects message comprehension in university students. title: Study of the industrial sectors of Bangladesh to analyse sectoral GHG emissions via SDA in an environmentally extended IO table
abstract: Abstract This study has been conducted to understand the patterns of greenhouse gas emissions in the industrial sectors of Bangladesh and to analyse the driving forces behind these patterns. Environmentally extended input−output tables of Bangladesh for the period from 1991 − 2021 from the EORA database and Asian Development Bank have been used in this paper. title: Long term averages and decadal trends from 20-year time series of the Lecce micrometeorological station (Southern Italy)
abstract: Abstract Time series from October 2005 to September 2025 from the ISAC-Lecce Micrometeorological Station database have been analyzed with main attention to the surface energy exchanges and possible decadal trends. title: Recombinant expression of single eukaryotic-like proteins changes bacteria-sponge interactions
abstract: Abstract Eukaryotic-like proteins (ELP) are often found in intracellular symbionts of insects, plants and evolutionary early-branching sponges, however their functions remain largely uncharacterised. Here we show that the recombinant expression of single genes of various ELP classes can confer on free-living cyanobacteria the capacity to escape phagocytosis by sponges and thus enable intracellular survival. The findings establish ELPs as molecular factors that can control sponge-microbe interactions, which has implications for the evolution of microbial symbiosis.

title: Community Assembly Processes in Tropical Intertidal Rockpool Fishes
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the drivers of community assembly in extreme and dynamic environments, such as intertidal rockpools, requires the integrated assessment of environmental filtering, species traits, phylogeny, and species interactions. This study aimed to quantify the multi‐faceted drivers of rockpool fish assemblage structure by examining: (a) the association with physical and structural pool attributes, (b) the influence of species functional traits and phylogenetic relatedness, (c) residual co‐occurrence patterns suggestive of species interactions, and (d) temporal and spatial dynamics.

abstract: Premature loss of primary teeth during the mixed dentition may reduce arch length and favor malocclusions. The objective was to analyze the indications and clinical effectiveness of space maintainers. A narrative literature review of publications from the last five years in scientific databases was conducted, with a detailed analysis of five studies: one systematic review with meta-analysis, two clinical trials and two in vitro studies. title: Integrated Farming Systems in Bangladesh: A review of Agricultural Sustainability and Livelihood Diversification
abstract: A comprehensive strategy for improving agricultural sustainability, resource use efficiency, and livelihood diversification, especially for smallholder farmers, is represented by Integrated Farming Systems (IFS). This review draws on current literature to assess the effects of IFS on agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, and rural livelihoods in Bangladesh. abstract: Bilateral sagittal split osteotomy of the mandible is one of the most widely used procedures in orthognathic surgery, and its most frequent complication is neurosensory disturbance of the inferior alveolar nerve. The objective was to analyze the incidence of paresthesia after this osteotomy and the associated risk factors described in recent literature. abstract: Introduction: Elasmobranchs are particularly susceptible to handling-related impacts, making careful management essential to avoid excessive physical trauma and stress. In pregnant females, capture may trigger induced parturition, which is generally considered abortion because survival rates have not been evaluated. Objective: To document and describe capture-induced parturition events in rays and their implications for the protocols used during monitoring efforts. abstract: Abstract Irrigation scheduling for peanut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) in Georgia increasingly relies on soil moisture sensing, but it remains unclear whether stage‐specific soil water tension (SWT) thresholds improve on a season‐long static threshold. From 2020 through 2025, a randomized complete block split‐plot field experiment was conducted at the University of Georgia Stripling Irrigation Research Park near Camilla, GA, using a variable‐rate lateral irrigation system. abstract: El presente artículo busca analizar el vínculo intermedial de las poéticas de Jaime Pinos y Carlos Soto Román, a través de sus libros Documental (2018) y 11 (2017), respectivamente. title: The role of international courts and tribunals in shaping expertise – the ITLOS Advisory Opinion on Climate Change in an Arctic expertise context
abstract: Despite a considerable focus in the literature on how expertise comes to be defined, there has so far been little interest in how expertise is shaped in the wording of treaties and the subsequent application by courts. This presents a gap in the literature, as international treaties and courts have significant impact on the definition of expertise. title: Genome Mining and Comparative Analysis of Secondary Metabolite Biosynthetic Gene Clusters in Selected Streptomyces Species Reported from Indian Biodiversity Hotspots
abstract: Actinomycetes, particularly the genus Streptomyces, represents most prolific sources of bioactive secondary metabolites (antibiotics, anticancer agents, immunosuppressants and other therapeutic molecules). Advances in whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics enabled identification of numerous unexplored cryptic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) In our study, a comparative genome mining analysis was conducted on selected Streptomyces species reported by various research groups from Indian biodiversity hotspots (Indo-Burma, Himalayan, Sundaland and Western Ghats). title: Floristic diversity and vascular plant contributions of Wari-La trans Himalaya Ladakh India
abstract: Ladakh, a high-altitude cold desert in the Indian, Trans-Himalayan region, is home to diverse and ecologically significant plant species, many of which possess high medicinal properties. However, due to its harsh climatic conditions, rugged terrain and geopolitical constraints, floristic research in this region remains incomplete. The Present study focuses on the documentation of the Wari-La region, a high-altitude pass between the Indus and Nubra Valleys, which has been largely overlooked in previous botanical explorations. abstract: This article proposes an interpretative framework for inclusion in global higher education, with the aim of conducting a critical analysis of the international academic literature published between 2021 and 2025. By applying the Reflective Thematic Analysis method developed by Braun and Clarke, a corpus of 34 articles indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was systematised. abstract: The sophistication of human life with the inventions and infrastructure development that followed the industrial revolution has one unintended consequence—plastic pollution. Their exponential growth, accumulation in all the environmental systems, persistence and low rate of decay have made them unique polluters of this century, to which no wise management practices and mitigation strategies are known currently. abstract: The construction sector is one of the largest contributors to global energy consumption and CO 2 emissions, with cement-based materials playing a central role in its environmental impact. Cement tiles, despite being marketed as sustainable alternatives to ceramic coatings due to their artisanal production and long durability, rely heavily on Portland cement, a material with high carbon intensity. abstract: The conclusion of negotiations for the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (India-EU FTA) on 27 January 2026 represents a major development in bilateral economic relations and creates a new framework for trade liberalisation between two large and increasingly interconnected economies. abstract: Environmental management has become increasingly important in Africa because environmental degradation directly affects livelihoods, public health, food security, and community resilience. This study examines the relationship between environmental management and community well-being in African countries by focusing on institutional capacity, major environmental challenges, socioeconomic and governance factors, and sustainable development strategies. abstract: Abstract Vanadium(V) is considered a critical metal due to its increasing use in low-carbon energy technologies, particularly V redox-flow batteries. Black shale-hosted deposits represent an important unconventional V resource, where enrichment is closely linked to depositional redox conditions, organic matter accumulation, and postdepositional processes. abstract: This article presents the results derived from a bibliometric review of scientific production on the tourism-education binomial. The research aimed to analyze the perspectives from which this relationship is approached, based on the literature published between 2014 and 2024, in order to identify the predominant approaches, quantify scientific production, recognize who publishes, determine which journals disseminate the knowledge, and identify which countries conduct the research. abstract: Agrochemicals are a fundamental component of modern agriculture, although their intensive use raises concerns regarding human health, biodiversity, ecosystems and the sustainability of production systems. The aim of this study was to analyse the regulatory, environmental and socio-economic differences associated with the use of agrochemicals between Europe and Latin America. abstract: In an active suspension, hydrodynamic interactions between constituent microswimmers play an important role in their collective motion and rheological properties. abstract: Introduction: This work contributes to the understanding of Social Appropriation of Knowledge (SAK), addressing the academic need to clarify its meaning, scope, and impacts. abstract: Background: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects memory, thinking, and behavior, and is the most common form of dementia. The majority of cases occur sporadically (95–99%), while only 1–5% are hereditary. The main pathological processes begin decades before they can be clinically detected. As a typical dominant species in this region, the Gull-billed Tern ( Gelochelidon nilotica ) can serve as an indicator species reflecting changes in the wetland ecological environment. title: Sasi as a Cultural Practice and Ecosystem Regulation Mechanism for Sustainable Ecotourism
abstract: Sasi, a customary resource management system practiced by the people of Eastern Indonesia, has been largely understood as a conservation instrument, while its contribution as a cultural ecosystem service and regulation for community-based ecotourism has not been critically synthesized. This study aims to identify and synthesize scientific literature on the dual role of Sasi as a cultural ecosystem service and regulation, and its relevance to ecotourism development in Menarbu Village, West Papua. title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. Together, these processes provide a framework for understanding long-term climate evolution over the past 540 million years.

abstract: Two new COI haplotypes of the invasive Callinectes sapidus were reported for the first time in the western Iberian Peninsula and one of them in Europe, providing new insights into the origin of this species' invasion in European waters. abstract: Background: A resilient public health supply chain will ensure the sustainability and accessibility of essential medicines during a conflict as demonstrated during the war in Sudan. Aim: To assess the resilience and strategies adopted to sustain and strengthen public health supply chain during the war in Sudan. abstract: Scholarship on the Anthropocene remains divided between Earth-system analyses of material change and environmental-humanities readings of crisis narrative, a split that leaves each side under-equipped to explain how industrial power, ecological rupture, and cultural meaning shape one another. title: Socio-Environmental Controversies in Chile’s Peatland Governance: From Global Climate Discourses to Local Extractivist Realities
abstract: This article analyzes the legislative process that culminated in Chile’s 2024 Peatland Protection Law (Law 21.660), employing critical discourse analysis to examine the parliamentary debates that shaped this regulatory framework. Unlike previous studies on environmental governance in Chile—which have focused on identifying specific conflicts, characterizing extractivist patterns, or diagnosing institutional fragility—this work exposes the socio-technical controversies underlying peatland governance. title: Plant invasions threaten a critically imperiled inland salt marsh ecosystem
abstract: Abstract Inland salt marshes (ISM) form in non-arid regions when mineral soil is infiltrated by salt-saturated groundwater that rises to the surface in natural saltwater springs or seeps. ISMs were historically found across the eastern USA but presently the few remaining intact are critically imperiled natural communities. Due to their highly saline conditions, ISMs support regionally rare halophytic plants, and they are also susceptible to invasion by salt-tolerant invasive plants. title: Patrones histopatológicos hepáticos en peces fluviales de la Amazonía ecuatoriana y su asociación exploratoria con partículas compatibles con microplásticos
abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo caracterizar los patrones histopatológicos hepáticos en peces fluviales de la Amazonía ecuatoriana y explorar su asociación con estructuras morfológicamente compatibles con microplásticos. abstract: The oropharyngeal cavity of turtles exhibits considerable morphological diversity associated with differences in habitat, diet, and feeding strategies. title: Cobamide-based interactions between soil bacteria can be predicted based on monoculture growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Interactions between microbes shape the structure and function of microbial communities. While studying interactions is key to understanding microbial communities as a whole, gaining a detailed mechanistic view is challenging due to the number of co-occurring interactions. Here, we focus on a single class of shared nutrients, the cobalamin (vitamin B 12 ) family of enzyme cofactors known as cobamides, to study nutrient interactions in laboratory consortia of increasing complexity. abstract: Penggunaan pewarna pada produk pangan seperti kue, olahan perikanan, dan makanan penutup bertujuan untuk meningkatkan daya tarik visual serta minat konsumen. title: Phytochemical Profiling, In Vitro Antioxidant, and Anticancer Activities of Ethanolic Extract of Salicornia Europaea L. Flowers
abstract: Salicornia europaea L. is a salt-tolerant halophyte of increasing scientific interest because of its nutritional value and potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals. This study investigated the phytochemical composition, in vitro antioxidant capacity, and anticancer activity of an ethanolic extract from S. europaea L. flowers. Dried flowers were extracted with ethanol and subjected to qualitative phytochemical screening and chromatographic profiling to identify major secondary metabolites. title: Hydropeaking Catalyzes Redox Reactions in Impacted Aquifers: A First Field Evidence
abstract: Abstract Hydropeaking indicates the sudden and frequent fluctuation of river stage caused by the operation of hydropower plants. This river alteration affects numerous physical, chemical, biological, and ecohydrological processes in surface water bodies. The impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydraulics has been investigated only recently through modeling and experimental studies at multiple spatial scales. title: Genome report: sequencing of Helicoverpa- infecting Ophryocystis sp. confirms cryptic diversity and changes in gene content of Lepidoptera-infecting apicomplexan parasites
abstract: Apicomplexan parasites of insects represent a largely unexplored branch of the tree of life. Their small size and lack of informative phenotypic traits can obscure their diversity and many lineage-specific adaptations to different host species. To better understand how these parasites have evolved, we have sequenced and annotated the genome of a neogregarine parasite of moths in the family Noctuidae, including Helicoverpa armigera. title: Omni-Directional Wall-Climbing Robot: A Novel Mechatronic System with Propulsion-Based Adhesion
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, prototype development, and qualitative evaluation of an omni-directional wall-climbing robot using a propulsion-based adhesion mechanism.

title: Phylogenetic evidence for the Taxon Cycle: contemporary tests across island and continental systems
abstract: Abstract Modern phylogenetic evidence offers novel opportunities to test classic models in island biogeography. One of the earliest, E. O. Wilson’s Taxon Cycle, proposed that insular lineages progress through sequential and predictable phases, beginning with geographic expansion, followed by ecological specialization, and ultimately range contraction (and even extinction), shaped by dispersal and interspecific competition. title: Actinomycetota-Derived Metabolites in Pancreatic Cancer: Chemical Diversity, Metabolic Vulnerability, and Translational Barriers
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the deadliest malignancies worldwide, and effective therapies are still lacking. Actinomycetota are among the richest microbial sources of bioactive secondary metabolites, and three agents in clinical use against pancreatic malignancy derive from them — streptozotocin, everolimus and doxorubicin — though all three are indicated for neuroendocrine rather than ductal tumors. title: Legal System Challenges in Environmental Governance in the Case of Benoa Bay Reclamation
abstract: The controversy over the reclamation of Benoa Bay demonstrates that environmental governance depends not only on the existence of regulations but also on legal structure, legal substance, and legal culture. This study aims to analyze environmental governance in Benoa Bay using Lawrence M. Friedman’s Legal System Theory. This research employs normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and historical approaches. The legal materials consist of legislation and various policy instruments related to Benoa Bay. title: Colonial Alien: House Crows, Disposability and Necropolitics in Urban Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT Which lives are allowed to flourish in the city, and which are rendered excessive, alien, or disposable? This article examines kunguru (a Swahili term for crows/ravens, commonly referring to the house crow, Corvus splendens , in urban Tanzania) in Dar es Salaam as a lens through which to analyze colonial afterlives, urban waste infrastructures, and the biopolitics of multispecies life in a postcolonial African city. institutions: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences

title: Trolls, Giants, and ‘Other Folks’ in Finnish Folklore, Archaeology, and Landscape
abstract: Finnish folklore involves numerous stories, tales, and legends that describe human encounters with non-human beings, such as giants, trolls, and earth-dwellers. While this folklore has sometimes been interpreted as reflections of historical events, the consensus today is that such an approach is inapplicable. This article proposes, however, that folklore can provide clues about the dynamics of certain long-term historical cultural processes and how they were anchored on ancient sites and other landscape elements. title: The role of local governance and financial capacities in the effectiveness of international environmental agreements: Evidence from the Ramsar convention
abstract: ABSTRACT Wetlands are critical components of natural water infrastructure, delivering hydrological regulation, biodiversity support, and climate resilience, yet they continue to deteriorate globally. This article provides new causal evidence on the effectiveness of International Environmental Agreements (IEAs) by examining the impacts of wetland designation under the Ramsar Convention. title: The vegetation associations and flora of Hi’Tara, a shell cay, Te Whanga, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island
abstract: The islands of Te Whanga Lagoon, Rēkohu / Wharekauri / Chatham Island are scarcely documented. Two of the islands are shell cays, Moturangaranga and Hi’Tara. In this paper the geology, physiography, landforms, vegetation associations and some of the biota of Hi’Tara are documented. Hi’Tara has a vascular flora of 50 taxa and four fungi (two rusts, one leaf spotting fungus and a mildew). Fifty-two percent of the vascular plants and fungi are naturalised to the Chatham Islands. title: The Maghribi Scholars and the Development of Islam in Bilad al-Sudan up to 1900 AD
abstract: From the emergence of Islam in the Arabian Peninsula in the 7th century AD, to its expansion and development across continents of the world, series of factors have come into play to make the religion distinct among other forms of religions. This is in terms of ideology, ideals and practices. On the other hand, its mode of dispersion as well as expansion from the Arabian Peninsula to other parts of the world became distinct and have resulted to its wide acceptance as well as resurgence of its decayed ideals centuries after another. title: Field Preparation, Sampling Protocols, and Pilot Study of Amoebae in Freshwater Bodies
abstract: Free-living amoebae, living in freshwater ecosystems, constitute an important ecological group among microscopic eukaryotic organisms. Various amoebae belonging to the order (Adl et al.) can be used as potential bioindicators in assessing the trophic state, organic matter loading, microhabitat characteristics, and ecological variability of water bodies. Since most of these organisms are microscopic in size, their study requires proper field preparation, standardized sampling, preservation of living material, and laboratory microscopic analysis. title: Classification of mobile robots for rescue operations
abstract: Search and rescue operations in case of disasters are typically time-sensitive and are conducted under hazardous conditions, with limited access to the affected area. Despite the advances in disaster risk management, events such as earthquakes continue to cause significant loss of life, underscoring the need for more effective rescue techniques. In this context, mobile rescue robots are emerging as a promising tool to support traditional search and rescue operations and to reduce the risk to rescue teams. This study proposes a classification of ground-based mobile robots used in rescue mission

title: East–west asymmetry of Lamb wave amplitude generated by the HTHH eruption and its effect on GPS-TEC variation
abstract: The eruption of the Tonga submarine volcano on January 15, 2022 generated a strong pressure wave, so-called Lamb wave, which orbited the Earth a few times. From high-time resolution pressure observation, it was found that the mean amplitude of the pressure waves separately averaged for the stations on the west-side and on the east-side of the volcano at the first three passages of the waves has a clear east–west asymmetry. title: Assessment of Sustainable Indigenous Building Materials in Selected Resorts in Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: In Nigeria, the move towards sustainable construction has spurred growing interest in locally sourced building materials that meet climatic and cultural needs while minimising environmental impact. This study examines the use and perceived adoption of five sustainable indigenous building materials (compressed earth blocks, bamboo, laterite, timber and stone) in three case-study resorts in Lagos State, Nigeria: La Campagne Tropicana Resort, Ibeju-Lekki (Case 1); Whispering Palms Resort, Iworo, Badagry (Case 2); and Rosh Beach Resort, Badagry (Case 3). title: Ecological Preaching Communication Strategy as a Response to Social Change in the Digital Era: A Comparative Study of Al-Ittifaq Ciwidey Islamic Boarding School and Fish Bank Indonesia
abstract: The global ecological crisis and contemporary social problems compel Islamic institutions to respond through concrete action rather than verbal preaching alone. This study analyzes ecological da'wah communication strategies in responding to social change through a comparative study of Pesantren Al-Ittifaq Ciwidey and Fish Bank Indonesia. Both institutions demonstrate how Islamic theological values are operationalized through action-based programs in distinct institutional contexts. title: Professionalism: the Australian Emergency Management Uniform Minimum Dataset
abstract: The professionalisation of emergency management in Australia is ongoing. Supporting that process is the development of a body of knowledge to support the new profession. The body of knowledge for emergency management requires that emergency events are recorded in a manner and format that supports ongoing learning and research. There is currently no agreed format or standard for the recording of emergency events in Australia. title: Biocontrol potential of a rhizosphere-associated Bacillus amyloliquefaciens F2 isolate against Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4 in Pakistan
abstract: Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense is a serious fungal, soil-borne disease. It is also known as PANAMA disease, considered a major threat to the yield and quality of Banana worldwide. In this study, endophytic bacteria were isolated from soil, roots, and leaves of healthy banana plants growing in Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (Foc) tropical race 4 (TR4) infested soil. title: Optimizing sampling and monitoring of species interactions within Biodiversity Observation Networks
abstract: Abstract Optimal monitoring strategies should be designed to efficiently monitor all essential facets of biodiversity. Yet, species interactions are often overlooked in monitoring designs compared to spatial coverage and species richness, partly due to the inherent difficulty of sampling and monitoring interactions compared to species distributions. Here, we used simulations to test the efficiency of monitoring species interactions within Biodiversity Observations Networks (BONs). title: The Nexus Between Agriculture, Cattle Breeding and Climate Change in The Island of Crete, Greece
abstract: Climate change threatens human prosperity as it affects many economic sectors including food production. Agriculture, cattle breeding and climate change are interrelated and interconnected affecting each other. Agriculture in Crete was in the past an important pillar in the local economy while nowadays its role has been decreased. The linkages between food production and climate change in the island of Crete, Greece have been analyzed. It has been indicated that climate change affects crops, trees and cattle breeding in Crete. title: Influence of Nonpolar Amino Acids on Phase Transitions of Atmospheric Aerosol Particles
abstract: Abstract The fate of aerosol particles in the atmosphere depends, in part, on their composition, morphology, and phase transitions. Studies of aerosol phase transitions have focused on aerosol particles with organic compounds consisting of C, H, and O atoms, although a substantial fraction of organic compounds contains heteroatoms such as sulfur and nitrogen. In this study, nonpolar amino acids were used to study the effect of organonitrogen compounds on phase transitions of droplets using optical microscopy. abstract: Abstract The steel industry accounts for approximately 7–9% of global greenhouse gas emissions, making it a key sector for decarbonization. Here, we quantify current and prospective greenhouse gas emissions from crude steel production facilities worldwide. Based on life cycle assessment, current greenhouse gas emissions of global crude steel production are around 3.7 gigatonnes carbon dioxide equivalent per year, highly concentrated in Asia. title: Coupling of sedimentary environment and hazardous trace element enrichment in lacustrine oil shale: evidence from the Lunpola Basin, Tibetan Plateau, China
abstract: The Lunpola Basin, developed during the Cenozoic era on the Tibetan Plateau, serves not only as a sedimentary record of plateau uplift but also as a significant reservoir of oil shale. This study focuses on the sedimentary environment of the oil shales in the Lunpola Basin and the enrichment mechanisms of trace elements, particularly hazardous elements, within them. A total of 38 samples were analyzed for major elements, trace elements, total organic carbon (TOC), and total sulfur (TS). title: UVC-LED Disinfection Technology: Mainstream Waveband Characteristics, Applications and Challenges
abstract: Driven by the global demand for public health security, ultraviolet C light-emitting diode (UVC-LED) disinfection technology has emerged as a promising mercury-free alternative to conventional methods. Adopting a wavelength-based comparative framework, this review systematically synthesizes the disinfection characteristics of four mainstream UVC-LED wavelength bands (233 nm, 254 nm, 260–270 nm, and 270–280 nm), facilitating direct cross-band comparison of inactivation mechanisms, biosafety profiles, and practical applicability. title: The volcanic history of the late Pleistocene Shamao complex, Tatun Volcano Group, northern Taiwan
abstract: Abstract Although the Tatun Volcanic Group (TVG) looms over the metropolitan capital region of Taiwan, the threats it poses are only vaguely known. Here, as a first step toward improving understanding those threats, we investigate the Shamao complex, one of the youngest and smallest features of the TVG. title: Municipal Libraries as Community Learning Spaces: A Model for Educational Resource Management in Western Visayas
abstract: This mixed-methods study used a triangulation design to evaluate municipal libraries in Western Visayas as vital community learning spaces. The paper emphasized libraries' transformative role in supporting lifelong learning and social engagement in the digital age. Thirty-seven librarians and library staff participated in quantitative data collection, while fifteen librarians took part in qualitative interviews. title: Production and Characterization of Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) from an Agricultural By-Product Using Bacillus thuringiensis CICIM (B2031)
abstract: The widespread overuse of petroleum plastics has led to serious environmental challenges. This has necessitated the pursuit of greener alternatives that would reduce or eliminate mankind’s unsustainable and toxic dependence on the recalcitrant petroleum plastics. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) is a potential substitute candidate for the production of biodegradable plastics. In this study, Bacillus thuringiensis CICIM (B2031) was utilized for the production of PHB using the agricultural by-product corn silage as a carbon source. title: Combined toxicity of cyanotoxins and anthropogenic contaminants on Chlorella vulgaris: insights from single and binary mixture exposures
abstract: Aquatic organisms in eutrophic brackish and freshwater systems are chronically exposed to natural and anthropogenic contaminants, including cyanotoxins, metals and pesticides, mainly driven by cyanobacterial blooms and human activities. However, the environmental risks posed by their combinations to the aquatic environment remain poorly understood. This study investigated the growth response of Chlorella vulgaris exposed to four single-chemical compounds (microcystin-LR, cylindrospermopsin, terbuthylazine, and cadmium) and five binary mixtures for 7 days. title: Autobiografía beat: la reescritura de los mitos beat en Recollections of My Life as a Woman de Diane di Prima
abstract: Por su cuidadosa atención a la construcción subjetiva, su relación ambigua con el Künstlerroman y su empeño en los detalles en lo que se refiere a la descripción de la comunidad artística neoyorquina, la autobiografía de la poeta beat Diane di Prima es un texto clave en el acervo de este movimiento contracultural de mediados del siglo xx. title: Patronage and Accounting Between the Philippines and China, 1733–1797
abstract: Abstract Missionary efforts followed the expansion of the Old World’s frontiers, often entwined with trade. This article reviews the accounts of the Franciscan mission in China and of the obras pías of Manila during the eighteenth century to analyse how local conditions and empire-wide structures translated into specific actions on the ground. title: Urban Memory and Experiential Learning in Architectural Education
abstract: This paper proposes a workshop-based framework that applies experiential learning to the interpretation of urban memory through the travel narratives of three visitors to the Turkish city of Trabzon. Grounded in Kolb’s (1984) experiential learning cycle, this study examines a workshop in which architectural students transformed textual narratives into experiential and representational learning processes. title: Genre Asymmetry and Diasporic Meaning in English-Language Literary Scholarship: Poetry, Fiction, and Critical Attention, 2000-2025
abstract: This PRISMA-informed qualitative thematic review examines recurring patterns in a selective corpus of English-language literary scholarship published from 2000 to 2025 across poetry, fiction, life writing, and performance. Rather than claiming a statistically representative survey of the entire field, it analyzes scholarship itself as an organized pattern of critical attention. title: Consumer perceptions and acceptance of fermented aquatic foods: A systematic scoping review
abstract: Fermented aquatic foods are increasingly recognised for their potential to enhance food quality, functionality, and shelf life while supporting innovation in sustainable food systems. However, evidence on consumer perceptions and acceptance remains fragmented. This systematic scoping review synthesised evidence on consumer perceptions and acceptance of fermented aquatic foods from 30 eligible studies. abstract: A transição energética contemporânea tem impulsionado a busca por alternativas capazes de reduzir a dependência de fontes fósseis e ampliar a participação de recursos renováveis nos sistemas energéticos. abstract: The estimation of Post-Mortem Interval (PMI) remains a global challenge, but the estimation of Post-Mortem Submersion Interval (PMSI) in cases of drowning or those submerged from aquatic ecosystems is still particularly difficult. title: Halophytes-associated endophytic fungi for sustainable development
abstract: Abstract Halophytes, naturally adapted to survive and grow under high-salinity conditions, harbour complex internal microbiomes composed of endophytic microorganisms that persist within plant tissues without causing disease. Among these, endophytic fungi play a crucial role in enhancing host plant growth and stress tolerance. Halophytes host a diverse community of endophytic fungi that are naturally adapted to extreme saline and arid environments. abstract: The increasing complexity of maritime logistics activities requires an integrated information system to support efficient container movement management. PT. Perusahaan Pelayaran Nusantara Panurjwan (Samudera Indonesia Group) utilizes the Shipping Information System (SIS) as a digital solution to improve operational effectiveness, information accuracy, and coordination among stakeholders involved in container transportation. abstract: This study determined the level of awareness, the extent of integration, and the degree of challenges encountered by science teachers in integrating the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into science instruction. title: Examining Relationships Among Sexual Self-Schemas, Attachment Dimensions in Close Relationships, and Sexual Compulsivity Among Young Adults
abstract: This study investigated associations among sexual self-schemas, attachment-related anxiety and avoidance in close relationships, and sexual compulsivity among young adults. The main study variables were sexual self-schemas, attachment dimensions, and sexual compulsivity, with particular attention to relationships among their respective subscales. title: Heritage everywhere and nowhere: displaced heritage discourse in Swedish hydropower transitions
abstract: Hydropower infrastructures are central to sustainability transitions but are also embedded in historically layered landscapes of meaning, identity, and governance. This article examines how cultural heritage is mobilised and constrained in the relicensing of Swedish hydropower facilities under the National Plan for Modern Environmental Conditions (NAP). abstract: Abstract Comparison of cellulose 14 C of the growth rings 1962–1965 of Norwegian Scots pine with Norwegian atmospheric 14 CO 2 over these bomb spike years indicates that tree rings can provide a good proxy for atmospheric 14 CO 2 . The sub-seasonal cellulose 14 C values of five trees from 63° to 69° N reveal local atmospheric 14 CO 2 values for the growing seasons 1950–1965. abstract: Abstract: This paper explores the social and spatial mechanisms of two community festivals regarded as cultural capitals through a comparative lens. One is the floating Hikiyama in the Karatsu Kunchi festival in Karatsu City, Japan; the other is the revival of the creation and procession of Sapao in Chiang Mai, Thailand. abstract: The cooling system of an injection molding machine plays a critical role in the production process by preventing overheating during injection molding. If the cooling system malfunctions or ceases to operate for even 5 to 10 minutes, the mold becomes overheated, causing the molded parts to stick—a scenario that results in both lost production time and wasted material. abstract: Abstract Emissions of nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO 2 ), a precursor to ozone and secondary aerosol formation have become increasingly important to understand as ozone production transitions to NO x limited in most regions of the US. Recent studies suggest that NO x emissions associated with agricultural activities, particularly cropland soils, are an increasingly important contributor. title: SMONG'S NARRATIVE IN THE CHILDREN'S BOOK "ITAM AND U": INTERTEXTUALITY, SIGNS OF NATURE, AND DISASTER EDUCATION
abstract: This study analyzes the representation and function of smong narrative in the children's book "Itam and U" as a disaster literacy media based on local culture. Smong is an oral tradition from Simeulue that functions as a tsunami early warning system through poetry and collective memory. Using a computer-aided qualitative content analysis approach, the study extracted and analyzed text from 48 pages of the book to identify patterns of smong representation, nature signs, and disaster risk reduction education. title: Effect of Selected Food Crop Outputs on Poverty Level of Farm Households in Rivers State
abstract: This study examined the effect of selected food crop outputs on poverty level of farm households in Rivers State. The primary data of the study were collected from a sample of 820 respondents based on the copies of questionnaires completed and returned. The data collected were analyzed using binary logit regression involving the odd ratios and marginal effects. The estimated binary logit results showed that yam production decreases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.028%. The results showed that an increase in cassava production increases the probability of poverty reduction by 0.034%.

title: Review on Comparative Analysis of Geoponics and Hydroponics Cultivation Methodology for the Enrichment of Leafy Vegetable
abstract: Geoponics refers to growth of plants in soil, which is the traditional method of agriculture, While soil less cultivation stands for hydroponics (growing in water) and aeroponics (growing in air). In present scenario hydroponic techniques have proven to be far more efficient and crucial to geoponics. title: Challenging the Terra Mamaizinha–Terra Longe dichotomy: Migration, Gender, and islandness in Nha Fala, Vitalina Varela, and Hanami
abstract: This article examines how contemporary films from and about Cape Verde articulate new poetics of islandness at the intersection of migration and gender. Focusing on Nha Fala (Flora Gomes, 2002), Vitalina Varela (Pedro Costa, 2019), and Hanami (Denise Fernandes, 2024), it combines perspectives from Island, Migration, and Gender Studies to analyse how islandness is shaped by mobility, absence, and return. title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. title: Economic, environmental and public health impacts of gas flaring in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria
abstract: Over the past six decades, billions of cubic feet of gases associated with crude oil exploration have been flared. Unfortunately, gas flaring has continued despite successive legislative interventions, with limited implementation of effective remediation strategies in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria. Gas flaring involves the combustion of associated gases produced during oil extraction, which contain particulate matter (soot), carbon dioxide, sulfur oxides (SOx), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and volatile organic compounds. abstract: Domestic boreholes are essential for self-supply in cities with inadequate public water services. This study examines household practices and perceptions of borehole water in Lambanyi, Conakry, Guinea. A descriptive cross-sectional survey covered 383 households in four neighbourhoods from 5 to 25 June 2024. Data collected through a Microsoft Forms questionnaire were processed in Microsoft Excel using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended responses. abstract: Abstract The present study reports the first records of the viviparous monogeneans Gyrodactylus atratuli and Gyrodactylus mediotorus from leuciscid fishes in Mexico, providing new insights into intraspecific haptoral sclerite variability across hosts and geographic regions in North America. abstract: Abstract Natural product (NP)-based chemical libraries are a rich source of antiviral compounds that can serve as the basis for new therapeutic leads to treat viral diseases, particularly for individuals lacking sustained access to existing vaccines and therapeutics. To identify new NP-based candidate inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 cellular entry and viral replication, we screened the pan-African Natural Products Library (p-ANAPL), a collection of physical pure compounds obtained from African medicinal plants, for NPs that can disrupt the in vitro interaction of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike receptor-binding

title: Hydrogel application as a soil amendment to mitigate water deficiency effects on flaxseed cultivars grown in sandy soils
abstract: Abstract Water scarcity is a major constraint for flax production in Egypt’s sandy soils. This research aims to investigate the use of hydrogels, as water-absorbing polymers can enhance soil moisture retention and improve crop performance under water deficit conditions, thereby increasing flax yield and seed quality. Two field experiments were conducted during the 2022/2023 and 2023/2024 winter seasons at the National Research Centre, Al Nubaria, Egypt, to evaluate the effects of hydrogel (0 and 80 kg/ha) on three flax cultivars (Giza-11, Giza-12, Sakha-3) under full water irrigation quantity

title: Assessing the impacts of scientific theatre on the audience
abstract: Climate change communication aims to enhance climate literacy, strengthen public engagement, and foster attitudinal and behavioural change. Yet, its effects are rarely evaluated in a systematic way. This study applies a mixed-methods approach to assess the impacts of an arts-based activity on the audience using a combination of surveys and post-performance debates. title: Floristic Diversity and Ethnomedicinal Importance of Vaatangi Sacred Grove, Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Sacred groves are patches of forest under community based protection, revered as the abode of local deities and maintained through indigenous cultural beliefs. The present study documents the floristic diversity and ethnomedicinal significance of the Vaatangi Sacred Grove located in Rajavommangi Mandal, Alluri Sitaramaraju District, Andhra Pradesh, India. The grove, presided over by Lord Shiva, encompasses one hectare of dry deciduous forest with a documented history exceeding 100 years. abstract: Abstract A well-preserved late Hellenistic workshop in the agora of Kos provides a rare opportunity to examine pigment production embedded in a multicrafting setting. Excavations of a room in the eastern stoa have revealed fire-structures, Egyptian blue pellets, a range of mineral earth pigments, litharge rods, lead slag, tools and other production debris, demonstrating both pigment manufacture and lead metallurgy within a single workshop space. title: Recent geographic dispersal and environmental adaptation of indica rice
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa), one of the key domesticated cereal crops, is comprised of several subspecies or variety groups. A major variety group, O. sativa var. indica was domesticated in the Indian subcontinent ∼4500 years ago via introgression of domestication alleles from var. japonica and today represents the predominant rice that is grown worldwide, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions in Asia. abstract: Exploring the patterns of biodiversity across multiple facets of river ecosystems and their driving factors is crucial for biodiversity conservation. As the most important tributary of the lower Lancang River, the Buyuan River remains largely unexplored in terms of systematic research on its fish diversity patterns and driving factors. abstract: O objetivo deste trabalho foi avaliar o efeito do ácido salicílico na germinação de sementes e crescimento inicial de Vachellia caven (Molina) Seigler & Ebinger expostas ao estresse salino. title: The surgical symphony of human efficiency: a structured intraoperative workflow model for high-volume cochlear implant missions
abstract: OBJECTIVE: High-volume humanitarian Cochlear Implant (CI) missions require highly organized workflows to maintain efficiency and safety. This study describes the intraoperative model used during a large-scale CI campaign. METHODS: A descriptive observational design was used to evaluate operative workflow across multiple operating rooms using standardized surgical protocols, structured shift-based assignments, and digital coordination. title: Infrastructures of differential inclusion: accommodation access for displaced persons in Italy
abstract: This article examines how Italian migration policies are translated in accommodation infrastructures at a local level. Applying the perspective of differential inclusion, it compares institutional reception pathways for people displaced from Ukraine under the Temporary Protection Directive (TPD) with ordinary asylum procedures. abstract: The shared socio-economic pathways (SSPs) provide storylines for plausible future global developments under a consistent set of assumptions. Primarily, the SSPs have been used to derive quantitative scenarios of greenhouse gas emissions for use in general circulation models and other large-scale, physically based models of environmental change. abstract: A green and efficient method was developed for propranolol delivery utilizing manganese‐based bioactive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as biocompatible drug carriers. Mn‐based bioactive MOFs with a high aspect ratio were synthesized and characterized for size (average, 17 µm), morphology, stability, elemental composition, crystallinity, functionality, charge character, and biocompatibility (a protein adsorption capacity of 0.03 µg µg −1 (5 h) and a hemolysis ratio of < 0.5%). title: TRANSFORMING THE IMAGE: REFUGEEHOOD, AESTHETICS AND THE POLITICS OF EQUALITY
abstract: At the centre of the image representing refugeehood are bodies forced to leave their homelands. Yet the political significance of refugee images cannot be inferred from visibility alone: visual representations may document suffering while also fixing refugeehood within recognizable figures of tragedy, victimhood, and helplessness. This article asks how different visual regimes configure the relation between the refugee, the image, and the spectator, and under what aesthetic conditions that relation may become a site of political subjectivation rather than the reproduction of victimhood.
