abstract: This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of elementary school heads in School Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (SDRRM) in the Fourth Congressional District of Quezon, Philippines, during School Year 2024–2025, as a basis for developing a School Safety Manual. Anchored on the Knowledge–Attitude–Practice Theory and Comprehensive School Safety Framework, the study employed a quantitative descriptive–correlational design involving 38 elementary school heads selected through cluster sampling. abstract: In the 1920s, Rio de Janeiro emerged as a cosmopolitan capital marked by rapid urban development and profound social change. During this period, women experienced greater freedom of movement and expanded opportunities for participation in social life outside the home. abstract: Abstract Calculating equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) requires simulations of a thousand years or more for the climate to re‐establish equilibrium, but most ECS estimates are derived from shorter model integrations. The widely used “Gregory method” for such estimates systematically underestimates ECS, a bias previously attributed to the time‐dependence of climate feedbacks. abstract: This study investigated the impact of electronic permit-to-work (e-PTW) systems on operational efficiency in the Nigerian oil and gas industry. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, and a questionnaire survey was used as the instrument for data collection. Collaboration, productivity, communication and error reduction were constructs used to capture operational efficiency. abstract: Hexastylis viridistylis (Aristolochiaceae) is described as a novel species distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of morphological characters including style and ovary color and dimensions, stamen morphology, calyx tube dimensions, and fruiting characteristics. abstract: Este trabajo reconstruye los orígenes de la simulación computacional aplicada a la planificación socioeconómica en América Latina durante la década de 1960. abstract: Climate change is increasingly affecting Pakistan’s livelihoods, human mobility, economic stability, and national security. This study examines the relationship between climate change, migration, and national security in Pakistan, focusing on how climate hazards disrupt livelihoods, generate displacement, and create wider security pressures. abstract: The emergence of life on our planet occurred somewhere before 3.48 billion years ago, and was predated by a poorly defined period of appearance and accumulation of chemical intermediates commonly known as biomolecules - which includes amino acids, lipids, sugars and components of genetic polymers. abstract: Haberlea rhodopensis Friv. (Gesneriaceae) is a Tertiary glacial relict endemic to the Balkan Peninsula and belongs to the rare group of vascular resurrection plants capable of successfully withstanding long periods of almost complete drought. In addition, the species is valued for its multiple applications as a rich source of various biologically active compounds and as an ornamental plant in rock gardens. abstract: Since the 1890s, the Danish Single Grave Culture (SGC; c. 2850-2350 BCE) has been recognised as a distinct cultural complex with its core area centred on the sandy regions in Mid and Western Jutland, often associated with a pastoral-based economy. However, the absence of animal bone material from this area seriously constrains interpretations of prehistoric subsistence strategies and human-animal relations. abstract: Cocos is well-known as a cash crop across the world for its beans. Its fruit weight influences both the internal and external characteristics of the pod. The objective of this study was to study the physical properties of pods and beans under Gazipur conditions of Bangladesh and observe the effect of fruit size on the physical attributes of cocoa pods and beans. abstract: Abstract Objective The implications of climate change are unfolding in riverine systems, carrying consequences for fish populations and further challenging fisheries management. abstract: Boiruna sertaneja is a large snake primarily associated with the Caatinga and recognized for its pronounced ophiophagy. This study evaluated the extraction yields, qualitative phytochemical compositions, and cytotoxicity of sixteen medicinal plant species traditionally used for tumor management in Northwestern Nigeria to prioritize candidates for anticancer bioprospecting. abstract: Abstract Latrinalia, or the study of messages left in restrooms, provides a unique record of shared communication among message writers within gendered spaces. Drawing on a conventional content analysis of 1,378 messages left in the women’s restroom of a mid-sized Midwestern university from January 2022 through November 2023, this study contributes to an understanding of women’s lived experience by identifying themes that illuminate how restroom users enact, resist, or reinterpret gender roles, especially within gendered spaces. title: Temporal shifts in insect cuticular hydrocarbons in response to experimental desiccation
abstract: Insects are vulnerable to desiccation as they are small and have a high surface area-to-volume ratios. Over 80% of their body water is lost through the cuticle, but insects possess specialised cells that synthesize cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) to form a hydrophobic waxy barrier that reduces water loss. However, how rapidly CHCs are synthesized and transported across the cuticle under desiccating conditions remains poorly understood. abstract: This research article analyzes the U.S. military operation “Absolute Resolve” on Janu- ary 3, 2026, which resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife by Delta Force units supported by air and naval assets. Employing a qualitative interpretive case- study design, the study examines the event through five analytical levels: civilizational, geopoliti- cal, international relations, political philosophy, and military. abstract: Over the past decade, the construction industry has increasingly prioritized climate neutrality. In line with this, the EU Green Deal and its ‘Fit-for-55’ legislative package aim to reduce total emissions by 55% by 2030. A major challenge in achieving this goal is addressing the embodied carbon of building materials, which arises from production, transportation, and end-of-life stages. abstract: Healthcare-associated neonatal sepsis is one of the main causes of morbidity and mortality among newborns hospitalised in neonatal intensive care units. The study therefore aimed to analyse nursing interventions for the prevention of healthcare-associated neonatal sepsis. A literature review guided by PRISMA was conducted in SciELO, PubMed, Redalyc and Google Scholar, with a sample of 20 studies published between 2020 and 2025 in Spanish and English. title: Travel history and occupation among diagnosed Cutaneous Leishmaniasis cases in Guyana: A multi-site retrospective case series, 2017–2021
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (CL) in Guyana has not been systematically characterised in the peer-reviewed literature for several decades. This study aimed to describe the demographic, occupational, geographic, and clinical profile of diagnosed CL cases at Guyana's principal diagnostic sites, and to test, within this case series, whether field-based occupation is associated with reported interior travel and whether travel history is associated with time to presentation. title: Ultraviolet Fluorescence of a Black Horse Fly (Tabanus atratus) Larva
abstract: Many insects fluoresce when exposed to ultraviolet light, and it is becoming a useful tool for surveys. The availability of low-cost ultraviolet flashlights and their ease of use is providing an opportunity for researchers and citizen scientists to explore fluorescence in insects. This note reports the ultraviolet fluorescence of a Tabanus atratus (Black Horse Fly) larva.

abstract: The rhizosphere is a very favourable environment for the presence of a wide range of microorganisms, which allow many beneficial interactions between the plants and microorganisms. Bacillus species are known as plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to improve the growth and productivity of plants, among these microbes. abstract: The processing of cassava for human consumption leads to the generation of large quantities of cassava peel waste. The continuous accumulation of these peels has contributed to environmental pollution, thereby placing significant pressure on waste management systems. This study aimed to assess the biodegradation potentials of Aspergillus niger and Bacillus subtilis, individually and in combination, using cassava peels as the substrate. title: Ritual as regulatory technology: governing change and the embedded circular economy in Balinese living heritage
abstract: Abstract Balinese temple restoration is commonly interpreted through symbolism, belief, and architectural tradition, yet such readings leave how ritual regulates material action insufficiently examined. This article reconceptualises ritual as a regulatory technology: a procedural infrastructure that authorises intervention, defines thresholds of acceptable change, and structures material circulation within living heritage. title: Oportunidades y Barreras de la Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria frente al Desarrollo Sostenible en América Latina: Una Revisión Exploratoria
abstract: Introducción: La Economía Social, Popular y Solidaria (ESPS) abarca una serie de prácticas colectivas que parecen contribuir al Desarrollo Sostenible (DS) pero cuya evidencia se encuentra dispersa en América Latina. title: Trastorno disfórico premenstrual y su manejo con terapias alternativas
abstract: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) causes severe emotional and physical symptoms in the luteal phase that impair quality of life. The study therefore aimed to analyse the available scientific evidence on the use of complementary and alternative therapies in the management of PMDD. A systematic review guided by PRISMA was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science, with a sample of five systematic reviews on acupuncture and herbal medicine. abstract: Abstract This paper identifies and traces a persistent yet largely unrecognized literary motif that I call “late-life worldbuilding.” Alongside the familiar portrayal of old age as a condition of physical decline and retrospective wisdom, the western literary tradition repeatedly imagines elderly protagonists embarking on visionary journeys toward the creation of new worlds and new forms of life. title: Traditional preservation practices of asala fish (Schizothorax spp.) among Himalayan communities of Darjeeling, India
abstract: Abstract Traditional fish preservation practices are an important part of the cultural heritage and food systems of the Darjeeling Himalayas. In this study, the traditional methods used by local communities to preserve asala fish ( Schizothorax spp.) have been documented. Data were collected from the 50 respondents over the age of 18 including fish farmers, hatchery operators, fish processors, traders, and household members engaged in fish production, preservation, and marketing. title: Drivers of the likelihood of evolutionary rescue in response to novel infectious diseases
abstract: The introduction of novel infectious diseases has caused significant declines in many species, and in some cases, local extinction. Simultaneously, hosts might adapt to these novel pathogens, allowing population recovery, an example of evolutionary rescue (ER). Novel infectious diseases differ from sudden, abiotic stressors in that disease only impacts a subset of individuals within the population and individuals might be affected for a finite period. title: Climate change threatens montane and cloud forest tree species in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
abstract: Abstract Montane and cloud forests are high-elevation ecosystems dependent on specific environmental conditions and increasingly threatened by fragmentation, isolation, and climate change in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. We quantified changes in climatic suitability for two characteristic tree species of these ecosystems, Drimys angustifolia and Ilex microdonta , under future climate scenarios, assessing range contraction and expansion, potential losses of suitable areas, and opportunities for ecological restoration. abstract: Abstract The Irish immigrant experience in 19th-century North America is often framed in terms of processes of oppression and racialization. abstract: There has been no dearth of interest in the politics of IPTA in Indian intellectual circles. abstract: Abstract This paper examines how news media textually and visually represented the protests, arrests, and criminal trials of climate activists in the U.S., U.K., and Sweden during the early-2020s—a period of heightened anti-climate reactionary backlash in response to the progressive and transnational climate movement of the 2010s. abstract: Unscripted dialogic campaign programs remain underexplored as integrated political marketing strategies for candidate positioning and youth engagement. This study analyzes the political marketing mix of “Desak Anies” during the 2024 Indonesian presidential election, examining its role in candidate image construction and young voter mobilization. title: Parmotrema trippianum (Parmeliaceae): a Morphologically Distinct New Species in the P. reticulatum Complex and Key to North American Parmotrema with Salazinic Acid
abstract: Parmotrema trippianum sp. nov. is described as new to science and named in honor of the lichenologist, botanist, and biodiversity scientist Dr. Erin Manzitto-Tripp. The new species grows on rocks in rich, mesic, montane canyons in the Colorado Front Range of the southern Rocky Mountains and the Chiricahua Mountains of Arizona. Phylogenetically, it is a member of the Parmotrema reticulatum species complex, and indeed, does share some morphological similarities with members of this species complex, including the production of medullary salazinic acid, reticulate maculae, and submarginal soredia.

abstract: Dental caries is one of the most frequent chronic diseases of childhood and affects children's eating, well-being and school performance. abstract: Hypertension affects about one in four Kenyan adults, yet only 15.5% of those affected are aware of their status. title: Técnica de Bass modificada y estrategias lúdicas para prevenir la gingivitis infantil en un orfanato de Riobamba
abstract: Gingivitis is common at school age and is preventable through adequate oral hygiene. The objective was to synthesize the evidence on gingivitis prevention in children to support an educational program for children aged 8 to 10 years at the San Carlos orphanage in Riobamba. A narrative literature review was conducted in PubMed, Scopus and SciELO; 19 documents were analyzed, and an initial educational activity at the orphanage was described. title: Host–virus interactions dominate fitness and conceal additive genetic variation
abstract: Host-parasite coevolution is expected to generate strong selection for resistance and infectivity that has the potential to erode genetic variation. Despite this, natural populations often retain extensive genetic variation in these traits. Genotype-by-genotype interactions on fitness can generate negative frequency-dependent selection, which helps maintain this variation by preventing any host or pathogen genotype from retaining a permanent advantage. title: Circular economy effects-a literature review
abstract: This paper is intended to present the current state of research on the effects of the circular economy. Thereupon, the research field is analysed for possible shortages in the literature. To ensure practicable results on CE effects, a review protocol was used covering relevant publications released between 2021 and 2025. Our study provides a theoretical/conceptual framework based on secondary literature rather than new empirical data. title: Purple Phototrophic Bacteria as a Novel Platform for Coenzyme Q10 Production from CO2, Syngas, and Sulfur Waste Byproducts
abstract: Abstract The efficient conversion of CO2 and industrial waste streams into value-added products remains a critical challenge for sustainable microbial processes. Here, we present the first systematic demonstration of purple phototrophic bacteria (PPB) as platforms for the autotrophic valorization of CO2 and industrial off-gases or sulfur byproducts into valuable metabolites. Genome-guided screening combined with experimental validation identified strains capable of coupling photoautotrophic growth with the production of CoQ10 and carotenoid pigments. title: Development of a Mountain Landscape Conservation Model Based on Local Knowledge and Indigenous Identity to Support Environmental Sustainability at Mount Ebulobo
abstract: Mountain landscapes are complex socio-ecological systems where ecological processes, cultural values, local knowledge, and community practices interact to shape environmental sustainability. This study aims to develop a mountain landscape conservation model based on local knowledge and Indigenous identity to support environmental sustainability at Mount Ebulobo. A mixed-methods approach was employed, integrating field observation, interviews, focus group discussions, and structured questionnaires. title: Integrative multiomic characterization of the methylome and restriction-modification repertoire of Mycoplasma hyorhinis SK76
abstract: Restriction-modification (R-M) systems are widespread in Mycoplasma species, contributing to defense against foreign DNA and epigenetic regulation. However, the limited genetic tractability of Mollicutes hinders the functional characterization of R-M systems. Here, we characterized the R-M repertoire of Mycoplasma hyorhinis SK76 by integrating comparative genomics, structural modeling, quantitative proteomics, and genome-wide methylome profiling. title: Growth, hydrogen production, and community dynamics of Rhodopseudomonas palustris cultivated in forward osmosis-concentrated municipal sewage
abstract: Abstract Municipal sewage represents a sustainable resource for biohydrogen production; however, its direct application is hindered by low concentrations of soluble organic matter and elevated ammonium levels, which suppress nitrogenase activity. In this study, municipal sewage was concentrated approximately 20-fold by forward osmosis (FO) prior to cultivation experiments. title: Muslim Students Trust in Government Institutions: The Role of Religiosity, Administrative Transparency, and Public Service Quality in a Muslim-Majority Context
abstract: Public trust in government institutions is a key element in achieving effective governance, particularly among the educated youth within a Muslim-majority societal context. In this regard, the formation of public trust is influenced not only by administrative performance but also by the social and religious values inherent in citizens. University students hold a strategic position as they are both users of public services and future bureaucratic actors and leaders. title: Biological and Ecotoxicological Responses of Daphnia pulex to 2,4-D and Malathion-Contaminated Laboratory Microcosms
abstract: Industrialization, urbanization, and agricultural practices have substantially increased the accumulation of contaminants in the environment, often adversely affecting nontarget aquatic species. Cladoceran species are considered valuable bioindicators in ecotoxicity studies because they are easy to culture, have transparent bodies, and are highly sensitive to chemical pollution. This study aimed to determine the acute and chronic toxicity of two selected pesticides, namely Malathion 50 EC (a.i., Malathion) and 2,4-D ethyl ester 38% EC (a.i., 2,4-D), to Daphnia pulex. title: Contemporary Management of Human‐Caused Hybridization in Mammals: A Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Anthropogenic hybridization (AH) is increasingly recognized as a conservation issue, as human activities facilitate interbreeding between previously isolated mammalian taxa, potentially threatening genetic integrity and population viability. Aims We synthesize current knowledge on AH in mammals, with the aim to fill a knowledge gap on how to address AH and assess the feasibility of management interventions. title: Clinical and Microbiological Features of Acinetobacter lwoffii Bacteremia in Children: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Objective: Acinetobacter lwoffii is an environmental organism and skin commensal with low intrinsic virulence. We describe the clinical, laboratory, and microbiological features of pediatric A. lwoffii bacteremia. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 50 pediatric patients aged 2 months to 18 years whose blood cultures grew A. lwoffii at a tertiary pediatric center between January 2015 and December 2023. title: Climate Adaptation as Politics under Hybrid Governance: Risk Redistribution and Local Authority Resilience in Sweden
abstract: Abstract Climate change increasingly generates conditions of persistent governance turbulence, placing growing demands on local authorities as frontline risk managers while simultaneously exposing them to new forms of vulnerability. Despite extensive knowledge about climate risks and growing policy attention, climate adaptation remains unevenly implemented and institutionally fragmented. This article conceptualises adaptation as a governance process embedded in hybrid, multi-level governance arrangements and examines how such arrangements shape local authority resilience. title: El Estado estratégico: el surgimiento de un nuevo modelo de Estado a nivel europeo
abstract: El presente trabajo sostiene que, en la actualidad, se han producido fenómenos políticos, económicos y sociales que transforman profundamente a la Unión y los Estados. En concreto, se identifican varias tendencias –geopolitización, securitización y supranacionalización– que explican la configuración de un Derecho europeo orientado a la consecución de nuevos fines: autonomía estratégica, resiliencia y defensa. abstract: Abstract Hunting American black bears ( Ursus americanus ) for the Penobscot Nation, an Indigenous tribe located in Maine, USA, is a regulated process that respects both traditional customs and contemporary wildlife management practices. Each year, the Penobscot Department of Natural Resources (DNR) manages a spring bear hunt on 7 Tribal Trust properties of varying size across the state. abstract: The nutritional status of Ascophyllum nodosum powdered seaweed, as a natural dietary supplement, was evaluated on common carp (Cyprinus carpio) in terms of productive performance, FER, blood parameters and selected biochemical parameters in the present study. The fish were randomly divided among 4 treatment groups: non-supplemented (control), 5g/kg, 10 g/kg and 15 g/kg of the powdered form of A. nodosum. title: Implementation Challenges of Environmental Laws in Bangladesh: A Critical Analysis with Case Studies and Judicial Perspectives
abstract: Bangladesh is considered as one of the most environmentally vulnerable countries in the world and faces serious risks from industrial pollution, rapid unplanned development, river encroachment, and the growing impacts of climate change. To protect and improve the quality of the environment, a wide range of environmental laws have been enacted, such as the Bangladesh Environment Conservation Act of 1995, the Environment Court Act of 2010 and several sector-specific regulations. title: Secretome-dependent antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity of Lactobacillus johnsonii against multidrug-resistant Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli
abstract: Abstract Background: Enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) is a leading cause of persistent diarrhea in children in low- and middle-income countries, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains necessitates non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated Lactobacillus johnsonii , previously characterized by our group, as a probiotic candidate against a clinically confirmed MDR EAEC isolate resistant to ampicillin, ciprofloxacin, azithromycin, amoxicillin, and gentamicin. abstract: Brinjal requires the judicious application of fertilizers, particularly nitrogenous fertilizers for its satisfactory yield. abstract: Introduction: CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technology has revolutionized biomedical research, offering precise genomic manipulation. However, its translation into endodontics- specifically for biofilm disinfection and pulp-dentin regeneration- remains a subject of intense investigation and debate. Materials and Methods: A narrative review was conducted based on the electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar from the year of (2000 to 2026) to identify studies investigating CRISPR-Cas9 applications in endodontic pathogens and dental pulp stem cells. abstract: With the preparation of the FLEX satellite mission and other platforms providing quantitative measurements of solar-induced fluorescence (SIF), the calibration and validation (Cal/Val) of SIF products is becoming increasingly relevant. Owing to the dynamic nature of SIF, cross-validation requires synchronous data acquisition when performed on vegetated targets. title: Asymptotic behavior of lidar scattering properties of absorbing dust aerosols across Rayleigh and geometrical-optics regimes: theory and implications
abstract: Lidar ratio (S), linear depolarization ratio (δ), and single-scattering albedo (ω) are central quantities for dust typing and property retrieval in lidar remote sensing. We investigate their dependence on size parameter (x) and iron oxide fraction of mineral dust using TAMUdust2020 and triaxial-ellipsoid calculations. Results show a consistent asymptotic structure that is weakly sensitive to particle shape in both limits of scattering theory. title: The environmental aspect of eco-design in an urbanised area
abstract: The article outlines the background to the emergence of design and one of its promising areas – eco-design. The preconditions for the emergence of eco-design and the components on which it is based are examined. The paludarium, as a tool for shaping the contemporary physical and spatial environment within urbanised areas, can be regarded as one example of the application of eco-design in design practice. abstract: Las órdenes militares en el Oriente latino ejercieron un control sobre una población diversa que comprendía tanto a cristianos orientales de diferentes denominaciones como a musulmanes, judíos y francos. abstract: The study investigated the influence of capital market on infrastructure development in Nigeria, which utilized a quasi-experimental research design and time series yearly data from 1981 to 2025. Autoregressive distributed lag model (ARDL) was employed and the data of gross capital formation was proxy for infrastructure development, while instrument of capital market such as all share indexes, government stocks equity and corporate bond are utilized as independent variable in the study in order to determine the influence of capital market on infrastructure development in the country. title: Natural analogies and TRIZ
abstract: From the discipline of design science there are several design methods. One of this is the TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving). It is a very important method, because this so popular that man use this not only for technical problems but for agriculture, business, management, economic, marketing, social relations or any other human problems. This paper draws a parallel between TRIZ principles and nature analogies.

title: Electromagnetic Compatibility Testing of Military Ships
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing of military ships is an essential process for ensuring the correct and safe operation of electrical and electronic systems under complex operational conditions. This paper presents a methodology for assessing electromagnetic compatibility at the ship level, considering the vessel as an integrated system. The objectives include determining overall electromagnetic susceptibility, optimizing operations by reducing interference, and verifying the self-compatibility of installed equipment. abstract: Flowback and produced water (FPW) can serve as sustainable feedstock for the industrial chlor-alkali (CA) process, but elevated concentrations of multivalent cations and dissolved organic matter cause severe diaphragm and membrane fouling, scaling, and efficiency loss. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates significant Italian banks' exposure to climate‐related physical risks from the perspective of operational risk. Focusing on acute physical risks, proxied by floods and storms, the analysis adopts a microeconomic and spatial perspective to assess how the territorial distribution of banks' branches at the provincial (NUTS3) level interacts with the geographical incidence of extreme climate events. abstract: Autobiografía del algodón (2020) de Cristina Rivera Garza articula una escritura que entrelaza investigación archivística, memoria familiar y trabajo literario para reconstruir la historia del auge algodonero en el noreste mexicano, una huelga campesina borrada de los registros oficiales y la genealogía de una familia fronteriza. title: Radial glass/carbon layer sequencing in low-velocity impacted filament-wound hybrid composite pipes
abstract: Abstract The low-velocity impact response of hybrid glass/carbon filament-wound composite pipes with a nominal outside diameter of 24 mm was investigated experimentally, analytically and numerically. Two radial sequences, 45G45C and 45C45G, were tested at nominal conditions of 40, 60 and 80 J (n = 3 per condition). The 80 J condition also involved a higher impactor mass and momentum. title: Understanding Landslide Risk, Building Resilience: Integrating Science, Policy, and Practice for Safer Communities: The Sierra Leone Experience
abstract: Landslides are complex natural hazards resulting from interactions among geological, geomorphological, hydrological, climatic and anthropogenic processes. In Sierra Leone, these risks are intensified by rapid urbanisation, environmental degradation, inadequate land-use planning and limited institutional capacity. The 14 August 2017 Regent landslide in the Freetown Peninsula demonstrated the severe consequences of rainfall triggered slope failure interacting with flooding, infrastructure vulnerability and human exposure. title: Petrology and Geochemistry of Ciremai Volcano, West Java, Indonesia: Evidence of Open-System Magma Dynamics
abstract: Ciremai Volcano is the youngest active volcanic system within the Ciremai Volcanic Complex (CVC), located on the northern coast of West Java. This study aims to further investigate the characteristics of the magmatic system as part of the Sunda Arc. The activity of the CVC is divided into four periods: Putri Volcano, Gegerhalang Volcano, Wurung Crater, and Ciremai Volcano with its parasitic cones. abstract: Sitka spruce (Picea sitchensis [Bong.] Carr.) was introduced to Europe from the Pacific coast of North America in the early nineteenth century and has become an important commercial forest species in the Atlantic-climate zone of north-western Europe. title: Dynamics of abundance for chum salmon of Russian origin
abstract: Periods of high and low abundance are revealed in dynamics of the Russian chum salmon population in 1907–2025. The period of high abundance with recorded annual catches from 58,000 to 185,000 tons lasted from the mid-1920s to the mid-1960s, followed by the low abundance one with the catches from 21,000 to 70,000 tons lasting until the mid-2000s. Currently, the stocks are at a high level again.

title: Toll‐Like Receptor 4 Signaling in Natural N‐Acylethanolamines and Derivative NAE ‐Like Compounds: Mechanisms and Implications for Neuroimmune and Inflammatory Processes in a Systematic Search Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT N‐acylethanolamines (NAEs) are endogenous fatty acid amides structurally related to the endocannabinoid anandamide and function as bioactive lipid mediators with broad regulatory roles in inflammation and neuroinflammation. Among pattern‐recognition receptors, Toll‐like receptor 4 (TLR4) occupies a central position in innate immune surveillance, sensing pathogen‐associated molecular patterns, such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS), as well as damage‐associated molecular patterns. title: Evidence for funerary behaviour and lethal trauma in a new Neanderthal individual from Shanidar Cave
abstract: Abstract Shanidar Cave has long featured in debates concerning Neanderthal cognitive capacity and behaviour, including evidence for care and intentional burial. By identifying additional individuals, including Shanidar A reported here, new excavations have expanded a burial cluster first identified in 1960. Shanidar A, an older adult, was deposited around 75,000 years ago, decayed, and their skeletal remains were subsequently disturbed by a flash flood. title: La instrumentalización del diseño gráfico en la industria musical: de la experiencia material al consumo digital.
abstract: Este artículo analiza la transformación del diseño gráfico dentro de la industria musical a partir del desplazamiento de los soportes físicos hacia los entornos digitales. Desde una perspectiva histórica y critica, mediante una revisión documental cualitativa, se examina el trayecto de la portada musical como objeto material y comercial hacia su condición contemporánea de imagen integrada en interfaces digitales y sistemas de recomendación. title: Production Risk and Productivity of Smallholder Onion Farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the production risks and productivity of smallholder onion farmers in Taraba State, Nigeria. The study specifically analyzed the production risk associated with onion production for each input, assessed the contribution of major production inputs to onion output, and estimated the returns to scale in onion production. A multistage sampling procedure was used to select 254 onion farmers from Jalingo, Ardo-Kola, and Wukari Local Government Areas of Taraba State. title: The Fragmentation of War and Peace: Rethinking Peace Processes in a Polycentric World
abstract: This Special Issue argues that fragmentation is a structuring condition of contemporary conflict, operating within domestic conflict systems and across the international order. Domestically, authority is dispersed among elites, armed groups, and civic actors; internationally, peacebuilding frameworks have given way to parallel mediation, regionalised intervention, and competing geopolitical projects. title: Experimentos Mentales y Racionalismo Modal: una evaluación crítica del enfoque de Chalmers
abstract: “Thought experiments” are common in many scientific disciplines and can have significant theoretical consequences. However, we know they can fail, which leads to the question of how to establish that a thought experiment legitimately achieves its result. Given the modal dimension of thought experiments, one plausible option is to address this question within the framework of a particular modal epistemology. title: Fabrication of a paper-based microextraction tool for monitoring volatile emission associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: Abstract Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ), an opportunistic bacterial pathogen, causes severe respiratory infections. Rapid detection of bacterial species is important for switching from broad-spectrum to narrow-spectrum antibiotics when antimicrobial resistance is present. Here, we designed paper-based hydrophilic-lipophilic balance/divinylbenzene/polydimethylsiloxane polymer-coated TF-SPME patches and integrated them into a bacterial culture to extract volatile emissions associated with the P. aeruginosa (ATCC 27853) strain. title: Vivencia de la sinodalidad en clave de pastoral de engendramiento: Una reflexión teológico-pastoral desde el ver-juzgar-actuar
abstract: This article offers a theological-pastoral reflection on synodality as a constitutive form of ecclesial being, interpreted through the lens of generative pastoral care based on the contributions of Philippe Bacq and Christoph Theobald. The objective is to address synodality as a theological-pastoral response to current challenges using the theological method of hermeneutical circularity (seeing-judging-acting) for the revitalization of the Church's evangelizing mission. title: Leveraging Cultural Events for Destination Branding: Assessing the Impact of the Radin Jambat Festival on the Image of Way Kanan Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the strategic role of cultural festivals in shaping destination image within the context of emerging tourism regions in Indonesia. Specifically, it examines the influence of the Radin Jambat Festival on the destination image of Way Kanan Regency, Lampung Province. Utilizing a quantitative approach, this research surveyed 95 respondents who attended the festival. Data were analyzed using Simple Linear Regression via SPSS. title: Optimization of Zn(II)-Diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) Complex Formation for UV–Vis Spectrophotometric Determination
abstract: Direct UV–Vis spectrophotometric determination of Zn(II) is limited by the absence of a suitable intrinsic chromophore, necessitating complex formation to obtain an analytical absorption response. However, comprehensive optimization of the Zn(II)–diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) extraction system remains limited. This study optimized complex formation and chloroform extraction for Zn(II) determination and preliminarily examined Cr(III) interference. title: The Kārṣāpaṇa and the King's Share: Currency, Taxation and Fiscal Administration in the Empire of Aśoka
abstract: Aśoka's empire rested on two fiscal instruments that the epigraphic and archaeological record allows us to see with unusual clarity: a silver punch-marked currency denominationed in kārṣāpaṇas and paṇas, and a land-based revenue system whose central levy, bali, is named by the emperor's own inscription at Lumbinī. title: Reindeer herding in the face of climate change: how do the Saami adapt?
abstract: Both climate- and land-use change threaten the very essence of what it means to be a traditional Saami reindeer herder and potentially the ability of future generations to uphold this way of life; underlining both the cultural and economic costs. We report on a set of contingent valuation questions to improve the understanding of how reindeer herders adapt to climate change by either using supplementary feed or reducing their herd to ensure that future generations can uphold the traditional way of life. journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy

title: Placental Interdigitation Is Associated with Reproductive Pace across Mammals
abstract: Abstract The placenta is a transient organ mainly derived from fetal tissue that is essential for establishing metabolic and immune interactions that support healthy pregnancies in eutherian mammals. Across mammals, placentas show high morphological diversity in both the degree of tissue invasiveness and in the complexity of tissue integration between maternal and fetal tissues. This variation is thought to reflect strong selective pressures on reproductive strategies, balancing maternal investment, offspring development, resource transfer, and reproductive pace. title: The Semiotic of the Igbabonnenlimi Acrobatic Dance
abstract: The paper is an examination of thetraditions of the exoteric performance of the Igbabonnenlimi acrobatic dance of the Esan people of Edo state, Nigeria. It is an attempt to study what ordinarily cannot be comprehended through the orthodox Western scholarly tradition, an art, which nonetheless was experienced by a privileged group of initiates, that you may consider to be adherents of ancestral religion. title: Análisis textual de Ravens (1986) de Fukase Masahisa
abstract: Este artículo analiza la serie fotográfica Ravens (1986) del fotógrafo japonés Fukase Masahisa, centrándose en la construcción de la escena fantasmática y su capacidad para generar conexiones emocionales profundas con el espectador. La metodología empleada se basa en el análisis textual desde la Teoría del Texto, que permite articular los niveles semiótico, imaginario y real en la interpretación de la obra. title: Association of Dietary Carboxy Methyl Lysine in Adult Women With Central Obesity: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: The prevalence of central obesity, which is associated with the risk of hypertension and diabetes, has increased drastically, both globally and in Indonesia. Unhealthy dietary patterns, such as high sugar and high salt intakes, ultra-processed foods, and high dietary carboxymethyl lysine (dCML), are frequently associated with an increase in waist circumference (WC) that is used in evaluating central obesity. title: Numerical investigation of supersonic jet using a two-fluid turbulence model
abstract: In the present work, numerical simulation of an axisymmetric jet at a Mach number of 1.63 under temperature-matched conditions was performed using an improved two-fluid turbulence model. The proposed model includes an additional transport equation for the relative molar velocity, which enables a more accurate representation of Reynolds stress anisotropy, compressibility effects, and structural changes in high-speed shear layers. title: Economic Inequality and Economic Growth Trends of China and India (2000–2024) A Comparative Study
abstract: Economic growth and income inequality are two important indicators of a country's economic development. China and India have experienced substantial economic transformation since 2000. China has become a major manufacturing and export centre, while India has expanded in services, information technology, manufacturing and domestic consumption. However, economic growth does not reveal how evenly its benefits are distributed. This paper compares the growth patterns and inequality-related challenges of China and India from 2000 to 2024. title: ‘Somewhere between Ireland and England’: navigating gay politics in the 1980s through the housing experiences of Irish men in London
abstract: Focussing on the period from 1970 to 1990, this article examines how gay men, many of whom moved from Ireland to London, adapted their activism in the face of evolving housing pressures. It pays particular attention to how housing reforms, the AIDS crisis and notions of national identity shaped gay politics during this period and how the social crises of the 1980s transformed gay radicalism as conflict over identities and AIDS redefined gay activism and interactions with the state. title: The effect of various fiber surface modification on the microstructure and strength of sisal-reinforced mortar
abstract: This study investigates the mechanical performance, workability, and durability of sisal fibre-reinforced mortar (SFRC) modified through alkali treatment (NaOH) and combined alkali-paraffin treatment. Three mortar mixes were evaluated: untreated sisal fibres (USFRC), alkali-treated fibres (ATSFRC), and paraffin-alkali-treated fibres (PATSFRC). title: The Effect of Using Iodized Salt on Sensory Properties and Spoilage Processes in Foods
abstract: Iodine is an essential micronutrient, and iodine deficiency remains an important public-health concern worldwide. Although universal salt iodization is an effective strategy for improving iodine intake, food manufacturers have raised concerns regarding the possible effects of iodized salt on sensory quality, fermentation, spoilage, shelf life, and iodine stability. This semi-systematic review evaluated the available evidence concerning these outcomes in food systems. Searches of PubMed, Google Scholar, and DergiPark identified 6,041 records. title: Co-producing development: Yugoslavia and the UN Centre for Housing, Building, and Planning
abstract: This article examines the reciprocal relationship between Yugoslavia and the United Nations Centre for Housing, Building and Planning (CHBP) within the framework of the United Nations Development Programme's technical assistance. abstract: BACKGROUND: Massive bee stings can cause systemic manifestations and life-threatening complications. In French Guiana, data on such envenomations are scarce. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and management of patients presenting to the emergency department. title: Governing parties’ regulatory responses to informal miners
abstract: How do governing parties regulate informal miners and what explains regulatory response variations? Drawing on Ghana and leveraging original and secondary data, this paper shows that National Democratic Congress (NDC) incumbents tolerated most local miners even when President Mahama raided the informal mining sector. By contrast, while the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP’s) Kufour and Akufo-Addo attacked local miners, Akufo-Addo largely let off Chinese miners and their local collaborators. title: La nostalgia en las canciones de Rubén Blades: memoria afectiva, pertenencia y conciencia histórica en la salsa narrativa
abstract: Este artículo de reflexión analiza la nostalgia como una estructura de sentido recurrente en la obra de Rubén Blades. Aunque la recepción crítica ha privilegiado, con razón, el carácter urbano, narrativo y político de sus composiciones, la nostalgia constituye uno de los principios que articulan esas dimensiones. No aparece únicamente como tristeza por el amor perdido, sino como operación de la memoria mediante la cual el sujeto intenta restablecer continuidad entre pasado, presente y futuro. title: Fabrication of Lantana camara Extract Integrated Nanofibrous Membrane and Evaluation of Antimicrobial Activity
abstract: Plant-based extracts have long been used for their therapeutic potential. Lantana camara, an invasive perennial shrub, has exhibited antimicrobial activities, however, its potential antimicrobial activities in fibrous nano-formulation have not been reported yet. In this study, we report the integration of ethanolic extract of Lantana camara in polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) nanofibers by electrospinning method. title: Metabolic bone disease in juvenile zoo-housed black howler monkeys (Alouatta caraya)
abstract: Metabolic bone diseases (MBD) can occur in any animal due to insufficient vitamin D, which is essential for calcium absorption and regulation. New World primates have higher requirements for cholecalciferol (D3) than African or Eurasian primates, along with a decreased ability to utilize ergocalciferol (D2), the form associated with plants and fungi. abstract: The presence of Raoiella indica in Cocos nucifera plantations in Baracoa prompted interest in investigating alternatives for managing this invasive exotic pest, based on the damage it has caused in other regions. Therefore, the objective of this study is to determine the effectiveness of essential oils in managing R. indica in coconut cultivation. title: Effects of biochar and vermicompost application on the physicochemical properties of acidic soils in Sidama Region, Ethiopia
abstract: Soil acidity is a major constraint on crop productivity in tropical agriculture, particularly in regions like Ethiopia, where smallholder farmers often lack access to conventional amendments such as lime. While biochar (BC) and vermicompost (VC) have been studied individually, their combined potential for remediating acidic soils under local conditions remains insufficiently explored. title: Effects of dietary quality on type 2 diabetes risk and the mediating role of inflammatory markers
abstract: This study aimed to explore the association between multiple dietary quality indices and diabetes risk and investigate the potential role of systemic inflammatory markers in such relationships. Data were obtained from 21 476 participants in the Fuqing Cohort Study who completed a FFQ. Dietary quality was assessed using the Healthy Eating Index (HEI), Diet Quality Index (DQI) and Diet Balance Index (DBI). title: Female Leaders and the Populist Radical Right in the Nordic Countries
abstract: This article examines female leadership in populist radical right (PRR) parties in the Nordic countries, challenging the traditional view of these parties as “Männerparteien.” Building upon research on the centrality of gender to the radical right, we analyse biographical material covering the private and professional lives of two generations of female PRR leaders in Denmark (Pia Kjærsgaard), Finland (Riikka Purra), and Norway (Siv Jensen and Sylvi Listhaug). title: Experimental and life cycle assessment of reclaimed asphalt pavement modified with nano Fe2O3 and waste cooking oil admixtures
abstract: Abstract Thermal cracking, rutting, and moisture damage are common pavement distresses caused by heavy traffic growth, construction deficiencies, and environmental effects, reducing service life and performance. Asphalt additives can improve pavement behavior; however, a single modifier rarely enhances all properties simultaneously. This study investigates a composite modification approach using dual additives in reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP). abstract: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections is a serious threat to human health. Biofilm formation and limited antibiotic penetration reduce the effectiveness of conventional antibiotics, highlighting the need for more effective drug-delivery strategies. Niosomes, as promising vesicular drug delivery systems, have shown potential to enhance antibiotic efficacy. abstract: Gulf aviation has made significant progress in this century. While Gulf countries have achieved success in global recognition through significant advancements in the aviation sector, they have also become dependent on air transport. With the war centered on Iran, which began in February 2026, civilian settlements and airports in the Gulf countries became targets of attacks, disrupting air transport. abstract: Abstract This article challenges the image of Cold War Pakistan as a passive client state, arguing instead that Pakistan’s early international history was shaped by friction between a pro-Western elite and a domestic polity animated by anti-imperial solidarity, socialism, and Muslim internationalism. title: Institutional Openness and Cross-Regional Investment of Enterprises: Analysis Based on the Pilot Free Trade Zone
abstract: Institutional openness is a key policy in China's high-level opening-up and the construction of a unified national market in the new era, and how it affects the cross-regional capital allocation behavior of enterprises can promote the stable operation of the domestic economic cycle. title: High Yield of Pharmacogenetic Testing for Clopidogrel Resistance in a Canadian Outpatient Stroke Population
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clopidogrel is commonly prescribed for secondary stroke prevention, but routine pharmacogenetic testing is not typically performed. As the CYP2C19 enzyme activates clopidogrel into its effective form, clopidogrel-treated patients who carry CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles may face an increased risk of recurrent stroke. title: Molecular and haematological characterisation of haemoglobin G-Georgia: a case series from Terengganu, Malaysia
abstract: Haemoglobin G-Georgia (HBA1:c.287C>T) is a rare and benign alpha globin chain variant with amino acid substitution of Proline to Leucine in the alpha gene. title: Women as Ecological Leaders: Ecofeminism in the Context of Karampuang Indigenous Community
abstract: Women are often the victims of the destruction of nature caused by the exploitation of nature. The similarity of oppression between women and nature brings the same spirit to the ecological struggle. This study looks at the relationship between the values of local wisdom of the Karampuang indigenous people and ecofeminism principles. title: Assessing the Day Delay Effect of Port Congestion on US Agricultural Exports
abstract: ABSTRACT Relative to the rest of the world, shipping delays have been a problem in the US even prior to COVID‐19 but became more publicized and exacerbated during the pandemic. While previous studies have focused on COVID‐19 shocks using event study methods, we quantify the effect of congestion, measured as the average number of days a vessel spends in port, on US agricultural container exports using monthly export data from US ports. title: A striking new species of stick insect in the genus Micropodacanthus Brock & Hasenpusch, 2007 (Phasmida: Phasmatidae: Tropidoderinae: Tropidoderini) from Tropical North Queensland, Australia
abstract: A new species of phasmid within the seldom observed Australian endemic genus Micropodacanthus Brock & Hasenpusch, 2007 is described and figured herein. Micropodacanthus cyanops sp. nov. is described from female and male types, also eggs. Tables of notable and distinct characters are provided to compare with related spp. Habitat type and known host plant is noted. Other known Micropodacanthus spp. both described and undescribed are discussed and figured, providing a contemporary overview of the genus.

abstract: Armed violence spreading from the Sahel since 2021 has reached the farming systems of northern Benin, but we know little about where agricultural losses are heaviest and why. A multisectoral survey interviewed 350 households in Alibori (116), Atacora (110) and Borgou (124) between 29 August and 4 September 2026: hosts, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and refugees. abstract: Oxytetracycline (OTC) dihydrate, an approved broad-spectrum antibiotic, is widely used in aquaculture to combat bacterial infections like Aeromonas hydrophila in rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ). However, its optimal dosing, residue depletion kinetics, and withdrawal times remain underexplored in exotic species under Indian conditions, raising food safety concerns due to maximum residue limits (MRL) of 100 µg kg − 1 in muscle. abstract: Traditional healing practices constitute an important form of cultural and ecological knowledge that requires documentation and preservation, particularly as oral traditions face the risk of declining transmission across generations. This study examines the representation of natural elements and spiritual values in the Sembur Pansang Mantras practiced by the Malay community in Kemuning Village, West Kalimantan, Indonesia, from an ecocritical perspective. abstract: Viktor Frankl views self-transcendence as a key objective in developing into a fully realised human being. Hesychastic spirituality in Orthodox monasticism has a similar aim. During the transition from the secular to monastic life, monks go through radical self-transformation from the egoic to Edenic state. In that setting, self-transcendence becomes the ultimate aim of deification and a coping mechanism to deal with the suffering experiences often accompanying monastic spiritual development. title: Beyond the Ban: A Comparative Study of U.S. and Chinese Humanitarian Mine Action in Cambodia
abstract: This paper explores why the United States and China have supported humanitarian mine action in Cambodia although both have stayed outside the Ottawa Treaty, and what their involvement shows about the influence and the limits of international legal regimes. Cambodia serves as the case study, and the materials come from government documents, treaty and Review Conference reports, publications of international and Cambodian mine-action organizations, as well as secondary scholarship. abstract: The rising levels of heavy metal pollution in water bodies present major environmental and public health issues. Conventional methods for remediation often come with high costs and produce secondary waste, which can pose additional environmental risks. As an alternative, chitosan-a natural, biopolymer derived from chitin-has gained attention as a promising biosorbent for heavy metal removal. abstract: Heutagogy – commonly understood as self-determined learning – emphasises the learner’s agency in shaping their developmental journey through proactive, self-determined engagement. In the context of Christian discipleship, self-determined learning can foster spiritual growth across a range of personal convictions, denominational traditions, and theological frameworks. abstract: A dinâmica da superfície de água a variação espacial e temporal da extensão dos corpos hídricos é um indicador direto da disponibilidade de recursos hídricos e da resposta da paisagem à variabilidade climática e à pressão antrópica. title: Ancestry without identity? Generational identity change among Chinese descendants in Peru: A life-course perspective
abstract: Peru hosts one of the oldest Chinese-descended populations in the Americas and presents a striking numerical puzzle. Popular and community sources routinely claim that as many as one in ten Peruvians has some Chinese ancestry, yet in the 2017 census only 14,307 people described themselves as tusán, the Peruvian term for a locally born person of Chinese descent, and in 2025, the first census in which tusán was a printed response option rather than a write-in, the share remained near 0.06%. abstract: ABSTRACT Food sovereignty is increasingly promoted as an alternative to dominant food systems. In Aotearoa it is inseparable from Māori relationships to whenua and from colonial dispossession. This paper presents a kaupapa Māori review of academic, policy, and grey literature, with insights from the Manawatū region. abstract: The research analyzes the regulation of noise pollution around the Guayaquil Land Terminal and determines whether the municipal ordinance on environmental pollution prevention and control allows action against noise from mass transit and commercial activity. abstract: The study aims to identify the factors driving the accelerated economic development of Almaty, Astana, Shenzhen, Chengdu, and Xi’an and to determine the conditions for adapting the Chinese experience to Kazakhstan’s urban policy. The analysis covers 2010-2025 and combines complete annual series of Kazakhstan’s real growth with a comparison of the five cities in the reference years of 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025. title: Evaluasi Keandalan Buffer CCPM Melalui Back-Testing Fever Chart dan Rantai Markov pada Proyek Kompresor Bertekanan Sangat Rendah
abstract: Perilaku dinamis buffer selama pelaksanaan proyek masih kurang dipahami apabila penilaian kinerja hanya mengandalkan satu indikator pada akhir proyek. Penelitian ini bersifat studi kasus tunggal yang retrospektif/kontrafaktual: penelitian ini mengajukan kerangka back-testing dinamis yang mengintegrasikan Schedule-Weighted Progress Analysis (SWPA), Buffer Consumption Index (BCI), pemantauan Fever Chart, serta model rantai Markov yang bersifat eksploratif. title: Transformación digital del proceso crediticio en una financiera no bancaria mexicana: diagnóstico de fricciones y modelo estratégico por fases
abstract: Las sociedades financieras de objeto múltiple (SOFOMes) mexicanas han digitalizado la captación de clientes, pero muchas conservan procesos manuales en la validación y la formalización del crédito, lo que rompe la continuidad de la experiencia del cliente. El objetivo del estudio fue diagnosticar los puntos de fricción del proceso crediticio de una SOFOM mexicana especializada en crédito con descuento vía nómina y, con base en ese diagnóstico, proponer un modelo estratégico de transformación digital por fases. abstract: Abstract Background: Primary postpartum hemorrhage is one of the leading causes of maternal mortality and morbidity. abstract: Background: Nigeria’s persistent infrastructure deficit and constrained public finances have increased reliance on Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for mobilising private capital, expertise, and innovation. abstract: This article presents the results of the archaeobotanical study of the site Shuqayra al-Gharbiyya, which was founded as an Umayyad palace or qasr during the Early Islamic period and was continually occupied until the Late Ottoman period. Within the study the major crop taxa cultivated at or nearby the site, including a range of cereals, pulses, and fruit and nut trees, were identified. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Outpatient hysteroscopy is an essential gynaecological procedure used to evaluate and treat any intrauterine pathologies. However, the most common reason for procedure failure is pain. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) and music for pain management during outpatient hysteroscopy. The objective was to analyze the effectiveness of manual toothbrushing techniques, with emphasis on the modified Bass technique, and of their adjuncts. title: Comments on three invasive Rubus species: Rubus ellipticus Smith, Rubus rosifolius Smith and Rubus niveus Thunb., in Colombia
abstract: The occurrences of three invasive Rubus species, namely Rubus ellipticus Smith, Rubus rosifolius Smith and Rubus niveus Thunb. are analysed in three locations in Colombia. R. ellipticus and R. niveus are invasive species that form dense patches and threaten native vegetation. Due to their highly invasive nature, these two species should be given high priority in the development of an eradication programme. R. rosifolius was not seen to form thickets or to cause major environmental issues.

abstract: Due to institutional pressures within neoliberal university environments, faculty are experiencing heightened burnout. Exploring ways to reduce burnout in accessible and creative communal ways is significant. To counter experiences of burnout, two professors and one emerging academic examined the three tenets of the self-compassion framework through arts-based inquiry. abstract: This article examines how international and domestic legal instruments, particularly the 1964 Cairo Declaration and Eswatini’s 1968 independence Constitution, have shaped the management of Eswatini’s irredentist project in the postcolonial period. It argues that, rather than pursuing territorial revision through overt confrontation, the Eswatini monarchy has strategically navigated the normative frameworks of international law and domestic constitutional order to advance claims to territories lost under colonial rule. abstract: The development of the feed industry in sustainable aquaculture activities largely relies on plant-based proteins, which are widely available and relatively inexpensive, to address the global fishmeal shortage. However, these plant-derived protein sources contain various anti-nutritional factors, such as non-starch polysaccharides, phytates, protease inhibitors, tannins, and saponins, which are less utilizable by fish, thereby limiting nutrient utilization and disrupting mineral bioavailability in aquatic species. abstract: This study presents a literature review on the relationship between diabetes mellitus and periodontal disease, highlighting the bidirectional interaction between these conditions and the underlying inflammatory mechanisms. title: Effect of Accruals Quality on the Firm Value of Construction and Allied Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
abstract: Accruals quality is a dimension of financial reporting quality because reliable accrual information enables investors to assess reported earnings and firm performance. However, evidence on whether accruals quality translates into higher firm value remains limited among construction and allied firms listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange. abstract: Abstract Despite significant advances in early detection and therapeutic opportunities, cancer remains a critical global health challenge. The greatest barrier to reducing cancer‐associated mortality is the persistent problem of therapeutic resistance and metastasis. Standard treatment approaches, including surgery combined with chemotherapy and radiation, are effective for many patients with localised disease. title: Internationalisation by appropriation: Expertise, empire, and nineteenth-century health governance
abstract: Abstract How did health governance get internationalised, and with what effects? In the early nineteenth century, a range of transregional sanitary councils were responsible for mitigating the pandemic spread of diseases such as cholera. The International Sanitary Conferences, first convened in 1851, centralised this arrangement but also discriminated against non-European public health expertise. This article argues that this was a case neither of imperial power politics alone nor simply of functional problem-solving, but of the appropriation of pre-existing governance structures. abstract: Three-dimensional seismic exploration performed in the Cis-Urals area by the common depth point method enabled the author to investigate tectonic structure of the axial zone of the Inzer-Usolka trough representing the eastward extension of the Kama-Kinel trough system’s Aktanysh-Chishmy branch. abstract: Aquaculture policy must reconcile rising food demand with ecological limits and equitable livelihoods. abstract: O objetivo deste artigo é analisar a Educação de Jovens e Adultos como espaço de resistência ao neoliberalismo, considerando as relações entre educação, desigualdade social, abandono escolar e transformações do capitalismo contemporâneo. abstract: This paper contributes to debates on green states and green macrofinancial regimes in the Global South. It analyses Thailand, an upper-middle-income country that, although subject to international financial subordination, has sufficient domestic finance to support renewable energy rollout. abstract: Justification: Student persistence remains a major challenge for public higher education in Ecuador. abstract: Si bien la efectividad de los estilos de enseñanza de las ciencias (EEC) ha sido objeto de numerosas investigaciones, los factores que condicionan su implementación eficaz han recibido escasa atención. abstract: La enseñanza del inglés en la educación básica mexicana se ha orientado desde 2009 por el enfoque de prácticas sociales del lenguaje (PSL), promovido por el Programa Nacional de Inglés (PRONI) y reafirmado en la Nueva Escuela Mexicana (NEM). abstract: Dental caries is one of the most prevalent chronic diseases in childhood with an impact on quality of life. The objective was to synthesize the evidence on the magnitude of caries in schoolchildren, its risk factors and effective preventive strategies. A narrative literature review was conducted in SciELO, PubMed and public health portals; 20 documents in Spanish and English were analyzed. abstract: Scholarly discussion of Roland Leighton has previously been limited to his relationship to Vera Brittain and his role in her life as depicted in her memoir Testament of Youth. abstract: This paper examines the judicial application and evolving jurisprudence of equitable maxims within the Malaysian legal framework. abstract: This article examines virtual production as a critical infrastructure of contemporary audiovisual practice, moving beyond its restricted understanding as a technical innovation or a set of tools designed to optimize shooting processes. abstract: Eschatological traditions in Islam, Christianity, and Judaism share recurring motifs of cosmic disruption, an adversary figure, an agent of final justice, resurrection, and divine judgment, yet these parallels are often asserted rather than tested against specified sources. abstract: How, in oral performance, do we know that the end of the recitation or display has been reached? And how, too, in a manuscript context, can the end of a work be signalled to the reader? Such bringings-to-an-end were often loci of creativity, and I discuss the authorial ending (here termed ‘explicit’) and the scribal signing-off (here invoked as ‘colophon’), as well as scribal colonization of the authorial adieu; in all, an element which has often been dismissed as sterotyped, as fixed or as fossilized is shown to be in constant, often subversive, evolution. title: The Hidden Effects of Company Strikes: Workers Made Idle in UK Engineering and Metalworking From 1920 to 1970
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines a neglected aspect of industrial relations: workplace disputes in which workers are incidentally made idle because of strike actions of others. These spillover effects have received little systematic attention despite potentially accounting for a substantial share of the employment consequences of industrial conflict. The analysis uses a comprehensive dataset of company strikes compiled by the UK Engineering Employers' Federation (EEF) between 1920 and 1970, recording both workers directly involved in disputes and non‐striking employees made idle. title: Extreme Heat and Food Price Inflation in The United Arab Emirates
abstract: The UAE is one of the world's hottest countries and imports more than 90% of the food consumed by its population. This study asks a simple question: when UAE summers become more extreme, do food prices increase? To answer this, annual temperature records and annual food price inflation data for the UAE from 2013 to 2025 were collected and compared using straightforward statistical tools - averages, percentage changes, year-on-year comparisons, and the Pearson correlation coefficient. title: Integridad vs. Fraude científico
abstract: La integridad científica y la veracidad académica son los pilares fundamentales que sostienen el avance del conocimiento y la confianza social en la ciencia. No obstante, el entorno académico actual enfrenta retos significativos que ponen a prueba estos principios morales y profesionales. Objetivo: Analizar los desafíos que la cultura académica contemporánea plantea a la integridad científica y proponer estrategias orientadas a consolidar una práctica investigativa ética y transparente. abstract: This study identifies the scale-dependent processes that sustain turbulence in dense submerged canopy flows. abstract: Gingival inflammation is common in young adults and is related to habits and psychosocial factors. abstract: This study examines the ways in which anti‐immigrant right‐wing populist discourse is produced in Türkiye within the framework of population politics. abstract: Abstract The hemlock woolly adelgid (HWA), Adelges tsugae Annand, is an invasive pest devastating hemlock ( Tsuga ) forests in eastern North America. title: Geology of the Cambrian Marinkas Quellen carbonatite–alkaline complex (Southwest Namibia)
abstract: We present a new geological map of the Marinkas Quellen carbonatite-alkaline complex (Southwest Namibia), which forms part of the Cambrian Kuboos-Bremen Igneous Province. Our mapping reveals that the complex was assembled through several pulses of alkaline silicate and conjugate carbonatitic melts, which formed by liquid immiscibility from strongly alkaline, mantle-derived parental melts. abstract: El concepto de algoritmo suele asociarse en la actualidad al concepto de programa o a desarrollos tecnológicos contemporáneos. title: Scale insects (Hemiptera: Coccomorpha) found in Moroccan avocado groves; their distribution, importance and natural enemies
abstract: Abstract A study of 89 avocado ( Persea americana ) orchards in eight provinces in north‐western Morocco was conducted between October 2023 and September 2025 to detect scale insects (Hemiptera: Coccomorpha: Coccidae, Diaspididae, Monophlebidae and Pseudococcidae) and their associated natural enemies. The objective was to identify the factors associated with the formation of dental calculus and to apply preventive measures in schoolchildren aged 11 to 12 years from a school in Ambato. title: Soil Memory and Dryland Restoration Failure: Legacy Effects, Functional Thresholds, and Recovery Pathways: Review Article
abstract: Restoration projects in drylands fail in more than one way: some never establish, some decline after early success, and some gain vegetation cover while soil and hydrological functions remain impaired. Across 174 dryland seeding sites worldwide, 17% established none of the species sown, and seeded-species occurrence declined as projects aged. abstract: Frugal Innovation (FI) within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) has the potential to drive sustainable and financial value in resource-constrained environments. abstract: Este artículo analiza las experiencias vividas y los significados construidos por profesores universitarios en situación de precarización laboral y sus implicaciones para la gobernanza académica y las políticas universitarias en Colombia. El estudio se apoya en aportes sobre la neoliberalización de la educación superior, el capitalismo académico y la teoría crítica de la organización, junto con literatura reciente sobre precarización laboral del profesor universitario. abstract: Pepper cultivation provides an income opportunity for smallholder farmers, but information on the varieties grown, production practices and farm-level profitability in Benue State, Nigeria, remains limited. The study analysed the profitability of pepper production and varieties grown among smallholder farmers in Benue State, Nigeria. abstract: As buildings become taller, seismic control structures using hysteretic dampers have become widespread. These dampers yield at low load levels, mainly for earthquakes. abstract: Abstract This study presents the first micro-wear analysis of stone tools made from volcanic rocks from the Olduvai Bed II FC East (FCE) and FC West (FCW) sites at Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania, dated to approximately 1.6–1.5 Ma. These sites form part of a key stratigraphic interval documenting major technological and biological transitions during the early Pleistocene. abstract: Climate change has manifested as a primary catalyst of extreme weather patterns in Karachi. The rise in temperature has disturbed the conventional climate cycle, leading to extended periods of drought, heat waves, and erratic rainfalls. These extreme weather patterns are a direct result of wide-ranging climate unpredictability intensifying local vulnerabilities. title: Participación política femenina en la era digital
abstract: El artículo analiza el papel transformador de las redes sociales en la participación política de las mujeres. Destaca cómo estas plataformas permiten la movilización feminista, amplifican voces y desafían estructuras patriarcales. A pesar de su potencial, persisten desigualdades estructurales y violencia simbólica. Se propone una mirada crítica de la participación digital con enfoque de género, y se enfatiza la necesidad de políticas inclusivas y prácticas mediáticas feministas.

abstract: Scholars and policymakers increasingly use ecological metaphors such as “information environment” and “information ecosystem” to describe contemporary informational spaces. Ecology offers more than loanwords. Its concepts and frameworks can help researchers understand relationships among people, technology, content, and society. abstract: This article reads the Old English poem traditionally known as The Descent into Hell as an example of sophisticated, creative and speculative theology in the vernacular. abstract: Soybean production in the Chugoku region is often limited by environmental stresses, including excessive soil moisture at sowing and typhoon-induced lodging. title: Black Chickpea: Nutritional Architecture, Seed-Coat Phytochemistry, Techno-Functional Properties, and Processing Challenges
abstract: Abstract Black chickpea is a subgroup of desi chickpeas characterized by its black-colored seeds. title: Intervención o marginación institucional: relaciones cívico-militares en Latinoamérica a partir de Argentina y Ecuador
abstract: Este artículo compara las relaciones cívico-militares en Argentina y Ecuador tras la tercera ola de democratización, aplicando el institucionalismo histórico y el método comparado para explicar dichas relaciones en la actualidad. title: Eviction, Home and the Spatiality of Shame
abstract: ABSTRACT Rooted in the scene of residential evictions, the present article examines the intersection of shame and eviction through intimate group interviews with family members in gentrifying Mexico City. It makes three contributions: highlighting the role of shame in facilitating evictions, presenting a spatial theory of shame and offering strategies for resolving shame and restoring political agency and connection. abstract: Acne vulgaris is a widespread chronic inflammatory skin condition particularly affecting the pilosebaceous unit, with its pathogenesis intricately linked to excessive sebum production, abnormal follicular keratinization, overcolonization by Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes), and dysregulated host immune responses. Beyond its dermatological manifestations, the disorder is frequently associated with psychological comorbidities such as anxiety and depression, significantly impacting patients' quality of life. title: Mídia e imperialismo digital
abstract: Este texto apresenta o dossiê temático “Imperialismo, informação, comunicação e cultura na fase da digitalização”. Argumenta-se que a digitalização reconfigura, em vez de substituir, os fundamentos do imperialismo. O texto retoma brevemente a emergência histórica do imperialismo, examina como as plataformas digitais reconfiguram o imperialismo midiático e sintetiza diferentes abordagens teóricas sobre a relação entre imperialismo e tecnologias digitais. Por fim, apresenta as contribuições reunidas no dossiê.

abstract: Water sources serve as a requirement for human consumption, industrial, and agricultural needs and a resource for valuable ions. Appropriate treatment of water that captures ions from the aqueous solution can give rise to suitable `products', such as critical ions (such as Li$^+$) in selective ion recovery and usable water in the case of desalination (i.e., removal of non-essential ions). abstract: Emerging data-intensive space applications generate large volumes of data that must be processed, stored, replicated, and delivered efficiently. However, relying on terrestrial cloud regions can expose satellite data to high delivery latency and loss of timeliness due to intermittent satellite-to-ground visibility and limited access to ground infrastructure. Space Data Centers (SDCs), which organize collaborative satellites into logical compute and storage clusters, offer a promising approach for in-orbit data management and service continuity.
