title: A Physically-Motivated Stochastic Model of Tropical Cyclone Dynamic Wind Fields
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) pose significant risk to infrastructure and human safety, and the frequency and intensity of large TCs are expected to increase in the future. Quantifying such risk to coastal and inland regions is challenging, largely due to the rare nature of TCs which limits historical data availability. We introduce a new stochastic model of TC wind fields conditional on a small number of physical variables commonly found in synthetic and observed storm track databases. The model consists of a physically-motivated mean trend and an expansion of the residual field into a wavelet fram

title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

title: From Earth to Mars and Beyond: AI-Driven Cosmic-Ray Validation and Prediction with CorsikaAgent
abstract: We calculate the sea-level cosmic-ray muon flux with CORSIKA and develop CorsikaAgent, an auditable large-language-model-based system for configuring, executing, and validating air-shower simulations, and for predicting particle fluxes in unexplored environments. The physics calculation uses proton primaries described by the solar-minimum spectrum of Papini et al., with UrQMD at low interaction energies and either Sibyll 2.3e or QGSJET-III at high energies. This calibration score drives performance-based weights and implicitly assumes independent seed variables, although seeds often share a common driver, such as the same indicator in several regions or periods. title: Parameterizing Cluster Editing by the Number of Deletions
abstract: In Cluster Editing, we are given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$ and ask whether at most $k$ edge insertions and deletions turn $G$ into a disjoint union of cliques. abstract: Digital nudges have become a prominent area of research in human-centered interaction, yet little is known about how they interact when deployed together. abstract: Excitation of carbon and oxygen ions is the primary mechanism by which collapsing gas clouds dissipate heat to form new stars. At early cosmic times, in galaxies with chemically pristine gas, many stars are expected to have masses far larger than the mass of our sun due to the deficit in these elements. abstract: Artificial warming via engineered aerosols presents a novel pathway to bypass volatile scarcity on modern Mars. Utilizing the Generic Planetary Climate Model, we evaluate the physical feasibility of aerosol-induced terraforming over a full Martian year (669 Sols). title: RTISSLAM-3D: Full 6-DoF SLAM With an In-Air 3D Imaging Sonar
abstract: Echolocating bats navigate dense forests using sonar alone, and in-air 3D imaging sonars now capture the entire frontal hemisphere with every pulse. Sonar SLAM, however, has so far been planar: current systems estimate a 2D trajectory and discard the elevation information in the sonar images, an assumption that does not hold on rough and sloped terrain such as a forest floor. In this paper, we introduce RTISSLAM-3D, a novel 6-DoF SLAM system for a wheeled robot that carries an in-air 3D imaging sonar, an IMU and wheel encoders. abstract: Amino acid enantiomeric excess (EE) is a potential biosignature, but its measurement requires sufficient surviving material as well as preserved chirality. title: Personality Without Persons? A Psychometric Critique of Big Five Testing in Large Language Models
abstract: Human personality inventories are increasingly used to characterize large language models (LLMs), compare systems, and inform downstream governance claims. Yet, these inventories were developed and validated for humans, and it remains unclear whether they are valid for non-human systems. We present a systematic psychometric evaluation of Big Five personality measurement in LLMs. We ask three research questions: Do Big Five inventories a) appropriately describe LLMs, b) capture meaningful differences between models, and c) reflect internal factors consistent with human personality? abstract: Detecting biosignatures on Earth-like exoplanets from the Proterozoic era requires instrumentation capable of probing near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectral features, particularly ozone (\ce{O3}), which serves as an indirect proxy for molecular oxygen (\ce{O2}) when direct detection is challenging. title: Image CL-SEC: Cross-Layer Semantic Error Correction for Image Communication
abstract: Semantic error correction (SEC) uses the semantic knowledge of pretrained models to complement conventional channel decoding. By combining physical-layer decoding information with application-layer semantic predictions, cross-layer SEC (CL-SEC) has demonstrated substantial performance gains in text transmission; however, its applicability to image transmission remains largely unexplored. abstract: Feature caching has become a mainstream training-free strategy for accelerating video diffusion models by reusing intermediate outputs across denoising steps. However, existing adaptive methods rely on heuristic difference measures misaligned with actual generation quality, employ a single global threshold that ignores heterogeneous phase dynamics, and never validate their budget estimates against true approximation error, allowing systematic bias to propagate uncorrected. abstract: We provide a theory of optimal trade sanctions with three strategic players: Home (sanctioner), Foreign (target), and Bystander. First, members of a coalition generically set different tariffs either under Stackelberg timing or when transfers are imperfect. title: Atmospheric channel model for QKD over satellite megaconstellations
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. title: Millennial‐Scale Climate States Alter Atlantic Multidecadal Variability Mechanisms in a Climate Model
abstract: Abstract The Atlantic Multidecadal Variability (AMV) influences North Atlantic sea surface temperatures and regional climate phenomena such as European droughts and hurricane activity. abstract: Phytopathogens pose a persistent threat to global crop production, necessitating the development of sustainable biocontrol strategies. Microbial biopesticides offer a promising alternative to chemical pesticides; however, their industrial application is frequently constrained by low production titers and high substrate costs. abstract: Igneous centres across the Taranaki Peninsula represent the southwestern limit of arc volcanism associated with the Tonga–Kermadec–Hikurangi subduction system. Taranaki Maunga, the youngest and largest of three andesitic stratovolcanoes, dominates the geomorphology of the Taranaki Peninsula along with the eroded remnants of the Kaitake and Pouakai edifices. abstract: Abstract The under-development NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to provide breakthroughs in exoplanet science, yet the most effective approaches to modeling the detection and characterization of potentially Earth-like worlds with HWO remain uncertain despite being essential considerations for mission design. abstract: Abstract Effective conservation efforts are contingent on understanding the underlying demographic processes that regulate wildlife populations. abstract: Abstract The paleolatitudinal change of the Lhasa Terrane is critical for estimating the timing of the India–Asia collision and associated syn‐to post‐collisional crustal shortening, but its paleoposition is highly debated. Here we present integrated geochronologic and paleomagnetic results from the Lower Eocene Nianbo Formation in the Linzhou Basin. abstract: Abstract The combined use of detrital and inherited zircon U-Pb age spectra provides new insights into the crustal evolution of the Iberian Massif as part of the North Gondwana margin. title: Sulfide‐Ene Reactions by Visible‐Light‐Mediated Phosphine Redox Catalysis
abstract: Sulfur‐containing compounds play a crucial role in many biological processes. The important gasotransmitter hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) can be metabolized by cellular enzyme system for the biosynthesis of amino acids and regulatory effects related to diseases. Although the photocatalytic thiol‐ene reactions have been widely developed, a general H 2 S‐ene reaction by organic photocatalysis remains elusive. title: Gaussian process inference of stochastic magneto-active dynamics and viscosity in Swift J1727.8-1613
abstract: Linking X-ray variability to the underlying magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics of black hole X-ray binaries remains challenging. We systematically investigate the stochastic and oscillatory variability of the black hole X-ray binary candidate Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 outburst using Gaussian process (GP) regression applied to Insight-HXMT multi-band light curves. The variability is modelled with a physically motivated composite kernel comprising one stochastically driven damped simple harmonic oscillator (SHO) and two damped random walk (DRW) components. title: Near-bed hydrodynamics controlling fine-sediment erosion over immobile coarse-grained beds
abstract: The erosion of fine sediments from an immobile coarse-grained bed depends on the degree of exposure of the coarse grains. In an earlier study (Trevisson & Eiff, Water Resour. Res. , 2022, vol. 58, issue 11, p. e2021WR031837), we showed that, under sediment-supply limitation, erosion evolves through four regimes of alternating enhancement and sheltering. title: Owned dog population profile, dog ownership and bite risk determinants: Key steps to rabies control in Antananarivo, Madagascar
abstract: Rabies remains a significant public health threat in Madagascar, with dog-mediated transmission causing approximately 1,000 human deaths annually. In Antananarivo, the capital city, control efforts are hindered by limited up to date knowledge on the dog population. This study aims to provide updated estimates of the owned dog population characteristics, identify determinants of ownership, and assess dog bite incidence and risk factors to guide effective vaccination and prevention strategies. title: Simulation of errors related to the VLBI transmitter on Genesis and their impact on the terrestrial reference frame
abstract: Mission Genesis of the European Space Agency has been approved for launch in 2028. Its primary goal is the enhancement of the terrestrial reference frame by establishing a space tie on the Genesis satellite between all space geodetic techniques used for the determination of the frame. The satellite will be equipped with a dedicated Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) transmitter for geodesy. abstract: This research is aimed at Applying Bayesian decision model in Agribusiness value chain intervention project in Niger Delta. The objectives are: to determine Prior (Prototype) and Posterior (Model) Probability, Expected Monetary Value (EMV), Marginal Probability, Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI), Expected Profit in Perfect Information (EPPI), The problems the study solve were: inadequate funding of multipurpose scheme, inefficient economic benefits and losses. title: Reframing the Gender Hierarchy: Challenging the Patriarchy Through Visual Analysis of Photos on Agriculture Organization Websites
abstract: ABSTRACT Gendered systems of power in agriculture underpin a heteropatriarchy that disempowers women's participation. To interrogate how imagery may function as both a reflective and perpetuating force in maintaining heteropatriarchy across the agricultural sector we analyzed 357 images on 36 Australian agriculture organization websites, coding them for key attributes. We found most images coded ‘farming’ as inherently masculine and drew on stereotypical notions of the ‘rural man’ and ‘masculinised farmer’. title: Hexafluoroisopropylthiolation of Ene‐yne‐ketones with HFA · 3H 2 O / SOCl 2 for Modular Synthesis of SCH ( CF 3 ) 2 ‐Functionalized Furans
abstract: Comprehensive Summary Notwithstanding the importance of the hexafluoroisopropyl group (CH(CF 3 ) 2 ) in medicinal and agricultural chemistry, convenient access to hexafluoroisopropylthiolated (SCH(CF 3 ) 2 ) compounds remains challenging, limiting their exploration. Herein, we report a straightforward and efficient hexafluoroisopropylthiolation strategy using readily available hexafluoroacetone trihydrate (HFA·3H 2 O) and SOCl 2 as practical reagents. title: Dreams across borders an Indian woman’s journey from academia to Australian politics
abstract: Abstract In the twenty-first century, where inclusion and diversity are vital to the advancement of countries like Australia, the stories of women navigating multicultural and professional boundaries offer valuable insights. In this article, we explore the journey of a Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) researcher, Parwinder Kaur, who migrated from India, completed her doctorate at the University of Western Australia, built a successful academic research career, and recently entered the realm of Australian politics. title: Diversity and structure of soil nematode communities under Heracleum sosnowskyi pressure: latitudinal and invasion-driven variations
abstract: Soil nematode communities under invasion by Heracleum sosnowskyi Manden. (Sosnowsky’s hogweed) were studied in habitats of different latitudinal locations. The research was conducted in four hogweed sites located between 61° and 55° N, in the Republic of Karelia (Shuya and Essoila villages), and the Leningrad and Moscow Regions. Soil samples were collected beneath dense H. sosnowskyi stands and in adjacent control meadows that were not invaded. institutions: Institute of Biology of Karelian Research Centre

title: Analysis of options for building an orbital constellation of a multifunctional personal satellite communication system
abstract: A comprehensive analysis of the construction of a promising orbital constellation is presented, as a result of which it was found that the existing four-by-seven structure, corresponding to four orbital planes with seven spacecraft in each, with an orbit height of one and a half thousand kilometers and an inclination of eighty-two and a half degrees, is initial for further optimization. Analysis of the instantaneous position of the orbital constellation four by seven, taking into account the radio visibility zone at an angle of ten degrees, demonstrates a coverage close to one hundred percent.

title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe–N–C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe–La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. title: A microwave-based system for hydrogen production by using CNT/rGO catalyst
abstract: Due to strict environmental requirements and problems related to fuel use and shortages, hydrogen energy has emerged as a pivotal clean energy carrier. However, conventional production methods are often energy- and carbon-intensive. In the present work, a novel approach for hydrogen production was investigated using a microwave-assisted pyrolysis system. abstract: When conducting studies on animal production, data must be analyzed with appropriate statistical methods. In reserach, One Sample Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test was used in comparisons made according to a certain reference value. Milk production data used for Türkiye and Bingöl province were obtained from TUİK. title: Field-induced near-unity spin polarization in a highly emissive organic diradical
abstract: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. title: Piperaceae Giseke. no Município de Vitória da Conquista, Bahia, Brasil
abstract: O presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar o inventário florístico das espécies de Piperaceae ocorrentes no município de Vitória da Conquista, Bahia. O trabalho foi desenvolvidocom base na análise de exsicatas provenientes de herbários, consultas a bases de dados virtuais e expedições de campo realizadas em fragmentos de floresta estacional decidual e floramentos rochosos. Foram registradas três espécies: Piper arboreum Aubl., Piper umbellatum L. e Peperomia blanda (Jacq.) Kunth, sendo esta última uma nova ocorrência para o município. title: Multiscale computational modeling of photoacoustic generation from micrometer-size polymeric bead suspensions in liquid media
abstract: Photoacoustic sensing has emerged as a promising technique for detecting polymeric particles suspended in liquids through the conversion of absorbed optical energy into acoustic signals. Here, we present a multiscale computational study of the photoacoustic response of polystyrene (PS) beads suspended in water under pulsed optical excitation. The framework combines particle-resolved simulations of individual beads with point-particle descriptions of randomly distributed multi-particle suspensions. title: Numerical Solutions of Inelastic Compressible Fluid Flow in Two Dimensional Square Cavity
abstract: In this study, inelastic compressible flow within a two-dimensional square cavity is investigated using the Galerkin finite element method. The main goal is to investigate the effect of lid-driven boundary conditions on the flow characteristics. We apply two types of boundary conditions, a constant lid velocity and a given analytical velocity profile. title: Extending the Martian landslide inventory southward: distribution, landslide types, and latitudinal extent
abstract: Martian landslide inventories remain concentrated near the equator, particularly in Valles Marineris. We present 411 previously uncatalogued landslides spanning 63°S–34°N, extending coverage of the southern mid-latitudes and increasing the existing global catalogue by approximately 13%. Most events (73.7%) occur between 20°S and 50°S, and 84.9% originate within Early and Middle Noachian highland units. title: Borders and boundaries in words: The linguistic construction of Mediterranean migration in EU/UN and MSF texts
abstract: Every year, thousands of people flee war, persecution, and poverty in their home countries and make the dangerous journey across the Mediterranean in search of a safer future. In response to this ongoing humanitarian crisis, organisations like Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) conduct search and rescue operations to prevent the loss of life. title: INDIGENOUS CONFLICT MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES AND RURAL COMMUNITY PROTECTION IN SOUTH-SOUTH NIGERIA
abstract: Persistent rural insecurity in South-South Nigeria has continued to undermine community safety despite the expansion of formal policing and state-led security interventions. Incidences of communal violence, land disputes, theft, cult-related activities, and other localized conflicts have exposed the limitations of conventional security approaches, thereby reviving interest in indigenous conflict management mechanisms. abstract: La Informática Forense es una rama del conocimiento que trabaja con evidencia digital, información almacenada en un medio digital que es relevante para una investigación. title: Comparative efficacy of new-generation fungicides against major fungal diseases of rice
abstract: A field study was conducted during the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 at the Rice Research Unit, Agricultural Research Institute, Rajendranagar, using a randomised block design (RBD) with 8 treatments and 4 replications to evaluate the efficacy of seven multi-active combination fungicides against three predominant fungal diseases of rice in Telangana, namely sheath blight, blast and grain discolouration, which limit rice productivity and grain quality under intensive production systems. title: A Cost-Illness Analysis of Economic Burden of Unimproved Water Use on Households: Empirical Evidence from Dhaka Urban Riparian Areas
abstract: The rapid urbanization and increasing industrial establishment near Dhaka’s rivers are creating environmental pressure on nearby communities. And people due to several factors are forced to use unimproved water from the nearby waterbodies. This study looks at how using unsafe water affects the health, health expenditure and poverty of 1,826 families living near the Turag River in Dhaka. It uses two main ways of measuring the impact: one that looks at the cost of getting sick and another that considers what people miss out on when they are ill. title: Party Membership Rolls on the Open Web
abstract: Enmarcado en el campo de la Computación y Sociedad, este artículo analiza la difusión reciente de padrones de afiliados a partidos políticos en Argentina, a partir de casos masivos detectados en 2026. Examinamos la tensión entre la Ley Orgánica de Partidos Políticos y la Ley de Protección de Datos Personales, que queda sin resolver, poniendo el foco en cómo los cambios tecnológicos transformaron el significado práctico de que dichos padrones sean “públicos”. title: Taking Value Constitutionalism Seriously: Migration and Values in EU Law and European Society
abstract: Abstract This article argues that taking Article 2 values seriously as a cornerstone of EU constitutional law requires analysing domains beyond the rule of law and judicial independence. It investigates the role of values in migration management by taking the EU–Turkey Statement and temporary reintroduction of border checks within Schengen as examples through which to tease out how values interact with non-values-based priorities, the indeterminacy of divergent interpretations of values, and the value of freedom. title: Impact of weather parameters on the progression of bakanae disease (Fusarium moniliforme Sheldon) in aromatic rice (Oryza sativa L.) in the north-western region of Haryana, India
abstract: Various biotic constraints affect the cultivation of aromatic rice in India, especially in the North-West Plain Zone and bakanae disease is responsible for high economic losses ranging from 3.0–95.4 %. It occurs in Haryana and the adjoining states, particularly in early-transplanted rice crops. Weather influences all stages of the host and pathogen life cycle, as well as disease progression. To manage and forecast bakanae disease, it is important to understand the interaction between the host, pathogen and environment. title: Selective Logical Acquisition Model for Low-Intrusion Mobile Devices with Integrity and Traceability Guarantees in Field Contexts
abstract: La adquisición forense de dispositivos móviles en campo presenta desafíos en integridad, trazabilidad y control metodológico, especialmente cuando se utilizan métodos descentralizados o documentación manual. Estas limitaciones introducen riesgos de sobreescritura y cuestionamientos sobre la validez probatoria de la evidencia recolectada fuera del laboratorio. Se propone un modelo de adquisición de baja intrusión basado en detectabilidad verificable en lugar de inviolabilidad. title: Recent advances and emerging mechanisms in graphene-based materials for cartilage tissue engineering
abstract: Graphene-based materials offer tunable mechanical, electrical, and biochemical properties that address longstanding challenges in cartilage tissue engineering. This review synthesizes recent advances in graphene derivatives, scaffold fabrication strategies, and emerging mechanisms governing cell-graphene interactions. We evaluate how graphene enhances mechanical reinforcement, bioactivity, and matrix production across hydrogels, polymer composites, and ECM-derived scaffolds. title: Luxury hospitality meets sustainability: crafting impactful stories on social media
abstract: Purpose Luxury is synonymous with quality, exclusivity and rarity, characteristics which do not hold sustainability as a core consideration in service provision. This study aims to investigate how luxury service brands craft stories on social media around their sustainability practices. Design/methodology/approach In-depth, semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of informants using an interview protocol informed by consultation with literature in storytelling and sustainability marketing as well as four pilot interviews with practitioners in luxury hospitality. title: A deeper look into the diversity of suckermouth catfishes (Mochockidae: Chiloglanis Peters 1868) of southern Africa, with the description of four new species
abstract: Suckermouth catfishes of the genus Chiloglanis Peters 1868 are small and predominantly rheophilic fishes endemic to Africa. This genus is quite diverse, with over 70 species distributed across most river systems on the continent, except for the Cape Fold ecoregion and most of northern Africa. The present study undertook detailed genetic and morphological examination of suckermouth catfishes collected from multiple localities across the Zambezi River system. Results from this study support preliminary field observations that had identified considerable morphological and colour pattern variation

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
abstract: Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. title: Dos nuevas especies de Agave (Asparagaceae, Agavoideae) de Oaxaca, México, y nueva circunscripción de Agave isthmensis, A. marmorata y A. scaposa
abstract: Antecedentes y Objetivos: Con 45 especies de Agave, Oaxaca es el estado con la mayor riqueza y endemismo del género en México. El conocimiento taxonómico y biogeográfico de sus especies ha variado con el tiempo, reflejando cambios en su nomenclatura y diversidad. Este estudio tiene como objetivo describir dos especies nuevas para la ciencia, segregadas de especies previamente descritas, redefinir la circunscripción taxonómica y geográfica de los taxones involucrados, proponer el cambio de sección para una de ellas y especificar los usos y la nomenclatura tradicionales.Métodos: Se realizó traba

title: Measurement of the neutrino cross section across the TeV scale using IceCube data
abstract: Neutrinos interact with matter exclusively through the weak force, resulting in extremely small cross sections that are difficult to measure. At TeV energies, neutrino-nucleon interactions probe the structure of the nucleon in regimes where our knowledge of it is less complete, and signatures of physics beyond the Standard Model could manifest. Recent measurements using collider, atmospheric, and astrophysical neutrinos have begun to explore this regime, but no single measurement has provided precise coverage from sub-TeV to tens of TeV, and uncertainties remain at the level of about 20-40%. abstract: The nearly pure TeV-scale Higgsino dark matter provides a natural explanation for the high-energy nuclear-recoil excess reported by LUX-ZEPLIN. title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
abstract: We perform direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence to investigate the mechanisms responsible for the maintenance of large-scale geostrophic vortices. We confirm that the Reynolds stresses generated by inertial waves are consistent with the Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes balance of the large-scale flow and demonstrate the predicted cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, with cyclones exhibiting stronger azimuthal velocities and more compact cores. title: Stockmayer Fluid with a Shifted Dipole. III. Ion Solvation
abstract: Though ion solvation is well understood for the standard Stockmayer fluid, the effect of displacing the point dipole of a Stockmayer particle, a simple geometric modification, on ion-solvent structuring and solvation thermodynamics remains less understood. We use molecular dynamics simulations to describe how a dipole shift affects radial and orientational solvent structure around centered ions, how strongly the solvent distinguishes cations and anions, and how the solvent mediates ion-ion pairing. title: Optical constraints on intranight variability in TeV HBLs from a two-year Asiago Schmidt monitoring campaign
abstract: We present a two-year homogeneous optical monitoring campaign of three TeV-emitting high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac objects, 1ES 1959+650, H 1426+428, and PG 1553+113, carried out with the Asiago Schmidt 67/92 cm telescope. TeV blazars are key targets in high-energy astrophysics, relevant for relativistic jet physics, particle acceleration, multiwavelength variability studies, and, in selected cases, multimessenger programmes. title: Organisation and aggregation of calcium carbonate ions in water via molecular simulation
abstract: Crystallisation of calcium carbonate (CaCO$_3$) in aqueous solutions is essential for carbon dioxide sequestration and the sustainable production of calcium carbonate materials, which are widely used in industry and increasingly explored for novel applications. While crystallisation is often analysed within the framework of classical nucleation theory, CaCO$_3$ and other ionic crystals often form through amorphous precursor phases, motivating the need for alternative descriptions.
